The Best Professor. Dominates most econ professors regarding teaching, difficulty of material, and caring about student. Super genuine and accessible outside of class. Dont believe comments about "cannot explain things clearly", basically for hard materials like game theory, if you cannot understand Dilip's explanation, just quit any advanced Econ.

Dilip is one of my favorite professors at NYU. He is truly caring and is extremely good at teaching. Besides being a fabulous teacher, Dilip is a highly-respected economist. Taking his class is such a once in a lifetime opportunity that gives me some taste of what microeconomics really is. I admire Dilip's research so much!

Game theory was interesting but v hard, prob wouldn't recommend unless you're rly interested or want a challenge. Got a 60% in the class and ended up w a B+ (somehow). Prof is knowledgable and happy to explain things in OH but the class gets technical with definitions and lectures can be confusing. Take it only if you're willing to put in the work.
Probably the best, in terms of teaching.

No need pointing out avg.55 to suggesting the prof isn't fair with grade. The final grade's really just about how you stack up with the rest of the class. Heads up, a 70 can actually land you an A range. It's all about the class curve, not just the raw points you rack up. Maybe take a sec to reflect on how many lecture/recitation\OH you've skipped.

Cannot explain clearly about classwork. 
Very hard exams and homework. 
Sample exams are not trustful
Average of one midterm is 55 score
hard understanding of slides
Very boring and slow speaking class

Prof Abreu is one of the pioneers in contemporary game theory. Intuitive content at the beginning but will get much tougher, but he is patient to explain repeatedly. Assignments are challenging but helpful, but exams are easier with a generous curve. However, I don't recommend taking it without solid calculus and probability theory knowledge.

He is passionate and insightful about game theory and is very patient when answering questions. Homework can get really tough but exams are easier with a generous curve. However, I wouldn't recommend the course if you are not into game theory or don't have a solid understanding of micro theory and calculus.
Challenging course materials, hard homework and exams, but he is willing to repeatedly explain during lectures and office hours. Also a generous curve up at the end.

Difficult in terms of the material, but he's willing to repeatedly explain things in class and in office hours. He's patient when you don't understand things. It can be hard to teach yourself the slides without explanation or examples, so definitely come to class. Exams are curved generously and not as hard as the problem sets
unless you're either very smart or very interested in game theory, i would avoid this class... extremely difficult material + difficult to follow slides, and he is not good at explaining it
He is so so, nothing earth-shattering. Wish him luck

Amazing. Material is extremely difficult, but he knows this and encourages questions and office hours visits, even if you ask the same question 15 times. He's extremely intelligent and passionate about the subject, and he genuinely cares about inspiring his students. Problems sets are impossible. Tests are fair (and curved). He's seriously awesome.
Took his class randomly as an elective, but was amazed when it quickly became one of my favorite classes of all time. He's super engaging and listens to student feedback very well.

For ethics, hes great to take at the end of the day. He often lets students out early or has films related to class topics. Overall, he's also extraordinarily compassionate and understanding. He almost seems uniquely in tune with the issues Tandon students face. He cares and feels like a respected friend rather than professor. Offers extensions too

He's funny and an amazing professor. He makes crazy jokes and make sure the lecture is engaging so students don't feel bored (although I had him at 8AM). If you want a free A on top of your other hard classes i would suggest you take him. He doesnt give out weekly assignments, you really just have 3 essay assignment throughout the semester.

I had a great time being part of his lecture. He doesn't give out much assignments and definitely not a tough grader. The topics he goes over sometimes might be a bit weird at times though. But overall an amazing professor.
He is literally the best, I wish I could take all my classes with him.

One of the best professors at NYU. He is very caring, and you can learn a lot from his class. If you want a class that helps you take a break from all the difficult classes at NYU, take him. Show up to class and pay attention. The papers are a bit confusing, but if you ask him, he is very understanding and can help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the most funny and kind teachers I have ever had. He really cares about his students and wants them to do well. He's so chill about the assignments and is really understanding. Take him! And treat him well!
An easy A where you actually learn at the same time! His class was a lot of discussion and we watched movies from time to time. The assignments are also not that difficult. Just show up lol.
Super chill guy will super chill assignments. If you just show up to class you're bound to learn some interesting stuff. Totally recommend taking him for ethics!
One of the best humanities professors at Tandon

Great, easy going professor. Genuinely interesting topics. Not much technology. You don't need to do the readings. Understandable and approachable. Minimal effort class, you can tell he cares about his students. Accommodating, overall great teacher and guy! You get a fun final that other professors wouldn't give. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Andrew is a good professor, he really cares about our thoughts and adjust his lectures.
Really great professor. Highly Recommend!
Really great professor, super understanding, easy to do well. Highly recommend!
GOAT! Very humorous teacher, his jokes are interesting.

Andrew is such a wonderful and knowledgeable professor. He really cares about what he's teaching and even brought in guest lecturers. He's super engaging, funny, and chill. He assigns a lot of reading but is open to our opinions on what we read, so the readings gradually became more interesting. I hight recommend any class he teaches.

This course over promised and under delivered. The professor presents professionally but it's obvious that it is inauthentic. She does rage bait. It is made to be over complicated. She states that she created her book for her students. — yes to profit off of more when it is not worth it. She said she wrote it with AI as well.

Nancy is very passionate however her class is incredibly mundane. Her instructions are consistently unclear despite her having multiple books released that emphasize the importance of clarity. We were also all made to buy her book that she wrote... It is not worth buying the book.

It's not a hard class but she makes it so complicated. Unclear with instructions and expect students to do it. A little harsh grader and she cares so much about the zoom camera angels, she said the ratio above my head is not right lol. she is very picky and rage baits students so much. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS.

Avoid this professor's class. nancy's class has a lot of homework every week and she never gives feedback on the assignments. Whenever a student has a question for her, she uses ChatGPT to answer the student's question. Also she treats students very rudely. Nancy's assignments are also very confusing, no clear instruction was given all the time.

Prof. Bari is an outstanding educator. He connects theory to practical applications and encourages critical thinking and creating an engaging classroom environment. His enthusiasm and dedication inspire students to learn deeply and actively participate. Overall, he is not just a great professor but a mentor who leaves a lasting impact.

Professor Bari is an amazing professor! Even though his grading is strict (he uses binary grading), he does it to really nail in the stakes of making mistakes in the computer science industry. He is funny, does his best to support his students even through his many other professional commitments, and is practical about how we should learn CS.

He is knowledgeable, but the teaching did not feel friendly. It can be hard to keep up, especially before the midterm. The grading is one of the biggest issues. It feels strict-- you get one wrong will get 0. The midterm seemed to allow some partial credit, but in practice, the deductions still felt very heavy. Also he isn't willing to answer Qs.

Prof Bari is extremely caring and a great teacher! Course is graded on HW, Quizzes, and 3 exams but he tries to give people ample opportunity to make up for mistakes. Quiz questions are based on HW. Small part of Exams are take home which allows you to boost your grade and he sprinkles in extra credit for writing chap summaries and attending class.
Professor Bari is so demanding and pushes you to your limits, but he's unequivocally the greatest professor of all time. The legend.
Be ready for a truly impressive number of in-person blue book quizzes. Blink and you're taking one. Sometime he does two in one session.
Be ready for an olympic level number of in-person blue book quizzes.

The course was definitely challenging, with frequent pop quizzes and a strict, binary-style grading system that made expectations feel high from the start. In hindsight, it's clear that he genuinely wants students to learn and succeed. Although it was tough in the moment, I  appreciate his approach, and I would consider taking him again.

prof was extremely hard on us with pop quizzes and BINARY GRADING. Lots of people didn't do well on the midterm so there was an unbelievable curve. Looking back, professor truly does want us to learn, and gave us extra tips/hints on what would be on the final. Although I couldn't see it then, I believe I would take his course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: too many in-person blue books quizzes (over 20), he even can not carry them to our large class, but he works so hard to make us learn and at the end you end up with so much knowledge and a good grade! he is a legend! a GREAT professor. Highly recommend Prof. Bari!

Prof. Bari did an excellent job teaching the AI seminar course. The course was well-structured, engaging, and intellectually rewarding. I gained a strong understanding of AI fundamentals and would highly recommend this class. He is an excellent educator.

Professor Bari is an excellent computer science professor. His lectures are clear, engaging, and make challenging concepts easy to understand. He is approachable, supportive, and genuinely invested in his students' success. I learned a lot from his course and would highly recommend him.
Prof. Bari is the Tupac of computer science. He iconic & unforgettable. You will actually learn how to handle CS interviews in his class. TAKE HIM!!

Prof. Bari has been one of my favorite professors during my time at NYU for 101 and now 102. I gained so much from everything she had to offer, and I truly enjoyed her class. I was always excited to come to class every Tuesday and Thursday. He consistently made lectures fun and interactive, which made learning engaging and enjoyable.

It was one of the best experiences I've had since coming to NYU. I learned so much and felt challenged in the best way. Prof. Bari genuinely cares about his students' success, and that support motivated me to work even harder and do my best. It's truly special to take a class with a professor who is so invested in their students. He is the best!

Prof. Bari, the best CS professor I've had so far, truly cares for you! Enriches the learning process, and you really learn the material to prepare for exams. Pop quizzes, 1 midterm & final, and some HW assignments, MUST be prepared on the side. Grades will curve to your favor. TAKE HIM for CS102, and if you're interested in his AI/Analytics work!

The professor is a very nice person and gives everyone high grades at the end of the semester. Nevertheless, I don't want to take his class again. The surprise quizzes every week and the random roll calls in class completely wore me out.
Run! Read books and powerpoints by yourself. Choose students to present their code without teaching anything. Pop up quiz every week even he did not teach anything. The worst prof!

I took an AI summer research class with Prof. Bari and honestly, he's on another level. He's super dedicated, makes sure no one gets lost, and somehow explains complex stuff like it's storytime. He's always there to help, no matter what. I swear, if every prof was like him, our world would be a paradise. Prof. Anasse Bari is the GOAT!

Prof. Bari is extremely responsible and dedicated. He is always to ensure that students understand the materials. His clear communication and willingness to help others had a significant positive impact on my learning experience. I love Prof. Bari, he is the best!!

Professor Bari is super supportive! His grad summer class on predictive analytics and generative AI was one of the clearest and most valuable learning experiences I've had at NYU. He shares practical resources, gives detailed feedback, and is patient with questions. Even across time zones, he makes accommodations. His assistant Harrison helps too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He seems really intimidating in the beginning and gives pop quizzes, but he's really chill with grading and does make sure that everyone does well. Does random attendance and gives extra credit for those who show up.

What sets Professor Bari apart is not only his deep expertise, but also his passion for applying AI to solve real-world current problems. I highly recommend taking this seminar to any student serious about pursuing AI or data science. It's a rare opportunity to learn from a world-class professor and leader in the field.
Bari made learning AI truly inspiring. I recommend taking the graduate AI seminar course with Bari.

I had the incredible opportunity to learn a lot from Professor Bari, and it was one of the most enriching academic experiences I've had at NYU. Professor Bari has a rare ability to make complex concepts both accessible and engaging and entertaining. His his teaching style strikes the perfect balance between theory and realworld applications.
Professor Bari is funny.
He is the goat
Very passionate, and great at making topics feel relevant for professional preparation. A phenomenal teacher.

I believe Professor Bari is one of the main reasons that I started enjoying computer programming. He is very helpful and caring with the students who actually want to learn. I never hesitated to go up to him when I had questions, and he has always been willing to help.

This class is amazing. I didn't study, didn't understand most things, and the final was super hard I couldn't do anything but still got an A 😂 Some people scored way higher but were quiet, so they got B. I just said a few easy things in class and smiled. So yeah, talking works better than studying here lol

His quiz/exams are easy but a little bit heavy as number of problems is bit overwhelming. Nevertheless, he clearly knows the reasons for taking this course, to prepare for your future interviews. Interview questions are much harder and stressing, so his exams are giving you confidence in your future career path, but not merely getting A on grade
Professor Bari is awesome! Very coherent at explaining concepts and can guide students in a very organized manner. Definitely recommend.

As far as professors at NYU go, despite all of their research and outside work commitments, he is one of the few who still goes out of his way to help students struggling with content/material. You cannot find a more dedicated teacher than him. Even though some people will complain about the weekly/daily pop quizzes, they are meant TO HELP YOU.

The professor is intense, but fair. Exams are challenging, but extra credit opportunities help. Attending class and using Unstuckstudy for practice can really pay off. Overall, a rewarding experience if you're willing to put in the work.
He is so nice and interesting. He is the best professor I met at NYU.
The best prof!! very reasonable. Gives extra credit.

Professor Bari may seem a bit strict and intimidating at first, but when you get your midterm and final grades you will know you picked the right professor. My friends and I all think we got more than we deserved. He just wants to see evidence of efforts/progress: like steadily improving HW/quizzes or active participation in class/office hours.

Great lectures. Midterm was had mostly exercises we did in class, assignments &on the quizzes. I did well in so far with A-. But, there are a lot of bad students taking CS classes who are not working hard and they are thinking they will get good grades by doing nothing. I am sure many will fail his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took him over the summer. He spent half of the time teaching and the rest we would complete programming questions. I did good on homework's and quizzes but failed one of his exams. Still, I was able to receive an A. He doesn't want to see anyone fail and boosts your grade as long as you go to office hour and show him your trying to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Smart Professor. Exams and quiz were very hard. But he tries to make up for with it extra credit. Go to tutoring, their the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Such a fair, genuine professor. He gave tons of extra credit and was open to extending deadlines when it seemed like the class as a whole needed it. His exams were pretty straightforward, similar to what we covered in class. The material wasn't exactly easy but he clearly wants you to do well. Go to lectures and office hours, and visit the tutors!

I really enjoyed this class, this is the 2nd time I have taken Bari for a cs class and he always comes through. Although his explanations can be a bit long-winded I believe he provides contextualization for how the information taught can be utilized in programming. I don't believe this class prepared students for cso, that is a problem for later.

Sit in the front of the class and try to participate and learn DS. He gives out very fair quizzes/exams. He can come along a bit loud but I think that's apart of his charm lol. He can be a bit hard to get in touch with cause he's busy, but overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Totally undoable exams. Ask to write down all 6 sorting method codes and stack trace and so on in 75 minutes. Final is stochastic graded.

Bari was the best professor I've ever taken! He cares so much about his student's success. Show up to class. Be engaged and participate. He will cold call on people who don't. Ask questions and talk to him at his office hours. Go to the tutors for the projects, they are so helpful. His class is so well structured too. I cannot recommend him enough.
The class is very manageable. The quizzes seems to be preparation for the exam. Good lectures. HW1 was extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 11/10. Gave take-home exams to offset any bad exam scores. 6 hw's, 2 midterms, 1 final, 2 quizzes. A lot of it was take-home so we could fix our grades, and exams were very similar to practice questions we did. No pop quiz. Got extra credit for doing textbook chapter summary and showing up to class when attendance was low. Accommodates deadlines.

Contents of the quizzes and exams required more time to be able to finish all number of questions being asked especially some detailed requirements in questions are specifically different from the previous works we had completed and designed with own design of number of inputs, different arguments or other details.

CS102 was a very hard class. We did practice questions in class. It was a good structure because we learn it one day, and apply it the next. I found that to be very effective and it helped understand the content better. There were so many quizzes, they were fair.
Bari is the best professor to exist! He is passionate, understanding, and engaging in teaching the material. CS101 was so much fun

He's spontaneous when giving extra credit or changing assignments. Class is time consuming and unpredictable. I don't do well with the in person exam format, so I rely on hw and extra credit. Exams can turn from in person to take home because he randomly decides to. Dismissive in OH, felt like he just wanted me to leave. Tutors are great though.

CS102 was a challenging class. The content Prof. Bari covered was hard but he did explain everything and provided applications of what the topic to job interviews, data science and algorithms. The homeworks were very time consuming. It was a good class overall in terms of both learning and grading.
I'll definitely take him again and I didn't think his exams were difficult at all. However, I do sometimes have a problem with how he talks to people, I don't think it's very professional.

I took cs101 from another professor and took data structures from prof Bari. If you took cs from another professor, you will know how durable prof Bari's class is. I think people who complain about his class never have taken other prof's classes. If you need to put the effort into prof Bari's class, you can get an A.

Bari is very caring and flexible with deadlines. You still do a lot of work but with joy and lots of fun. Easy A if you put in the work and attend the lectures. His army of TAs know almost everyone by name and they are aware of what everyone is doing in and out of class.

The best professor in CS102. I love the graph theory lectures and real life applications. 
102 have been very fun. Few homeworks, four quizzes and two exams.

Understanding, very flexible, tries to help students as much as possible. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, if he sees that you're trying to learn and improve, it will mean so much to him and it will improve your grade. He is honestly incredible and a very good professor and human being.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gives bonus points to exams. However, exams and homework are much harder than what he teaches in class. Rather than teaching useful things, he wastes a lot of time forcing unnecessary participations in a big class, and he only is patient to students he knows well. His class is okay,  but I definitely will take another prof's CS102.

Great class and flexible deadline.
I love Professor Bari

I feel that I am learning so much from this class. There is a lot of work and so many homeworks assigned in a short time. Prof. Bari is pushing everyone in class to work. Be aware he will call on you randomly to answer questions or solve programming problems (he is doing that in a large class of  200 students). Overall it is a good class.
He is fantastic! As long as you participate and show hardworking, it is an easy A

CS102 is online this semester and it is harder than the in-person version from what I heard, however, Prof. Bari is using his tablet as a board in every lecture to go over the algorithms. I like the class, he also gives a lot of bonus points and he curved the midterm grades. The recitations are very helpful, Chris and Siyi are amazing.

Overall it is a good class, the homewroks and exams are manageable. Professor Bari is very helpful, holds long office hours, and is very enthusiastic about computer science. He helped me get an internship and I am thankful to him for all the efforts he put in to teach and help the students.

The midterm exam was very fair and easy. He gave us similar questions to the second quiz. 
Clearly he wants us to learn and do well in the exam.

Great class and great lectures. 
Professor Bari is the best professor I has ever had at NYU. He cares that everyone in class succeeds. He trying his best to get to remember the names of every students in 150+ class. He does quizzes before each exams to get us ready. He is an amazing professor. I love Bari!

I especially dislike it when he calls some students names during lectures. I get it, he wants to encourage students to participate, but it makes me feel it might be very unfair when he ends up only calling several students names (the ppl he knew). I feel extremely discouraged. Quizzes and exams are too hard for an intro level CS class.
the quizzes and exams were just way too difficult, and he didn't give any similar practice problems before those quizzes. I don't see the point of torturing students like that.

He's fair, but I don't think he's this good. Bari's lectures and assignments are way too simple, but his quizzes and exams are not.  I dislike how he attempts to promote himself during lectures; he's more like a businessman rather than a scholar. U need to spend much more time than u expect to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is intelligent and knows a lot about CS. However, I think his class can be improved if he could gauge his students' levels of understanding of the material and give exams that adequately reflect what is taught. Class can be more engaging than simply recycling slides and explanations can be provided without condescension. Don't take him.

I am learning a lot in 102.  Unfortunately, there are a lot of students with very weak background in our class that I think they are failing the midterm, they should not be in CS the first place, they are slowing the prof and everyone in class. He is doing his best to answer everyone and he explains the same concepts repeatedly.

Absolutely a prejudiced professor. If you have taken his cs101, he will like you more than those who didn't. When you keep raising your hand in class, He simply ignores you if he does not really know you, while always calling those preferred students first. This really kills my enthusiasm for participating in his class.

Great data structures class! His quizzes were a good practice for the exam which was challenging but fair. He repeated most of the questions from 
the homeworks.
Extreme har quiz and midterms, Extreme short Time to finish! DO NOT TAKE!
unclear instructions and does not give enough time to complete in-class assessments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He thinks of no one more highly than himself. Be prepared for a lot of useless busywork, and for him to talk about his newest consulting projects and how incredibly life-changing and impactful his work has been. While he holds marathon office hours to try to help as many students as possible, he is often irritable and tired.

Compared to what I've heard, I think he's just overrated. He expects to do a lot of research on our own for most of the hw questions and a lot of hw questions are ambiguous. However, he does give out a lot of extra credit assignments, which is a plus. Still he doesn't cover important functions in class and expects us to memorize them for the exam.

I've heard many great things about Bari so I was excited to be in his class. But, reality hit me very quick and I realized that it was a complete mistake. Professor Bari's quizzes are extremely long and difficult to complete in the given time. This class makes me miserable - so many things due in short time with short notice, pls avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly don't really get the hype; quizzes are difficult and take a lot more time than what is initially given in class. It would be better if he was mindful that people have other commitments. I understand that Data Structures is a tough course, but workload could be a little bit more spaced out or lighter compared to the other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Great class, he creates a comfortable and fun environment for
students to learn.

Great at making sure we understand the material. Professor Bari is willing to repeat and explain in
detail until we understood. I really appreciate this because some of the topics we learn are very
challenging, and I understood them better after multiple rounds of explanation. Quizzes were unannounced!!

Professor Bari is a great professor! I learned so much from him!! He teaches concepts in a way so approachable to students! If you participate, you will guarantee succeed in the class. I hope I can take class again with him sometime :)
I learned so much in CS102, the midterm was hard, he also covered graph theory and related algorithms based on DFS. great class overall, I love Bari! He is the man!!!!!!

Professor Bari was by far one of the best professors I have ever had at NYU. Very organized lectures with so much in-class practice. Exams were fair and his assistant Chris is amazing and very helpful. I highly recommend taking the class with him.
average at most
If you want to seriously learn and be inspired, no. If you want an easy transition into CS, yes.

His lectures are so great! Overall, homeworks and exams are not hard. One drawback is that he did not cover all of the data structures, and some data structures are very important in future classes. It is an easy A class, but you should catch up by yourself if you want to prepare for interviews or taking Algorithm/CSO classes.
He explained all concepts very well! A little disorganized in terms of time planning, but he really wants you to understand everything. He's a great professor!
Such a good Professor! I hope everyone had a chance to take his course!

Some professors get a bad wrap because they teach challenging subjects, although computer science gets tricky at times. Professor Bari always breaks concepts down, so they are comprehensible. His exams are composed of material of the same difficulty level as discussed in class. If you put in the effort, you will succeed in any of his courses.

Professor Bari is an intelligent professor, looking to allow his students to succeed and foster their growth. He taught the information well, was super flexible about deadlines and took into account our other commitments. He provided us with all of the notes and code, which made it easier to follow along during class.

Bari is a great guy but all these 5s are a bit misleading. He isn't always so put together and he does not finish all data structures that need to be taught. You will need to teach yourself a bunch for coding interviews. The TA I had was very helpful and the tests are very fair. (he gives you alot of hints for what he will ask on). Few HWs
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has great lectures and slides. The materials that he provided are the best since I've ever taken CS courses. He may have pop quizzes, but he will notify the students in the previous class, so at least watch every recording, if you cannot go to every class on time.

A bit off putting and cold at first but once you get used to his style he is great! Clear grading criteria, topic schedule, and syllabus. HW and quizzes every week and they're pretty long too (3-5 hours) but he gives lots of extra credit/bonus points. take-home Midterm and final are fair (time-consuming, bot not difficult). Must read textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Definitely the best professor Ive ever met. The kindest professor in CS department when you should get 95 for A. I would still like to take his class if I can.
The best professor at NYU!
Prof Bari truly cares for his students and helps us a lot. He is very generous with grading and DDLs and wants everyone to do well in his class. Take him for any cs classes I would say!
Incredibly supportive of students, really believed in our success in and outside the classroom. I love Bari!!!

Professor Bari did all he could for the students given this remote environment. He has a unique ability to answer all student queries in such a way to peak interest. He also makes a point to prepare students for the real world via interview situations and his personal anecdotes.

Hands down, Prof Bari is one of the best professors I've had at NYU. He explains all concepts so clearly and would like to go through them again if anyone has any questions. He cares about his students and would like everyone to receive a good grade while actively learning. HW isn't hard as long as you pay attention in class. Take 102 with Bari!!
Prof. Bari was extremely accommodating of the circumstances this semester; and graded very fairly. He was always available to us if we needed help; I'm glad to have taken this course under him.
Prof. Bari is one of the best teachers I have had so far at NYU. I am learning so much Java programming this semester. Take him. If you do the work and on time, you will do well.

Bari always claims himself to be very generous but actually his workload is high. He doesn't organize the class very well. The content after midterm is much more difficult than before but he goes over it quickly. He just reads the powerpoint. It may be easy for students who have learned about Java before but not friendly to green hands.

Great professor! He really cares about his students and wants everyone can learn something from the class. He may gives extension on several the HW if there are some festivals. His class really evoke my interest on the CS!

A gem of NYU, funny, and caring. He has done so much exceptional work outside of the field and just being able to sit in his classroom is an honour. TBH, if this class seems unbearable, do not do CS. Workload IS manageable w/ balance + Prof. Bari will make every attempt to inspire and help you succeed. If(canTake ! take) you are inting.

Demanding class with a great Professor. He tries anything he can to eliminate our stress for grades and motivate us to learn. Reuses questions from homework for tests just to make sure we understand the important concepts. The workload is actually reasonable.

Professor Bari is the most caring professor I have ever had! His lecture is very clear and he can explain difficult concepts very well. In class he always solve examples by hand step by step so it is much more easier to understand. The quizzes are straight from ppt and class examples. He gives A LOT OF TIME for the midterm too. Strongly recommend!
It will be wise to take his class. Most of the quizzes and exams are take home. The homework seems much, but really helps you practice. It won't be hard to get a decent score if you do learn.

There were several homeworks and a semester project.

This is the first semester he is teaching at NYU. I took Predictive Analytics under him. He is a very nice professor, and has many office hrs. Since it was his first time teaching at NYU, the class was unstructured, and we didn't really learn many topics in the class. Involves a lot of work.

Anyone able to take a class with Prof Berthe before graduating is very lucky. Highly recommend. Learned so many useful vocabulary terms in Business French and classes were very engaging. He encourages participation during class and discussion topics were always very interesting. He is very understanding and has an amazing sense of humor too.

If you show Professor Olivier that you want to be there and put forth effort you will get the grade that you want. He gets a very good gauge on your improvements through the class. be prepared to speak in class but he makes the environment very welcoming. one of the best professors ive had so far
He is absolutely the GOAT in the whole french department. Very kind, vert nice, easy to get the grade you want.

Genuinely the best teacher I've had in my life and probably the best anyone can experience in the language department. He cares for student mental health and is very reasonable in grading and is a great teacher overall.
I love him he's so funny and makes learning so much easier esp a language that gets tedious. He's actually the best I've ever had i will probs always take french so i can stay in his life LMAO

i love him. seriously, take him. hilarious, kind, feels more like a friend than a professor. interesting class dynamic - fun homework assignments (songs, movies). we take tests but expresses to us heavily that they don't define us/our grade. i will miss him sm.
The best french class I've taken in my life

The way class was laid out helped me learn everything I needed to know. He is very accommodating of student's needs, and makes class engaging and lively. I highly recommend taking any of his classes if you can. He is definitely an excellent teacher who's classes are fairly difficult. 

P.S.: It was the one class I never wanted to skip!

One of the best French teachers at NYU. He is very lax about attendance and understanding if you need to miss class. Participation is really important in his class, and as long as he thinks you're trying, you will get a good grade.

You do a lot of work (many many hours) but he is a lenient grader. I thought I was just kind of average but i was pleasantly surprised to get an A in the class. I think he grades mostly based off effort
Professor Berthe is one of the best prof in NYU. NYU french department is great but Prof.Berth is absolutely one of the most kind and supporting person you will ever meet in NYU. Love him.

Olivier is just the best prof I have ever met. Incredibly caring, encouraging, amusing, and accessible. Share so much of his life that you will regard him as a dear friend. Lots of homework, but for those who love movies and songs it's not a problem. Gives extra credit now and then, so never worry about your grade if you work. 100% take his class!
Amazing professor. Take him if you are truly passionate about learning.

Olivier is the best French Professor I've had in the French department. I took Topics: Paris and it was just a fascinating course. He does give a lot of homework, but was extremely accommodating. After struggling in a quiz, he messaged me personally to reassure me that my grade would be ok, just a true gem and really cares for his students!
Most amazing prof at NYU. Just take the class bro

Olivier is a once-in-a-lifetime professor. I took both contemporary conversation & advanced conversation just to stay in his class. Forward-thinking, flexible, and very sweet. He's the type of prof that wants to see you learn & grow, genuinely. Yes, he assigns tons of homework. But you'll have no trouble passing.

Olivier is the best French professor I've had to date and is definitely one of the best professors in general at NYU. He is caring, thoughtful, and incredibly helpful - his teaching style is quite holistic and he really cares about his students. I definitely improved after his class and I feel much more confident in my French. 10/10 Take his class!

Olivier is a 100000/10 professor. My French greatly improved after taking his class. He is motivational, and pushes you to do your best. He also recognizes and heavily prioritizes progress. Workload is not too heavy, and he is very accessible outside of class. I wish he taught every french course at NYU.

Best professor! He puts you on to French songs/culture, puts everyone out of their comfort zones in participation for better french speaking (a great thing that you'll get used to)! Gives fun extra credit options and corrections on essays for a better grade. Cares about our mental health; checks in on us! Take him to be a confident French speaker!

Professor Berthe is definitely the best professor I have ever had. Take his class if you have a chance!!! He knows what to teach and how to teach. He is also innovative in teaching, making learning a language so engaging. I really had a lot of fun in lectures. Even when doing homework, I feel enjoyable!!! Best Olivier!!!
Amazing prof
Great teacher

Olivier is such a wonderful professor and person! He makes class very interesting and he truly cares for each and every one of his students. The classes are sometimes difficult to participate in if you don't prepare by the doing the hw beforehand. He does assign 2+ hours of hw for each class, but he's also an easy grader as long as you try.

Professor Olivier is my first French teacher. He's respected and a wonderful person. He's more than a professor, but also an advisor for life in general haha! Initially, the class was challenging for me, but he's there to help! The class is every day, but I'm always excited to go to his class and learn. He makes me love French.

Olivier is one of the best teachers I've ever had! He is just an amazing person, genuinely cares about his students, and made me excited to come to class everyday. There's a lot of homework and attendance is mandatory but even if ur struggling, he's always open to meet & participating, showing effort, and having a good attitude go a long way

I took the 6 credit class so it was every day and he was the BEST. I did not like taking language before him but he is just such a gem that it quickly became my favorite class. Its a challenging class but because he makes you care it is very doable and everyone is inspired to do their best. A beautiful soul, I could not recommend this class more.

Olivier Berthe is one of the best professors at NYU. He made me love French even more and made me really want to work to know the material. I loved the way he taught and the cultural artifacts he showed us.

Beyond being an amazing professor he's just an altogether incredible person. I would recommend his class even if you have no interest in learning French. I was excited to go to class everyday, and satisfied with myself when I left. I have made so much progress in my French thanks to him, but this class has also just changed my love for learning.

Getting to learn from him has been the best thing that has happened to me at NYU. Beyond caring, like a father, and just so badly wants you to love learning French. He grades based on effort so doing poorly on a test is not a big deal, but I still felt so bad when I did just because he cared so much, I didn't want to disappoint him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hands down best French professor I've had at NYU. Engaging, thought-provoking lessons. The workload can be a little intimidating at first, but it will push your French ability to places you didn't even know it could go.

Unbelievable professor and an inspirational man. Olivier is the kind of teacher who can revolutionize the traditional meaning of a professor, because he genuinely cares more about your effort in his class than any grades. I unconditionally recommend Olivier for any student that has a true interest in French. Do be prepared for an immense workload.

Hands down the best French professor I've ever had in my life. I can't describe how much I've enjoyed and loved his class and I know that I'll miss it so much next semester. Take him!!!! Don't hesitate!!
Olivier is a real gem. He cares a lot about his étudiants! Lots of work- homework everyday. 10/10 would do it again
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olivier was the best professor I have ever had. He cares so much about his students and really wants everyone to try their best and learn as much as they can. As long as you do the work and participate, you will do really well in his class. He is the first french professor I have that really encouraged me to learn and love the language.

What a great professor. He truly cares about each student and his class isn't hard if you do the work. I really want to learn French, so I approached this class with that goal. Some people just needed to fulfill a credit so it was harder for them. He is caring, compassionate, and the grades are fair (he grades your level of effort, too!).

If you ever have a chance to take one of Olivier's classes, whatever it may be, TAKE IT. He is one of those respected professors who you will want to know for the rest of your life. Although seemingly strict, he simply wants to improve your fluency and he REALLY knows how to teach and gain respect quickly. His lessons are unique and interesting.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. He assigns a ton of work, but it's manageable and I'd take his class again. He made French really interesting for me and genuinely cared about my success. Really great and cool guy all-around.
amazing professor and human being. the kind of professor that you remember for the rest of your life.

Oliver is a shining example of what every professor should be. Not only is he a master of his field, he checks up on students individually, fostering relationships nd helping us create individual plans of study. My entire class loved him. There is a lot of work iLrn assignments, etc, and you are going need to participate but he is a fair grader! :)

Don't take this class if you don't care about French-- don't waste his time or yours. Olivier does everything in his ability to set you up to learn the absolute most you can and receive the best grade possible. If you don't it is on you. Best French teacher I've ever had. Absolutely the most caring professor I've ever had. Ever.

by far the best french professor I have ever had since learning french. Olivier is not only an incredible professor who truly cares about helping you improve your french, but his actual day-to-day course setup is so engaging, entertaining, and truly an amazing experience. Your french will improve A LOT in this class. The class IS intense though!

About to enter my last semester and Olivier has been the most caring and helpful professor I've had. He really is "there for you" and helped me when he saw I was having bad anxiety. He wasn't invasive, condescending, or dismissive. Also, he is animated and lively! Take any class with him! Sidenote is you DO have to do the hw and discuss it daily.

Outstanding professor, seriously. Workload fluctuates but is always manageable and he's very understanding if there are any issues. Will go out of his way on his own time to help you if you ask. Also very funny and livelylectures are always fun with him. I HIGHLY recommend taking a course with himhe's a great professor! You'll learn a lot.

Best french professor hands down. Guaranteed to improve your french very much if you try. He is kind and understanding but he makes you work and likes to watch you improve. Do not miss taking a class with him, even if you're lazy, you will be a better french speaker for it.

Best french profteacherperson I've ever had or met. Super understanding. Lots of homework but it's all pretty easy and short and you will definitely notice an improvement in your french. Plus he's hilarious and makes class very enjoyable.

Best French teacher I have ever had. I learned more about the French language and culture in his class than I did in an entire semester living in Paris. The workload is intense, and at times seems unbearable, but he is there to help you and if you do the work you will see an amazing improvement in your French. If you work hard you will get an A!

Very, very demanding. Intimidating at first, but as the semester goes on you can see how charming, sharp and sympathetic Olivier really is. The workload is immense but in return he is not a harsh grader. But you gotta show the  effort - he is very observant and will know when you're slacking. And this is why I adore him so much. Thank you, Olivier.

I wish I could take Olivier each semester for the rest of my life.  He is easily the most incredible and influential prof/teacher I've ever had.  His philosophy on learning and grading is amazing and he pushes you so hard without you feeling stressed. Learned so much, laughed so much, and gained a lot more confidence when speaking French. TAKE HIM

Best French prof I've ever had. Classes were fun and hilarious but still challenging, so my French improved a lot. Work may seem overwhelming at times but he is very understanding, accommodating, and helpful.
Great professor. Cares more about progress and learning than grades. Really engages you and makes time fly. Very personable, loved him.

Olivier makes class truly engaging and your French improves immensely. He makes you forget you're doing school work and gets you interested in the subjects you talk about. He's approachable, lenient about deadlines, and has a great sense of humor. The work can be time-consuming but it's useful, straight-forward and pays off.

best french teacher ever. so caring, concise, helpful, and has realistic expectations. he wants you to learn and will make sure you do. lots of work, but it's worth it. learned so much about french culture. good use of class time, organized structure, can't say enough good things. so glad i took this class, he's gorgeous too!

Hands down, without a doubt the best professor (French or otherwise) I've ever had.  Incredibly helpful, passionate, and fun.  He really wants you to learn and you really will.  It's a lot of work but it's entirely worth it and you'll walk away a significantly better French speaker.  Absolute highest recommendations.

Olivier is the best French professor at NYU, and that's saying something. He is charming, approachable, intelligent, and beautiful. He genuinely cares about all of his students, in class and out. The work load is very heavy, but get through it and actually do the homework; it all pays off tenfold in the end.

Olivier was the best French teacher I've ever had (and I've taken 7 years). He has a great teaching technique, makes class quite entertaining, and you learn a lot without even realizing. Take Olivier's class if you can, you won't regret it.

Great professor!  You may feel overwhelmed by the workload at times, but your French will improve tremendously.  If you ever feel lost with Olivier, just talk to him.  He's reassuring and wants you to improve your French above all else!

I took Conversation and Composition and Spoken Contemporary with Olivier. He is one of the best professors I have had during my four years at NYU. Insightful, helpful, and speaks both French and English beautifully. I wish I had time to take more of his classes...
best french class ever!
HOT

Olivier is one of the most involved, comprehensive, devoted French teachers at NYU.  I took his Translation class; it was a lot of work but I definitely learned more about French grammar, culture and language than any other French class at NYU.  Olivier creates a great working environment by being impassioned by his class, and his students.

Olivier is fantastique! I took my 2nd class with him this year because he's so great (last year took Translation - his specialty). He's really funny and sarcastic but ultimately wants you to learn and have a good time. He cares about each student and the subject and is really flexible - he finds ways to help you succeed. Take ANY of his classes!
Best French teacher I've ever had. He teaches both academic and contemporary French to vastly improve your knowledge of the language and your ability to converse fluently.
He is the best teacher that I've had at NYU. He really knows his stuff, plus he's nice and helpful and encourages you to learn, above all. Worth taking his class.

He is my absolute favorite professor. He cares about each of his students, despite the wall of sarcasm he puts up. Take the class just for his commentary. Spoken Contemporary French s basically a cinema studies course taught in French, but it's worth it when he asks you to learn swear words. Mon prof prefere.

Absolutely the best French teacher at NYU.  Even if you have to get up at 8am 5 days a week, it's worth it.  He's funny, willing to help anytime, will meet you outside of class and very understanding.  I wish all my profs were like him!

Awesome, awesome teacher. Extremely hilarious, funniest teacher I've ever had. Yet he still teaches a lot and really cares about the subject. He's a pretty easy grader, but there's a bit of work for the class. However, if you are going to take french, try to get Olivier...one of the best teachers I have had.
Hands down the best professor I've had in a while. A lot of work but this guy is extremely nice and so funny. You actually WANT to go to classes.
Olivier doesn't care about NYU. He just wants desperately for you to learn some damned French. Funniest, most personable teacher I've ever had, and he taught me more French than any other teacher.
Olivier is the bomb, he's really helpful and cool. I wish i could havehim every semester

I love this guy! He's super friendly and helpful, and wants everyone to understand and enjoy French. He helped us learn it with movies, songs, idioms, book-work, and just chatting about being Parisian. I wish i could take his class every semester becuase i have learned SOO much! J'aime beacoup Olivier! Prennez son classe!
Olivier is hilarious.  Once you get past his sarcastic remarks, he's great.  Plus you'll learn more French than in any other class!

Absolutely funniest teacher I've had.  Well worth taking one semester with him.  And he knows his stuff and is willing to help too!  And he likes teaching in various ways to keep things interesting.  Highly recommended.

Gift A - especially if you've done chemistry in high school. Professor is old and grumpy and inaccessible but honestly you wouldn't need help in this class at all. Labs are only tricky part of the class with mandatory attendance and he has connect homeworks which take up to 3 hours and keep repeating till you get the question correct.

If you took chem/physics back in high school, class should be a breeze. Personally did not go to a class after like the 5th one and am still doing well. Lectures boring, with quizzes. Labs are the hardest part, get to know the TA's and know how to ask for help. Outside of class, prof is super rude/unreachable, though he might just be old/grumpy.

The homework, quizzes, and tests are online and easy as long as you read the textbook, and the TA's and labs are chill and fun, but lectures have almost nothing to do with the material. He is near impossible to reach outside of class, and he goes on massive tangents about how useless our generation is and how we are at fault for society's decline.

Rude and mean, never responses to emails. TA and labs are chill but don't expect to learn anything from the lecture. The slides are probably older than you, and he speaks with a very low voice making it incredibly hard to hear.

He's really rude and mean to all students. On the first day of chem recitation he said that none of us would ever become doctors, and every class he doesn't fail to brag about his own MD and PhD. Yes, that's super impressive, but he doesn't have to put his students down at the same time. Difficulty doesn't apply because he's giving Halpin's quizzes
I love this course! The test is similar to our homework. If you do your homework carefully, you will get good grades.

Professor Goldberg's ENERGYENV class is a chill, straightforward option for a core requirement. Lectures can be disorganized, but exams are easy if you do the HW, slides, and quizzes. I found unstuck study super helpful for test prep too.

This class is good if you need an easy A as all homeworks and exams are done digitally (and everyone cheats their way through them), but he was the most unfocused and uninteresting professor I've ever had. Seems like a nice guy but lecture was totally unengaging and the readings were incredibly long and unnecessary. Not helpful outside or in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As people have said, lectures often went off topic. Also, grading criteria was a bit unclear. I just learned the material myself by reading the textbook - if you do that, and study the hw and lecture quiz questions, you're truly good to go for the exams. Not everyone cheated!

On the contrary to the recent reviews, no not everybody cheated. That accusation just shows students like to lash out when things don't go their way, but in all fairness the lectures tended to go off topic always. Lectures were not useful but tests were really just questions from our homework and quizzes, so if you do those you are solid for an A.

I fear that for this class, cheating is not just possible but necessary. Everyone cheated. And I mean EVERYONE. Unproctored exams. The tests would be stupid hard otherwise. The lectures, oh my god, he is not a good teacher. He would make a solid drinking buddy to discuss his war stories, but I would discourage taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Goldberg is a gem!! A lot of these reviews are complaining but he is genuinely very kind and understanding. The class is very easy and he understands that no one in a core class is taking it to become a scientist. Attend class and his special lectures!

Burt is crotchety and not very good at teaching. The textbook, TA's, and ChatGPT will be your teachers. Three exams are online and unproctored so everyone just cheats anyway. Everything else besides labs is graded for completion. Very easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is very easy - 40% of the grade is obtained by attending class and doing quizzes/lab/homework that are extremely easy for anyone who doesn't have a previous understanding of chemistry (which is basically what the class is about). The remaining 60% is spread across 3 in-class laptop quizzes which are 20% each and MCQ only (insanely easy)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love Dr Goldberg. He cares about his students and the wisdom and experience he has is unmatched.

The McGraw home work he gave was killlerrr, not gonna lie. But most of his tests were based on the homework and the quizzes we did in class. Every lecture there was a quiz for attendance but honestly you just need the code. He's sweet when he wants to be, but hes a little older so naturally he moves a little slower.

Goldberg's physical science core is incredibly easy if you do the bare minimum of studying for the exams. Also his lectures are just him yapping ab random stuff so there is literally no reason to go. Take it with your friends or meet ppl and switch up who goes to class each day and have them share the code with everyone else for attendance credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a chill guy, albeit a little odd, but chill nonetheless. Goes on tangents A LOT, but his tests are easy if you study the HWs, slides, and especially the lecture quizzes. Wouldn't take him again because of the disorganization, but being there for his lecture about whether or not vampires and werewolves exist was definitely a highlight.
Had him for CHEM125 recitation. Always off topic talking about his personal life, but I preferred the distraction over a second chemistry lecture; he is quite funny.

Not difficult, lecture quizzes are not graded (they do have passwords, so make some friends to divide who goes to class each week). Labs are fun, lectures are completely useless (he is never on topic). Tests are simple, homework takes a while but is not graded on accuracy. Lab quiz questions come straight from lab book.

Professor Goldberg is not a great lecturer but this is a core class for non-majors so the class itself is fairly straightforward. The exams are mostly just homework and quiz questions verbatim so studying is pretty clean. You can definitely get an A w/o too much brainpower but the HW takes forever. Also kind of a weird guy (not a compliment).
Interesting & easy class to take for core. Everything is graded for completion except for lab and exams. Labs are fun too. Advice: do lecture quizzes.

BG is an amazing guy very funny. However, he is very unaccommodating he will not answer your emails after the first month of school and is quite unorganized. This class has changed a lot since the prior year adding a lot more chemistry and a lot less learning about the environment but the labs are very fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The modern-day learning environment is in desperate need of more people like Burt. He's a straight shooter who'll tell you what you need to hear, not what you want to hear. He teaches clearly, and effectively. To add to that, he has an entire treasure trove of hilarious, and completely irrelevant stories to share with the class.

Rude and always makes an effort to make it known that he is better than you, smarter than you, has done significant research, and has written college curriculum. He discourages students from continuing the course. He will tell you (repeatedly) that you will never be successful or become a doctor, and he will pick on you in front of the whole class.
Lectures are very dry and he occasionally talks more about his life rather than the subject, but exams are incredibly easy and straightforward.
Lecture is boring but the three midterms are easy, questions are the same as the questions in lecture quiz. HW only count for completions. Lab is not bad.
Easy class even tough I did not know anything about chem. HW and quizzes based on readings and graded just for complete them. Extra point of you submit everything on time. Quizzes are extremely easy.

Good professor. I did knot anything about chem, but the online book he uses is really helpful. Hw and quizzes are based on the readings which is super easy if you read them. Extra points if you submit everything on time. Really easy quizzes.

I took this class for my core requirements. I did not know anything about chem, but the online book he used was very helpful to understand the class. I just needed to read 1 chapter per week and the hw was based on the readings. The quizzes were also based on the readings. He gave the class 10 extra points if you submitted hw on time.
His lecture is very disoriented, but exams are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Burt is a great guy. He is so interesting and if you take the time to listen to him you will be pleasantly surprised on how awesome of a person he is. He is an extremely smart man and has so much to teach you if you are willing to listen. He sometimes goes off track but that is what makes his class bearable because he does not just spill content.

This man will tell you so much about his personal life and so little about chemistry. However, the class was extremely generous with grading (In person but still during covid times) and the exams were essentially homework questions. The McGrawhill Connect taught me most of the material and was very easy to understand

this man never shuts up about his stupid personal life and does not take any time to explain concepts and dodges questions about the actual material. the quizzes are easy but he did literally nothing to help me pass them he just yaps on about how you won't get into med school

Be prepared to learn the content yourself but Burt is a great guy. Attendance is graded by pop quizzes but they are online so you can do them from home. Lecture pretty much always ends in him telling stories about his life and now about chemistry. Can be a little hard to talk to but overall loved him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had to teach myself absolutely everything in the course but at least Goldberg wasnt a bad guy (so not the worst case scenario). Very sassy and cute. He gave up by the end of the semester and talked about his cat for 20 mins at the start of lecture.

I'm surprised to see that Burt is getting such a hard time on here. During this semester, he was caring and extremely fair (he went out of his way to stop the lab professor from switching to this new ridiculous format online). Sometimes he does go a little fast during lecture, but he always will stop if you have a question and will answer clearly.

By far the worst professor I've had. His whole class is so unorganized, and his syllabus gives me a headache. He's also extremely rude, passive-aggressive, and sassy for no reason to his students. Like hello? We're all just trying to learn here, just cut the attitude. His classes have absolutely no form.

Incredibly rude and condescending, had him for two sessions of Gen Chem II recitation until I switched out. Very confusing too, he explained a concept completely incorrectly despite the entire class arguing with him (I googled it and the class was correct). Avoid at all costs.
his way or the highway

Dr. Goldberg is a fun and fair professor although he can come across as rude. The exam and quiz questions are from the textbook so if you do the HW and sample problems in the chapters and LGs you're guaranteed above an 80 on the exams. He pretends like he cares about attendance by passing quizzes during class but I never showed up and got an A...
He is an ok professor. He is very hard to talk to. Lectures aren't helpful so I just learned on my own. LG Sheets and HW's are fair questions to be on the exam. Thats how you prepare for his exams.

The class boils down to you doing the LG review sheets. If you did the homework and the review you are guaranteed at least a B on the exams. He does take attendance in lecture, and recitation quizzes matter. He likes to lecture on things other than the material but he's a really nice person. Its chemistry so still hard but he makes it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: burt himself is a very smart man, he has so much knowledge stored in his head and he teaches fairly well. the course itself is pretty easy as well, he gives textbook questions that are the "study guides" and a lot of the test questions are directly from these questions. lecture quizzes don't count at all still got an a and never went to class.
he is brilliant and updates his study guides often. helped me through mcat studying. Updating the study guides helped me with self-discipline and studying more efficiently. def recommend!

Lectures hard to follow, pretty rude in office hours. You understand the material with his study guides, which are nearly identical to the exam he gives you, but he doesn't give you the answers, and you have to look for them in his disorganized lectures/google. 95-100 is an A which is pretty ass, no drops, no curve. But Rohini Qamra was lit.

One of the most brilliant (although slightly condescending) professors in the Chem department.  His exams are easy as long as you study the way he tells you to and drill yourself with the study guides.  Overall a great class from someone who has a passion for the subject material.  If you took MCB (BIOLUA 21/22), this class is essentially a repeat
Extremely arrogant, rude, and mean. He knows nothing about mutual respect, but his class is easy. Do his study guides and you will get an A.

Dr. Goldberg definitely has favorites, but if you ask good questions and pay attention to him during class, the class will be well worth it. Doing the Study Guides makes the difference of whether you get an A or D in the course. Try to do these in a good time span since he tends to put a lot of questions on them. Highly recommend taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Burt has a "very bright" personality which is not understood by some, but he is The Best in his specialty. Make sure to absorb all the knowledge he has to offer! The subject is difficult with a lot to memorize/learn, yet he teaches only what you need to be successful in med school! Very fair grader, honest and charming. Take him at all costs!!!

He is the best. He's rude but only to students he knows and he's always joking! It doesn't matter if you listen in lecture because if you complete the study guide that he sends you, you will 100% get an A.

It hurts me when people say bad things about BG because he genuinely is the kindest professor i've had at NYU. He cares about all of his students, he just has a funny way of showing it. Lecture is worth going to not even for the material but purely for his stories which are extremely entertaining. Love him!

Dr. Goldberg is definitely not one to mess with, but with that in mind as long as you pay attention in lectures and DO THE STUDY GUIDES then there's no reason why you shouldn't get an A. Make sure to ask more questions during office hours rather than in lectures themselves. Forming study groups is really helpful in the class as well.

He's one of my favorite professors. He comes off a little intimidating at first, but a week or two into the semester you'll figure out he just cares a lot. The lectures aren't overly helpful, but worth showing up to if you have the time. Find a couple of friends to study with. DO THE STUDY GUIDE - IT IS THE EXAM. Put in the work, it'll pay off.

This dude is great. Gen Chem 2 was a class I feared, but I loved it a lot. The class is designed in a way that allows for everyone to get as much as they can out of it, and I really appreciated that. Goldberg does get tied up in his own interests during lecture from time to time, and office hours might be daunting, but the product is really great.

He renewed my interest in chemistry after Mandziuk had destroyed it. He's by far the best science teacher I've had at NYU. He even made me want to switch my major from Biology to Biochemistry (Still debating that). Hopefully I'll have him for Biochem!!

Best Chem professor I have ever had! Aside from having interesting lectures, he is also very inspirational and wants to motivate us all to continue strong in our desired career paths. He really did save my semester and thoughts about continuing with pre-med! I owe it all to this man
Burt Goldberg is the best professor I've ever had at NYU. Do not believe any negative thing you hear about him. This man will change your life. I love him.

Was continually disappointed by his lectures. He does yell a lot and insults people, but as someone mentioned he's a softie, you can see that he means well. At first I liked him, but I learned almost nothing from lecture cause of his rambling; he goes off on a tangent with stories from his youthetc. Which is sad because he's obviously intelligent.
Best prof. I have ever had.

One of the best professors I have taken! He may seem intimidating in the beginning, but he is a softy at heart. He appreciates people that do the study guides on time, show up to lecture and make an effort in class. Answer the study guides and you will do fine on the exams.

He comes off as intimidating at first, because he tends to yell and make fun of his students. But I think on the inside he's an extremely nice man that wants you to do well. He is a very fair grader. Answer his study guide questions and memorize them word for word. That's all you need to get an A, because his exams are exactly the same.

Goldberg is like a resourse you have to use. He is one of the head of the Chem department and getting a recommendation letter from him for med school would change everything. Classes are short and he tells stories. He makes sure you get the material. He works with Yoel to give you the best resource available. He can be mean, but just to push you!

Burt Goldberg is by far one of the best professors at NYU and my favorite person EVER. He can be a bit intimidating, & if you are a sensitive soul, you may find him rude, but he's a really wonderful guy. He bends over backwards to help his students succeed. Fill out the study guides, go to lecture, and ask questions. It's an easy A if you do that!

Man, what a piece of work.  Never in my entire life have I been so consistently disrespected and insulted for absolutely no reason.  Professor Goldberg has issues (a lot of them) and he generally takes them out on his students.  At the same time though, he's an amazing professor and presents an exceptionally interesting and well managed course.
Truly an amazing professor. Loves to help and teach, unlike a lot of other professors doing research. Listen to his lectures and classes will be interesting, exams easy.

Don't judge a book by its cover. Don't judge Goldberg by his first impression...or second...or third. He can be mean and insulting, screaming at students but he's a real softie at heart and it shows. Funny as hell, both his stories and him as a person.
Excellent Professor! One of my favorites. Really makes you excited about the topic in a way you wouldn't otherwise be.

A very complex guy, in a nutshell. He was a terrible adviser but a brilliant prof, and good educator, though usually extremely pompous. Just do well on all the study guides and you'll do fine on exams. Lets you pick and choose questions on exams. Girls can ask dumb questions in class, but if you're a guy, don't talk unless you have thick skin.

He was not a good teacher for Nat Sci II. I didn't learn anything; he would just ramble on about random topics that had nothing to do with the material that was on the tests. The TAs were the only ones that every actually taught us anything. He's also REALLY mean and arrogant.

Best professor ever! His exams are straight from the study guides and are super easy if you read the textbook. It isnt mandatory to go to class but this guy is very entertaining so i wouldnt miss his class! he might come off as moody but just dont piss him off and he'll be fine

Alright, he's a Biochemist at heart, but there's no denying that the man knows his stuff.  Although he goes off track for about ten minutes per class discussing whatever has ticked him off the most or a random personal story, he always comes back to what we need to know.  The ego comes with being in the science department.

I dont know about him as a professor, but why is this clown the advisor/director of the chem department? They could have at least found someone who doesn't rage and throw books at students who come in asking for help.

Goldberg... Rude? yes... Insensitive? definitely... Condescending? at least once every class... Favors the girls? uh huh... Fantastic, passionate, engaging lecturer? You betcha. Despite what's been said about him, Goldberg is truly a great prof. Lectures were always interesting and fun to attend. Forget about him as a person, think of him as a prof

There is no reason to have to put up with this man for a whole semester. He started his course with a lecture about how disrespectful and stupid all of us underclassmen are.  He went on to continue insulting the whole class and then proceeded to brag about his accomplishments.  He is the rudest professor I have ever encountered.

Wow, so many different about him here. Well, for me, I thought he was a funny and nice professor. The lectures were interesting and his study guide questions were VERY helpful. I took him during the summer and he graded our exams (lack of TAs). At first, I was scared cause he was the one grading our exams, but he turned out to be a nice grader! ;)
Can't believe that this kinda person is being called as a professor.. Worst communication skill, insulting students, and overwhelming narcissism.. ugh!

Goldberg spends most of his time insulting students, talking about his own life and achievements or yelling at students for asking questions.  He is the biggest ass I have ever encountered.  The class is easy, but not worth putting up with Goldberg.

I don't know about him as a professor, but he's the director of the chem department and he's an absolute joke. Goldberg could care less about you if you're not a chem major. His attitude towards students in general is ridiculous. Why is he the chemistry advisor?
This guy is useless. He lies and blows kids off most of the time. He also has a bias towards hot girls. He should be fired from the chem department.

Just wanted to comment that he is NOT by any means affiliated with the Biology Dept. I do not know why he is listed under biology here. Biochem is a graduate-level bio course open to undergrads, but that doesn't make Goldberg an undergrad bio prof.

Best teacher everrrr! His lectures are very entertaining ...sometimes he goes off topic but it's still interesting. For Natural Science II his labs are easy, the midterms too, he gives you study guides which are basically the same as the tests and he is just awesome. I would take absolutely any class he offered!

I took the NAT SCI II: How the Body Works. Funny teacher. Good lectures, but he talks about a lot of things that have absolutely nothing to do with the contents of the exams. Labs are annoying, but easy.
Goldberg is the****. Those people that can't stand him can't get past the fact that he is accomplished enough to be full of himself. He's a walking brain and does often go off topic. Great man.

Goldberg is amazing. Some people may find his personality obnoxious or overbearing, but he is such a comical, jocular person, and he truly cares about what he teaches. True, he spends a lot of lecture going off tangent and talking about current events or funny stories, BUT all you have to do to do well in the class is read!!! Enjoy him while youcan

I LOVE GOLDBERG!!! yes he does show fondness for his female students (sometimes) and yes he does play favorites but what can i say?? just be one of his favorites! the things that he talks about in class are exciting and interesting. he'll always help you if you have questions. another good thing is that you'll do well if you study enough.

Goldberg thinks he is a very funny man, he spends a mojority of the classtime telling you "jokes" about his accomplishments. The lectures aren't boring but the whole time I sit there thinking $4000 for this! Lectures for biochem II are podcasted, I don't know about experimental bc or the map class though. Not too much studying required.

Dr. Goldberg is freakin hilarious. He is a GENIUS. so smart, so funny, good teacher. his tests are pretty easy and doesnt assign alot of homework. he is very straight forward and loves what he teaches.

Brilliant Biologist/Chemist. Class is VERY interesting and he is so knowledgeable and always answers any questions. He does like to go off on tirades about his very liberal personal/political views (and how the American educations system has "gone down the tubes"), but I found the NatSciII class very useful as an owner's guide to my own body.

Extremely rude, chauvinistic, inappropriate and downright obnoxious. I will never see him again for anything and will not come near him with a ten foot pole. Other advisers I have spoken to think the same. He is a bitter, old and mean person. Why the hell is he the head of the chemistry department??!!
