incredibly arrogant and pompous man. spends the majority of class time discussing himself and his own accomplishments. refers to himself in the third person and constantly talks about how the average person cannot comprehend science and that scientists 'want it that way'. class was easy though, posts lectures online, tests are straight from text.

Professor Goldberg is a great professor.  He has a lot of character and interjects personal anecdotes during class.  His style is unique but the material is spoon fed and the exam questions were given as homework, in advance.  I felt that I knew what was expected of me.  Never a dull moment!(I took his MAP class)

He is really funny and explains things really well. He wants you to come to lecture but he makes the lectures fun and he doesnt always keep you the whole time. his tests are not too hard and the grading was really fair. for someone who does not do well in science I got a good grade and genuinely enjoyed the class

Although he is arrogant and spends most of lecture talking about his life, I learned a lot in Biochem II. He is very passionate about the subject! I found it very interesting, but a very difficult course. You will be spending a lot of time doing the study guide, but at least he has a study guide! (exams reflect study guide, not the textbook)
Really up on his field.  Plays it for laughs--if you think he taes himself seriously, you're too thick to get the joke!  Earnest and pasionnate and no chauvinist.

This is by the far the most horrible person I have ever encountered in my life. Not only does he toot his own horn beyond belief, he is a cruel human being and by far the most demeaning professor, I cannot understand why they made him the academic advisor unless they want everyone to drop their chemistry major.

While he is an engaging lecturer and sometimes amusing, he is often rude to students and is offensively arrogant. His testing methodology is inappropriate for the subject material and answers often depend on obscure terminology that doesn't appear in the text. Also, the test-grading process is entirely opaque. This was the hardest MAP course I took
He's arrogant, but deserves to be. He's been around the medical world for decades, and has the knowledge to show for it. I enjoyed the class.
its a pretty fun class that keeps you interested.  exams are not that bad.  if you read the book theres no reason why you shouldnt do well in this class.
Great teacher. Really explains! Brilliant and engaging!!

I'd agree that he's self-congratulatory, but I always saw it as more amusing than pretentious. He's a nice guy and he makes lectures interesting. Labs are clear and tests are straight from study guides. Not an easy-A, but not too difficult.
The best professor I have had for any class any school.

Excellent prof! Walking, talking book of medical knowledge. Amazing how much he can store in his head. Funny, but also teaches very pasionately and you'll learn a good deal.Definitely one of the best MAP classes I've taken and I've taken a few good ones.A bit above average workload, but all is pretty easy.Exams are just the study questions he posts

Wow. 'dr.bg' is insane, always look forward to his classes. Tests were pretty easy, labs and grading were amazing. Knows HW copied (back of book) doesn't care. Knowledgeable about the subject, great sense of humor (not corny). Labs are tied to what we learn in class. A lot of material is the only downside. Highly recommended NatSci II, go for it!
Extremely fun, semi-nuts so makes lectures interesting. Presents info in a very coherent manner and really available to students and receptive to questions. Clearly loves to teach.
Loves to talk about his prestige more than the science.  Endlessly self-congratulatory.  Hope you love him as much as he loves himself.

Dr. Goldberg is brilliant. He is absolutely my favorite prof ever. No sci prof I ever met can spit out so many biology facts in a minute. He is a walking textbook.. if not better. I agree he digresses a lot in class but at least  he keeps you awake. He's easy to approach and is fair with grading.

Professor Goldberg is absolutely my favorite-- he made it fun to get up super early and go to his class, and that's saying a lot. He really knows his stuff and I loved his class. I have no complaints.

Spent most of the class tooting his own horn. I was suprised that he didnt make us line up and kiss his feet. I mean honestly--this was a science class and  he spent half of it yapping about what he has accomplished and how he could be doing such great things! Like he is doing us a favor by being there. Exams are a piece of cake though.
loved this class! funny, entertaining in a self-deprecating way.  made the material super easy to understand and digest, no pun intended.
Barely spends any class time actually teaching because he spends most of it focusing on self-indulgent digressions.  He really doesn't seem to be that well informed about the environment.
Professional, funnyand really cares that you understand
Made it easy and fun--always approachable and helpful.
Made it fun!  Knows his stuff!
The best!  Hated the course in HS.
such an idiot. doesn't have basic sense of science. don't know how he is a professor at NYU? he just can't distinguish between g/mol and Dallton
Good Professor, syllabus gives good focus on important topics.  Has tendency to digress during lecture, which sometimes is a relief.  Enthusiastic to teach and is well prepared.
Digresses a lot.  But on uninteresting things.  Doesn't explain things fully.  Doing well but still dislike him. Yuck.
What an awful, self-obsessed man.  He gets in the way of his own teaching, when he does attempt to teach, that is.
Insipid, silly man.  His perpetual jokes become draining, his poor teaching skills frustrating, and his obnoxious demeanor revolting.
I guess I am retarded cause i got an A-. Explanations are long winded and lectures unfocused; this guy goes everywhere...

Won't let you forget he's Senior Faculty.  Infantile and self-aggrandizing.  Wastes obscene amounts of course time attempting to appeal to the testosterone in the class.  Reminds you of his credentials more than he teaches.  Lacks teaching ability. Ugh.

I liked him in the beginning because he's comical. But if I hadn't taken Chem in highschool I'd be completely lost. He's competent but seemingly weak at conveying his knowledge to students. His routine gets tiring and repetitive after a while.

Always fun to listen to in lecture, has a genuine love for biochemistry so he loves teaching it. Gives mock exams to study from, then uses, almost exclusively, questions from those practice tests for the actual exam.

THIS DUDE ROCKS!!!! NOT only does he give you the EXAM questions ahead of time, but he is VERYYYY helpful after class. Unless you're retarded, impossible NOT to get an A in the class. This guy rules!! very well read, friendly and ALWAYS a comedian.
Not very helpful in general if you are really into fashion.
Ms. Marcus treats others with contempt. She is not pleasant as an educator or person. Advise against taking her course and advise Ms. Marcus to examine her behavior.

History of fashion photography class. Very good lectures. Interesting. Don't hesitate to say that you like field trips. She brought my class to the Avedon Foundation and it was amazing. Very kind and easy to talk to. She likes participation in class.
Tough grader. The average for the midterm is 78.3% possibly without a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader. The average for the midterm is 78.3%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved the class, MUST TAKE

Took GPH 2995. Brian is phenomenal, kind, clearly cares about you learning the material. I recommend him to all of my peers to take Biostats with him. It's clear that he puts in alot of work and thought to teaching the material well and making it equitable to students. He is easily accessible and tbh, should have a full-time position.
great overall
Professor Spitzer is passionate and genuinely wants his students to succeed! He is so understanding and he embodies how a teacher should be.

Dr. Spitzer was the best professor I've ever had. He's young and very passionate about psychology and teaching. He includes the bulk of information in his lectures but reading is encouraged as well. Attendance is mandatory but a Zoom option is available as well. His lectures were so entertaining and I always left class in a good mood.

goes on unhelpful tangents to flaunt knowledge, doesn't explain content on slides (which only include diagrams, images, and a few words, so it's hard to catch up outside of class). laughed when i asked for extra help/tutoring for exam. grades harshly, only 4 grades total. doesn't answer in class questions. don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable on memory and psychology overall but can't transfer it to a teachable manner. He went on long rants for the 2hr so it was difficult to decipher when something was important to note. Grades were only based off 2 take home exams which had ambiguous prompts, slides were often unhelpful. I would not recommend this class at all.
He means well. But I would not recommend this class to anybody. His grading is extremely confusing and all over the place, and his lectures are hard to sit through.

he is just super unclear when teaching and the lectures feel all over the place. the exams are extremely difficult and ask for a lot more than we learned in class. the class did pretty bad on the midterm which shows that something is not right with the teaching or exam structure but he pinned it on the students.

(Psych-300: Memory) 
He is very knowledgeable on the topic but transfers his expertise neither clearly nor concisely. Two tests, 50% of your grade. Half the class stopped coming to lectures after the midterm. 
Said everyone would get an A --> not true :) 
If you miss a lecture good luck deciphering the gobbledygook that are his powerpoints!

Thought I'd put this out here: Prof McElree doesn't care enough for his students, even those needing a break. I did very well grade-wise in his class, but I dislike the way he treats other students. I wont say any specific things he did because idk if that violates guidelines. But yeah, I dont advise taking his class unless it's for credit.

Although he's a nice guy, Professor McElree does not have a clear teaching structure. His lectures contain numerous tangents deviating from the material, he repeats himself a lot, and the slides make 0 sense. Reviewing the slides on your own proves to be unhelpful--he has vague statistics from experiments without telling you what is being tested.

There is neither really a clear expectation for the class nor for the exams. The materials are dense but the professor cannot really unpack them and explain them clearly. Meanwhile, the course is only graded based on four exams, all are extremely difficult if not excel in every detail he discussed in class. Simply do not take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very detached as a professor, the criteria of the class is extremely unclear. Basically this class is based off of pure memorization and not learning the material. Very hard to reach, unless required for credit try your hardest to avoid this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily worst professor I EVER had in my undergrad career. He's unavailable/ unreachable. Does not respond to emails. Lectures are all over the place& is not specific what his expectations are. When it comes to discussions &perspectives, it's his way or the highway. He is tenured & does not care about his students& is consistently late to class

I'm writing this because I took Cognition with him over summer and feel bad that this guy has really bad reviews. The material he teaches is kind of confusing, but I just did the readings and got an A. He has a dry sense of humor which some may not like, but he is a nice person who will respect you if you respect him. Just gotta put in the work.

I did not interact with him much outside of class, but he seems nice and very knowledgeable about his field. His lectures can be a bit hard to follow and focus on but I found that when I applied myself and paid close attention, I was able to understand them.
Awful lecturer, his TAs taught a lot of the classes as well but I always found that his lectures were the hardest to follow.

Truly the worst professor I have ever had. Incredibly vague and unclear, impossible to follow, and a terrible lecturer. Very intelligent and established, but under no circumstances should be teaching this material. Material is contradictory and impossible to follow. Slides make no sense. Seriously a terrible experience.

Will contradict the texts he assigns without telling you what to ignore from the readings. Often defensive and patronizing and will not be helpful when you are confused. His PowerPoint slides are confusing but he bases his two exams on them. Do not take his class if you can help it.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He has some nice insights, but doesn't care much about transmitting them in an accessible way. You'll need to go over his slides in your own time to put the concepts together.  Fails at fact-checking dept'l plans for major req courses. Almost messed up my graduation schedule. One-word answers to (slightly long) emails, with a period at the end.

So unless you already have a good grasp on neuroscience you won't pass. He talks extremely low and is scattered, he is extremely unclear. Everything i've learned i learned from my TA'S and by staring at the slides until it forced itself to make sense. He acts like the tests are easy but they are extremely difficult and wordy .DON'T TAKE !!

I took his Language and Mind course. He's a little scattered so you have to actually pay attention in class. Fair grader. If you're struggling, go talk to him outside of class and he's ridiculously helpful. Definitely go to his office hours at least once - he's much more clear 1-on-1 and gets excited when students show interest.

This guy is a total nut job who gives impossible tests, hates questions, and is rude to his students. Unless you have a requirement with him avoid him at all costs and if you do have to take his class be prepared to be slightly miserable and EXTREMELY confused. Ask TAs questions instead because he does not care about what you have to say

Best professor I've had at NYU so far. David's knowledge on sound is so extensive, and he is always making sure you're able to understand and grasp concepts. He's super understanding, and really accessible outside class if you need any help.
Consider taking other
Constantly go off on a tangent. Nice person, but not the best person to learn from.

This is my last NYU class, and I took 130 credits. Not sure what happened... this is probably the only class I thoroughly did not look forward to coming. I never receive anything below a B+, except this class. I don't think I would rly want him as a teacher... Not because the bad vibes but bc he is dramatic about any critique and will boss over.

I would NOT recommend this class. For a gen course he makes it entirely to difficult. He assigns a lot of readings and project, and can never fit all of his teaching. You are expected to go to class but also learn everything on your own. Take this course with another prof, and save yourself stress.
He's very insightful, and he wants to help you. Not much work from classes, but constantly go off on a tangent. Nice person, but not the best person to learn from.

I have David for Sound Image and his class is definitely my favourite in the audio semester!! We just had our last class and I wish we had more;(( He is kind, thoughtful, funny, smiski-loving, Park Chan Wook-loving and makes the 5.5hr class feel like a breeze. TAKE!! HIM!!! (I haven't got my grade yet the A+ is just me manifesting for a good grade)

I appreciate the David's passion in teaching, but difficult to understand the relevance and purpose of what we're learning. The amount of work and digress, and the grading and feedback, can be unhelpful.
Basically, a Logic class. Take it if you don't know how to use logic
Bugged me at first but he's a really sweet guy. Very passionate about what he teaches and will get you interested too. Have to watch a movie for homework every week but you choose from the options.

David is a phenomenal instructor!! He continuously raises the bar as a mentor. Trust me, you'll learn saur much & have a great time. He fosters an open environment for students where we really all left as friends. Truly a gem & definitely a Professor you'll want to be able to reach out to in the future for any sort of advice. Favorite Professor!!
David is one of the absolute best professors! He literally rocks. I agree with the genius comment.
Very effective use of the f-word. 16 use cases, brilliant employment. He is a genius.

David is one of my favorite film professors I've had. His class made me a lot more confident about sound design, and even though I don't want to go into sound, I have a new appreciation and understanding of it. He's super understanding, especially around personal stuff, he gives extensions and checks in when he can see you're not doing well.

David cares about his students as human beings. He really wants you to succeed in whatever you wish to do, even if it isn't sound. If you put some effort and care about the class, you'll get an A. He's also fairly young, and understand his students very well. He's also currently working in the industry, and shares a lot of his knowledge to us.

"Well!"

I wish David could be my professor for every single class for the rest of my life.

David is a seriously fantastic professor. He clearly knows his stuff, and he is eager and capable to answer questions, as well as give really helpful, thought-out feedback. He's also great at fostering a fun class environment, and it never feels like he's talking down to anyone. On top of all that, he's just a really cool dude.

David is genuinely one of the best teachers I've had in my life and made my sound class something I looked forward to each week. He's really funny and always gives great feedback on weekly assignments. Sound was not something I was super interested in before taking his class but I came out loving it.

David is one of those people that you never forget. Although it was only my first semester, I seriously doubt any professor will be able to top him. He cares about his students and their projects (whether they're for his class or not), and is the most down-to-earth person that you'll ever meet. His class is amazing and you'll learn so much TAKE IT.

David is a wonderful professor and made me look forward to coming to a 5.5 hour class. He's down-to-earth, incredibly funny, very accessible, and invested in students, whether helping with assignments or just having a conversation.
Best teacher ever had in Tisch

KING. Literally have had the best time in his class. The assignments are fun, and he's hilarious, very relatable, and down-to-earth. The classes can get long, but that's because they're six hours, not because he doesn't try to make them interesting. As long as you do the work and put in the effort, you get an A. On top of that, you actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I had David for freshman Sound Image class and I'm so glad I chose him as a professor! He was my favorite this semester by far

He is such a joy to have for sound. Very inspiring and helpful. Always there when we needed him. His course can be a great time for learning techniques and for workshops. Also very friendly and reachable outside of class. Felt respected and cared for as a student. Recommended

He sparks your passion to learn and encourages you when youre down. He opens up as many office hours as possible, being present with his students. He is relatable, respectable and inspiring. He works in the industry and gives deep dives into his project files. Of course he also knows what hes teaching but also admits when he doesnt know.

David is a new sound professor at Tisch but he's already experienced and works hard in the industry. He is patient with outsiders like me to sound production. Meanwhile he is caring and giving useful feedback on every project I worked on, and you can easily schedule a one-on-one meeting with him outside the class to chat about everything!

One of the sweetest human beings on the earth. Caring, patient, and humorous. Not only guides you like a professor but also helps as a friend. Very passionate and professional in his beloved field. TAKE HIM!!

Please do yourself a favor and do NOT take this course!! All we do is watch Italian tiktoks, movies and listen to songs. She claims that this "helps with our pronunciation" but none of the things we do appear on our homework, quizzes or exams. Be prepared to self study, she's very unhelpful and says, "just give it time" when you ask her for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tina is amazing! She really cares about her students and is very understanding. The workload is very manageable and you learn a lot about Italian culture with her. She gives a lot of resources for the quizzes and exams.
She is SO funny & cares a lot about her students; two hours flew by in her class. Quizzes are very easy and projects very enjoyable. Take her!!

I love her so much. She is the best professor I have had in Italian so far at NYU and I recommend everyone to take her. I really respect how caring she is to her students and for me personally. I will never forget this class!!
Very helpful and engaging

Tina is wonderful! I have taken two classes with her now. She makes class a fun and safe place to learn and practice. She is always open to suggestions. We played Italian card games occasionally to connect as a class and learn more about Italian culture. I highly recommend her as a professor!
Professor Sebastiani is an exceptional Italian teacher. The class was enjoyable and interactive. You won't regret enrolling in this course!
100% take this class, tina is hilarious and she really cares about her students.  Workload is very manageable because you learn a lot in class, and the class is very fun
Tina is the boss. Her class was so much fun and she really cares about the language and making sure you have fun while learning it. Also the lore goes crazy... Tina's opps are our opps now...
Tina is the best professor ever! Class is so fun and always entertaining. I wish I could take Italian with Tina again.
Not a good experience at all, despite doing well in the class. Would not take again and would not recommend.

I loved Professor Sebastiani's class. You can tell she really cares about her students + wants to make sure they understand the material. Workload was super manageable, and she was also very responsive over email if I ever had any questions. :)

sebastiani was an amazing prof for me! she is very considerate and cares a lot about her students and why they're doing well / not well in her class. she's a very funny and forgiving person that always tries to make the class laugh.

I literally love Tina, she makes online class fun and helped me understand more about Italian culture rather than just the language. She's so sweet, responds to emails super fast, and is always smiling and asking students about themselves in a genuinely caring way. The one thing is she cold calls but if you don't know the answer she doesn't care.
Great Italian professor, really cares about her students and engages the class in fun ways.  The exams/quizzes are not bad if you pay attention in class.  Definitely would recommend!

I LOVE Tina! She's so understanding and makes learning Italian so enjoyable! There are a lot of fun video projects/presentations. We do have lots of quizzes, but they aren't too bad as long as you pay attention in class. We do many helpful reviews for the midterm and final. She frequently calls on students randomly, but it's not pressuring at all.

You can tell that Professor Sebastiani really cares about her students and wants us to learn. She is so nice and really engaging during class, which can be hard sometimes during an online course. Workload is very manageable. Could not recommend this class/ professor enough!

she is an amazing professor! she makes learning italian so fun and encourages you to speak without too much pressure and is very engaging. the work is not too hard but allows you to learn italian well and she is very understanding. she is so kind and i loved learning with her, would 100% recommend

Tina is the best! She always finds a way to make the class interesting and will pull out some fun videos/films/music that give you a better idea of Italian culture. If you're involved, act like you care, and do your work then you'll be good! She's also the sweetest and will let you do extra credit to boost your grade if needed. Highly recommend!

Best/nicest professor out there. She couldn't care less about letter grades, she genuinely just wants you to learn so if you show some sort of interest in her class (which I recommend doing) she will reward you with a good grade. She is very funny and her class feels more like a get together with friends than a college class, strongly recommend her

Tina is nice but not a good professor. We mostly repeat after her, watch movies/music videos, and she pairs us off into groups to do the workbook on our own while she checks her phone. Class participation is harsh, but a must. Terrible if you have 0 foreign lang experience, but manageable if you have some Italian knowledge or is fluent in Spanish!

Tina was amazing! I had her for both elementary II and intermediate I. The most understanding, caring professor i've ever had. She cares so much about her students and makes the class extremely enjoyable. The class is based on group discussions but there is little pressure. I wish i could take her again!!

She is very caring and will definitely help you if she knows you are really trying. Participation is key, so try not to miss class. But it is very enjoyable and laid back with her. She's funny but also takes teaching seriously. Our class was very enjoyable. We all had a lot of fun, watched movies in Italian, listened to music, and learned a lot.
She was always understanding and so funny. Made learning a language fun, and gives bomb foo recommendations

Tina is an unbelievably excellent professor! I recommend her if you want a simple foreign language even if you hate learning new languages you will love it. You don't have to spend TOO much time studying , as the bi-weekly or hw 3 times a week is basically studying. Extra studying will earn you an A+
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best language professors at NYU. Made language fun in a way that a lot of other professors cannot. Class isn't easy but the workload is relatively light and the tests are manageable if you know the material well enough.

She's super nice, very engaging, and makes learning Italian as painless as possible. She does give quite a few hw assignments, but they're usually pretty simple. If you participate in class, and show you're trying, she's very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is really helpful and understanding when it comes to missing assignments. She makes very funny jokes and makes class a good time. I'd definitely take her again!

She's a really sweet itlalian woman who doesn't speak in all italian the whole time, so you can understand whats going on in the class. She also has pretty easy quizzes that you can pass easily with at least a b-.
She makes class enjoyable and easier for students to learn. She is very helpful and she'll answer any question student have.

Tina was a great teacher who always supplied pretests before our quizzes, so nothing on the quiz was ever really a surprise. We had 6 quizzes; plenty of opportunity to boost your grade! Just show up and participate and you will leave Italian with a decent grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Sebastiani was such a pleasure to have for Elementary Italian I! Although I took some Italian in the past, Professor Sebastiani really helped solidify my understanding of Italian. You'll be very lucky to have her as your Italian instructor, she is very accommodating, helpful and wants you to succeed!
The classes are relaxing and low pressure, though participation is encouraged and easy enough. learned a lot!
Really cares about helping you learn the material. And she makes it fun!

She is really cool and funny. She makes learning fun and easy but you still have to learn something in order to do well on quizzes or the exams. Quizzes were harder than the midterm and she'll answer any questions you have. Participating can only help your grade and she encourages it. Not a stressful class.

Great Professor. She really takes the time to make sure you understand the material. She gives mock quizzes, mock midterms, and mock finals and then goes over them in class before you take the real one which is super helpful! There isn't a lot of note taking. Most of the class is discussion based with exercises in the two workbooks. Solid professor
Always open to taking questions from students. Makes sure everyone is caught up with the assignments and makes sure you know the material for every quiz and test. Would recommend her to anyone!
Italian I is a great class and Tina is the best. You will never be bored in class and you get to watch very interesting movies and play Italian bingo to learn numbers. You won't regret it.
Great professor! Really cares about the class and wants you to learn italian. Makes class fun and isn't too tough on you.
THE BEST! YOU WILL ENJOY GOING TO CLASS!

Tina was the best of the best. I wish I could take classes with her next semester for Elementary II. She was very understanding of everything and she was very helpful in learning a new language for the very first time. I really suggest everyone to take classes with her. Classes consist of engaging stuff like watching movies, singing Italian songs!

Tina is awesome! Best professor I've ever had at NYU. I would definitely take her again if she were teaching Intermediate 2. She genuinely wants you to learn and really cares about her students. She's a fair grader and her work load isn't bad at all. If you have the chance to take her class then definitely do it!

My third time taking Italian at NYU and she is by far the best professor I've ever had! Very clear in teaching, helpful with feedback, and genuinely wants her students to understand the material. She will not kill you with work, but she will make sure that you learn the material. Definitely take her if you have the opportunity!
Woohoo!

Tina was an awesome professor! It was obvious that she wanted everyone in the class to succeed and really understand the material. She's very helpul, easier to comprehend than other language professors I've had, and a fair grader. She was also super nice and funny. I would 110% reccomend Tina to anyone taking Italian at NYU!

She is a wonderful person! Our class is discussion based and it really helps you grasp the language better. She really wants everyone to speak better Italian by the end. We went on class trips to different Italian restaurants and have good conversation. She's also really fun! I recommend you take her for any Italian level.

This is a language class! It's not here fault the course ends in a semester. We have to get through a lot of chapters in a short amount of time, that's where it gets difficult because this class builds on itself. She could be a little more clear on certain things, but if you bring something to her attention she will do her best.

She is absolutely wonderful. It's my first time taking Italian but I feel comfortable in her class. She is very nice and understanding. Go to class, do the homework, participate as much as possible in class, and study for the quizzes/tests !!!
She is great for the most part. She is willing to help, but her advice is not useful. Nice lady. Fairly easy grader.

Tina is amazing!! Class with her was easy and fun, but I still learned a lot. She teaches about both the Italian language and culture in her lessons. She is laid-back and an easy grader, but you still have to do the work because otherwise you'll fall behind. Overall, I love Tina and recommend taking any class with her!

Tina is wonderful and vivacious. She makes learning italian much more interesting and has quite a fun class, though it lacks come structure it is very conversation and culture oriented. I loved this class and would recommend it to others looking to become acquainted with the language.
Tina is awesome, take her class. She is a great teacher as well as person. I LOVE TINA!

Tina is an amazing teacher.  You should definitely take her if you have the opportunity. Very sweet and funny..engaging and helpful as well.  Quick with emails and super down to earth.  You're the best Tina!
Tina rocks!  Take her if you can.  Super nice grader and really nice woman.  Will definitely make sure you get a good grade!
She is great, a very good teacher but also a great role model. She is kind, compassionate and makes learning a new language fun.

The material was taught in a very engaging and interesting way and I felt I learned a lot from outside ? the - book teachings. Tina is one of my favorite professor at NYU. She understands how to relate to students  and makes the class fun and engaging despite the boring curriculum.
Very nice, highly recomend
Really nice native Italian professor.  Sometimes a little hard to understand, but she will always re-clarify if necessary.  Easy grader.

A native of Italy, she is very good at the language and its intricacies. Understandably, her English isn't perfect and thus her clarity in teaching suffers. A VERY easy grader, you simply need to study for the midterm and final. Quizzes and "tasks" are almost guaranteed perfect marks. Although she's nice, sometimes she literally ignores questions.
Really good, especially since its an introductory class.  Not bad on the eyes either!
You will never know if you understand what he teaches because you have no practice exam. Hw is the only way of checking your understanding but it's not related to exams.
He can't explain the concept well and he has no practice exam. The only thing you can do is review slides and hw, but it actually not relate to the exam.

when students ask questions, he struggles to clarify concepts in a way that actually helps. The exams feel disconnected from what is taught in class, making it difficult to prepare effectively. Grading is also very harsh and does not reflect students' understanding of the material. I would not recommend this course unless you want to suffer a lot.

He just wrote the equation and theory on his mac, even though they are not making any sense for me. And the midterms are really difficult, those questions have no any relation to what you learned in the lecture. If you dont want to get B or B-, RUN!!!!

He is an awful professor. Only 5 out of 50 students in class actually listened to him. I deeply doubt he knows the material he taught. He cannot explain the concepts or answer students' questions. Most of the time, he silently wrote formulas on his iPad (or more precisely copied the formulas from textbooks). He is not responsive after class either.

This one is also off topic. His son Joseph gave me some nerds. they were scrumptious. Thank you for raising your son well. I rate you in your ability to raise children 5/5. Job well done. Truly job well done
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very good class.  He related the lectures material to real life finance.  This class helped me get an internship at a major firm. Hope to take a class he teaches
Interesting material discussed in this class Learned alit during lecture. Enjoyed interacting with him
Great lectures.  Learned a lot in the class.
love him

The whole course is basically to read the textbook and do the confusing homework and exams. He may be trying very hard but has no teaching skills. Often cornered by questions and horrible handwriting.

Really enjoyed this class.  The homework were very relevant to learning the material.  The lectures were interest.  It was great to have a class that applies mathematics to real world problems.  He was very responsive to emails and office hours. I hope I am able to take this professor again.

Professor Cerniglia did a very good teaching this courses. He balances teaching the mathematics along with the underlying financial concepts.   He communicates well and responsive to questions.    Homework are challenging.

If you are a math major with no interest/experience on finance, you might avoid this course and Professor Cerniglia for the following reasons:
1 involves many terms about finance
2 He will avoid math induction and the specific step. Not interesting
3 Not easy A
4 In his hw/note, many definition are blur but his email response is slow

Cerniglia is a kind individual. He chats with students a lot about course materials, internships, and future plannings. However, he is not that a good instructor since he is an adjunct one. He makes mistakes on the board, in the homeworks (challenging) and in the exams. Moreover, he does not explain the ideas behind materials, which could be tough.

Mr Cerniglia is an outstanding teacher. He blends both finance experience with a strong understanding of mathematics. His classrooms communicates the core concepts clearly. His homeworks are challenging and useful for understanding the material. I really enjoyed my experience in the class and would highly recommend hoim.

I have him as my professor for my korean class at Ramapo College. He is such a sweet and kind man. He tries to make class so entertaining even though it was an 8 am class and brought food in for us. He really wants us to learn and lets class out early. Definitely take his class, he is my favorite professor I ever had.

Love this guy. I had him at SUNY New Paltz. He's super understanding and sometimes he would bring in food for us after exams. Even if you make a few mistakes on speaking quizzes, he still adjusts your grade if you clearly put in effort. I took Korean 1 with him and highly recommend his class.

Professor Choi is very patient and caring; if you want to do well in the class you will do well. I handed in 5 out of my 9 homeworks on the last day of class and still got an A. He's very forgiving about missed classes, but attendance is important for speaking practice and learning colloquialisms and usage that isn't in the textbook or slides.

Took basic korean w him- He is so nice guys yall don't even understand. I feel so bad when I don't participate so definitely be loud and proud in his class! Very easy to understand and will always take his time with the lesson if you need it. You need the workbook for credit but it's not a crazy class, workbook and quizzes then midterm n final.

I had Professor Choi for my FYS and he was one of the most kindest professors I had. He brought in snacks and food some days and he would reply to emails within the same day. He was super open to what students had to say and wanted students to participate. His presentations were easy to understand and it's important to take notes on his lectures.

He is such a sweet professor and lets you redo any assignment you would like. He brings in snacks every week, lets you out of class 30 minutes early and is compassionate.  This class moves VERY quickly and will be a lot of work. But if you work hard and study you can get an A and learn how to speak and read Korean in a few weeks! Lovely Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most caring and effective professors in teaching Korean to absolute beginners! He takes time to give easy ways to learn certain alphabet and grammar rules. He often treats us with many snacks, especially during the holidays. There can be many exams and quizzes, but that is solely due to the curriculum. Take him if you can!!

Amazing professor! Super kind and caring, lectures go beyond the PPT slides as he provides us with a lot of extra info which is really helpful because sometimes the PPTs from the dept. are not super accurate. Gives us a lot of information about tests and exams beforehand, and is quite lenient with grading. He also gives out free candy & snacks :)

I wish I listened before I took Packard. First of all, his syllabus is so confusing and TEDIOUS. It's on a Google Docs and he doesn't post ANY assignments on Brightspace so you have to keep track of deadlines and upload it on a shared Google drive. I had to do 3 presentations in this class and I had less work in my harder classes. Don't take him!

Was really sweet and made me actually interested in the subject. He gave honest and detailed feedback, which genuinely pushed me to try harder. Quizzes were 20% of the grade, and he allows a makeup, so it's easy to get a good grade. Very helpful in office hours and genuinely listens. Highly recommend!

Sweetest guy ever, but his class has unclear expectations and rubrics. PARTICIPATION IS SO IMPORTANT. He is a tough grader, especially when it comes to essays, but you can go to him to retake quizzes for an A.

Packard is a professor that will spark your natural curiosity if you let him. He's a great professor and gives second chances when needed. Just show up, read, and get the work done. The class has a lot of work sometimes, but it can be manageable.
SOOOOO MUCH HOMEWORK. Lowkey my heaviest and hardest course this semester, Unclear essay evaluation criteria! Gives super low participation grade

he's a great guy and so nice and understanding. only thing is that he doesn't use brightspace and only uses google drive which gets really confusing sometimes. also there is lowkey more work than necessary, like even he admitted he gives more work than any other arts & cultures professor. but he's really funny and sweet

His instructions are so unclear, and half the assignments are literally just busy work. The energy in his class is so depressing that I hop the turnstile in front of cops in hopes that they arrest me so I have an excuse not to come to this class. Hes nice though.

Nice guy, very prepared for each class. However there was a lot of homework and a lot of in class group projects. Have to admit this class kept me on my toes. No final test, just an essay, same for the midterm. Wouldn't take him again because I feel like it's just too much work for a simple class. Good guy though, always willing to help.

bro i don't think he graded my final paper but still gave me an A, the lectures itself were pretty fun (even if I didn't read the material). One of the nicest professors I personally know, and was really helpful during office hours.

Nice guy but instructions are sometimes unclear on papers and assignments, and his explanations do not help. I think he is vague on purpose to let your creativity take over or something. Overall his class is pretty easy. There's lots of reading, but hardly any of it is necessary to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's not funny because he is trying to crack jokes, but because he's not great at tech and other things. Sometimes he will get your name wrong on the second-to-last day of class, but I am pretty sure he likes me because he sent me kudos. This is my second review for him cuz I took him twice. I highly recommend! Hes sweet too.

Be ready to read. Each class starts with a discussion based on the materials in the documents, he never uses Brightspace, so all assignments and class content are in the current unit's doc. 

Almost every class has homework that you need to submit to the folder; he doesn't give you any grades or feedback on that homework(feels pointless, right?)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
2 papers
3 quizzes(you can retake them outside class)
Cares about feminism and queer culture
if you participate he will help you out. He wants discussion in his classroom. He loves natural back n forth between students without his intervention
he cares a lot about attendance
fair grader and tells you where you lost and gained points
great guy!

I love Prof. Packard. He is actually such a caring and nice professor, and he genuinely cares about all of his students. There are a lot of readings, homework, and group projects, but honestly, it's not that bad. He encourages you to talk a lot in class, and he encourages class participation. But overall he's actually great.

He was very kind and clearly super super passionate about what he teaches! I took him for ACA and came back for ACM. I was having trouble keeping afloat in my assignments and he was very understanding and generous with extensions. The most important thing is to speak up and participate. He really values every contribution. Take him!

I can't seem to understand why his ratings are so low. He is amazing. His grading is very clear and accessible to the entire class. He is a very fair grader who gives in-depth feedback and is always happy to help with any questions. The topics he covers are fascinating and you can tell that he genuinely cares about what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Packard is an awesome guy who I can tell is extremely passionate about his subject. However, his assignments can be unclear, and it's confusing which you actually have to complete or not. I felt like the work was easy though, and he fosters a great learning environment. Three group presentations as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Cares for the class and easy if you put in the bare minimum. There's no midterm or final!! There are a few quizes with one retake, 3 projects that are not difficult, and like 2-3 papers for the entire semester! He is very caring and encourages participations, but can get away without. Clear schedules, lots of reading but easy even if you don't.

Great guy and I liked the queer readings he did of some of the poems but he was a hard grader with papers and a big stickler for attendance. Really valued participation, so if you're someone who doesn't like speaking in class I wouldn't recommend. Also lots of reading.

Professor Packard had various teaching methods. He asked us to watch plenty of movies and brought us to different museums. If you have questions, you can meet with him in person every week. His class has lots of group discussions, so you will definitely improve a lot from his class.

He is nice. His syllabus has so many hyperlinks so it could get confusing. His grading criteria is clear, but his verbal instructions are not. He does not use bright space so that's also confusing. 10/10 good guy. Coursework is not thattt bad. Just take him if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice person in general, but it was overall an unorganized and confusing course. Most of the day to day homework didn't really relate to anything you were eventually graded on, and it felt like a lot of busy work

He is the best professor I have had so far. He will look over your essays and provide feedback if you ask and his feedback is quite extensive, which is amazing! He truly cares about his students. His workload is not much different from any other professor I have had, however it does get difficult if you let your work pile up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Packard is super nice, but my problem was the appalling lack of clarity in assignments and grading criteria. I really like him, and the topic theoretically, but it was kind of ridiculous how unclear it was on what we were expected to do and where our grade would come from. Seems like he just operates on vibes. Also not the best with tech.
Nice guy but not a fan. Annoying about attendance which feels very gaslight-y since this class was lacking in any real substance.
Great professor!

I love Mr. Packard and I think he liked me too. He gave good feedback and always let us retake tests at home and he is a super fare graded. I heard he races horses with his husband named Gilgamesh and Enkidu. He likes people to be out of the box and he wants people to participate. I didn't read though so i was a lil behind in that which was bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Packard is one of my favorite profs/teachers I've ever had, and I hope to take him again. As long as you're able to articulate any sort of considerate thinking about the media you study in class, you'll get an A no matter the opinion or complexity really. He was so easygoing and understanding and lightened our workload whenever we needed it.
His course has three quizzes, and the format is mostly classroom discussion. It's not an easy A, but if you study well you can get A
He is a great professor. His class is fair and interesting. I will take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Packard was a great teacher this semester. He definitely has a lot of written assignments, but nothing too overwhelming - plus he is a fairly easy grader. Lots of group work for sure, but overall he really tries to make a (in my opinion) boring class interesting. Sometimes unclear in criteria, but always offers timely feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took his Cultural Foundations class four years ago during my first semester at NYU and he is to this day one of the best professors I have ever had. Super supportive and accessible and I felt as if he was very passionate about what he was teaching us which I loved !!

Professor Packard was one of the more eager professors I've had - really passionate about his teaching. He actively inspired class debate and organized great discussion. He was also good in giving essay and research feedback. Real gem in the LS department; be sure to take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Packard is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students. I took him first semester as a first-year year and he was always incredibly supportive. He also introduced me to some of my best friends!

Professor Packard is a wonderful person and professor. He cares about every student individually and fosters a wonderful learning environment. I met some of best friend in his class due to his group project pairings. I would die for Chris Packard. <3

He gives you good feedback on essays, but it is very difficult to meet his criteria. He likes kids who talk a lot in class, even if it's none sense. His office hour doesn't very help. Lots of readings go undiscussed. Many presentations during the semester. Don't recommend for people who want easy A. Participation required.

He's very diverse with his readings, sometimes it's heavy but not too bad. HW is easy and simple. Grades essays/paragraphs through google docs + gives good feedback. One huge google doc of all the notes from the class. He emails back fast and helps during office hours. Light lectures. One pop quiz. Super funny and caring, highly recommend!
He is such a sweet person! I wish he was teaching CFII last semester. Overall a very easy course, and he was never hard on grading. He cares about his students grades. 10/10 recommend.

He's awesome! Taking him again because he is engaging, informative and cares a lot about his students. He does his best to accommodate people that aren't in his concentration either so everyone is included.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed his WF2 class. I advise going to office hours/meetings when you get the chance; he's incredibly helpful and insightful. And the work load isn't too much either. Don't hesitate on taking his writing class!
Amazing, take him and ignore those who tell you otherwise. This is coming from someone who's not interested in doing any more work ever than whats needed to do well.
He is a good professor. His work is easy and he is extremely accessible. His score is way lower than it should be.
Great professor, easy grader and not too much of a work load. Works had to be accessible.

He is a great professor, the review don't give him enough credit. I had him for writing 1 and writing two, and he is such a great teacher. He is a really fair grader go to office hours it gives him an insight in your point perspective of the paper which really boosts your grade.

When I took Packard's class he was really demanding about the work we had to do for the class, it was really excessive. At one point I had an extenuating circumstance and asked for an extension ON A DRAFT and he was so rude about it. It was honestly the worst experience I had at NYU thus far.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!! Do not take him for CF or Writing. He will assign work that is half thought out and unclear. He will make you write a paper after you immediately turned in another paper. Be expected to be given readings that will go undiscussed and serve no overall purpose to the class.
Great professor.

His lectures are a long ramble of nonsense that often times doesn't even have to do with what we are studying in class. We have a huge amount of work expected for every class time, whether it is an essay or a group project, and he takes no pity in you asking to cut some slack and not have to learn about stuff that you didn't even see in class.

Packard cares about teaching but unfortunately, he is terrible at it. His assignments are work intensive and often unrelated to what we learn in class. He assigns us long, technical readings that we don't cover in class and then expects us to know the information for tests. His lectures are long and unorganized and complete bs. Don't take his class

1. How can you assign midterms covering material that was not at all touched upon in class? I teach myself the material in this class by myself. 2. What is the structure of your class? I come out of it more confused than I was entering it.  3. Unnecessary assignments...  - He's a teacher whose hearing his students but not listening to them.
Famous for giving vague assignments, rambling through confusing lectures with no logical organization, and not caring about whether or not his students learn anything
Honestly the worst professor I've EVER had. I used to love writing but he ruined that for me. He's very critical and rude. He gives vague prompts and then grades them harshly.

I personally do not feel like I learned anything in this class. This is for people who do not have a lot of other work because you are asked to interview and crowdsource quite a bit. The assignments are different and interesting but take too much time.
Students find Professor Packard, or as we call him -- Chris, very clear and helpful. He is an attractive gentleman with a delicious moustache. Beware!
Great prof
Very vague about assignments... erratic grading... not helpful when it came to asking questions. Really was surprised to find such a prof at NYU.
terrible teacher, treats you like you are in kindergarten and grades as if you are writers for the New Yorker... not helpful at all... avoid avoid avoid...

One of the best profs I've had at NYU. had him for topics in modern culture (middlesexes).  the class was all reading interesting books and watching interesting movies.  workload wasn't bad.  3 essays. great class discussions.  would take him again in a heartbeat!

Packard tries hard to make you a better writer, but most of his day-to-day assignments are absurdly vague, leaving you with no sense of direction. He doesn't seem to be a hard grader - I haven't met anyone yet who has gotten lower than a B on a paper. He's very nice and very chill, but the vagueness of his instructions drove me insane.
Excellent teacher, don't know why people bash him. He helped so much and his work load is manageable. Highly recommended.
this teacher is bogus! his instructions are vague and his grades are based on bs standards... he judges on how much he likes u, not on the writing! avoid!
I don't know what people are bashing him for, I got an easy A in his class.  If you put in any effort (not that much) you'll get an A.  He wants you to do well
do NOT take him... worst teacher I've had at NYU yet, and I hope ever.

Despite the fact that Packard was vague and awkward, I learned a lot from this class.  He does really push you as a writer, even though most of the time you'll have no idea where he's pushing you.  I'm sure there are much better GSP writing teachers

Packard is great. He really wants the students to do well on essays. He always writes very lengthy and helpful comments on rough drafts. You do have to work hard, but he is very helpful at getting you there!

do not, really i mean it, do not even think of taking this class or any class that has chris packard teaching it.  this guy has absolutely no idea what so ever as to what he is doing, and he has no idea how he grades.  i think he is lost in his own head.  trust me, save yourself so much time and work, take any one else but him!!!
avoid at all cost! worst prose comp teacher!
just don't!!!!!! most people who took his class this semester regretted it!! very unclear about expectations, you never know what to do.

STAY AWAY! worst teacher ever! even after an entire semester nobody in my class knows what it is that prof packard expects from students. he is extremely vague about his expectations and his essay topics are extremely boring. the workload is insane, much more than in any other prose comp II class. seriously, stay away! worst class ever!

This prof always makes him available and accepts your drafts whenever and gives you feedback asap. The reason why people hate him is because he actually teaches and expects a lot from gsp students who arent really at the level. I had a bad grade in his class but learned a lot. v.fair teacher.

reviews.comment: Canary was an excellent lecturer and a great professor overall. He followed the textbook closely so it was easy to get ahead by reading the assigned chapters. His exams were moderate to challenging, but working through his exams from previous years helpsed.
Extremely clear and helpful, made orgo easy to understand
Very insightful and passionate teacher. You will learn a lot if you pay attention. He also has a very good sense of humor. Exams are a bit hard, but they are all based on what has been taught.

Seems like a smart guy, but he isn't the greatest teacher. Exams were hard, answers to practice exams were illegible, and he often forgot things in class that an organic chemist shouldn't forget. His jokes will make you laugh though!

hard prof. weekly timed quizzes (usu. 30 min long) given on Blackboard & no retakes are allowed unless you get a quiz grade lower than 5. grading for lab reports are inconsistent & there's a pg limit of 4-6 single-spaced typed pgs. final was hard. if you want to do well, definitely don't type lab reports at last min, review all labs for final!

PING PING DING IS THE GOAT

For CS-UH 1052G (algo), which wasn't listed on rmp:

She does not know how to teach. Learnt nothing.

Many codes and method needs to be remembered. Takes time after course. But she is willing to help you outside the course and grade leniently.
But it just takes so much time on remembering methods for exams, which is pretty boring.

Good

Dr. Dina is truly my favorite professor at NYU! She's engaging, knows her stuff, gives great feedback and above all else, actually cares about her students. She teaches nothing. And there are a lot of readings and videos to watch. It sometimes feels as though students are being treated more like employees facing potential legal consequences, and the tone of the emails can come across as somewhat intimidating.

Recommend !

Second time taking MFE III after a bad experience. Prof Chikhany is a savior! Everything ins so clear and manageable. I dont know how can he got this score at rmp

Fantastic professor. Made me excited to show up to an 8am math class. Made very abstract concepts easy to understand. Workload is very manageable if you stay on top of it and exams are similar to homework and lecture problems.

Take him!! Exams are very similar to homework/quiz/recitation questions. Attending lectures and recitations matters. TAs were great. great prof and course is not bad just abstract

I seriously can't recommend this dude enough. He's one of those rare professors who genuinely cares about his jobs and students. hes great. The course materials are tough, thats just how it is. but he explains them super clearly. you get some credits just by doing hw and going to class. tbh best math prof so far.

HWs and lecture notes are so helpful when reviewing for exams. Best prof in the math department!

FRIENDLY!!!

There is a lot to do in general but the everything is manageable by the way his deadlines are set. He is so caring and genuinely wants us to succeed.
He is the most responsible professor I have ever met! He replies all the messages on time. He answers all the questions students ask!

MFE 1 was great, but heavy workload. MFE 2 is a bit different, he does not record the videos but he goes over everything in class thoroughly. The videos are helpful if we have to miss class or start early. No quizzes but there is a take-home exercise that we have a day to complete. Overall very strong and caring but do not take him for easy A.
His lecture videos were very organized and clear, and the homework and exams were of reasonable level.

Had him during covid and he wasnt bad. Taking him in-person this semester and his class is terrible. His flipped lecture style is a disaster, especially since HE isnt teaching the pre-recorded videos. Hes not that bad, but if youre not very good at math, dont take him.

reviews.comment: I took linear algebra with Professor Chikhany in the summer session. The problem sets and quizzes are definitely not hard. He explains concepts well and is very patient with questions. Also super accessible outside class on campuswire.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and explains everything well. Really enjoyed how he explains how to think about proofs rather than reading over them. His availability outside of class and how patient he was with questions really helped me on problem sets.
One of the best professors Ive ever had, very open to any kind of questions, seemed to really care about his students. Would recommend!!
Just no. There's better teachers. Don't take him for your own sake. If you take him, say hasta la vista to your math grade

Good at teaching and is VERY accessible outside of class. All Im going to say is to not take this prof if youre a slow worker, dont have a lot of time on your hands, or if youre unwilling to go to office hours to get clarification on some things. As a prof, he could be a tad bit more lenient with his studentsespecially during the pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly it is hard work but you can definitely get an A. I did have calc experience before so most of the material was already familiar to me, but Ralph and his TAs are so accessible outside of class I really think anyone can do well. The tests are as hard as the quizzes, practice problems and lectures so there are no surprises. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No matter when you send him a direct message, he will immediately reply to you with an enlightening hint or a clear explanation for your confusion. The best math prof I've ever met at NYU. And his grading policy is generous with three lowest homework and quizzes dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class has a heavy workload, maybe 1-2 hours of vides to watch before class each week. Two different problem sets and a quiz at the end of every week. Need to put in effort
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Grading's too strict. Put in so much work to get an A. In my Calc classes i took here before this one, they were much easier and covered the same material. Econ concepts aren't hard but the way he teaches is atrocious. You'll hate math by the end of his class. For ur own sake, don't take him unless a different prof is worse than him. Then good luck

Many reviews below are inaccurate. Yes the class is hard and there's a lot of work but that's just the class. He does not "hate emails" , he is very very accessible outside of class on Campuswire and replies almost directly. He met with me many times individually before the final. I have never had a professor who cares that much, take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best Professor Ive ever had. They are extremely caring yet strict, and everything is manageable when I do the work weekly. Ive met many times with them and they always explain things as good as in lecture, if not better. Weekly HW and quizzes but drops 3 lowest. Definitely take him as long as youre willing to put in work.

Class failed a quiz and had to give a makeup one. Hates when you email him. Accessible but arrogant. MFE1 is basically AB Calc but he makes all the concepts harder than they need to be. Takes time off of exams unnecessarily. Don't take him if you love math so much.

The class has A LOT of work (3 assignments every week) and the work is graded very strictly BUT he drops your 3 lowest grades in each of the 3 assignment categories. Assessments are short on time which sucks and you have to rush BUT he is very nice, accessible, and clearly cares. Hardest I've ever worked but would take again. Don't take for easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a caring teacher. He appears to be passively aggressive sometimes but if you ever had office hours with him you know he's a friendly dude. The WebAssign and Gradescope assignments are totally manageable. It's a reasonable amount of workload.

Ralph Chikhany is a great professor. His ability to break-down complex concepts is second to none. But his tests & quizzes are extremely challenging. Even after putting hours to study, complete homework and work on quizzes, I wasn't able to do well on exams as there was never enough time.

workload is heavy. two Psets & a quiz every week. grading is nitpicky and very specific. tests are extremely tough w/no curve & very different from lecture. very conceptual, if you dont think w/numbers, avoid. good teacher & very accessible, but material/grading is more difficult than it needs to be. feels like an 8 unit class, wouldnt take again

Standard math teach. Adheres closely to textbooks. Grading is way too specific, though: docked points if they don't like how your graph looks, if your paragraph-length explanations aren't long/'good' enough, etc. Very accessible.

They assign a significant amount of homework, but more importantly, the quizzes and tests are much more challenging than the homework and you're given little time to complete them. Don't take the class unless you're willing to commit lots of time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professors at lectures. He gives an absurd amount of workload. His tests are significantly harder than the homework and gives you minimal time to complete them. If you can I would try to avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Chikhany was amazing. There is weekly homework and quizzes but they are very similar to class work. Recorded lectures are detailed and enough to study for the tests. Exams are similar to class. He is funny and tried to make class inclusive by using pronouns and dedicated time to talk about transgender week, no other prof did. A true gem!

The course itself has a lot of work so cannot blame him for the homework and quizzes. He is very caring and is always available to clear doubts. He explains the concepts very well and if you ask him to explain it again he will do so. The midterm was not very difficult if you practice and come, the final was long but not very difficult.

The homework took forever and it seemed like I had never done calculus before (and I usually get high grades in math). Any NYU class giving a final gives 1 hr 50 min to complete it. He decides to shave off 10 min not even 24 hr before. He repeatedly said in class it'd be 1:50, so this caused lots of unnecessary stress. Avoid him at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will work VERY hard in this class (I spent a minimum of 5 hrs/week on homework- and that's on an easy week!), but he is SO great at teaching! His lectures are in depth and make sense, the problems he goes over are very useful for hw and exams, office hours are helpful, and he is always open to questions (no matter how dumb you think it is ;)

Professor Chikhany is a good lecturer and can explain ideas very clearly. He is very accessible outside class and willing to answer any questions you have. There are quizzes every week. Those quizzes are not hard but the time limits are very short. Exams are easy if you understand all the ideas in class.

Prof. Chikhany is a great lecturer. He was very accessible outside of class, especially via Campuswire and office hours. My main struggle in this class were the quizzes and large exams (midterm, final). It took me a WHILE getting used to finishing quizzes on time. My advice: BE CAREFUL OF TIME, be a fast test taker in general to pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Harder than expected. Nice professor.

Professor Chikhany is fantastic. He lectures very well and I genuinely learned a lot from his course, even with my astounding hatred for mathematics. His homeworks are long and much more difficult than his lectures or quizzes. Final and midterms are unfortunately the same, with no curves (significant ones, at least) to help. Slow workers, careful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is super kind, relatable, easily accessible outside of class and made my first remote semester very easy. Lectures and course are insanely organized. Amazing professor, guide me through MFE1. Accessible outside of class, reply to every message I sent him on CampusWire. Also he lets you drop 3 lowest quizzes, hw, very generous. Easy A.

Professor Chikhany is a great person and professor. Although the workload may be challenging, he tries to help as best as he can. If you get the chance of taking him, take it!

Nice professor for MFE I. Clear lectures, engaging materials. Accessible and friendly. Word hard and you will be fine.

Professor Chikhany is a nice guy. However, the material is really hard, and his tests are difficult. He gives out tough homework assignments every week, and he's a fairly strict grader. Overall, he's a great person who cares about his students, but I hope he will be nicer to his future students.
Dr. Chikhany is a well-guiding professor and would take his classes again. He is very helpful with interesting homework that make you think beyond the lectures.

very bad professor and even worse class. DO NOT TAKE!

He is a nice dude and not too bad of a professor. He tries to remember everybody's name in lecture. His class wasn't too difficult. He made his tests relatively easy.

Omg noooooo. if it weren't for my wonderful high school Calc AB teacher I would have failed this class. his lectures will cover 1+1 and then his homeworks/exams will ask you to cure cancer. he posts a lot of review work but if you ask him to check your answer he'll say "idk i didn't solve these". either take AP calc or start praying if u get this.

Lectures will make the material seem doable until you get to the homework/exams, they are 10x more difficult and the lectures only provides you with the most basic examples. There's a reason even after over a month since course registration opened up, his course is still available.

I don't think he is as bad as what is said here. His exam was indeed a bit difficult. But it was all based on what was taught in class. If you study hard, you can get a good grade. He uses a curve grading system, but not very much.
I saw a review on here about feet pics and decided to take the class anyway. I hope future me goes back in time to stop past me from taking this class. Saw the feet pics, they were . #Horror #Trauma

For Calc III, I really liked his lectures. Pacing was difficult at times and he made mistakes somewhat often but nothing too detrimental. Came off condescending at times when questions were asked but overall good.

He is the worst professor at NYU!!! I would never take him again. Wait for another professor if you wish to take MFE1. The final and midterm were ridiculously hard and nothing like what we learned in class. People didn't even finish the questions. Averages are in the 50s and 60s. Worst experience in my 18 years of life.

He is the worst professor I've had in college and throughout my entire education. He offers no real test prep, uses irrelevant study guides, avoids hard questions. Not to mention he has an insufferable attitude. Must be fired.

Lectures are very easy to follow but do not prepare you whatsoever for the exams. He seems like a genuine guy, he makes jokes, but not a good professor. Very nice and genuinely wants to see his students succeed, especially if you show up to class. He's not the best at explaining concepts or answering further questions. I wouldn't recommend taking him for more challenging courses if you aren't prepared to learn independently.

The material he teaches in lectures is easy and has nothing to do with the assigned homework or quizzes. Does not prepare us for exams well or give any clarity on what is expected on the exams. this man is just walking ragebait. lectures are okay but won't help you with homework or tests. if you even attempt to ask him a question, he will look you dead in the eye and tell you it's prerequisite material, and then proceed to fail at basic algebra on the board.

Do not take this professor if you want to have an enjoyable experience. Genuinely the stingiest professor I've ever had, and expects you to know everything before hand. He constantly gets his own problems wrong and doesn't know how to explain things to save his life.
I took he's classroom for math-ua-131 and I was just studying all the information for online and not even form his lecture. He's quiz heavy, and just jump out the class

His lectures are fine, but if you want help on homework, good luck...
Absolutely no help and unclear grading criteria. He's super condescending. He cares more about his syllabus than he does about actually helping students understand material.

The class wasn't too hard, but I wouldn't take him for a higher-level course—he struggles to explain complex concepts (i.e., he skipped teaching synthetic division, calling it “too difficult to explain,” despite saying it was more efficient than normal long division). Expect three weekly homeworks: written, WebAssign (45–120 questions), and a quiz.

Very condescending professor. Assigns a lot of homework. He does not necessarily introduce the materials, he just assumes students have some understanding of whatever he's introducing, even though we don't. Does not provide preparation for tests.

Assigns WAY too much homework. I attended every lecture, and he answers questions in an incredibly condescending way. It was basically impossible to complete the midterm in the allowed time. Whatever you do, DO NOT take this course with this professor. I went to every lecture, and the exams were literally a foreign language. If you want to keep your sanity, find a different professor for the course.

He is a tough grader and isn't really accessible outside class—I went to his office hour in person and he asked me to ask my question online instead. I found the class difficult mostly because I am not good with math, but he could be a better professor to support us.

I had Sanfratello for Calculus I, and I believe that he gets too little praise for his quality as a professor. His lectures aren't life changing, but they are hard-nosed and practical. I dropped this class during the first week of classes!!! He is not only a terrible professor with no skills regarding teaching the lessons to students, but a very off-putting person. He is rude to students when they ask questions that he finds elementary. his lectures are fairly engaging and his slides are organized... however, what he teaches in class gives students a sense of false confidence because it does not match the difficulty of problems given in the exams and other problem sets. So terrible at teaching. Doesn't explain topics from the beginning. He expects everybody to know everything. Gets mad when nobody asks questions, but if you ask a dumb question, he embarrasses you. never taking again...

By far the worst teacher you will ever have. This class is designed for the students to fail. The lectures are straightforward. This guy is son of B for sure！No fking curve when the average score of midterm is 58/100. Super rude.

He is personable if you talk to him one on one but generally is standoffish and does not inspire. Preparation for exams doesn't match exam difficulty.

He assigns a lot of homework that does not match the content on the exams. The worksheets given to us also did not reflect the content on exams. The sample exams do not help. Too much HW and you need to spend several hours to finish it. He gives a review sheet before the exam, but the content of the exams is very different from what is on the review sheets. This professor is just bad. I've taken him twice now (not by choice), and both times his lectures are awful and you end up learning the material on your own. Idk what to rate but heres my take. The lessons were fine. Wouldnt give much examples, but would give decent notes. Quizzes werent bad, but the homeworks were hard af.
