reviews.comment: Somehow made such easy material so incredibly hard to understand. Your grade relies primarily on three tests, and the first test many people bombed as it was completely different than the homework and quizzes he gave us. While he slightly curves grades he overall just seemed to have an unapproachable demeanor.

Went to office hours and dude just didn't care basically told me to study harder and review the same useless notes. Psets are just LaTeX busy work and the proofs are near impossible to get full marks on. The good reviews are straight CAP and I feels like they're written from Sanfrantello's burner accounts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
if you value your mental health and time, do not take Sanfratello. The lectures are not even worth going to because he does not try to teach you the material. it is a mandatory self-learn class.

He will take points off your participation grade if you ask whether or not he is going to curve a grade because "you didnt listen in class"
SO much homework and basically ALL self-studying -- exams are brutally difficult compared to the lectures which are not even that helpful

MATHUA 9- PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF AND AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COST!! He gives an INSANE AMOUNT OF HOMEWORK AND HIS TESTS ARE SO DIFFICULT. This class requires a lot of self studying. His lectures and his responses to questions are NOT helpful! this class was a terrible experience!! I SERIOUSLY CAN'T TAKE IT ANYMORE. trust me don't take him

Awful professor, a hard grader, and the teaching way is insufficient. The lecture is not useful and never gives useful replies and feedback. DO NOT TAKE THIS UNLESS U WANT BAD GRADES AND A BAD LEARNING EXPERIENCE.
He does not care for students. He gives his students 0 points for just some little issues. Trust me. Drop his class immediately.
professor sanfratello, You are not a good man.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: (MATHUA9) BRO Ive literally never written a rate my prof but i cant take it anymore. this man is not REAL. Hes not a real human being because how can one assign SO MUCH HOMEWORK for a class that isn't even that important, its just a requirement to get into other classes. there is an UNHEALTHY, UNHOLY amount of hw weekly and i cant take it anymore

He's pretty good at teaching, lectures were kind of boring because of how many definitions he had to go through but that's just Linear Algebra. The biggest drawback about taking him is that his notes are not really organized well, he will send lecture slides over announcements so it's very annoying to go back to study/work on worksheets.

He doesn't deserve all those negative reviews. A good professor. The lectures are very concise and slow-paced. Exams are not easy, but linear algebra is not easy no matter who you take it with. As long as you are  confident with the lecture slides you should be fine because exam questions mostly resemble questions from lectures and problem sets.

I don't know why so many classmates gave him low marks. I 100% recommend him. I also takes LA this semester. But I think he is very responsible, his lectures are clear. Since it's online, it is obvious that the number of participants is getting smaller and smaller. When you complain, please think about whether you are serious about studying.

DO NOT TAKE. my first review on rate my professor bc that he's bad. Exams were AWFUL: way too many questions, no time. one exam had a massive error in it. Gives practice exams that are completely different format and cover stuff not on the exam...so useless. too much hw and it sucks. Never gives solutions to problems in class. condescending man

Like he wants students to fail. Doesn't teach everything that is on the worksheets but also provides no answer keys - lots of self-teaching and scouring the internet to find teaching material and verify answers. Worksheets are the only practice given for the quizzes. Doesn't give back midterms - no way to see what you did wrong.

Please don't listen to other reviewers who say that this professor isn't that bad. I listened and regret it deeply. He reminds of my 7th grade pre algebra teacher in the way he teaches. His style of teaching wouldn't be awful for elementary classes, but when you delve into linear algebra, a complex and intricate subject, he frankly fails to teach.

Strange (in a bad way) - smiling and chuckling when students are struggling on exam, giving hw problems that are unnecessarily hard. Messed up a problem on our midterm, typo made the problem impossible, took majority of most people's time. Examples in class DO NOT cover the hw or test problems. Be ready to self-teach.

Horrendous homeworks, quizzes, and tests. Made an error on the second exam and caused everyone to waste a ton of time. I swear he doesn't proof his homeworks and tests or even take them before he releases them. Some homework problems are made to be absurdly long for absolutely no reason but for random algebra irrelevant to the topic. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First rating ever. Was compelled to rate because this is the worst teacher I have ever had. Have taken calc 3, ODE, data analysis, discrete, never struggled until this. Lectures and gives very few examples. Examples do not cover what is on the tests or the homework. Questions are so obscure that you can't even find them on the internet.

I had Sanfrat for discrete math (&took Linear Algebra with another prof) & Ithe ratings on here miss the point.
Discrete Math &Linear Alg ARE HARD COURSES with all profs. 

Professor Sanfratello was very accesssible during in person & online office hours and his lectures overall were clear. The exams and homework were hard but standard for Courant.

He is underrated. He's not that good but definitely not as horrible as some reviews said. Quizzes are hard. Drops lowest 2 quizzes and 1 HW. Exam 1 is easy while Exam 2 are a bit harder (but he took one question off and gave everyone 4 extra pts). He did kinda read off his notes and poor explaining, but nothing is impossibly hard in this class
Messed up professor teaching a messed up course.

Just avoid him. Jesus. He does explain the concept; however, he assumed that all the concepts you learned just suppoed to provide you a base. And he is asking you to build a landmark on it by yourself. All tough problems you saw are easiest problems for him. No wonder why exams are hard. You will find Q1 a)is easy, and b),c),d)you'll have no ideas.
Extremely hard exam
Second exam was so much harder than the first exam. The numbers were not easy to work with and the exam was super long.
First Exam was really easy, second exam he made impossible without any forewarning
Atrocious exams, no one had enough time for the test. Skips a lot details in lecture that helps make the content intuitive.

He is frankly an insecure control freak that doesn't allow you to do anything besides his way. He requires people to work on the HW PDF. Doesn't sound bad until you get points off for writing your HW answers clearly on lined paper with work shown. When you email him you have to email him in a specific yet tedious format or he won't respond.Insecure

His teaching style is divisive, you either understand him or you don't. And if you don't you are on your own.  The exams were wayy to hard for a pre-calc class with the averages being around 50-59%, he does curve at the end of the semester but really plays with your confidence and those scores reinforced my hatred of math.

Lecture materials were taught well, but exams and quizzes were extraordinarily more difficult that the materials taught in class to the point where students were not taught more difficult concepts that showed up on exams/quizzes. Allowed a cheat sheet, but not enough time on exams. Overall professor was rude and dismissive when asked questions.

Makes ZERO exceptions, lectures fail to explain the simplest of concepts, quizzes are online with a 20-minute time limit, and requires you to do your HW using LaTeX software, which he never explains how to use in class. Went to his office hours, but he was standoffish and didn't seem to care. One of the worst professors in the NYU Math department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take! Forced to self study and basically teach the material to myself. I have taken this class in high school and yet he still makes it confusing. Passive aggressive, unresponsive, and does not care. Stay away if you can.

I HATE him PERIOD. I wasn't able to access the webassign. Even though i texted bunch of cengage people and they say its the prof problem and our "respected" professor sanfratello respond is: You have to figure it by yourself...thank god I drop his class and you know what, i got placed into cal 3. GOODBYE

DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU HAVE OTHER OPTIONS!!
Give two quizzes with in one week (one of them is pop-up), and there's still quiz right after midterm. His grading rubric of polished proof is basically asking you to publish another textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When I have a better understanding of "passive aggressive"

Just avoid him. Very nice guy, but does not care about you in the slightest. Lectures are irrelevant and goes on a tangent. If you want to learn your better off learning calculus through YouTube. If you're praying for NYU just avoid him since the payment is better off going to a YouTube channel or a tutor since you will need that.

Does not give enough time for exams, even with letting us make a reference sheet to use. Quizzes tended to rely on tricks/manipulations rather than actual computations or applications. He did teach things very straightforward (nice), but in the process omitted the concepts and connections needed to understand the overall concept, and skipped steps.

Engaging lectures (mostly) explained well. I feel like he lectures based on his old notes so he doesn't remember all the things he's lecturing about (so might not answer questions well). He glosses over some concepts he thinks are "basic" or doesn't cover more examples in class but the homework are good indicators of what to see on tests/quizzes.

He seems to really care and his lectures are engaging. However the problem is that he glosses over so many things in class assuming you already know everything. His example problems have giant leaps in the process for the answer which make using them to study useless. HW and exams will only vaguely if at all resemble what he does in lecture.

Please for the love of God ignore the students giving him 5/5. 

Imagine paying 80K a year at school only to get a teacher that cannot properly teach the concepts. He constantly glosses over the basic, important steps to understand the work. You either have to be math genius or you already know Calc

Professor Sanfratello doesn't deserve the amount of criticism that the reviewers are giving. He explains concepts clearly. The concepts can be challenging to grasp at first. Some HWs can take a while. The exams can be a bit of a time crunch, but they aren't that hard.

Absolute legend, he is hilarious and really smart. His lectures are clear, hws are easy, but exams are a bit hard. Make sure to do a lot of practice and go to his office hours. Overall, an absolute star!!!

I don't know why there are so many negative reviews...give this man some credit!! Speaking from someone who has ALWAYS struggled with math, this class is relatively clear and well-organized. Linear alg isn't very hard and there are TONS of resources online, so u can't blame him if u r not doing well. He is a humorous guy who cares about the topic.

The course is OK. The professor is OK. He can explain basic concepts of Linear Algebra. However, Time for test is absolutely not enough, and he do not know how to accommodate student who take this course online. Students wasted 10 min because of him and he did not give extra time to compensate. Number is his HW and quiz is disaster.
Incredibly amazing, except that he is one of the worst I have seen in NYU. Choose him!
bagayalu
Pretty chill guy to learn LA from. Pay attention in class and it is an easy time.

Homework is easy and the quizzes are a little tricky, but the exams are a false mirage of being "easy." You think you studied enough for the exam, but it humbles you. Recitation leaders are more helpful than him. Sanfratello is good person, but not the best at lecturing. Unless you live, breathe, sleep matrices, I would find a different professor.

exam 1 was based off of topics that were not taught in the class yet, he graded the tests even though he knew that the exam questions were wrong. overall not very accommodating. lecture slides are ok, he gives them to you filled out. quizzes are pretty easy. TA's have argued over correct answers with him. if you can take someone else please do.

Sometimes it feels as if the professor of the class has made himself the king of zoom just because he has online exams and proctors them. Unsure whether the professor is proficient in his own material because we are often referred to high school algebra for help. Would not recommend, especially online.
Does he understand the knowledge himself?

His lecture makes no sense since he only teaches matrix calculation omitting the meaning behind it therefore his math class looks that a remembering class. I am not sure if he really understands linear algebra himself or just too lazy to teach in detail.

Isn't great at giving lectures, slides are poor, make sure to take good notes. Definitions/theorems are significant portions of exams, make sure to memorize important ones. Familiarize yourself with proofs and know the general format. Make sure you understand HWs for exams. Quizzes often, but usually on the lecture he just gave. Exam averages: 65s

For his linear algebra, very heavy workload. You're expected to read the textbook word by word, and homework amount is insane.
I had him for online class, the midterm and final exam are terribly difficult compared to the in-person person.
Try to avoid his online class. Tough grading for ONLINE linear algebra.

He is a decent choice I would say. I didn't have any complaints and thus he deserves 4/5. Unlike other professors his classes are bearable to watch so I will give him to that. Class work is normal, not crazy. Exams are fair but the quizzes are hard.

He doesn't understand half of the really complicated topics and his lecture notes are a mess. Towards the end of the semester, the proofs he teaches in class become logically incoherent. I compared his content with a different professor's, let's just say the latter made a lot more sense. His exams are easier though, and plenty of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a normal professor but sometimes can't explain deeper concepts clearly to students. Normal exams but quizzes are hard.
To be honest, his class is relaxed and fun. He is very inspirational! For the group project, if you put your heart into it, you will get a pretty good score. He is a real GEM.

Quite literally the worst course I have ever taken. The lectures drag on eternally, the content is either excruciatingly boring and useless or needlessly complicated. This is a required class, and it seems like Prof Sanfratello is either unaware of that, or is completely insensitive to it. I wish I could rate it a 0.

Every single class theres a pop quiz. Every week you have to do a polished proof and code it into Latex. Every other week you have to do 10 problem sets with multiple parts. He rushes for over content for the quizzes that don't matter and makes the dumbest jokes. Overall not the greatest and annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Sanfrantello is a very solid professor. He is a bit funny and helps you learn. Issue is, since he is new and the homework is from NYU the stuff you learn in class does not always relate to the HW. The problem sets are a lot of work. However the exams are fair but require a ton of self study to do well on the proofs part.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Sanfratello is the new professor here and he is very hilarious. We can get a full mark in quizzes as long as we read the book ( the quizzes are pretty short! 3-4 questions per quiz). He is always there to help me and encourage me to learn discrete math. Listen carefully and you will get great grades! Choose him and you won't regret : )
The course is easy, and I don't listen to him at class. His exams are really basic and not difficult.

Prof Sanfratello is great! His class policies make it very easy to learn well. He lets you use a cheat sheet for the midterms. Homework is standard, and so are the exams. He quite funny, but sometimes makes arithmetic mistakes that can be really annoying.

Lectures are interesting, he is funny, explains material well, and is always open to questions. You may skip a few classes, but he gives a pop quiz almost every time. There are a lot of assignments, but if you understand the material you'll be fine. Also, some quizzes/assignments are dropped so you if bomb a few you'll still pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Only covers the basics in class, and makes a lot of arithmetic mistakes. Questions given in HW & exams are far more conceptual and complicated. Doesn't even follow the guideline sometimes on what to expect for weekly quizzes. However, he does allow us to bring in a cheat sheet for exams, and gives out extra credit problems.

The professor is great and explains things really clearly. If English isn't your first language, definitely go to every class and preview the material beforehand. After class, you'll realize it's not as hard as it seems. Duman repeats key points, which really helps. You can tell he genuinely loves neuroscience—her classes are actually enjoyable.
Took two classes w/her and she's a nice prof but the courses are pretty boring... Attendance not mandatory but you need to go to pass the exams.
It's not an easy class
There were things on the test not taught in the classes. She not put a lot on the slides and I felt lost at times
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Going to lecture will definitely help with information reinforcement/she's very repetitive. Can get a good grade without though. Exams are pretty straightforward

Personality is extremely easy if you have any sort of background in psychology or related fields. Even if not, all you have to do is listen to what she says in lecture or read the slides and you will be set. Grades made up of a short literature critique, 3 exams, and some random 5-minute assignments, all of which are simple and straightforward.
Amazing. She really knows what she's talking about and give great advice for how to succeed in her class. 10/10!

She makes it so easy to remember everything that I barely had to study for the exam and did well on it. She reviews everything a million times so you can NOT forget it. Her lectures are funny so you actually want to show up, and if you go to lecture, there's barely any memorizing/ studying you need to do outside of class.

Go for recitation!! And go through her slides well, exams are fairly easy and she is always willing to offer makeup exams. She repeats the content a lot of times in the lecture which helps drill it into your brain so its easy to remember.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (personality) The class was not very difficult. Take notes on the lecture slides and recitation slides and you will be fine, there's an exam study guide before each test, leaving very little reason not to do well on them. I don't think you need to go to the lectures to do well as I didn't.
Very caring professor, exams are difficult so it is necessary to go to lecture (take good notes) and review using the study guide provided before each exam. Exams are not cumulative.

(personality). Take notes during class and fill out the study guides to study for exams, they are extremely useful. Super nice professor and really fun, really values getting the class involved in discussions. Really fun class and the exams are easy as long as you actually take notes in class and fill out the SG.
Amazing lecturer, never rushes or goes too slow on certain concepts; Exams are a little hard and weight 72% of the overall grade, but the review sheets are always very comprehensive.

Professor Duman is great. I love her teaching style and the exams are incredibly fair as long as you go to class. The class is super interesting and she is clearly passionate about it. I would def recommend Social Neuro.

Took Personality. Overall really good at teaching, her exams can be tricky so make sure to review all the class slides before exams. There is a textbook but I didn't read it and still did well. She's very clear at teaching and reminding you when things are due. In personality it was 3 exams and a short 2 page lit review.

Prof. Duman is funny, but her exams are tough. Exams have multiple choice, brain labeling, true or false questions, and an essay. If you peer pressure her enough she'll remove the essay and make the final easier though. Content is heavy and difficult, and each exam is worth a lot (25-30% of the grade), so if you mess one up you might not get an A.

She is very sweet and makes her lectures interesting. I took both personality and social neuro. Social neuro was much easier for me. Personality was sooo much information and the tests were tricky! You def need to read and memorize the book for the exams, also she does brain labeling on her social neuro exams which were tough. TAs helped me pass!!

I love Prof. Duman!!! She's probably one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She is so nice and teaches the material in a very clear way. Exams can be difficult but definitely doable if you attend class (lectures aren't recorded!) I genuinely don't think I've ever learned as much in a class as I have in this one. She's awesome.

Really sweet professor! Makes classes interesting by showing videos and trying to interact with the class, encouraging everyone to participate. Attendance is required in recitations. Material is not that hard, but it is information and detail-heavy.

She is such a sweetie. She makes lectures interactive and enjoyable. Grade is mostly determined by midterms and final which are in person, they're not easy but with some studying are just fine. Attendance isn't mandatory but I would highly advise attending bc the slides are harder to understand without her explanations.
she's not a great teacher, not really accommodating and puts content that we barely talked about in class on the exams and acts like it's obvious that it should be there

She's not flexible w/ students. I had to get a 0 on the 1st exam bc she wouldn't let me take it early even though I had a family emergency. Not the end of the world but still frustrating and affected by grade because the tests only get harder throughout the course so I HAD to do well on the other 2. I didn't have any wiggle room left.

I really enjoyed prof Duman's class. I felt like I always understood what she was talking about and if I didn't she had lots of resources to help, including talking to her directly. Yes the tests were more difficult than I expected but, as someone who is horrible at studying, if you put in the work it's very possible to receive a good grade.

She is not a good teacher, puts way too much content on exams, and does not give any study help until about four days before an exam. She calls them quizzes which is genuinely insane and her grading criteria are unclear. She also has not expressed if she will have a curve even though the class average is low.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Let this example speak for itself: for an entire semester, the first thing that she lets us do in every class is a kindergarten-style "can someone tell me everyone's name in this class?" and we go around. But as of week 10 out of 14, she, herself, still doesn't remember the names of some of my peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Has a lax grading system if you just submit everything (which isn't much) and show up, pretty much guaranteeing at least a B+. 

1-on-1 meetings are pretty nice. Clear she knows what she's talking about and wants to be constructive, but it really doesn't come through in class.

Had her for an early morning, but she often felt passive aggressive.

not AS BAD as the 1/5 comments claim, but she's definitely NOT a good professor in almost any way. like sure, you can get by pretty easily, just do your homework. but her personality... she treats you like INFANTS, and there's ZERO enthusiasm in class (she SOUNDS enthusiastic, but never successfully produces anything that's worth any enthusiasm).

She was my first writing professor, and I found her class quite engaging. Doesn't give you too much homework, but requests submission two days before your actual class. I found her quite interesting, even though the way she explains homework or an essay can be quite confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't understand the negative reviews. If she's confused by what you're saying in class/thinks it's shallow she'll question you on it, but she isn't passive aggressive at all, just honest and direct, and she's always respectful and cares about students (she even brings in food sometimes). All the in-class writing exercises were rlly helpful too.

She's quite hypocritical. Not a terrible choice like you'll be fine but if you can take someone else, do. Her instructions are weird but she's pretty hands off when it comes to essay writing. She's very strict about her attendance policy, but if you always show up you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Emily was nice but I was often confused by her class. She used Brian Eno's creativity cards to help us with ideas which was awesome. It felt like she hadn't made up her mind with how the class was going to be taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: God I hate this woman (and I got an A!). Unbelievably rude and snarky to students. Her class may be technically easy in the long-run but her instructions feel like deciphering ancient texts. Also, her essays somehow like aren't graded on the quality (mostly) so uhh it's really hard to want to put in the work to write something actually good.

She is definitely a strict grader, but I don't think she deliberately gives students a hard time. She is just really specific with what she wants. If you pay close attention and work hard on every assignment, you would find all the assignments manageable.

She is kind of bipolar but is very nice in the end. Her classes are fun and you can get an easy A if you submit the HW. She got us free movie tickets and brought donuts and different stuff to class. She might have favorites in class but you are never sure. I would take her again, personally I really enjoyed her classes despite some random moments.

Take this class if you want somewhat of an easy A but you will be miserable for the entire semester. She is very passive aggressive and gives confusing directions. I got low grades for every assignment but somehow I ended up with an A.

Runs class in a questionable way and has clear favorites. Only redeeming quality is the grading policy - it is basically impossible to fail as long as you go to most classes and turn in the assignments.

easiest class this semester, she had a fair grading system where everyone started with an 85 at the beginning of the semester and could increase their grades through bonus points from assignments etc. she credits students for trying their best which i appreciated a lot throughout the semester. would recommend taking her for an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An acquired taste. Very bipolar personality - one class she's fun then the next she's in a bad mood putting students on the spot. Lots of participation but never seems to like what we had to say. It was unclear what she liked to read so I never understood the grades I got on my essays. I didn't learn anything from her only my classmates tangents.

There are definitely times when it's questionable with how she runs the class or asks her questions to the class for discussion. However, she is a pretty fun teacher and she grew on me a lot by the end of the semester. Try hard on your assignments and you'll enjoy them better bc she gives a lot of freedom with your writing (encourages risks)
avoid her at all costs

she is the most cruel teacher I have ever taken, one time she said that I was the worst writing in the world by calling me a disgusting disgrace of a person who should never touch a pen or a keypad again. I feel so discouraged by writing, and as a former dramatic writing major at Tisch I feel sad to ever write again. I am now a sophomore in film.

Emily is definitely an acquired taste when it comes to whether or not you'll like her. She does have favorites and if you're not one of her favorites the class might not be as enjoyable. But the grading criteria is very clear and if you make the most out of it, it can be a relatively chill class. If u just do the work and you'll at least get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Often shuts down the person in the class, doesn't like questions, and makes students seem like they are at fault for not understanding things. We do not learn much in class and discuss our assignments too much.

She comes off as nice (esp in the beginning) but became very irritable in moments and has a judgmental demeanor. She isn't too harsh of a grader in my opinion (EXCEPT WITH PARTICIPATION! I don't know anyone who got above a C in that). Her feedback on assignments and rough drafts is horrifically vague and unhelpful, and I don't feel I learned much.

AVOID HER CLASS. She is very unclear in her assignments and gives difficult, broad, and unhelpful feedback. She has a stringent attendance policy and is very curt and passive-aggressive with students she doesn't like. She gave me a C- in participation after only missing 2 classes over the whole semester and participating in ALL class discussions.
She is very kind as a person and a grader. Genuinely an interesting person who is honest and cares about what she teaches. I liked her a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives very confusing commentary that is often unclear and overall vague. She is overall a nice person, but doesn't connect with students on a real, meaningful level.

Emily is a great teacher. She is strict in classes. We read lots of materials in and after class. Attendance is required for her class. There will be homework after every class. But she really have great teaching content and clear feedback after every essay. Her goals are clear and if you fulfill all requirements, you get good score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Emily's like a friend to us than a teacher. She's interesting and inspirational as a writer and teacher. Although her assignment description is sometimes vague, I can always reach out to her after class by email. She can always be the choice that opens the door of college writing for you.
She is kind. However, she gives vague and confused comment. And she normally did not provide unanimous comments on your work.

Emily is totally a great professor to take for international workshop 2. Because this is a small class. As long as you are willing to answer her question and communicate with her, you will get good grade.
Not as bad as other claims. If write all three essays, 100%B.

Emily was very clear in what she expected from students because she had clear grading criterion for each essay and explained them well in class. My writing skills improved a lot, because she structured her class in an organized and reasonable manner, presents useful skills to be applied in your essays, and gives very helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Stone always has a mindset that she is always right. She dismisses every single opinion as wrong before taking a look into your argument (especially in an editorial assignment). She always comments that our essays are not deep enough and judging by all the other people who rated this professor, this wasn't unique to me. very condescending.
Emily is nice and caring. But for the essays, it's hard to know what she likes and hopes to read. Lectures are good but not related to the essays.
You need to write in the way she likes in order to get a good grade. Also, I don't like the way she teaches. She treats you like a middle school student, which makes me feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Emily Stone clearly has her own "outstanding" understanding of how an essay should be structured. Yet whether this system of standards is truly objective or valuable is debatable. Apparently Stone knows that all her students are idiots that she has to pay efforts on. So a minimal B score would be the best gift she could give.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emily was very friendly, but she can be a tough grader. Be ready for weekly assignments and to participate in class. The worst part was that she isn't great at giving feedback on drafts of essays so make sure that you ask the questions you want answers to.  The majority of your grade is based on 3 essays that you write, so keep up with work!

He's so chill the class is a bit long and was kinda late so it wasn't that good for my schedule besides that it was easy there's a lot of reading but no one ever read and the exams were easy one take home final and one midterm in class

Overall, I enjoyed the class! It was interesting, particularly for those interested in law/politics. Professor Gioia had an abundance of stories that, coupled with lectures, made it easy to stay engaged. I do wish the structure of the class was a bit more grounded, but I learned a lot, and there were quotes said that I will forever remember.

Clearly thinks he is above this class, usually does not provide feedback but when he does, it is harsh and he is not open to listening. Funny guy with  interesting stories, but still. We were graded off of three things, two of which we never got back. Syllabus wrong, readings barely mandatory, easy to get away with little work. Easy, but annoying.

Professor Gioia is a really really really impressive person and his lectures (more like storytime) are amazing. However, he's like entirely inaccessible outside of class (WILL NOT RESPOND TO EMAILS) and he made us buy like 6 books that we didn't use and now I'm just stuck with Abundance by Ezra Klein forever. Really wants you to think about it!

This class has a great opportunity to be amazing, but it feels like Prof. Gioia does not really have time for his students. He is definitely a well accomplished and smart guy, but he is so busy with other stuff that this class feels like an after thought. the syllabus is wrong, he is hard to reach, and does not know our names :( graded off 3 things

Very caring and driven professor / attorney / former city council member. The classes are scheduled for 150min but he lets you out 10-30min early, especially when we have movies to watch for homework.
You can also find almost all the required books at Bobst or the NYU library online database. Participation counts, and please answer his questions!!

Loved this class! It's really mind-opening and he poses questions about real-world policies that really get people contemplating. He does random cold calls so you gotta do the readings, but the class's graded only on the two exams and final project (all take-home). He brings up a lot of stories too, which are pretty interesting to hear about.

I loved this class as a FYSEM! I think it opens up your mind to thinking like a politician looking at real-world problems and being able to discuss them intellectually. This absolutely spiked my interest in public policy and really got me thinking about hard questions we need to think about. Side note: He will cold call so be prepared

Honestly he is one of the best professor I have ever had, his lectures were also very engaging and interesting. His assignments were all from the content of his lectures and I learned a lot. Plus he has very interesting anecdotes and is very knowledgeable about politics. A top notch scholar, Gioia is a great choice for a future professor.

Professor Gioia squarely fits the "prone to tangents professor" vibe. However, if you're interested in politics or public policy, those tangents will often be a joy to listen to. He's a very engaging professor, and everything said in lectures typically is relevant to class. Very open to changing assignments if needed. Great prof, would recommend.

His 2:30-long lectures are a drag, but Mr. Gioia tries to keep it lively with vids and anecdotes. He is very well-connected and will often tell stories of X politician or CEO, and he offers so much insight for someone interested in the field. Very little homework and commitment but you can learn a LOT by just listening in class and asking questions

There's literally no graded homework. Your two grades are the midterm and the final project. The readings are short and you can just skim over them without actually reading it. Gioia seems nice and likes to hear himself talk (a true politican). The class is interesting and relaxed, if a little boring occasionally. Overall, a definite GPA booster.
lectures are kinda hard to follow and the class as a whole is hard. but go to his office hours, he will explain everything again. he is kind, helpful, and incredibly smart.

Hardest class I've ever taken. The mean grade on the final exam was 30/100. The lectures are way too theoretical and are not actually helpful when it comes to taking the exam. You will need to self study everything. However, Professor Madsen is very kind and has good intentions, he is very accessible outside of class.

Professor Madsen is obviously very smart, but not great at communicating ideas because he thinks everyone is as smart as him. Lectures are completely useless. Class is very exam heavy and he doesn't curve your grade until the very end of the semester. This sucks because he gives no review sessions or practice exams. AVOID!

Not only is Erik extremely intelligent, he's also quite patient and always willing to help out. The grading policy is extremely fair - he drops your lowest exam. Problem sets are thought provoking & help you consolidate what you learn in lecture. Lectures are admittedly hard to follow, but put in the work outside class and you will learn a lot.

READ FOR COMPLETE HONESTY. You will not understand a thing that is going on in lecture but that is fine. Self teach yourself the material from the slides & do all the hws and practice problems in the slides to prepare for exams. If you arent ready to spend hours upon hours self teaching yourself the materials for the exams then dont take this class

reviews.comment: Awful notes and lecture
His class is really hard but he's really nice! Super responsive to emails and very helpful during office hours.
Awful Lectures and notes, but TA is really nice(Lara). Hard exams, weekly problem sets. Do not go to the Lecture, it is the waste of time. Take Recitation and you will get A.

He is a nice person who is approachable. However, the class itself can be quite challenging. If you're aiming for a good grade, attending the recitation (led by Lara), visiting his office hours, and dedicating time to thoroughly practice the material. Overall, I have learned far more in this class than I have in others.
If you need to choose any TA for this course. Choose Lara at all cost. She's the ultimate GOD of the course
If you don't know how to teach, go back to elementary school, middle school, and high school to see how teachers work, instead of wasting students' time in college.

Erik Madsen was one of the best econ professors I've ever had at NYU. Lowkey I feel like all the bad ratings come from people who don't go to lecture or don't pay attention. He's super smart, and accessible outside of class. He cares about his students, and the TA's are great as well. This is a hard class, so don't expect to do well without trying.

Being "smart" or a "genius in research" is no excuse for teaching a poorly designed course. Teaching should focus on helping most students learn, not catering only to a small group of "smart" students while leaving the majority behind. Classes should prioritize inclusivity and fairness, ensuring education benefits everyone.

The worst professor ever. Never explains the examples clearly, and his questions on the exams have not been taught at all. If you can't do one of those questions, you will lose over 33% of the whole exam because he thinks it's your duty to figure out how to solve a question you have never seen by yourself. NEVER TAKE HIM!!! RUN!!!!
so interesting, never listen to anyone's suggestion and never consider the feelings of student.

Hes so smart that he created this course, so it follows no textbooks and he uses his own complicated notations so if you dont understand something from the slides unless it is like a common concept you wont be able to find anything online. Also i dont like how he uses examples and there are like basically no practice probelms.

Professor Madsen is one of my favorite professors at NYU. He is smart, caring, and super sweet. I didn't learn to appreciate his class until I took a Phd micro class. Erik's lectures had great depth and they were actually not as stupid as most underg econ classes are. Madsen is a true genius!
I get mental health issue due to this course. If you care about your health, please avoid this professor. Run as far as you can from the course he taught
Worst professor ever. Has no clue how to teach, and doesn't really take feedback.

Insanely horrendous professor. Lectures are so confusing that the TAs can't understand them. Without the TAs, hws are impossible. Exams have NOTHING to do with the hws or lectures, average on final exam was 40. The TAs complained to him, and he said, "I don't care! Stop arguing with me!" What kind of a professor does this?

reviews.comment: I'm curious who's getting A in this class. I try sooooo hard and still got C
Insanely crazy exams and useless slides and lectures. save your GPA. do not take this guy unless you have to.
exams are way tooooooooooooooo difficult
exams are way too difficult
bad
Too smart to teach. Clearly has his mind on something besides teaching, i.e. research. Be prepared to teach yourself.

He is disgracefully bad. His lectures are completely useless. His hws have nothing to do with the lectures. Exams contain questions that he didn't teach us! The only way to learn is from the TAs. NEVER MISS RECITATION OR THEIR OFFICE HOURS! I don't even know how he is allowed to teach. He has no clue what he's doing. I wish I could give him a 0.

It is useless to attend class, participate in lecture, read the textbook, and look at the slide. It's also useless if you go to the professor's office hour. The only thing that can help you to learn is the TA. I suggest you to go to the TA's office hour, and also please attend the recitation of all the TA.

Your lecture, recitation, textbook, and another recommended textbook actually teach you 4 different courses. So, he recommended another textbook that is usually used by graduate schools.

My personal top1 prof in econ department for now. Responded to emails within 10mins most of the time throughout the semester even if it was 11pm with extremely thoughtful and structured answers to your questions. Accessible outside of class, smart, and caring. Respect

I love the difficulty in Prof.Madsen's class, and got 93% for the midterm. To those of you who fail, stop complaining about the professor. The main issue is that you are very lazy and want to get good grades with little effort.

In a hard class it doesn't help that Professor Madsen is a terrible professor. He does not teach any math or do any math in lectures. Instead he spits out textbook definitions and draws terrible graphs on the board. He is a nice guy but he is an awful professor and should really change the way he teaches because this class could be much better.

Erik is rigor with math definition for econ intuitions, and lectures are filled with very confusing math notations and often times he has to rush through the lecture. But it will help you so much for most upper level electives. Exams are curved based on relative class performance, so don't freak out if you got a 50 for exam.

Please read all comments before you choose to take Madsen. The class should be classified as a mathematics course, the TA's have all-over-the-place grading, Madsen tends to be snippy. Clearly very smart, but should not be teaching undergrads. Absolutely soul-crushing course, so be careful and read every post here!!!

He goes too fast in lectures, so you can't take notes but his slides are very unclear so studying takes much longer than necessary.

Madsen should not keep teaching economics at NYU. He doesn't care about students at all, is not helpful at all, and does put a LOT of effort to make sure students FAIL this class. reviews.comment: We learned a lot of kinks about economics in class. I loved the concept, very intellectually challenging.

Literally do not take him. He does not explain the multivariable calc that he throws up on the screen. Impossibly hard problem sets, with random grading from the TAs. Is rude to students when they ask clarifying questions, holier-than-thou attitude. Absolutely miserable. Save your GPA and take any other prof.

Firstly, Madsen is very knowledgable but he tries to prove this. We were given an Intermediate Micro textbook, however we don't follow it and go far beyond the class. Most lectures do not cover the economics topic but dive into multivariable calc with lots of confusing notation. Feel like I can do math but don't actually understand the economics.

Smart guy for sure but seems to be disconnected to what Interm Micro actually is. Compared to other classes he doesn't cover lots the material (ie. game theory, asymmetric info, barely cost minimization). Instead, he focuses super in-depth on utility, which is interesting but not relevant to half the advanced electives we're being prepped for.

Look up concepts from class and slides are Advanced Micro Theory. He has openly admitted to assigning homework problems on concepts not covered and does not explain the concept if you go for help. "Look at lecture."

Despite the general difficulty of the content, I've learned more in his class than I've learned in other economics classes. As there's no standardized curriculum for this class across the department, he chooses particularly relevant and fundamental topics that have helped me in every other economics class that I've taken. Professor Madsen rocks.

This guy does not know the first thing about writing exams. He asked students in his Intermediate Microeconomics to build an ALGORITHM on the exam. Who does that? He is a terrible professor and he does not have the slightest clue about the actual caliber of undergraduate students and thinks we're all PhD students back in Stanford with him.

Professor Madsen is going to ruin your GPA and you are not going to learn. His homework are extremely difficult and his exams are even more exponentially difficult, impossible even. His exams and homework do not resemble the slides he teaches from, which he did not even make. He is the worst professor I've ever taken in my life.

Terrible Professor. His lectures are him reading off slides that he downloaded from the book which are completely different from the homework and exams. Everything is beyond difficult in his class. You will not learn anything in this class as his teaching style is horrific. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!
Hardest Professor I ever had at NYU. The tests and homeworks for his class are extremely difficult. He teaches undergrad economics at a graduate level.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. Professor Madsen is very inexperienced and it shows. His exams are unreasonably difficult and have very little to do with the homeworks and exercises he assigns. This class is supposed to be on the policy track but he is teaching it in a completely theoretical way. He seems like he doesn't care about how hard people are working.

Worst professor I have ever taken. Do not take him if your life depended on it. Makes everything unnecessarily more difficult than it already is. Intermediate Microeconomics is already a hard class, but he loves using complicated language and notation on his exams to make everything harder. Does not care about you or about whether you learn or not.

This guy gives extremely hard exams and hws. My classmates and I worked a lot during the whole semester but we only get average 35 in midterms out of 100. The highest score is 66.  And this guy doesn't curve the grade.....

Unorganized.although ProblemSets are supposed to be assigned in the beginning of the week and due by the end of the week he assigns them late and only gives and extra day.His lectures are mandatory for attendence yet they are useles when it comes to exam questions and the readings are too shallow for the actual exam yet take up so much time to do

you can tell he cares about the class, but not so much when he writes exams. the wording is convoluted, making it SOOO hard to get an even mediocre grade, I wish he cared as much on wording his tests better as he did for the overall class feel
This class was filled with many concepts, and the exams were too hard

reviews.comment: People writing bad reviews are geniunely salty they didn't do good. Even though he has over 700 students he replies to emails right away and is geniunely caring. His tests are definitely challenging but if majority of the class gets a problem wrong he will give points back. If you do the codons and go to lecture and pay attention you will do well.

The tests are more based on reading comprehension than actual biology and are SM harder than the practice test he assigns on Codon. The median for the tests was often in the 70s, yet he would say good job and never share the mean. Lots of homework, ridiculous tests. Study hard.
you can really tell he is writing some of these, esp after someone writes a bad one

Yes, there's a lot of work in his classes, but you need to learn time management and truly work through his assignments and take advantage of his student hours. Yes, the tests are hard. But he preps us a LOT, so getting a good grade in the class is 100% doable. He's very approachable in office hours and obviously cares (even with 900 students!). POB is not the easiest class, but it's very fair and he gives us many drops and ways to raise our grades. Don't expect a free A, but work hard and you'll be okay.
His exams are way too hard like why is the practice exam so easy and then the actual exam so hard and worded difficulty. Also this is for bio 2 not 1

This professor is the best professor I have ever taken and it's very possible to succeed if you actually try and study
very nice but a lot of work outside of class

reviews.comment: Very cruel man. He is nice to a very select few and can put on a very good persona. He belittles students in his email replies (if he even chooses to reply). You can get an A easily but beware his ego.

HE'S THE BEST! The coolest guy and a very fair and well respected teacher. The class is definitely challenging but it's a hard science class so it should be. His lectures and slides are very helpful and the online textbook/study platform he uses is great. Very fair policies like dropping one of three exam grades and option to not take the final.

Nastiest grader ever was .01% from a B- and wouldn't round my grade. Test are ridiculously hard for an intro bio class. Lecture information does not match exam questions and everything is application based. ALSO changed the final location and time last minute! You can tell this is his first time teaching... Anyone rating this professor harshly just didn't study enough ngl he was fantastic and I learned so much from this course. The Codons were long but they really did help. You get what you give in this course

nice guy blah blah blah. Exams are absolutely ridiculous and so hard for no reason. Is absolutely NOTHING like other older exams when it was taught by other professors

Professor Plavskin has clear guidelines outlined in the syllabus. There are a lot of assignments, but most of them are easy As if they are completed. He is very lenient with dropping assignments. Try and do well on the first three exams to avoid taking the final. He is open to listening to students and adjusting the course as requested.
Professor cares about students' learning- not your easiest A but definitely possible if you put in the work. Exams are difficult but lectures are great and super helpful in learning the content.

VERY different from reg & AP Bio (extremely lecture heavy). VERY content dense and requires lots of independent work (ULC, practice problems, reviewing lectures). hes passionate and reachable, but exam wording is often confusing and overcomplicated. grades aren't exam heavy, but expect to study a LOT. i spent 6 hours everyday studying for exams.

I had no prior bio experience but still did well because he drops the lowest few homeworks and lowest exam grade. He gives a decent amount of homework and the wording on the exams are confusing so you do have to work for it, but he cares about his students and cares about bio so he will help you (he won't round your grade tho, even if its 0.01 off)

Very good professor, super passionate about Biology. I took AP Bio in high school, so this class was less challenging for me. reviews.comment: The course is formatted in a way that is very easy to understand how to get the grade you wish to achieve. Overall, very nice guy and knows Biology well.

His exams are extremely difficult and he sometimes include things we have not learned and you are expected to cues to know it. He is extremely petty when it comes to to rounding, an 84.9999 does not round to a 85, so don't even bother emailing and asking. He will ignore you.
ive never been so shocked. hes "nice and caring", only for some time... exams were absolutely insane. made absolutely no sense. theres no reason for exams to be so difficult beyond belief.

I didn't do good cause I procrastinated but you can just tell that the prof really cares about his students and their learning. Professor Plavskin, while very kind and clearly passionate about the subject, writes incredibly challenging exams without providing adequate practice. He's a very kind person who puts a lot of effort into the course. There's a heavy workload through Codon, including pre-class assignments, weekly study path questions, and problem sets. Wonderful professor! Very kind and very responsive with emails. He is very passionate about his work, and he's very supportive and accommodating. The tests are pretty hard, but he provides lots of opportunities to do better and to improve. Thank you, Professor Plavskin!

this was his first year teaching PoB I and it showed.
