He is very passionate about Biology but his exams will take you OUT. Theres no reason the exams have to be this hard. I've poured everything into this class and still have yet to succeed... Its draining

Guys. He's a good professor and all I think that he is very smart and knowledgable but his exams are so hard just get ready to cry a bit and deffently study in advance :). This class is for sure a very advance biology class and Im sure they made it hard so they can wed out some students because again there were a lot of people in this class.
He has so many drops which make it easier for students to get a good grade!

He seems intimidating but is really caring and passionate. Fought for my life on exams but he gives plenty of resources to study, has office hours twice a week, and pretty fair in terms of grade impact. People have cheated on exams so it's understandable why he is strict for them. Never taken AP bio but passed--he's strict, but fair. Kind too!

Was WAY harder than I expected it to be, but with enough practice (like a lot) you should do fine in this course. The professor cares about his students, but tests tend to be harder than what's offered as practice. (I also have no past bio experience so I'm not biassed and it IS possible to excel in this course without prior knowledge)

This class was far more difficult than I expected, and I'm unsure how someone with limited biology experience can excel in this course. However, Professor Plavskin is incredibly caring, understanding, and passionate, and he was a great professor. 
His exams are not easy, and the course feels unnecessarily difficult for an intro to bio class.

It seems to be that the ratings are heavily skewed. Those who are getting A's have a huge superiority complex over those who are struggling. (By the way if that's the case,  develop compassion and empathy for the fact that not everyone learns at the same pace.). Admit that his exams are too tough for an Intro to Bio course and get over yourselves.
People should not be complaining this much. Prof Plavskin grading criteria was really clear and his exam were easy as long as you watched the lectures.

He's a very enthusiastic professor-- most people here complain about the exams, but the exams are pretty standard as far as college-level exams go (and his test prep problems are really similar to the exam). He gives many assignments outside of the exams that boost your grade, so you can get a good grade if you do the bare minimum.

Guys we are so creative here 🤣. 
Prof. Plavskin is definitely one of the best during my four years of college life. The syllabus is cleverly weighted, so just completing all the homework and get medium in exams can guarantee you a A-!
Difficult exams. A lot of content covered in the course as well. You do need a strong foundation in biology in order to really succeed in this course.

exams are 50% of your grade and the wording could not be any more challenging. i feel like he expects us to know how to read more than how to know biology. hes very nice and cares about biology but doesnt care enough to word his tests appropriately
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams? As a freshman, theyre NOT for freshman. They are worded SO BAD and make absolutely no sense... and theres no curve! so if you get a 79.99999 he will give you a C+ its so ridiculous, if his exams werent a mouse trap and a maze maybe students would actually excell in this cource...

Tests aren't too bad as the other reviews say. Just solve problem sets and watch lecture notes and you should be fine. Very passionate and generous professor, often gives dropped assignments and bonus points.

exams were hardish, but similar to tutorials/problemsets, so manageable if you study! anyhow, i do not tolerate plavskin slander! he's a great professor, super passionate, and his way of teaching is super compelling and makes you properly think rather than just memorize. if you're pre-med and complaining about him, reevaluate your career options...
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a professor, he is really passionate about what he does. The Codon pre-class readings, Study Path, Flash HWs, and Problem Sets are all super helpful. The exams are pretty difficult, but I do think it's essential because they get you to think rather than memorize. Some of the questions can be super nitpicky, but the tests are totally doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: his exams... good god. they are in no way intro level.

Best prof ever. Highly structured class with curated, paced pre-class assignments, problem sets, and practice questions. Not hard to succeed if you keep up with content and adapt your learning strategy.
Genuinely cares about our scientific thinking, growth, and the bigger picture in addition to content. 
10/10 would take a million times again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Eugene is a very caring professor who clearly wants u to succeed in the class. He records his lectures and balances the grades so that you have some wiggle room for doing badly on the exams. With that being said, you need to engage very well with the material on the exams if you want to do well. The exams are very very difficult!! Study ahead!!!

He definitely cares about the subject. Going to lectures is pretty essential, but sometimes he rambles about unnecessary information for the exam. However, I would say he is kind enough to post his recorded lectures if you miss any. His exams are hard, ngl. You should definitely study at least a week in advance if you want an A (for most people).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy but his exams are evil. Lectures are not engaging and contain so much information that he rambles on and on about. Makes POB much harder than it should be and his exams test you more reading comprehension than it does the material.
exam questions are pulled straight from hell

Guys I fear we are losing the plot. This class (and the exams!) are objectively not difficult. Plavskin's lectures cover everything that he tests on, you just need to take a little bit of time to go over it and think logically. That's literally it. He's also very nice, clearly very knowledgeable, and is accessible to ask questions.
Great professor who is obviously engaged with the material, interesting lectures and exams can be a bit tough but are pretty fair if you study enough.
i dont know how to put this into words, but get ready to cry. never thought orgo could be easier than POB

this is insanity. he will teach u like youre in elementary, and then exam u like ur albert einstein. he will respond to emails, but dont be fooled by his "niceness" because once u walk into that exam room, just know youre DOOMED.

Horrible exams do not reflect the difficulty of the things taught. Very disorganized with his lessons, which makes it hard to follow him. Makes intro-level material more difficult than it needs to be. Nice when asking questions, but be prepared to put in a lot of work. Every time you walk into an exam, get ready to enter the tarantula hawk!!!!!!!
interesting man to say the least
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He needs to chill out
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Plavskin is very caring and he really cares about making sure people understand the material. However, even if you understand the material the exams are very difficult. But he does drop a lot of assignments and one exam so it kind of balances out. You just have to put in a decent amount of work. Just do the Codon assignments and you'll be okay

I have no clue why Prof. Plavskin's rating is low. He is AMAZING. He is very caring for his students and wants everyone to understand the material. He is incredibly passionate about biology, and will answer any question with no judgement. The exams are tough, but if you understand the material you can absolutely get an A.

this class is straight from hell. The exams are so difficult compared to the previous POBI professor - they are beginner graduate level and make you think outside of the box which is helpful but his material is not enough to cover all that.
Midterms are hard. They cover materials that you do not see anywhere in the class. He's a chill professor, but his tests are just brutal. That's it.

What he teaches in class and what he assigns for homework does not help with the exams at all. Exams the problem sets are tough. The problem sets have strict grading, but the exams grading aren't as strict. The topics are hard to understand because he overloads you with many different topics that shouldn't be taught in first year biology,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about what hes teaching and it is obvious to tell he is passionate about it (which makes attending lecture nice). 50% of our grade is attendance, homework, and pre-class assignments, and the rest are 4 exams (lowest gets dropped).Only thing is that the exams are hard (questions aren't things we've seen before).

Honestly not bad as a professor, but his midterms seem so different from actual content. Make sure you really understand the class content as the tests are lowk worded differently. His codon prepares you for lecture but he covers so much more in lecture so actually pay attention. You do have a loaded week with this class but it can be manageable.

i personally think his usage of codon is really helpful and he's always been very accommodating and helpful when providing resources and guiding you towards the right answer. very nice guy in general and anyone who thinks he sucks just has a pea brain and i hope to god they never become a doctor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Guy is hella chill these bad ratings aren't indicative of him. 50% of the grading is literally homework and easy assignments. The other 50% is exams and one is dropped. So long as you put the work in and listen to him(not cramming the week before the exam but actually doing codon over time) you're chilling

Good luck, the midterms have nothing to do with what you are learning in class. I would say that he is a good teacher and very smart he just isn't teaching the right way for you to succeed in this class. I would say you really have to work hard in this class and cry a little bit.
Awful exams with no resources given, and he will make you hate bio.

A great prof who cares for students and is very passionate. He provides helpful resources and gives back a few points for questions that most of the class got wrong. His exams are way too hard for an introductory class. There's 3 midterms and a final, you can drop one. It's doable, but be prepared to study LOTS on top of your other work (esp GCI)

Professor Plavskin is an AMAZING and WONDERFUL educator and I mean it! His lectures are very very interesting, very clear grading criteria. There are a few short assignments and a problem set (a little bit challenging) due each week. The class is very well organized and very well planned. He knows what he does. Amazing person!
Amazing professor! I never cared about science or bio before, but his class made me super interested in the subject and want to pursue it more!

One of the BEST professors in NYU. He's caring and very clear about what you should expect on exams. Just pay attention in class, study outside a bit, and utilize the resources he gives you and there's no way you'll get anything lower than a A- or B+.

Very caring and passionate professor with decently fair exams if you actually put forth an effort to study. I didn't take any previous AP science courses, and still succeeded. The online learning tool Codon is super helpful, and Plavskin utilizes it beneficially. Problem sets (homework) are harder than the actual exams and kinda unhelpful/useless.

Passionate about biology and clearly knows his stuff, but that passion doesnt translate to effective teaching. Doesn't teach in a way everyone understands. He spends too much time talking about his biokogy hobbies instead of exam material. His tests feel like grad-level exams. Slow to respond too. Take AP Bio or another bio class first for B+ min.

It's literally so hard. He's actually nice and very passionate about biology but he expects you to have prior knowledge about chemistry and I have none so I'm struggling it's just a lot of work and a lot of studying on your own time!

his midterms are soooooo difficult
there are molecular bio and developmental bio questions in pob 1
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
hey eugene plavskin 
whats going on???
great professor, cares a lot about his students and breaks topics down very simply and clearly puts a lot of effort into content both in and out of class
Difficult Exams and Content heavy lectures with high expectations

This course is hard. It is dense with material and the homework assignments take a long time. Dr. Plavskin is incredibly enthusiastic about his course and it shows in his teaching. His office hours were many hours long, and he stayed until the last student left. If you are willing to put in effort to learn difficult concepts, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult class.Coding assignments are useless,exams are difficult,TA was not helpful.Eugene is great however it is clear he purposely makes the class difficult since he knows bio majors are forced to take. Avoid if you dont want your GPA to tank.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! Stats Lab assignments are so useless and he makes the exams so difficult for no reason. If you're thinking about taking this to fulfill your bio elective... don't.

this rating should not be as high as it is, the number of false cheating accusations made has to be a world record and the "code" he uses to "catch" people is almost certainly nonsense The focus on R coding is totally useless to the majority pre-med class. He's charismatic, probably why his rating appears as good as it is, but its a trap. stay away

This class is dense in content and it will be quite difficult for you if you're not a biology major, especially if you are not familiar with the concepts of genetics. But trust me, you will learn a lot in this class even though it's heavy on stats + bio, and also coding in R, but it will be rewarding.

I learned so much in this class, and Professor Plavskin really knows what he is talking about. Although it is a lot of info and R assignments take a long time and can get draining, there are drops and both Professor Plavskin and the TAs set aside a lot of time outside of class to help students, please take advantage of it. Do every practice problem
Focus on his lecture material. R is difficult unless you go to recitation. Growth bonus is available
Eugene is an amazing prof! Cares a lot for his students and is very welcoming of questions. I had him for Biostats and ATB: Genetics and Genomics, and he was great for both. Take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear, concise lecturer that wants you to ask questions so you understand. Grade comes from R assignments, preclass quizzes before every lecture, 2 exams and a final. Exams aren't the easiest but are generally fair and based on quizzes and core concepts/problems went over in class. TAKE HIM FOR YOUR QUANTITATIVE REQUIREMENT BIO MAJORS!!

Lectures are easy to understand. And 45% of grading comes from R homework which is good (can ask for help and try ChatGPT :)) and bad (too heavy: each time about 300 lines of coding). Fair exams and give extra credit when needed (curve the exam reasonably). Caring and really accessible outside of class! Have great feedback for every HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly recommend this professor and his courses. He will teach his ideas and opinions very carefully. In this course, he will divide a paper into several paragraphs, and then let students show their own understanding and the logic shown in the paper. The assignment is a small paper twice a week. You only need to write one page of this paper.

Prof Nicholson is genuinely the sweetest kindest guy ever, he teaches with so much passion, hes super knowledge about everything, which is also why he tends to go on long tangents sometimes but other than that hes amazing. pls take this class.

Highkey easiest course I've taken in a while. All you need to do to get an A is show up and write something on the required assignments. I BS'd ALL of the required essays and got A+ range every time. Classes are boring, but it's a small price to pay.

Such an iconic professor at NYU Florence! Took him for ACA + ACC and loved class every time I went. He is hilarious and passionate about what he teaches. Lectures are long but engaging, and field trips really bring the course content to life. He is friendly and genuinely cares about his students. I was also in the spring play he directs, fun times!

TAKE HIM. yes his class is easy and he may ramble on but besides that Nicholson is so passionate about art history and he genuinely wants everybody to succeed in the class. he is funny and has sudden outbursts, gives GREAT feedback on essays and hw (may take some time to grade). also incredibly talented (theatre) and he loves his students

GOAT. He is so passionate and knowledgeable, I feel like you could ask him any question and he would know the answer. I would be genuinely impressed if you did not get an A in this class. He yaps the whole class, but he is so interesting, his lectures are so theatrical and engaging, I am going to be sad that I can't take his class again. MY KING FR

Overall a great professor at NYU Florence! His lectures are indeed hard to follow at times, but if you truly try to listen, you will learn a lot from him. Lots of extra credit opportunities and just as many out-of-class essays, but he's a light grader. Excited to take him next semester for ACC!
super enthusiastic and knowledgeable, lectures are a bit hard to follow but you can do well in the class with very minimal effort.

Without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. He is so kind and caring and gives so much feedback and will help you in any capacity. He gives many opportunities for grade boosts and is genuinely passionate about the content. Take Nicholson if you can, you won't regret it.

Nicholson is an amazing teacher, he is so knowledgeable about what he teaches and is always so excited for every day.  He gives you the test a week beforehand with exactly what is on it, so you're almost guaranteed to get an A.  The only thing is he's a little monotoned and he goes on random tangents, but besides that he's amazing.

He's incredibly funny, kind, and knowledgable about what he's teaching. If you bring up literally any art piece or historical event, he will have a handful of facts about it. His class, midterm/ final, and homework were pretty easy and I really liked the class! My only complaint is that he tends to interrupt students while they're talking.

Nicholson is very passionate about what he teaches and he is also very understanding. His lectures are a little hard to follow but you can only fail his class if you're actively trying to. His study guides for midterms and finals are perfect and he's funny too :)

I took his class fall and spring. He's very passionate about what he does. Lectures can definitely be hard to follow, but he is a really amazing person who wants nothing more than for his students to succeed. Easily one of the most loved profs at NYU Florence and definitely the most loved among LS professors. Bonus: field trips both semesters!
He is a very easy grader and a great professor, but his lectures can be hard to follow
Two words: Silver Fox.

best professor ive had, you can tell he loves what he does and truly wants to see his students succeed. super understanding and accommodating if anything comes up and is always willing to provide extra feedback and help with assignments. his instructions are incredibly clear and study guides perfectly outline the exam. took him for both ACA and ACC

one of the best professors at nyu florence. i took him for CFI and made SURE to take him for CFII too. very kind and an easy grader, lots of extra credit opportunities. assigns a LOT of reading but i skipped almost all of them and was fine. just listen and take notes in class and you'll be ok. his study guides are literally the exam. love him!!

TAKE HIM!!!!! My Favorite CF Prof in Florence. He is sooooo nice and inspirational, and he is passionate about what he's teaching. Very accessible outside class, and he is such a caring and kind person. Not really an easy A, but as long as you do the work, you will be fine.
Professor Nicholson is the most knowledgable, insightful, and inspirational person I've ever met. He is so caring and encouraging, just like an Angel. Everybody loves him!

Nicholson is BY FAR my favorite professor at NYU Florence. He is insanely smart, knows everything, is super passionate about what he teaches and hilarious. It's super easy to get an A because he tells you exactly what is on the exam and if you submit your essays early he gives them back with notes so you can fix it. A little heavy on the reading.

Nicholson is amazing - if you have the chance to take his class, take it!! He's really passionate about the subject, and very entertaining. His tests are easy - sends out study guides that basically have everything on the test on them, read these and you'll do well. Slightly harsher on the written assignments, but honestly still very fair. 10/10

I took Prof. Nicholson's CFI class at NYU Florence and he is by far, one of the most passionate professors I've ever had! He does assign a lot of reading, but it's not necessary to read all of it since he tells you what will be on the tests. Great man with a caring attitude towards his students and his acting in class is always hilarious!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nicholson was one of my favorite profs and made cultural foundations a pleasure to take. He's very energetic and lively and loves to grab your attention through plays and whatnot. I would definitely have him for a teacher again if possible.

Awesome teacher, gives you in-depth details of what will be on the two exams. He likes to give you the chance to be creative when it comes to essays, but you can also stick to a more traditional way of writing. He is very passionate and quite entertaining. Essays aren't always an easy A, but if you work hard on them he grades fairly.

Everybody around me seems to love him, but I cannot say the same thing. I can barely keep myself awake in classes and lectures are long and dry. However, he's very passionate and is ready to help you, so I guess it's just me who's not adapting to his way of teaching.

Great Professor! Easy A if your willing to put in the time for the work. Makes the class interesting and fun with his humor and acting skills. He does this show when he puts on masks and it's hilarious. Show him that you care about the course and he'll take care of you.

He is one of the best professor I've ever had. He's clear, very organized and he tells you what he expects form you. I do admit that he is tough, but if you keep up with the readings and hand in papers in time you will be fine.  He is very passionate and he will make you love what you're studying.
best professor at NYU Florence. Period.

One of the most brilliant professors I have ever had. He is engaging and energetic and you want to consume a coffee or two before class to catch each semantic and analytical gem that comes from his mouth. He will sometimes come to class dressed up as a character when reciting plays and he does this quite well because he is also an actor. Get pumped
He is the MOST AMAZING Prof ever, Take his class and you will never regret it!!!! I LOVE his classes.
Love this guy! He's absolutely the greatest and his enthusiasm is contagious. I have him for Cultural Foundations I and absolutely adore it!

He's a fantastic teacher who is so passionate about his subject that it only motivates you to learn. Send him your rough drafts before the papers are due and he'll fix them up and you'll get an A every time!

best teacher i ever had! don't miss his class, it's the highlight of my week! he knows absolutely everything about his subject, no question is left unanswered, every student comment is discussed. very enthusiastic teacher (often acts out scenes from plays). encourages individual essaz topics. fairly easy exams and good review sessions. overall: A+

First, I was not interested in Art history AT ALL!!! but after taking his class, I am seriously thinking about art history as my major. He is not an easy teacher, but not hard. If you do work hard, you will get good grades. He is so passionate, so brilliant, so helpful. The best professor i've had yet!
Wonderful teacher. Great explanations, my best college class ever so far! I recommand him very strongly. He puts passion into his work...
interesting, passionate teacher whose lectures are easy to follow, though he talks rather fast. can be quite dramatic at times, but it only adds to the fun.

I adore this man so much. So smart and funny, the class topics were really interesting. A great teacher. Was also so kind and understanding to circumstances and lateness. Made me enjoy writing again. Amazing. Miss him.
He did not like me. He hated my writing subjects and then took it out on my grading. He said some mean things to me as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love Ozawa. Sadly couldn't get him for next semester, but if you can get him do it! Super fun class, can get long at times but is very engaging. Great guy, just a great guy!

Ozawa is actually the best. Literally everyone in my class was trying to make sure they had him again for next semester. Lot of creative freedom and insightful feedback. Readings were incredibly diverse, creative, and interesting. Also, very empathetic. Made expository writing one of my favorite classes of the semester.
The absolute best writing professor at NYU. Fun, knowledgable, yet not too lenient and knows how to give excellent feedback.
Kind, lenient, and super knowledgeable in just about everything. Every class I went to was enjoyable and he has great insights.
Eric was inspirational, he truly supports and guides his students through.I genuinely enjoyed his class, and would take it again.
arguably the best professor in the program.

For a required Tisch class that can be hell, Prof. Ozawa was one of the best. He's a harsh grader because he genuinely wants you to succeed and he actually cares about you. Also his class craters to everyone in tisch not just film or drama majors which is rally nice because a lot of professors don't. amazing prof!!!
interesting lectures but a tough grader.

I had a great time taking both Tisch Writing the Essay classes from Ozawa. His lectures are really engaging and although he's a tough grader he gives great feedback and you can tell he really cares if you do well or not in his class. Great prof.

Eric is super engaging, funny, and understanding, but he is a tough grader. You really need to read all the material and understand it to include it in your work. There are a fair amount of readings and sometimes they're especially long and difficult, but he's nice and lets you write about what you want to write about.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: 10/10 would recommend. He makes a difficult required class so much more enjoyable.
While his classes can confusing sometimes, and homework heavy, he gives great feedback and is one of the better writing the essay professors at NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors of all time  He is the one of the reasons why I thrived in my first year at NYU. I hope to take one of his classes again, because he is literally one of the most respected and helpful teachers ever. 10/10 recommend

highly recommend for writing the essay. chill, cares about his students, and doesn't baby you. actually made me look forward to the class, though I will say he is a realllly slow grader. not that important in terms of this class, though.
Makes Writing the Essay fun (which is a hard task to do). Very helpful and nice, you read a lot of really great essays and articles in his class.
Awesome guy. Great teacher. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The very best- saved me from a terrible first year at NYU. He's exactly what a professor should be; doesn't let you slip by with mediocre work, always pushes you to do better in a positive way. The class requires a lot of time commitment, but it's completely worth it. This is why you come to college.

Eric was really great in the long run- he definitely cares about his students and will go out of his way to make sure you are doing okay (both in and outside of the classroom). When his feedback is unclear, ask to have it clarified. Feedback sessions with him can be a little confusing if you're not specific about what kind of help you need.

Ozawa is a really cool guy. I transferred out of NYU, but can easily say he was my favorite professor while I was there. Incredibly interesting to talk to about ideas (& anything, really) during conferences, & this is where he clears up as he can be a little vague in class. My ability to convey ideas in my writing improved immensely in his class.

He's a tough, but awesome teacher. I respect him a ton. He's well organized and expects a lot from his students, like any good teacher. He's actually a super cool guy, you'll get to know him as the semester goes on. Don't be afraid to take his class.

He starts off sort of awful, but over the semester as he gets to know everyone he's a lot better. He is as far as I know the only WTE teacher to be currently on schedule, and we are actually weeks ahead of most other classes. He is the self-declared "most difficult teacher to have for WTE", but honestly he's not that bad.
Straight up the man.

Literally made Writing the Essay a class where I no longer want to pull my hair out. He's very easy going and one of the coolest, most cultured teachers I've ever had. If you make the effort, you will do well. He's open to any ideas and will help you whenever you need it. Very lenient on attendance policy and gladly gives extensions w/ good excuse.

Many of my friends found him to be vague but I never felt that way. He left things open-ended and up for interpretation (It was sort of a creative writing class after all). He was never confusing, despite the fact that the subject was potentially confusing. Down-to-earth, pleasant teacher who made WTE engaging.
Great professor. He's very helpful and very open to things students have to say.
I really loved Ozawa's class. He is vauge at first, but is super helpful during confrences! He is great at introducing you to unique and creative ways to write.

He's a really awesome teacher. I had to switch to another professor for my second semester and it made me value him and his teachings so much more. He's pretty easy honestly, just do the work and if you need help or more time ask him. He can be helpful but he does want you to do it on your own. He's really chill and class can be fun if you make it.

Ozawa is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met in my life. He has a lot of interesting ideas to share with you in his class. I have become a much better writer thanks to him. And whoever thinks he's vague is simply not intelligent enough to appreciate him. You can't say Descartes is stupid just because you don't understand him, right?

Look, writing the essay sucks. But compared to the other teachers you can get, Ozawa is by FAR the best. Yes, he's vague - but all that really means is you can do whatever you want. He's really open minded and will give you a B+ for doing what he asks. B's get degrees, guys.

Everyone I know hates their writing the essay class, but he is one of the most interesting teachers I've ever had. If you meet with him outside of class he can be very helpful, he's knowledgeable about an eclectic and varied spectrum of things. Overall, a difficult teacher but one who will improve your writing and makes you think for yourself.

He is the most unhelpful teacher I have ever had. I asked him to clarify comments he wrote on my papers, and he proceeded to repeat what was written and confuse me more. He suggested incomprehensible texts to use as evidential support, then could not explain their relevance to my topic when asked. I am tearing my hair out, it's terrible.

Don't let the other comments fool you. He is about as vague as a teacher can get. The assignments are vague, his responses are vague, the class is vague. Class time is a waste of time. He does not help you, nor does he even guide you like a teacher should. Smart man, but a horrible teacher. And he's definitely not as hot as people say he is.
Ozawa is the best. Great teacher without being annoying, which is impressive for this terrible class. Highly recommended.
A lot of work. Terrible class, but down to earth teacher. Bored.
super chill, understanding, and sweet. great guy. makes writing the essay bearable. nice to look at.
A great teacher, great guy. And if that last poster knew anything about the literary history of belly-button phobia, he'd know that it's as important of a trope in early American classics as whales.

If you have to take Writing The Essay, take Professor Ozawa's class. Thanks to him, I realized fully what my strengths are when it comes to writing, and how to be a better writer when it came to what I wasn't good at. Plus, he tolerated my goon-ness.

If you're an okay writer he reads your drafts and tells you everything is fine...and then gives you Bs...vague. He also read us a piece of his own work, in which he writes that he's scared of his own belly button...totally normal, right? WTE is a terrible class, he makes class time ok, but grading sucks.

Seems like a really cool guy until you try to relate to him. Doesn't like that. Rude and does not really help the students. Honestly made me hate Mondays and Wednesdays knowing I had to go to his class.
looks like keanu reeves!! Hottttttttt!
i don't understand the hype, he is very nice and approachable but i think there are definitely better ACE professors who arent as vague or unclear.
Excellent Professor.  Can't wait for his novel to come out.

I am not the best writer: fact.  But Eric Ozawa is an AMAZING professor.  He is helpful, cool, fun, and really wants you to succeed.  He is down to earth and willing to help you take your writing from eh, to yey!  Definitely a catch when it comes to Writing the Essay teachers.  But make sure you're willing to work.  You will not get the A for free.

Fun, brilliant, and helpful.  Only mildy interested in writing or in essays before this class, I am now incredibly into it.  Made me a much better writer.  Was always interested in my writing, had thoughtful criticisms and ideas, and was just flat-out fun to talk to.  An excellent professor.
I LOVE THIS MAN. Interesting, funny, lenient grader, and I think he realizes that not everyone is stoked to be taking the class. Get him if you can.

Class sucks, no one likes writing the essay. but you have to take it and Eric is great. easy to talk to and fun, treats you like an equal and makes class bearable. since you have to take it, take it with Eric.

writing the essay is awful no matter who you take it with, maybe thats why i didnt love him, he was nice yea but didnt make any of the readings interesting, im not a great writer so i didnt get a lot of the abstract stuff he described and then obviously had issues incorporating those ideas in my work not the easiest grader but you could do worse
WTE would have been god-awful if it hadn't been for Eric.  He's funny, interesting, and really makes the class appealing.
funny guy good teacher knows what hes doing
Great teacher, very helpful and makes the class fun and interesting

Not pleasant. Came off unnaproachable. Openly rude + condescending to students. Stickler and strict. Unjust to students w accomodations, would single us out, + for the writing pop quizzes she would "just give everyone extra time to be even" when thats obivously not how that works. Topics unbalanced + often had nothing to do w production.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid her at all costs. Genuinely. Rambles on for hours about god knows what and then assigns the longest pop quizzes (all free response/essay responses) and gives you 2 minutes to respond. Makes us call her “your excellency”. Not as a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I truly think Prof. Mee is a very passionate professor who truly cares about what she teaches! There is a lot of work and an expectation to show up to class and be on time, but she is so understanding (to a reasonable amount). Overall just pay attention, do as you're supposed to, and be ready to put in work,  and it will be worthwhile!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is required but she teaches it like it's an elite masterclass. Obsessed with Indian theater, barely touches actual production. I already wrote a review but after the final I had to write another. It's a handwritten essay marathon with zero grip on reality. Academic gaslighting at its finest.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Im writing ANOTHER review because the final in this class is so difficult for no reason - she makes no sense when she structures the questions, the short questions with 5 mins each ask 15 different things from you, and the 'long' ones ask one and take 5 minutes. like help. don't take this class.

She is genuinely the worst professor I've had at NYU. She insists that we need to take notes in her class to get a good grade in the exams yet her lectures are practically incoherent. She claims to teach in a diverse way when in reality she is just obsessed with Indian theatre. The only reason I am able to pass this class is because of the TA Annie

She uses incredibly bizarre anecdotes and phrases to explain anything and everything and it makes every confused+uncomfortable. Also, she tries to incorporate theatre from other cultures - not in a thoughtful way. Also, the way she structures class is not helpful. I think she means well but avoid her classes if possible. free Annie fr

Erin Mee creates an environment of fear within her students. She has been known to call you out in the middle of a lecture, if she does not like your behavior. She loves Indian theatre and culture to a strange extent. She is white. However, she can be negotiated with and she has a caring side. Her TA, Annie, was very helpful. Free Annie.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: erin mee creates a tense environment.. her classes are more stressful than they need to be. she is a little weird about indian theatre and she really tries to be ethnic,, her TA does most of the grading. would not take another class of hers.

Couldn't wait until the end of my semester with her to describe how terrible this class was. We learned absolutely nothing about theatre production, though she claims we do by learning about other stuff (meaning just her fascination with Indian theatre). She can't take criticism at all. Didn't have a choice but to take her class. Sorry to all.
she's mean, and self focused, and i hated her.

Does not actually teach theater production at all and creates ridiculous standards for note taking and grading, which she does not do herself, by expecting students to give the exact answer in the exact phrasing she uses. Has no consideration for our time or our note taking which is ironic considering that is the most important part of her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mee does not teach what she wants us to know she just shows off her knowledge the entire time. She makes us feel belittled by making “jokes” as she calls them. She always talks to us like we are freaking out when she's the one that needs to chill. She always says we need to save the “panic attacks” for later. She doesn't sit well with me.

Erin Mee is terrible. She doesn't care about access needs (from personal and friend experience), she has boring lectures and talks down to us like we are in middle school, and she gives no guidance on her fast responses which then leads to 0's. Awful experience. I will go out of my way to never take a class with her again.
worst teacher i've ever had by far

Here's the thing I can understand why people struggle with her, because she's tough. She will call you out in front of everyone for eating in class or whispering to someone or something else relatively inoffensive. However she really cares about the process of learning and she is really trying to ensure that you get as much out of it as possible.

I feel so strongly about this, that I am submitting now once I realized my review from last year didn't go through. Aside from being spoken down to more than any teacher I've ever had, ridiculed for asking questions and more, this class did not leave me with anything substantial. My time was wasted on a subject I was previously excited about.

She is genuinely one of the sweetest and most kind professors I know. She is very and I mean very knowledgable on her stuff and she is in fact a hard professor, but she always wants the best for her students. I would 100% recommend the class.
she sucks straight up doesn't understand students

Supposed to be an INTRO class. Erin is a borderline ableist teacher who goes by the rule every hour in class, is five hours of work out of class. She pretty much fetishizes Japanese and Sanskrit theatre, be ready to cringe. You're allowed 2 absences before your grade goes down a letter. Best part is the shared trauma you and your peers will have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers I've ever had.

Do not take digital theatre. I repeat. DO NOT TAKE IT. I wasted an entire semester because this was the only class that worked with my time zone. What did I learn you ask? Nothing. Absolutely nothing. The best part about this course was watching myself and my classmates make a fool out of ourselves during projects. Don't do it. Please. I beg you!!!

Oh got do not take a class with Ms. Mee. She is all over the place, biased and unfair, will not take responsibility for her mistakes but will shame you in front of the whole class for yours. She is living in her own privileged bubble and has no idea how useless her classes are. Should not be teaching IMO because she only assigns her own stuff.

She assisted me two times with an assignment, and after I asked for help the third time she said I could no longer ask her any questions again, and that there were "other people to help" and I would have to figure out the rest on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very offensive. Tries to preach tolerance and then fetishizes the "exotic" works she teaches.
my friend quoted one thing she said in class in my paper, and she accused himof plagiarism

Didn't get my first semester grade until the beginning of second semester. I would not recommend taking a class with Erin Mee. She is extremely pretentious and gives a lot (A LOT) of readings. Found myself painfully counting the minutes until class was over every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Mee is so, so knowledgeable in the course, and she comes to class with such enthusiasm for whatever she's teaching that day. However, she gives far more work than should be given for the level of class. Most of the grade for her class is from participation, so talk in class (it's mostly opinion based conversations) and you'll do fine.

Actually took a Rasa class of hers. There was no set syllabus, the hw changed all the time, the entire course was fueled by questions not answers. Few in the class can actually grasp the content. The worst class I've taken at NYU besides Writing the Essay. Also hates if you're late (god forbid miss class) but she's late all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A large percent of your grade is based on one paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Intro to Theatre Studies -awful class. Makes you read her own readings that she wrote, and then write about live performances in a high school defined style with no freedom of writing. Doesn't take blame for anything if concerns comes up in class and has no empathy for anything when you try talk to her one on one about any genuine personal issue.

I LOVED Drama in Performance! Such a great class! Basically, you go to a different show every week, write a 400-word paper about it, then sit around and talk about the performance in the next class. It's definitely a participation heavy course, but so worth it! Wish I could take it again! No tests, only papers. Extra credit offered.

Not a fun class. Come parts were interesting, but the curriculum was mostly scattered. Very long class. Tries to make it a "conversation", but this is difficult in a class with at least 50 people. A lot of reading, some of it is her own writing. Would not recommend. Very passionate, but poor planning.

She's a nice lady and she's extremely knowledgeable - you really get the sense she knows her stuff. As for the class however, it's not at all easy. (It's more about performance than literature.) There is no textbook, but a dense amount of reading regularly required and she's a harsh grader. You'll have a hard time staying focused in class.

With the title "Introduction to Dramatic Literature", one would assume we'd be studying literature. Nope, the class was all over the place. One week we would look at optical illusions, the next week we would cut up news papers and to make poems. There are pop quizzes every week and it's difficult to stay awake during class, because it is SO BORING!

One of the worst classes I have ever taken. The teacher treats you like a 5th grader giving homework quizzes every week and making essays follow a 5 paragraph essay format instead of higher level college writing. The expectations for assignments are never clear and she keeps changing what it says on the syllabus in terms of what she wants.

The class was not at all what I expected. One would expect the class to be readings on plays but instead it was more a history of theatre. To add to this the professor often assigns papers topics which are very vague and open to interpretation. She also focuses too much on the stylisation of the paper and not on the topic/content itself.

She made me rewrite a paper because she didn't like my style of writing. She assigns unrealistic amounts of reading (you'd think you'd read plays in a Dramatic Lit class but for the most part you don't). You have to answer questions at the beginning of the class on reading that was basically unfathomable. Nice lady--don't take the class though.

I did not like this course. the course is listed as being an Introduction to DRAMATIC LITERATURE (Literature being the key word). I expected to be reading plays such as Shakespeare and Brecht, etc. Instead I found myself reading huge texts on memory neurons and medieval life which bore little to no legitimate relevance to the course. BORING. AWFUL

Theories of Acting/Directing was easily one of the best classes I've taken. Erin is extremely knowledgeable & helpful; class grade is 50% attendance/participation and 50% a term paper that is worked on all semester. Anyone with a fairly solid background in theatre/performance studies will love this class!
Not a hard class but average is so high and messing up once can kill your shot for an A. Stern curve so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad curve, If you mess up 1 test you lost your shot at an A. Group project is ok but random attendance, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Only 2 quizzes (both of which were open-note). Group project and in class participation/attendance heavily matters so make sure you don't miss class. Truly the best professor I have had at nyu. Take her for an easy A
The best professor ever, GOAT of Marketing department.

Responsible and caring teacher!  BEST prof I've met
Whenever students have questions, she patiently takes the time to explain. Also she thoughtfully recaps the previous lesson, helping us deepen our understanding
She said she will always open notes for exams, cuz she said we can search when we work after all, so why not be kind to students!

Prof. Hogan might seem strict at the beginning because she spoke fast and sounded uncompromising, but actually she is nice. She appreciated all our opinions and respected everyone's voice. Her weekly journal assignments seemed tough, but she graded them quite leniently. I got all A's on the assignments and got an A in the end.

She is one of the kindest, passionate, and inclusive professors that you will ever meet! Her syllabus literally has all the details, dates, explanations for the readings and assignments. Class is more discussion based but often among small groups/partner. She really values hearing your experience and connections to the lessons. 100% worth it!

Great professor! Her classes are very discussion heavily but you will be fine and if you contribute regularly you will get an A in participation easily. She gives the clearest rubric on everything and is just so nice and kind. She is fair and friendly to all students but it is hard for her to remember your name if you have a foreign name.
weird......

She is awesome and knows her stuff. Fast engaging lectures and no tests but definitely homework. I love that she is outspoken but sometimes it was sometimes overwhelming with the amount of correct political terms. I was never bored though.

Easy A if you just pay attention and participate in class. She really cares about students, pay attention and respects their opinions, and was the first professor who remember my culture on name preference. One of the best prof and highly recommended.

This lady is the epitome of the woke mind virus at NYU. She polices the language of students and even deducted points from my work for not using the most up to date politically correct terminology. If you take her class, simply use every liberal buzzword and she will give you great grades. As a POC, I also felt like she has a white savior complex

Would definitely take the course again! Clear grading criteria, inspirational lectures, and she truly cares about her students. She reads your response and gives thoughtful feedbacks. The workload is not very light, but the readings are not long, and as long as you pay attention in class, you will be fine.
She's really nice! While I was not a big fan of turning the cameras on during certain times in class I did learn a lot.
very good prof
Very organized and easy grading. would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elizabeth is an amazing professor who cares about her students and their future as academic writers. While the class is difficult and is more strictly graded, she makes sure that you are set up for success in future college classes. Personally, I did not enjoy the material of the progressions, but she was always there and provided great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very fair and accommodating + super organized and structured. content is not super interesting for first two progressions, personally. homework is pretty easy, takes

Elisabeth made this class fun and enjoyable! 2 papers make up 70% of your grades but are relatively easy as you choose your own topics to write about. She makes you go through peer feedback and one-on-one meetings to check in with her. She is very caring and open, please ask for support when you need it. Short readings, little homework and amazing!

Very fair class, always show up prepared to class as your participation and what not is a good part of what brings your grade up if you don't do as well on the essays. Very easy to talk to outside class just shoot and email and see will provide feedback or help you out. They care about student well-being and make it simple to ask for extentiontime.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Elisabeth is an accommodating professor that will help with anything as long as you communicate. Sometimes her feedback on papers can be given close to a deadline and a bit nitpicky about concepts and structure. That being said, I would still take the course again, she genuinely cares about her students.
Gives clear feedback, very little homework. Only two papers and was always open to meet outside of class/help you with your work. She's very lenient with giving extensions.
She has a very understanding perspective on students' busy lives and her feedback is very clear. Her essay assignments are open-ended and students can choose to write about topics that interest them.

I didn't have prog Fay for a class but went to her for my writing center appointment. She was AWESOME. Gave so many really good and thoughtful feedbacks, and was able to hold a conversation with me that guided me and gave me inspiration on things I was stuck on. Highly recommend her for the writing center!

AMAZING!! I had her first semester freshman year, and she is such a caring and funny professor. Extremely accessible outside of class and always gives very precise and helpful feedback! Her assignments were very clear and always helpful for the final essay. Definitely take her! She is probably one of the best NYU professors; I would take her again!

The absolute best professor I have ever had. She's incredibly caring and understanding of her students. And considering that it's a writing class, her lectures are actually so useful and helpful. Gives incredibly helpful feedback, as well.
Amazing professor, only two 6-8 page essays and annotating short readings graded by completion. Very accessible and helpful professor when helping formulate essays.

Elisabeth is hands down one of my favorite professors at NYU. It is required for me to take Advanced College Essay and Elisabeth made the entire experience extremely comfortable and enjoyable. She is super open-minded, kind, and truly cares about your academic growth AND personal well-being. TAKE HER CLASS!

I loved her so much. The reading is heavy, but the content combined with her helpful feedback will really help improve your writing. Get help when needed, participate, and you'll do great! I would highly recommend taking her class especially since it's usually required!
Elizabeth was a fantastic Writing the Essay professor. I genuinely loved the class.
Elisabeth was perpetually peppy and engaging, even when the energy in the room was at rock bottom. Her advice was constructive and helped me significantly as a writer.

Take this class. Elisabeth is hands down one of the most caring professors I've had the pleasure of having so far  at NYU. She is always willing to go out of her way to help students who come to her for help, whether that's setting up an office hours appointment or granting additional extension hours on top of the ones given to every student.

Elisabeth is truly amazing, and I could not recommend taking her class for WTE/ACE enough. She was able to make a class as dreadful as a required writing course entertaining and somewhat enjoyable. She also is extremely caring and is always willing to make accommodations to meet her students' needs.TAKE HER CLASS, you won't regret it!

Amazing is an understatement to describe my time in Elisabeth's class as a student! She is so sweet and understanding, and the work was thought-provoking. I can genuinely say that walking out of this class, I feel more confident in myself as a writer, and she was always willing to help out. If you can take her class, please do!

Elisabeth is one of the most caring professors I've had; she is extremely understanding and respectful of students' time, even has a "grace period" on almost all due dates for this reason. The class is engaging and makes you think, and her feedback on essays really does help you improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely recommend taking Elisabeth's class! WTE can easily be a dreadful class, but Elisabeth's class is so well organized that the workload doesn't feel overwhelming at all. She's very caring, understanding, and super accessible to students during and outside of class. I wouldn't say this class is an easy A, but it's definitely obtainable.

TAKE THIS CLASS! She is so aware of students' needs & gives great accommodations  she lets you rewrite a paper at the end of the semester, and is very understanding/generous with extensions. Feedback is clear & I def improved as a writer. If you do the assignments, follow her feedback, and go to office hours once or twice, you'll get an A.

Great teacher! Cares about your writing and is understanding towards her student's workload. She definitely grades your writing so it is not an easy A class but as long as you do the work you should be fine.

Elizabeth is a very understanding professor. Probably one of the nicest ones in my whole career in NYU. She specifically adjusts her leniency when noticing a student is really struggling and is super nice and cool. Leaves easy to read feedback on essays and there is no chance of a bad grade if you do all the work and attend class. Would recommend!

Take this class!!!! My favorite professor as a first sem freshman during COVID and online learning. Went out of her way to make accommodations for students and really made them felt seen/appreciated. You will have to work hard on essays but if you put in the work and address her feedback you will do well.
The class (WTE) can be a pain during drafting and editing, but she provides the tools to make it much simpler (and better.) Your writing will improve.

Professor Fay is a true gem. I was going through a lot during my semester in her class and she was always SUPER understanding! Leaves very clear comments on your work and structures homework in a way that you are not writing your entire essay the night before. The class is quite a bit of reading but it's expected from a writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is SO nice and caring. She gives out a lot of optional extension time for papers throughout the semester with no penalty and gives great feedback. I would definitely recommend taking ACE with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Fay prepared students for essay writing with many guiding exercises. She provided feedback for all of the exercises and drafts and made you think about issues in a deeper way, questioning motivations and cultural expectations / norms. She made expository writing enjoyable and interesting. Take Professor Fay if you can!! She's great

I've taken two of her writing classes and can honestly say she is the best. I've heard of tough professors, but Elisabeth is very fair and straight forward. She has helped me grown as a writer. Her class isn't difficult, you just got to put in some effort and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Elisabeth Fay her classes were great and super enjoyable. Classwork is manageable and she's really good about not letting anything build up. I wouldn't say its an easy A, but if you go to office hours and take her comments to your work seriously you can do well. She's really accessible and always responds if you ever need her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good choice for WTE. The exercises she makes you do before writing an actual essay are really helpful, and she's good at meeting with you out of class. It isn't an easy A, you may think you're a good writer and end up with a B+/A-, but it feels satisfying, and as if I've learned something from the course.

She gives good feedback on your essays, and as long as you put in a lot of effort into your papers and show improvement, you'll receive the grade you deserve! My writing really improved while taking her class, and I totally recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Everyone must experience a class with Fatiha you have not lived until you have. She is the sweetest, most caring soul on this planet. Just trust me. Take her. You will do well. No need for a long comment. Just trust me.

She is so unbelievably sweet, and such an amazing professor. I cannot stand language classes but I enjoyed and was excited to learn French. The class is a lot of work for sure but you will learn French. Cannot recommend enough.

She's the best French professor at NYU. If you can, take her! Intensive courses can be bit much in terms of the course load but she is extremely understanding and somehow makes you look forward to morning classes. Attendance matters A LOT so be present and on time, it all counts for participation.
I love Professor Bali's class! She makes it so interactive and fun! Highly recommend for anyone who is looking to improve their French and learn more in a caring environment.

Professor Bali has been my favorite professor my entire time at NYU. She is so sweet and always goes the extra mile. She is always there to help and is very understanding. She wants you to do well and I want to do well in French because I want her to be proud. J'adore le professeur Bali et à cause d'elle, j'adore le français. Take her if you can.

Prof. Bali is the best!! If you struggle in French- take her class. She genuinely wants you to do well, so just show up and ask for help when you need it. She is very kind and wants to help you learn French. I enjoyed her class and actually improved in French, without google translate.

One of my fav profs ever. I never liked taking foreign language classes in hs and was never good at learning a language but prof bali makes me want to become fluent in french. I wish I took her earlier in college bc then I would 100% major in french.
An actual queen. So caring, cool, and dedicated. Everyone in the class loves her.

I took Fatihas class in the first semester of my college life and she was just AMAZING! Nothing seemed to be hard as long as she teaches me. If I have the chance I would definitely take her classes again. I miss this wonderful teacher and her class so much.
I loved having Fatiha as my French prof. She truly helped me enjoy learning the language and often cracked jokes or played funny videos to keep us entertained. So sweet and so caring, she is amazing!

Professor Bali is an amazing professor. I had the class 2x a week for 2 hrs but it was never a burden! The class is super chill. When I had it it was in Lipton lounge and she would bring in croissants/pastries when we had exams. She is super understanding and you can email her about anything!!

I love Fatiha so much!!!! She is literally the best professor. Soooo understanding and really wants her students to do well. She brings us croissants on test days and is just an ANGEL. She really does an amazing job teaching french to students who are struggling and helping those who need it

Croissants on test days, SNL videos at the end of class, and a teacher who will make you laugh. She uses the textbook in class but also writes extra on the board for tougher grammar. Favorite class of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Intensive Elementary French with Fatiha Bali was my favorite class of the semester. She genuinely cares about her students and makes hard French concepts easy to learn. She makes an effort to make classes enjoyable (and usually brings croissants on test days). AMAZING PROFESSOR

Fatiha was by far my favorite french teacher ever. She made learning fun and would encourage everyone to participate. Everyone should take this class! on quiz days she brought croissants for the class !

The nicest, most understanding and helpful professor I have ever had. During the hardest semester of my life she was the only teacher who showed any hint of understanding and that I really felt wanted me to do well. You do have to put in work to do well but the tests & assignments are all reasonable. I learned a lot and I will miss her :)

Really nice professor, had such interesting readings, though can be quite a lot sometimes, but they really gives you a comprehensive knowledge and depth towards East Asian Nobel Prize literature, raising critical questions, debatable topics, and having good analytical writing practices. He is very encouraigng and accessible, super sweet too!
He is good but there are four papers in a semster, be ready to read different books or articals every week but it is an easy class btw. If you follow him everey week you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: He is good, but is ready to read the paper every week. There are four papers in total, but each paper is relatively easy to complete. As long as you attend class and read carefully, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The strictest professor, without a doubt, has no exams but has extremely high requirements for the essay. You can't consult any other materials and must write entirely based on the text he provides. Moreover, he is a very, very, very harsh grader. Run away as soon as you see him!!

Prof. Foley had the best method of any prof I've had of ensuring we did readings and watched the films without aggressive cold calling: we would all write discussion posts that would become the basis of our in-class discussion. I enjoyed his nuanced explanations of modern Chinese history.

TA does all the grading on papers and pop quizzes and grading was NOT friendly. Reading is very heavy and they could be boring. Professor Foley is passionate about cinema but the course is not organized and it's hard to systematically understand Chinese cinema after this course. I would say only take this if you are genuinely interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Professor Todd's Cinema class. It's really a very relaxing course that we watch a Chinese movie together weekly. This course truly allowed me to learn about the refreshing cinematic and cultural knowledge that I had never considered before. The professor is a very nice and empathetic person. I highly recommend this class.

Professor Foley is definitely very interested in what he teaches, but he sort of expects his students to have this same passion as well. Readings are SO heavy - we literally were assigned like a 500-page book to read over a few days multiple times last semester. If you aren't interested in the topic don't take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very inspiring class! Professor is kind as usual. There are three responses required in around 1000 words and a 10-pages final essay. There is also a translation workshop/presentation needed. But over all, very recommended.
Not an easy A. You must work for this class but it is very entertaining and well taught!
Professor Foley is great. Great professor, great guy. Readings are heavy sometimes but he's very accessible through office hours and very kind. Highly recommend :)

The way this class worked was a mixture of theory readings and novels/short stories. Some of the readings are pretty thick. Some probably won't take more than an hour. There are two 5 page papers, plus a 10-15 page paper at the end. Professor Foley will give you feedback on paper topics. Readings are a mix bag for interest. Overall decent class.

It turns out to be my favorite class of the first semester! Firstly, the class requires participation. Students who do finish the readings could really enjoy the class. Secondly, there's no extra quiz for classes. Last but not least, Professor Todd Foley is very humorous and caring. He shows great appreciation when students have extra researches.
Todd is a nice guy.

He's not really hard, but it's stressful. You will NEVER know what your grade is. He doesn't talk about modernity. It was chemistry. Changed syllabus/grading 3 weeks before the end. SO disorganized; nobody knows anything about our assignments or what is expected. He just wants to see u care, so have a general idea of readings, talk A LOT, and pray.

He is a really sweet guy, and he's very educated on what he's talking about; however, he strays completely from what Global Works classes are supposed to be, and instead, we spent the semester learning about Biomimetics and AI usage. He is super disorganized and it makes it kind of stressful on students. But he will do what he can to help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please. Please. whatever you do do not take this professor. He is the most disorganised person you will ever meet. I nearly cried at multiple points throughout the semester because he randomly created an announcement that I could not make head or tail of, the night before the class.Very unclear assignments, cannot stick to his own syllabus,

A knowledgeable professor who brings a lot of energy to the classroom. You really need to love the subject matter to keep up with him. There is some reading involved, but not an overwhelming amount; it's not like 1,000 pages a week. While he is a tough grader, he is also understanding and offers students a chance to improve their work.

He is a chill and nice guy, but sometimes the course just gets really unclear. Whether its about the grading, or due dates, or what he is saying in his lectures. 
You can take the course and do okay... its just average.

Very chill guy and the content is pretty interesting. However, it took forever to get prompts and even longer to get grades. I only got 3 grades from him (w/ very little feedback) despite how much we did. Lectures are long, but survivable. This class is not worth the unnecessary stress was caused by his lack of communication and organization.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible, rude, and uninformative.

He was a really nice and down-to-earth guy. He was just a really tough grader, and assigned really difficult assignments, with very UNCELAR directions. He also takes a while to post assignments and by the time he does you have a few days to complete them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unclear Grading scale, Does Everything last minute. Don't take him unless you have to. The only upside is he gives entertaining lectures
shi

funny, passionate, and nice but all over the place! he pulls assignments out of thin air and takes forever to grade! added on to my stress during the semester especially with two 10 page papers given to us a week before they were due. if you really love philosophy take him. if not, DO NOT!!!

Readings are extremely long and time consuming as well as last minute 10 page papers before breaks. You will not know where you stand in his class as he does not grade anything until the very last second. Lectures are dry and disengaging. I still do not know my midterm or final grade in his class and it is already the second semester.

reviews.comment: Might be easier than others, but no consistency. If you care about philosophy then take his class, otherwise avoid! He's silly, caring, but hard to follow and all over the place. No clear assignment schedule so might randomly have a quiz or paper. Returns grades months late or not at all. Time consuming and long papers. No motivation to be there

reviews.comment: submttd big assgnmnt sept22 n received grade dec10, class based on abstract concepts, impossible 2 understand if ur doing things right until he returns grades 2 late(@ very end of sem). makes it impossible 2 improve, lectures dry, boring, not attention grasping, confines students to ither getting it from the start or never understanding the class.
