reviews.comment: -not a good professor. if you actually want to learn something , dont take him. he goes off topic all the time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you're really into philosophy and like to read tons, don't take him. He was nice but I didn't understand what was going on the entire semester. We didn't really have many assignments and the goals of the class were unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to have some laughs in class, then definitely take this class! If you want to know your grade, what is going on, and what you are being graded on, then you should steer away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His grading scale is very unclear, somehow it's a B or C. The midterm grade may be an A, and the final and final grade becomes a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aside from the negatives, there are many bright sides to taking his courses. He is a very forgiving grader, and dropped our two lowest assignment grades from the final grade calculation. The course content is also very interesting, but active participation is required if you want to make the most of it. He is also passionate about what he teaches.
He is a nice person but his class is disorganized and boring. It was an easy A but I basically learned nothing in his class.

I took him for liberal studies core classes twice and he was such a fun teacher. He assigns a lot of readings but he goes over all of it in class and you only have a few hw assignments the whole semester. And most importantly he's a super caring and passionate teacher. If you raise your hand and answer a question he gets so genuinely happy.

Professor Mahootian can be disorganized at times, but his lectures are amazing. His lectures are funny, interesting and he really tries to be likeable by students and encourages you to ask questions otherwise you would feel dumb asking. Papers can be extensive, but he is open to answer any questions you have and provide you with feedback.
Worst professor I have ever had. EVER. So disorganized, mean to the students, and took so long to grade I had no idea how I was doing until 2/3 weeks before the semester ended. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor Mahootian is a wildly intelligent man, you can see it in the way he speaks. However, he is incredibly disorganized. He often went on tangents in lectures, changed due dates or assignment criteria, and was very slow to grade. I didn't have any knowledge of my standing in the class until he released midterm grades and the same with finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his Science of Tech class. The reading material and his views on the philosophy of technology are fascinating (if you're interested in that sort of thing). He's flexible w/ assignments, easy to talk to, and genuinely interested in what he teaches. Only negative was his unclear grading criteria (although his grading was lenient and flexible).
Okay, Prof. Mahootian's class was all over the place. If you are an organized person, avoid his social foundation's classes. Is he passionate, yes, but I am not entirely sure what we learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As a 4.0 student trust me: the worst professor you will ever come across. Complete inability to speak coherently and extraordinarily late to grade anything. It's almost impressive how his prompts can be interpreted in at least 4 different ways due to his horrible grammar and misuse of words. No regard for student interest, rambling on for hours.

Mahootian is such a genius and seeing himself get lost in his own thoughts is one of my favorite things about his class. Studying and following instructions will get you a good grade and he's always available to talk outside of class if needed. A super cool guy that will talk to you about anything and is very funny/lovable

This man single-handedly my first semester GPA. This isn't a class where you can work hard to get an A. If you aren't good at philosophy, even if you're willing to learn, you won't get a good grade. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rambles. Completely philosophy based. If you aren't good/into that do not take this class. One of the hardest classes Ive ever taken.

His lectures are convoluted and he goes on many tangents. Had three graded assignments total the entire semester: a 20 point quiz and two longer essays. I was not able to get any feedback on my last essay, he didn't give any comments. I have no clue why I got the grade that I did. He is passionate about his class, however.

The paper I submitted in the third week of the semester was returned to me with two weeks left in the semester. This made it impossible to know how I was doing in the class. The only written assignments we had were the first paper and a 10 page final paper. Being graded on two things makes it much harder. I would give him a 0 if I could.

Super intelligent. laughs at his own jokes, can't bring the class to match wits with him. You can just be on ur laptop when he talks in class he wouldn't care. But u'll see he's actually a genius if u keep up with him. Super layback too, flexible with deadlines. Very openminded and caring. Only wrote 2 papers and a worksheet for this class

It is hard to follow Prof. Mahootian's thoughts during his lectures. Although he is incredibly passionate when teaching the class, and genuinely cares for his students, understanding the course material is often confusing. There is an incredible amount of reading for his class, and the text is usually very dense, and dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Farzad is interested and knowledgable in the material. BUT his class is confusing, grade boundaries no clear, and he discusses too much heavy content all at once so you leave the class confused and overwhelmed. Grades aren't really known until the end. If you take him, go to office hours for extra help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Loved him. Tough grader and rambles, but so sweet. I used to love going to office hours just to talk to him, he's so brilliant! He lets you rewrite papers and take quizzes you miss. The final is a take home. Work hard, go to office hours, and you'll get an A.

I did not like it at all. Lectures are very dry, texts hard to understand. I did not learn anything useful in his class. He might seem funny at first but it is really hard to follow his thoughts. So think twice before taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The best SF teacher. Loved the class material and he really knows how to teach well. Interesting lectures too.

He's super passionate about philosophy and what he's teaching, which is great! But as the other reviews have said, his lectures tend to just go on and on and you'll realize that you have no idea what he's talking about anymore. His readings are also a pain in the ass at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the course, however difficult to follow. The coursework is relatively unorganized which makes it difficult to complete his often vague essay prompts and test questions. Very easy to get lost in the course's material, doesn't need a lot of effort but demands attention. Very nice and funny guy and available during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a really passionate man, but is extremely confusing. He provides no clarity on the lectures, rambles incessantly, and takes months to return a paper. Although he is cool and funny, I would never, for the life of me, take this awful class again. So many papers. Very harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: i really do appreciate how passionate he is about philosophy. however, his lectures are extremely confusing and he tends to ramble on and on, jumping from topic to topic without clarification. sure he's funny and entertaining, but i wouldnt take his class again if someone paid me! going to class is a waste of time cause i dont understand anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Mahootian is really nice and cool, but he is a tough grader - he looks for very specific answers. One thing I did really like about him was that he was always open to help me during office hours with correcting my answers and you could rewrite every single essay to get a better grade. But beware, he rambles on and on in class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Philosophy of physics/chemistry/sciences (he was a philosophy/chemistry major and references science in class often), philosophy of religion, epistemology. If you don't like writing about these things and/or can't write coherently on these topics, this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You either love him or you don't. While he is funny, passionate, & knowledgeable, I did not enjoy his class. His bi-weekly reading quizzes are so specific. His essay prompts are too vague & he is a really harsh grader. However, he does lets you resubmit. Also, if you are not the slightest bit interested in philosophy this is NOT the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is an amazing teacher! very inspiring and fun. Highly approachable and understanding!

He's very confusing. He might be a funny guy, but he's not that great at teaching the material, if there even is one. Half the time, I'm completely confused by the class, no matter how hard I read the text. The essays are also really open - as in you can literally write about anything and everything and that's not a good thing in a freshman class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: good guy; gotta meet him in office hours if you like the philosophy of science. I see a lot of people who arent too into Plato and Phil though so if you not interested in philosophy, you probably wont enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's a fun guy and a good person, but can be very confusing. His lectures can be hard to follow, but he is easy to approach and will try to help you whenever you ask for it. Yes it is confusing, but that is the case with all SF class. With Mahootian the time you spend in the classroom would be entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's really confusing, but so is the work. If you want to do well in the class, do the readings and go to his office hours if you don't understand them. He gives quizzes a lot in the beginning but then stops after mid-terms. He's super helpful, but you have to ask for it. Not a lot of papers, the tests questions are often taken right from the HW.

Professor Mahootian is one the best professors I've had at NYU. His discussions of philosophy were outstanding, the work is relevant and balanced. His lectures are entertaining, interesting, engaging. We started Day 1 by watching Monty Python's Meaning of Life. You'll love class with him. And if he's still doing Tea & Philosophy, do it.

Yes, the class is confusing, but that's the material, not the professor. Mahootian is honestly one of the more helpful professors I've had this year. He really wants you to succeed. If you're having trouble on an essay, go to office hours, and he will help you SO MUCH. He even allows revisions. He's truly a nice guy & is very passionate.

He is an intelligent man who is passionate about his subject. However, he is very CONFUSING. There is A LOT of reading assigned. He tends to talk about the material as if you already know what it is. You must READ CAREFULLY because he gives QUIZZES often. His essay prompts are COMPLICATED. He's also a HARSH essay grader.

He's a little kooky, but very intelligent. Lectures can be dry--I didn't pay attention most of the time. The class is super easy though, and the content itself is pretty interesting if you're into philosophy.

Cool, interesting guy but his lectures are extremely confusing. He talks about the material as if you already know it therefore doesn't go in depth and assumes you understand everything, making it easy to get lost and feel inferior for not understanding.

I was confused for 80% of SFI. You go over confusing philosophical topics and most of the professors explanations are even more confusing. Not a bad professor just hard to understandnot very helpful. The essay prompts are beyond confusing. Just trying to figure out what you are expected to write is almost harder than writing the actual essay.
Without a doubt the worst teacher I've ever had, and that's saying something.
Just don't.
Do not take his class if you know what's good for you!!!!!!!
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! He may be nice and funny but the readings are incredibly confusing and he doesn't help much in explaining. Clearly plays favorites and also grades unfairly.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! Mahootian is "funny" for the first day but he uses this as a trap. He's passive aggressive and doesn't let you go to the bathroom or use laptops in class. He picks dry, difficult readings and assigns hard essays. He will grade you poorly if you don't use flowery language/agree with him. Totally useless class.

He's hilarious!  Loves to make jokes and have some fun in class, he gets bored simply lecturing.  However, his SciTech class was pretty difficult considering the concepts.  He's very understanding though - a good professor to have overall.

Professor Mahootian is an incredibly engaging teacher. Although he often goes off topic, he is always bringing up different topics and theories that are not in the textbook. You need to be genuinely interested in the class in order to really appreciate what he teaches. So long as you work hard in the class, you should be fine.

This professor is the funniest and most interesting. You have to see him in office hours, talk to him in between classes, and raise your hand sometimes. If you make the effort and put yourself out there, he will reward you. However, he is super paranoid about computers, so look up every once in a while so he isn't suspicious of you. HE is the man!
Completely useless class. I only go to class  for attendance. Can't care to listen if he doesn't care to grade fairly. That's all I have to say

At first, I thought his class would be good because he's goofy, friendly and tries to be funny. However, his class has become completely useless. He's all over the place, picks the driest texts (which I think he likes just because they confuse and bore everyone) and always gives last minute flowery assignments.

His teaching style places emphasis on actually getting the kids to learn, through discussion, not merely regurgitate a textbook. I love his class, it's pretty easy but also enjoyable if you try to participate!

Farzad's really nice, goofy clumbsy, but a poor prof. He also teaches philosophy & spends most of class lecturing on material that doesn't relate to class. When you ask simple questions it takes him forever to respond. It's very difficult to understand what he wants in essays, etc. and his responses are convoluted. Not a hard class, but a lot of BS

Dr. Mahootian is an extremely nice man. He gets off topic very often, but he's always talking about science or philosophy and always with a smile on his face. Very approachable, also. He was very unorganized, but he really likes what he does, and he wants everyone to do well. Don't be afraid to ask him questions and to go to his office hours.

Not a good professor. A nice guy who used to work at NASA, but not clear or interesting and not really an easy A either. Found myself waiting for class to end every time. Going to his class three times a week was dreadful.

Really, really hard class; left every class completely confused and frustrated. Not a science person? Avoid Mahootian. Gets off topic VERY easily, and ends up talking about things not in the curriculum, which he decides to add to the test. Takes on much more than he can handle.

Seriously, Mahootian is the best. He's funny and weird (in a good way), keeps you engaged and makes you REALLY think about things. Had him last semester for HOU and this semester for SFII. You really do learn things in class and he really values what you have to say--it's refreshing to have a professor that actually cares.

I had Professor Mahootian for History of the Universe. He could get off topic really easily, but I always left class knowing something new. The midterm and final weren't bad at all, especially if you paid attention in class. He worked with students who needed it, and overall made a class that would have sucked really cool.
Kuaiii pao jiarenmen
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Foley at the Writing Center was incredibly helpful and kind. He reviewed every word of my essay and provided detailed feedback. During the discussion, he discussed my ideas with me and documented our discussions and give it to me afterward. His  questions helped me better structure the logic of my writing, which I found truly inspiring.

You have so much homework every class that doesn't even contribute to your essay. all of the lectures are long and boring and filled with things I knew since middle school. I can imagine him being a good teacher to someone who needs help learning how to write but if you have these skills already the class is just painful.

Professor Foley's classes were well structured and clear- he always had a concept or idea for us to focus on each class. His feedback is helpful and he created a good atmosphere in the class. Although difficult, I feel that my writing, comprehension, and thinking skills have improved immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dont take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From the beginning, class was always super engaging and David was passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He fostered a fun but hard-working classroom environment, which was very conducive to work. He gives a moderate amount of work, less than other teachers, and always gives great feedback. Grading is very fair, great class overall!

You definitely have to put in the work when it comes to this class. He gives really great feedback and he really takes the time to read and reread your work. He makes himself very available if you need any help outside class whether that be with finding sources or figuring out the topic of your essay.

I know this keeps getting said but he changed the way I write. I think he's either a hit or miss professor. It can be quite a bit of work at certain times and it can be a bit repetetive to some people which is why everyone may not like him. However the work eventually builds up and if you actually try in the class essay writing becomes easier.

David Foley changed the way I think about writing. He negotiated a perfect balance between work with specific technical elements and allowing for abundant creative freedom. The homework is, I believe, about the average for this course; but it is RIDICULOUSLY helpful. The class may be a bit dry, but it is worth it for such excellent instruction.

tbh the whole expository writing program does not make a lot of sense. You will barely write like this in your other classes. Professor Foley made this whole thing even tougher. Lectures are boring. He assigns hws every class, and most of them are not what you are passionate about. Grading is ok, but I did not gain a lot from the class.

Foley is a teacher that you must put in the work in order to gain from this class. If you arent willing to write a lot in the beginning then this probably isn't the class for you. Although I will say, his homework can be a little overwhelming but when its time to write the paper, you technically have written a good amount of it beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Foley is a teacher that will force the work out of you. If you are not ready to work ie. write, read and write some more. He probably won' be a great choice for you. Also there were many times when I was confused with the criteria but Foley does conferences for each essay and they were extremely helpful. Overall eye-opening experience of my growth

David is very accessible outside of class and will give you extra hope if you want to It. The homework, although it is more than the Usual, it helps you in the end when you were constructing the essay drafts. Amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Okay heres the deal, yes theres homework but it kinda therapeutic to write in a starbucks nearby. Its not even a lot, all the people commenting are slackers. You can easily finish an essay over a weekend without stressing because he gives really good feedback and individual attention. Sometimes class is a bore but hes GREAT!!!! Pls take

David Foley is a wonderful professor. He gives you good notes on essay drafts that help you develop your ideas more thoroughly. The exercises We do in class are very helpful and they are not just busy, irrelevant work. I have grown so much as a writer in his class. He is amazing. Definitely recommend as a professor.

-will make you a better writer but you're gonna have to actually try -do all the assignments and hit the requirements for your paper and you'll be fine -participate every now and then -bit of a stickler on attendance but if you reach out about illness he's a bit flexible -Nice, but will give you a bad grade if you don't do the work

Go in ready to learn, don't feel bad when he tells you don't know as much as you thought (he's right.) The only way to do well is to participate and do all the assignments. No BSing your way through. Very flexible with late assignments & missing class provided you have a good reason and are participating in class. He will challenge you!

After starting my second semester with a new teacher i realized how much BS work we had to do in his class. The stuff we did in class was for the most part a waste of time. And the homwork can sometimes take FOREVER. I feel like I grew a lot as a thinker, not so much as a writer though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Too. Much. Work. This class is taking up a good 3/4 of my weeks work time and is almost irrelevant to what I came to study here. Means well but just stresses and depresses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You definitely need to put some effort into this class but he is an amazing teacher and really helpful. He wants you to learn and become a better writer and critic. I learned so much in this class and really recommend him to any student who is serious about their education and their voice in the world. Great teacher!

Foley is a stereotypical English professor who believes everything he says is incredibly profound and complexly interesting. He is generally known as one of the worst Writing the Essay teachers at NYU. BUT he is a surprisingly forgiving grader. I was stuck with him for both semesters and it was NOT a good time.

Ok, so David Foley is bae. If you actually make an effort and engage yourself, you will grow so much. You need to give yourself to him if you want him to give anything to you. He's witty and sweet and so clever and I am basically in very deep platonic love with him. I have incredible conversations with him, he's amazing, I can't even. Bae, I swear.

David Foley is the worst! I was taking his class while struggling with depression and anxiety and he upped that with his confusing advice and inconsiderate attitude. It did not help having him at 8 in the morning, and he talked down to  his students. He was not very helpful and contradictory. He made us hate an already notorious class even more!

He's well meant, but doesn't teach that well, instead trying to focus on developing the student's thinking. This doesn't work because he overloads the amount of work that he assigns, which doesn't work well if you're trying to develop your writing. Instead you just end up spitting out irrelevant exercises and then failing up your final papers.

This guy is super into his own intellectualism.  Every single thing that came out of his mouth was vague; nothing in this class made any sense whatsoever.  He's very particular about little details that don't matter; for instance he refused to accept an essay because I didn't use the right kind of folder.  DO NOT take his class.

So...he is actually a kind and caring guy. He's pretty flexible, but don't push it. He is SO CONFUSING! My exercises didn't help me get to my final essay. The in class prompts were not helpful. He always asks "what are the implications of this?" and I feel I did not grow as a writer in his class. Everyone pretty much gets some sort of B.
Very good class, loved it. Any professor who will quote DFW on syllabus gets an automatically great rating.
the worst prof ever.... dosent help at all... only attacks your ideas... he dosent even tell you what is wrong... DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS every one hates it
Did not answer questions and was very vague if he did answer anything. Pretty much gave everyone a B
He was a great teacher. He was challenging yet always there to help.

genuinely one of the worst professors i've had. rambles way too much and barely teaches what you actually need for the exams. tests are super specific and qualitative, but he doesn't explain the math clearly at all. way too many readings, and 90% of your grade is just exams. just so full of himself and its insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazingly engaging lectures, well-organized class with examples of previous finals. You know exactly what you're getting into- the exams are hard and require intense memorization, but the content is laid out easily and you know what you need to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Foudy teaches an engaging class, is funny, and relates course concepts to current issues. He cares about encouraging questions/participation and making his lessons as clear as possible, though he sometimes cuts off/speaks over students. The exams are based on memorization of the readings (reading-heavy course).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very fun professor, provides years of past exams, so you know exactly what it looks like. Will need to participate and get ready to memorize 20+ articles by name. Other than that, the man is chill, take him!

might just be one of the worst professors at NYU literally just doing this as a job for a salary so dry and literally the most annoying style of humor i may have every come across. tests are incredibly difficult and topics emphasized in class are almost completely absent form the test and topics that are barely covered are emphasized in the exams.

Professor Foudy is incredibly engaging and light. He's funny and extremely well read. Global Business Trends with him becomes an easy 2 credit class that delivers valuable insights into real world business dynamics and economic trends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Foudy's engaging lectures make the 9:30am class bearable, but the exams are heavily quantitative and not well-aligned with his teachings. Using unstuck study alongside the textbook is key for exam prep.

Mandatory class with dense material. Lectures are very engaging and helpful (in addition to the many readings) to take notes on. Participation matters, but he tends to steamroll people to continue the lecture. Provided past midterms to study against, textbook and articles are given as PDFs, slides on paper. Doesn't like laptops.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough class, but well worth it. Need to pull out specific information from the readings.

Had super engaging and entertaining lectures. Participation is important but he tends to speak over students' opinions to talk more, whether that be about Chappell Roan, how the latest Taylor Swift album sucked, or his personal vendetta against Sweetgreen. There's never really a dull moment during lectures

The class covered concepts covered by outside readings but was easy to catch up on before the midterm exam and to follow along in class. Discussions were fun and engaging rather than a simple 75 minute info dump

an interesting choice for the bpe freshman class, i liked his lectures and class but he is so annoying - count the amount of times he talks about asia, the upper west side, says "food for thought", or hands out twenty dollar bills, oh and he def has a napoleon complex

His lectures are very interesting but it doesn't matter as long as you do all the readings. 
Make sure you participate in the class. 
He has a super fast pace in the class. You'll feel stressed at the beginning, but then you'll miss his lectures. 
A very respected, knowledgeable gentleman. Would want to take his class again if possible.
What other students said. Too much testing on niche, too much yapping, impossible tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are fun if u can get his jokes. Prof. Foudy has lived in Asian countries for years & knows them comprehensively. Participation matters & u have to speak at least once per class. Exams covers readings so lots of work memorizing names & the readings' contents. He's cool.

Class was a super interesting to me. Pretty challenging yet learned a lot. I discovered an app, Quizard, which seamlessly integrated with our class materials. It was surprisingly effective in helping me navigate through the toughest parts of the course. Highly recommend both the class for its depth and Quizard for making it manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Foudy seems like a great person, but I honestly was never able to keep up in class because he talked non-stop and would often go off on a tangent. Studying for his exams was actually the worst thing ever because he would test us on the most niche details from the 20+ readings he assigned, which he never talked about during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Foudy was an amazing professor because he knew a lot about topics and made class more interesting. There is a lot of reading, but the tests are not too bad because of the past exams, and I found them easier than other classes.
Awful. I took this class for easy A. But the grading was so tough.

Professor Foudy does have engaging and upbeat lectures that make you want to learn about economics of global business. However, I found that most of the things he talks about doesn't translate on exams as there are lots of quantitative problems to which he doesn't give much instruction to. Professor is knowledgable but class is still confusing.

Professor Foudy is an expert in his field but I didn't have a great experience. He doesn't grade with partial credit, so if you get all steps of an algorithm correct, and your final answer is off by a decimal point, he will give you zero credit. He was also unhelpful after class, and was standoffish. Very disappointing because I did enjoy the class

his lectures move fast but the slides are great and you can keep up easily. never a dull moment in his class. very funny. grade is almost all exams but if you review the slides the weekend before an exam you'll be fine. you can get away with not reading the textbook but there's always a few exam questions that were only in the textbook.

Class is graded by going to lectures and exam scores. Foudy's a great lecturer but talks very quickly. Exams test for lecture concepts, assigned readings, textbook knowledge, and most of all mathematical application of in-class theory (which he barely goes over). Luckily he provides multiple years of practice exams very similar to the real deal.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade based on 3 exams, each worth 30%, and 10% for participation/attendance. Zero HW or group projects. Textbook reading technically required but none of it is tested on exams so nobody does them anyways. Everything tested will be covered by his slides/lectures. Super funny guy; makes 9:30 AM lectures more bearable. Tests are generously curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are like Ted Talks but for the exams, you mainly need to know the readings instead of remembering the lectures. The class is pretty interesting but he does seem rather opinionated and his jokes sometimes get a bit old.

Foudy is a great lecturer; the lectures are interesting and engaging, but not really useful at all for the exams. Speaking of exams, they make up 90% of the grade. There is no homework, which is deeply needed since Foudy sticks to concepts/real-world situations in his lectures and barely covers problems which are on the test. READ THE TEXTBOOK!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GBT with Prof. Foudy is a really chill class. Assignments consists of 5 "memos" which are essentially short answer questions that are roughly a page and then 1 final essay. If you participate a lot (or even a few times) you easily become memorable and he'll keep referring back to moments in the class, which can be good or bad. Would take again!

Attendance and participation are mandatory but his lectures are BORING and useless. He loves talking about himself and his trips to Asia, Europe instead of covering exam materials. Grade is based on 3 exams + attendance/participation. Exams are difficult with an ok curve. Put in the work and you'll do well, but the subject is boring and so is he.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Cons: attendance is mandatory, has a hard time explaining concepts sometimes, and lectures are not very useful. Pros: gives tons of old tests that are extremely similar to the actual test (no surprises on exams), mostly responsive by email, and seems like a good/funny guy. Other EGB options are also pretty terrible...

He has to be one of the worst professors I've taken. He does not care about students. He is very rigid in his rules and makes no exceptions for anyone. He made my friend take her exam with a high fever. He gives no partial credit on exams. He purposely picks the most obscure questions. He talks about himself incessantly and offers no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Foudy makes the class very interesting and engaging. Course is test heavy though. The concepts can be a bit difficult to understand at first but once you have it down, it's easy to apply to different scenarios as presented on the exams. Midterms and final are just like the ones from previous years that he provides as study material!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Having other professors makes me appreciate Foudy even more. He's by far the best professor at NYU Stern. His lectures are actually engaging and he's interested in teaching, unlike some other professors who prefer researching and are forced to teach. I'd highly recommend Prof Foudy.

This class is not hard as long as you complete assignments and do the practice tests before exams. He is also pretty flexible and understanding. However, lectures feel useless as he often talks about irrelevant info and makes tired jokes. Other than that, not bad.

Cons: Rigid grader, lectures are useless, super super dense textbook reading, participation was crucial (for online you had to keep cameras on constantly)
Pros: gives you tons of practice tests that are basically the same as the actual exam, has a review session that is useful, talks about other things which are kinda entertaining.
Grade is only dependent on one paper.
Participation and attendance are graded. Professor Foudy is a tough grader but has engaging lectures that make going to class worth it.

His lectures have very little to do with what is tested, and he "doesn't believe in rubrics", which makes completing assignments and getting a high grade completely impossible to evaluate by yourselves.

Professor Foudy doesn't believe in lecturing on topics covered in the readings, despite all the tests being on the readings. So his lectures (where attendance and participation are graded) end up being 75 minutes of him talking about his daughter or his trips to Japan. The readings are dense and long, too, so studying is hard and exhausting.

Had a great time in EGB. Found the lectures interesting but the reading a bit dry and very long. Doing all the practice tests, reading the textbook, and reading the supplemental articles was enough to get an A on all the exams. Preparing takes a lot of time but is necessary since lectures do not explicitly cover expectations for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor's lectures were really interesting for this 1 credit class, I really enjoyed his insights on business trends in film. 10/10 great guy would definitely recommend taking his classes!

This was a 1 credit class and I loved it. There were only 2 class sessions and participation is 25% of your grade so that was a bit stressful (the TA kept track of who spoke when), but the assignments are short and we spent most of the lectures just watching movies. I'm not a film person so I got a bit bored, but I'd take it again for the easy A

I really liked this class. It was super chill as an elective and one of the least stressful I've taken. There aren't long assignments besides a 5 page final paper (not even long tbh) and he doesn't grade harshly. His lectures were super interesting and he prints out the slides and gives them to you so you can annotate them.

Took his Global Business Trends class for a simple 2 credit course and it was really chill. He kinda takes over the discussions but he's a passionate and knowledgeable guy. Workload is light with six 1-page memos and a final paper. Not a bad class at all especially if you're into current events

The course material is actually pretty interesting, but the professor loses his charm over time. The lectures are interesting but don't align with the readings as well as I would have hoped because the exams are solely based on the readings. His jokes got old and he didn't really like it when students would question him. It's not too hard though.

I think Foudy understands content well and his classes are not boring by any means. However, I think his lectures suffer. They are interesting but useless overall. Only the readings matter. He is also somewhat funny, yet he also gets upsets easily, acts unprofessionally sometimes, and tells you his opinions too easily(bad for writing classes).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very knowledgeable and accessible via email. Shows he cares a lot about his students. You will get a good grade if you follow the test and study instructions. Highly recommend him.

I didn't feel that he indeed cares about the students. Attendance is mandatory, while he's lecture is very different from the exam. You have to spend a bunch of time after class to study the materials required for exam on your own. He posts the materials very slowly. Probably one of the worst professors I've had in Stern.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very good speaker, very much a classic Stern Professor. Interesting, funny, and genuine person. Workload was very light, but discussions were engaging.

I know the pandemic has made everything harder on everyone, but I've never had a professor make it harder to get feedback, be more opaque with their grades, and be more unfriendly when I asked for help. He shouldn't take out his inadequacy in remote teaching on his students, and he definitely did to my class.

Foudy is incredibly full of himself and lectures are a time for him to chat about his life. His lectures are very conceptual, and yet the exams are wicked hard and rooted in numbers. There's no clear connection between the two. Prepare to fail every exam and be saved only by the curve. Not terrible, but be prepared to cry in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Global Business Trends is a fairly new class I believe and is totally like current events. The only homework is 6 1-2 page double spaced memos on topics discussed in class and a final paper. Lectures are interesting bc they apply to life right now, and participation is important but easy.

Really great professor all around despite his reputation. Classes aren't particularly helpful for scoring well on the exams but they are still very interesting nonetheless. Be prepared to do a lot of reading as well as all the past papers he gives you. Difficult class but a very clear path to get an A if you put in the work.

Everyone here complains that the lectures are useless for the test, and that is why he does not care if you show up. His lectures are interesting if you care about the global economy. Just grind for two days and do the mandatory readings for the test and you will get at least a B in the class. People here only care about learning for the test lol.

I had Professor Foudy for International Political Economy at Hunter College back in 2005. He was a fantastic professor. Extremely knowledgable about the subject matter, funny, and able to put difficult concepts into understandable terms. The entire class loved him. The exam was straightforward and fair. Glad to see he is still teaching.

PLEASE do not go to class. it is the biggest waste ur of time. his lectures are interesting, but nothing of it is related to his exams. the key to this class is just to do the practice exams and shockingly, it is enough for u to get a b or above. use his class time to sleep, watch tv, start your company idc. you'll pass regardless.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He usually just goes through slides sloppily and spends most of the lectures telling stories that only he thinks are funny. Lectures are useless, pretty sure you can still get an A by studying on your own. The materials are not hard, but he makes the tests unnecessarily difficult by requiring you to use the calculators that are so hard to operate.

If you do the readings and don't try to cram the entire syllabus in a few days leading up to the exam, you'll be fine. His lectures are amusing and he's very responsive to questions, whether over email or during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I quite enjoyed Professor Foudy's class! The class is graded only by three tests, and attendance is completely mandatory. However, I would heavily recommend going to class. The professor is interesting to listen to. He goes over things very quickly so it'd be good to read the notes beforehand so you can follow easier. Also, go to the review session
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever taken please take anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he just gets up there and quickly flips through things, full of it, math heavy exam, pretty much have to teach yourself but the book helps practice test is similar to the same as the one you get but the class grade relies only on tests, take literally anyone else- NO POINTS FOR SHOWING WORK ONLY IF RIGHT ANSWER (EGB)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: so full of himself for no reason. just trying to be funny and flip through slides. very little learning
interesting but heavy lectures, tons of readings, difficult exams...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fantastic Prof. Difficult yet knowledgeable. Be careful with word choice. Took for IEPT

His lectures are funny, but never specifically touches stuff that comes up on the exam (He focuses more on big concepts and making jokes). Basically, lectures are only helpful if you thoroughly studied slides and the readings on your own. To ace the tests, do all the practice exams he gives you & go to the review session he hosts.

Tons of reading so keep up but lectures are really interesting. Exams are difficult and are based entirely on the homework. Definitely increased my understanding on a variety of economic and political ideas. Had him for BPE EPT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Yes the tests can be brutal to study for, but Foudy's class will truly teach you the material and allow you to actually understand what you hear/read in economic news. Read the chapters, take notes, and do the practice exams and you're golden. It was challenging, but I am super grateful I had Foudy for EGB. He's awesome. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome professor to take for EGB. In order to ace the tests you just have to do the practice tests over and over. The final isn't cumulative unlike the other EGB classes. Foudy knows a lot about what he teaches and the material is actually really relevant and interesting. Definitely take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're in Stern and you don't take Foudy, you will miss out. I took him for both Asian Economies and EGB and he's a real gem. Amazing lectures and extremely knowledgeable. For Asian Econ, just make sure you go through the readings and the Miracle book, memorize that and you'll ace the class

Foudy is one of my favorite professors at Stern.  His lectures are very entertaining and informative.  However, to do well on his exams, you need to read every single page of the books he assigned you.  He really knows his stuff and his lectures reflect that, so you don't wanna miss them.
awesome.

Definitely study the old exams because the stuff on the test is calculation stuff that isn't really covered in lectures. Lectures are mostly interesting because he gives a lot of real life examples to make lessons applicable.

1) I went to all of his lectures and listened very carefully. 2) I didn't even buy the textbook. 3) I did all of the sample exams (almost 10 year worth).   This was enough to get an A. More than 80% of exam questions are the exact same thing as those in the sample exams. I think I did more work in Texts and Ideas than EGB. Nonetheless, good class

Professor Foudy really makes you think critically whether it's during his enthusiastic lectures or the accessory readings he picks. If you take his ept class (bpe), you. gon. read. Material is non cumulative so you have a finals for each half of the course. Readings total up to 400 pages per exam so if you slack off weekly, no one can save you. :)
Really amazing professor. Couldn't ask for anyone better for EGB. Keeps the class engaged and is really good.
Foudy is a great professor.  Took his introductory Econ class as well as Asian Economies. Lectures are very clear and engaging.

He is very honest about grading and what to expect on exams.  There are 3 exams that make up your grade- no HW, no participation, no projects.  Lectures are interesting at times but won't necessarily help you get a good grade.  He posts all old exams so study those front and back and READ THE TEXTBOOK!!!

Foudy's a great lecturer and keeps class interesting. EGB is really not too hard - just memorize all of the charts and quantitative problems and you already know about 70% of the exam. You don't even have to study that much for them and you will do okay. The class itself is pretty dry; just general macroeconomic concepts and the like.
Talks really fast and incorporates a lot of interesting research not directly related to the course.
Excellent teacher and interesting lecturer, definitely understands the material. Get ready to read.

He was a good professor. His lectures were very interesting, and I recommend showing up to them as it makes understanding the textbook easier. He may be very tough in the sense there's a lot of specific material to cover, but he is very fair and clear. His practice tests outline what will basically be on your test, so study them well and also read.

Tough grader, massive exams, but the curve is pretty generous (The B+ is in the low to mid seventies, the flat A is generally well below 90). Far preferred to the ultra-tight micro curve, but WachtelWaugh give tests that aren't going to involve massive, all-weekend studying ordeals. Your choice.

You can choose not to pay attention and just do the readings, however, the conversations in class are very interesting and you can tell he knows his stuff. Its up to you how much the class will interest you, depending if you do the readings before or not.

Beneath the comedic act, Foudy just isn't that great of a teacher. His lectures are pretty much optional. Go over the slide, read the book, and do the practice tests for a pretty likely A or A-. In fact, going to lectures and not reading the book will guarantee you less than a B+. Therefore, reading is essential to doing well and lecture irrelevant

Foudy does a good job in scaring students early, and it does tend to make the less ambitious Sternies all the more complacent when studying. He literally gives 10 past exams for practice for each test. There is no excuse for not doing well if you study the practice tests and read the book. Lecture is fun for the first third, but not essential.

Hey, BPErs! Foudy is difficult but fair. He's also very engaging. Do the readings and participate in class. Take notes as you read throughout the semester because it will help and save so much time when it comes to the midterm and final!

Fantastic professor, very clear with regards to conveying knowledge as well as what is expected of students if they want to earn an 'A'. Only caveat is that the class is indeed pretty hard. There is no homework, but reading the textbook and out-of-class articles is *essential* and can be time consuming. Otherwise, has a great sense of humor.

Every professor should be like him. He gives you every single possible resource you could possibly need to study for the exams. The exams are hard but predictable. He is also very entertaining. Remember, your grade depends on the curve.
Best professor ever. for REALZZ

The class is all rote memorization and reading. Nothing that goes on in class actually prepares you for the exam. Class is amusing, and Foudy manages to keep students engaged but when exam time comes you will realize every second you spent in class was a waste.

EGB is all about the readings. Do the assigned readings and you will do fine. Even if you go to every lecture, if you don't do the readings, you will be screwed. However, Prof. Foudy will expound upon the readings extremely thoroughly in lecture, and will make it more digestible and, dare I say, entertaining for you to understand and appreciate.
the first grade we got in the class was two thirds into the course... doesnt teach what's on the exams, just blabs and likes to hear the sound of his own voice. also class grade is only exams

Worst professor i've ever had in stern. pretends to teach but wastes valuable class time telling "funny stories" that he thinks pertains to the material. the class in general covers the equivalent of two, maybe 3, CAS classes ... so i don't get why he doesn't directly teach. maybe his style works for other students. be aware.
Ditto the other reviewers. Great professor, great sense of humor. Extremely difficult, but makes it easy to get an A if you put in the effort (which is a tremendous amount).
Foudy is great! He's funny and extremely intelligent. His tests tend to be very specific and require a lot of studying, but it's definitely do-able.

He's a great professor, his classes are truly interesting and he makes them fun! His tests tend to go on specific concepts of the books and readings, but if you read them thoroughly you'll do just fine.

He is one of the best professors that I have ever had. Yes his class is hard, yes exams are though, but hey it is tough for everyone and you are here to learn... He gives you a very clear idea about how the economy works globally. If you want to improve your economic knowledge take him. If you want an easy grade, don't.
Foudy is incredibly difficult. however, with the stern curve things balance a bit. for example, a 66+ was B+ min. It makes you study alot but he is funny, and knows what he is talking about.
If you want someone who knows his stuff and makes it crystal clear what is expected then he is your guy. Makes boring Lectures entertaining.

Foudy made the few days before an exam living hell, because his goal is to make exams as difficult as possible. He curves insane amounts, so most people pass. No assignments aside from reading 30 incredibly boring pages for each class. Weird sense of humor that not everyone appreciates. He was just okay for me!

Foudy is a great professor. He has a good sense of humor and tells jokes all the time. Economics of Global Business is a hard class in general regardless of what professor you take. Given this, Foudy makes the class a lot easier by providing everyone with equal access to previous exam! Overall a good choice!
Amazing guy, hard tests but he really knows his stuff!
No Comments
Foudy is THE man! He is a very down-to-earth professor, and his class is challenging but always interesting. Work hard, and you will undoubtedly do well!

I love Fanny Shum!! She is so so wonderful and caring! I can feel her passion on math during class and she is so inspirational! Explaining complicated concepts clearly and logically, and she is so patient and welcoming and accessible in office hour! You will definitely not be sleepy during her class!!

Precalc setup was confusing. No actual lectures, just problem sets. Every week at recitations you need to do a ton of problems, and if you get a single one wrong, you fail. No explanation about what you got wrong or why. No calculators allowed. Very stressful. I'm just going to review the material and hope to test into calculus 1.

Very structured lectures which I appreciate. I did not feel like the homework's were adequate preperation for the exams. The exams are very difficult and introduce unfamiliar ways of thinking about concepts under very tight time pressure. Otherwise nice professor, accessible outside of class and clearly very passionate and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Shum is a great teacher and knows how to explain concepts clearly and in many ways. She clearly likes teaching the subject. Lots of practice through Web Assigns, Written HWs, and weekly quizzes. Test questions were of similar form to those we had seen in class/in practice problems (no surprises!) Hard class, so need to put in the time and work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fine professor and accessible at office hours if you don't understand concepts. She assigns a lot of work to ensure you achieve mastery of the concepts, so ensure that you are capable of dedicating a sizeable chunk of time to her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty good, though it felt like she slightly rushed the last half of the semester, which is where all the hard topics are. Overall, I would take her class again.

Very structured lectures which was really nice although she does tend to move faster compared to the other professors. Still it is not a problem though and I enjoyed her style of teaching. Textbook says is required but didn't need to read it as the lectures were better for understanding content. Curve at the end based on individual performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good curve. Good lecture. Good office hour. I am bad at math.
Tough exams but good at explaining. Very accessible at Office Hours. She gives good curve based on individual improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Shum is a great professor. She's always available after class for questions and she explains concepts very clearly. People say that she's a tough grader but I haven't really seen that. Every calc 2 class gets the same amt. of homework, and they're very effective for testing your understanding. Exams are similar to HW. 10/10 recommend!!! :D
The exams were much harder than the homework, quizzes, and examples in class. She does not explain the material thoroughly. The TAs won't help you much as they forgot most of the subject.

She gives lots of work but as long as you stay on top everything will be fine. Complete web assigns directly after the lecture. This is easier because she lets everyone leave early after finishing the lecture. Study before each quiz, and try to maximize that grade. For the final, focus on previous topics just as much as the new topics.

Good professor, but be wary of the heavy workload. She gives 6 assignments a week so you will almost always be busy with this class. 

Tests are not curved individually, but there is a generous shift of ~5% on final grade if you improve over time and show up (lectures, office hours.)

Overall a great professor, but you have to stay on top of work.

You'll have homework 5 days a week in Calc2. Be prepared to devote a lot of time to this class so dont take anything else challenging. Many people fail the finals. knew someone who got arounf 32 on one of them. shes willing to raise ur grade if u improve so if you fail something hope is not lost, but the tests are CHALLENGING.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives you everything you need to succeed, there is no reason to compain. She is the most available teacher I've had at nyu, always answering questions and has long office hours that probably boosted my grade a whole letter. Exams are very fair and she explains clearly. You actually have to work in this class though.

she's a great teacher and provides so much organized material to help u succeed in calc 2. requires a lot from u on a weekly basis, but is kinda generous in how many quizzes, hws, etc. she will drop. not an easy teacher, but a very fair, very good one. not super flexible, but understanding. u will always know what to expect

Prof Shum's class is challenging, but worth the effort. Her grading is strict, but the material is engaging. I found unstuckstudy and the free textbook helpful for study prep. Overall, a rewarding experience.

A lot of prelecture work that may get overwhelming. Prelecture videos are around 1 hour long, comparative to the actual lecture. Homework is pretty straightforward, two prelecture quizzes, two webassigns, and one/two post lecture quizzes. Three tests that counts for around 65% of your grade. Her lectures are recorded. Take detailed notes.

An experienced professor who teaches lectures very clearly and is super nice. Enough time for Q&A after each class. The exams are moderately difficult but fine. She determines your final grade based on your overall performance rather than just one exam and tries to give you the best grade possible.

Gives a ton of homework but it prepares you well and forces you to understand the material. Lectures are good and she is happy to answer questions in office hours. Good curve at the end of the semester. Organized and is good about staying on track with all the curriculum. Do all the work and it will help you a ton for the exams.

she's a pretty engaging lecturer but exams are difficult and the questions are unpredictable. there's so much hw (5 assignments/week) that take so long to complete and the tests are weighed so much more than the assignments themselves so it's hard to do well in the class. she gives a pretty good curve tho like a 5% increase.

She was the most tolerable calc teacher out of them all. The quizzes & exams are 10 times harder than what she actually teaches. I used the lecture time to watch organic chem tutor videos and then review her lecture slides cause he explains it much better.The final exam was complete nonsense so make sure you are on top of HW, Quizzes and midterms.
If you like your life, don't take this professor. Her quizzes and tests are 10 times harder than what she goes over in lectures. She's pretty fair with the grading scheme though I will give her that

Great Professor! She is caring, and her lectures are useful and comprehensive. However, we need to watch recorded pre-lectures and complete pre-lecture quizzes. In return, we can learn new material more effectively and end the lecture one hour earlier. Her curve is great. If you want to have a great learning experience, choose her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
While she is a lovely person, she is also extremely difficult to learn from. 

Unlike other calc 1 classes, she gives a quiz every week, even if that quiz is a day after a midterm.

We also varied in the pace of our lessons wildly. We started off very slowly compared to others, but by the end it definitely felt like we were rushing.

One of the best professors I've had - gives you every resource you need to succeed (recorded lectures, pre-lectures, practice exams, etc.) Offers office hours at least twice a week! really nice and very accessible by email outside class. willing to answer any questions you have
Great professor, very patient and caring during office hours, and gives out clear lectures.

A great professor who is both caring and knowledgeable. The recordings of the class are posted onto Brightspace, but you're better off just going to class in person because it's much easier to ask questions that way. Weekly assignments/quizzes are manageable and exams are fair.

Professor Kayar is a great professor, super helpful and willing to set aside one on one time to help you if you are struggling. She has clear lectures and homework assignments, and very fair exams. He's a talented researcher, but I don't think he cares much about teaching. Very relaxed and chill in a way, but I wish he put in more effort in another. TA was extremely helpful and available.

Gollwitzer is pretty boring, and although his intentions are probably good, he doesnt seem like he puts in any real time or effort on teaching and preparing lectures. It's hard to understand him, but you can do well just by reading the textbook. The TAs were awesome!! Attendance is mandatory, because you have to write a response for every class. Very cool guy but isn't clear with the papers you need to write, if it's a required course you need I would find another professor.

He was good professor, who cares and gave me lots of grace on late work. His lectures tend to be a bit rambling. In class time is spent discussing readings. Doing the readings and attendance was mandatory.

Professor Vargo is really passionate about students reaching knowledge for themselves, so class was mostly based on discussing the readings.
Such a nice professor! He's really understanding when it comes to giving extensions and he's also a super easy grader. He knows that no one does the reading but he still doesn't really care.
He is amazingggggg and very sweet!
Nope nope nope

The worst lab instructor there is DO NOT TAKE HER AT ALL. I'm not sure why the reviews are so terrible (although I took Gen Chem 1 with her and not Orgo), but Melissa was a great lab instructor, and anyone else in my section would agree. She genuinely grades down to your handwriting. She does not know how to give partial credit and when she helps you during the lab and post lab, she still ends up marking the answers wrong when she grades it. Not at all fit to be a lab instructor and grader. Do not take her.
Just thinking about her makes my skin crawl
give us a break

She is a heathen. Take Angelo as your TA or Dr. Martinez!!!

Very rude and does not give partial credit at all. Other TAs in the lab are much nicer, take anyone else for your own sanity. She takes the title of "TA" very seriously despite it her being her first time ever teaching Organic Chem and it makes life awful for all of the students in her section. AVOID
she hates herself and projects onto her students. maybe relax a bit

Worst TA I have ever had in my life. She thrives on seeing students struggle. For someone who just graduated in 2023, she sure has a big ego. I hope she gets fired. Next Maitland Jones.

Big ego, unclear feedback, no rubrics for assignments, no online syllabus, unrealistic expectations, (especially for people new to journalism) and the thing about getting one grade for the whole semester is true.

I respect Professor Hochwald; she cares deeply for her students. However, you either understand the advice she gives or you don't. Prepare to focus on this course, as there will be a lot of trial and error when writing your first stories. There are last-minute print jobs, outdated resources, and no online resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved her class! She didn't have favorites, the whole class felt fairly equal and participated greatly in discussions. You do have to do a lot of outside work and reporting. If it's your first journalism class brace yourself to jump right in, but as someone who had a bit of prior experience, it was nothing crazy & great exposure to the field!

Overall, great professor that knows a lot, so be ready to intake a lot of information fast. I was able to learn A LOT. Weekly deadlines. You WILL HAVE TO interview people! If you're ready to get engaged and out there, this class is perfect. Lots of fun conversations and events! 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Learned alot, but tough grader. Once you get your first grade, you will recieve that grade for the rest of the semester. Provides little to no explanation on it, and is not fair. Has favorites and treats them differently. Dont take her class.

She was great at introducing different types of writing, and really pushed us to go out and do our own reporting which was a ton of fun. I greatly improved my writing and reporting skills in this class. 
Her feedback wasn't always the best, but she helped me find a passion for journalism and learn more about New York City. Definitely recommend.

This summer class proved invaluable as a journalist. Hochwald's real-world expertise made a six-week course into a richer experience than a full semester. Field trips to interview businesses, politicians, and a Food Network editor were transformative. I highly recommend her comprehensive journalism education catering to all levels of expertise.

Kind-hearted! She loves when students reach out. If you're thinking about expanding your network and getting more opportunities in journalism, she'll love to help you. Her classes are very dynamic: she invites different guests ranging from social media managers to politicians; and she also takes students to different field trips. Take her class!

BEST professor I've ever taken in NYU, period. In a semester, she transformed me from a total noob in journalism to someone comfortable reporting and writing journalistic pieces. She really paved my path and ignited my passion in journalism.

Professor Hochwald really taught me how to write as a journalist. She does a lot of hands-on teaching, and is very encouraging of us to go out and do reporting. Gives good feedback on your weekly stories. Can sometimes give impossible deadlines (ie a story in an hour in class) but overall is very caring of her students and taught me so much.

Yeah, don't take this class. Got an A, but at what cost? Worst professor and class at nyu especially for starting off in journalism. Made me want to switch majors. Don't know why she's allowed to teach. Don't believe the 5 stars.

Got an A but hated this class. Don't believe the good reviews. She tells her favorites to go on here and post. Tough grader without explaining her logic. Unnecessarily difficult assignments that don't help you grow. Has the biggest ego ever. She also said I treat everyone well, "even prostitutes." Um, why do you have to say that if you do?

I absolutely loved Hochwald's JOUR 101 class. A lot of the work done is real-world experience; you are taught the basics of interviewing and are expected to interview someone every class, (this may turn away some people, but I loved the experience). Also be prepared to write news stories every class, your writing will greatly improve as a result.

I took Professor Hochwald's class during the Summer session, and I have no regrets! She is a caring and devoted professor. Her course was challenging but the knowledge acquired from her assignments is so worth it. I got out of my comfort zone, and would have never done so without her care and encouragements. The best professor in the department.

I took Hochwald over a year ago and it's one of the worst classes I've taken at NYU in any major. While she seems okay in class, she truly doesn't have any consideration for outside issues students may be dealing with. Also, she's a tabloid journalist and her feedback made me a worse writer. Assignments were busy work and her grading was ridiculous
