It was very insightful. I learnt many interesting facts. sir made the presentation very interesting. it not only kept us focused throughout but it also taught us important concepts in a fun manner!

Mr. George is an amazing lecturer and guide, his way of explaining concepts, makes everything more interesting to learn and easy to understand. His method of using the students favorite (well-known) brands to explain his concepts and show the practical use of those concepts, really fascinates me. He also responds to everyone's questions.

Professor Benaroya is great! Believe or not, he makes learning fun and is able to teach his student complex materials in an easy way to understand. He takes real life situations and teaches his student how to apply them and use them in the real world. Would highly recommend this professor!

Really great, funny and interesting prof - truly cares for his students and makes the class easy to follow and fun. He's very funny and uses a lot of real world examples to teach his classes, as long as you show up and pay attention youll do well! hes the best though, cant say enough good things about him

Professor Benaroya was one of the most amazing professors I have ever had in both my undergraduate and graduate career. His class was my favorite during the semester and I cannot tell you enough how much I enjoyed the class, the subject, and Professor Benaroya's personality. He made finance interesting & easy to learn. Definitely take his class!

Professor Benaroya was my favourite professor during my first semester at NYU. I was new to finance and totally clueless - Professor made it so easy for all of us to understand complex concepts. The best part of the class is the projects as they help you apply the concepts you learn. No textbooks, easy quizzes is the best part of the class!

Benaroya is a rare find when it comes to professors. From his lectures, assignments, and tests, the class is meant to be stress-free and he works with you to help you succeed. When you enter his classroom, you are going to learn how finance is applicable to a career in marketing (not just a bunch of technical terms). His class is a MUST at NYUSPS.

Wonderful professor. He genuinely cares about teaching his students and having them engaged during class. He teaches from personal experience, and he sure does have a lot of it. The group project during the semester is interesting and the guest speakers he brings adds an extra level to the course.

Professor George Benaroya is not teaching based on just some book. His lectures are based on real life cases and concrete financial reports of existing public companies. In my opinion that's the best approach when you want to learn to apply the knowledge. I wish every class would be so useful.
Such an incredible professor. His lectures were very interesting and inspiring. Definitely sign up for his class if you have the opportunity!

George is a real gurus on finances. Great resume, experiences and knowledge make his class useful in real world. He also takes great care to his students. In my startup company, he offers great help and resources. True inspirational, noble and treasurable choice.
I really love the professor!

Benaroya is one of the very few instructors Ive come across in my educational career who truly goes above and beyond for his students. He really knows how to challenge a student and help them reach their best potential, even if that requires extra time outside of the classroom. Would recommend him 110%!!

Professor George Benaroya is one of the best professors I have met. His lecture is beneficial in real-world business and easy to understand. The homework is helpful to understand the lecture and practical. He likes his students, and he is willing to help students too. I strongly recommend taking Professor George Benaroya's classes.

He is the best professor I have ever met, very professional and responsible. He help me with some problem I dont get and offer me extra meeting to solve my problems and he really encouraged me to study and build confidence to me.

Professor Benaroya is everything you can ask when registering for a class. Worked so much but learned even more. Its the most rewarding class I have ever taken in my life. I highly recommend and make sure to take advantage of the best professor for Finance. He makes finance FUN.

You know these grandparents characters in films that you JUST CAN'T HATE ON cuz they're just so lovable from every single angle and in every single way, and if you still manage to hate on them then you might need therapy? Yep. THAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super supportive, intelligent, and helpful learning environment that Jason Hwang creates over the semester. Prioritizes creativity alongside effective learning about Pro Tools, which allowed me to come out of the class with so much knowledge in many different areas of film, not just strictly sound. Also, he's just awesome.

Jason is a great professor; I had zero knowledge of audio going into the class and came out of it having solidly acquired an entire new skillset. Academically rigorous but never strict or unreasonable, and very flexible. He genuinely cares about his job and his students, and makes sure everyone has a positive academic experience.

Jason was an amazing teacher. Super knowledgeable about Protools and all things sound. He is easily able to find points where the sound could be improved, and is always helpful whenever you ask him about it. He works hard to make sure every student understands the assignments and is able to understand sound in films.

Amazing professor! I don't know what I was expecting for sound and was lowk scared but Jason made the class so welcoming and nice. He gives really good feedback and is super passionate in what he does. He has a musical background and it definitely comes out in his teaching and is super interesting to hear about. Highly recommend!
Jason gives really great feedback, and he's so fun! He's also really understanding when you need help or an extension.

Jason Hwang is INCREDIBLE!! If you have the opportunity to take his class, DO. And, whilst it is possible to get by in his class without putting in a ton of work, DON'T. He has invaluable knowledge when it comes to sound and film in general and he will totally improve you as an artist.

Despite having probably more work for this class than any of my other classes this semester, it was the class I spent the least time stressing over. This was a really hard semester for my mental health but Jason was really encouraging and accommodating and I could tell he really cared about my wellbeing. And I learned a ton about sound!

You have to take Jason! He is super accomplished but also so down to earth. Show up to class and actually put in the effort and you'll do well in this class. Jason gives such great feedback! Very charismatic!
He makes a long class really fun, I ended up really looking forward to this class every week because of his positivity.
Jason is such a beautiful human and I look forward to his class every week. He's so encouraging and pushes us to do our best. #king

This is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I learned everything about Pro Tools, and I got basically stand up comedy for hours every week from Jason. Such a kind human being, treats you as a real true equal and he does real nuanced real world art. He learns from his students and you learn from him. I can't recommend him enough. TAKE HIS CLASS.
Best professor at NYU, take him no matter what, soooo worth it.
AMAZING. Best professor at NYU. Best Sound Image professor hands down.
He's just an overall nice dude. If you're not showing up to classes and missing assignments he'll actually take the time to try and check in with you, to make sure everything is going okay
an amazing professor. the literal goat. my favorite professor by far. learned so much and he really cares about all of his students. A+++++++

Professor Hwang is an incredible professor who was super patient and critiqued in a firm yet kind way. He starts off lenient and he warned us a couple times he would get more strict as the projects went on, which did not happen, he's so nice. But he still grades really efficiently. Would 100% recommend taking him- he's the best!

Easygoing, kind, and most importantly, an incredibly skilled man. I'm in awe of his ear for sound and his knowledge about production and technique. You won't regret having him for sound image. He cares about developing us as holistic artists and even brought in a professional actor in class for us to ask questions to. Insane industry experience too

Best Sound Image teacher! Jason is an amazing instructor allowing lots of creative freedom on the weekly assignments. He was very informative and incredibly knowledgable about all aspects of sound, but allows students to joke around and have fun while learning. Easy grading, lists answers to the midterm ahead of time! PAGES of feedback!

Took his Sound Image class in Fall semester 2021. Jason is one of the best professors I've had at NYU so far. He is caring, ALWAYS willing to help. I would not call him a tough grader, but you have to work in his class. His grading criterias are clear. In your evaluation he mentions every pros and cons in your work.

Jason is one of the best professors I've had at NYU. He genuinely cares about your learning in and out of the classroom. He gives pages of feedback on your project- showing the time he puts into each student I wasn't loving the idea of taking a sound-focused class before Jason, but after him, I feel I want to look into the field.

When you take Sound Image, Jason is a solid choice. He's a really nice guy and you will learn a lot about Pro Tools if you pay attention. Yes, he can go on a little but he's very easy to talk to and he's quick to help if you have any problems. Do make sure that all your homework is thorough and submitted on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jason is the BEST sound image professor. He is extremely passionate with what he teaches. You will be very savvy with ProTools and sound recording by the time you finish his class. He gives tons of great feedback that will help you become a better artist both in terms of concepts and skills.
Jason is the absolute best for sound image. Gives amazing feedback, has useful projects and clearly cares a lot about his students and audio! Totally recommend!

Jason is an absolute legend. I had him for Sound image, and as someone with terrible ears, I totally expected to dread this class, however it ended up being one of my favorites. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about film and sound design and makes his students excited about it too. He's super understanding and flexible too.

Jason is such an incredible professor for Sound Image. He genuinely cares about his students and our success, and respects each student's unique vision and tries his best to help you improve technically and creatively. He has a lot of knowledge and jokes to share, and he truly tries his best to keep you engaged in a relatively long class.

I love Jason! Such a kind and caring person. I really felt that he cared about me and my work. He's very understanding towards absences or being late and overall he is just awesome! His tech seminars are fast and can be hard to follow, but he will always answer your questions and try to help. Amazing guy!

Jason is the absolute best. He is by far the best sound image teacher and is totally underrated. Sound image is my favorite class this semester because of him. He is really lenient with projects and allows so much creative freedom.

Jason is a really good professor. He is really good about letting students take artistic freedom with the projects while also expecting quality work. As long as you put in the effort and listen to his notes you should do well. He tends to show videos in class that can be kind of excessive and boring but they're not without purpose. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jason can be a nice guy, but will only really like you if you are super talented with music. He is a musician and only cares about other musicians. He also shows a lot of pointless videos in class and the already long class goes by really slowly. His feedback is not super helpful and his instructions are confusing, so ask questions!!!

Jason is so sweet. He reminds me of a dad or an uncle. He laughs at his own jokes and he's very laid back. He can sometimes be very difficult to keep up with when doing tech seminars, but paying attention for later tech seminars don't really matter. As long as you pay attention in the first two tech seminars. He is very kind and an easy grader.

Friendly and with some quirks, Jason allows his students to express their inner artist through his assignments while providing in-depth feedback on technical skills. He provides his students with great resources, and is very responsive to questions about assignments and Sound Design in general. Very caring and understanding.

He's a phenomenal teacher. Records all lectures, releases his notes and extra practice problems, and textbook is optional. Overall Hesam was great. You must be able to do all the problems from his notes to pass his exams. Just do the problems, and the exams aren't bad at all. They're the same problems. HW is hard too, but it's HW and not on exams.

The homework and quizzes ask you to solve 1+1. The exam asks you to solve cancer. Very hard exams, even if you study from his notes you will still be surprised that in the exam you will find stuff that you do not know how to solve and start questioning whether you took it before or not.

If you need to meet the math requirement for the Econ major, take the Calc sequence. Even though it goes through Calc 3, I'd still choose Calc II over this class. The professor is passionate and clear about grading, but can come off egocentric - more focused on lecturing than student success. If that works for you, stick with him.

Honestly, people give such low ratings makes me wanna write this. Yes midterms and final are hard, but everthing on exmas are covered in the course. Apart from the exams everyone complain about, this guy gives the best Math lectures I've ever had in my life. He is so passionate and sophisticated in what he teach. Will definitely take his class more
Very hard exams that he does not prepare you to take. What he teaches in class is different from what is on the midterm and final despite what he may say.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: difficulty of the tests is much higher than what is taught in class. Oveys' class also received less time for the midterm than other classes taught by other professors. He kept telling us to review from class notes and quizzes, which were not that helpful because they didnt rlly match the difficulty of the final
so much harder than MFE1, oveys is fine as a professor but MFE2 in general is just a difficult class
Great professor, watch his lectures and go through the types of question in his homework quizzes and recitation sheets

tough grader b/c of the TAs & administrator. final was EXTREMELY hard but won't blame oveys b/c the test was made by administrator. wish he prepped us more for it though. weekly quizzes but is generous, allows us to drop the 3 lowest quizzes. pretty generous with end curve. homework felt unrelated though. records lectures and gives class notes.

You can take online course and read his notes, which covers everything. The practice example cover every single part of course so that even though you don't take class sometimes, you can also get very high score in exam. Homework is kind of heavy to be honest. In this course, you need to take time and do more practice.

Oveys has a clear passion for maths and teaching but I'm not sure if he's the optimal choice for all students. Personally, I struggled with his methods despite studying and scored poorly on the exams. He definitely knows his stuff but he doesn't do the best at teaching them at all times. Also which TA  you have matters in your weekly quiz grades.
DO NOT TAKE. ME AND EVERYONE IN OUR RECITATION STRUGGLED. EVEN THE TA SAID THE EXAMS ARE BEYOND DIFFICULT. THERE'S NO WAY ALL THE 5/5 REVIEWS ARE ACTUAL PEOPLE

mid. exams r much harder than class notes and quizzes but keep emphasizing to use them to practice. expects us to have a very clear understanding of complex topics when thats not covered in the class. in class he's a good teacher but comes off a rude. good curve but still not good enough to account for the difficulty of exams - just alr

The best math professor I've ever had in my life, period. I'd already taken AP Calculus in high school but Professor Oveys' style of lecturing engaged me without fail and helped me deepen my understanding of concepts I thought I'd already known well. He's the only rational choice if you're planning to take MFE I.

Very good at explaining concepts. Hard exams but similar to his lectures. I went to his office hours and he's really helpful. Big curve at the end. Don't take MFE if you have a busy semester. I spent 10 hours a week studying

Decent at explaining the concepts but does bad at preparing you for the exams. Always tells you to review the notes and practice set, yet on the finals nothing close to what we learned appeared. His 4.7/5 rating here is definitely not true. Even the TA mentioned how the midterm wasn't fair for many, the final was worse.

Teaching wise, he does a good job in explaining concepts and making them easier. Does a bad job in preparing you for the midterm and finals though. Just tells you to study the quizzes and practice problems, but both midterm and finals, some of the questions on those exams never once were discussed nor appeared in problem sets. Not good.

Expects extensive self teaching and assumes strong knowledge of complex concepts. Midterm was very difficult and unrealistic given the time limit. Even the TA, a master's student in quantitative finance, stated he could not finish the exam in time. Joke of a class, considering students are paying lots of money to only have GPT teach them...

He is probably the best math professor I've ever had. MFEII is a hard class, but he really does his best to prepare you. My biggest piece of advice would be GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He is willing to help and wants you to get better. Definitely recommend!!

arrogant and condescending when asked a question by a student. Makes you feel dumb for having an inquiry about something. He teaches as if you are supposed to know everything already and its just a review course or something. Not a bad teacher, but he is way too arrogant and discouraging to ever take again.

Professor Oveys is the best professor I've had at NYU. His passion for math and teaching shows, even at 8 am. He's always willing to help beyond office hours, offering both math help and career advice. After a few years away from school, I had all math and MFE 1 fundamentals forgotten, but with his help, I still enjoy MFE 2. Highly recommend.
Unnecessarily hard quizzes and tests. Will include random math that he didn't cover in class on exams and expect you to know it.
Took his calc 2 class over the summer. His class is great, but I didn't put in much effort and got a B+.

I liked him a lot. He is very enthusiastic which made it easy to listen to him. Highly arrogant, he definitely gives all of his students funny looks if they ask a simple question. Calc is hard, but you can't get a much better math teacher than him.

calc 3 is already hard enough, so take oveys to make your life easier! he is a great teacher, explains stuff super clearly. everything you see on the exam can be found in examples given in the class notes and taught during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Might be one of the easiest courses I've taken at NYU. Professor Oveys is a great lecturer but there's no need to attend in person, as all of his lectures are recorded via Zoom. Super helpful outside of class if you email him. His pace is super slow with new material, which means that it is super easy to catch up! Take him! Easy A!

He made a math class so much less daunting for someone who doesn't like math! He is super clear and concise, so organized, drops 3 lowest quiz grades and lowest hw grade. Exams and quizzes are structured the same as problems done in class. Attendance is not mandatory and he records all the lectures. He makes the class really easy to do well in!

Prof. Oveys is very very clear and organized. He explains everything step by step and thoroughly. He is kind of scary and his exams are hard so make sure you study for them early. Overall, a great professor and I recommend.
Great professor. very accessible outside of class. wants people to do well and is very generous in grading. take for calc 3
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His Great Ideas in Math class was great.  Pretty interesting topics and made showing up to an 8am worth it.  Total of ~11 quizzes, 6 problem sets, and 3 significant tests.  He drops your 3 lowest quizzes, 1 lowest problem set, and (this semester, not sure about others) replaced your lowest midterm with your final exam grade.  Definitely recommend.

This professor is a GEM. I have been afraid of math all my life but Professor Oveys really made this course seem like a piece of cake. He grades you with 5 problem sets, 2 midterms, and 1 final. The final was basically a combination of both the midterms, so as long as you put work into this class and study, you should be good. Definitely pick him!!

It's honestly the content that is challenging but his exams are totally doable the problem sets are very challenging but he gives 2 weeks to do them so dont hold them off. Quizzes about every 3 classes total worth 20% of your grade so dont slack off. there will not really be a curve maybe 1% if any so dont rely on that

Professor Oveys makes this QR course really manageable, even for non-STEM students. The class policy is generous - no calculator needed, and you can drop quizzes and problem sets. Unstuck ai was a big help for studying too.
This was a tough class and I don't think the professor made it more manageable.
Nice professor. Make the effort and you get an A.

I took this class in the summer when it was very fast paced. Professor Oveys made that harder by speaking really fast and expecting students to know exactly what he's saying without giving explanations. I had to rewatch most of the class recordings and also watch youtube videos to basically teach myself the content. Would not recommend.

Such a good core class- take it! Drops 3/10 quizzes and 1/6 problem sets. Final was basically the 2 midterms thrown together, so very easy to do well if you study. He is super available outside of class hours and wants to help students succeed- could tell he loved teaching this class :)

Amazing course if you aren't very good at math! The problem sets are a little bit of a pain but the weekly quizzes and exams are pretty easy. Professor drops the three lowest quizzes and two lowest problem sets (plus there are two surveys that you get an automatic 10/10 on if you do them) so it's not too hard to get a good grade in the course.
PROF OVEYS IS SUCH A KING. i was scared i wouldn't even pass this class at the beginning of the sem, but ended up with an A. all thanks to him

Hadn't taken a QR course in years. Professor Oveys organizes the course to make sure you never fall behind and have access to all of the material needed at all times. All of the problem formats that you will run into on exams and quizzes are covered in lectures. Best professor at NYU. Take his classes for QR credit!!

he is so kind, so nice, really care about students. Lecture always so clear and focused, the class material was really easy it's just basic stats concepts and you don't even need to bring a calculator or GDC. Class policy also nice, drop your lowest 3 quiz and 2 problem sets. You can always ask your questions online and he respond very quick!!

Attendance was mandatory in recitation (through quizzes), but not the lecture (which was posted online). As someone who is decidedly not a STEM person, FDTD was very much catered to us, making it not nearly as painful as it could have been. Steep difficulty curve that hits in the 2nd half of sem, but I managed without studying Too much.
He is overhyped on here. Decent at best, exercises in lecture are very easy compared to the homeworks and the exams.

Great professor, really knows what he's doing and his lectures are great. The best thing about him tho is that his notes are very neatly organized and easily accessible for when you are studying for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures. Generous grading, plug a big curve after the final.
Great professor, everything is very straightforward. If you do homework and look at problems discussed during lectures you'll do good on exams and quizzes. In-class quizzes are announced in advance.
Super clear lectures and straightforward tests. Exam questions are even discussed in class. He is funny and a lil sassy too. Take this class for CORE!
Great professor!!!

The reviews don't lie, literally the best professor. Class is set up so that it is easy to catch up if you start falling behind and he is very lenient. Problem sets were kind of a nightmare but that was the only thing that was hard.

Professor Oveys does a great job at making lectures easy to understand. The homework was a bit much but that's because summer classes are 6 weeks long. He made calculus easier than professors who taught full fall/spring semesters. He always makes sure you understand the concepts thoroughly and makes himself very accessible outside of class.

Professor Oveys is by far the best math teacher I've ever had. He's a very thorough teacher, is open to students' questions, and is very accessible via email and Campuswire. I was never good at math, but I actually understood what I was learning in his lectures, and though there was a decent amount of homework it wasn't awful. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best math professor I have ever had. He brought back my love for math, and it was because of the way he taught it in such an interesting and easy-to-understand way. He made Calculus easy to understand, and the fact he prioritized us actually understanding the concepts and not just the answers made Calculus an easier and more fun class for me.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! I despise Math, but I genuinely enjoyed his class. Lectures are very useful and clear. The quizzes and exams are very straightforward and are not made to trick students. He honestly made me consider taking Calc 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take him! BEST professor ever in NYU!!!

Pretty easy for me. The professor explains everything clearly and at least twice. Attendance is not necessary and the quizzes are easy. Problem sets are sometimes challenging but I enjoyed it. Highly recommended!!

The BEST math professor. period. Did not even take precalc in hs and I still managed to get an A in his class. I genuinely have never enjoyed math so much my life-- it was my favorite class last semester. The coding part may seem challenging at first but once you get used to it it's easy. If you are struggling, definitely show up to office hour.

Prof. Oveys is absolutely the best professor at NYU. He is good at teaching and making students understand difficult concepts. He will respond to your emails or questions on websites on time. He gives many examples in class to help you understand the ideas.
Professor Oveys is such a nice guy, he records lectures, writes notes in front of you, and is an easy grader. You learn a lot, and can do well in class. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: See the reviews, they aren't wrong. One of the best, most caring, and clear teachers I have ever had. Responds extremely fast outside of class for support, and the lectures are easy to follow and comprehend. If you have the opportunity to take his class, you are doing yourself a favor by enrolling.

Please choose Pro. Oveys's class if you can. His classes are structured, extremely clear, and funny! He will answer your questions immediately, and he also welcomes you to ask extra math problems which may not be in syllabus during his office hour. I will choose his math class with no doubt!! Please choose him for Math!!!
He is definitely a perfect professor but his tests are harder than others.

Professor Oveys is very passionate about the material he is teaching, however the lectures and the problem sets that acted as homework did not match. The work is primarily about coding, but the lectures and tests are statistically based. He's a great guy, but the course was a little misrepresented.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Oveys is an absolutely exceptional math professor. His office hours are very helpful. His exams are fair, and consist of questions previously discussed in lecture. He usually writes the final, so style is very familiar. I felt that the course prepared me well for how to handle more complex, interesting problems as well.
Best prof at NYU!! take him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hesam is the best professor I've had so far at NYU and I usually hate math classes. He really cares about his students succeeding!
Truly talented at teaching. Clearly cares about his students and will do everything he can to help you succeed in his class as well as actually understand the material.

This man is a bright ray of subshine on a rainy day. He is so passionate about math and it's apparent that he really wants everyone to understand and get excited about the material he's teaching. I've never written a rate my professor but this was an exception - I've been bad at math my whole life but he teaches in a way that is easy to understand.

Professor Oveys is a very good teacher in a difficult subject. Despite me not getting a great grasp of the material, he was constantly there to help. He made sure that I did well enough to move onto Math for Econ 2 although it would've been very easy for him to give me below a C and make me retake the course. He is extremely helpful and caring.
If you have the opportunity to take his class then choose him. I cannot imagine a better math professor.

do not listen to the reviews. although he is a very caring professor, the way he teaches is all over the place. he is always willing to help which is really good. honestly, I would recommend taking him but do not have high expectations as the reviews are saying. his tests are very hard but he will help you figure it out after. he is nice tho

He is god. Take a look at his rating. I have never known that a rating can be 5.3/5, literally off the chart. Really cares about students and even gives extra simple quizzes to improve everyone's grades. Drop a lot of low grades. Just pick him if you see his name on the course you have to take. You will know how professional and kind he is.
Professor Oveys is extremely helpful and willing to resolve any questions and concerns from students. He makes sure that everything is clear and organized. Choose him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I recommend this professor to everyone. You will not regret it.
Take his course. He is a patient and very clear professor.
This professor is awesome.
Truly has a gift for teaching math. TAKE HIM!!!

The course is hard but Dr. Oveys does his best to help out students and make it as easy as possible. He is a very caring guy and genuinely has a passion for the subject matter making him very willing and able to help students as much as he can.

For MFEI, there are 3 exams in total, weekly quizzes, several web assigns and problem sets. This may sound like a lot, but it is necessary for the understanding of this course. And for each category, only the first few top scores will count towards the total. His notes were clear and organized. If I get the chance, I'd like to take him again.

He is really helpful on and off the classroom. Cal 3 definitely isn't an easy class, but he is inspirational and makes the class flow well. Homeworks can be tricky, but as long as you follow on classes you should be alright. Really great professor with solid knowledge storage and clear logic, take him if you can.

Professor Oveys was by far the best professor I had this semester. He is thorough with his lectures and wants you to learn. I don't really like math, but I enjoyed this course. 8 am's are usually a drag, but his class was worth it.

Giant in the Maths department. He is really good at explaining things and provide intuitions. His lecture notes are the best that I've ever seen. If you ask a question on Campuswire, you may get his reply alomost instantly. Detailed instructions, caring and helpful, recommended.

He is a really good professor. He took good notes in class with helpful examples and easy to access outside of class. He is willingness to help student when you don't understand the concept. I email him my question and he asked me to go to his office for better explanation not during office hour. Please do not hesitate to take his class.

Easily one of the best professors NYU has to offer. His lectures are great and he truly has a gift for explaining things. There is a good amount of homework and they were challenging, but overall they were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very clear in presenting material, and quickly responsive in answering questions outside of class. Don't expect the questions on the exams to be very hard or unfamiliar since they're basically the same level of difficulty of the examples he gives out in lecture.
He is a real gem! I like him! his class is very organized and interesting!
The most well-rounded professor I've had. The other reviews summarize him well; he is friendly, well-organized, accommodating, but also good at what he does. Take Professor Oveys!

Really good lecturer, I love his energy, and he reviews stuff nicely and succinctly. Generous grader, even gave a free 100 on a quiz that happened to line up poorly with a tough exam. Extremely accessible outside of class, he responded to campuswire questions insanely fast. Fair tests, and psets can be tough, but he helps a lot if you ask.

Why can't give 0!The WORST professor ever! Definitely destroy my semester! Do not care about anyone even she attempt to pretend she does. The only answer is the one that she agree with. Vague grading standard, seems like she want to fail EVERYBODY in the class!If you even care a little about your mental health and grade, DO NOT TAKE HER ANY COURSE!
She is not inspiring teaching at all, as long as your answer is not the answer she wants, she will torture you like a prisoner.

Contents are okay though. But as an instructor, she is puzzling, not caring, not easy to communicate. She loves cold call and will not agree with what you said if your answers are not what she wants.
Extremely tough grader.
RUN AWAY AT ONCE!!! TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE!!!

gives bad feedback on assignments and you will never know what you lost points for. probably worst prof ive had at stern so far shes genuinely so not understanding of anything; wont give you leeway at all regardless of the circumstances. havent got my grade yet and ive never felt this compelled in the middle of a course to write a review

Participation matters so so much in Dr. Hall's classes, and as long as you talk and pay attention, you'll do perfectly fine. Spends a lot of time giving feedback (GO TO OFFICE HOURS) and will reward improvement massively

Were you the star of the Socratic seminars back in high school? Then this class is for you. Classes are 20% intro and maybe lecture, then 80% class discussion led by group discussion leaders. For Hall's first year teaching the class, she did well and learned along the way. Feedback helps struggle with transition from high school to college essays

The exams (60% of your grade, all free response) are super heavy on memorization of facts, places, things, and years. And that information is nowhere on the slides (usually just pictures), so you better hope that you have good notes because the grading isn't lenient. I and several of my classmates had the worst exam grade of our life in this class.

Course is not very organized, but workload is nonexistent. All you need to do is memorize the names, facts, and significance of archaeological sites and a handful of important concepts covered in lecture for the exams. A few chances for extra credit. Very light, but not an easy A as you still have to study. Overall a decent choice for soc sci core.

Not very engaging, and the lectures are essentially just images with no captions, names or dates that he will expect you to memorise and discuss in detail on exams. The course itself is not very well organised and professor provides very little framework to think about the VAST amount of information you are expected to internalise.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A kind, knowledgable, + accessible professor. I think he is a quiet lecturer who is not super engaging. Try not to skip lectures since he goes over a lot of info that's not on the slides (they're basically just pictures). A *lot* of memorization, tests weighed 60% of final grade and I spent quite some effort studying. Don't take if you want easy A.

Prof Iovita is clearly an expert in his field, but he forgets that he's teaching an intro-level class with students who have no idea what he's talking about. Harsh grader on tests and expects you to remember a tiny details. Also the textbook covers a lot of material that you need to take notes for. TAKE HUMAN EVOLUTION BEFORE TAKING THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My least fav class of sem. He spoke so quietly & lectured the whole time. Said we needed no pre-reqs but each week would talk about how we should already know things he was referencing. Final paper is on nothing he covers, it's 15 pgs of research on anything. He's nice, but all the readings are very data heavy. Don't take unless you're in anthro
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: IGNORE OTHER REVIEWS, unless you're reading for the drama. This is one of the most interesting, funny and help professors at NYU. He is passionate, caring and more than willing to work with students.

Professor Iovita is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject, and his lectures and discussion classes reflect this. The readings assigned are very interesting, but do require engagement. Additionally, Professor Iovita is generous with his time and his office hours are very helpful. Overall, this class was fascinating and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Iovita has a deep command of the subject matter, and the time he takes into preparing for lectures--even online ones--really shows. There's a steady stream of work--you can't coast, but the work pays dividends. He draws connections between the big questions in the field--which are big questions about life--and the reading for each week.

It might be bc we're online, but it was really disappointing, I would've thought a class on migration would be a lot more interesting. It was an endless cycle of reading 4-6 10pg papers, writing a response every week to them, and a lecture/discussion about what we read. There's also two 10 page essays as a midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class wasn't super hard, just go to lecture and pay attention you should be fine. However Radu is the most egotistical narcissistic human on the planet. Seriously very rude, never want to interact with that dude again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The midterm was 30% and final 40% of the grade (30% for lab) which makes this class very difficult because your grade relies almost entirely on the exams. He was new to teaching Early Societies and Culture so I think thats why, however he's very enthusiastic about what he's teaching and I never dreaded going to his lectures

Okay prof. The class really isn't AS hard as other people are saying - you just need to go to every lecture and pay attention/take notes and actually listen to what he says. The tests are stressful, but not impossible (and he's very generous with grading). Didn't even touch the textbook - didn't need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I thought I'd wait until after the final to post. This was ridiculous for an intro course. It's not that the material is that difficult to digest -- it's that Radu gives no guidance in terms of what to study. His tests are practically impossible to prep for, and 2 exams  70% of your grade. The TA's are great. He's unhelpful. I did well, but no.

If you're not an Anthro major, don't take class with Radu. His lectures involve quite a bit of rambling, he's non-specific about what'll be on the midterm or final. His TA's are wonderful. But unless you want to memorize an entire textbook and half a semester's worth of lectures for a test with 14 questions on it, take another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Radu seems very passionate about his field, but for a non-anthro major taking the course as a core requirement, it could be intense at times. Go to lectures... the tests are almost entirely on the material covered in lectures (and the slides he posts won't be v. helpful since there are few words). TAs very nice, and little weekly work, just tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Thoughtfully designed course that integrates storytelling from his real cases, key concepts, and readings effectively. The prof is extremely knowledgeable, experienced, super kind, and engaging. One of my favorite professors and classes. It's remarkable how much I've learned so far and the friends I've made. Posting now as reg. is soon-. Take it!

Extremely smart and absolutely knows his material. Kind and funny professor. But a large percentage of every class is just him telling funny or interesting stories that don't relate to the material. The homework thoroughly incorporates concepts and cases, but don't expect educational material in his lectures.

He is a great professor. His lectures are genuinely interesting, and he encourages participation. 

He is a very helpful and reachable professor. But his classes are demanding and require you to actually read and do the work. Make sure you do the required readings!! His assignments were helpful and relevant. I gained a lot from his class.

definitely would describe him as "quirky". his classes aren't your typical lecture style, he encourages participation and WILL call on a random person if he wants to. I really liked his option of opting out of the final in exchange for a B/B+ in the class

E&L is the first class that genuinely feels like i'm having a conversation with an old friend (coming from someone in Gallatin). He is very talented in his delivery in that you will be engrossed in the class and he has a great personality! Very caring professor and truly wants his students to succeed. Sad I can't take more classes with him (senior)

Goated professor. My favorite class I've taken throughout university. If you want a "sage on the stage" class where the professor sits and reads slides at you while you memorize definitions and drill content - Rich isn't the professor for you. Much more of a collaborative approach and you need you get out what you put into the class.

I will forever remember Professor Rich and his class. Rich creates such a friendly and interactive learning environment where I not only learn about law, but also about life. He built community both with him and with my fellow peers. I left the class knowing everyone's name and speaking to all 25 students at least once throughout the semester!
Unc is the goat

Rich is the BEST professor at Stern! His teaching style, the use of telling stories, allows for us to have a real world grasp of the concepts taught in this class. The stories help a lot when writing the legal papers. Rich also cares immensely about his students!! If you ever have a problem you can always talk to him, he gives the best advise!

Rich is one of the best professors that you can take at Stern!! He cares tremendously about the well being of his students. He is very accessible to talk about class, career advice, or just life in general. Although he does not use lecture slides, his use of story telling provides a better outstanding of the topics learned in the class.

Professor is well-liked by many of his students across different classes, likely due to his friendly/peer-like approach. However, I believe that it is negative to blur teacher/student relations – it obvious in class and a bit uncomfortable to witness at times. The class itself: a good intro to law, weekly stories, no slides, very fair grading/hw.

He's a tweaker, I can't lie, but he's a super fun professor who cares if you get the content. If you can deal with his "bits" and understand the meaning of why he does it, you'll do well in his class. If you ask for help in your life, he'll buy you dinner to talk about it. 10/10 would geek in his class again.

Rich... I have so many good things to say about this professor. Ultimately, he will be one of the best professors you take at NYU - if you have the opportunity to take his course. I highly recommend that you take this opportunity, as taking his class was transformational for me and many others. He is a truly caring and exceptional person.

He is the best professor for LBS. It was an amazing class and I'm smarter and better because of Rich. So grateful I had the opportunity to be in his class. I've never had a professor who does more for their students. It's truly surprising how much effort he puts in, with unique sessions and opportunities both in and outside the classroom.
GOAT! Clear, informative, and fun lectures; always available for help; one of the best humans you will ever meet; holds the benchmark at a respectful high level. It was an honor to be in his class.

He's an exceptional professor, engaging, entertaining, and incredibly knowledgeable. This course and the professor have been a highlight of my four years at NYU. Every class was enjoyable, and the effort put into the work was absolutely worth it. My advice to future students: ask questions about assignments — it's a great way to earn higher scores.

Yes he is nice, but don't take this class. His grading is hard and inconsistent. The assignments aren't helpful in learning the material yet time consuming. In class we would spend the whole time talking about anything but the course material. I didn't learn. I am an extremely dedicated student yet feel it was merely impossible to get an A.

Rich is not only an amazing professor, but a caring mentor and an adult the students need. He is always willing to make time for the students for anything, and is very responsive to any kind of questions the students may have regarding the course. I consider myself lucky to have met Rich throughout my time at Stern.

Rich genuinely tries to build relationships with every one of his students, and fosters a caring community within the classroom. As a practicing attorney, Rich prefers to draw upon his own experiences to teach fundamental concepts. Classes can be lecture-y but overall a great experience if you buy into Rich's style of teaching. Highly recommend it.

Rich was, in my opinion, overall lackluster. Frequently got sidetracked and most of class time was spent on him rambling. I would recommend taking another LBS prof if you want to actually learn something.

Rich's ELAW class is engaging and challenging, but worth the effort. While the workload can be heavy, his interactive teaching style and relatable stories make it an enjoyable learning experience. Unstuck study was a game-changer for my study prep - highly recommend!

Rich is an amazing professor. His classes are very engaging and are something to look forward to every week. He is always happy to help in any way that he can outside of class, and he goes above and beyond. I would definitely take any other courses that he teaches!
The best professor I have ever had throughout all my education.

THE GOAT! Rich is one of the most amazing instructors I've ever had. From telling amazing stories in class to offering unique perspectives on life itself, Rich stops at nothing to foster an amazing community in his class. I plan to take just about every other course he offers. He is amazing!

The best professor I've had at NYU, and that's not "puffery." He truly cares about all his students, and his classes are always engaging, and filled with relatable, real-life stories. This class, my second with Rich, was another incredible course. I learned a vast amount of valuable information. Hands down, he's the perfect professor for anyone!

Among the best educators I've ever encountered. Rich speaks well about every topic that is discussed and is very engaging. This class was by far the best class experience at NYU. Overall, he is very easy to talk to and it is so obvious he cares about everything and everyone. Grading is honest! Work hard! Don't BS! Learned a lot! Loved it!

Among the very best professors at NYU. Classes are engaging and Rich has plenty of insight into the topics. His stories are a very pleasant way to learn the material. I found all the deliverables enjoyable opportunities to learn and he is available at all hours to answer questions or for advice. The class is challenging but definitely worthwhile.
He is such a good person but like for a 2 credit class he gives so much work. He doesn't teach and grades harshly. Don't take this class unless you wanna get HELLA work for little payoff.

I like Rich as a person, but as a professor, he's hard to follow. He encourages class connections, and I appreciate that, especially in Stern courses. However, he has no slides, class notes, etc. and tells stories rather than actually lecture. There is a significant amount of coursework, and thankfully you can do it in groups.

Professor Hendler (Rich) is AMAZING! He is a fantastic prof and storyteller. A lot of work but definitely worth it. I learned about law and myself working with my group. The LawGame was definitely the best experience at NYU. Rich is so enthusiastic about what he teaches and always willing to help. Rich, the course, and my new friends are awesome.

Rich is awesome - the class has a solid work load, but his comments on the briefs and papers are super clear and help you know how to improve for the next assignment. Classes are engaging, and he's genuine and really cares about his students and how they perform. He's very reachable and great with arranging meetings with students for questions!

He's entertaining and "cool" at first since he has no slides and just tells stories each class. Then it's annoying knowing other LBS classes learn useful content that'll help them in the business world and we just get performative stories about how he changes students' lives. I wish I took a diff prof and actually learned something concrete in LBS.

Rich is an incredible professor, and I've learned a lot under his guidance. 

Elaw has been an engaging class and a great experience overall, as Rich makes the class a comfortable space to learn. While the class is demanding for 2 credits, if you have the time and want a fun but challenging course about law, I definitely recommend taking this one.

Course was awesome and informative, and I received the best life advice. Very fun and engaging professor who knows his stuff and uses interesting ways, in class activities and stories to teach the material. Enthusiastic about the topics and life and very willing to help students. Rich is a fantastic person and professor. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The kindest, most joyful, honest  and caring professor I've ever had so far. Full of knowledge and wisdom. Rich made law very interesting and is encouraging towards students and understanding. Grading criteria and expectations are clear. He is everything I've ever wanted in a professor. Rich has bern the most impactful prof in my college career.

This class is a fan favorite for a reason. I wish it was a little more structured but I still felt I learned a lot. Rich wants to build connections with all his students which is really special. Grades wise it's a lot of group projects and briefs. So stimulating assignments but not too many. The course objectives were clearly stated too.

ELaw is definitely tough but so worth it. I never plan to be a lawyer, and never thought I would take a law class, but I'm so glad I did. He is the funniest guy ever, with so many good stories to tell!

I love Rich. Ask anyone who's taken his classes and they'll tell you the same, for good reason. He's so caring and kind with his students to the point where it inspired me. He just has such warm energy. Entertainment Law is two credits but the workload is pretty heavy, but nothing unmanageable. He gives lots of pointers. One of the best profs here.

Rich is awesome, but the class definitely requires effort. Not a light workload and could be challenging but you get the most out of it if you participate anyway so overall it's a great class. Rich is always easy to reach and helpful, he cares a lot about his students.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Whether you're planning on law school or not, this is a really interesting class and Rich was an amazing professor. He always provides helpful feedback on assignments and genuinely wants students to do well. If you have a chance to take ELaw, you should!

Rich is such a caring and fantastic professor! He is knowledgeable about the law and is able to express the information clearly. There is a lot of work, but Rich was super easy to contact if I had any questions, and I felt that all of the assignments were actually relevant and worthwhile. Truly someone who wants to get to know his students better.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rich is a phenomenal professor - one of the best I've had at NYU. He cares so much about his students and clearly values each individual and their effort. Feedback on assignments and grading criteria was always clear, and Rich took extra time to discuss any questions or comments that we had. Workload is not light, but the class is so worth it.

Entrep. Law in Practice was definitely intense. (Make sure you have someone who's super part time/multiple members part time or the workload will crush you near the end). The law game ranges from drafting contracts to writing motions/pleadings. Rich as usual is intelligent, caring, and inspirational. He makes you work for that A. Love him.

Rich is a great professor who really wants to see his students succeed. He's a tough grader, so meeting with hime outside of class is invaluable to understanding what he is expecting to see for assignments. This class is really fun as long as you choose your group members wisely. Keep in mind it's more like 4 credits than 2 credits.

Prof Hendler is a great teacher who explains concepts in a fun way and makes every class interesting. He tells stories and uses examples of cases that are really engaging. However, the feedback on grades is a little unclear and you don't really know how you do until the very end of the class. Though he is accessible in and out of class for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The toughest professor I've had at NYU. However, he deserves to be respected. A great man who knows his stuff really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is the single best professor you will ever have at NYU. Professionally, Rich possesses a uniquely powerful ability to engage you in Law, a conventionally boring subject, through stories. I seldom pay attention in school, here, I never missed a beat. Personally, he is an inspiring mentor, a wise guide, and a true friend.

Rich has been a standout professor in my college experience. I've never met a professor who is so proactive in reaching out to and caring for his students. He has an ability to make you interested in anything he's saying. I took the class solely because it was a requirement, but left the class with a genuine interest in the topic.

Rich is an excellent professor and great person to be around as well. His lectures are very gripping, seamlessly humoring students with life stories while also tying them into the material masterfully. Excellent professor that makes sure you feel good understanding the material and as a person as well. Very understanding and friendly. Best prof!

I absolutely love Hendler and his hilarious stories. He is a well respected professor at Stern and is always available to chat with his students even when class is not in session. He is very fair and you can tell that he loves to teach, which motivated me to try hard in his class.

He's a nice guy and is always there for his students. He is very respectable. His grading toward the end of the course was a little unclear. If you make plans with him, show up and double check and confirm, otherwise he will get mad.

THE BEST PROFESSOR AT NYU HANDS DOWN. Rich is honestly such a genuine human being who actually cares about the people he interacts with. I highly recommend his class and getting to know him as a person. He is there for his students and doesn't try to make the class a stressful environment. Love him to pieces!!!

Absolutely recommend!!! He actually cares about each individual student and is willing to help regardless of your level of understanding in his class. He's willing to make career connections for you as well. Attendance is required and the workload is fair. Definitely take any of his classes. Such a great professor. Thanks Rich!

rich is so nice and kind and honestly my fav prof in NYU. He is caring to all students in and outside the class, gives a lot of advice on life and law-related career path (and 5$ Starbucks gift card lol) His lecture is fun and inspirational. tough grader but you learn

During this semester of Zoom, Rich made himself accessible at nearly any hour of the day to help my team and me. He invests so much of his time in us. Amazing how much he cares! Super entertaining lectures. Assignments can be a lot for some so start them early. Rich is great guy, fantastic teacher, and a great resource for anyone. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Rich is the greatest professor on planet earth. He makes NYU and the world a better place. Great teacher, incredibly passionate and attentive, extremely caring. Love his lectures. Work is moderate to heavy, two/ three group projects, readings are manageable, and final exam (can be done in groups). Do the work and you will learn. A must class!

Rich is an incredibly caring and kind person, but his teaching style isn't for everyone. I oftentimes felt lost in his class, and while I enjoyed hearing his stories, I oftentimes didn't quite see how they connected to the law concepts we were supposedly learning. Grading criteria really isn't clear and the workload is more like a 4 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rich's Entertainment Law course is one of the best classes at NYU. His lectures are well-thought-out, educational, and amusing! He makes sure you will laugh, learn, and form lifelong friendships with your classmates. You will also become very comfortable with reading cases quickly. No matter your major / career goal, this is a must-take class!!!

Rich is the best professor I have had the pleasure of taking! He truly wants his students to perform well and succeed. His lectures are entertaining, engaging, and fruitful for many aspects of life. His teaching style and warm heart will leave you wanting to take every class he offers. The Law/StartUp Game will teach you a lot and is loads of fun!!

Learned a lot of material. Very entertaining and educational class. Rich was terrific in front of the class or by zoom. Totally engaging, wonderful, fun and clear lectures. He and his teaching are awesome. Classes were the highlight of my tough semester.  He is simply a great person. Wish there were manymore profs like him. One of the best at NYU!

Rich is a very nice man, yes. However, I felt that my time was often wasted in his E-law class. We only met once a week for an hour and fifteen minutes, yet consistently the only time we spent discussing homework or entertainment law terms/language were the last 15 minutes of class. You're going to have to teach yourself in this course.

Rich is the most caring professor at NYU. He really makes a space where he has everyone treat each other like family as interpersonal relationships are important in life. E-Law readings may be difficult in the beginning, but they get so much easier each time. I promise. P.S. Meet with him outside of class! He's also a great friend to have.

A great teacher and person. A very kind prof who really takes you through how to think about law in the business world. Rich is a special person and his class was a special experience. There is no one else like him or nothing else like his class.

Law through the Lens of Film is a broad overview of law so you'll learn alot. Since it's not law school, it won't be too specific. Rich is lenient with the grading if you do the work, if you don't, bad things happen. The class is mostly discussion/trials. I honestly enjoyed it. The hw is movies and law memos, not bad, and enjoyable if you care. :)

Hendler is an amazing person and one of my favorite professors. He definitely cares about students' academic, professional and wellbeing. I learned a lot of new material and new skills, grew as a student and enjoyed every class. I wish the class was 4 credits. Rich provides quality feedback and is very approachable and inspirational. Def take it.

Rich is a great human and a caring and excellent teacher of so many things. Rich is the best prof and his class is one of the best at NYU. He is super-engaging and makes learning law very enjoyable. You will learn lots more than just the law. The way he talks about life makes everyone in the room feel loved. Truly an experience!

Rich is by far one of the best professors in the world. He is inspirational, genuinely cares about everyone, and is very willing to meet outside of class to discuss anything (reserve his coffee chats early). He is dedicated to teaching and you will learn so much. Awesome class.

Rich is awesome and incredibly caring!! Over the weekend before the break, he spent hours with me talking about class material and my life. Amazing, right! He is equally awesome in front of the class. Totally engaging, wonderful, fun, and clear lectures. I can't wait to take his other classes.

I really wanted to love this class, but it was a bit of a let down. The professor doesn't so much lecture as share personal anecdotes and you won't learn more than what the average person already knows about law. I'm pre-law and I can say there are much better classes for BEMT at Tisch or CAS for media.

I love this class. Everything is clear, the atmosphere is qreat. The workload is heavy but manageable. I learned a lot about entertainment law and about me. We're encouraged to ask questions, foster new friendships outside of class, and develop as a student/person. Prof's feedback was excellent. I highly recommend Rich's class to everyone!

Rich is great! He is very caring and inspirational. You will learn a lot of good information about Entertainment Law and also about life as well. Quite a bit of reading and work for a two credit class, but well worth it!

Rich is the best professor at NYU. However, his final exam is very difficult. Everything besides homework is allowed in groups and his class isn't a simple lecture. It's an experience. I didn't get an A but I am so glad I got to know this professor. I learned how to make contracts and to really talk to other people. He's so loving. Take him!

I joined a class with Rich after reading all the rave reviews. All I can say is, no one was exaggerating. It has been a true blessing to meet him, as he is a brilliant BRILLIANT professor who cares about and inspires every single student he works with. He enlivened law in a way I would never have thought possible. No superlative could be sufficient

Most fulfilling professor I have ever had. His approach and class are such refreshing approaches to the standard approach to teaching. Rich is unbelievably caring, gives solid feedback, is a very fair grader, and he is the best even with a heavy work load. I give him an A+.

One of the most sincere and warm-hearted persons I have ever met. Rich is great in front of the class. He's totally engaging, wonderful and fun, and he is all of this and more in person. His lectures are clear and every class makes you love the material as much as he does. (I don't want to be a lawyer.) Hendler is a rock star!

Rich is hands down the best professor at Stern. He enjoys what he does and is very passionate, understanding and supportive. Rich is always available and gives you excellent feedback on assignments. I have learned more from his class and him than I thought possible. Seriously, take elaw and seek his help in anything and everything.
Great
Rich lights up the classroom, NYU, and the world.

E-Law changed my life forever. Rich's class made me fall in love with law and figured out my career. His lectures and style are exceptional. He's a great storyteller and he makes class fun to learn. He's always approachable and willing to help. If he is not the best professor at NYU, then I don't know who is. Take his class!

Loved his law classes, and love the professor and the man. He is INCREDIBLE! ELAW and E&L were great classes that covered an in depth look into laws affecting the entertainment and entrepreneurial space. The delivarable and games are so worth it. I am a smarter and more adaptable person because of Rich. I would take any of his classes again!

Rich is the best and most caring professor I have ever had. Wish the class was twice a week. He is a sensational professor and person. He uses up to date cases and scenarios that add to the readings. His ability to make the class and law fun and break down legal principles into an understandable framework made this the best class I took at NYU.

Rich is an unbelievable professor and person. He is inspiring and loving and cares like no other. The load can be daunting for some but we are at NYU to learn and work hard. And I am proud to say I definitely did both. Rich is the BEST. Take his class and you'll leave a better person and student. Ask anyone, except the writer below.

Richard Hendler is funny, caring, nice, and smart. Prof Hendler is intense, purposely assings more homework than you can handle, and a little crazy. Very imporatant to understand the difference between the person and the Professor. In many other classes they are the same. In his classes, they are not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Rich is the best prof Ive ever had at NYU. Hes literally the reason why I decided to stay at NYU and not transfer out. Hes so inspirational and has changed the way I look at my acedemic career. However, there is a lot of work involved in the class so dont take the class if you already have a lot. But hes a fair grader. I recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Just took class; fantastic prof, really cares and his stories have a purpose - they help you learn. Great at keeping my interest and so helpful outside of class. Connects concepts to real and new legal cases. Rich cares about students and his lectures. He's knowledgeable, dedicated and so positive. Take Rich's class; best prof I've had yet.

Definitely take any of Rich's classes if you get the chance. One of the best classes I've taken at NYUStern. He is not only a great prof but he is also a ridiculously amazing person. Highly, highly recommend Rich. He changed my life. If you keep up with the projects, most are group ones, and readings (many but manageable), you'll be more than fine.

Hands down most awesome professor that NYU has to offer. Very inspirational person and very knowledgeable about the subject. Great storyteller, he helps always, and makes you excited for class; Genuinely cares for you, your well-being, and your future. Heavy workload; very real work . Class becomes your 2nd family and is life changing.

One of the best at NYU! Rich is awesome, intelligent, laid back, funny, and helped me understand many facets of entertainment law. No doubt he knows his stuff very well and will make sure his students do too, inside and outside of class. Terrific feedback on assignments. There is a lot of reading and writing but it helps you understand the material

Rich is a must-take for anyone with an interest in law or entertainment. Rich is a spectacular professor and an even better human being, His classes are very interesting and relevant. His workload is heavy, so manage your time. In the end, it as so worthwhile as I learned more than I could ever imagine and I found my passion by taking this class.

Hands down and by far the best class and professor at NYU. Rich is smart, engaging, funny, and understanding, and he managed to the get the most out of me. There is a lot of work, but all of it is very interesting. I cannot express how much I disagree with the other student in my class. I learned so much from him about entertainment law and life!

Alright, so I know NYU says this class is 2 credits but don't believe them, its more like 6. You will have a ton of hw if you take this class, specifically group projects. DONT take if you have a lot on you plate. The actual class also isnt great for actually learning about the law. Rich is really cool though, very caring, and is funny. 3/5.

Rich is really the best professor I have ever met. He is so kind and devoted to his students. Love him! There were many readings but the course was inspirational and interesting. Because of this course, I know that law can also be an interesting thing. The lecture was full of happiness. I enjoyed a lot.

A legend and iconic. He is by far the best professor I have ever had in life. He knows all of the material and his lectures are amazing and fun. He develops a community, is very approachable, and creates a very safe place to learn (no fear about making mistakes; in fact he refers to those as pre-successes.  Many deliverables/readings, worth it tho.

Rich is the best professor at NYU.  I'm going to be honest, this class is absolutely a challenge, but I have never enjoyed a class so much at NYU.  You don't mind the work because he is so supportive and is there to help you whenever you need.  He loves getting to know his students, and his stories are amazing.

Fantastic teacher! Engaging and fun. Hhe brought entertainment law to life, and helped us to understand how law works in the entertainment sectr. Not only is he a great professor, but he also is one of the most caring persons I have ever met. You must take this course. It's a wrap.

As a Tisch student who grew up in a family of attorneys, this class is ridiculous. This Stern class in particular did not offer the information I was looking for - considering it's called Entertainment Law, I expected to learn about drafting contracts and optioning, not case law and judicial opinions. Tisch BEMT classes are more practical by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing class! One of the best professors. Rich loves to teach and it shows. He brings unbelievable energy and passion to law with his engaging discussions. Rich constantly inspires through his lectures and personal anecdotes. The amount of deliverables are not for the faint of heart. Put in the effort, you will learn a lot about law and yourself.

Learned more in Rich's class than I have in any other. His expectations are high; class material is very relevant, current and interesting. You must put the time in. Although it's a two credit class, you will learn more than most four credit classes but don't expect a light load. His teaching style is amazing and he is more than an amazing person.

Hendler's an amazing professor who cares about his students. Course material is very relevant to many aspects of life. He's very intense, though; wouldn't recommend his class if you're not comfortable being put on the spot for no reason. Lots of case readings and group work. Enjoyed the class but wish I'd taken it when I had a less hectic schedule.

By far the best professor I have ever had! Excellent class, excellent lecturer, and excellent person. Really knows a lot about the subject and presents the material well. More amazing he cares so much for students and supports you in and out of class. Only downside for some is there's a lot of readings and work. Well worth it in my opinion.

Absolutely the best professor at NYU!! He's extremely caring, understanding,  and smart and his lectures are entertaining and interesting. They are more like a conversation. I always look forward to class and  I have never met a teacher who cares so much for his students, in and out of class. Lastly, I learned so much for and made new friends.

Awesome and an extremely caring professor; he knows his stuff and he is very open to questions and makes class incredibly interesting with videos, discussions, videos, simulated trials, and cases. Honestly, he is terrific professor and person and the best professor I have ever had anywhere.

Incredibly warm and caring professor that I will remember for a long time. His class is very clear and he repeats the main ideas many times. A fair amount of work but you learn a lot and he lets you work in groups. My only regret is that I took this course senior year and didn't have a chance to take any of his other classes!

Hendler and all of his classes are amazing. He is one of the best professors/teachers I've ever. He’s well prepared; his class discussions are current & interesting; and he tries to get the entire class involved. Regarding feedback, he gives plenty during one on one time. Before you graduate, take any class with Rich. You will be thrilled you did.

Best teacher at NYU, so much passion and care. Classes are always engaging and thought provoking and Rich brings out the best in you. He cares about the person behind the student and works with you to become brighter and to find your passion. Rich will always make time for you for anything you need including feedback. You must take this course.
Didn't provide any feedback or engage independent thought from his students. Rich is a nice guy, but that's about it.

Rich is the nicest, most caring, and most supportive teacher I've ever had.  Not just in my college career, but in my entire life!!  He has completely given me a new sense of hope in teachers which I never would've had before I took his class. This is a man I plan on staying in touch with LONG after this class is over.
Wonderful class, wonderful guy. This man genuinely cares about his students.
One of the best professors at NYU, someone who truly cares about teaching and ALL his students

Hendler is incredibly smart, sharp, and passionate. Class is based on mini trials and is open discussion. His class will make you smarter, and a better thinker and speaker. Also you'll make lots of new friends. If you put in the effort, you'll do well. Hendler is generous with his time and will help you in any way possible. Great guy and class!

Don't graduate without taken Rich as a professor. This class is amazing, i never wanted to miss class, and you will learn so much. One of my favorite classes and professors. He encourages you to speak in class and sometimes he cold calls on students. So be prepared by reading the cases and announcements.

Rich is by far the best and most caring professor I've ever had at NYU. His ELAW class is engaging, challenging and fun. Rich is dedicated and available at almost all hours, cares about students and loves teaching. His class follows the syllabus (read it and the cases) but allows flexibility based on students' questions and comments. You'll learn!

As a person, I think he's great and very inspirational at that. But as a professor, I found his teaching methods to be unclear. It's never straightforward; he tries anecdotes that don't work. I'm all for a good time but he uses the exams as a way for you to learn (just google-ing everything like mad) which makes no sense to me.

Rich is a fantastic professor. He goes out of his way to make the class interesting, and has a ton of both legal and teaching experience to draw on. His final is tough, and he asks for your full attention on a lot of assignments, but if you want to be anywhere in the entertainment industry, his class is worth taking for sure.

Pf. Hendler is the best professor I've taken at NYU. I learned a ton and had a blast in the process. He really tries to make the class the best you've ever had. I'm taking him for LBS now and it's even better than ELaw because we have class twice a week. I highly recommended his classes.
Great professor and very interesting class, but there is A LOT of work - it's all worth it though. Not difficult to get a good grade.

Amazing! Made me want to go to Law school! He's a kind, caring, understanding professor, and wants to make sure you have fun and learn something. The work is tough but he knows that college is tough too, so as long as you're honest about your stress level, he'll always be willing to cut you a break. He really respects honesty and hard work.
Richard Hendler is the best teacher professor at NYU.
Seriously the best professor I have ever had. Makes the whole class a family. No joke. Difficult course but you won't regret taking him :)

His class isn't easy, but neither is law. You WILL learn a lot by the end, and despite the work, you'll have fun too. He's about as understanding, magnetic, and genuine as they come.
