Yes, his style is unstructured, but it's not that hard to keep up thanks to how fun he makes the material. People walk out of this class calling it the best in Stern.

One of the best and only professors I've encountered that is genuinely concerned about his students' well-being in and out of class. Rich's teaching style is engaging, and his personality is addictive- his class will become one that you will look forward to and one you wont want to miss. I urge even those without interest in law to take his class.

Coolest guy i no.. got to know him personally and really gets close with his students if he sees a spark of interest in them.. Chill guy once on his good side and the most down to earth professor out there
Hendler is the man. He's a great teacher - makes the material crystal clear. Also a great motivator. Loves what he does and it shows.
Great professor, very knowledgeably and helpful, and a amazingly fun class.  The exams are not easy, but I would highly recommend, and you really do learn a lot.

LOVED his class! It's not supper structured BUT he emphasizes actually learning rather then just spitting out information for a test.  I really enjoyed the class and I'm looking forward to taking business law in the fall!

Rich is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Having said that, however, if you are looking for a structured class with a fool-proof calendar so that you can read ahead of class, do not sign up for Entertainment Law. In my honest opinion, I do not believe that is the best way to learn anyways; Rich's class is entertaining and insightful.

The best professor I have ever had for my whole college career. Unlike other professors he treats students with understanding and respect and knows how to make a class interesting. Amazing person and professor, highly recommended.
Difficult but fair.

The class structure provided students with room for creativity, relaxation, and fun. Rich emphasizes the importance of networking and friendship in the business world, which is really appreciated. I loved this class!
He was the best professor I've had at Stern and one of the few professors in years that kept me interested for the entire class every week.

Hendler does not have a conventional teaching style. If you are looking for a strictly outlined class with all assignments and lectures standardized, this is not the class for you. A lot of reading and research is done on your own time because there is no book and an unclear syllabus. However,I learned a lot and it was in an enjoyable enviornment

Rich is quite unlike any other professor you will ever have at NYU. He teaches his students to seek passion in life, and is devoted to making lasting relationships. He sponsors networking, relationship builders for his student at local restaurants out of his own pocket. Class is fun, I look forward to it, it's of an hour and 15 min of entertainment

Hendler's kind of amazing. He's one of those teachers who "focus on the learning outside of the classroom." So he gives you the tools- you sort of interpret the material and figure stuff out. Lots of reading... but it's actually good stuff. he genuinely loves his students, and takes interest in our personal lives. All around great guy. Will miss.
I was skeptical at first, but I really like Prof. Hendler and think his teaching style makes this awful material much easier to learn. I really enjoy his class (and I HATE law).

He's a wealth of information if you really care about what your learning and you take the time to ask him.  Student line up to ask him questions after class and he's always attentive to them.  He catered the class to what we wanted to know and it was a completely stress free environment!
Rich is a great guy. His class is not for the faint hearted but you get to learn alot in his class and it's extremely enjoyable and challenging. By far one of the best professors in Stern!

This professor is by far one of the most challenging.  He does not flirt, but knows how to be humorous.  He does not brag about his achievements, but rather, brags about how happy he is and hopes that others will find that same hapiness out of life.  He's more about just class, he knows that we are not only students, but human beings as well.
He's an awesome guy!
Professor Hendler is incredible... VERY easy to connect to... he's totallt genuine despite his apparent over-mushiness!  Sweet guy!
No Comments

I am a female and I never even thought about any of those things being said about flirting...  Anyway, I got an okay grade and I thought he was a great teacher.  He is one of the few who truly cares about all students and loves to teach.

One of the best professors at NYU. He really makes class fun and you look forward to going to his class every day. I think the best thing about his class is the fact that everyone in his classes end up knowing each other, becoming friends, etc.
He is a little too fun... you are left to learn the material on your own when the final exam rolls around! Be prepared for lots of reading and two weeks of HELL during the Law Game!
No Comments
He is great.. I learned a lot

AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!! would take it again if I had the chance. Can tell he's very passionate about the subject matter and knows a lot about it too. Always added a layer of depth to the lessons and course!
he is the best professor

Professor Isikara is very understanding. He explains concepts very well, and I have learned a lot from him. He makes sure that class is not an added stressor. The quizzes we have are online, our assignments are group ones, and the exams are reflective of what we do in class.

Great professor, explains everything well and sets students up for success
Has a good personality as well

Professor Isikara was super understanding, and tried to make the best of online classes. He gives extra credit and does everything he can to make sure his students get As. His assignments mirror the midterm and final, so studying those and participating almost guarantees an A. He is very smart, but his lectures can be kind of slow and boring.

Great Professor. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and genuinely wants students to understand the topics and concepts. Quizzes, midterm, and final are online. If you have to take econ in LS, TAKE HIM!!!!!!

My favorite course yet! I loved how Prof.Guney teaches orthodox economic theories prefacing and post-facing the assumptions, and even implications of economic assumptions. Many other economic classes often end up technical-heavy, but he facilitates discussions of social welfare and environmental justice––which I appreciate a lot! Learned a lot.

Great prof. Explains everything well, takes the time to answer questions, always reachable, and tests are online. He is relatable but very professional, explaining concepts super clearly. Make sure to just listen in class and everything will be clear after his lecture.
He's a great professor. Midterm and final were online, and he gives students options for extra credit. Take him.

Professor Isikara is very passionate about his subject. If you do not may attention during lectures you are screwed but he makes sure that his lectures are very interactive and engaging and if you genuinely have an interest in Economics and want to take it with a professor who cares take his class. The Midterm was very long but open note to be fair

Super great, he does take home test and quizzes as well as giving a week for assignments that are done in a group. Really recommend if you need to take an economics class, participation and effort goes a long way with him.

Took Intro to Micro with Isikara. Explains concepts really well, and tries to make content more interesting by bringing real-world case studies and issues. 

Assignments aren't particularly difficult, and if you do the readings/pay some attention in class, workload is totally manageable. 

Very solid class, would def recommend.

Professor Isikara is a great professor. He truly cares about the things he teaches, and wants the students to understand it. He has a very interesting socio-political approach in economics. Overall, if you need to take economics in LS, take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Isikara is one of the most caring and understanding teachers I have had at NYU so far. His lectures are clear and provide great resources for outside class material access, including copies of all slides, lectures, and Zoom recordings. I highly recommend you take his class if it is an option! He works hard to make sure his students are ok

I really enjoyed taking microeconomics with Prof Isikara. Prof Isikara gave wonderful lectures that put a social and historical spin on economics. The class involves four group projects, which were very accessible and fair, as well as open-note quizzes and exams. Attendance and a little participation is important. Highly recommend.

Professor Isikara is the best professor I have ever had at NYU! I never thought econ would interest me but this ended up being my favorite class. He is so knowledgable and really cares about your learning. It's social and political approach to econ but I found that this approach made it more interesting.Take his class! I wish I could have him again

He really cares about providing comprehensive, engaging lessons. Microeconomics isn't always a fun subject but he tries to make it enjoyable for students. He takes time to explain concepts and ask for questions, sometimes the format/working of the quiz questions can be confusing but if you put in the work you can easily succeed.
the best teacher ive ever had at NYU, must take him because he's such a nice instructor.

I absolutely loved professor Isikara. The class really is designed to ensure that students thrive; he WANTS you to learn and get a good grade so he will go out of his way to make sure you do. Theres 4 group assignments (which are very easy), 4 multiple choice quizzes, midterm and final exam. Everything is open note. Definitely take him

Really nice guy, lectures are super straightforward, and he explains everything really well. He's clearly designed this class for students to do well in, just read the textbook (for your own sake if you are interested in econ) and you will most definitely get an A in this class. There is a midterm, final, 3 online quizzes and 4 group assignments.
What an incredible professor. If you have the chance, take him! He opened my eyes to a completely new type of Economics and made the class interesting. I wish I could take him for all four years.

Absolutely wonderful teacher. One of two profs I've had at NYU that's a 10/10. Truly passionate, cares about making his lessons interesting... if you want to start economics, and if you like participating, please take his class, because he's incredible.

Awesome guy. You can skim the readings, he goes over material a lot. He loves to relate textbook stuff to current events/progressive economic ideas, which makes class really fun; engage with him for sure. Exams/quizzes are fair, but questions are not too easy, you do have to prepalso, the time limits are the hardest part, make sure to go quick.

The prof gives a nice and interesting textbook with paragraphs corresponding to lectures, so it's enough just to either listen or read. He is nice and accessible. 4 quizes, 4 group projects and that's it, the exams are similar to them and graded not strictly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Isikara is one of the best professors at NYU! The course guidelines were clear right from the beginning. He makes sure each and every student understands the economic concepts clearly. Very caring, an easy grader, and makes the subject extremely interesting! One tip: The more you participate in lectures, the more fun you will have!

had him for my intro to econ LS course. All in all, excellent professor. Wasn't too fond of econ in HS but he really takes the time to introduce what many would consider as an otherwise tedious course to learn. Just participate, actually study with a friend or something and DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. As long as you work, you'll get an A.

He is honestly the best professor I have had at NYU. He is always available to talk to and really explains everything so clearly that you dont even need the textbook. He will make you work your ass off for a good grade and his homeworks/quizzes are hard/fair.

Course has very clear guidelines and assignment/quiz/exam dates are charted out from day one. Easily accessible through e-mail and office hours. Participation matters but can come in the form of forum posts, speaking in class, etc. Exams, group assignments, and quizzes all open note and fairly easy. Lenient and kind. Don't need to read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best teachers I have ever had. Super caring, always accessible outside of class, and an amazing person to have a conversation with. Readings are optional (but if you've never taken econ like me) they are SUPER helpful when following the lecture. Because its blended he grades on participation, but office hours satisfy that. study!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course material itself is not too hard, but he makes everything clear and understandable. Love the amazing analysis and "rants" he goes on in class about the defects of capitalism. Learned more than just boring textbook economics, he gave many relevant outside examples. Helps the student see the world of economics from a different perspective.

She gives you a decent amount of work but she is a nice teacher and it is fairly easy to get an A. I revised one of my drafts in like 30 minutes and she gave me a 92. You will have to read out loud and talk to others tho.

Tough grader, but amazing professor. She really cares about you and has good exercises to improve. Attendence is mandatory, but if you're actually sick and usually go to class she'll let some stuff slide.
I took her over the summer and she was an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about the students and tries her best to be understanding.

Great Professor, she was very kind. There will be a lot of group discussions, but most discussion topics are very interesting. If you tell her any concerns with your essay during your meetings, she will help you tremendously. Like every writing class, be prepared to read. She gives enough time for assignments. She has the best style of clothes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The assignments given are simple and help build up towards your greater progression; however, they may be quite lengthy. Whatever effort you put into the exercises, she will notice and keep it in mind. She is very accessible during office hours and offers good feedback. Attendance and assignment completion is considered in your final evaluation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you put in the work, class becomes fun and the homework becomes very straightforward.
You need get get an 96% or above to get an A in this class. Lenient but also strict at times. Very emotional and takes things personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Classes were much more interesting than my other writing professors, but she is a really tough grader. Isn't explicit about what she wants. There is an insane workload, and I felt like a literature major by the end of the semester. She offered a lot of extra credit though, and I think most people got Bs and As.

Don't know why she gets such a low score. She definitely deserve a five. Reasonable workload and fair grading. Care about students very much and would accept late work if the accuse is reasonable. Love this professor!!
She is nice and accessible Outside of the Class however she gives lot of homework. Could give better feedback. You need to work a lot if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Professor Im is a great Expos professor. She cares for students and gives meaningful feedback. Her class was not boring because there were many discussion periods with your groups about your readings and essays. Also, she had a clear grading chart of essays and assignments. Lastly, she gave a total of 3 extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a responsible prof, but is really strict in grading. It's impossible to get an A in her class. Normally, we get a B -. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, but she has so many assignments to the point where you start feeling like you are majoring in English with a minor in entrepreneurship. She's also a super tough grader, so do the ECs and get as much feedback as possible. What's super cool is that she is willing to write recommendation letters for everyone at the end!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the new pilot course for entrepreneurship with her. Let's just say she's a VERY tough grader, which you can especially feel if you had a wonderful professor in EXPOS-UA 1. Don't rely on her initial draft comments!! How much ever encouraging she might seem initially, she ends up being rough on your final grade (always go to her office hours).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I've had so far. She is helpful both in and out of class. She often holds office hours to talk about essays. She offered extra credits twice last semester, which is very important in a writing class. She also offered letters of recommendation to the entire class at the end of the semester.

I thought I would have a hard time based on the rates. But it turned out that Professor Im is awesome. She put high expectations on students and I really learned a lot. She cares students and meeting with her is very helpful. Plus, she would give extra credit once or twice per semester.

Jeannie has a bad rep, but I actually thought her class was ok. Yes, you'll have to turn in papers but she outlines her grading criteria clearly and the reading isn't even that bad. She's nice and cares about her students, and even offered my entire class rec letters. If you're choosing between her and the other "bad profs" definitely go with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Im is one of the few best professors I have come across in my freshman year. I love how she challenges her students to become best writers. Of course, she holds her students to a high standard, while at the same time showing them the best route to achieve it.

Has high expectations for her students. Comments on papers are clear and helpful. Assignment (class/hw) instructions are sometimes vague, but she doesn't mind clarifying when asked. Conferences are extremely helpful. Rarely gives extensions for assignments, but will make an exception if you're struggling. Her "talking down" attitude is nonexistent.

Didn't like her at the start of the semester; Noticed she talks down to students and she's rude. You get used to that. The assignments are specific and extensive, however, if you do them correctly it entails everything she would want in the final essay. Meetings are very helpful, she'll tell you exactly what she wants. Work with the writing center.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She talks down to you, is unclear what she wants in the essays and good luck trying to get an appointment for office hours. Her writing classes are her priority, not this class. I have no ideas how my grade is determined. She is nice though.

When I first signed up for this class, I thought I Was going to have a bad time based on the reviews. However, after taking WTE with her first semester, I was completely wrong. Her assignments and essay prompts are clear, and is very willing to help if you want it. I am assuming the other reviewers did not take this class much seriously.
she is very tough and unfriendly. I would not recommend taking her class

She might be the worst professor I've had so far. Her approach in lecture and writing critique is layered with pretension. It gets even worse because, if you start running into problems (like people do), she begins to become very dismissive. Stay on her good side or else she won't even try to help you in class. Just use the Writing Center for help.

Although it often seemed like she was talking down to the students in my class, she honestly made me a better writer. She helped me on every essay and I was able to raise my grade drastically. GO TO THE WRITING CENTER for every essay if you can because they're sooo helpful. (I wish I had before the end of the semester)

It sucks that you have  an assignmentdue  every class; however,  that is not Jeannie's fault. She's a great teacher and has helped my writing improved. She's not rude, more like sarcastic. People have forgotten to turn in assignments and she'll still grade it. She's intimidating but you'll learn alot talking to her. She also brings treats!

This professor was not clear on what she wanted, but wasn't very helpful in getting us to that point. She expected a lot from us (for example assigning us to watch a 2 hr. film 2-3 times on Mon., with a 12 paragraph response due Wed. during midterm week). Overall not a great professor, not very polite. Knows what she's talking about but not helpful

In my experience Im isn't an easy grader, but she's definitely clear on what she wants and grades fairly based on those principles. email-wise her response isn't fast, but were helpful. Grades depend on what you put into it and how well you follow the instructions. Also, her criticisms can be super blunt borderline rude but be sure to follow them!

Firstly, this professor was amongst the rudest I've ever had. Furthermore, she often refused to explain vague statements or prompts. Her grading was tough, but it wasn't as arbitrary as other WTE professors' policies. She never responds to emails regardless of the circumstance. I would strongly recommend searching for a different professor.

While everyone complains about how hard this class is and how mean Professor Im is, she is actually a really good teacher. My writing has improved tremendously and that is saying a lot for me. TIPS: don't fall asleep in class, she will call you out. do not be obnoxious, she will hate you. pretend that you have interest and she will like you.

She's not helpful at all.  Very rude and totally ridiculous.  By the end of the class everyone stopped trying because they felt pleasing her would be impossible.  She is very pretentious and an unnecessarily harsh grader.
She is a very self-righteous teacher and continually gets mad or frustrated when we do not know answers to her questions. She is not an encouraging teacher and I would really not recommend her.

Professor Im is tough but my writing has improved a lot. She really appreciates students who contribute to discussions. Don't be sarcastic or funny in your writing--that's not the point of this class. If you don't like to be picked on, don't talk in class for the first two weeks. ALWAYS GO TO CLASS or else she will call you out publicly.

Very challenging class, but I have to say my writing improved so much. This class definitely is worth the money and she plans out each lesson very carefully. Take from Prof. Im if you actually want to learn something.

This Professor is not helpful or understanding.  Her instructions are vague.  I still do not understand what she wanted from my writing.  I spent tons of time on this class and only managed a C+.  Before this class I had a 3.86.  Take any professor but Jeannie Im.
This professor is not understanding , has poor manners and is not helpful nor clear.
Pretty self-righteous lady. Take a different WTE teacher. She's tough for no reason and used to be a TA for Renzi.
Funny dude. Great at lecturing. Clearly very knowledgeable. Attendance was only mandatory for 1/4th of the semester. Very light homework.
Great professor just pay attention in lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was funny and humouros. You only needed to attend about 30% of the lectures. His exams were very tricky, and getting an A required some luck. Overall, he was a good teacher and it was a good course, but the recitations were not beneficial at all.
Ok professor, not a hard class. You do not have to attend unless ur unlucky, bad recitations and tricky exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is challenging, but if you go to the lectures (though they are pretty unengaging) you should know most of the material on the test. There are questions he pulls from the textbook that I would say got the most people because they didn't read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Graded by 4 exams and attendance. Prepare with the textbook questions well to get an A in each exam. Decent curve at the end. class was in Cantor in the morning and he tends to ramble a bit, so it was really hard to stay awake. The last unit where he shows documentaries is interesting + helps, go to those. he's pretty inspiring, would recommend
He is very knowledgeable and good at explaining concepts. Sometimes he rambles but overall good. If you do everything he says to prepare for exams, you will do fine.

Not a good lecturer. He copy and pastes stuff from the textbook to the slides, then just reads off the slides. Whenever you ask him a question, he kinda just jumps around it. I got an A in the class but only because I was familiar with macro. If you have no prior knowledge of economics, his way of teaching may not be the best for you.

Professor Catovic is chill but his lectures don't seem to be too helpful. He tends to read off slides and his exams are 25 MCQ. His course grading scheme is ambiguous and impossible to determine on your own. Found many of his exam questions to be ambiguous or unrelated to the important macroeconomic principles. HW and attendance count for 20%.
Test heavy and no extra credit available. Not a hard class if you're a good test taker.

His final score was derived from four examinations. The last exam was the most difficult. But it only accounts for 5%. He will do everything possible to help you improve your grades. As the instructor for the introductory course, I think he did a good job.
Great class and not hard if you pay attention. You should take the time to do the optional homework, and it is an easy A. The lectures are reasonable and straightforward—great professor and guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are kinda tricky, but once you understand how to study theyre not too bad. Funny guy, straight forward, gives a nice curve at the end.

This is not a difficult class as long as you study. While macro is based on 4 25-point exams and some participation, the tests are weighted based on how everyone else does, so as long as you study, you should be fine. The lectures can be dry, but that is the topic, and he is good at explaining as long as you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is based on 4 tests, and he doesn't adequately prepare you for the tests with his lectures whatsoever. Beware, you have to learn everything on your own and the material on the tests is often unpredictable - very problematic because these tests make up your whole grade.

The class is not too bad, but the professor tries to trick you on exams. This semester, he ran an experiment and taught each of his sections differently. My section had a 1 hour and 15-minute lecture taught in 15 minutes and then in-class assignments that weren't graded that leniently. If you do take him, hope you aren't in that section.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made macroeconomics very VERY digestible. This course was very digestable and the tests were ridiculously easy if you studied. If you go to class (which you have to bc it's required for the first 3 units), pay attention, and do the homework, you should pass lol. Loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When taking good quality notes, I did learn some things in class, however it could have also been done from at home as he posts the slides online. As someone who struggles to take tests, BEWARE. You could study heavily days leading up to the exam (as I did), but his tests are designed to trick you, are worded weirdly, and make you question yourself
Terrible lecturer, contents are not difficult, but he meant to trick you in the exams, don't choose him if u still have other choices

Seeing so many negative reviews makes me feel bad for this man. He is not a boring lecturer, you just can't make learning econ that much fun. The hw problems and recitation hw (both are not graded) are vert helpful in terms of helping you to understand the concepts taught during lectures. This class is much easier than my previous microecon class.

He ran an experiment this fall b/t his macro classes. My class was his hour long lecture redacted to 15 min. + a graded in class homework of the content. A TON of key points were missed bc of the shortened lecture style. Don't take him for fear that he does this again and you get the one section with mandatory attendance (like I did).
Terrible teacher. Very confusing lecturer, unable to teach anything at all.

If you're a student looking for a teacher who will give a reasonable grade, don't take him. Only based on 4 25-MCQ exams. Everything is off the slides; he just reads off, and the questions on the exam are just a bunch of trick questions. Lecture attendance is mandatory, but the class is boring. Take this class if you want your GPA to be lowered!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework does not relate to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I just do not know why the thing in he slides is the definition of commodity currency but the question in his exam is which currency people use longest.
Irrelevant things: take a lot of exams
Key points on daily homework and slides: no test at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Catovic is always accessible outside of class, and he came to the recitations himself to answer questions. The course is based on four exams, each only 25 multiple choice questions. The exams are lecture heavy, and there is no graded homework, although you can do them for your own good. He gives a big curve at the very end of the semester
25 multiple choice questions for tests but he puts a lot of trick questions and the answer isnt always clear, curves half a letter grade up usually, also second test is usually the hardest

Only 4 exams make up your grade but as long as you study the slides you're good. Attendance isn't mandatory but he helps breakdown confusing concepts + accessible outside of class during recitation/office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was the easiest class I have taken at NYU. Professor Catovic does not attempt to reinvent the wheel with the coursework, which I respect. Macro is not meant to be hard, and he does not ask for much out of his students, in my opinion. Just study the lecture slides, and you'll be fine. I didn't find attending very helpful.

He's a nice and funny guy but not the best professor. He is always late and always struggles with technology, wasting so much time. The last fourth of the semester he just showed us documentaries instead of teaching. Recitations are useless, the exams are hard to study for because the questions on it are unexpected and meant to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 4 tests throughout whole course, drops lowest grade, study slides and you'll be good. Interesting lectures, nice man.
I didn't do a single homework, go to a single recitation, barely went to class and still probably did more than required. Review the slides before the exam and ur good. Very easy class.

Took him for Intro to Macro. The information was very clearly laid out in the lecture slides, and I didn't need to go to class to understand the content. However, the lectures were still interesting to go to.
Super easy class with 4 tests. Lowest grade gets dropped. Attendance isn't mandatory, and homework is optional. Tests are easy if you review the slide shows and the tests get curved.

Professor was a nice guy but not an amazing teacher, he went solely off slideshows and with his grading system it put a lot of pressure with 100% of your grade being 4 exams. It's not hard to do well in this class with homework being optional, just show up for lecture and you should be fine. I just wish exams weren't the only grade determinant

Great class, great Professor. 
If you go to class, do your homework and read the slides you will do well.

Good professor, but exams only for your grade isn't the best. No need for attendance grade based on 4 exams and the lowest one is dropped. If you solve and understand the hws you'll be good. Better to attend as he expands on concepts in his slides which are the only thing you need to use for studying. econ curve 30,40,30 (a,b,c and below)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very easy lectures and exams. All exam questions are very easy to tackle if you understand the concept. Even as a non-econ major, this lecture was the least stressful and the most exciting one to take this semester. Very fast email responses are also a very positive aspect. Just understand all the concepts and ideas and relate them to real life.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class isn't mandatory, but I highly recommend it. It will put you ahead of 90% of the class who don't show up because it allows you to ask questions, and he explains the topics a bit more beyond his slides. There is a lot of self-study, though; as long as you grill the homework (not graded) in your head, you will get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just a chill guy

If you are not a Econ major or never take any economics class before, run!!!! His exam questions is so random and unrelated to the homework, he doesn't give out the practice question… He ruined my first year of Univeristy…
Very easy if you do the hw regularly
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof is a nice guy but an awful teacher. You're better off not attending lectures and self studying based on the textbook chapters/homework. He's great at answering emails so if you have any questions go ahead and send them. But yeah, he's someone I'd maybe be friends with, not someone I would want teaching me.

reviews.comment: He only goes off of the slideshows does not teach a single thing. While he is a nice guy your only graded based off of 4 exams. I will say the curve for me did help. If you are good at teaching yourself then this class is easy but still very little help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for intro to macro. Didn't attend one lecture but still on track to get a good grade because he has 4 - 25 MCQ (you can drop one of the 4) exams that make up your full grade and are based only off the slides he posts. Class isn't hard but curve is pretty bad and he's absolutely useless outside of class. Get ready for a lot of self study.

This professor is unorganized and confuses himself a lot. If you know macroeconomics, this course will be easy. If you know nothing, beware. I had to stop attending lecture because it would just confuse me, but I do very well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He has a really solid grade system, which i appreciate, and he does not tolerate cheating (W professor). He's cool and funny, but i found his explanations a bit wordy. This depends on your learning style though. I respect his ethics.

You dont need to attend any lecture and recitation classes to get an A. His grade policy is very clear, so the only thing you need to do is reviewing the power points before 4 multiple choices tests. His powerpoint is very clear and the questions in test are kind of tricky but not hard.
How can a professor change its final grading composition after the final????
Nice dude but some exam questions are super weird. He sometimes asks questions not related to the class and the last part of his lectures were based on several long documentaries.

I just wished I had used his office hours more. I found the concepts he covered very interesting, and I definitely respect that he doesn't have a high tolerance for cheating. His grading is also generous. I missed an exam, and still received a passing grade since his curve allowed for our minuses to turn into pluses regardless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I believe we should really wait until the end of the semester to write ratings. Anyway, 3 important things: no tolerance for cheating, generous grading, and good design on course content. Anyone in our school should know that the first one is very important. For 3, he taught us the economic history of the US to illustrate applications of macro.

Professor civotac is really amazing. I only attend his class once but still get an A for final grades. Civatoc's course is 
so inspirational and interesting that I won't get an A if I attend his class more.

Catovic is a great professor who wants us all to do well and is there to help. Even though 4 tests determine your grade, brackets are not fixed and are relative to how you do compared to others. If you study and try your best, you will do well. People who give him bad ratings are the ones who don't study despite the many opportunities to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tbh I love this class; the ppl who write bad reviews are just salty about their grade even though he gave a generous curve. He is available for questions and is happy to help. definitely go to lecture if u want to do well bc he elaborates a lot on notes -which he made very clear on the first day. Course is also all exam based so keep that in mind.

reviews.comment: HE GOT A GRADING POLICY SO NICE
Easy class as long as you show up and study a bit

reviews.comment: Grade only based on 4 exams.... Exam questions weird, going to lecture/not going to lecture no difference at all. Homework and lecture are not helpful at all for the exam... RUN AWAY ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very reachable after the class, always patient and answers all of students' questions. Good person too. If you go to his lectures, do the hw and ask him questions, you'll be totally fine. I'm not econ major but I learned so much!!

Class is honestly fine and if you go to the lectures, take notes on the power points, and do the homework, you will get a good grade. People complaining aren't doing the bare minimum, and even though people got low scores, he said the end-of-year average will be a B. He also offers many office hours and occasional recitations, all done by him.

He was clear that if you don't come to lectures you will not do well in the class and I would say over half of the class doesn't show up so ofc they're failing. It is so easy to do well in his class I just show up to lectures and review the slides before quizzes. I have a 96 avg & never taken econ before.
TLDR an easy A if you just go to lectures

reviews.comment: The hw can help you understand the concepts but aren't a representation of the quiz questions. Just memorize the slides typically like half of the multiple choice questions are basic things from the slides. The rest you need to have a basic conceptual understanding and apply it ie: which of four options would decrease supply? stuff like that.

Anyone complaining about this class is insane. It is based on 4 multiple choice quizzes (25 questions each) but there are 2 CURVES. Curve 1 is the the quizzes are ranked by how well you do, your best quiz is worth 40%, the 2nd best 30%, then 20% and your worst is 10%. Here is the 2nd curve:

A: 88+
A-: 77 - 87
B+: 73 - 76
B: 65 - 72
B-: 61 - 64
Weird exam questions!! Loosely related to hw review questions. PPT from internet and Khan Academy! His teaching makes me confuse even though I know that run away!!!!!!!

reviews.comment: AVOID BY ALL COST

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! Good guy but the worst professor EVER. Grades are only based on 4 exams and those exams are NOT EASY. The class average of the current 2 exams is D+, and this guy is clearly still confident in his way of teaching. The only practice problems from a textbook are not related to the actual exam at all.

The worst professor I have ever had at NYU. Class is based solely on 4 exams and don't reflect the homeworks (which aren't graded or checked) and slides (also filled with mistakes and copied and pasted). The exam questions are purposefully confusing and his paranoia with cheating prevents us from getting our exams back to learn from our mistakes.

reviews.comment: DO NOT EVER TAKE THIS CLASS
