reviews.comment: Be ready to consume a lot of media and film, class conversations will be fun and interesting. Yet I don't recommend because of how all over the place everything was.

Very disorganized and not that open minded to personal opinions in class. It's also difficult to meet her outside of class hours, and she will send readings to do before class very last minute. Shes kind but the course overall didn't feel stable and consistent with the syllabus.
goood gooood goooood
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Langer is very educated on books, paintings, and movies. When it comes to discussions, she loves for students to be engaged. Her writing prompts will get you thinking about things you hadn't considered. She's a very nice and understanding professor. There are a couple of readings and movies, and you might need to purchase books.

Prof. Langer's course stands out as one of the most fulfilling and engaging parts of my first sem. Despite other reviews, she created a safe and encouraging space where I felt comfortable sharing my opinion. She was easily accessible and patient when working with students. I never witnessed her 'shaming' anyone, so be mindful of online reviews.

Prof. Langer is very easy-going and a fun person to get to know. The class itself isn't too difficult and feels fairly casual rather than strictly academic. 
I enjoyed that we watched many films throughout the semester. Professor Langer also offers many opportunities for extra credit.
Overall, this class is a great option for a relaxing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Niceish person, bad prof. Very disorganized, late to nearly every class and office hours/meetings. Grading feels arbitrary; taking her direct feedback doesn't improve grades on assignments. Assignments are posted late and in random places. Heavy reading load at times, but most of class is just watching movies. Long grading times. I learned nothing.
did not follow the syllabus and always showed up late and unprepared to every class. not very accepting of other viewpoints. don't take her.

Honestly to speak, she is amazing. Her class/lecture are splendid and full of respect. She is a very responsible person. If you have any questions, just go to find her. She will be there waiting for you.(Although you are introvert person, that will not too hard, she has good self-control.）A fair classroom, and efforts will surely be rewarded.

I took Professor Langer for both WRCI102 and WREX101. She was very understanding and one of the nicest professors I've met. She assigns great books. In class, we'd discuss the assigned reading, go over anonymous papers for feedback, or work in groups on activities. It's easy to do well in her class, and she was always reachable when needed.

Wonderful professor! Prof. Longer picks out wonderful, diverse books and readings plus, facilitates great class discussions. Her essay prompts are fun, creative and she always gives a more research based option for more technical people. Also provides detailed feedback. Great person and teacher. Would highly recommend!

Feedback on essays is not helpful. Gives a million paper handouts to hold onto. Sometimes posts hw on BS, sometimes on email, nothing is ever in the same place- just completely disorganized, and teaching methods seem very lazy. Not hard to get an A, but if you want to improve your writing, do not take her.

So mid. Nobody does the reading for her classes and she is extremely disorganized. Good person but just simply couldn't care less. She is always late to class, is late on the syllabus, takes months and months to grade, and misassigned us a paper she never even graded.
Best professor I've ever met. She is patient, caring, and nice. My writing skills improved a lot through her lecture. A lot of chance for extra credit!

I had Langer last semester, and she was phenomenal. Not only did I fall in love with reading again through the texts she assigned, but I learned so many different writing styles through them. Any student who doesn't have the biggest interest in writing, I advise you to take her. she You will become a better writer and broaden your outlook on life.

All I learned/read from this class is book about the first homosexual man in this world and BLM and female rights, but nothing about writing. I support all of the things above but I wish to learn more about writing, given that the class name is writing 2. Learned a lot about political correctness but my writing skills did not improve by a tiny bit.

Good professor, unfortunately she is a little disorganized and not reliable over email. But if you participate enough, pay attention and actually do the work, class is an easy A. She does get tougher and the work does get more grueling in the 2nd semester for Writing Critical Inquiry. Overall a solid professor I'd take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I seriously loved this class. If you have the chance to take her, DO IT! Her assignments are fun and homework is not rigorous. She is a very easygoing and personable teacher. She cares deeply about her students and completely gave me a new outlook on creative writing. Participation is very important to her but it is not difficult to get involved!

She is kind and funny and gives a detailed feedback if you ask for one. Participation matters you had better speak one or two times every class. The grading criteria is not always clear. You can get a first draft 95 and a final draft 80 after revising according to her feedback. She does not follow the syllabus and makes the schedule confusing.

I had Professor Langer my spring semester for WRCI. The course material was very expansive and allowed creative freedom when choosing topics to write about, all very interesting. Professor Langer cared about making personal connections to the students and their educational success. Loved this class!

I had professor Langer for my fall and spring semester (two different classes) and LOVED her. She genuinely cares about her students and went above and beyond last year to host classes in person. She ALWAYS wore a mask and was flexible and understanding with students regarding deadlines/workload. She's an insightful professor & an amazing person.

Professor Langer is very disorganized when it comes to planning out the class, it is also very unclear what your grade is going to be until the very end of the semester because she does not put anything in gradebook. The readings are boring and the class discussions drag on. She is a very sweet lady but boring when it comes to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly boring in lecture and as an online student I didnt feel that she gave me the chance to engage with the class as my other professors did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Langer is a great woman who tries to make the class engaging. Throughout the semester, we read multiple books, poems, and articles (some of which were not discussed in class). There were very few major assignments other than the midterm, final, and short essays. She's also very responsive. It's tough however to know your true grade till the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Langer was late (even when we had online classes) and very unclear in her assignments. She takes forever giving feedback and her lectures are not very interesting. She assigned light homework and readings frequently. She made it easy to participate in class and the 3 essays were easy. The topics discussed in class were somewhat boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Super sweet lady. I took her Writing I class and she was incredibly helpful and always accessible. We workshopped all of our papers in class and she is very clear with instructions and due dates.

I didn't realize just how awesome of a professor Langer was until my second semester writing class. She's organized and gets to the point with engaging stories that contribute to an overarching theme. If you take the time to go in and have her give comments on your essays, and you apply those comments. You'll become a better writer and an A student
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Writing 1 was a drag having Professor Langer, even if you make the corrections she suggest on the 1st draft you still might not even get a B. she will give you unnecessary readings and make you print out your own copy everyday before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is great. If you ask for help she won't hesitate. Edits on essays are based off of the rough draft itself (in terms of quality and length).
Great Professor, I miss her so much.
The professor is indeed a good one. She attempted to get to know everyone in the classroom to teach everyone in a special way. Thanks to her, I enjoyed my first semester in NYU.

Professor Langer really knows how to train her students into reading, writing and thinking with clarity, precision and grace. You get as much out of the class as you put in. If you want to improve your writing in a manner that is beneficial for the rest of your academic and professional career, definitely take her. (Also makes great jokes)

I loved being in Professor Langer's class. I found the topics that she taught to be relevant to my interests, and I loved the discussions we had in class. As a result, the papers were fairly easy and fun to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The class is pretty interesting but she's way too tough on grading. She assigns a bunch of reading homework thats unnecessary. If you want an A you're better off taking someone else's class.

Very nice person with interesting discussion topics.  I really learned a lot and cultivated my opinions from this class.  She is very disorganized and often posts homework at the last minute.  She can also be a harsh grader (if she finds something she doesn't like, she'll take off a lot of points).  Willing to help but rambles a lot.

She is a great writing professor! Often unorganized, but her discussions are really interesting. She listens very well to all the ideas. She is pretty lenient with her gradings. Her topics are really interesting.

I LOVE HER! She is so helpful and awesome. She's really nice and it's mostly a discussion class. She's very lenient and chill about deadlines and grading. She is very sweet and can be funny, too. I am taking her again next semester. As long as you show up and read the stuff, it's a total breeze. She's also there for office hours all the time.
Her class is really interesting. Her topics give us so much to talk about. She is my favorite professor so far. The reads were short and interesting. I just loved her class!!!

The class itself was okay. She seems to talk a lot and the daily freewrites are tedious. Towards the end of the semester she started to assign bigger workloads as if she was trying to cram information in. I also feel like she likes certain people and not others. For the most part, it's an okay class. Nothing great, I suggest taking someone else.

I found professor Langer to be mildly helpful, any writing class is bound to help you just by the experience, but I felt a little awkward in her class. She seems to have a very specific idea of what answers she wants to her questions and she knows exactly what kind of interpretation she wants you to have. She's okay, just a little narrow minded.
Her class is a little boring but she is an awesome person and thus, an awesome teacher!
she's awesome

A very nice woman. She tries to make the class interesting but sometimes it doesn't work. Personally, I loved the discussions and when you participate, it's like brownie pts. She doesn't make it too clear what she wants from your writing, but in terms of workload, it's good. Beware the workshops--totally pointless and unhelpful.
It's a pretty easy class. Very research based. Can be boring. Langer is nice and gives easy homework. Not the most amazing class, but it's fine and wont add very much to your work load.

she is a little tough on the grading. she started giving me better grades, saying how much my writing's improving. not sure if she does this for everyone. i honestly don't think she improved my writing THAT much. very nice and willing to help whenever. gives clear, helpful comments on the papers. sometimes asks stupid questions during discussions.

She is a nice person but grades kind of strictly.  We wrote about four different topics w/four main essays.  It's not too much work and she's pretty friendly.  She didn't help improve my writing that much though.
Genuinely the best prof at NYU. I took her for writing as exploration. She really cares about students, fair grader, clear rubrics, lots of time to complete assignments.

Totally the best professor I've ever met. The course is easy, you only have to finish one essay during the semester. A few readings after class. She is kind, caring, giving feedback patiently. You can talk to her without any pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take her!!

Prof. Chavoshan was so inspirational and taught me so many important things during Bridgerton. She is nuanced, she is aware and she is interested in learning with her students. She has never talked at us and rather beckons us to add to what we already know. She is fantastic at giving feedback and has made me a more aware person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took her for WRCI over the summer and she was great! lectures kept me engaged and easy A. Midterm/final is one paper and she gives feedback during the step-by-step process. Had some breakout room talks but nothing too serious. We had weekly posts based on the articles we read-prompts are very clear! highly recommend taking her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her online for WRCI, and she organized the course very well. She made her lectures as engaging as they could be online and was very clear with her class expectations. Most of the grade was one big project, which she gives good feedback on step by step, and the rest includes attendance, discussion posts, and a small presentation.
Very helpful class and makes writing better and also helps international students with writing assignments in other classes. Very nice professor.
she's great
Adorable, funny, intelligent! I am constantly impressed by his technology skills.

Goofy dude who is a bit too into the class material given that it's common sense, but success is heavily based off of participation and the passion you show for the class. Grade is group-dependent but you individually control ~60% of final grade so just try to yap and smile and all will be well. Always go to feedback meetings after presentations
As long as u participate and follow his conventions its a free A

The greatest C&C professor of all time. My only regret is not being able to take him for B&S. Participation matters heavily, but he is generous with grades and the class is fun. While other kids were busy reading 2000-word books, my class was watching great movies and having nice discussions.

Prof Schenkler is the goat.

All you have to do in order to get an A is to participate once every discussion and do well on the 3 essays. He will give out 100% to everyone that follows his criteria (which he states multiple times in class). 

Ended the class with 100% on everything, while not reading any of the material.
Nice professor that will give you feedback but lectures were quite boring but there's nothing that can be done about that

Despite the positive reviews, Schenkler has clear favorites in his class. He frequently makes mistakes while grading essays, such as claiming my evidence doesn't exist in the book while it does. He judges your answers to discussion questions and would take his bad attitude out on the class sometimes. I didn't enjoy taking this class.

What a guy. Hands down one of the best writing professors at Stern. Classes are engaging and organized in a great way. Understands we are busy and doesn't expect us to read everything on the syllabus. Gives weekly journals with great feedback and the essays (although tedious to write) are pretty easy to score well just follow the rubric. 10/10!!!!!
Professor Schenkler is a great teacher for commerce and culture. Grading is very clear and if you write the way he likes, you will do fine. Highly recommend.
Easy A
Has clear favorites. Don't take this prof if you have other tough classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall solid professor. Make sure you participate and be prepared by doing all the readings. Raise your hand in class and contribute meaningfully to class discussions.

Professor Schenkler was a very solid option for Org Comm. Had very clear grading criteria that were easy to follow for both presentations and written assignments. As long as you follow his instructions clearly & participate in class you will receive an A.

Kind guy who makes participation in discussion-based classes open and easy for everyone. Classes are always interesting and engaging. Very fair grader. The B&S course is underwhelming from a learning standpoint, but this is universal for all B&S professors. Good B&S teacher choice to help develop your writing a bit, while still enjoying class.

Overall, great guy! Loved coming to his class every Monday and Wednesday. As long as you do your work, participate and ask him for help whenever you need it, you should have no problem ending the semester with a good great.
Second worst professor ever. The most regretful thing is choosing him. The rating tricked me.
Good professor but worst experience this year. Would not have chosen it again.

Very good professor for Commerce and Culture. Clear guidelines for your writing and great feedback on individual assignments. Encourages participation and makes it easy for everyone to contribute. Somewhat strict on certain aspects of writing, but if you get those issues down, you will succeed. Definitely better than other options available.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Schenkler is the best professor I have ever met at NYU. He is like an inspirational mentor for me, and I believe he is the one for the rest of the class. All my classmates appreciate his works and comments. I would like to take his class one more time.

Prof Schenker is very old-school. He's been at Stern forever and is very respected. But, he's very particular about his grading and giving out As. A lot of his grading is based on how much he likes you, so go to office hours. Just know that getting an A won't be super easy, but his class isn't super hard.

He is very attentive to individuals and gives you good feedback on your papers. If you put in a good effort, he will notice. Participate in class discussions! Also can be sarcastic/make funny comments
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor definitely would take again
Really Great at improving your presentation skills!!
Prof Shingler really wants to help you improve your presentation skills.  He is dedicated and takes the time needed to analyze your posture, speech, etc
Hard to get an A, but makes it really easy to get a B+. He talks a lot and the class was pretty interesting.

Funny (sometimes sarcastic) professor.  He values participation a lot. He likes his students to think outside the box, so if you stick to the obvious, he won't give you  a good grade (obviously). He pays individual attention to his students and is very dedicated.
intuitive, but a harsh grader. if you are intersted purely in intellectual discussion regardless of your grade, take his classes.
hard grader, but he really helps you learn individually in the class.
Has favorites. Get on his good side.  Great at teaching, sucks at grading, and has an abrasive, in-your-face personality.

Very good professor - willing to help, focuses on individual improvement, always interesting.  He can also be mean, lets his mouth run, and insulting.  Despite that, his class and how he teaches is well-worth the anxiety.

Really not that bad. Fun lecturer, but be organized in this class and make friends. Also, getting a good TA means the world! Ece Gurleyik was a tough grader! But really not that bad, just be organized, know deadlines, take notes, and you'll be fine. The tests are MCQ, not much writing heavy.

Professor Ali is a fantastic lecturer whose main shortcoming is the slides to match, get ready to listen well and take lots of notes. The readings are pretty technical and not as relevant as the lectures themselves. The only complaint I have is her attendance policy, however it isn't unusual.

if i can give a 0 i would. no study guides, no real slides (js pictures that did not make sense AT ALL if you don't take notes of every word she says), basically you cannot survive this course if you are not a good notetaker. TAs don't even know what is happening most of the time, and everyone is just confused about what she wants. AVOID HER.

The worst teacher I have had at NYU so far. I do not think she knows what she is talking about half the time and her tests are impossible to study for. No study guides, and literally anything she rants about in class could be on the exam. No class have ever given me such anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: having taken Ali for both History of Media and her Inquiry Seminar, i can say the latter is definitely where she shines. she makes herself accessible outside of class, gives helpful feedback on projects, and is really quite hilarious during class discussions. a far better experience definitely don't write her off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do NOT take if you want to keep yourself sane. Talks like Eminem rapping and expects notes based responses when she rewords her sentences 5 times. And EACH explanation is a new one. Words her exams like she wants you to fail. Question would be about the most random thing she mentioned in lecture. Makes you giggle but, preferably, save yourself.

Prof. Ali is quite humorous, and I can tell she genuinely loves teaching. But honestly, her teaching style feels pretty chaotic to me... I don't think she's a very organized professor. I only managed to survive this class thanks to having a great teaching assistant.

Honestly, I was really surprised by the negative reviews. The class gives you a solid foundation for the major and Professor Ali is enthusiastic, funny, and genuinely kind. I didn't study as much as I should've, so my grade wasn't what I wanted, but she really puts in the effort. PS. Don't listen to people who fail the class; they're just salty.
I walked into this class hopeful and walked out questioning my entire academic life

This course felt chaotic! The slides are just some pictures, so you must create all the structure yourself. No study guides for any exams, including the cumulative final. MC questions are vague with multiple plausible answers. Recitations don't help. Heavy workload but unclear teaching. Run as quickly as possible

Lectures are extremely disorganized. The “slides” are just random images with no structure, and nothing on Brightspace is helpful. Exams are very detailed, yet no study guide is ever provided... Readings barely matter early on but become essential for the final. Expect unpredictable tests and unclear expectations...
took during the summer so it was pretty fast-paced, TA grades all the assignments and takes off points for lowkey no reason, super lecture heavy and she kinda just makes the same jokes everyday

Just awful. Does not take any late work even if it's one minute. Went to her to review an exam so I could improve for the next one and she said if she were my TA she would have given me an even worse grade. Lectures consist of photos and that's it. Also speaks like she narrating a movie??

RUN FOR YOUR LIFE. The material itself isn't hard, but she makes exams unnecessarily difficult to understand. She has no empathy for the students and doesn't take student circumstances into account. Missing an assignment puts you in a worse position than literally failing exams. Does not accept late work AT ALL. She straight-up gives you 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ali can be funny yet she shows no respect behind close doors. Both me and my friend went to her office hours and she literally traumatized us into depression throughout the semester saying how horrible we are. She only do that to certain students she like and some students told me they paid her an insane amount of money so she changed their grades.

Has a way of talking that is so confusing and completely unclear, genuinely impossible to follow. The TA's carry this class entirely. Midterm and final exam essays are tedious and memorization heavy. Unfortunate that she's the only one who teaches History of Media & Comm
As long as you take detailed notes and pay attention to the examples she gives in lecture, the class is super approachable and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is NOT helpful. Her lectures are mostly just her yapping and hopping from one irrelevant topic to the other. You can't properly take notes since her slideshows provide no context. And despite my best efforts, she's never given me an A+ due to her EXTREMELY picky and biased method of grading. And zero extra credit assignments. Just horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly don't let the reviews scare you. I was going through the trenches the semester I took her class but she was extremely understanding and honestly let me off the hook way more times than she should have. Her class was rather enjoyable and the assignments were a nice change of pace from the usual essays we have in MCC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's not as horrible as the review says she is!!! Yes, there's no bullet points or words on her slides, but that ensures that you actually pay attention to what she says in lectures. Just write down everything she says in lectures, and she also gives you the questions for the exam in advance.

Professor Ali is incredibly cold and unsympathetic, honestly evil. I missed a deadline by two hours due to my terminally ill dad being hospitalized, and she gave me a zero. Later, despite approved absences, she failed me for attendance. I had As on everything else. Avoid her if you expect basic empathy and human decency.

I think she changed her curriculum since last semester because previous ratings don't match my class experience. I found this class so interesting. Workload is not bad and exams are open-note. The lectures are very entertaining but her slides are literally JUST pictures... take detailed notes bc there's no way to re-study.
class was incredibly boring. ali herself was a funny person but the lessons were a drag. be prepared to do your readings because that's what you're going to need for the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ali was one of the best professors I had here at NYU, she was very kind and caring and understanding outside of class. She knew my name and always checked in with me and is very funny. Her lectures were good but there is always stuff to takeaway from it. Just sit in the front row and you will definitely pass with ease.

Isra Ali is getting coal for Christmas... 
Lectures were done without a microphone and only vague images on slides, so if you were in the back of the class you were screwed. There were 3 exams based on memorizing and regurgitating info from lecture and readings since questions were given in advance. This course left me and my friends frustrated.

Lecture's are SO hard to follow! You never know what's important and what's a tangent. THE SLIDES DON'T HAVE ANY WORDS!! So you have NOTHING to go by if you zoned out for a second. You MUST use only lecture examples in the exams so the lecture is essential but it's literally so hard to pay attention. Also if you miss over 3 classes points are lost
RUN!! NOT A PROF U WANT IF U GET TO PICK
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: your grade in this class heavily depends on your TA! Prof Ali's lectures are unorganized, fast paced, and hard to follow, but the class was interesting overall. I'm not a fan of the lecture-heavy exam content (you have to cite lecture examples), but it wasn't the end of the world.

The worse professor ever, if you miss lecture you will get so behind. She somehow expects us to know every single thing in exams and doesn't make what she wants exactly clear. IF YOU CAN AVOID HER PLEASE DO IT FOR YOUR MENTAL HEALTH
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to pay attention in class since the lecture slides are super vague. Can tell this professor really cares about this info, it's just super boring sometimes. Your grade will really depend on your TA, but tests are manageable as long as you take the time to prepare and pay attention to lectures and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the lecture's aren't well structured, professor ali is a really sweet professor who's accessible outside of class and is willing to help if you're struggling. The exam questions are given to you in advance and it's easy to prepare for them even if you've missed readings or course material. The slide's aren't very informative so take notes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't get how she hasn't been fired yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dear prof, humble yourself. You're not nearly as good enough of a lecturer to teach 200+ students lets be fr. Every single time you speak, I wonder what in the actual world you're trying to say. If you're going to be genuinely terrible at public speaking, then at least make your exams based on other stuff, not just your lectures.

Professor Ali clearly is a knowledgable person but she is a terrible instructor. Her lectures are hard to follow and she often goes on tangents. Her "slides" consist of literal screenshots of tweets or single words with no explanations or content. Your grade in this class is reliant on your TA so pick wisely. Studying for her tests is a nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went to her office hours but I didn't learn anything at all. She expects you to know the materials before you go find her or else she's just gonna ask you a bunch of questions and expect you to know the answers to them. She won't teach you afterwards but tells you to go back and read the assigned readings again.

I changed majors because of this class. I genuinely wasted so much time and energy on both her and the course material. She doesn't have proper slides, goes on irrelevant tangents, is not lenient, and does not seem to care for her students. I would highly suggest avoiding any class taught by her for your sanity. So not worth the headache and time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unironically one of the worst educators I have ever encountered. Horrible lecturer, no shows her own office hours, and when she does decide to grace you with her presence she's unhelpful. If given a grant I would dedicate hours of research to finding out if she and her TAs possess kindergarten level literacy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: no lecture slides or notes, nothing, very bad
Prof Ali is kind and her social media practicum was not difficult; I stopped doing the reading halfway through the semester and was fine.

maybe i'm biased because i had TAs grade all my assignments but ali's class was really enjoyable. it wasn't easy but her lectures are fun and she's pretty good at responding to emails. the tests were hard. it was 8 questions beforehand with 4 of them being on the test and each answer had to reference 2 readings and 2 lecture examples.

Genuinely terrible. She is nice and funny sometimes, but she grades so inconsistently and horribly. She is all over the place, and nothing she teaches makes sense. She goes on rants, and doesnt stay on topic. Doesnt give good feedback, except 'good work'. Doesnt seem to care at all. If you want to take this for an easy A save you're time.

Prof. Ali is an amazing lecturer, she is able to keep her students engaged into the lesson. However, just be aware that your grade in this class will be very dependent on your TA, as they do all the grading for the 2 midterms, final, and a couple other assignments. Easy class to do well in overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ali is funny and charming at times but not super lenient & genuinely impossible to reach outside of class. Lectures are interesting most of the time but make sure to take notes because exams are basically about regurgitating information from class and the assigned readings for homework.
i promise she's a great prof if you don't take her for the required mcc lectures

really love prof ali i would take her again if i could. hers is the only class i take notes in because her lectures are so engaging. the exams are a lot to prep for but they really make sure that you know the material so i appreciate it. she's so smart and doesn't speak that fast. overall very knowledgeable professor who enjoys teaching love her sm

strict about attendance but she's really understanding and caring about genuine circumstances when one misses lecture. Easily accessible in office hours and fun lectures. The exams are really easy with questions given in advance out of which 4 come on the paper. Overall, she's really sweet and chill just go for lecture and you'll be fine

Professor Ali gets a bad rep, she is not a bad lecturer the only thing is that she does talk fast, however, you can just tell her to repeat herself and slow down. the tests are pretty straightforward with 6 readings and 6 class examples for 4 questions in 2 paragraphs each. The ta's did most of the work but history was way better than intro
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Someone send her this site link because she needs to entirely change her teaching style. She is the WORST professor I've had at NYU. Lectures are boring with no substantial material. No clear instructions on assignments. Leaves students feeling more confused and offers no clarity in office hours. straight up AWFUL. please pick a new profession

Awful professor! Talks A LOT without saying anything. The whole semester was her talking about unrelated things. Gives no clear directions for Final project. I went to office hours multiple times and left more confused. Should stop teaching atp.

Usually easy to get a good grade but she is so confusing and I don't think she even knows what she's looking for. Everyone in the class is always lost because she changes the directions for things constantly and it seems like she's just making up random things as she goes along.

I was a little worried because of some of the other reviews, but I did NOT need to be! Professor Ali explained the material (which could get complicated) in a way that was clear and easy to follow--and she was also really funny, I loved her stories and illustrations from personal experience. Grading criteria was always clear as well.
was so afraid to take her due to such terrible reviews. so glad I gave her a chance because she is such a gem! hilarious, accessible outside of class, and her TAs were all fantastic.

i had prof ali a few years ago and would mot have given the same rating, but this time around she easily became one of my favorite professors. caring, understanding and knowledgeable, and more important unpretentious unlike many other academics.

Awful. Every class she just asks about our weekends and talks about nothing. Her lessons cover nothing and have no basis. She assigns readings but does not even acknowledge or talk about them during class. Her paper instructions are poorly made and she has the strangest assignments. Should be an easy A class but is made weirdly complicated.

Awful. For 30 minutes she just asks us about her day and then covers no topics during class. She doesn't assign homework or talk about the readings, but just expects us to know about them and write about them despite never acknowledging them in the first place. Also just really strange and weird assignments. This class is a joke.

Lectures are boring and never related to the readings. On a usual week, there are "expected" readings that can be up to 90 pages long (i doubt anyone did them, but you need to skim them and quote for papers). No guidance nor good feedback for grading and every grade is either a 100% or a 20% with literally no in between. Prof is also pretentious

One of the worst classes I've taken. She talked in circles all class and the assignments are extremely vague to the point of having no direction. When you ask her for help on the final project she's passive aggressive, rejects every idea and will make you even more confused. Plus sides are she doesn't care about late assignments or attendance

A completely different teacher in-person than online. Was not a big fan of her history of media, then took her for social media practicum and inquiry seminar in the same semester and she was excellent. flexible with due dates, easy grader, and gave great guidance feedback.
You can always send your drafts to Professor Ali before submission. Gave me very detailed feedback. go to her office hours before submitting your work, read the prompt carefully and you'll be fine.

Prof. Ali gets a bad rep from when she taught History of Media but she's one of the best MCC profs out there. She is obviously incredibly smart, classes, lectures, assignments are all planned and organized. She is super accommodating and funny (at times cringe but all good-hearted). Good feedback AND ON TIME!!! The class is also very interesting!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I loved prof ali so idk why there are so many negative reviews. social media practicum is graded by few assignments + a final project but they're all for completion so it's an easy A. as long as you raise your hand once in awhile to ask questions and show up to class semi-regularly she'll love you. i genuinely thought she was funny and caring!

She'll play videos for half of the class, and the other half she'll lecture off the top of her head without any notes -- literally just rambles. Don't ever really know where she's going with lectures, there's not really a main point. Tough grader, her essay prompts list 10 different instructions and you don't really know what the main idea is...?

I wanted to like Ali, but she ended up being angry with the class and started grading harshly. My conference with her was unpleasant for no reason, it seemed as though she wanted us to understand her course the way she did - impossible in a few weeks. The material is interesting but I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does not respond to emails, very tough grader, insane workload that does not consider students' other commitments. Very lecture heavy- zone out for two minutes and you'll be completely lost. Had to withdraw from class two weeks before semester ended to make sure I didn't get the F. Taking again with a different professor.

Professor Ali was one of the harshest teachers I've had at NYU. Her lectures are very unorganized, she goes off on tangents, and overall does not present the information in a clear way. She also has an extreme attitude if you upset her in any way, often times being very passive aggressive and rude. She can be funny at times, but that's about it :(

For History of Media and Comm, You have to go to every lecture because you can't miss anything... she expects you to remember every little thing. I went to office hours to get my midterm back and she was rude and passive aggressive. Thank god for my wonderful TA! Do well on the final. Be specific! When we moved online, she made the final longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Only cares about her own business. Never reply to students' emails. Never read your papers and only gave u tough grade. Never give suggestions.

Professor Ali is not as bad as some of these ratings say. Maybe it's different in an in-person class, but online and asynchronously, she makes History of Media & Communication a great experience. There is a lot of reading but it really helps and prepares you well. Her lectures are so funny and she has great energy. She made this class so fun.

Idk why there are so many bad reviews, I literally never watched the lectures or did the readings and I still got an A. Sure you've gotta do some more skimming come exam time but in an online asynchronous course that's easy. I thought her lectures were quite easy to understand, especially compared to other MCC profs. And she's super nice and fun.

Professor Ali's lectures unnecessarily go off-track, making it hard to pay attention. She also does not mention any of the concepts by name making it hard to go back into lectures to find what she's talking about, despite saying that she explicitly mentions the theories and examples. Does not make it clear whether we are learning theories or not

Her lectures are dense and convoluted, and she often will drift off-topic. This is usually not a problem in an engaging in-person class, but in a pre-recorded video, the lectures become far more difficult to get through. Often felt disconnected from the assigned readings. She is also a needlessly tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The online lecture format was great and easier to follow because there was a transcript below which made it easy to find things to talk about for the midterm and final. If you watch the videos, take really good notes, and do the assignments ontime it is not difficult to get an A. the lectures are really interesting and I truly learned a lot.

I personally loved Professor Ali! she did a great job of keeping recorded lectures engaging and fun (sometimes a bit cringe though). If you pay attention to lectures, take good notes, and actually do the readings class isn't hard. there is a 5 part project that honestly seemed pointless and weekly forum posts but both are just graded on completion

I took History & Social Media Networking with Ali. History: the class is a lot of work BUT it was my favorite MCC class - def worth it. SM Networking: much easier - do the readings and engage & you will do great. Not too much work at all. Also, the smaller class size makes the dynamic super fun and engaging.
Loved the class! Prof Ali was open to students discussion, not a harsh grader at all.

I really don't know why Ali has bad reviews, I thought her lectures were really interesting. If you know how to take good notes and do your work and understand the key definitions and concepts you'll honestly do fine in this class. Put in the actual work required outside and during class and you'll get a lot out of her lectures and material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really terrible communicator. Do not take this Professor she is way to invested in her class and wont understand if other things are happening in ur life. Gave me my worst grade ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's approachable, outspoken, but strict when in lectures & deadlines. Material is interesting & she gives examples for better understanding. In exams, multiple choice & open ended responses are trickier than you think (her wording is weird & she's picky when grading) but does review sessions for exams. If you want the A, REALLY work hard for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was able to keep up with her lectures but I'm also a fast note taker. She didn't allow laptop use when we were in person but obv that couldn't be controlled when we went online. Her jokes fell flat and were kind of annoying but I give her points for effort. The final was tedious but an easy A if you paid attention in lecture/recitation.

Her lectures are confusing. she speaks fast & goes all over the place but somehow wants you to connect every little thing. She expects you to remember every little detail and example too. Went to her for test feedback & she was super rude, condescending, and passive-aggressive. When class moved online, she made class harder with more papers. Study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am not sure why she has such a low rating. Her lectures were extremely interesting, even funny at times (though that may be bc I'm an MCC major). The one midterm we took was easy if you paid attention in class and took detailed notes. I never did a reading, and I still managed to get an A. The project was pointless though.

Avoid at any cost, although I think she is the only prof for history of media&comm. Tests are very difficult, I studied really hard to get a B+. I hope you guys go back in person for fall, otherwise you will write a 3000 words final for this class. Don't take this class unless you are mcc major lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've ever had in NYU. She has tons of things in one regular lecture which gives her 75 minutes to illustrate but usually she finishes within 50 minutes, extremely fast and can't follow. Test extremely heavy and harsh grade. If you are not a genius plz avoid her. Gives us take home exam but adds lots of things one day before the due date
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Isra is not nearly as bad as all of these comments make her out to be. Her lectures are definitely dense and you have to attend lecture, but if you take good notes you'll be fine. The exams are mostly multiple choice but as long as you study and understand general themes it's not too bad. It could be WAY worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ali is an engaging lecturer-- HOWEVER, her grading standards are absolutely ridiculous. Your grade is widely based on two tests that are heavily multiple-choice, with multiple right answers for each question. So even if you understand the concepts, you could easily still get a terrible grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Isra was the only option for my required class, so I had no choice. She's a very good lecturer and is very passionate about what she preaches, but she expects you to be able to memorize every word she's ever said without the use of laptops to take notes. She is available outside of class, but not super helpful and kind of condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very fast and it's important to write down as much as you can. It was slightly difficult to know exactly what kind of questions she was going to ask on the 1st midterm but it got much easier throughout the rest of the semester to know the themes she wanted to focus on. It is not a difficult class if you understand the main themes.

Take extensive notes because even if she says it only once, it will most likely appear on an exam. We had to do a "research project" on the side and it was pointless and not actually graded. One of the assignments was to go to the library and take pictures of books. She did not review for the final exam, she missed a lecture and did not make it up.

Worst class I have taken at NYU. Butchered what seemed a very interesting syllabus, doesnt explain essay grades, and likes to argue just for the sake of it. Dont challenge her, youll get points off. Basically, the only way to succeed in this class is to treat her lecture content as gospel, and reiterate her own beliefs/ideas in the essays.

Im not sure why Professor Alis ratings are so terrible on here. She is very kind and knowledgable and makes the material discussed interesting. While her tests can be difficult in that its hard to navigate what shes looking for at first, if you make use of her office hours theyre not impossible to do well on.

Her lecture consists of one picture and two words and explains that for an hour. Materials are useless and boring. What's most terrible is that certain portion of test consist of fill in the blank, yet with 3 other words in the sentence. Hilarious
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I worked so hard for a B in her class last semester. Absolutely the WORST class I have ever taken at NYU- she removed all the texts from her slides and does not allow laptops or any technology. If she mentions something once in passing- it might be on the test. Students did not have good grades, and her lectures are heavy and confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Smart and knows the field really well and seems like a really nice person but not the best teacher. Unclear grading criteria with vague feedback on assignments. Lectures are fun but you sometimes don't really know the point of it which doesn't help when you have to connect concepts. Sometimes there could be multiple answers but she just picks one.

reviews.comment: Prof Ali is one of the funniest, most knowledgable professors I've ever had. She can be a bit short during class, but makes up for it with amazing help and discussions during office hours (def go!). This would've been the best class I've taken at NYU had it not been for her out of this world expectations. Absolutely amazing if you put in the effort

The material is interesting and informative. Additionally, Professor Ali expects you to do all the readings, keep up with them, and also be prepared for pop quizzes on them potentially a week after they're assigned because she can get behind. The projects were fun but difficult. She's very knowledgeable, a boss, and absolutely hilarious.

Course material was interesting, but readings went over my head and grading criteria for projects was not clear. Projects were fun and creative because of that, but the vagueness was challenging for me. I did not do many of the readings and did fine, but participation is a big part of this course. Prof Ali is funny and relatable, too.

Prof. Ali is entertaining + very knowledgeable. At times readings were over students' heads, but she compensated with extended discussions in class time.  Assignments were typically long complicated papers, but with enough assignments and discussion beforehand to make them manageable.  Tough grader, but willing to work with students, I'd say.
lectures are chill but grading isn't cuz you don't get the grade you expect even when you follow everything on the syllabus, so gl! reading is not little but do-able if you try.
He is a really cool guy with easy to follow lectures. His assignments can be a little cryptic, but he clears up any difficulties when asked. Very amazing professor.

Amazing professor who is very good at teaching. He recognizes the changing landscape of technology and coding, and shapes his class to reflect current trends, also being a very respected professional in his industry.

Loved his teaching, also could use ChatGPT on the final which was clutch. I think it really depends on your TA because she was the one who graded all my assignments. He's very approachable after class and as long as you put your face in his brain, he will grade well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: panos is one of my favorite professors! He often brings pizza for the whole class and is very knowledgeable. Straightforward and will give you what you need to succeed.

Great guy, especially if you get him warmed up in his office. He is extremely passionate for his work, and if he feels that you are interested in learning the topic in depth he can spend a lot of time with you.
Nice guy, really passionate for what he is teaching. I wish all my other professors were as engaging as Panos

great guy, funny greek accent, and interesting class. he is enthusiastic about the material, but the class is so broad that we never get deep into the material. interesting group projects, boring individual assignments
No Comments
panos really knew what he was talking about and was always willing to answer questions. He has a great sense of humor and a funny greek accent. I would definitely take him again.
He is a great professor. He can explain. Although the materials in this class is difficult to understand, under this professor, you will be able to know what it is.
Panos is a great teacher. He really knows what he is talking about and he makes every effort to be available to the students. I enjoyed the class, even though I was not interested in the topic.
He's the best. Such an easy class. Everyone walked out with an A. Take him if you can.

Fantastic all around professor. His lectures are very useful and interesting, he's easy to reach outside of class for feedback, and although the course uses a textbook it's (intentionally) free and online. It's also pretty light reading every week, at least compared to most other history courses! Grading was clear, concise, and very fair.

An extremely kind and caring professor! This class had a lot of reading (like 100-150 pages a week), but that's expected with an advanced history seminar. Gave us two free unexcused absences for the semester and was understanding when I needed an extension for a paper. 10/10 would take again!
Really helpful and understanding. The discussion based lectures are very intriguing and interactive.
Chill professor. Easy going discussion. Involve yourself atleast couple times every week in the discussion. Workload was light.

A really sweet professor who cares a lot about his students and makes sure they understand the material. He made the workload extremely manageable because of the online format and the graduate student strike and was super accessible outside of class. He had really detailed and interesting recorded lectures and a Q and A every week. Highly recommend

Irvin was super accessible outside of class and really adapted well to the online format. The class is not really a lot of work, but it is very important to be diligent and stay up to date on lectures. As long as you do not slack you will do well in the class. Irvin is also super knowledgeable, and his lectures are some of the best I have ever seen

Where do I even begin. He uses slides from another professor and then is confused by the content and tries to figure out what is going on. Hates having to put in extra work (ie review sessions). He talks back and judges students on their questions. The midterm was nothing like the practice midterm/work, included content we learned in later units.

He is very kind and has a sarcastic sense of humor (that apparently everyone takes seriously). The subject is difficult, for me at least, but he is very understanding. I recommend going to office hours where it's a lot easier to clear up any misconceptions, and he was especially helpful after the first midterm.
Great sense of humor.
Nice dude, doesn't budge on his rules no matter what. Tests way harder than all the practice/hws, Class test average was a 62.5. Make sure to lock in on time management or else you'll get cooked.

Ignore all the other review, Jung is the GOAT. Boy oh boy where do I start. Every class, a smile comes on my face. He brings joy to my day and is the only 11am class I would ever wake up for (I typically wake up at 2pm).  Although our class average on the midterm was a 63, he is still the GOAT for the W curve. I love you Professor Jung

This guy is not it; pick literally anyone else. He's lowkey just a yapper. If you have a hard-to-pronounce name, beware. He won't call on you for participation. Hates actually having to host office hours and review sessions (sad that he "misses out on lunch"). Not as funny as he thinks he is.
utilizes peak word salad during lecture, nothing from lecture/practice exam actually ends up on the real exams. run fast kids
GUYS RUN RUN AS FAST AS U CAN

Jud is a great director. He's really great. It's just that his lectures were a little boring and repetitive. I wish he had spoken more on directing different types of actors, and how to direct certain genres. But he's a really charismatic person, and a great connection to have.

He's witty and caring, and even helped me and some of my friends get a connection for one of our film endeavors. Great guy, but the lectures are repetitive and can get boring. Some lectures are randomly extremely helpful, but most of the time it's the same ten things being covered again and again.

Appreciated Judson as a prof but absolutely could not stand his lectures. They went on for so long and rarely anyone even payed attention or showed up. He's passionate about his craft which is inspiring, but I couldn't tell you half the things we talked about. I raised my hand maybe twice the entire semester.
Judson is awesome and so passionate, performance strategies lecture is kind of a pointless class but his personality and presentation style makes it at least bearable.

Hypothetically an interesting topic but his lectures are useless and annoying. Keeps the class going for much longer than necessary and everything covered in class could be said in much fewer words through a slideshow. Mandatory class and its bearable and not much work for an A, but lectures are painful.

Every class with Judd is like watching a TedTalk, both because he's a good lecturer and because his lectures go on for way longer than they should. It's repetitive, but he's chill. You'll watch good movies.

I had him for lecture. He is a really sweet and supportive professor. He is very passionate about his work, but I wish we could cover more content in class. What you learn is important, but I just wanted more! If you have any questions in class, he is always willing to discuss. I wish I had him for something like recitation!

I only had him for lecture, but they were a lot. The class seems like it would be super interesting, but after the third lecture it becomes clear that this class is not. I think it could be, but this professor rambles on and on and on about the same thing every lecture, and loses a lot of the classes attention.

Had him for recitation. Gives really good feedback on our directed scenes at the end of the semester. Very knowledgeable about his craft and thorough when explaining what could have been improved upon. Also, the fluctuations in his voice are very theatrical and it's fun to listen to.
Grading felt inconsistent, and feedback was minimal, so it was tough to improve

Getting help was also difficult- questions were either brushed off or answered in a way that didn't really clarify anything. Grading felt inconsistent, and feedback was minimal, so it was tough to improve.

The class is challenging, and the teaching could be clearer. Lectures don't always explain the concepts in an easy-to-understand way, and the examples sometimes don't align well with the homework. The homework itself is difficult, and grading tends to be strict. Exams are also often harder than the practice problems provided.

Tough class and the teaching could be clearer. Lectures don't always make the concepts easy to understand, and the examples don't always match the homework. Homework is challenging and grading can be strict. Exams also tend to be harder than the practice problems.

Tough class but great teacher! Teaching style uses lots of examples and helps work out problems with us in class. Homework is difficult, but always available for office hours and recitation practices with a very similar problem set. Homework is graded very easily and tests are very similar in difficulty to homework.

Support beyond class time was limited, and building a meaningful connection proved challenging. I would not feel confident seeking mentorship or a recommendation from this professor. By the end of the semester, many students were relieved the course had concluded. If given the option, I recommend choosing a different instructor.

Support outside of class was minimal, and establishing any real rapport was extremely difficult. I wouldn't feel comfortable depending on this professor for mentorship or a letter of recommendation. By the end of the term, most students were simply glad it had ended. If possible, I strongly suggest selecting a different instructor for this course.

This guy made my econ experience at NYU worthwhile. Patient, answered all my emails, and showed me grace when my mom was ill. He also wrote me a letter of rec for law school. Can't say enough good things about working with him, and during our last class, all of us thanked him for a wonderful experience. If you have to take this class, go with him.

This is the best econ prof at NYU. Prof. Scianimanico uses guided notes in each lecture to make sure you have all the information you need to succeed. He is very accessible outside of class and even outside of his office hours. Although most of your grade is exams, he explains everything that is going to be on the midterm/final before you take it.
Grades are actually impossible, teaches work not on the slides, unavailable consistently

Do not listen to the negative reviews. If you do not like long classes, don't take a 2.5 hour class. That is the only option for her course at NYU. She always let us out a solid 40 minutes early and if you show up, the lowest you will get is a B. She is a very kind and knowledgeable professor who I wish taught more classes at NYU. She was great!

I disagree with the negative reviews. Very straightforward clear about what you need to know for the exams, and exams are open book. She is very accessible and encourages questions during lecture, so our understanding is partly student-led. Honestly my easiest class of the semester because I tried.

Unhelpful lecture slides, speaks in really confusing ways, and lots of readings that she doesn't even cover in lecture. Very abstract and theory-based class, so know the case studies very well. Doesn't really teach and only rambles to himself in class (keep in mind, I came in with zero coding experience). Ended up self-teaching with ChatGPT and asking CS major friends for help.

By far one of the worst teachers I have ever had. The homework does not reflect what we learn in lecture, and he does not grade work until the end of the course, meaning you have no feedback on how you are doing until AFTER you've taken your final, worth 35%.
Nice guy but not good at teaching. Lectures are extremely tedious and unhelpful. Minor mistakes on homework result in large point deductions.

Teaches horribly, material is difficult enough, and all the assignments and homework are impossibly hard compared to the material that is taught. Everyone in the class is equally as confused and average test scores are low. Indicates how great he is as a teacher. For this class you just have to self teach everything.

Absolutely downright catastrophically bad; socially hindered with severe awkwardness that can feel rude at times, grueling lectures that have no engagement with students, and enough coursework to guarantee you have no time for any other course. Teacher has a horrible reputation throughout the department and it's recommended you take someone else.

Prof is definitely shy but literally you can ask him questions about everything and he's SO helpful. Always willing to put in the time and effort needed to explain things and make sure u get it. Also his exams aren't bad if you just pay attention

Avoid this professor! He will take attendance seriosuly and teaching mostly by reading slides. He gives complicated examples on class that nobody can follow. He also gives very long and hard homework. You might need to study something extra from the syllabus to complete them. His test is nothing related with the homework and on the easy side.
not a good teacher, cannot teach at all. a good person, but he's just a bit awkward.
He is a genuinely nice person, he is simply not a good teacher at all.
A kind and generous person.  But he expects you to learn, which maybe some people don't like.

Don't understand why his ratings are so low. His teachings were satisfactory, though I learned more in the online modules/assignments than his lectures. He is a very kind and caring person and had a generous curve on his exams. Takes feedback greatly, and made the final a lot easier after realizing the midterm was a bit difficult

I ended up dropping the class because of how bad my midterm grade was and how little of a curve he gave. He is nice but makes tests so insanely hard, and most students just stop showing up halfway through the sem. Most people who had him will tell you his class was the worst, just avoid

He's a great person but not a good teacher. He releases retrospectives. He asks students for lesson feedback and check in with them if they have any questions. 
Has high expectations on students, would extend the material by "too much."

Sucks at teaching, socially awkward doesn't get to know his students at all. Don't take

It's his first time teaching right out of grad which makes sense why he is super disorganized and not a great teacher. And, for an intro course, expects too much from students and isn't very flexible especially with office hours. All his assignments have mistakes and aren't clear. He's not a bad person just not a good teacher. Also kinda awkward.

okay guys when i say hes disorganized like its so bad i literally cannot do these assignments because theyre worded so poorly and he is so harsh on grading and he literally changes the criteria in the assignments HOURS before its due... please explore alternative professors for this class especially as an intro class tis so bad

Never checks attendance or gets to know your name. Midterm and problem sets are very poorly worded causing lots of confusion on what was expected. The entire course is essentially self taught through modules but that is standard across all intro to comp prog classes as well as 30% midterm 30% problem sets 30% final and 10% module quiz/participation

His instructions on the assignments are so confusing and I needed to ask many clarification questions. The grading is extremely unclear. He is very kind and caring, so that somewhat makes up for it. But I would not take him again.

Dr. K is the real deal. While he focuses on making sure you understand the textbook concepts, he equally cares about ensuring you learn soft skills. If you show up on time, participate, and ask questions, you will be halfway there. Not only is he my professor, but he is also my faculty advisor. I now have a lifelong mentor in Dr. K.
Alot of research and readings. Group projects are expected. He is very passionate, respected, and inspirational. There is a field trip and alot of guest speakers.

Dr. K is a wonderful and inspiring professor who delivers amazing lectures and makes every class genuinely fun and engaging. The course material is incredibly interesting and valuable, and he truly cares about his students both academically and professionally. I have learned so much from him. One of the most rewarding classes I've taken.

With Dr. K, you'll learn the foundations of business and apply it to the hospitality and travel industry. But most importantly, you will learn how to be a more disciplined person by learning about essential soft skills. If you put in the work, it is guaranteed you'll learn valuable lessons about yourself as a student and as a future professional.

Best Professor ever, cannot recommend enough. He is so engaging in class and not only good at explaining the content but also teaches life lessons. He is very realistic about the society and gives great tips and advice. Very inspirational professor.

Dr.K is simply amazing. His classes are always so fun and engaging. He really cares for his students and is ready to help you. You will learn so much from him. The class is not difficult as long as you put in the effort. Easily one of my favorite professors!

Dr. K is the professor you hope to get at NYU. His passion is contagious and his industry experiences bring the classroom to life. On top of class visits to Google HQ or the UN, every class was insightful and inspiring. He truly cares about student success — always approachable, endlessly supportive, and genuinely invested in our growth.

Dr. K is an incredibly passionate professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. His classes are an excellent way to learn about Business and offer valuable life lessons. I recommend taking his class.
Dr.K is a really great professor, you should take his class, it is worth it. He has a great passion to teach which made the class really interesting and engaging.

Dr. K is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about business and marketing, making every lecture engaging and insightful. He genuinely cares about their students' success and is always approachable for help. I highly recommend taking their class!

Dr. K is an amazing Professor! Truly cares for his students, wants the best for them, and will push them to do their best. I genuinely thought that this class was fun, interactive, and very informative. His teachings about life and the business world are so meaningful and valuable. I would certainly take him again!!!!

Dr.K is one of the most amazing professors here at NYU. His lecture is amazing, and he cares for his students so much, which helps students make their future endeavors successful. Just keep your focus and try to understand what he is saying. Then all good! I highly recommend taking his class and also want others to get an impact from him, like me.

Dr. K is a very kind professor.  He wants us to succeed in life and is well-known in the industry. He teaches many life lessons along with the curriculum. Exams are challenging but not impossible if you study and read the textbook. It's not an easy A; work is required.  But you will learn. I enjoyed my experience with Dr. K.

Dr. K is a great human being and a great professor. He is hilarious, engaging, and inspirational. I have taken away so many life lessons from his teachings and advice. He truly cares for his students and the school. He places a deep focus on networking and encourages students to utilize as many resources that NYU has to offer. Read the textbook!

The best professor I have had so far in SPS NYU. Class is exciting, he's super funny, cares about your personal life and personal career more than your grades. Priortizes your understanding of the concepts and really cares for his students. Don't be afraid to ask questions in class, and make sure to participate! Offers immense support if needed.

Ok to be fair I love Dr. K. Such a respected professor with clear grading criteria. It's just a LOT OF WORK. I am repeating, A LOT OF WORK. Participation matters very much along with weekly group presentations. I love him, I think I grew a lot through his class, but it was stressful.

Most of the people who give her bad reviews don't show up to class then complains when they get a bad score. Data structures is a hard class and as long as you keep up with work and seek help via office hours or TA, Klukowska teaches the material better than any other professors.

This professor is great at teaching and you will learn a lot. However, there are quizzes and projects as well as a midterm and a final. The class is graded tough and can be a challenge. However, the professor is very kind and super helpful.

She really cares about her students and wants to see us succeed, often checking ed (the online discussion forum we used) late at night outside of school hours. reviews.comment: Heavy projects, inaccessible lectures, and tough exams make the class so stressful. If you want to be seriously challenged, take her, otherwise please avoid.

Extremely difficult exams with MCQs containing more than 8 choices and meaningless multi-select. Online quizzes were manageable but projects require an abnormal amount of time for a second-level CS course and grading is very strict and points are deducted for something as absurd as not enough in-code documentation. very awful, avoid at all costs.

This class was so draining. The projects and quizzes are nearly impossible, and there is no curve. The class average for the midterm was a D and currently overall is a C+ but she doesn't seem to care. Her lectures are entirely conceptual so there is very little actual code taught, so for projects you are left to blindly lead yourself. Dont take!!

Joanna's lectures really helps you understand. Event if I recieve a terrible final grade I will not regret taking her. If you want to be a good programmer and are heading towards CS major do take her, else take someoneelse for good grades

Avoid at all costs! While she does have a clear criteria, the workload is difficult, especially the last project, which will take up much of your time. Mental breakdown!!! But have to admit this professor teaches clearly.

Her lectures is useful and help you build a solid foundation in CS. She makes difficult concepts become easy to understand and engaging. Very organized she is unlike other professors I had who were all over the place confusing students. Go to her office hours if can, the best help ever. She does curve the class if she sees students struggling.

reviews.comment: Joanna is a nice person. She does give hard assignments but is very reasonable compared to other CS professors I had. She really does help you become a better coder and you really lot a lot of practical stuff. If you do all the work, you will succeed and get a good grade.
A very challenging professor with difficult exams and long projects. Only take this class if you're serious about cs and actually wanna improve. Otherwise, take an easier professor.
