reviews.comment: Why is there so much negativity? She is a tough grader, but she is also one of the few well-organized professors in the computer science department who actively teaches. The level of difficulty in her homework is pretty reasonable (reasonably hard, but they would help you develop good coding habits like input and error handling)
Don't take, otherwise you'll end up struggling throughout the course.
She somehow makes the class extremely stressful for no good reason, whether intentional or not. The teaching style will probably suit high school students more to be honest.

Reviews are not harsh. Projects require 30+hrs of work (you'll still do bad). Lectures and concepts seem simple but exams are rough. Pointless recitations. She expects 6-8 hrs of studying outside of projects a week. Could not recommend less. She's cold. RIP your GPA. You will become a good coder, but out of pain and suffering.

Clear lectures, but exams are much more difficult, testing things you thought were trivial. I recommend doing the practice sets and slide deck questions/examples. Tough projects that take a lot of time. Not approachable: condescending. Curved from a 75 (C) to a B- at the end of the semester. Wouldn't recommend for an easy A, but prepares you well.

Professor is pretty good compared to other data structure professors. You really do learn a lot. The projects are not that hard, if you start them sooner, there is just a lot of test cases to complete, but there was only one truly hard project. If you put in the work for quizzes and projects, you can do well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thought I would get a awful grade since it is a tough course and I didn't take the prerequisite course Basic Algorithm, but her lecture is extremely inspiring and useful so I paid some effort and got back on track. I end up getting an A despite the fact that I gave up half of the points on a couple of homeworks and got a B for the midterm.
Can't believe she can make data structure so difficult.
Sure she makes you a good coder. That'll be your consolation prize when she tanks your gpa after spending countless nights writing her projects. Do not be fooled by her 5/5 here like I was

I truly do not understand how this professor has a 5 on this website. If you truly believe this is accurate then I truly believe you will get an F in this class by looking at the star distribution. I truly don't understand why doesn't Joanna buy herself a punching bag instead of pulling up to CANTOR-200, as all of us could have better lives.
Pay attention during lectures and properly spend time to understand the concepts and this class isn't as bad as everyone makes it seem like it is.

Joanna's class develops a strong foundation in computer science that will help you with the rest of your computer science journey. Took this class 2 semesters ago, and I'll say this, if you ever want to work at FAANG or any other big tech/quant company: take Joanna's class and push your capabilities. Work in the present to succeed in the future.

Yeah the projects are hard but that's why programmers get paid a lot lol you can't get a job and cry about doing a big task or project. This class is NOT for the weak but Joanna will help you learn and get you HIRED. If you're not cut out for this workload, don't go into CS. Data structures are the foundation of CS and one day you will thank her.

Most of these reviews fooled me... Joanna is a BAD professor. Ask anyone in my Data Structures class, and they will say as much. Her teaching skills are awful in a REALLY intense class, she grades harshly, and her recitation leaders are equally bad. The ones who say she's the worst? - The 15-20% of us who got above a B. She does not prep you 4 CS.

you will become a good coder in this class but at the price of your gpa and your will to continue learning cs. Take anyone but her. Has one of the strictest grading policies of any professor I have taken. Her exams are HARD and very unforgiving and her projects will take you an insane amount of time.

People are too harsh. Projects are difficult, but they prepare you to become a good programmer. I have cried over this class but everyone giving a bad review is bitter. I've learnt a lot and the projects are useful. Joanna is a very good lecturer. I'm a humanities major and not great at CS but have done well in the class. Quizzes aren't that hard.
The review below this

Very harsh grader. Her assignments leave the university's tutors confused. Very easy to mess up her quizzes/ exams and a couple bad grades can bring your grade to a C. Is very knowledgeable but comes off as condescending if you ask for help. Take someone else if you haven't coded for your whole life
I had to drop my minor due to this course. If it was another professor, I know the outcome would've been different. If you learn through example, this is not the professor for you.

She is by far the most difficult CS professor I have encountered at NYU. Her lectures are structured in the sense that they are not appealing to all learning types and it makes it difficult to learn things. Very little example code, or explanation on how to execute the concepts. If you learn by example, this is not the professor for you.

Took Joanna last semester, out of 5 CS professors I have encountered thus far, she is the best one if you want to learn. I think she delivers material very well and is very engaging, the stuff she explained really stuck with me. Her quizzes are tricky though, a couple of missed questions and you're getting C, but she did have a curve at the end.
Best class of my life! Amazing lecturer and fair exams.

Prof Klukowska is the most serious prof ever. I recall her laughing only 4 times that semester(spoiler): 1. 8 rabbit=rabyte 2. Little vs Big Endian 3&4. Mock at others and me kindly for being dumb. She is very caring and answers all of your question, but she likely won't make you love CS. She is most helpful if you are already interested in CS.

Regardless of my grade, I can say prof K's lectures are very well organized, insightful and she's always willing to help, only if you ask her first. If you want to learn, take her class. If you are just looking to get through data structures with a good grade, take another prof. Would be very helpful the sooner you get used to her testing style.

simply not a good professor. quizzes and midterm are difficult for no reason and her answer keys almost always have at least 1 mistake or more. a very theoretical class with lots of useless "trace the output" like questions rather than actually writing/designing programs. take bari if you can. gl.

Aside from CS102 being a complete waste of time to begin with, Klukowsa makes sure it's as big of a waste of time as possible. We have the midterm in a few days and have so far covered Linked Lists in lecture. But not extensively at all. Nor have we applied them in any context. Four 30 min quizzes are 24% of ur grade and class avg is an F.

Don't take a class with her unless you know all the material already. Posts problem sets where the instructions are useless then spends 40 minutes each class explaining what she wants. When you try to reach out to her for help she actively avoids you. She does not even grade assignments and her auto-grader makes mistakes. Dont take her class
joanna is a good professor. projects get difficult by end of the year so make sure you start them early. quizzes and tests were harder than the projects for me personally. no curve.
Class isn't easy but you really learn. She cares a lot about the subject. Reminds you why the subjects are worth learning about

She is extremely condescending and unapproachable. Projects are horrendously difficult, quizzes and exams are much more manageable. Extremely rude when people asked questions during class. She teaches as though she would rather be doing anything else.
the GOAT

Joanna is useless to me. She is rude and condescending in class and that makes her absolutely unapproachable for me. Joanna is a super caring CS professor. She's willing to sit with her students and give them her full attention at all times. Lectures go a bit fast- don't fall behind on the material. Partly overlapped with CS 310 Basic Algorithm. Not difficult as long as studied well in Basic Algorithm course. Moderate (a little bit heavy) homework. Lectures are easy to follow up

If you get the chance to, absolutely take Joanna at least once during your CS degree. Her projects and recitation activities are difficult but really encourage full comprehension of the material. reviews.comment: I mean will I fail the final? Probably. Did I learn a lot over the course of the semester? Certainly. She has a unique personality thats not meant for everyone, be ready to take a joke. But theres no doubt shes incredibly smart at what she teaches.

I don't understand why she graded us so harshly. Lots of Quizzes at the beginning of a morning class. Really nice and warm person. But lecture not that informative as others said. Very few office hours, not wanting to help regarding grades.

reviews.comment: To be honest I withdrew from this class. I personally didn't find the lectures to be all that informative, and the things we needed to know for the exam were not clear. reviews.comment: I love Joanna. I have had the greatest computer science experience with her in Data Structures, and highly recommend for everyone to take her.

Many classmates drop/change the section from her class. We got a lot of work to do for each projects. She's really a tough grader for the exam, especially for some small details. Comparing to other sections, her section was tough and heavy. The way she assigns work is just like her students have only one course to take for the semester.

I adore Joanna. Took her for DS, and even took 8am just to get her again for CSO. Her lecture explanations are always crystal clear (go to them!). Start the projects early and they are no problem, spec is detailed on expectations (plus she is very active on Piazza). Tests are super fair, never any surprises - but they will test you thoroughly.

This is by far the toughest class I've taken at NYU and Joanna as a prof. certainly doesn't make it any easier. You really need to attend every class as the less you understand in lectures, the more you will need to read on your own time. She's a tough grader and overall, including reading and HW, this class took up approx. 10 hrs/week of work. GL
super great lectures, learned so much from her, would highly recommend. do as she says and you'll do great.
best comp sci teacher

Although Joanna is a relatively tough grader, you will ultimately get a higher grade with her than with another professor (e.g. Bari). Amazing teacher, she even takes questions from real CS interviews. One of the questions discussed in class was the exact same question I was asked in my internship interview. Personally got an A-, highly recommend.
Very difficult to get an A. Great lectures, test heavy, pop quizzez.. take Bari if you can  hes more chill. Shes a solid choice otherwise.

I have to say she's the best cs professor ever. She explains everything super clear and knows the class material very well. I took both Data Structure and CSO with her. I learnt a lot. Really tough work without enough hint. Comparing to other sections, the work is unreasonable.

reviews.comment: Go to class and take notes, you will learn so much and she explains things clearly and in depth. Adhere to her spec for projects or your grade will be wrecked; if things are not clear, ASK questions. Her exams are super fair, make sure you understand concepts and do not rely on solely memorizing code.

I honestly didn't think that she was too difficult as a professor, exam average is 80. She is very fair. Take the time to review the material on your own time and it won't be too bad. Make sure you're very thorough and efficient in all of your projects from the start because everyone gets wrecked on the first one.

She's highly recommended and now that I took her Data Structures class I know why! You will learn AND work hard. I recommend forming a study group in the class for studying purposes. There is no group work except in recitations. She only teaches CSO in the Spring semester. Most of the grade (65%) is only the midterm and final. She doesn't curve.

Despite that, she did an amazing job being thorough with the material, and is a professor that I genuinely like to go to her lectures.  TAKE HER 500% if you have a choice between her and anyone else for either 201 or 102!

An excellent lecturer, makes classes interactive and remembers the names of her students. Does pop quizzes if she sees attendance drop. Her exams are long, but she's up front about the material on it. She loves to assign stuff, so don't wait until the last minute to start something.  She's worth the effort, though.

reviews.comment: Joanna is a fantastic lecturer, extremely organized, and very helpful. She gives so many helpful resources and they are all extremely clear and concise. Read everything she posts! I will say, even though this is true for every CS teacher I've had, I wish she / the graders gave the assignments back earlier so you can get feedback quicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you're serious about Data Structures and really want to learn about it, take Joanna's class! She makes you learn more about knowing an algorithm rather than memorizing the code. She can be challenging, but she is one of the best teachers you will ever have. Her office hours are extremely helpful too.

I had Joanna for 102 as well and honestly I think it was a joke compared to 201.  201 lectures are just way more rushed and difficult to digest. Also, pop quizzes are weighed pretty heavily (almost 10%) despite them being quite luck based (there were only 3 of them and who the hell can always be caught up in a class like 201).  She's helpful tho.

Joanna is so solid. Her accent is both understandable and enjoyable (Polish-like tendencies) so I recommend lectures in a major way. I'm not gonna lie, this professor is gonna grade you. Her pen is a weapon and you have to battle it. Buy the book fam, save laundry quarters for a couple months or something, I don't know your life, but it's worth it
Super easy A, definitely take her. Jokes aside, easy A if you actually study the lecture notes and do the practice questions from the book.
Her projects are one of the simplest compared with other professors since all you need to do is implement classes and not start everything from scratch. Her tests, though, are difficult

I took the class before this in the curriculum with a very easy professor that made me think I was a coding genius, put Professor Klukowska kicked me into reality. She is really one of the best professors I've ever had, and I've learned more from her in 2 months of this class than in any class I've taken before. Take her take her take her!

She really goes into the algorithms of how things work and is big on visuals. Not much coding in class, and even then it is pseudocode. She cares more about your understanding. Projects are tough though and they come back-to-back, so be prepared to think and design your programs. Homeworks are not graded but prepare you for quizzes/tests
She is really nice and always there to help. Just do not be afraid to ask questions and work enough to get an A

I had Professor Klukowska at NYU this semester, as a freshman. Her class was a perfect introduction to Java and Computer Science, and I'm so glad to have her again in the Spring for Data Structures! Her class isn't easy but it's so worth it once you have those "ooooh!! OOH!!" moments. She's always available and there for her students. 1010.

Joanna is by far one of the best Computer Science teachers I've had. Her notes are clear and she provides source code for every problem. Exams are really straightforward  they test whether or not you've done the homework on your own. If you listen in class you will do well.

She is a helpful professor. The programming projects are a little bit tough if you pursue extra credits. The homework is manageable. If you want to get a high grade, read her lecture notes and complete all of homework.

She's a friendly and nice person, and is very helpful and understanding during office hours. Lectures are pretty boring. Her class is hard but she does her best to ensure the success of all of her students. Projects are extremely comprehensive so you spend a lot of time on them but still learn a lot. If you take her class, you better love Java.
She's funny and makes the subject engaging!

The class is hard. She makes herself very available to answer questions, but by no means will she ever give you answers. She'll make you work for everything and it's draining but so much better in the long run. I finally feel challenged for once at NYU, like I'm getting my money's worth. Be ready for hours++ of work per week though!

I took Joanna for C++ back in 2011 at Hunter. She will definitely work you but it will pay off in the long run. Get ready to program at least 30+ hours a week. She goes out of her way to help her students. She provides additionalsupplemental resources to help you understand the content as much as possible. No slacking allowed in her class.
Very unclear directions on the homework assignments and tests. Is not very helpful outside of class when asked. Not sure she realizes how difficult to understand her wording can be.

One of the best professors I have ever had at NYU. Clear, concise, and always very well prepared for lectures. Posts notes on every lecture, encourages participation. Very approachable and gives extremely fair exams. Definitely recommend.

Joanna was a TA for this class and tried to make it work while the professors were a mess. She really helped out making the class easier to understand. She would always make her self available for help and would try to assist in every way possible while the professors were mostly useless. She is willing to work with you and help you out.

She was a Data Structures TA and did well with what she was given. The professors posted incorrect code, poor examples, length and unclear assignments, and she was sort of the messenger for it all. The professors needed work but as a TA she was kind and helpful. She was very available and made the best of a sticky situation with bad professors.
She explains things well and is very helpful if you try. Attend classes, otherwise you will be lost on exams.

Completely unprepared; posted practice problems and sample exams without answers. Had sample code that you were supposed to follow along with during class, but wouldn't post them until after the class... and was, in general, very little help.

Joanna has a mean attitude and a lazy answer for everything. She has zero teaching abilities and blames everything on everyone but herself. Avoid her at all costs, taking a class with her will ruin your semester

I graduated from NYU a few years ago, and Professor Moore's class is the only one I think about years later. I learned so much in the time I spent in her classroom, and I cannot recommend her enough. It is a privilege to be one of her students. Grading is admittedly tough, but it's so worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Moore is an amazing lecturer and super sweet person. My only complaint is that the entire class was graded on two assignments (a midterm and a 10+ page final essay), and depending on who the TA is, the grading can be kind of tough. Interesting class but not sure I would take it again tbh.

yes. yes. and yes. Take race and media with prof. Moore. Her lectures are both informational and entertaining. Though the class is reading heavy, the readings are incredibly interesting. For the final paper you can write about anything related to race and media so there's many options for you to express yourself creatively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class in the Spring 2023 semester and returned to write this review now because I haven't stopped thinking about it. Out of every class I took at NYU, this was by far the best. It opened me up to a new level of thinking, and I will always recommend it. I will remember Prof. Moore for her intelligence and kindness -- sign up if you can!

Prof Moore is a very intelligent professor and challenges students to think outside the box. The grading is not ideal as it is based off two papers that range from 5-10+ pages and are assigned DAYS in advance. Ambiguous preparation for tests and unclear grading. Race + Media was insightful but I wouldn't take it again for the sake of my GPA.

Kelli is the best professor I've ever taken in MCC! She challenges us to think critically and look beyond our assumptions. I learned so much about the world and how to be a strong, compassionate woman through this class that I expected to just be like any other.

Incredible! So sweet, very helpful. She wants you to read in order to familiarize yourself with the subject matter but lectures are often discussions about modern day examples. Open to democratic classroom environment, i.e. suggestions. Wants students to explore new ideas and be open to new insights. If you're woke, she's for you.

Professor Moore is by far my favorite professor at  NYU. She cares about her students, is always available and willing to help, and is extremely intelligent and passionate about her studies. Though Race and Media is not an easy A, it is a great class and HIGHLY recommend taking it.

Dr. Ralph, very knowledgeable about Art History, is a difficult professor to work with. I thought it would be a great introduction, not nearly as writing heavy as it was. With that many written assignments, instructions could have at least been clear, (never the case). When trying to discuss the mixup she was dismissive and rude. Had to withdraw.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best class I've taken at NYU! Karen is incredibly knowledgeable about medieval art and her enthusiasm can really be felt in the class. The work is manageable and the grading criteria is clear (make sure to score the extra credit points!). Love her, love the class, would one million percent take again. No idea why bad reviews exist here.

Dr. Ralph is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. She knows a crazy amount about medieval art/architecture/life (+ way more) and is eager to share this information, making the class engaging and informative. There is a decent amount of reading but it's not too hard as it relates to the subjects discussed in lecture. Take this class!

Professor Ralph was one of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever had. You could ask her any question and she would give you a thoughtful and incredibly detailed answer. Though she is a tough grader, if you put in the work you will get a good grade. Highly recommend taking her course at NYU Paris!

Karen... You love her or hate her or both. She is insanely knowledgeable, basically a walking encyclopedia. She can sometimes be hilarious, when it has to do with art. But in class, her priority is Gothic art, and if you don't do your reading or follow her mega-detailed rubric, she/you won't be happy. She can come off really cold, but learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She genuinely doesnt care about her students. Never met a professor like her (and i mean that in the worst way.). Has a very strict grading rubric and only cares that you follow it specifically, doesnt care about your actual skill level. Gives you 10 minutes when you ask to meet with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best prof ever

Very organized and efficient! Tests and quizzes are fair, no tricks. Clear lectures, many online resources, many tutors available. A lot is learned through online videos that are then expanded on in the lectures, so if you don't like that maybe avoid. Easy to get a good grade if you just do the work.

He is the best professor that I am going to ever have in nyu, I knew this since the first week I have him. I take this course as an elective and choose cs and learn python because of him. Really love Prof. Kapp, take him if u can!!!!!!!!!!!!
only 1 month in and i already know he's the best professor ill ever have in nyu
Professor Kapp was incredible! He gave me such a good intro to the computer programming world.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: choose him, wont regret, mvp
such a funny and engaging professor. made learning to code for the first time so logical and fun, like solving puzzles every class. learned a lot without making the class too difficult

What else can be said about Craig at this point... he is obviously well respected and admired at NYU. Truly, a special professor. If you are looking to take a class from a great professor and become inspired, look no further! Craig gave lectures that were inspirational and very interesting. He is the BEST! You will be lucky to take his course!!!

LITERALLY WORSHIP THIS MAN BEST PROF IVE EVER HAD
Pros: Extremely kind (Prof Kapp has NEVER come to class in a bad mood); Engaging, amazing lectures; Organized; Very funny & talented at teaching; Homework is long but easy & instantly graded; Gives free snacks; Great office hours
Cons: Homework takes VERY long to do; midterm and final are difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: BEST TEACHER. I got a C+ and I'm still writing this because that was a me problem tbh. You have every resource and opportunity to succeed in this class. USE THE TUTORS- wish I realized that sooner. My only complaint is the weekly assignment took me 11+ hours every week... Although this is an intro class, you jump write in which was tough.
He is the perfect prof to get u started in computer programming. Take him if you can :)

He is a gem. Take his class if you can, its so well organized and you can contact him and the TAs trough text in this website where you can see other questions and responses and be anonymous. He also added 10 grace days to the 10 he already gave us to encourage students to keep going and get good grades.

Kapp is a great professor, he's very caring about students. However, his hws and exams are BRUTAL. He does give grace days for hws, which can be very helpful. Final exam was very hard and had too many questions; he had to give free points! However, you will definitely learn a lot of coding in this class that you otherwise would have never learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very caring and funny professor who makes his classes dynamic, and in this way, you learn the material well. That said, I've noticed he can sometimes play "gotcha" on the exams which is disheartening and can ruin your grade. He is a good grader though and understands where credit should be given.

BY FAR the kindest and most amazing professor I have met at NYU. He is not only incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about his subject, but he is always looking out for his students and giving them the best chance at success. He is flexible and understanding for each student despite the large class. Very encouraging and is a great help during OH

Amazing professor, I know I will come out of class understanding everything he teaches. He's a super fair grader and gives homework that is relevant to what we're learning. It's a LOT of hw tho so do not take this course w/ other intense classes! Exams are also hard but he is fair and adjusts accordingly. He just wants you to learn and succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have graduated and I took three classes with Craig. He was absolutely amazing and was one of the best profs I had at NYU. The stuff I learned from his lectures is so applicable to my current study and industry work.

He is one of the best professors in NYU. Truly kind and respectful. BUT, this class really took a toll on my mental health. You will learn so much about web development but it really requires a lot of time and work. Don't take this class if you have a lot of stuff going on or a lot of other important courses that are difficult along side it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: This man is going straight to heaven

He's a kind Prof. But he truly assigns way to much assignments that its overwhelming. Hw's were so long and tough, very different from lecture wheres hes so nice with easy questions. You will learn a lot, but at the expense of any free time you have sadly. Exams were pretty hard unlike review sheets easy. Too much workload for a level 60 cs class.

reviews.comment: Still taking his class but he had me when he brought snacks to his workshop today :) super helpful, really really nice and handsome too. Hopefully we get Oreos next workshop, I'll update at the end of the semester
absolute GOAT.
GOAT

Amazing and sweet prof, he wants you to learn relevant skills AND get an A. Although he is an easy grader and pushes back deadlines / gives grace days, he assigns waaayy too much work; his level 60 web-dev course was more work than CS201 and almost as much as linear algebra. Nothing was really difficult, but be ready to put in the work / time

Pay attention in class&do your assignments and you're set. I've never had concepts explained so clearly to me + he provides great examples to teach you further. Super friendly, accessible outside class, clear explanations, hws that help you learn, clear & FAIR grading policy. Best prof I've ever had in my life-- appreciate the time you have w him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kapp is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. His class (computer programming) is enjoyable and I get excited to go to it. There is definitely homework, but it doesn't feel like busy work. I feel like when I do the homework I am actually getting better at a skill. I would totally take his class again!!

This class is HARD for non-coders (like me) but Prof. Kapp is so accessible and such a great professor that as long as your willing to work, it'll be one of the most enriching classes at NYU. Take it if you want to learn and are willing to dedicate 4-10 hours on HW (there are like 12 of them).
Confused the whole time in class

He gives good lectures, but his homework is tough. You need to spend a lot of time working. And you have both the projects and exams for midterm and final. Too much workload for a 300-level cs class. The final exam is hard but curved. Don't just take his class because you see a 5 here.

Genuinely godsent! Don't know many professors who are as clear, understanding, and talented at teaching as Craig. I just wish he taught more classes in the department. NYU and his students are so lucky to have him.
The kindest professor in the world. I can't think about a reason that makes ma hate this class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Very caring and really looks out for all the students. Clear instructions, and exams are very easy. Have fun taking his class, you won't regret it! 10/10 will take again in the future.
Take his course, you can't have a CS professor better than Craig at NYU
He's the most organized professor I've ever had. HW and extra credits improved my grades a lot cuz I did really bad in the midterm. I wish he could teach more advanced classes.
He's the most organized prof I've ever had. I wish he could teach more advanced classes.
Great professor with inspirational lecture! Extra credits will boost your grade!

I came back to rate Dr. Kapp after taking my second CS class at NYU. My professor now is so bad and I started to appreciate Dr. Kapp a LOT more. now thinking back all the lectures were SO interesting I actually was excited to go.
a great professor with interesting lectures, extra credit for final grades

Prof Kapp is simply amazing. I love his lectures and appreciate the efforts he put in. I think the assignments could be way too long for an intro course but these long assignments did help me to understand and memorize the skills really well. So if you're planning to learn some solid coding skills, do take him and do the hw!

I have never seen a professor put in as much effort as Kapp; It's truly incredible. However, as a byproduct, the class is a lot of work for a minors-level course. The assignments will have you going for hours. You'll learn a lot, but be prepared to allocate some serious time - especially if you're only moderately comfortable with coding.

Spr 2022. This class takes way more time than my major courses!! Kapp's incredibly hard weekly assignments make me wanna smash my keyboard sometimes... If you do enough practice exam and save them with templates, the final exam will be quite similar despite very limited time!
Professor Kapp is a genius! His lecture is clear and inspirational. There will also be extra credits for hw assignments to boost your grade. Best professor from CS department!

He is a good professor and pays a lot of attention to students, however, the hw assignments are extremely long and time consuming. Requires self-learning, and repeats some contents during lectures which sometimes is tedious. But you will learn a lot in his class and is worth taking if you want to build a strong foundation for future coding.

It actually hard to grade. If we are only talking about teaching skills, he gets 5/5 as he is very good at that and he also gives extra credit as long as you work for it. That being said, his homework is EXTREMELY LONG and exam is nowhere near easy. The exam is not ez but the median is way too high. I also feel like a lot ppl in class had prior exp

OMG I LOVE HIM. TAKE HIM. best professor I've ever had in my life. he is also really cute and caring lol. However, he does give a TON of assignments that will make you go nuts. Go to the tutors for help with that. The midterm was simple but the final was hard - lots of reading code. I changed my whole major to CS after taking him. He is a real gem.

Professor Kapp is AMAZING. I can't say enough good things about him. I've had few teachers who care as deeply as he does about his students' success. If you have a question, he responds extremely thoroughly, often within 15 minutes or less. I have so much gratitude towards Professor Kapp; If you have the opportunity to take his class, you must!
He is the best. Definitely take him.

Professor Kapp is the nicest person I ever met. He is the best professor in the world:) He also teaches game design, but I will not take this course probably, bc I do not like the turtle thing in this course. In all, I recommend him to everyone.
This class is very hard and time consuming, but if you work with the professor, he will help you.

reviews.comment: Even though this was an intro course, professor Kapp has made it the hardest python class I have ever taken. I learned basic Java for two years and I still feel stressed learning Python.

reviews.comment: Dont take from this professor! The assignments are not hard to get, but take too much time. The tests are ridiculously hard and are timed.

Professor Kappa is the worst professor at NYU. He doesn't care about the students and will make your life hell. If you take from this professor, you will spend your whole semester working on it. It is not worth your time.
best cs teacher in nyu
You will definitely miss him after you go on to take upper-level courses. Best CS professor ever.
He is the Best.
Good at explaining things, but his pace is way too slow. Homeworks are easy, multiple choice exams which is weird but its fine as long as you be careful. Easy A overall.

Online midterm & final was tough but he curved it. The assignments get much more complicated half way throughout the course but I think they're worth it, especially if you really wanna learn coding. He was super accessible on Ed forum. Extra credits are available. Although his A range is 95+, it's not as crazy as it sounds. Super caring & nice

He is a very good professor but get ready to work. The extra credit isn't something to really get excited about because a kindergartener can get an A in the class if they wanna put in 40 hours a week alone on it. In other words, if you're already willing to go that far, you wont need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ya, hes a great prof but I had to p/f the class b/c I was spending more time in that class, doing the outrageously long WEEKLY hws, than in my other 3 classes combined and this is 100% NOT exaggeration. I had to work full t this sem b/c of fam financial hardship, so I just couldnt push through, shame! Material vry EZ, just inappropriate work load!

Kapp is such a great prof! Extra credit features on hw, midterm was a bit brutal but he curved it, and we get 7 grace days to turn things in. He does parts of the weekly hw in class and shares the code with us.

He is definitely a great professor, explains everything clearly, and always helpful during office hours. However, if you are not a CS major(like me) and have 0 experience in CS, this class is definitely hard. Assignments are lengthy and you have to spend tons of time in it. The final exam is too difficult. I would say that he might be overrated.

Professor Kapp was great - I'm actually a CS major because of him. He made learning Python super easy and fun and was great at clearing up any confusion students had. The class wasn't difficult - as long as you do the modules you'll be fine and there are many extra credit opportunities. Take him if you can! I wish he taught more CS major reqs

Best Prof in NYU!!! He's so nice and helpful, just like an angel!! His examples are fun and interesting which will keep your focus and pay more attention. His classes are not boring AT ALL! I enjoyed it so much besides his HWs might need some time to finish and his tests are a little bit tough TAT.

Teaching during COVID is not easy, and Prof. Kapp honestly such a g. Everyone starts off the semester with 7 grace days to hand in assignments, and he is continuously so understanding and contactable through email and the Ed class forum. Pretty lecture-heavy, but that's to be expected. He makes it fun, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Craig Kapp made me like Python. He explained the concepts in detailed and provided helpful examples in class. His homework was quite interesting.
Saw him at Penn Station once from afar, not in a weird way tho. Best day of my life. didn't say much. He's a hell of a guy.
Amazing professor, very caring; lot of extra credit.

Kapp is a wonderful professor, and is just an all around great guy. He is an effective professor, and is highly knowledgable at the same time. However, this results in people trying extremely hard to do well, which makes the curve somewhat unforgiving. If you want to learn Python well, this is the guy you want.

One of the best cs professors I've had the pleasure to take classes with. If your interested in learning how to code in an approachable manner and want to be taught by a professor that is enthusiastic and actually cares about his students then Craig is the guy for you. He's very generous in terms of grading and his workload is very fair.

Yes he is definitely a 5/5 meaning he know exactly what he is doing and teaches well, although don't take this rating as him being somewhat exceptional magician, he is not, and the course is pretty tough too, you will have to spend a lot of time working
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Craig really is the best. incredibly caring and just wants the best for his students. super accessible, he helps a ton in office hours. great lectures, makes sure we understand everything before continuing with the next topic. class isn't super difficult but there's also tons of extra credit opportunities

Craig is great and literally the best teacher, you could not ask for a clearer lecturer. Literally no ambiguity. The problem are the students (and myself). Because he teaches so well, people try hard... way too hard. As a result the curve is unforgiving and the averages for the exams are ridiculously high despite being fairly difficult.

Kapp is certainly a solid professor. However, his class is by far not an easy A. The HW's are long and arduous. Extra Credit takes forever to do, (my gf in CSO took 3 hours to do one of them). His exams aren't easy either for those who have no programming experience. People who say this class is easy have taken AP CompSci and here for GPA boost.
my guy a big G
show up and pass. this is going to be the easiest A I have ever got at NYU.
a great professor

Craig is very good at teaching comp sci. His in class lectures are clear and easy to understand, and he spells out exactly what he wants for the homework. Willing to slow down to accommodate people. Tons of opportunity for extra credit & the assignments are actually fun. Web Dev with Craig was my favorite of all the comp sci classes I took at NYU.
I think he's a good teacher but he's 100% overhyped. The homeworks are lengthy and the tests are hard and barely curved. I certainly wouldn't say he's God's gift to earth

One of my favorite professors at NYU, he is extremely clear and caring. He is truly passionate about Computer Science and his class isn't necessarily easy, but you have to put in the effort. As long as you do, you will perform well. He sets you up for success. Textbook isn't really necessary. Go to lecture if you want to see examples done in class.

Gotta jump on the bandwagon here. This professor is the highest rated at NYU for a reason. The class wasn't easy but his study material is top notch. Not sure about other classes but in intro to programming he had video modules (with text examples and practice problems). Makes studying really easy but you still gotta put in the work.
Perfect

Kapp is by far the best professor at NYU, both in the CS department and out of it. His classes are always waitlisted because that is how badly all students want him as a professor. I've met students who would rather postpone taking a CS class than enroll in one that was not taught by him. He is super smart and kind and NYU is lucky to have him!

Kapp is a GEM at NYU. He explains everything super clearly and is super accessible outside of class and responds quickly to emails. Get ready to work (and learn) a lot but he gives so many extra credit opportunities that everything will pay off in the end. Best professor at NYU !! He will truly change ur life!!
The best for a reason.

NYU is blessed to have this professor. Lectures are more of review sessions for the "modules" that you go-over as the homework every week. Modules might be confusing or difficult to understand depending on the topic so the lectures are helpful. If you don't find the modules difficult, you probably don't have to go to the classes. Very easy course.

NOTHING BUT RESPECT! The best prof at NYU ever! He's super passionate about what he does. Will replace previous exam score with later ones if you improve by 10 points or more. Always gives quick responses and very accessible outside class. His lecture is very inspirational, very lucky to have him for CS intro course. Highly recommended.

He is the type of professor you move your entire schedule around for. A true GEM. One of my absolute favorites and very understanding. He will replace previous exam grades with later ones, gives extra credit, and is very accessible outside class. I wish every comp sci professor was like Professor Kapp!

I initially took his class because I wanted to know what the hype was about, and I can completely understand why he gets this rating. You can tell he loves doing what he does, and his passion and positivity is simply contagious. He is extremely organized, understanding, and all-around a great lecturer. Not taking him would be a big mistake.
One of my favorite professors I have had at NYU! Gives loads of extra credit, EXTREMELY understanding, and just an all around good human.

Craig is an incredible educator who is innovative, yet humble. His class is engaging because of his enthusiasm, his ability to differentiate (and make you feel willing to take risks), and is immediately applicable. I wish I could take a class of his every year! Thank you, Craig.

Quite simply the best teacher/lecturer/educator that I have had the pleasure of taking so far. Blows my mind with his knowledge and insight. If I could have Craig for every class, my education would be complete!

Craig is one of my favorite lecturers of all time... in a subject area that I lacked confidence and enthusiasm. His calm, informative and dynamic approach to each lecture and each assignment was so valuable. He differentiated well and made the course worth our time, individually. Best ever!

When I think of Prof. Craig, I think: relevant content, encouragement to excel & feedback to improve every step of the way. I had an amazing time in this class. I felt especially supported to succeed and there is so much I can apply immediately. I would take this class again in a heartbeat because I know he would review to make it relevant. Thank u

Craig makes technology easy for even the technologically ignorant. He's very up to date with new technology and explains its value in the field of education. He's able to answer every question you may have or find the answers you need. He's easy to talk to and really wants the best for all of his students. Craig is truly phenomenal!
Amazing
nothing but respect for MY president.
inspirational
Amazing lecturer and cares for his students alot! Even passes out cookies in class!
I have taken four classes with Craig and he is just simply the BEST prof at NYU. There are so many reasons why his classes and himself are amazing. Just take him and you won't regret.

He is honestly my favorite professor I've had at NYU over my 4 semesters here. He's super approachable and really passionate about what he teaches. Gives lots of extra credit and chances at redemption. Helped me decide to be a CS major. Really nice to look at. Pretty fun assignments and he genuinely wants to help everyone. I love him :'(
Craig kapp is the GOAT
Great teacher but very hard class. Proceed with caution.
knows his material, is amazing at teaching it, understanding, approachable, caring, enthusiastic, prepared, organized.. I can go on for a while. 10/10

Very nice teacher who tries to help you every step of the way. Midterm and final review packets can be helpful. Even with the "blended learning" format, it's best to show up, if only so that you can ask questions and be up to speed.
He explains everything clearly, he gives LOTS  of extra credits, easy grader, use your higher test score to replace the lower one. Take his class by all means.

TAKE HIM! Don't even think twice. Weekly assignments and quizzes, 2 midterms, final and LOTS of extra credit! He genuinely cares for his students, lectures REALLY well, is relaxed and overall just a great guy. You will learn a lot from him and enjoy his class!

Simply the best. He showed up enthusiastic and willing to help for every single class. There was nothing that could stop him from teaching the best he could, explaining things in a very logical and accessible kind of way. He made computer science so much fun, I would take him for every single CS class if that were possible.

He's really good!! He's awesome at explaining things which is essential for a professor in this field, and this class actually got me interested in pursuing a computer science major. Wish the class size was smaller but that's not the professor's fault.

reviews.comment: Great guy

reviews.comment: Absolutely worth the hype.   His lectures are clear, engaging, and fun.  He always goes out of his way to explain everything patiently.  There are countless opportunities for extra credit.  He even brings cookies in for lab days!  If you are remotely interested in computers, take this incredible, incredible class.

genius at their craft + ability to teach it + exceptional organization & class structure + passionate about the subject + nice to look at + nice & approachable + relatable (if you like zelda and pokemon) +fair grading policy  the perfect professor. If this were a video game where I had to build the perfect professor, this man would be it.

One of the best professors that I have ever taken. The material isn't easy, but he really prepares you well for the midterm and exam. His grading policies are really great, and he also gives lots of extra credit which can really bring up your grade. Super nice and patient, and explains everything very clearly. He also makes the class really fun!
Great lecturer. Lots of opportunities to get extra credit. No textbook needed. Would highly recommend.
He is so passionate about his work, he is funny, and fantastic
I love him!!! He is soo great

Very good professor, articulate and interesting, clearly explains all the material in class. Also very lenient (to an extent) for assignments, and even tests. Interesting, kind, and patient, while also tries keep students interested through various assignments. Offers a lot of extra credit to boost your score.
Easy A, Awesome Professor, take him if you can

The best teacher I've ever had. I wasn't initially interested in Comp Sci but Professor Kapp inspired me so much that I now want to switch to major in Comp Sci. Hes always there to help. He makes you WANT to attend every class. His class wasn't easy but if you work hard he will make sure you get the grade the grade that you deserve. Take his class!
awesome guy. super helpful
this dude rocks

An AMAZING professor. I took his Intro to Programming class-- he really tries to get his students to succeed. He publishes modules online with videos that demonstrate everything you need to know. He's very helpful and clear. If you take advantage of all of the resources he provides, you'll be able to understand everything easily and do well.

I am convinced Craig Kapp is actually an angel. He's probably the most caring professor I've ever had in my college career. He's always there to help, and he wants his students to succeed in his classes. He finds ways to make the lecture entertaining, and is always well-prepared. Overall a really nice person, too. A+ 10/10 would take always.
Great teacher! Lots of extra credit, so there's always opportunities to make it up if you got a bad grade. Very friendly, and gives lots of help if you need it.

TAKE HIS CLASS! There's a reason why his ratings are so high. Go to his lectures, they're amazing! His assignments and tests lean more towards the medium/difficult spectrum, but because his lectures are so amazing, you'll do fine. He's basically always there for you if you need him. Never took programming before, but he made me wanna switch to CS!

One of my favorite professors at NYU. So friendly, approachable, and helpful. Always willing to help students, whether asking to take a test early, which class to take next, homework help, or personal questions. There is a lot of homework, but he gives you a lot of creative freedom and is very clear about what he expects. Fair/easy tests.

Professor Kapp is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. I'd never taken a CS class before and he made everything so clear and cohesive. He is always available and willing to help. HW assignments always have extra credit which helps at the end of the semester.  I will definitely be taking his classes again!

Craig was one of the best professors I have ever had at NYU. The class was NOT easy, but his devotion to helping you succeed made me WANT to work harder. The assignments were so time-consuming, but I felt obligated to go to office hours every week to get them done. I never had to cram for exams because I ended up understanding the material so well.

Craig Kapp is one of the most highly regarded professors not just within the CS department but overall at NYU. He makes it very clear from day1 that he cares deeply about his students and inspiring them to learn their absolute most every lecture through amazingly organized and clear lectures.   He is also very understanding and reasonable. 11/10

I have never wished I could take a class again until I took Interactive Computing with Craig. He is very knowledgable and goes through information several times to make sure everyone understands. Very willing to help if you need it. Most fun I have ever had in a class. Highly, highly recommend. Easy A if you do all the homework.
He will make sure you get an A
Best prof in nyu!

I really can't thank Craig enough for making me love comsci. He's so encouraging and will do everything he can to help each student. Almost every assignment has extra credit, and is so reasonable with grading. If you are lucky enough to take a class with him. DO IT. So many people want to take his class; there's a reason. Craig is honest the best
Craig is awesome!! He is the best professor I've ever met! The lectures are clear and he will help much on our programs. I like Cs and I like him! Besides, he is so handsome!
Great professor! Classes are very well organized and the professor is super helpful and approachable. Also, HE IS CRAZY HANDSOME.

By far one of the best compsci professors at NYU. Very approachable and sincerely cares about his students. I have taken two intro courses with him(java and python) and never left a lecture confused or frustrated. the best of the best!
Probably the best professor I've had at nyu. He truly has a passion for this and it shows when he teaches. His classes fill up so quickly for a reason

Craig is an outstanding professor who lives up to his reputation. Very approachable and knowledgeable. Engaging lessons, careful selection of material. Makes himself available to students even after course completed. Takes genuine interest in his students and what they get out of the course. Absolutely top-notch!
ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT NYU!!!! My favorite. So inspiring. I really admire all his work. Makes the class really engaging by showing you all you can do with CS.
Why can't there be more professors who teach like this?

Craig Kapp is an amazing professor. Just brilliant. Engaging, funny. I wish he could teach all CS courses. He is hands down the best professor I've ever had at NYU. I learned so much about programming. He prepares you well for exams and posts notes and lecture slides on the class blog. Awesome professor!

Perfect Comp Sci professor. Not incredibly easy, but you will learn obscene amounts from Kapp. He truly cares about his students as well as the course material. Very approachable and encourages everyone to go beyond his class. I wish I could switch to comp sci major =/

Just do yourself a favor and take his class. You won't regret it. Craig Kapp is one of the most helpful and genuine professors I've had at NYU. And did I mention he actually teaches you the material? And that he cares about whether you understand or not?? Just take his class already.

An amazing professor. Classes are interesting, and homeworks are extremely helpful. Attendance is mandatory (sign-in sheet). Lessons are very organized; all materials are posted on the course website. He's approachable and dependable. The best of the best!
He inspired me to change my major to compsci and he is now writing letters of recommendation for me. Phenomenal professor and person.

Very organized slides. Very organized curriculum. Consistent teaching method. Homeworks are useful and he drops the lowest one. Exams are fair. Always tries to show practical applications of the course as well. Very solid overall.

Professor Kapp is the best professor I've had at NYU. He made me want to switch my major to Comp Sci and I'm not a computer science person. His lectures are so clear, his powerpoints are amazing, he posts everything to a blog, and he grades extremely fairly. I have not a single bad thing to say about him. LOVEDDDD

Craig is a brilliant and enthusiastic professor, and overall awesome guy. You'd be remiss to not take one of his classes. He is extremely friendly, chipper, patient, and engaging. Some people are just born to teach, and he is one of those people.

Best professor at NYU. Very good at explaining concepts. Always prepared for class. Very willing to help and an overall great person. Only negative is that the homework assignments can be quite lengthy and time-consuming.
Great teacher. Makes the subject easy to understand.

He's a phenomenal teacher. He's challenging, but it's easy to maintain an A in the class. He's very approachable and shows interesting applications of the coding he demonstrates in class. Definitely take his class!

Truly excellent professor, one of the best I've ever had. I had no prior knowledge of computer programming but he explained all of the concepts so well and made the subject accessible. Exams directly correlated with the material taught in class. Does everything he can to help you learn. Highly recommended professor & class.
Don't hesitate to take one of his courses. Does everything he can so that you learn the subject, and goes out of his way so that you succeed in the class. Always nice and helpful.

It was truly a pleasure to be in Craig class. He is well organized, intelligent, kind and extremely helpful. He has a great personality, as well. You can't help but love the guy. I recommend taking this class, even if you aren't a computer science minor/major.

Great teacher and person. He takes attendance and there is a homework assignment once a week. However, Intro to Comp Programming was my favorite class this semester. Kapp is super organized, extremely smart, and really helpful. You won't regret taking his class!

Professor Kapp is the best professor I have ever had. He explains everything with the upmost clarity, is always willing to help you out if you have questions, and is extremely laid back. As long as you do the homework, the exams are simple as well. Overall, highly recommended.

The best! Very cool guy, explains very well, provides lots of examples, tests are fair, HW is fair, helps with HW,really nice and approachable, even inspired me to be a CompSci major. Gives plenty of study guides and by far this has been my favorite class and professor at NYU.

Craig Kapp is the best professor I've ever had. It was an absolute pleasure to be in his Intro to Programming Class. I've learned SO much and, suddenly, comp sci feels accessible for someone as humanities-minded as myself. He's a great professor, really helpful, super nice, laid-back, funny, an awesome guy. who made programming feel... do-able. :-)

He is the best professor I ever had at NYU! Extremely organized, exam questions are very fair, some extra credits available to boost up your grades, and very very helpful. There is no reason not to take him. Although there is a hw almost every week, it really helps you to practice what you have learned in class. I love the class.

Craig is an extremely helpful professor.  His methods of teaching far surpass the other intro to programming professors.  In this class, I learned a lot about programming in python and made many programs.  To keep it short, I don't think that there could have been a better intro to computer programming professor.

Craig is an amazing professor and is highly recommended. Super down to earth and friendly and willing to go out of his way to help any student in the class. The course itself doesn't go into any one topic in extensive detail but it is an excellent overview to a variety of computer programs and an invaluable foundation to have for the future.
