That's why only her sections are left open through the end of registration.

She will tell you that everything you do is wrong but won't say how to fix it. The course is not making me better, it's making me more confused. I've never felt so helpless with a class. She will tell you tell you one thing one day and then tell you it's wrong the next. SHE MAKES ME HATE MY LIFE!

One of the worst teachers you can have for Writing the Essay. I wish I switched out of her class a lot earlier. All her comments are negative, but she does not tell you what to fix in your essay. Does not give out good grades easily and gets very irritated if you are late. Do not miss her class more than twice.
I went to her at the writing center twice, the second time on accident. She is the single most unhelpful person at the writing center!!!!! Love the writer center though..
Kim is nice, but she does play favorites.  She has very high standards, so be prepared.

She makes WTE such a big deal, which it is not. She also expects too much, and wants things done in a very certain way. When reviewing your work, she criticizes everything, but doesn't tell you why or how to fix it.

she is THE. ABSOLUTE. WORST. if you have her, run away, back out, switch profs.  She is unhelpful, irritable, rude, close-minded, and wastes your time at one-on-ones after youve walk all the way to the writing center in guam. doesnt listen to students, contradicts herself, puts too much emphasis on WTE. grades/comments are ridiculous in every way.

I went from extremely aggravated at the beginning of the year to neutral by the end. Maybe it's because I got a good grade that I was able to tolerate writing the essay, which is going to be a pain no matter which teacher you get.

She doesn't do much to enrich your understanding of the texts you look at in class; conferences with her have a 50-50 shot of being useful.  She clearly plays favorites in her class.  The are much better WTE teachers out there; Kimmy shouldn't be at the top of your list.
Hard but you'll learn a lot in the end.
horrible, horrible experience. do not, i repeat, do not do it.

Close-minded professor.  Gave her opinion on my life choices in a personal essay.  Don't be 30 seconds late or she counts it as absent.  Unless you are her favorite, then you can come in 15 minutes late.  Talks very fast, unfriendly, unclear.  Don't do it.

I find it amazing that the "University of the Other" has hired an instructor who tells her students that they are wrong for having their own thought process.  She is simply frustruating, if you're taking Writing the Essay, find another instructor!
Thinks her subject is the Lord of all subjects and gets irritated wayyy too easily.  Could use a chill pill.  Doesn't explain things clearly either.
She constantly says one thing on one day, and another thing on another day.

Kimberly is certainly affable and can be genuinely interesting at times. The structure of the course makes it difficult to discern your progress, but I'm not sure that she was much help either. There are better WTE classes than this so look around.
She was so confusing and unhelpful.  dont take writing the essay with her!
sooooo much unnecessary homework & not that clear on feedback for essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schnairsohn is nice and will actually make you feel like you improved at writing without being unfair at all. Your grade is basically only dictated by your essays, but he gives great constructive feedback on essays, and the grading isn't harsh. The homework/lecture work aren't graded but it will actually help you write the essays a lot.

Leeore is a very chill prof, lectures are fun and engaging, its just that you have to participate a lot. As for the progression essays if you read the rubric and go to office hours he will give you helpful feedbacks. Sometimes his feedback might be confusing but you just have to talk to him a lot. If you do that you will get a pretty good grade

His lectures are interesting and enjoyable sometimes. lot of class discussions where he encourages ppl to participate. His workload is a lot and time consuming so don't take him if you're looking for a easy writing class but if you dont have a choice, get your planner ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting enough, class time was enjoyable. However, his feedback was extremely vague and low effort, he will not articulate specific issues with your writing, and grades according to his tastes. Following his suggestions does not result in a better grade. Not an awful teacher but for sure avoid if you have other classes to focus on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Leeore was a tough grader but clear about what was needed for a good grade. He was engaging and genuinely passionate about the material. His feedback on essay drafts was incredibly helpful, and he clearly cared about his students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You feel like you learn something, but you actually learn nothing in the class. Writing, knowledge, and confidence are lowered after the class.

I can't tell if he is an intellectual or a pseudo-intellectual. Good guy, but not a good teacher and grader. He thinks his answers and ideas are the only right answers in his class. He will try to make everything harder than it is and confuse everyone in the class. It's better to avoid him. He will tank your GPA and work-life balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take him. His grading is wack only because his feedback is so bad. Also, he is so incredibly disrespectful. I legit saw him literally snap at a student like he was a dog because the student was on his phone--and no, it wasn't me. Also, pretty sure he's a zionist, and he makes it very apparent that no view besides his own is worth speaking on.

Professor Schnairsohn's class is easy if you pay attention, write well, and do the homework. Class discussions are also very interesting. If you want to challenge yourself and genuinely become a better writer, take him.

He lacks a diverse point of view on world problems; he decides what is right or wrong based on his views as a Caucasian man. He cannot communicate without being passive-aggressive, i.e., "These lines are so close together it hurts my eyes," which is funny because my paper was, in fact, double-spaced. Old grumpy man, do not take, seriously, don't.

TBH he doesn't know what he's doing in the lecture, he seems guiding us to think, but sometimes the conversation will go to some directions of nonsense, and he WAS NOT TRYING TO STOP at all. Bro seems daydreaming during the class. He appears to be a listener lol, but you wouldn't want to waste your time on listening others yapping, SO DID HE.

Very abstract thinker. A lot of his lectures are pretty interesting, easy to get engaged with his lessons. He was a very interesting perspective in things. Nice professor. He does give a lot of homework, not graded but required. His feedback is very vague but I suggest you see him during office hours if you need a push in direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of essays to write, lectures are bearable but the grading was waaaaay too unclear, says you are a good track but then gives you a bad score, very high standards for writing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly he is very disjointed. His lectures are interesting, a little obsessed with Herzog, but often entirely unrelated to assignments / the unit. His grading is unclear and very vague, he tells you that you're on the right track and he still gives you a poor grade. Very heavy workload, long busywork assignments due every Mon and Wed. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool guy but a bad lecturer. He's obsessed with Herzog and his bear movie. The workload is intense, with assignments due every three days. The comments on the essay are vague and provide little guidance for improvement.

He may be pleasant in class, but his workload is ridiculous—2–5 tough essays weekly. His grading is vague, with previously not mentioned critiques on final essays. He doesn't even read your work before conferences, wasting half the time reading and rarely finishing. If you want improvement or an easy time, avoid him at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was way too obsessed with the Herzog bear man documentary. I would avoid going to class because I didn't want to watch any more of that documentary. He doesn't actually read over any of our homework and gives bad advice during one-on-ones. He never gives specific feedback. Harsh grader. He also wore open-toed shoes during the summer.
Good teacher. Lots of assignments, unclear grading. Very passionate, but thats a double edged sword.

but he a harsh grader and gave a lot of reading despite being aware of the demographics of the people taking his class, being people who don't care about non technical writing. Also, his topics were really weird, and he didn't know how technology worked despite being pretty young. Avoid this guy if you can if you like your GPA/sanity

Leeore truly cares about his students and will work with them if they communicate with him. He's passionate about writing and film and stuff, and he notices when you participate and put in effort. It's a writing class so there's a few writing assignments, and some feedback is whimsical. Ask him what he means and try. He'll notice and reciprocate

The teacher assigns a tremendous amount of homework. Do not take this professor if you can. By all means, attempt to take another professor because you will be stressing yourself out throughout the semester when trying to keep up with assignments. Imagine completing a three page essay in 2 days and another one that is due next week which is 5.5-7.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: interesting lessons, not so clear and harsh grading criteria, confusing and unclear feedback. if you want an A, you will have to work for it.

Good professor in the sense that he actually promotes critical thinking and thoughtful discussion, he's definitely left me with more interesting perspectives than most. but he's not-so-great in that his grading is unclear and inconsistent, and his feedback is equally vague/abstract. you rly need to meet with him a lot to understand what he wants

He gives entirely too much work and gives feedback that even when you follow, does not translate into good performance. His feedback is very abstract and hard to follow and so are his instructions. Especially if you are taking him for research based Expos, he makes it abstract to the point where it feels like overly demanding creative writing.
There're a lot of assignments, but most of them are not graded, and his grading is fair. For me, the feedbacks are not super useful for revising. The classes are somewhat interesting.

Sometimes there is a lot of homework, especially for essay drafts, but they are doable if you manage your time well. Essays are tough but he gives fair grades. He gives great feedback and his classes are enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Schnairsohn is good at lecturing and presenting, but quite harsh when it comes to grading. The grading structure is very heavily skewed towards essays (90%). Homework is not graded but mandatory (your essays will get a 0 if you miss a HW). I didn't learn anything new; he's not a bad option if you're just trying to get EXPOS credits.

Professor Schnairsohn makes you work for your grades, but he grades very fairly and works really hard with you to develop your writing and thinking. He was a great professor and as long as you listen and participate, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hes a great teacher and has a very interesting teaching style. However, his class isnt an easy A. He'll make you work for it and will let you know of his expectations during conference. Workload kinda heavy as well but his exercises do help build anticipation for the progression essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He can be relatively ambiguous when it comes to feedback, but going to talk to him about your essay and its flaws will almost guarantee a B+ or better on the rewrite. His focus on helping students find "intellectual problems" is very helpful for future essays you will write. Classes are also very entertaining.

Class either makes you understand something or leave you with questions. Every paper I've turned in so far came back as a C+. With the comments he made & going to the WC, a rewrite came back as a A-. He's very critical on grading making sure the essay meets his standards of having flow and logic. Avoid if you want a writing class that is calm.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely ambiguous. No clear grading criteria; you'll get comments and a lackluster grade but you won't know how to fix your writing. Asks questions but doesn't give answers. Doesn't give A's, makes you feel uncomfortable (very awkward) and doesn't help improve writing style. Doesn't help with writing structure at all and gives no direction.

Professor Leeore is a great EXPOS professor and he clearly outlines his course structure and what he wants from you in the class. His comments are super helpful when writing your essay and his lectures show that he is truly interested in what he is teaching. That being said, you need to do that work in this class to get an A, but it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Writing the Essay in 2015 and feel like Leeore scrambled up my writing style with the abstract structures he wanted us to use so badly that my writing became worse in this class and took years to finally correct. Maybe if he was better able to teach these structures, my experience would've been better, but I got nothing out of this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but really learnt a lot and in end, it was worth it.
He is friendly and his lectures are interesting and engaging. However he expects a great deal of work and grades very harshly

I really hated him when I handed in my very first paper because he said everything was wrong about it, but after multiple conferences with him, he really helped me expand my ideas and take them in the right direction. GO TO ALL HIS INDIVIDUAL CONFERENCES!!! He's super helpful one on one and will go through every detail in your essay to help you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Tries to make you write and think outside the box, so if you write in a contrived structure and you aren't interested in breaking out of it, avoid. If you want to expand your thinking, take him. Some say he's a tough grader, but I got an A+ on my first essay, so if listen to his comments and put in some effort, you def have a chance of doing well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Seems like an open minded teacher but there was so much writing in my opinion. Everything I wrote, he'd tell me I was wrong. In this class, opinions can be wrong. On my 8 pg essays he would stop at pg 3 (thesis location) and tell me I'm wrong. Each time I rewrote it and he told me it was wrong again and left me with little to no guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had in my life. He taught me how to write with an unlimited mind

I had him a while back, but I have to say that he's helped me grow insanely as a writer and his class was one of the best experiences for developing analytical skills. The class isn't hard if writing is your forte, it's more the way he pushes you to think. 10/10 would recommend, a truly truly valuable experience

Professor Schnairsohn has a unique method of teaching and I really enjoyed his class. He really awards creative writings because he wants you to be adventurous with your writing. During conference, tell him what you are trying to do and he is willing to help. I learned a lot from his class and would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. He's really nitpicky with grading and basically will give you bad grades just for disagreeing with you. I went to 3 different Writing Center tutors who all said my last paper for the class was amazing and that I did not need to change anything. I handed that same paper in and he gave me a C.
My writing definitely improved, but it wasn't easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Leeore is a hard grader, but he truly wants to help you develop your writing style. By the end of the course, you will feel that you received tons of helpful feedback to refine your voice as a writer. If you show your interest and dedication to his class, he will be willing to help you 100%. He's intimidating at first, but softens up.

Worst class I have ever taken; Avoid him for Writing the Essay at all cost, ESPECIALLY IF YOU'RE PREMED! To be fair, he's a cool guy and he shows interesting videos in class. But he never tells you what he wants on papers and won't accept any views that aren't his own. He also doesn't take essay rewrites, unlike EVERY OTHER WTE CLASS AT NYU -_-
Best course I've taken so far.

His class is definitely difficult, like any Writing the Essay class. But I would definitely recommend taking another professor if you can avoid him. He never tells you what he wants on papers, so you have to read his mind. He VERY RARELY gives A's and doesn't take essay rewrites. He shows cool videos, but they haven't helped my writing at all

I found past reviews of Schnairsohn to be incredibly accurate. It's an incredibly difficult class but your grade will accurately reflect the amount of time and effort you pour into these papers - definitely helped me refine my writing skills for college. If you're looking to learn - even if you may have to sacrifice your grade - take his class.

Unless you are a future Nobel-prize winning author, Writing the Essay will be a challenging regardless of which professor you get. That being said, I'm glad I got into Leeore's class. His anecdotes and lectures will eventually make sense you start the drafts, and we watch interesting films. Make sure you attend his office hours if you need help.

This class was extremely challenging and the professor always seemed to want us to read his mind for how the texts should be interpreted. I honestly have never worked this hard in a class and gotten such a low grade. I have to give it to him that occasionally we watched cool videos, but class was mostly confusing discussions that got us nowhere.

If you look for traditional class bounded by a rigid structure, don't take his class. Leeore uses very unusual, yet interesting analogies to help you understand the course materials. With Leeore, it is always about having your own voice and thoughts. He will not tell you what a text means because he's only interested in how YOU interpret a text.

I took WTE linked with Renzi's Text and Ideas, and I didn't think this class would be so difficult. It's a lot of work that requires papers full of substance and not your high school bs. It was nearly impossible to fully please him or understand what he wanted from your papers. However, I learned a lot and don't regret it. It was very rewarding!

Awesome class-- I was truly disappointed for the semester to end. Great teacher, a little hard to understand what he wants at first, and it's next to impossible to get an A in his essays, but he always starts great discussions and brought great insight, making this class I was dreading turn into one I'm sad to end.

He has very interesting writing exercises that not only help you develop your writing skills but also thinking skills. Weird analogies are funny. Interactive. Fruitful class discussions. Great use of multimedia. Gave us chocolates on the last day of class. Easy to share your ideas with and work with. Meaningful Class!

He is a very nice man, but would not repeat. independent reading is a must, content not fully covered/confusingly articulated in lecture. Heavy reliance on AI. recitation had helpful slides I learned more there than lecture. going to class or recitation not as helpful though as independent study from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take any other class for your psych requirements -- prof is dry, unengaging, and often confused about what is going on. Grade is entirely based on 4 exams which sounds easy in theory, but some of the content wasn't even taught in lecture. Class deflated my GPA and stressed me out -- avoid avoid avoid!

4 tests make up ur entire grade, but he cancelled exam 3 despite the class avg being a 67%. Slides are mostly pictures, so even if u go to class, if u don't read the book you'll prob fail. BUT even if u do read the book, you'll prob fail anyway bc its unclear whats gonna be on the test. TA's were awful too, super rude + only read off their slides
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Oh don't get me started on this man. I tried liking him, but no. He is so unclear, no communication, never responds to email and over all so unhelpful. The grading is so unfair. Like it deflates ur grade unless ur in the top 20%. I'm also disappointed in how things turned out because I genuinely did like the subject, but Proff's actions ruined it.

Quite disappointed with this prof: 4 exams make up your grade which is fine, except for when there's content from unrelated or, as seen on exam 4, UN-TAUGHT materials (the content wasn't taught in class (and I did not miss a single class), nor was it taught in the textbook). Unclear curve which changed last sec; dull lectures; disappointing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Intelligent and kind professor with interesting lectures. If you need help don't email just go to his office. Class is graded on only 4 exams. Practice exams are helpful, but the tests felt so random/unrelated. The curve sucks. You can put in your all just for cheaters to get the same grade. Overall, great professor but really bad class structure.

Overall it's an okay class. The exams r always so random, sometimes abt class content, sometimes abt textbook, or sometimes graphs. They are so confusing and unrelated that I feel like he isn't making those exams himself, but the recitation leaders r. After reading hundred pages I feel disappointed at the confusing Qs and students cheating behind.

He is the sweetest professor ever!! So kind and approachable. Go to his office hours and he will tell you random things that open your eyes about how we perceive the world. He is truly passionate about what he studies. Definitely talk to him personally instead of just listening in the big lecture.

Dr. Maloney is wonderful. He talks slowly but clearly. Two exams make up all the grade, but there are sample tests so not hard at all! Might be hard to reach by email, but if you go to his office he will always be there and welcome you in with a smile. Also definitly a caring professor and a helpful guidance on career path! Just talk to him.

Prof. Maloney's tests are not hard, but his lectures are boring and he is impossible to reach. He is kind and accommodating, IF YOU CAN GET HIM TO RESPOND TO YOUR EMAILS. He also is not at all tech savvy, so don't expect him to post what he says he will.

He isa nice person, but not a great professor. So disorganised and its hard to understand what he is saying. The exams are weird because there is so so much material, but only 30 questions asked. The class grade is based on only 2 exams, which is ridiculous, no extra credit available. If you want to read a lot of everything, then this is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall good class! The lectures can be boring, but Prof. Maloney takes care to present the information in a way that's not super hard to understand. Go to class, take notes, read the textbook (but don't panic if you fall a little behind). The grade is based on two tests, so make sure you study, but they're not hard. Skip recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Preposterously smart guy. Maybe one of the most brilliant individuals I've ever met. The lecture is a little dry but if you show up and take notes you will get an A. Seriously, talk to him outside of lecture. He's fascinating.

You'll have long textbook readings. Along with that, he made our final exam worth 70% of our grade based on the material we learned over the course of 2 months, which is a lot of material for an 18 question final since you won't know what to study. He didn't lighten the course load even though these are stressful times due to the coronavirus.

Prof. Maloney is easily one of the most brilliant/interesting people you'll meet at NYU if you get to know him outside of lecture. Guy is a straight up genius but the class is very dry. Show up to lecture, take notes, hit the practice tests hard, and you'll get an A. If you've taken premed courses, it's a layup. Don't bother with recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: paying attention in class is pretty hard cause he goes very slowly and the material is not that interesting. it is a lot more about the anatomy than I anticipated. study hard for the tests!

He's so boring. SO boring. But a nice guy and very accomplished. Don't get carried away and never go to class and then end up with a B because you didn't read the book. Its SO easy to because theres almost nothing required of you. Grade is the average of two exam scores. He's. So. Boring. But an awesome guy, really.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Brilliant man who won the closest thing to a nobel prize in Psychology. Come to class, give a damn, and it'll be the easiest A in your college career. Granted lectures can be boring as all the material is quite abstract but exams are a joke and all the material pertains to everyday life which goes along way in comparison to other courses.

Prof. Maloney is super sweet and funny. The class, however, is extremely boring. It's very easy to get lost and demotivated because the subject isn't the most interesting and attendance is not required. 2 exams each 50% of grade. Gives a practice exam and copies some questions on actual exam. I still wouldn't take again Bc it's so boring.

As a psych major, I took perception with Maloney, and he is a great professor. He is very knowledgeable, and is always there if you have any questions. The topics are very complex and since it is easy to get lost in his lectures, pay a lot of attention. TEST ARE NOT EASY. PLEASE SIT IN THE FRONT ROW SINCE IT IS HARD TO HEAR HIM IN CLASS. Funny.

Awesome professor. It's easy for many people to zone out during his lectures, but if you care to tune in, you'll recognize his brilliance and appreciate his extensive knowledge about his field. He's also super endearing and funny (: Loved his class. Easy A, no papers. Just make sure to read the textbook.
Wonderful teacher

Love this guy!! Extremely educated and intelligent, super nice, and very funny. Class has some pretty complicated concepts but he doesn't expect you to be an expert. Honestly cannot say enough good things about him.
awesome professor, one of my favorite at nyu.
He's the man.  He knows his field very well, he knows how to teach and he has a sense of humor, too.
Literally the GOAT. Must take his class
don't be scared of his syllabus - it looks tough, but he made all the exams take-home. Above all, genuinely learned a lot in this class and thoroughly enjoyed all the class discussions!

The GOAT. He tries to scare you during the first class (+ has a no devices requirement), but he's an incredibly chill prof. His readings were actually pretty interesting too. He made both the midterms take home, and is overall such a kind person

Super easy class to get your C&C requirement out of the way. Some readings can be a bit long, but he'll never cold call on you. Participation matters for your overall grade, so you'll almost guaranteed get an A if you raise your hand a couple times per lecture. The essays & tests are graded easily, as well as the 1 group project.

If you are reading this after your first class and want to drop it, don't, it's nothing like he makes it sound. Class is lecture-heavy, but you are never really tested on the stuff (and if he does, he gives you the questions beforehand). Very chill and easy class
Easy assessments, requires participation. Very cheerful and caring however lectures tend to feel repetitive. His classes are probably better in person.

He is so inspirational that his speech from the last class almost made me cry. He gives inspirational lectures every class. Even though he seemed serious in the first class, later you'll he is genuinely the sweetest person ever. If you read and do all the work, you would not be worrying about your grades.
Professor Ramos types every important contexts in the chat box for his students not to miss any important class material. He smiles at every class participants.

Comes off kind of strict but is actually really chill and understanding. Class is discussion based so participate once in a while. You'll probably have a few response papers but nothing to worry about, light work. Midterm is all about what was said in class so show up and listen. Lots of reading but you can slip by. no final exam, just a paper
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So nice, happy + excited to teach. Loved his ability to analyze texts, art, + movies to help students better understand the material. papers are very straight forward w option of three diff prompts to choose frm. might get behind on syllabus because he's so busy and slightly unorganized but really great professor!

Ramos is a great guy and professor. He really cares about his students and the topics we dicuss in class. Classes are very lecture heavy/discussion based but if you pay attention you will get an A on almost everything. Take this class if youre looking for an easy cultures and contexts class!

One of my favorite professors at NYU! Smart, witty, accessible, and kind. He gives great feedback. Listens well. Cares about his students. Wants us to learn how to write well, how to express our ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love Ramos! The class are dense with information but the exams are soooooo easy! He tends to hand out exam suggested questions and he's such an easy grader! Super nice. Always smiley when you see him! You get to learn a lot but at the same time, you don't have to worry about grades! Amazing professor!

Ramos is an awkward guy, but he is genuinely very sweet. His class is not intense and tests are very simple. He seems intimidating on the first day, but he really is not. I have gotten an A on everything so far. His readings are interesting and also makes us watch movies which are great too. It's a rather simple class! TAKE HIM

Professor Ramos is amazing! Took him for both CFI and II. He seems really tough and intimidating at first, but after a couple lessons you'll soon see that he's so caring and such a lovely person. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches and enjoys stimulating class discussions, so be sure to participate and get involved! Love Ramos!

Great professor. I took him for CF I and II. He is a bit awkward and unsure of himself, but he is truly a great guy. You don't need to do the readings; just show up to class and try to participate. Easy grader- I don't know anyone who didn't get an A. Says he will do pop quizzes, but does it once and it never happens again. Interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Funniest/most enjoyable class by far

Professor Ramos seems like a tough person at first, but when he opens up, he is simply the best. Must confess I considered switching professors on the first week, but I stuck with him and have no regrets. At the end of my 2nd semester with him, I must say he genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about his job. Just put in some effort

Ramos, while slightly socially awkward, is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet. His classes are heavily discussion based and he likes people who speak up. His class is super easy if you do the readings, and even if you don't, an A is possible if you listen in class. He has a specific preference for paper format though, so go to office hours

At first, he seems very intimidating. Then, he backs down. If you participate, you will most likely get at least a B+. Two long midterms, and a group project. Must do readings because there are weekly quizzes.

I absolutely adore this man, as both a professor and as a person. He is extremely intelligent and his class discussions are interesting and thought-provoking, provided you pay attention and participate, which is easy because he values everyone's input. He's also a very sweet person and he's willing to help his students out as much as they need.

Other comments talk about social awkwardness, but it's easy to overcome if you're willing to meet him halfway. Much of the class is discussion based, and students tend to get annoyed because he doesn't spoon feed information. If you want to get something out of the class- you will. He chooses fantastic readings and has a very unique insight.

You will do well if you show up, participate in lectures, and go to office hours to ask about papers. He's also a nice guy and genuinely wants his students to enjoy the class. He plans fun trips for the class if you take him in Florence.
He has a very strict style that he wants in essays, but it's not hard to meet those expectations.  Always willing to meet with students outside of class and genuinely a nice person.

He's knowledgable, but fails to communicate this knowledge to the class owing to his poor social skills. He also does not know how to grade a paper. Gives you a good grade for a bad paper and visa versa. Sweet guy, but avoid.

The professor is completely incapable of expressing himself.  Good readings, but spendslectures trying to guide students to his pre-prepared points, at the cost of being unable to acknowledge other ideas.  He accepts writing at only a kindergarten level, and will penalize students for more complex writing styles. He even explains what a thesis is.
Most disorganized prof ever. Grades hard and arbitrarily. Avoid at all costs.

Definitely one of the most stressful classes ever taken. Homework was hard but not worth a whole lot grade wise. He will lie to you about only giving you a small curve but the curve is massive trust me. I got away with doing minimal pre-lecture work and pay close attention to class and hw. Love the prof tho gives good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are not helpful if you don't already have some basic understanding of topics. Very easy to fall behind in this class. Problem sets can sometimes take many hours. On exams he picks very specific, quite difficult questions that he went over in class briefly. If you didn't pay attention to that one topic then you fail. Lectures are recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great professor for a tough course. It's a lot of work, but he ensures to keep lecture information valuable, and it is all relevant to what you will be tested on. Hard, but fair.
He gave a bad curve for final grades and he doesn't teach well. He just shows a problem and the answer, barely reviewing the steps that lead you to the answer.

DON'T take him as your Discrete prof. Nice person, but man, he goes way too fast in lectures. Very hard to keep up with; not the most helpful when trying to understand which specific areas I should practice for the exams. If you're a math nerd, you'll love him. If you're taking him just for credit, good luck... don't take him, ruined my semester!
I am not able to get 4.0 even in the first year of college....I am cooked. X_X
Bad Midterms, His slides are not great and doesn't teach that well overall, I personally just self studied the whole thing

He often uses videos from Selin Kalaycioglu. Just take her if possible. Prof Leingang is for the ones who love math. 

Only nice things were that he is very supportive of trans folk and I had kind TAs who gave a lot of credit on FRQs.

His reviews sum it up: most will struggle, only few will soar. LOTS of hw. Can't stress this enough. LOTS of hw, but they help you learn. Not very helpful in explaining concepts. Not like other math profs (beware). Records/posts all lectures. Can join on Zoom. Attendance not necessary. Difficult exams compared to other profs. Friendly enough dude.

Poor at explaining topics and his slides can be hard to follow. I learned a lot more about this course by myself rather than his slides that he speeds through. There is a good amount of homework but it's spread out somewhat to where you can manage it. I would say the course isn't even that bad, but personally I had to teach it all to myself.

if you are bad at math AVOID 100% !!! super hard. while he is a nice guy himself, lectures make no sense and he DOES NOT CURB even tho the average is always 60%. only good thing is he has a bunch of assignments so like if u pass fail it u can get away with DOOK scores on midterms and final. never take this class if u r not good at math tho horrible

You get pre-quiz, post-quiz, in-class poll for EVERY single lecture! Also, he has homework sheet every week (also counts for grade). Totally 2 midterms and 1 final, which is graded HARSH, the mean is about 60% and this man only curved slightly. The content is way over scope (lots of niche theorem), I would never take him again.
good professor, pretty kind and caring about his students. tests are surprisingly difficult, averages are very low. doesnt seem like we're quite prepared for what's on the exams in class.

He's an amazing person and lecturer. Everything is so organized in lecture. A lot of work tho, you have quizzes before and after lectures. However, they are super helpful. Lecture is proof heavy, and a lot of definitional questions on exams, and some of them are tricky. Amazing professor! Take him if you love math!
he's a good person, but needs to slow down in lectures
The exams average are all about 60, and he gives almost no curve. Run!
F this mf he ruin my whole semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For the people who say Calc 3 is easier than Calc 2, it is not. I personally would not recommend the YT videos he has in brightspace. Instead, learn a bit about the general topic on your own, then look at the textbook. Sometimes, trying the WA can also help. Put a genuine question into the pre lecture survey. Finish assignments a day before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's great at teaching and very nice. He actually answers questions on the discussion boards & he gives pre-class surveys where you can ask more questions. That said, tons of work, quizzes every class, & you have to read the txtbk to do the surveys. Lectures sometimes have extra info not in txtbk that you need to know. Curved a lot in the end tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class hit me like a truck, but professor Leingang was great. He's very passionate about math and energetic in class. There is a lot of homework to help with practice as well as weekly quizzes that I tried my best to prepare for and didn't do very well. He does have a lot of office hours which can be helpful if you have a specific question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very passionate lecturer, but forgets that students are not going to pick up a concept as quickly as he thinks. Pure attendance not graded, if you want participation points you have to actively participate in class and go to office hours. A lot of work outside of class, exams are exactly like practice/homework. Very responsive outside of class

reviews.comment: Has a MASSIVE ego. Very unapproachable and does not offer help on HW. Weekly quizzes that and other bs in the class that feels like "busy-work" rather than actual learning. 5% participation grade is graded subjectively...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Leingang is the best professor at Discrete Math I've seen! You can attend the morning class via Zoom and he'll still count your attendance. The lecture typically starts with a funny poll, and the contents are interesting and easy to follow. The course is well organized. Take him for Discrete!
The course is not extremely difficult, but he assigns a lot of pointless tasks that makes it very painful.

Tends to lecture beyond what is necessary to understand Calc 3 which can be confusing but exams are reasonable. Spends time getting to know each student and will notice the effort you put into the class.  Slideshows and brightspace page can be overwhelming but are useful if you don't take notes. Posts everything after or a bit before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is fine person, he's lectures are fine and interesting. I think most of the time he covered much more than the text book, but sometimes there are also ocassions that he didn't cover the textbook. That's a little bit tricky. Also he suppose you to spend a lot of time on this course. I think he is a teacher between ok and good.

This guy is a dry but fine lecturer, but has an enormous ego about his teaching and his courses. He expects people to commit an insane amount of time to the course. Assigns so much work—all small, but annoying and not helpful—due daily, even on Sat. Can't ever seem to get a break from this class even though in reality it's easy stuff. Strict tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I don't know why this guy is getting paid.

Do better Mat.

Decent instructor, lectures were pretty clear and easy to follow. Only issue is if you don't understand on the first explanation, he wont break it down but just expect you to understand it. Quizzes before each class are kind of annoying but its not too bad. Weekly quizzes every other class as well.

his lectures are just whats on the textbook. he assigns a quiz before each class GOING THROUGH THE MATERIAL FOR THAT CLASS, and the entire course is literally just read the textbook chapter -> do the quiz -> go into class and learn what you just read. at the very least he simulcasts lectures on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
One of the worst subjects to learn in my life!
And the worst teacher I have had so far.
Spending more time figuring out how to get rid of him instead of how to study for this course.
The class is literally a bomb.
I really wanted to like this professor. But I end up feeling stupid in his class instead.

Meticulously organized. Always posts some enrichment material after lecture on Brightspace. Goes above and beyond the textbook at times, although lectures mostly regurgitate said book. Unfortunately has a tendency to neglect struggling students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: he is good person, but his slides are useless
Definitely take his class

Slides are useless and his way of explaining Calc 3 makes this subject 10 times harder. Lots of workload and homework is hard and useless. Relied on youtube to understand this subject otherwise I would definitely fail this class. Exams are extremely hard so be prepard. Generous curve though.

He explains everything very well and clearly, and he is very responsive and caring. But he is a tough grader. 4 quizzes per week, strict grading criteria of polished proof, and seldom give full participation grade.

2 post quizzes and 1 written hw per week is a lot but it actually helped me a lot to understand the material way better. The lecture would not make sense if you dont put time into the textbook readings and exercises. The class itself is fun but is indeed challenging since it is so different than calc or any other math classes ive taken before.

No doubt that calc 3 itself is really hard.. Prof. Leingang actually tried to make the dull material more fun and more engaging in class. Weekly written homework + weekly in-class quizzes + 2 midterms and 1 final. Not hard if you are interested in math. DO go to his office hours; he replies email very fast (within a day normally)

Tough grader, Too many slides, Online quiz before and after each class, Very fast homework deadlines (quiz due second day after each class), Very heavy exams: multiple choice, check all that apply, true/false with justifications, and free response and they are very challenging. Be prepared to put in intense amount of work if you take him.

organized class but a lot of work. lectures are boring and grades really strictly. he doesn't really answer questions and just gives u a shrug when u ask. definitely more organized than some of the other discrete profs so wouldn't be a bad option for a required class but be prepared to put in a lot of work. accessible outisde of class
His lectures are inspirational, diving deep, and also very hard. His course involves a lot of professional mathematical knowledge and lets you have a profound understanding of every aspect.

I found his course more frustrating than educational, and I think there's much room for improvement in teaching methods to make the material more accessible and the assessments fairer. The assessment methods were tough, with frequent quizzes and a strict grading curve which shows off his math talents instead of helping students learn effectively.

This semester has been extremely tough due to the way the course was taught. While he is knowledgeable in math, the teaching style didn't work for me. The lectures were complex and felt like polished long essays, which made it hard to understand new concepts. It often felt easier to learn from the textbook than to follow the lectures.

His lectures are organized and he keeps all the materials organized but the lecture is copied straight from the textbook without elaborating. He also does not answer questions and rarely provides useful feedback. If you love math take him, otherwise avoid.

he seems like a nice person but he just cant teach. He reads off the slides and repeats everything out of the textbook. The polished proofs are graded very heavy and the midterms are very hard. The homework is very time-consuming because we have to code them on latex and he assigns 4 quizzes per week. I'd avoid him tbh.

Very accessible if you have any questions but is not super lenient. Grades the polished proofs are very hard but the weekly homework papers and the post quizzes are decently easy. Midterms are a bit tricky and the questions are hard the understand in the writing section and the MC section is a bit hard. Other than that, not bad.
He is a nice person, but a tough grader. His grading criteria is stricter than that of any other sections. If you want to challenge yourself, then take his class. Otherwise, avoid.

Second semester having him, this time for Discrete Math. Very heavy exams - multiple choice, multi select, true/false with justifications, and free response questions. Very tired of them. There are online quizzes before and after each class. If you take him, be sure to get ready to work for this or Calculus III.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader
I get all A except for this class. If you want to get a good grade, avoid this professor at all costs. Four quizzes per week, an extremely tough grader, and a lot of homework.

Not the worst, not the best. There was a lot to take in for Calculus III. The course itself was also difficult. Midterms were heavy as it had all sorts of questions. Also makes us do pre-quizzes; they were annoying but only requires us to ask a question to earn full credit. Overall mid professor, but a nice person.

He was cool. Super funny if you like dry humor. The content of the class we quite heavy but he explains everything fairly well. Not a bad choice for a Discrete Math Prof. One con was the pre-quizzes due before class, but luckily they force you to learn and they're graded by completeness. Had a lot of office hours and was very responsive by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the worst professor out there. He's pretty fair about grading. Class is pretty dry as it's just a regurgitation of the textbook, so you can get by the whole class yourself with the assigned readings. He is very organized so there won't be a problem with that, but if you aren't on top of your schedule, it'll be a hard time for you.
The hardest I have ever worked for a C. Never have I done so much homework for one class. Upwards of 5 hours every day. Avoid if you are able.

He truly cares for his students, and provides fair exams. He explains concepts clearly and in a manner that's easy to understand. He gifts you with a strong foundation in Calc and in Maths in general. He will challenge you, and patiently explain to you until you understand. He, inspired me to pursue Maths. Don't hesitate to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Harsh grader but caring and wants you to succeed. If you attend his office hours regularly you will be fine.

Truly wants to get to know you as a student. Helpful during office hours throughout the week. Lots of time is required/effort to do well in the class if you aren't naturally good in math, but he sees your efforts. Super rewarding because you'll learn a lot. Exams are created super fair if you keep up with material from slides/past exams he posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Super caring and friendly. The friendliest professor you will find at NYU.
Only tests on whats taught. Very accessible and passionate guy. I love him
You will do well on his class if you figure out the content in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Extremely condescending and doesn't listen to student feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and nice person, but he is a really tough and strict grader. The rubric is not clear at all, I got points taken off for not assigning pages when turning in works on gradescope, not simplifying fractions, or didn't put fractions into decimals. Also assigns heavy readings that make going to lectures pointless. 4 quiz per week.

A lot clearer in lectures than previous math instructors. He has a good vibe and tries to get to know his students. I took a medical leave and he was very understanding and flexible with me as I got back on track. Course material is challenging but he explains it in a way that makes it as easy as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments, lots of reading, some jokes. Passionate about math and educating. Repeats the entire textbook reading in lecture plus worksheet problems here and there. Personally, one of the classes that drained me the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's super nice & chill and I had him over zoom. Just look at his slide and understand the material, most test material is from slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang gives different kinds of assignments to help improve all kinds of learning skills. Discrete math is definitely difficult, but these assignments help a lot. They improved my ability to write proofs and learn from textbook to a huge extent. Attendence is not mandatory, but you will do much better if you really come to class.

Bad studying habits aside, this class is definitely manageable. MATHUA120 can be dry since it's mostly getting familiar with mathematical language, but prof Leingang made it interesting where possible. He's really tolerant and understanding, so I can imagine enjoying his class a lot more for another math class (like calc). I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang is best suited for individuals who are truly interested in math. That being said if you are looking for an easy math class where you rinse and repeat formulas, this is not the class for you. I think many of the bad reviews are biased by the difficulty of discrete math, not Professor. No one is just immediately great at proofs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Could you imagine a 10%-weighted group project damaged my overall letter score from A to B+? My points lose here are the same as those lost at the other 90%... Overall, he's not an unacceptable guy, but be careful that you'll face a bunch of tiny homework that only counts 3% and DIFFICULT midterm 3. Kind of a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang was a nice lecturer. Those who participated all thoroughly understood concepts. He has a lot of small assignments (more so to check understanding) and is really good about helping students and applying concepts. Honestly, I have no clue why some of these other ratings are so harsh to him.

Pretty good professor. Good at helping to understand the material, is accessible, and kind. The workload can be sometimes heavy but is def manageable if you manage your time correctly. Test are hard but fair. Weekly quizzes are not as hard. There are also some easy A assignments he gives that allow you to boost your grade too.

Prof. Leingang reminds me of a grade school teacher. He marked attendance, graded participation, had student do Do Now questions at the beginning of lecture, and remembered every student's names. He manages to make the complex concepts of Honors Calc III digestible. However, midterms and weekly quizzes were rather difficult.

He's an okay teacher. He's bad at explaining things so I used Youtube and the textbook to learn. Lectures were just a repeat of the book. Even when I asked for help I usually left more confused :( . But you can tell he cared because he always gave help. HWs are due every fri and quizzes every mon (so time-consuming). Exams were pretty hard.

Class reminded me of my hs classes tbh. Encourages group participation and has mandatory attendance. As for the guy himself, he has a pretty dry personality and seems to try to apply what he learned in psych 102 to his interactions with his students. Also felt the need to mention that he drove an electric car.

This professor gives very clear explanations to even the most complicated concepts. His classes are very organized, strictly following the syllabus. Grading is a bit strict but definitely fair. Homework are carefully selected, very entertaining to work with. Definitely don't regret taking his course.

Like his class in general. He is a kind and easy-going teacher. You may also learn a lot about math if you take his class frequently. Homework is not too much. The only frustrating thing is that Latex is a mandatory requirement, which costs lots of time.

Leingang is a great teacher, and if you're some one who likes math, you'll find the class quite fun. (Discrete Math). Weekly quizzes are straight from the assigned textbook problems,HWs will usually be from the book but must be coded on latex (time consuming). Exams are easy! I've heard that he' s really tough on his hon calc 3 class though.

I had Prof. Leingang for Discrete Mathematics and he was not the best at teaching. He went incredibly fast and expected you to know the complex material after a 30-minute talk about it. His lectures are entirely based on the textbook so going to class is the same as just reading the book, negating the entire purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took honor calc3 instead of the regular calc3, which is by far one of my most irrational decisions. Leingang is a tough grader, even if you attend every lecture you still couldn't get full credit of participation. He has great passion in math especially geometry, which means he expects you to be as passionate as him to attain his standards.

Very respected and teaches great. You can tell he is passionate about math and teaching and really knows his stuff. But avoid him unless you are okay with getting a B-level grade after spending 20hr weekly on this course.

Honors Calc III is a lot more about the conceptual than the practical, so be prepared to study calculating examples on your own in the book. However, Leingang does a good job of getting weird concepts to be understandable. Hard-ish weekly quizzes and homeworks, so study up and learn LaTeX. Make sure to participate and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Leingang is a seriously underrated prof. Sure, he gives a decent amount of work and he makes you use LaTeX, but if you go to class, do his homework and pass his quizzes, you'll be in good shape. For a lot of profs this is NOT true. Not to mention he really cares. He'll go out of his way to help you and puts so much effort into teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Leingang teaches well but taking his course isn't the best idea because he gives a lot of homework which requires writing tedious LaTeX code. There are weekly quizzes. The lectures, quizzes and homework are entirely based on the book. But he experiments with his exams and gives challenging questions. He does curve his exams which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really tricky, I only suggest to those who are able to give up on everything else in their semester. HW qs are very interesting, but you budget most of your week to be working on them, quizzes are every other class. Exams are definitely tricky, but he curves them up quite a bit. If you want a real challenge, take this class, otherwise don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is smart definitely. However what he taught in class is exactly the same in the textbook. Gives lots of homework and requires us to use Latex. Although I love coding, the homework process is tedious and time-wasting as you actually can complete it way faster if written homework allowed. Midterm is standard, but every weeks' quiz is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Easy class if you've already taken at least Calculus AB. Hard class if you haven't. Lectures are half-baked and studying the webassign questions is your best chance at doing well on quizzes and exams.

He was such a fun teacher. He had a lot of fun with the subject he taught. Even though he would let out the occasional corny joke, I still laughed. He's the epitome of a dad. He was very helpful with feedback and made sure you really understood it. He was very accommodating with office hours. Had him for Calc I and II. Would recommend
Lectures were always very well planned and structures - his notes were abundantly clear and were always followed by practice worksheets and in class exercises. Homework was challenging but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I admit that he is a very smart guy, buy he regards himself a genius. Sometimes His hand writing can be illegible, and  he talks  too fast. Homework and midterms are tough. Don't recommend to take his class if you are not interest in calculus.
Very clear in his explanations but gives ridiculously tough test questions.

Great professor, but he gives extremely challenging exams and homework. Somewhat of a tough grader. He speaks really fast and assumes previous knowledge in Calculus, so if you don't have a strong interest or foundation in Calc, you will probably have a hard time.

Leingang is definitely one of the smartest and most friendly professors I have had so far. Lectures are crystal-clear, and office hours are helpful. However, his major downfall is assigning ultra-difficult problems on both the written assignments and midterms. I would only recommend him if you're really into math or wanna tackle difficult problems.

He went to univ of Chicago and Haravard so he knows he math and knows how to make diffcult problems. Test and quiz averages are often below 70%. Weekend webassign proofs are difficult and take hours. Calc 2 is not a required course for premeds. I recommend taking a more useful math class or an easier calc professor so you can balance your classes.

Quizzes every week, but he drops the lowest 2. The homework is ridiculously hard, but he grades pretty leniently and drops the lowest grade. Grading isn't too bad. Just pay attention and take good notes.
In class: this is how you integrate. Exam: find the total perimeter of an infinite ever-growing fractal in series form. What even.

The class structure is awesome. You learn the lesson through clear examples and then do a worksheet about what you learned/harder examples. Quizzes and exams are really straightforward. The only draw back is he does written homework through web assign so you have to scan in your work to your computer.

Flexible, committed, and knowledgeable. Requires participation - which is kind of difficult for a calc 3 lecture. If you are there to learn and work hard you'll do fine, he is very understanding and helpful.

By far the best professor I have had in all of my years at NYU. He is extremely intelligent, approachable, and caring. He wants all of his students to succeed and understand the material. He does an excellent job of explaining the concepts and getting the class involved through worksheets. You will leave this class being amazed with him knowledge.

I do not know how he got his PHD from Harvard. He is not good math at all!! He can only cover what text book says, but cannot explain anything complicated. Even though he is nice and approachable, he is not a genius in math. No wonder he does not do any research now, simply teaching calculus....

His teaching techniques makes sure you learned the material before you leave class. After he teaches a section, he hands out worksheet to do then he calls on someone to do it on the board and goes over the answer. He is excellent, funny, and answers all questions.
take him if you really like math and really GOOD at math!

Professor Leingang is one of the best calc professors ever.  He's clear in his lectures and uses worksheets to get students involved.  He's dorky and quirky in an adorable way.  His tests/quizzes aren't unfair or extremely difficult.  I learned a lot from him.  Highly recommend!  Do whatever you can to get in his class. :)
Best. Professor. Ever.  --> Take him for the upper level Calculus Classes and you will not regret it.  You get the grade you deserve and he does everything he can to help you learn.

He's a smart guy, but his downfall is that he teaches straight from the powerpoint, so if you don't kno how he got from step 1 to step 2, you'll be pretty much lost as to how he got to that answer. My class did horribly on the final, therefore the curve was pretty generous, although he doesnt curve all the time..Prior AP Calc is a must to get an A

Intelligent and clear in lecture. Class, however, is HARD. Especially calc2. Very concept heavy. Seems more geared towards math majors than anyone else. Webassign (online hw) was torture. So was written hw. Had to do proofs for hw in calc2! I say avoid, there are prob easier profs out there

Leingang is an interesting character. He is nice he does the "this is my favorite calc class joke" in every calculus class. He does the tree strech when ppl are falling asleep in his class. He is a very nice profesor . But calculus itself has concepts that are hard to grasp or easely undertand so you will need to do use the txtbook alot
Take him if you're really good at calc. And I mean REALLY.

I recommend him if you have taken AP Calc in highschool. Otherwise, he is really conceptual and you'll have to teach yourself most of the stuff. He uses webassign for homework (in addition to written hw) and that's basically death. If you know calc, you don't have to go to class. Not the best, but at least you can understand him.
nice and funny guy. expalins things well

If I had never taken AP Calc in high school I probably would have done terribly in the class. The professor is a nice guy but he moves through topics quickly and spends too much time on proofs which confuses everyone. If you've taken calc before, this class will be a breeze. In my opinion, all quizzes and the midterm/final were easy.

He's brilliant and funny. Reminds me of Ted Mosby from How I Met Your Mother. He is the head of Calc Prog, so he writes the finals. But both the final and midterm is hard especially the conceptual word probs. He cares about his students.Very helpful and approachable. He would respond to e-mails. There'll be quizzes. But again, brilliant,choose him.

He really knows his stuff. Powerpoints are very clear. Spends too much time on origins of proofs and deriving them. All we want to know is how to get the right answers! The Web-Assign is extremely time-consuming but you can't avoid it. HW is graded strictly and the quizzes are short and a little tricky. Just a midterm and final. Best CalcI can get.
His lectures are very interesting and he is very hot;)easy A without worries
His class is interesting. It's not hard to understand and the quizzes are easy.
I have had friends telling me that they hate him. I dont, but the class is not easy. Word of advice, take Harvey instead. His midterm is so much easier than this prof's.

I liked his powerpoints - saves a lot of time and easy to review later for exams. hated Webassign - hwks are very time-consuming and not necessarily reflective of exams. He's no Jaime Escalante, but the man is very passionate about teaching calculus. Go see him during office hours and get to know him.

Matt spends too much time on concepts, and not enough time doing problems! His tests are hard, but with a LOT of work you can get an A. The TA's are really helpful, though. He teaches everything on a powerpoint; i personally hate that. On the bright side, he speaks english and makes the final for all sections. Good Luck!

Funny guy, approachable, wants to get to know his students. I personally wasn't too big a fan of his teaching style, since it involved too much theory and PowerPoints. But if this is your second go-around at Calc 1, I'd highly suggest him, because he does give you a deeper understanding of the material as promised.

Leingang is truly an amazing professor. If you have to take calc, make SURE you get into his class! he made calc lecture somewhat interesting, and has great powerpoints that he posts that you can study off of later.also, he's super funny!

Leingang is an amazing professor. In a class of 200 students, he actually takes the time to try and get to know everyone personally. He tries to make the subject material interesting and sometimes he incorporates his daughter which is adorable. He assigns 1 homework per week and he has a midterm and a final. He's awesome! Don't hesitate to take him

Seriously I found him to spend wayyy to much time dealing with concepts that were irrelevant. He is so much harder than the other professors and his midterm is by far harder than other professors. Plus you can't argue with him because he is head of the department. He is a smart and nice guy though

Leingang is the deputy departmental head for undergrad math. He writes the final for all classes, so if you take him, you'll be used to him for the final where others won't. His teaching is very fluid, but he spends far too much class time covering theory for its own sake without demonstrating how to apply it to exam-style questions.

He'll make you hate calculus. You can tell he's very intelligent and knows what he is talking about, but he makes concepts too complex and wastes time deriving proofs you'll never need to know again instead of doing examples. Overall, fairly decent teacher. Quizzes are easy. Online homework each week is tedious, but thats all calc 1 classes.

I really enjoyed taking Calc I with Leingang. Though I didn't get a very good grade, that was not his fault by any means. Makes lectures really interesting: interjects math-history and even pop-culture trivia in them while not losing sight of teaching important concepts. Really friendly and approachable. Highly recommended!

Makes the final for all classes, but his midterm is the hardest, as well as the quizes. Hw is the same for all calc classes so there is no way to avoid that. If you're good at calc and understand the material he presents you should get at least a B+.

He is a really smart teacher who knows what he's talking about.  he's very into theories of math which can be very boring!!!  if you are a hard-core math person, then take him.  one good thing about him is that he makes the midterm and the final for all calc classes.
Super nice teacher. Haven't finished the class yet, but she explains all the material very well so far. No complaints!

she was okay. attendance didn't matter and the lectures were online and recorded. felt bad because not a lot of people responded during zooms, but also the class was boring and a bit disorganized. Felt like lectures didn't help too much, it was mainly my TA and practice problems that helped me on exams. she did not know much about the exams at all
No curve at all throughout the semester and extremely difficult final. She's kind of mediocre, a bit disorganized. Lots of practices and self study needed to get a good grade.

She is very disorganized and doesn't know much about the tests being given. Attendence isn't needed but if you've never taken calc this class will be kinda hard. I just took it for my calc requirement for the bio major and struggled a lot. No curve was given either
maybe the most unorganized person ever. do not take her if you are already not an A+ student in math. run

It would be difficult to take this class if you've never taken calc before, because the lectures were taught in a way that felt as though you should already know key calculus concepts. Even though I took calculus in high school, I found the course challenging and relied on lots of information I learned in high school.
She was my 8 am, slept through most of her (online) classes, still passed.

lectures and notes could be confusing, but she posted recordings and digital notes which helped. problems on homework and exams were harder than those reviewed in class, but the final was not as hard as the exams before it. there were weekly quizzes, but some were dropped

Very tough class. I had to get tutoring throughtout the entire semester. I had taken AP calc which prepared me a little, but if you haven't taken calc before then I would not take. Her teaching style is quite confusing and there is little instruction. The only things that saved my grade were the curve for the final and all the online homework.
Professor Stepp is an amazing Professor. She cares greatly for her students, and her online lectures are awesome. Don't hesitate to take her class.

Prof. Stepp is a great person, but I don't think she is the best at teaching. She assumes that most people already have knowledge about probability/statistics, which sucks if you don't. Her notes are a bit of a mess but they are not too bad. 1 midterm and 1 final, no curve. She's hilarious though, and shows us her cats all the time.

Do not take her. Especially if you are taking another stem course alongside. everyone does badly on the midterms and there is no curve. lectures are based on her knowledge not the book. Had to self-teach myself and at the end i wasn't willing to get a C on my transcript so i withdrew. Asked her for help and she was not helpful and even rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: kind of the goat tbh, super nice and explains concepts clearly w lots of examples. i personally didnt find her notes confusing and she was pretty okay about recording lectures. exams were way harder than the material taught in the lectures tho, mid 70s avgs on both midterms so far, no EC. long hws and webassigns but shes still a great prof imo
prof stepp's notes are disorganized and her explanations are always unclear and difficult to comprehend
i gotta run, but, to whom it may concern: do not tak
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Made the online class interactive and encouraged participation. Will definitely be on her good side if you go to all the lectures and make an effort to participate. Go to class because notes can be confusing at times and lecture recordings are not guaranteed! Weekly hws but they prepared you for the tests + quizzes so definitely do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Stepp was decent at teaching concepts, but her notes could be confusing on times. I mostly just focused on doing the homework and it was similar to the tests. For the midterms, the first one was difficult, but the final and the 2nd midterm were not too bad. She is really helpful if you ask her questions and the quizzes were really easy.

To be fairly honest, I didn't think that Stepp taught very well. Her lectures were merely useless and disorganized since she just based everything from her own knowledge instead of actual textbook-based material. First two midterms were mediocre (given no curve) and the final was just horrific. She curved everyone's average at the end.

solid explanations, answers questions over zoom. doesn't interact much with her campuswire. test wording can be oddly tricky. there was extra credit for the second midterm, and the final was optional. my biggest con was that her notes were a little disorganized (they were just all one one giant page). really nice and casual/chill tho. uncurved.

Not a bad teacher, but gives 3 homework assingments plus a quiz each week. The exams are definately harder than the lectures. She has a bunch of extra credit and it's super easy (one of them was literally to take a picture in front of the math building). If you take her online, just know she struggles with technology a lot of the time.
TAKE HER CLASS!!! Best Professor in NYU. Really caring. Normal exam and super kindly curve.

W professor tbh. Stepp knows how to teach especially online. She makes clear proofs during lectures and gives obvious hints on testable materials. She then expects you to do well on exams and of course you will do well!
She was so good, She is the only teacher who believes that grade does not matter and makes the course ez. The final can be substituted for your lowest midterm and counted twice.
Professor Stepp cannot and will not teach students. We had to read the textbook for the entire course and were left trying to figure out the assignments ourselves. She is not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Shes okay. You're graded by 70% exams and if you take her class online her exams don't reflect what was spoken about in class so learn on your own. Many students complained about running out of time for the exam and she didn't really care. The final exam is in person so don't just coast through the online quizzes and exams. Homework heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was overall a great teacher, she is very patient and kind. She thoroughly helped students be able to understand the units she taught by providing a lot of practice problems and was very accessible if anyone needed extra help. There are 2 hw assignments, 1 written and online (very easy). If you are looking for an easy A, take her, shes great!

She is very nice and patient. But indeed a lot of HW.
Be prepared to face a huge amount of work and hard exam that does not look like the actual ones at all.
Study hard, then a B+ or A- wouldn't be a prob!

Her class is great if you are a Tandon student, but if you can take a CAS class, you can get a better grade. Got an A in honors algebra and other two upper level electives but not in this class. She's a super nice person and a great professor! Cares about her students and adjusts the grading scale accordingly. Take time to do practice problems!

Prof. Stepp was great for the data analysis course and had good lectures. She was always available in office hours to answer questions and was very good at explaining concepts. Overall a great professor for math.

Dr. Stepp is really sweet and cares for her students. She will take the time to explain concepts if you need them. She likes questions! Her explanations are clear, and she is engaging. You get HW every week and learning modules. There is a lot of work, but what else would you expect for math. Overall a really great professor. I recommend her!

She adapted to the pandemic well and really cared for her students' wellbeing and success in the class.
