Really great professor- taught me a lot about writing and made the class really interesting. Assignments were reasonable and actually engaging (they weren't that hard overall). Definitely cares about his students.

I absolutely loved this professor. He has students read interesting articles and relates them to writing concepts that he consistently refers to throughout the semester. Polchin is also willing to help his students when they don't understand anything. You are only assigned 2-3 major papers that go through multiple edits before the final draft.

I took him for writing 1 and got an A so I took him for writing 2. I met with him a bunch a lot and got to know him during WR2. I felt that my writing was really improving and he seemed to agree with me, and then I inexplicably got a B- in writing 2. I didn't know why. He's a GREAT guy personally but a tough teacher.
Polchin was always there to help when we asked. He is demanding but very supportive. I definitely improved my writing skills. He is good fun too, good irony.
Whoops I mean reading IS NOT deathly. Lol

Polchin is a really funny guy but only certain kinds of people can appreciate it. His humor is very sarcastic/blunt, but he still remains lighthearted. VERY insightful, very helpful, workload is completely doable (reading is deathly) and very clear. Really interesting essay topics and methods of writing development. Definitely improved my writing
He made me think a lot. It was somehow a new experience for me but was the best course ever.

Polchin was my favorite Professor freshman year. But I think certain kids gravitate towards him, while others lose interest. For me he really understood the way I wrote. Meeting with him to discuss my writing was the highlight of some of my days. Work hard on assignments (do them)  and be invested in class discussion and you will do well.

Had him during Freshman year. While he wasn't easy, I enjoyed his class. When it was time to turn in my final essay, I had it in hand, but told him I wasn't happy with it, so he let me take a couple extra days to work on it! Very understanding & wants to see you do well & produce works you're proud of. Encouraging & you'll like him!
The word mean does not even begin to describe him. Got anxiety attackes frequently before going to his class. He'll ruin your semester abroad in Paris. C'est la vie!!!

Great professor and truly knows what he's teaching. Will be of great help if you approach him. Really helped me gain confidence in my writing and was able to improve my writing drastically. I highly recommend him!

really great guy, very informative, good class discussions. very sardonic and sarcastic sense of humor. assignments were very manageable, not a heavy courseload but still makes you think. learned a lot from him. very organized

I took Polchin's class for the first two semesters of my freshman year.  He's forever changed the way I write, and the way I think about writing.  I also learned a lot about myself as his assignments allowed me to write about almost anything.  I highly recommend his course.  He's very helpful, personal, and has such interesting perspectives! Love!!
Run for the top of the Eifel Tower. After a semester with him you'll be traumatized. Ron Howard should make a new version of An American WErefolf in Paris starring James Polchin.
Good luck keeping your sanity while in class. Thanks to him, i go to therapy every week.
Excellent teacher, very funny and at times a bit awkward.

I am now a senior, but I took prose comp 1&2 with polchin. His classes are very valuable. I don't think I would be able to write my lab reports, now for psych, as well as I do without having taken his classes. He really promotes speaking your mind in class, you don't have to BS that you liked the readings. Very helpful if you utilize office hours.

i took Prof. Polchin's class in freshman year for both semesters and those were by far the best classes i've ever taken. he cares a lot about his students and their writing and is always willing to help. just pay attention in class, make a bit of an input in discussions and write and rewrite your papers. he truly is an amazing professor.
He clearly cares about his students but is somewhat vague when explaining things. Extremely arrogant. Take Nina D'Alessandro instead who's the hottest and collest writng teacher.

I'm currently a senio and am still traumatized after my freshman writing course with Dr. P. He is arrogant, condeascending and just plain mean. My writing never improved as a result of his class. I might as well have donated the tuition money to charity. When I finally write a novel it's going to be titled "The Devil is Mr. Polchin"

Great teacher. The beginning of the course is frustrating because you are writing personal essays, which are different than the typical paper. Polchin gives you the time to find your own style in this field of writing and offers valuable advice in person and through comments on drafts. Papers must have clear central ideas that are well developed.
Scary! Grades so hard, you'll be lucky if you get a B.

Polchin is very passionate about what he teaches and wants to help his students become better writers, while exploring a topic they care about. His classes are very thought provoking and engaging. He assigns a lot of reading, but is usually more concerned with the writer's style than with the work's content content.

A rarity at NYU. Inspiring. He may come off as unclear at first; eventually you will have an epiphany and recognize the brilliance of his teaching. Everything is connected. Be patient. There's no point in writing to his taste -- a sign of an excellent professor. Introduced me to the world of photography. I thank him for this.

He is a very nice, funny, and open-minded professor. The homework for this class was usually very light. We did a lot of peer editing which helped improve our writing & he was really good at explaining his ideas. A lot of class is centered on class discussion and basically writing about stuff you like. He's very relaxed & easy-going.
Very open minded, students do pretty much all of the talking in the class. He is very vague on his assignments, which I actually thought was a good thing because it gave us creative free-reign.

polch is the most amazing teacher at nyu. he is so funny, cute and nice. he is always willing to help and listen to your ideas. he is not very hard but still makes you want to learn. i am in love with him and want to have his babies.

i dreaded going to his class for the last half of the semester. i hated his writing assignments. they are way too long and you'll spend more time bsing than speaking your mind. no matter how hard he tries to explain, i never understand what he wants. im glad his class is over with though. he's a nice guy though. doesnt assign a lot of reading.
awesome teacher! great sense of humor-fun class, made my writing improve A LOT, not EASY but not HARD... very fair teacher. u'd be VERY lucky if u got him as a teacher

He has a very unique style of teaching: he presents the ideas about writing and our thoughts expand upon them.  The problem is that he is a bit too unclear; we need a place to start our papers and he doesn't give us one. Grading is rough and sometimes subjective...If you want to learn to write, take him, but be aware that this IS NOT A QUICK "A."

I think he was a great teacher and he made my writing improve significantly.  He goes through the writing process step by step which makes it easy and he's a great teacher.  The essays can be a little tough but you just need to work for your grade

Most unlcear teacher i've ever hard. Youll think the classes are all fun and easy until he gives one of his ridiculous essay prompts to write about !@#$, like actually nothing, and chances are you'll stuggle to make the page limit and then he grades it like you were suppose to know exactly how he wanted it.

i admire him more and more everyday. he is so amazing, so intelligent. everything that comes out of his mouth is a masterpiece, hes really good with words and everything he says makes you think. hes really funny too, makes you want to go to class. adorable.

He's a nice guy, but he's extremely unclear with what he wants.  I never understood what the assignments were, because he's really vague and makes no sense.  It's hard to do well in his class because he's so unclear with his assignments.  He gives really helpful criticism on papers, though, and he's pretty easy on the eyes.
Class if fun but he is very unclear with essay topics
No Comments

Polchin is a great professor. He makes time to discuss your paper in detail and gives helpful advice rather than criticism. He even gave me an extension when my laptop crashed during the same time I had roommate problems. The essays require effort but they consist mostly of your own opinion.

Not a good class whatsoever.  He's not clear, you have to do alot of writing, and your classmates will be more helpful with your papers than he will be.  His grading is vicious too- I got a C- on a paper once and he said it was "a good struggle". I don't recommend.
great teacher- fun classes- tough grading.

He is extremely vague and it was very frustrating to get ANYTHING done in his class because I never knew what he wanted.  He appears to be easy but his grading sucks...I would definately NOT recommend him to anyone.
Very nice and helpful (considerate too), but extremely confusing. He's good looking by the way :-)
No Comments

I have no idea who wrote those positive comments, maybe himself.  6 essay tasks, extremely boring lecture, for the feedback you get from essays you are going to see a question mark on every paragraph. 

If you are interested into "liberal studies", then yes go take his class, maybe you will find it interesting. 

If you simply want easy A, AVOID!
BY FARRRRRR BEST TEACHER I've had at NYU. you will benefit from his class very much.

Dr. Paliwoda is definitely interesting. He's unlike any professor I've had here so far, but with that being said, PLEASE TAKE HIM!! Oh my god he's so good. His lectures are so insightful, and I left every class questioning what I already know about the world. He can be a little intimidating, but if you get to know him and talk to him, he's amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who genuinely wants to see you learn. He's also very passionate about his class. I struggled at the beginning but he let me revise my work which was really nice. Lecture driven, not too much reading. He assigns a lot of papers though, but its generally not too demanding. Fav prof this semester, maybe so far in my time at NYU.

Professor Paliwoda is so sweet and genuinely such an amazing professor. His class is about War, something he is very passionate about, and he makes his lectures very interesting. He is big on participation, and there are 6 "papers" but some are only 2 pages minimum so it is not that bad. Do take this class, it is so interesting and not very hard!

Paliwoda gives great lectures and puts a lot of effort into each one. All about war btw. He gives a bunch of papers tho (7). Way more than any other professor for this kind of class. His grading and feedback is very unclear. He write the same things on each of my papers and I feel like he would just come up with a grade for them outta thin air.
Big yapper but nice guy

You can really tell he cares about the content he teaches with all his heart. He is so inspirational. The whole class is based on the topic of war, so if this is something that may be triggering or upsetting, would not recommend. I learned a lot. Participate and share your thoughts because he cares! All tests out of class. Not the easiest grader.

He is a very passionate lecturer and clearly cares about what he teaches and his students. His grading criteria aren't too clear but he is very accessible outside of class (via Zoom meetings whenever he is available) and always answers emails very promptly.
Definitely would take again.

Amazing passionate professor. If you genuinely want to learn this is the professor for you. He will give amazing lectures and he deserves students who want to engage. You *can* take him if you just want a nice relatively easy professor but if you just want to just sit on your laptop the whole time (not that you couldn't) Id pick a different proff.

Dr. Paliwoda is my favorite LS professor! He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches that it makes you want to actively listen. Our class only focused on war and the inhumanity/humanity of it, so be careful if this is a sensitive topic for you (or if you're more interested in the format of other AC classes where it's mostly literature based)

Professor Paliwoda is a lovely professor who is willing to talk to you even on weekend if needed and takes care of the students. His class does have a lot of writing (all the grade comes from writing). However, if you go to class, and listen to his lecture, you will be fine. Attendance is not required. Overall recommended
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A pretty good prof who is very interested and well versed in his class topic; however, his class topic, war, is pretty depressing. So be warned if you don't want to learn about the horrors of war pls do not take this class
Overall pretty good and patient

I just wanted to warn other ls students that this class is only about war. Every artwork and lecture revolves around its horrors. I sincerely wish that  would have sent us an email or something ahead of time instead of waiting till the first day to reveal this. Me and many others are now scrambling to find another acm class when most are closed

Great professor with heart in the right place. Can ramble a bit too much sometimes, but that's only because he's passionate. Very understanding and a fairly easy grader. Requires a lot of introspective work so prepare for that. The only downside: he's pretty set on his topics and does not give one much room to choose, but I guess that's college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. Caring, passionate, professional. He has a lot of stories waiting for you to discover. Take his class and talk to him after class. He will be a great mentor for life if you can bond with him.
Professor Paliwoda is certainly passionate about his studies and will lead you into that mood. The class was great but I think he is not an easy grader. Need to work hard to get an A.

Dr. Paliwoda was an incredibly caring professor whose course was quirky and inspiring, connecting often to the city. His homework is minimal but interesting, and his grading is clear and fair. He was also very accessible outside of class and office hours were always very helpful. Essays were personal and the topics broad enough to allow creativity.
The class is all about war, so it can be a bit depressing. However, I learned a lot and was exposed to a lot of new things. There are next to no tests/quizzes, besides the final, and only two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He is an easy grader but his lectures are boring and sometimes depressing
His lecture is usually boring but he's chill about late assignments. He takes attendance sometimes

subject material was really interesting, but the classes got a bit repetitive sometimes. He's really nice, and if you hand in your paper a bit late he's chill about it. Lots of papers though, most of them short (1/2 pages) but a couple long . but he's an easy grader, i got an A on my first paper. also  guest speaker. Def participate he loves it
Professor Paliwoda is not exactly inspiring, but an easy A. We watched some interesting movies in class. If you answer questions in class, he'll like you. Easy grader.

Prof. Paliwoda was an exceptional Writing I professor. The course theme of Hope and Cynicism was hugely interesting and offered flexibility in terms of paper topics. There are readings for each class, but they are light and interesting. I went to office hours before each paper was due and always got super helpful feedback. Very much recommend.

Quite a good lecturer but very work heavy class. You do learn a lot towards the end though. Every exam of his is True/False questions only and they're quite difficult. Lots of extra credit opportunities that boost your grade though. Would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great class and learn a lot. Worth to take again!

Makes things overly complex. The syllabus was 16 pages long. There isn't much connection between the lectures and the homework's and projects. Can be very unapproachable and interrupts students when trying to speak to him. This discourages participation in class. Homework's were easy. The final was very hard but isn't a huge part of the grade.

Pascal is a really dynamic and engaging lecturer. After PODS 1 I wanted to quit the major, but I took this class anyway just to be sure. Completely changed my mind. 

One thing is that sometimes he can be careless about the math, but if you're willing to overlook that, he gives a very good intuition of the central topics in data science.
Simply the best professor at NYU, and it is not close.

You'll learn a lot if you put real effort into the class. However, the course overall (slides, grading, assignments, and labs) can feel somewhat disorganized, and the professor interrupts students everytime they're speaking.
good at making people's life harder.

I couldn't remember what exactly Albert Einstein said explicitly, but my idea is from him: "Education is the process by which students gain intuition after they leave school and forget the details of everything." Tbh, Pascal is the professor who practiced this the best that I have seen until now. Also, he introduced my soul mate to me. Grateful.

Great lecturer, but could sometimes focus on random things and get sidetracked occasionally. Office hours are great. The final exam had question with confusing wording, despite him saying no trick questions. I did not do that well on the final but got very close to an A overall. The capstone project wasn't difficult.

There are three midterms and one final, all really hard with tricky questions, although he always says no trick questions. You would still do badly if you think you know everything. The content is hard to understand, and he doesn't explain very well.

A skilful course designer that crafted the course to avoid the knowledge useful in the workplace. Disrespectful to guest speakers. Repeatedly emphasized unimportant pronunciation of some certain terminologies, but at the same time making pronunciation mistakes on some other words like "Cauchy." Teaches history instead of technical skills.

Competent lecturer and story-teller, but sometimes engages the audience to a fault by relying heavily on student's answers rather than leading the discussion of the material. His office hours were another matter, going there was like going to a tavern; "f–– this" and "f–– that" and "f––ing p-value", and Red Bull cans everywhere. Good overall.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grading is super straightforward, if you attend lectures (which you should, they're amazing) and pay attention, he is absolutely fantastic and you will do well. Highly recommend and super interesting class!
Amazing lectures. Good scholar but not helpful. Never respond to emails and msgs.

Has a passion for DS that really shows in lectures. A bit scatterbrained but makes sure to clarify misconceptions. Provides so many resources it's almost impossible to not understand what's happening (just make sure to make time to go thru them). Weekly quizzes in recitation. Very accessible, fair amount of hw.

Very engaging and knowledgable. Really wants to give you practical skills and focuses on the practical theory. Lectures are engaging and he's super nice if you participate at all. The final project took a lot of work but was one of the most meaningful assignments I've done so far

very weird second tier psy phd who thought he knows all machine learning but actually not. Weird lectures, weird weekly quiz. This man can never get a job in real interviews and it seems he never understands what a tech interview is, as well as research. I heard PhD students are also required to take this BS, sad for them.

Wallisch is engaging and passionate, but the class can be chaotic at times. Attend lectures, use the free textbook, and try unstuckstudy for study prep - it really helped me manage the demanding coursework and project.

Pascal is passionate about DS and wants his students interview ready. His lectures are awesome, ranging from abstract ideas to exact algorithmic details.

My only gripe — the final. It reflects Pascal's precision — wonderful for ensuring grasp of the core concepts, but painful when aimed at minutia.

Though, maybe that's just how interviews go.

An Abel Prize level mathematician for claiming that “all square matrices are diagonalizable.” Always calls his obscure nonsense exam questions as “fair” or “not unfair,” as if he is a devil making a deal with you. Lectures are full of irrelevant content or useless citations—you'd be hard-pressed to find useful new knowledge within that stuff.

Very useful class! Pascal is very funny and makes lectures interesting. Light workload, there's a project which is fun but very time-consuming, so be sure to start early. Final exam has 64 T/F questions. However, you lose 0.5 points per wrong answer (you earn 1 per correct answer and 0 per question left blank), and the questions are poorly worded.
You will be well prepared for the Interviews!

Great professor, great lectures. Be sure to stay engaged and do all the assignments, they help a lot. Capstone project was time consuming, but worth the time. Don't take this class nor a DS major/minor if you are not willing to put in the work. Only bummer would be the final (64 T/F with half penalty for wrong answers), but overall a fun class.

Pascal needs to stop telling stories and get to the point.
Also, stop giving tricky questions with wordplay, it is just bad data science
more of a scholar than a lecturer.

Took his course over the summer. Best psych professor at NYU; extremely funny, very open, and has amazing slides. Great at conducting the flow of conversation in class and you will definitely be engaged. Very cool, quirky, and knowledgeable. If you're interested in his psychopathy course - I 100% recommend.

The best professor I've taken at NYU - genuinely interested in the subject and great at explaining. Interesting lectures, very inspirational & you actually learn a lot. He is ready to help and responds to feedback. If you attend lectures, HW & exams are pretty easy to complete.

Final project for which the lectures did not nearly prepare us for enough on their own. I'm lucky to have had a lot of prior data science experience cuz I had to use basically everything except the class notes to do it. The project was probably the most stressful thing ive had to do at Nyu and it's during finals week and it's not even the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: While this subject is relatively simple, professor Wallisch makes sure that the students understand the smallest of the details, which differentiate a good data scientist from a bad one. All lectures were simultaneously available via Zoom as well, and he tries to be as engaging and humorous as possible, while maintaining the right pace.

The content and slides are above average, although he tends to be disorganized from time to time. 
I give him a 3 because forcing interactions in a large class is unnecessary, especially when he's falling behind the material and doesn't explain things in detail. We come here to learn, not to learn about his or some students' personal lives.
Wallisch is super passionate about data science and does his best to fit as much as he can into a semester. At times the class is chaotic but mostly in a good way.
He knows nothing about machine learning and he does not even try to learn. You CANNOT LEARN ANYTHING ABOUT MACHINE LEARNING in this course, except how to import scikit learn. WHAT A SHAME!

Always in a rush. Spend your own time reading the slides and codes would be much more efficient. The exam is more mathematical (am I taking intro to stats?). I actually encountered a question on the final that required me to download a software to do things I have no idea about. Definitely not a 4.5+ professor, but an ok professor (3.0).
He did NOT provide rubric for project and won't release the grades at all.  Be prepared to receive a surprising final grade.  Avoid him by all means. Worst prof ever.

Pascal is a great person, but it was just very difficult for me to follow his lectures and labs. He was pretty disorganized, and since 112 was a super conceptual class, this made things much more difficult. His python code made me feel so confused, considering how simple they are supposed to be. The capstone project was also quite unclear.
There was no way to prepare for the project, which is worth 30% of our grade. The labs barely help with the project. Legit the most stressful project in my life

Felt that he goes off topic too much during lectures by introducing too many irrelevant concepts. Also, there is no way to prepare for the project (30% of our grade) ahead of time as he literally covered the codes required less than a week its due. Also the questions on the project are vague, so it is impossible to know which method to use.

I think he could have explained topics a lot better and I wish he integrated the code into the concept lessons. However, it's a really straightforward class that will get you ready for the job+interview with each homework assignment building on the last. He even reached out to me to make sure I would finish the extra credit assignments, he cares!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have many machine learning experiences before this class. But still, I put so much time into his homework because they are not designed to make you learn but to make you suffer. Doing his homework doesn't make you get better at machine learning, especially if you want to be an algorithm engineer in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was a *ton* of work. Not sure if I ever worked this hard in any class. But tbh, I expected as much - machine learning is just hard. I also never learned this much, and landed an internship from what I got out of this class. All in all, I would do it again, but go in with eyes open.

This man is an absolute beast and I would love for my other professors to be on his caliber. Word on the street is that he knows if you watch lectures on 2x speed just by looking at you. I am happy to report that this is not true.

His teaching is chaotic and unorganized. He digresses easily and barely goes into the main idea. HW problems are basically calling sklearn functions and lots of repetitive tasks. You have to write four paragraphs for each problem, which is absurd for a CS4XX. And he doesn't have a rubric for grading. Avoid him at any cost.

Love his passion for data science and had his intro to ds before. Yet his machine learning is a mess. Over 150 students and only one grader? It's been close to the end of the semester but the hw2 grade still hasn't come out. I followed TA's instructions and the grader gave me zero. Everything responds really slowly. Everybody is confused.

Great professor, absolute genius, but also can convey stuff. There are some things about linear algebra that only fully clicked during his review lecture before the ML content began. Great guy, surprisingly funny. Very nerdy but I mean its Courant of course. The guy really knows his stuff. Highly recommend.
Amazing professor and an even better human. A must take for anyone interested in data science! Very enthusiastic and approachable

I don't know how he does in his psych, but his Machine Learning is so pathetic. Why NYU let a psych prof(not tech person) teach Machine Learning. His lecture is full of useless jokes. The worst thing is his homework. Why does a 4xx level ai course require homework to be in pdf & py file? And why you don't mention that in class? What about Jupyter?
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at NYU!

Another professor I don't understand the hype about. Most disorganized lectures I've ever attended, and I'm pretty decent at math. He goes on long tangents, doesn't follow slides, and starts a new thought before he finishes his old one. Was a big headache. Hard class, but he made it harder with his style of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pascal Wallisch is one of my favorite teachers. He was well prepared for the lectures, taught the material very well, and was in-tuned with how students were feeling during the class.

A lot of content in the class, and Professor Wallisch is a solid choice to get through it. He is a bit inaccessible because of the class size, and often has a bit of an ego when he teaches. He is effective though and deserves credit for that.

Pascal is amazing. Don't let previous ratings here fool you. Those students likely didn't have the necessary prereqs, which is the fault of the department and never the professor. Be prepared to work a lot--data science in *not* for everyone.

Pascal is definitely the smart guy. you could feel his passion in what hes doing. However, this relatively new course is somewhat disordered. lot of content in lecture. Codes only appeared in lab. Too many work to do from different critia, readings, functions, data analysis every week, a final and a project at the end. Inspirationa lecture though.

I loved Intro to DS with Professor Wallisch, and it's actually the class that got me into data science. He covers a lot of content in a short span of time, so get ready to do work. But if you want a professor who is passionate about their work and genuinely interesting to listen to, take his class! You won't regret it.

Professor Wallisch is amazing. I've taken him for three classes over the course of my time at NYU. He is by far one of the best professors I've ever had and would recommend him to anyone who can take him. He's definitely not easy, but he makes things so easy so it's worth the extra work

I've heard good things about Pascal from my friends in psych but this class was a disaster. If you don't have a strong background in coding I really wouldn't recommend. Very unstructured, online coding labs are pretty useless and a heavy workload. The data science concepts are easy to follow, the execution (coding) part of the class is a shambles.

Best professor ever!! I took all the classes he offers because he is so awesome but his Data Science class was truly exceptional! The way that he explains the concepts and his focus on their real-world application instead of blindly giving random facts is truly remarkable. Do yourself a favor, if you are scared of data science- take this class.

Pascal is an extraordinary professor. He does not make students do silly calculations by hands, and all the assessments are open notes. His office hours are not only informative, but incredibly fun. He gives ample, easy opportunities for extra credit, and is a genius.

He doesn't know how to teach at all. His lectures are irrelevant to most part of his assignments and you need to learn most of the things by yourself. I don't really know why he doesn't want to teach at least some coding during lecture time because labs are short and your TA is just reading through code, not explaining them. I would say avoid him!

The most disorganized professor I've ever had. I absolutely hated his class and his lecture style. I'm good at math but I felt terrible for students that aren't - they were so lost. Loads of work too - 2 paragraphs after EVERY class about what you learned and what you'd like to learn. 8 article summaries. Multiple games taking 1-3 hours. Ridiculous
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course would take a lot of work, likely becoming the class you spend the most time on in the semester, but he it clear that this course is going to be time-demanding, and coding can get sometimes hard to keep up with. Every accessible outside of class, even volunteered to do two live sessions of every lecture to accommodate for time zones

Pascal is amazing, both as a teach but foremost as a person. I've never learnt so much from a class, ever. With that being said, you're challenged in this class - but if you really think it's interesting and ready to put in the work, there's no better class this Pascal's. Also, lectures are a blast - he encourages good vibes and is super available.

Most of the hws (like 65%) are not related to lectures at all so you have to do some self-learning. He sets respond assignments so that you need to attend 20+ lectures to get 10% of the course grade. He is a nice person but his lectures are unorganized/hard to follow, but YOU HAVE TO ATTEND THE LECTURE. I used to love data science but not any more.

Pascal has funny, interesting lectures that he seems to put a lot into, which I learned a lot about DS from. That being said: His Intro to DS is awful. Syllabus is convoluted. Assignments have no relation to the lectures. Labs are a mess. Python code makes no sense. Deadlines are changed. Never responds to emails. Do not take.

Had him for Stats+Cognition. First I was confused (i.e. what is a QDAFI) but he explains quickly. A lot of hw is a completion grade (5% of my grade was an immediate 100% for filling out a pre-course survey). Do the extra credit, listen to him, complete your work and you won't have to stress about a grade- just enjoy listening, he's very engaging.

Professor Pascal is the most unorganized person Ive ever met. His syllabus doesnt make sense, his exam questions are worded bizarrely, and his lectures are useless. He spent more time clarifying than teaching. I learned 10x more in my recitation groups than with pascal. Avoid this professor

Pascal is an interesting professor. He got me into statistics and data science (even though I was on track for Psychology). He farms his own water, and doesn't believe in astrology. His classes are entertaining and engaging even through zoom. Students really respond well to him because he can always make hard/boring topics more interesting.

Yes, there are weekly quizzes or assignments depending on what course you have him for but he needs to have SOMETHING to balance out how great of a professor he is knowledge-wise, teaching-wise, and student-care-wise. Even then, they're not hard at all if you're actually listening to his lectures. Very smart, fun, good-hearted professor.
He was a really fun professor to have, and the lectures were pretty entertaining, even if there were times where nothing made sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would take a bullet for this man. Easily the most inspiring professor I have ever had. He makes daunting subjects (neuroscience and statistics) really engaging. He's an absolute genius which makes him hard to follow sometimes, but if you ask clarifying questions he's more than helpful. He wants you to succeed! This man is the GOAT

Pascal is a genius, but one of *those* geniuses, if that makes sense. He's a bit fast to follow, but is super accessible and wants you to learn and succeed. I think Zoom impacted the quality a bit, but he's very compassionate and understanding. Emphasizes real world application. Lots of extra credit.

Pascal is a great professor. His lectures are interesting, really goes out of his way to engage with students. I've never had a professor that makes asks students' names when they ask/answer a question so they can address them. Very reasonable, lots of extra credit opportunities, super interesting! Never thought stats would end up being this fun

Pascal is someone who understands the material he teaches very in-depth; however, that doesn't always translate to his teaching skills. I've had Pascal for two classes now: Cog Neuro and Adv Stats. In both classes, he really emphasizes understanding the content. That works for Cog Neuro, but not for Adv Stats. It's very easy to get lost in Adv Stat

As a psych major I loathed intro stats but now advanced stats is one of my favorite classes because of Pascal. Fantastic lecturer. Teaches concepts in a really accessible and engaging way. Lots of work outside of class (an open book, untimed online quiz and a "game" every week) but its a great grade booster. Go to lecture.

Professors as enthused and intelligent as Pascal are few and far between. Cognitive Neuroscience sounds like an intimidating course, but he makes each topic exciting to learn about and really wants everyone to succeed. He's very unique, and that makes lecture different and maybe intimidating, but entertaining nonetheless. Loved.

Pascal is funny & approachable. He's too smart, which sometimes makes him hard to follow bc he forgets that we don't know what he knows. Ask questions & he's happy to elaborate. tests are multiple choice and strange, but not necessarily hard, and are 95% based on things he says in lecture. you have to know concepts & understand how pascal thinks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In lectures, he's a superstar. Sadly he's not very accessible outside of class. Very few of his lectures were "misses" in the sense that they failed to capture the students' attention. The tests, while long, aren't particularly hard if you go to lecture and pay attention.
Pascal is the greatest human and greatest teacher. nuff said. Im a film student and ADVANCED STATS was my favorite class because of him... In his words, thats weird.
Talking to Pascal is good for your general well-being :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: GO TO HIS Office Hours!!!!He's more himself in the small-scale conversation than he is in the Large lectures. He is very inspiring, always willing to help (so much), and he won't care about the "format" or "manner" u talk to him. He cares about content and inspiring ideas. He will not hesitate to pass down all he knows, about PSYCH and about LIFE!!

In one word, Pascal is the goat. No other professor in the world will ever be as passionate about his subject as this man is. Goes the extra mile to engage everyone in class and is always open to criticism on his classes/teaching style. Grateful to have taken him by chance in Stats, I'd follow this dude to the ends of the Earth.

So intelligent.. willing to listen to students.. funny.. makes lectures engaging.. ugh.. I love him :( BUT don't be fooled by the laid back vibe of his lectures. Exams are hard, but I think it's fair considering the content and nature of the class (Adv Psych Stats)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Psychopathy with Pascal is an AMAZING class. Its a great option for your elective if you're a psych major because as long as you are kind of interested in psychopathy, you will do well. You have to do the readings because there's a reading check at the beginning of every class, but the readings are really short and interesting. take this class!!

Pascal is one of the most passionate and engaging professors that I have had at NYU. He talks really fast and bombards you with information, but it's all worth listening to. A bit unorganized, but his class was definitely one of the most interesting classes that I have ever taken and if anyone has a chance to take Pascal as a professor, do it!

Pascal is WILD. He's a solid professor with very few limits to how the class discussion can go and what content is okay for both presentations and projects. This is definitely a good elective to take as a final semester senior.

I had Pascal for Advanced stat and loved his class so much that I took his psychopathy class the next semester. In both classes he was hilarious and engaging. I wasnt interested in either topic but Pascal made both classes some of my favorite to look forward too. For stat, just pay attention in class and do the homework. Psychopathy is an easy A.

Pascal is an incredible reasonable professor that's clearly passionate about what he teaches. He has very few expectations, if you don't slack on those you'll be fine. He likes creativity and new ideas, and is always open to chat. Class can sometimes get off topic, but is usually entertaining.

His psychopathy class seemed a bit disorganized due to the fact that lectures ended up being more like discussions and conversations rather than actual lectures. Certainly a very interesting class though and you definitely won't be bored. Presentations are very low-key and the readings were pretty interesting. Pascal is very receptive to questions

Took Pascal for Advanced Psych Stats and Psychopathy--both were great. He values succinct work and doesn't care for busywork at all. The more you participate, the more he'll give you chances to do well in the class, so make sure to raise your hand. He gets a bit carried away on occasion but it's only because he so clearly enjoys his work.

I took his Psychopathy course; there's a lot of reading, but most of it is pretty interesting, and lectures are great. The course got a bit disorganized over the course of the semester, but definitely worth taking if it's a topic you're interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class, very interesting, lively and informative, learned a lot.

Pascal is passionate for sure. A little weird. His lectures are fun, while his exams are challangening. He definitely cars about what people wrote about him. Encouraged us to write about him on here during class

WOW. The most incredible professor I've ever had. Each one of his lectures is like performance. He is so funny, passionate about stats, and makes his lectures informative yet entertaining which is pretty rare. I actually looked forward to going to class. Also he's brilliant. Tests are hard but doable. Please take this class, you won't regret it.

I love Pascal!! Great professor, and considering the fact that Stats is a pretty dry subject, it's amazing that he made it so engaging. Always available to talk about/help out with the material. Go to his office hours, even if it's just to kick it and talk about life -- he's incredibly insightful about things in life beyond statistics.

Pascal is one of those teachers that you'll want to take over and over again regardless of the subject. He's brilliant and makes lectures on what can be a dry subject quite fun. Lecture isn't mandatory, but if you don't go to lecture you won't understand. If you need extra help or have questions he's always willing to meet in office hrs and assist
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pascal's classes are always amazing. I've taken his stats course as well as his cognitive neuroscience course and he is consistently passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are clear and engaging. Though his tests are open book, his lectures still encourage you to go to class and review course material. Definitely take his courses!

Pascal is the best. Advanced Psych Stats with him was fun and engaging and I found myself excited to go to lecture and recitation even though recitation attendance wasn't taken. The quizzes help you and the exams are open-book (because they're conceptual and don't rely on formulas). You'll learn a ton here.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pascal is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. It's clear how much he values statistics and how much he wants to pass down his own knowledge to his students. Your grade is a combination of attendance, quizzes, assignments, papers, and two exams (midterm and final). It may seem like a lot but it all helps when studying for exams.

One of the best professors you will have at NYU. If you take one class with him, you will want to take all of the classes he teaches. He makes Advanced Stats super interesting and it will change your life. TAKE HIM!

He's such an incredible lecturer! I was terrified of taking this class because I almost failed PSYCHUA10 but thanks to Pascal I'm on the track towards an A. Takes attendance through multiple choice questions (doesn't count towards the grade) with iclickers. No textbook needed. Open-book & fair exams (1 midterm & 1 final) & lots of EC opportunities!

Pascal is very passionate about statistics which makes it all the more interesting for the students. He always makes use of interesting examples and keeps students engaged in the topics, always makes sure to clarify concepts that may be confusing, very open to questions. He's hilarious and his lectures are so worth going to. Exams are open book.

Best professor I've ever had. Super knowledgeable, passionate, caring, and helpful. He teaches better than anyone I've ever met & you will learn a LOT. Classes were were fun, interesting, applicable, and interactive. Don't buy the textbooks, they're never used. Can use any resource on tests (notes, textbook, Internet, etc.). Lots of EC opportunity.

Pascal is the best professor I've ever had. I made this account just to review him. His enthusiasm about the course material was hugely motivating in my decision to continue learning about computer science. He welcomes student feedback and adjusts the course accordingly.  If you have the chance to take this class, do it.

srsly one of the best professors i've had in my time at NYU! somehow he manages to make hilarious jokes throughout all of his lectures, which definitely helped me to stay engaged. exams are open-notes/laptop/book. only thing, is that his exams are not based directly on lectures. he expects you to know how to apply the details on broader concepts.

Pascal is by far the best professor I've had. He teaches you so you actually learn and remember the concepts instead of just memorizing and forgetting. I highly recommend him and wish every professor adopted his teaching style. He's also super sweet and has the cutest accent.
Easily the best professor in the psychology department.
amazing

Absolutely great professor.  Goes over the weekly assignment in class and actually fixes or writes the code from scratch in front of us while explaining it.  Definitely open to questions and keeps the pace nice for struggling students.  Also a bit eccentric with his choice of slidesexamplesquotesthoughtseverything.  Funny guy, I suppose :)

Pascal is an absolute sweetheart and the best, most wonderful professor I've had at NYU. I'm actually pretty sad that the semester has come to an end as I loved Cog Neuro. He was always there for me, took out so much of his free time to help his students and made lectures so interesting, it was impossible to get distracted.

Everyone says you have one professor who changes your life. That's Pascal! Once you take one class with him, you'll want to take them all. He is supportive, funny and so intelligent. He truly serves as a mentor IF you are worth his time.  Take his classes and get to know him! Just be prepared to work for an A

amazing teacher, wish I enrolled with him for more classes. he makes it clear that the class is for students' benefit, so he'll cater to your pace and is very open to feedback. class is always fun and interesting, assignments posted online, and professor is quite charming and very intelligent (and has an adorable accent)

Pascal really cares about us and whether we learn or not.  He caters the pace to what we're comfortable with and actually goes over our quizzes (yes, you get quizzes, but, no, they're not going to kill you... probably.) and revisits topics if we ask so we always come out of lecture (or the next one) understanding what he talked about.

Pascal is an extremely knowledgable guy who actually cares about the fate of his students.  His no bs mentality regarding pseudoscientific claims in the field make lectures that much more enjoyable to attend.  Doing well in this class takes work, so make sure to have a good understanding both of lectures and research articles

Pascal is excellent. Actually cares about whether his students learn, and is completely approachable. Both hilarious and brilliant. He manages to make full-sized lecture classes discussion-based, which is awesome. Tests are fair, but hard, so study up. Also, tends to veer off-topic during some class discussions, but it's not too much of a problem.

He's incredibly engaging and loves his students. Totally chill. Messed up extra credit so the whole class pretty much got A's. Tests are open notes, laptop/internet included. TAs are great, especially Wayne. Take CogNeuro with him if you get the chance, but make sure you pay attention in class because he's probs gonna fix the extra credit problem.
Utterly brilliant. BUT don't be fooled. You WILL have to study to get a reasonable grade. A lot.

Have to echo many of the comments here - Pascal was a great lecturer and overall teacher. His attitude brought out the best in me. Tests included many essays and required attention to detail. Challenging but fair.

Pascal is one of the best psych professors I've had at NYU. He's open-minded and warm and cares very much about his students' welfare. His lectures were also extremely engaging and interesting. Definitely an awesome guy all around!

This has been my best experience with a professor at NYU so far. Pascal's lectures were clear and interesting. He also did extra activities to keep the class interested and I actually looked forward to attending class. He also genuinely cares about his students and was always willing to help.

after three years at NYU, i can say Pascal has been one of my top 3 professors, perhaps #1. he is a very talented educator with the ability to explain everything clearly, and keep it all interesting. he's also hilarious. take his class if you can

he was honestly one of the coolest professors i've ever had. he is very funny and always throws in something interesting every lecture to keep the class involved. the tests are based almost completely on what he talks about in class, but they aren't exactly easy. you need to study but if you go to class and pay attention you should do great.

pascal is one of the coolest professors i've had.  he's incredibly laid back, but don't let that fool you-- his tests are not a piece of cake.  does require some memorization, but he's all about the 'big picture.'  and don't be fooled into thinking this is easier than cog neuro-- this class is very biology intensive.

I had him for perception this past semester. Hes a nice guy and very knowledgable. Attendance was not mandatory but it did help for exams. The workload is not too bad, so if u read and understand the slides you should do well on exams, however his curve is not too generous so make sure you study!
Personifies greatness.

He seemed like a good professor in freshman year, for intro to programming. However, he is very biased, even though this class is for beginners, he expects you to have an understanding of coding already, and favors students who peeks his interest. He failed a few students in my year because we didn't understand coding fast enough.

Took his Game Studies class, Charles is a great professor who clearly knows what he's talking about, very knowledgeable and passionate, answers questions inside and outside of classroom. His advice might sound redundant at times but his feedback will help you improve on your writing. Take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favoutie course this year! ! If you do not have a lot of programming background this course might be challenging. There is a weekly quiz for the first 5 weeks(if you do not like exams this is hard) and a weekly hw project for the whole semester, so do expect to spend a lot of time and learn a lot. Mr Pratt is super helpful and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's okay. Pretty passive aggressive at times. The class is easier if you have prior coding knowledge. The lectures he gives have basic info, so if you really want to make your project nice then you have to do a lot of your own research. Felt a bit anxious attending his class sometimes due to his critiques but he acted like that toward most people.

He is a good lecture speaker, charismastic even, yet, he uses his personality to get away with working with every group and spends ALL of his time in his favorite, while neglecting others. A lot of people struggled for his favoritism. He also gaslights groups of mostly females into changing their genre to narrative. Not sure why he is still here.

The course itself is coding-heavy so don't expect easy A or easy hw. Weekly lecture video and weekly programing hw would be assigned. The class only met once per week and it was for reviewing your hw code. The course would be a bit easier if you have previous coding experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gives good lectures, but not a very good professor. Charles is very biased, he loves action shooter games and ignores narrative games. Get prepared for a poor grade if he doesn't like you. Sometimes too strict and unreasonable in terms of participation. Gives out a scammer vibe. Talks too much, not sure what he is capable of.
He should teach philosophy not game design
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He gives pretty interesting lectures, but they are all really long and there is always a quiz on the lecture next class. He does a pretty good job at making it interesting though, even if it can sometimes be a lot of notetaking. Make sure to take good notes to do well on the quizzes, and to send emails with questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are entertaining, especially if you care about games. You have to go, as there's a quiz guide that answers all the questions that you'll be asked in recitation. Some of the speakers don't do too well and some of the lectures aren't very entertaining (ancient board games). The weekly writing isn't hard once you know what they want.

Games 101 Great Class. Note: Don't take if you have trouble with memorization and you're not an avid gamer. Because you'll probably fail or get a low grade. Lectures vary because lecturers vary. Notes can be difficult because of that. But you need notes! But he's very helpful and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Charles is easily my favourite professor I've had at NYU. Great lecturer, fair grader, and just an interesting guy overall. Really liked the course.

Class was straightforward game history. Lots of memorization. Was flexible on midterm by for final you need to know every detail. The TAs are the people you go to with most questions. Overall seemed like a nice guy. No textbook. Hw was to play specific games and write analysis. The games are provided in the game library.

This class is great, this professor is great, this material is great. Probably the best class I've taken in college so far due mostly to the material covered and recitations. If you go to lectures and recitations, do the weekly reports, study maybe 5-10 minutes for each quiz, you're on track to an A. I loved his class and highly recommend it.

I've had Charles for three classes now. He's a great professor, always willing to engage with students. He is rather hardheaded about his views, but he does have the evidence to back them up, and invites a good debate.  I've never had someone lecture better than him.

Make no mistake, games 101 is hard. It sounds like a joke but each exam will have you memorize the gameplay, history, precedents, designers, platform, and year of release of 60 games + other lecture topics. Additionally, you have to be able to identify these from a picture. I was told this is to fight "grade inflation."
Charles is the best!
taken 603 and 604, goat business professor. You won't regret it.

In 603 and 604, students will complete a realistic corporate advertising task in the form of a group project, which is a valuable and engaging practical opportunity. The professor is not only kind and approachable but also deeply cares about her students—she replies to emails instantly and will go out of her way to help students.

The 603 course includes an interview project, two enterprise-related projects, and several guest speaker lectures. Most assignments are applied: you analyze real situations, prepare presentations, and reflect on what you learned. Overall, the work focuses on using course concepts in concrete projects rather than only taking tests.

Students from different cultural backgrounds fit well in this class, and a wide range of opinions is encouraged. Class participation and discussion are a major part of your grade. In general, students and the professor will share the talking time. If you rarely speak or do not like group discussion, your final grade will be affected.

The assignments can be daunting for a non-native speaker, but she emphasizes students should just try their best and gives excellent support and feedback!!

She's a bit strict at first, but she is very well prepared and knows what she's teaching/how to teach it. She is also very accommodating to students and made the class very fun. As long as you put in the effort, it's a very fulfilling class. For a beginner learning Chinese, she makes it easy. She is one of my favorite professors so far at NYU.

She is one of the best teachers that I've ever had. The class is terrifyingly hard if you have little background in Chinese, however, she makes it approachable and is very helpful and accessible through both email and after class. She's sweet, I'd recommend her to anyone, but especially so to those with no/little background in Chinese.
Literally the best teacher I have ever had! So kind and understanding, and while the material can be challenging as long as you put in effort you will receive a good grade.
Choose her without a doubt. Her class is so fun. She is innovative and spent quite a lot of time and effort on the class. One of the best professors in East-UA department in my opinion.

Professor Wang is great, definitely one of my favorite professors in NYU. She is very genuine and patient. Also, the course material she provided are practical and insightful. I would 100% take her class again.
My favorite professor at NYU !!!
I love professor Wang so much. She is very patient and put  a lot of effort into her classes. The wl is not large at all, I will definitely take the course again. Highly recommended professor
Nice professor, you'll learn a lot.

Great professor, I really enjoyed our group projects and the guest lecture with Yamibuy's CEO, although the class is a bit slow-paced for me. She is also fun and knowledgable. Take her, you won't regret it.

Prof. Wang is genuinely one of the best professors that I've taken. The class teaches practical skills that would be really useful in future work settings. She also shares a lot of her previous work experiences to help us understand business communication in Chinese. Moderate workload and interesting contents. Highly recommend!

She was my first ever Chinese Professor. She never fails to make us laugh and she really encourages her students to learn. The goatThe goatThe goatThe goatThe goat

Easiest class ever. Attendance isn't mandatory, you don't have to talk if you don't want to. Class is super relaxed and he's funny so he always makes jokes. Him and TA's want everyone to pass so they make every quiz (3 content, 2 memorization) and final EASY. There are 3 papers throughout the semester, but again easy and the TA's give good grades.

Great professor--involved, caring, and overall a great lecturer. His best quality is how in touch he is with internet culture. The work is balanced; 2 to 3 essays throughout the course. Would recommend! Makes a required class really funny and interesting! Not too much work and we were allowed an index card for our midterms and final!

Very interesting course given current events. Hard course but nice professor

dont take her. Her lectures are useless, youre on your own in the exams
I wouldn't recommend if someone wants to genuinely complete their econ major with a good grade. worst nyu professor till date after bhiladwala. maybe she this one beats her to it

really tough class, esp her exam average about 40-50, she really wanna teach everything, but her explanation is confusing. Best Writing the Essay professor! You can actually learn things in her class. She's inspirational, caring, and gives amazing feedback. She is so knowledgeable and will give you so many ideas on your paper's topic. She's very understanding and accessible after class too.

Jenni is amazing, the best professor I've had so far. Her lectures are clear and concise, she gives really helpful feedback on essays, and she cares deeply about all of her students. She makes time throughout the semester to meet with each student individually to make sure they're doing well. If you have the chance to take her, don't miss out.
Whatever you do, if you have to take writing the essay, make sure you get Jenni.

Jenny is the teacher that got me through my 1st year of college. I am graduating now and I still think of her when I think about positive figures in my college experience. I was a very engaged student but not very motivated and she took the time to get to know me and help me grow as a writer. If you commit to the class and try hard, you'll do well.
Cares SO much about her students, and completely transformed my understanding of essay writing. My favorite teacher I've had at NYU.
A genuinely kind and understanding instructor who really cares about her students. Assignments kind of lengthy but is very understanding with extensions etc.

Best Professor you can ask. Cares deeply about her students, very fair with grades and students investment in class, funny sensitive and extremely inspiring. There to truly teach. Seriously, your win.

Truly the most wonderful professor I've ever had. I learned more about writing during my semester with Jenni than I ever did before. If you get the opportunity to take her class, do it. She makes you work pretty hard but it's really worth your time.

Jenni is literally the greatest professor! I had her both semesters and learned so much. Not only has she changed my outlook on writing but my outlook on life. You should consider yourself lucky if you have the privilege of having Jenni, and if none of that conveys how cool she is, just know she has a really cool New Zealand accent.

I could tell you a hundred times that Jenni is the best and it wouldn't accurately convey how much I love her class. She's just brilliant! My writing has improved strikingly because of her, and even the students who are totally disinterested in WTE are obsessed with Jenni and show up wanting to engage. Best choice for WTE professor!

Jenni made the most dreaded class in my schedule one of my favorites (can't believe I'm saying that about WTE). She is an incredible teacher, clearly passionate about what she is teaching. She is by no means an easy teacher - but if you work hard, you will succeed, and you will be proud of the work you create.

Jenni made WTE fun and interesting.  She made me think about writing in a whole new way and really challenged me to think of new ideas. You definitely work hard in her class, but the skills you take away are really valuable.  On top of all that, Jenni is really sweet and funny.

Great professor. Don't try to slide any BS by her, because she will catch it. No, she will. Really. You learn a lot from this course and she makes it engaging and challenging - my only complaint is that she can be pretty blunt at times and it may come off as condescending. Don't take it personally, though.

Jenni is tough but an awesome person and teacher.  She's incredibly dedicated to helping you improve - and you will.  She makes class challenging but always interesting.  You'll have plenty of work but it's very rewarding when you turn in something you feel good about.  Jenni will teach you a ridiculous amount and you'll want to learn in her class.

shes a really amazing teacher, makes you want to learn and do better...she is extremely clear in everything she does -- its all she cares about is clarity....you do have a decent amount of work to do...and she's understanding when it comes to handing them in, but will not accept bs so dont even try

She was an amazing teacher, so helpful. Conferences with her are mandatory/suggested and they are extremely helpful. The class (WTE) is hard itself but she really wants to make you a better writer. Although I really hated this class and NYU's requirement for it, I thought I became a lot better because of Jenni.

Jenni is a fantastic professor, albeit a difficult one. I suggest doing EVERY assignment she gives out; none of them are extraneous. She knows and appreciates good writing, and it is extremely rewarding when you work hard and earn your grade. She's also very helpful when you're having a tough time. I highly enjoyed and recommend this class.
Awesome but tough teacher.

I was really dreading this class but Jenni made it worthwhile. You can't BS any assignments and she makes you actually think a lot but she made me a better writer. She's also the most helpful teacher I've ever had. She genuinely wants to help us become better writers.

I was NOT looking forward to taking Writing the Essay, but Jenni made this class enjoyable. She's not an easy grader- she has pretty high standards- but she's really helpful and always clear. I'm actually going to miss this class as weird as that is. I definitely recommend Jenni- my WTE experience was so much better than any of my friends with her.

i thought this class was going to be a huge waste of time. but jenni is absolutely amazing. learned so so much from her, even though she is REALLY hard... if you take her advice to heart, you will become a much better writer, without question

For WTE Jenni is the best you can have. though shes a tough grader at times, its worth it because she definitely improved my writing a lot. she was super helpful and easy to understand. most people at nyu dread wte but i considered it one of my best classes, and it was all because of Jenni!
She is the best WTE professor out there. She pushes you hard to reach your fullest potential and it's worth every moment of it. It's a hard class but it's the best WTE class here at NYU.

The most amazing writing teacher I've ever had. She expects a lot of her students and in turn gives a lot back. Expect to give a lot of your time and sanity to her assignments but to feel incredibly accomplished in the end. I'm one of few people at NYU who enjoyed their WTE experience and it's all due to Jenni.
I adore Jenni as a person. She was incredibly helpful but expected a lot. By no means an easy class and definitely caused a great deal of stress. Without a doubt, I am a better writer though.

Jenni Quilter is the best you can have for Writing the Essay. She will make you think hard and work hard, this class is by no means easy. But you will definitely get your time & effort's worth in the end. Highly recommended, but move on if you want an easy A.

This class tanked my gpa, caused me untold amounts of stress, and wrecked havoc on my circadian rhythm. But it was worth it. Take this class, but know that you will have to work for your A- (which was a 91% at the time I took the class). This class will expand your mind and teach you how to really think.

Jenni Quilter is a sweet but tough WTE teacher, as her class grade averages will show.  Though her grading is hard, it's just the product of her attention to precision and quality in her students' writing.  She ACTUALLY cares about how much her students learn, and as such is willing to push them to actually improve.  Difficult class, but recommende

Dr. Quilter is very clear and very helpful. She does interesting stuff in class and even though she can be a little cold and expects you to do a lot she really teaches you a lot and makes it rewarding
Almost every hates writing the essay but I loved it because of Dr. Quilter.  It was my favorite class even though she demanded a lot and there was a lot of work.  I HIGHLY recommend her.
No Comments

Rehder is deeply caring and a great prof. Took Lab in Cog & Perception with him and it was definitely an easy-A class. Low-stakes group presentations every class plus a 2 question quiz on the readings. TA grades everything so I can't speak to how he is as a grader, but he's very responsive out of class. Given the opportunity, take his class!

requires lots of studying outside of class for a decent grade, lectures are all posted online, test questions are made up of multiple choice + written questions, and grades depend on how lenient the TA is

He's a great lecturer and explains material very well. Definitely had to put a lot of effort into studying; concepts aren't hard, just a lot of material to study for the exams. Extra credit opportunities on the exams, reflective of lecture material and practice questions in recitation. Light hw assignments. Don't really have to read the textbook.
Rehder is a great lecturer who gets through a lot of content very effectively. The course is relatively easy to understand and very interesting

Sure the class requires some memorization but that's just the nature of psych. The exams are very accurately reflective of lecture material, and we get SO many generous extra credit opportunities which are easily obtained by just skimming the textbook. It's definitely not a free A but just have an idea of the lecture content and you'll be fine

Great professor. However, be warned that this was the hardest class I've ever taken at NYU. So much content and the class is graded on a curve, so your grade heavily relies on how your classmates did. I learned a lot from this class and enjoyed the content but I definitely had to put in a LOT of additional studying time.

Please don't take this class if you value your GPA. The exams are very tough—you're expected to memorize almost everything from the PowerPoints (not only memorizing but also knowing the theory very well). The examples given in class are often too abstract to be helpful, and the practice exams don't reflect the actual test content.

RUN if you value your GPA! He assigns ton of excessive homework and paper, while the 3 exams alone weigh 75% of the total grade. Lectures are poorly structured, failing to connect examples with core concepts. The exam questions have nothing to do with the given review questions. Grading is harsh, and the workload is overwhelming.

This class is very tough. 75% exams, each without a study guide and covering 400 slides and textbook readings, and 25% HW and a paper. Prof. Rehder did well by connecting what we were learning to real world examples, however even so, this class was not a walk in the park. Get ready to study for days on end if you want to succeed...
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
This class was wayyyy more difficult than I expected it to be. It's also graded on a curve so 22.5% of students get an A, 45% get a B, 22.5% get C, etc. This is the only class I've ever had that has a grading scheme like this. 

75% exams, 10% homework, 15% final paper (5 pages). Also, your grade matters HEAVILY on who your TA is. Choose wisely!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Professor Rehder!!! I've had so many awful profs and unhelpful profs but I really enjoyed Cognition with him. Went to his office hours once for a good amount of questions and he was super nice and super helpful. You can tell he puts effort in making his slides, they are organized, clear, funny, and related to the real world. W prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing! slides are long BUT most are just experimental data, concepts are easy to understand, first mt was long but difficulty is very reasonable, questions are similar to review questions(6 extra credit problems) very accessible, answer my questions patiently. Don't give him a low rating because you didn't study hard enough. 100% RECOMMEND

The most difficult elective I've taken at NYU, saying that as a senior! He jam packs NINE lectures worth of content into 38 MCQ and three multi step short response questions. It is incredibly difficult to prepare for this class because it's nine super long lecture slides (40-50 each) plus recitation content. AVOID THIS CLASS! Take another elective!

Really enjoyed his lectures! I really liked the content of his course. His exams are based on the PPTs he shares in his lectures and are not difficult to score well in if you study from the PPTs and read through the textbook. Also gives extra credit questions in his exams. Definitely recommend taking his class!

Read the slides, read the textbook and you will be fine. If you have any problems, Professor Rehder, despite his position at the university is very accessible so do not be afraid to pop up during office hours he loves it. Skipped half of the classes and was hospitalized the semester I took it and still easily got an A.

I honestly really liked this class. Professor Rehder's lectures are extremely informative and clear. Attendance isn't counted, but if you go to each class and pay attention, you'll probably do well in the course.
rly enjoyed this class!

Prof. Rehder is the BEST. His lectures are sprinkled with funny slides and in class 'experiments' e.g. how many people will miss the gorilla. When the course began, the test was lecture + textbook, scores weren't bad but not great, so he decided to make the tests only based on lecture. He is so kind and great to speak to during office hours.

Well-intentioned guy but lectures were incredibly boring--he just read the PowerPoint in a slow, monotone voice. Exams were rough, even when you study a lot-- 40ish multiple choice questions and 3 difficult essay questions. If you want to do well you NEED to attend every lecture/recitation, do all the readings, and study hard!

Nice guy, genuinely wants you to learn in his class. Tests are based on powerpoints/ recitations/textbook but mostly on those powerpoints (which are incredibly thorough). Yes, this course is going require work but he definitely is one of the better professors out there.

He's very nice and his power points are very clear and well planned out. But, he lacks in clear directions and the test is based on everything on powerpoint, recitation, and textbook even if he did not go over them. For his final, it's a paper AND a test. Don't take this class, such a hassle.

Rehder is honestly one of the most organized professors I've had. His PPTS are thorough and so long as you go to class, those slides that otherwise wouldn't make sense, do. Seriously just study those PPT slides before the test - all the answers on them!! The problem is that the PPT info can easily be mixed up in your mind so just study hard!

An amazing lecturer. Very straightforward; heavy reliance on PPT. Honestly, just studying the PPTs got me Bs, but whenever I went to the lectures, I definitely enjoyed his teaching style. My TA was extremely helpful and available as well!

he's very knowledgeable about the subject material and his tests are very straightforward, although slightly difficult because of the detail it goes into; but otherwise, pay attention, study hard, and you'll do completely fine
The course was extremely informative and this professor is particularly thorough. He is tough, but extremely fair and helpful if you ask him for assistance.
Avoid at all cost! I was so interested in this class and now I am so disappointed. Ruined my GPA! Guys, mercy yourselves.

Professor Rehder is an excellent teacher. If you go to class, pay attention, and take solid notes you will do fine. His lectures are interesting, straight forward, and extremely helpful for the tests. He's all around a great professor and I really enjoyed his class.

Do not take this class. He is the worst professor in the psychology department. He does not teach. Your entire grade consists of 3 tests, which are really hard, and cover material that he does not even teach. If you have one bad exam, you are screwed. DO NOT take Cognition with Professor Rehder, he will kill your GPA!

This class sucked! Rehder's lectures are completely uninteresting. He just reads power points out loud. Does weird things with his mouth when he speaks that are very distracting once you notice them. The material itself is basically just things that are intuitive and then you learn who studied it, when, and how their exact experiments worked.

He's extremely interested in the topic and it comes through on his teaching. He gets into very complex ideas but he always eases you into them so that everything is logical. hes got a serious demeanor but hes still approachable. His powerpoints are the best
Immensely interesting class which is very well organized. I actually enjoyed classes, and never felt too lost, there is a lot of information to memorize.
Talks about latest and coolest stuff in ai
Knowledgeable professor
If you do all of the work you will get an A. Professor is pretty knowledgable in this subject, you will learn a lot from him.
