reviews.comment: Professor Ted Alcorn is very caring towards students in a way that not every teacher is. He really puts in the extra effort to meet outside class and is always willing to connect students to people he knows. He is also very clear about his expectations for the senior seminar class and gives detailed feedback. I'd definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
If you care about learning and developing your critical thinking/writing skills, I highly recommend Ted's class.
Grading criteria is very clear and professor is always accessible outside of class to provide detailed feedback and discuss any work prior to submission.
He genuinely cares about all students and pushes them to be the best possible.

Senior Seminar is challenging as it's largely self-guided, but Alcorn is very supportive and accessible. He's passionate about the course, helps shape your policy memo, and is always willing to connect students with professionals in the field.

Prof Alcorn's class was awesome! He has amazing real world experience he infuses into his lectures and he has great ways of getting you to think through the landscape and obstacles of crafting policy. He'll teach you to be a savvy writer and he's super communicative about what he expects and gives instructive feedback. Highly recommend!

Ted was a very understanding professor. He would take the time to workshop any policy solutions we would have. I liked how he integrated our discussion posts into discussions and guest lectures. He has a passion for policy and emphasizes how to effectively communicate policies!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The 2.5 hr classes were always a waste of time and unhelpful. I couldve structured and taught the class better. His critiques on my paper over the sem were contradictory, lacked critical thinking and offered no clear direction on a fix. Best advice is to put a lot of time and effort into yours and do what you think is best regardless of his advice.

He's a good lecturer in class, but be aware that he relied heavily on reading. His feedbacks on assignments are harsh, so be ready with critics. His class is not really helping towards the final projects, so you will have to basically work on yourself. If you are OK with yourself and only taking his class learning advocacy, this class is for you.
The class was very interesting, however was data heavy and lecture heavy. Alcorn was an okay grader, however his comments were very harsh and stated what you did wrong, rather than how to improve.

professor would be bearable if his feedback wasn't so UNNECESARILY scathing. reading the feedback he gives on assignments is difficult bc it feels rude and condescending instead of constructive criticism. he's friendly in class but his feedback feels like hes undermining your intelligence and hardwork just because he doesn't like/agree w the idea

All he did as a professor was tell us to read studies rather than teach the actual material and teach us how to apply the material to the real world. class is VERY statistics heavy. reviews.comment: Great professor, very knowledgable and kind professor. The class includes 2 short 750 word in-class essays that you know the prompt before and can prepare what you need to write. 2 essays. And 1 in-class final essay (you also know the prompt before). Grading is very clear and it is very easy to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice lady and clear grading with easy assignments. Would def take to fulfill culture requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In Class essays were manageable with minimal prep. Very clear with grading on how to get an A/B/C, and readings/videos was 1-2 hours MAX

PSA: There is a lot of writing in this class, with three in-class exams and two essays. The course can also feel repetitive as every class revolves around small group discussions. However, Prof Thorpe is extremely kind, knowledgeable, and understanding with her students. She grades fairly and is always open to chat. I recommend taking her class!

Too many essays for one class: 2 in-class essays for midterms + 1 media analysis essay + 1 long paper + 1 in-class essay for final. Before every class, we have to read articles or books/watch movies/do pre-lecture quizzes, not hard but unnecessary work. Don't take her if you want an easy A to fulfill college requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor, clearly cares about the content. Clear feedback and clear criteria to get an A. Definitely would take her again.

Dont be fooled by the old ratings. New syllabus now. 3 tests and 1 paper. Work is manageable but unnecessary - she will assign 4 hr long movies/readings per week. Most of class is discussion, but frankly, most students arent knowledgeable enough to provide anything too insightful. Barely teaches. If you want to use your time wisely, dont take her.

Great Professor, an excellent choice. The curriculum itself is a good amount of work, but that is standard for a global cultures class. Prof. Thorpe knows how to engage students, and her genuine kindness makes class dialogue nuanced and inclusive. Exams are take-home. Highly recommend.

It is very clear that Prof Thorpe cares about the well-being of her students. She is amazing at giving constructive feedback that helps students succeed. She is one of the sweetest people I have met at NYU and just seems like one of those people you can have a nice conversation with. She never stops smiling and radiates positivity. TAKE HER!!!!!!!
Prof.Thorpe is so nice and caring. Best prof ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: A really good prof, she cares about the students and is very accommodating!! Content isn't too hard and she always breaks it down and has slides with exactly what you need to know. Also is very helpful with feedback and really just wanted everyone to succeed and grow.
she was super nice and her class was very accesible tbh
I love her so much. She's literally one of my favorite profs at NYU. You can tell she really cares about both what she's teaching and her students. I 1000% recommend.

She was the best. There is a bit of work in the class but it's manageable if you've ever taken any history or english AP's in high school. She genuinely grades very kindly and offers tons of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is genuinely kind, and interested in students' discussions. Her lectures are very clear and tell you exactly what you needed to get from the class readings, and they are exactly what you are tested on in the exams. There are two papers due in this class but you choose what you want to write about for both. Cannot recommend Prof. Thorpe enough!!
he just reads the slides during lectures but makes you do a 1-question quiz every lecture
he just reads slides during lectures but he makes you take a 1-question quiz every lecture

Very test heavy class, even specified that they were difficult on purpose. Seems nice but much more of a research professor than a teaching one as I was incredibly confused by the way he explained things even after taking AP Stats

He explicitly outlines in his syllabus that he will make the exams harder on purpose, but unfortunately he was the only professor available so I had to take his class. Quizzes every lecture and then a quiz every week in recitation, so 3 quizzes per week, and for some reason 3 coding assignments??? A miracle I got the grade that I got
Im pretty sure he curve your grade down. I got my final grade and by syllabus it just doesn't make sense.
run, trust me

He is such a chill professor & you NEED to go to his office hours, he is there to help. Also all his exams are similar to the practice exams he gives, so the class isn't as hard -- but it is test heavy. He is also very accesible to different learning styles. He has lecture videos, his own textbook, and slides.

He uses proofs a lot, and to be honest, I am just not smart enough to understand all these proofs. I wish he can just show us more examples instead of proofs. Also I feel like everything is unorganized, its hard to study for this course on your own. The curve is generous tho
Basically received no (actually only one, but out of over 15) grades back until two thirds through the semester. Friendly enough guy and heavily curves.

he's honestly not that bad like his exams are just like the practice exams that he gives and he gives you a good amount of practice before every exam, so the exams aren't actually too hard. his lectures are pretty good as well if you pay attention, but defo review notes after class. he's kinda rude sometimes tho

Really competent both in statistics and at teaching. Cares that we fully understand the material as opposed to mindlessly knowing formulas. Great guy. Responsive to emails and questions in class. Expected intro stats to be an easy A, but his course is not. I think other profs will give you an easier A for this course.
Chill guy. Solid lectures, however exams are very hard. You must understand the concepts in depth, do the practice questions, and understand every part of them. Curve is very generous.

The actual exam is totally different from the practice. The professor is not a bad guy, but you did better by a Stats genius who actually understands the concepts rather than just memorizing the formulas.
Easiest course i've ever had in NYU, best prof.

Lectures are not that helpful, the tests are intentionally set to be challenging. Post previous exams, but the solutions are likely to be wrong(all kinds of mistakes, incomplete, or just messed up). Just get rid of the original solution and use AI to double-check the solution while you do the practice.
Great prof! best prof since I came to NYU. Take his class if you want an easy A
Nice person, but hard test, HW and test are not matched, R assignment seems to be useless.
explains things so that they're difficult to understand and answer sheets wrong or incomplete
He was great, uploaded tons of resources to do well in the class, and was very organized. It was easy to follow lectures and exams closely reflected the practice problems and homework he gave.

He doesn't give answers for practice problem, and problem sets. His exam prep questions are not related to the lecture he gave. Awful teacher in general, attendance is mandatory, and he doesn't give full credit even if you get the attendance question wrong. Just a unprofessional person who cannot teach anything.
awful professor, give wrong answers to the sample exams.

Took Econometrics with him. Get ready to teach yourself everything. He's not a bad professor at teaching, but his course is set up so you learn only concepts in lecture and the exams are really tough applications. Overall its not difficult to do well, as long as you study the review he uploads before exams which are almost identical to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why people here hate him so much but he is a very nice guy. He gives a very generous curve for the Midterm. This is my first time writing a review so trust me he is nice.

Roeper makes this class way harder than it has to be. Exams look nothing like homework's or practice exams. Expect theory questions way above the difficulty level of the same class taught by other professors.

Took his public econ course last sem, was just checking RMP to see how other students felt about him. Decided to toss in my two cents, worst professor I've had so far in econ department. Hard to talk to outside of class, horrible class notes. Clearly more of a research prof as opposed to a "teaching prof". Definitely avoid!

Took Timmy last semester. One of the worst experiences I've ever had in undergrad, horrible teaching style, mistakes on slides, and no answer keys for any content during the semester. Please avoid this professor as it will be an insane amount of stress and difficulty.

I will say that 351 has been less transparent about answer keys and problem-solving than his other classes. That being said, when it comes to tests, he provides a copious amount of practice problems that closely mimic exam questions - exams are also graded pretty fairly

The material is interesting, but the professor is so tough. There are almost no solutions to assignments/exams and the ones provided usually contain mistakes. The recitation solves problems differently than the professor and everything is just a mess. I studied more for this class than any other class in my major and still have a failing grade.

Avoid this man at all costs, he seems like a nice guy but his grading. is completely awful. If you aren't naturally gifted at math run away, you won't get the help you need. Never responds to emails, TA teaches things differently. This course has been an absolute nightmare with him and a lot of friends of mine have dropped

I have never in my life had such a terrible and careless professor. He didn't post any answers to any practice exams or home works and would often times confuse himself in lecture and not know the answers to his own questions.I understand NYU is a research school and maybe hes a good one but hes is not a good teacher and is affecting many students.

Hardest teacher I've ever had as an economics major. Doesn't post solutions for homework or exams. Lectures are confusing and pointless because the exams have nothing to do with what you learn in class. The slides contain errors as well. Dreading the final exam

Worst professor for teaching labor economics. Horribly lazy and complacent and he genuinely made this class horrid. Avoid at all costs this class will ruin your semester. Complaints include: no answer keys, hard to reach outside class, very difficult exam material, and general errors in slides and class information.
A nightmare, avoid at all costs

The worst professor at NYU. If I don't graduate this semester and have to take one more semester and stay in the US deferring my job offer he is the reason. This is not the same person as the one who had to defer his offer below. Professor Roeper breaks the lives of his students and he doesn't care.

Worst Professor in my life. The last weeks of material in Labor Econ are beyond the scope of an undergraduate economics major. None of the classes taken before prepares you for the horrors of this class. There are no answers to homework and practice questions for exams. The last weeks of lecture notes are extremely confusing and completely useless.

I was supposed to graduate early this semester and begin working but I've had to negotiate my offer (to less favorable terms) and take a 300-lvl elective next semester. Roeper is genuinely a horrible professor and this class felt harder than econometrics but more so due to his horrible lack of guidance and mediocre slides. Do not take w/ Roeper!!!!

Genuinely one of the most difficult professors I've had. He has a lackluster and ineffective teaching style where he leaves students more confused after every lecture. The slides contain errors and are a chaotic mess to understand. It is extremely disheartening that we aren't left with the necessary material and help to succeed in this class.

Worst economics professor in my 4 years at NYU. Take any other 300-lvl econ professor than him. Worst experience ever and very unstructured class material and quite honestly it seems as if he is lazy towards teaching.

From the other reviews he seems to be an okay Econ UA-18 grader but for Labor Economics I had a horrible experience. Never gives answers to any HW, Practice Q, or P-set so it is incredibly difficult to learn plus his slides are filled with errors which furthers the difficulty. Passing numerous difficult Econ cores this remains the hardest thus far.

I was really hoping to have some positive things to say about him but he has made it very difficult for students to learn Labor Economics. He does not upload HW solutions, frequently makes mistakes on his lecture slides, and exams are insanely difficult. Recitations haven't been helping either. Avoid unless you are an innate genius

His policy of not handing out answer keys to midterms, practice questions, and problem sets is really problematic and makes it very difficult to learn the content. His slides are highly theoretical and rarely include answers to even the practice problems in class. Would heavily recommend against taking this professor.
Gentle pace while lecturing; really hopes that students succeed

I can't get over with the fact that he doesn't post the solution to neither the homework nor the practice exam. Like I understand the homework part cuz he wants us attend the recitation, but no solutions for practice midterms as well???
Absolutely the worst. Exams are so hard. His lectures are useless.
really good prof.
He is alright. His grading scheme is very reasonable and fair unlike most Econ professors. However, his teaching is a bit boring. But you can deal with it.

Very theoretical class while very practical tests. What I mean is the prof likes to teach things by 'proving' them, but then gives little guidance on how to use these 'proved' concepts to solve test-problems. Fair grader and wants students to be successful but can be frustrating when trying to learn concepts with videos, as lectures are review.

He is undoubtedly a responsible teacher and I'm sure you'll learn a lot of stuff, but some of the curveball question in his exam makes me wonder whether am I destined to be a low-IQ person in this life.

He is a fair choice for econometrics. Make sure you understand everything on his slides. 90% of your grade depends on the three exams. He follows the econ department curve but in a more lenient way, so there is nothing you should complain about your grade.

Logic is clear during lectures but his handwriting is just terrible and he gave out the printed notes after 2/3 of the semester has already passed. Tests are hard and consist of 90% of the overall grade, with an average around the pass/fail line before curve.
Tough tests. Lectures are pretty average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good test indicates how well the student grasp and understand the knowledge. A bad test does the opposite to a good student who has been working hard. Be ready to be surprised.

Spring 2022. Tim's handwriting is absolutely unbearable, and lectures can go off tangent from time to time. Exams are okay, but it comes with curveballs. Overall a pretty standard professor. Note: linear algebra is not actually required for this class, only mentioned in lecture, but never showed up in neither homework nor exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy! He made econometrics easy and understandable
Studied so hard for his class this semester, but I ended up dropping it. The exams were SO difficult. Tests have nothing to do with practice exam and homework.

Lectures are hard to follow, mostly example-based with very few definitions for students to first understand the concept. 
Disorganized, posted his typed lecture notes when we were 2/3 of the semester in. 
Difficult exams. His curve is only good because otherwise half of the class would fail. 
Avoid at all costs.
RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a free A class. You can get an A by showing up to every class. Exams are very easy and can be done in 20 minutes. Not hard to get 100,100,100 on Midterm 1,2 and Final.
nice guy but exams are impossible which is what makes most of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took him in spring 2020. Absolutely terrible experience. He goes on tangents during lectures and recitations serve more as an R tutorial than for the overall content of the class. His tests were ridiculously hard and organized. Study material was nothing at all like the midterms and final and curves are heavy.

Not as bad of a lecturer as the reviews suggest, he's very patient to go over concepts and give a lot of help during office hours. The homework and exams are difficult, but he makes sure to give a lot of resources that are very helpful in preparing for the exams. Big curve if you don't do well.

Professor Roeper explains everything really clear with multiple examples. His exams can be hard. But if you can work out all the problems in his practice exam questions, he will also do well in his exams. RECOMMEND HIM!!!

I had Roeper for both AnaStats and Metrics. Can't speak for his past or other students' experience, but he is the clearest lecturer I have ever had in college. The workload is decent but not overwhelming. The only thing I hope he can improve on is responding to email in time. But other than that, he gives us all sorts of exam prep materials. Nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He never grades or responds to concerns on time. It is incredibly frustrating to have to contact your professor before finals and have them not respond. He is also incredibly confusing and vague when explaining course concepts. Do not take his class, try to get anyone else.
Very caring prof, despite sometimes being able to confuse himself slightly, takes a lot of time to address questions each time. makes econometrics as pain-free as can be

Very clear and responsible lecturer. Take no sick days. His statistics is perhaps more challenging than his Econometrics, but the former's workload is still reasonableabout 12 hours outside of class per week including reviews. Not too much homework, but extra practice problems and solutions are always available before exam. Highly recommended.

his exam is awful and so anxiety inducing. he only gives u 20 mins per question and then docs one point per late minute for each question, so you can never go back and fix problems earlier on. the course content is so confusing and this unforgiving format just makes it harder. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Took it fall sem. but withdrew bc it was so hard (flipped class so we had to learn the material alone). Taking it again this sem. and can say confidently that he's gotten much better. He still gives us slides/vids to prepare for class but his lectures go at a good pace, always down to answer questions, and also started giving concrete examples

He's pretty nice and he's considerable regarding students' understanding and levels. But his explanations are so abstract, and I understand he always asks whether we have questions, but we are put in a situation where we don't even know what we don't know. Hope he gets better because he is a nice guy.

I took his stats class at remote times. He had no homework but provided questions related to final grades in every class. You have to self-learn a lot based on the materials he provided. However, he made a lot of mistakes in these materials, even in the practice exams before midterms and the final. Also made mistakes in class. Think carefully.

I took AP stats and felt this class genuinely challenged me to learn the material in more depth, in a good way. He's also really helpful and caring in office hours. However, I will say it's not an easy class. The exams were difficult, but I appreciated them because it wards off large-scale cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Didnt explain a single thing covered on exams and purposefully complicates easy concepts because he just cant teach. The good reviews are clearly written by him and he 100% reports the bad ones. Get ready to teach yourself everything & enjoy trying to decipher his answer keys bc he doesnt show his work. Asst profs shouldnt be teaching req courses

The final grade is mainly graded by midterms and final. He is a fair grader in general, with lenient curves, but I don't think he explain things explicitly during lecture videos this semester. You have to learn by yourself to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kind of a tough cookie. Either it's his teaching style or the way the class is structured, but a lot of students found it difficult to do well under his flipped classroom strategy, and time cooker exam structure. If I had another option I would have taken it. Honestly - you'll just have to bite the bullet and try extra hard to do ok in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Roeper's class is challenging but mainly because of the content. He is a good professor and his interest in student's learning is evident. His lectures are clear, concise and he provides an incredible amount of resources. Though the class requires much effort, there's nothing to complain about Prof. Roeper. Would take again.

He's super nice, will answer all your questions, and he's a fair grader. The way he does class online right now is that he makes you do lectures before class (like 20min videos or less usually) and then live in class you can ask a bunch of questions and you solve 2 or 3 problems on a Google form and that's what counts as attendance. He's good.
Good choice

Good guy but hard to pay attention in class for me personally, and online classes halfway made that even worse. He is accessible outside class and homeworks are decent, and he curves very generously. If you don't pay attention in class, be consistent with self studying outside class otherwise you'll have a lot to catch up on near the exams

Took econometrics with him. He cares about his students and replies emails really fast. He's willing to discuss materials outside of class with you. Assignments per week and R is used, but not really hard. Tests are fair, usually with some tricky questions, but the TAs grade generously and he curves greatly. In general, a solid choice.

IDK why ratings are low, he's a decent prof. Never taken stats before, but he teaches it well IMO. I got shellacked on the 2nd midterm but thats b/c I chocked. Exams are hard but curved. Homework's not hard and mostly graded for completion. He's very accessible. I think I was unqualified for analytical stats but doing OK. Don't be afraid of R code!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not very good at explaining things, I've had multiple stats professors throughout my life and he's definitely the worst. Material is introduced in a much more convoluted way than necessary, makes way more sense after someone else explains it. Hard tests but they're curved pretty fat.
Statistics is hard, point-blank. Second time around taking a statistics class and he was a hell of a lot better than my first professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures are horrible because he explains concepts very abstractly with few examples. The homework is ridiculously hard, not only because of the nearly impossible problems he gives us, but because he includes R code, which he never covers in class and basically tells us to figure it out by ourselves. Tests are hard, but curved. Avoid
He is GOAT prof in this university. Once you take his class you will know what I am saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good Class
Just do not take his class, lectures are useless and you will be even more confused. You basically have to go over the notes yourself anyways. He also gives hard tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I got 5 in AP Stat. Despite that, his lecture even confuses me sometimes. AVOID him if you don't have experience in stat. His lecture moves fast and gives few examples to reinforce understanding. Poorly structured lecture notes: throwing bunch of things to you without any explanation. If you are new to stat, be prepared to read textbook on your own

Timothy Roeper is a terrible stats professor. He moves very quickly through the material and has weekly hw assignments that take hours to finish. This is mainly because he includes R studio (coding). He also does not spend any lecture time going over R as it is "a waste of lecture time", but continues to assign it and includes it in his tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty hard to follow along and the class lacks examples that create a strong base understanding. Roeper's office hours are useful but there is rarely an opportunity to clear up a lot of confusion that is created in his lectures. For those that have little to no experience in stats, this class is unnecessarily challenging.

Attending lectures is pointless. You will learn nothing. For those of you who have taken AP Stats in the past, this class is a waste of time. You have learned all of this information before, however it is presented and tested in a terrible way. The homework & tests are written poorly & you will be marked as a fool if you ask any questions in class.

Guys I AM SERIOUS. I STAYED FAITHFUL TO THE PROFESSOR AND TOOK HIS CLASS AGAIN THIS SEMESTER!!!! THIS IS 100% reliable, listen to me. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR AT ANY COST!!!! MY FAILURE IN THE PAST TWO SEMESTERS OF TAKING HIS STATS AND ECONOMETRICS HAS PROVED HE CANNOT TEACH. FUZZY NOTES AND HARD PROBLEMSET CANNOT PREP FOR EXAMS

I'm not really sure why Prof. Roeper has any bad reviews, most people in my class really like him. The material is sorta tough but if you put the work in and go to his office hours I think you can do well! he's a v approachable dude, definitely can help you out if you're struggling

Yes, econometrics is kinda tough, and math-heavy classes in econ are never easy, but Prof. Roeper does everything he can to make sure his students understand what's going on. He's a good lecturer, the content is clear and interesting, and he's very accessible at office hours. Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: VERY lenient grader. Tests are very hard, but curved. His lectures are highly theoretical, so if you known nothing about Statistics, it will be difficult to pass.

This class is 90% AP stats, but the econ department still requires it. Love the prof though he's not always clear in lecture, but he really is approachable during office hours. A fair grader (homeworks are hard but graded for completion), and generally pretty chill.
Great Prof, wants you to understand the material, will work with you if you put in the effort
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Listen in class and you will be fine. His exams are relatively easy
HWs answers are given by TAs. Exams are relatively easy. Easiest class in NYU econ major.
Nice teacher who takes pride in teaching his students. Go for his office hours to get the easy A

Looking back after comparing with other stats professors, his grades are extremely lenient. The average grade in this class is 20 points above other stats professors. I wouldn't have scored A- in stats if not for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's relatively new at teaching so he's not the best. That being said, the grade was mainly determined by 3 exams (and 9 HWs at 3 pts each which didn't really help much). You get to bring 1 notecard for each exam but the grading was pretty harsh and it's easy to do poorly. I would try to take it with someone else or take a different stats course.
The course was relatively easier than other professors' course. As long as you understand the basics, it is easy to score here.

Doesn't assign readings, doesn't assign homework problems for practices, doesn't prepare for lectures, read off slides and have students confused throughout the entire lecture for the whole semester. This was an essential class for me and unfortunately, because of how bad the professor was I am taking it again this semester. STAY AWAYYYYYY.

If you thought you were a klutz check again. The probability of this man being more clumsy than you is 100%. Looking for a teacher to nearly trip & fall every class, break a whiteboard, too weak to pull down the chalkboard & have a real rat present for your lecture this is the man. His clumsiness translates to his confusing & unorganized lectures.

The worst teacher I have ever had. The nature of the course should primarily be learning statistical formulas and learning how to apply them to draw conclusions. However, this man is incapable of even teaching a basic formula to the point where he will literally have lecture slides with incorrect formulas.

The professor's lectures just doesn' t make sense. I go to his office hours, TA's office hours, and attend group study sessions and my grade is still a low B. The subject is just too hard to have a professor who doesn't teach. The 5's seem really fishy because I talk to a number of students from the class and all seem to be troubled by this class.
I would definitely recommend him to anyone! His lectures are very clear and he is a great teacher!

Class slides contained many errors / incomplete examples, yet the prof only does a decent job going over the slides in lectures. This is a not a high level course in econ and the materials were fairly easy, but the way the prof teaches is making it more painful than it is supposed to be.
Great professor who makes the material clear and even Econometrics bearable! Would recommend to anyone!!
Came in with zero statistics knowledge and surprisingly still got a B+. A good teacher.

He seems to be confused about the topic and doesn't really know what he is doing. He writes his own test but usually procrastinates. Doesn't give proper review, lecture notes usually have a bunch of example questions but don't have any answers. When i am studying for this test, I am completely lost and hopeless,don't know how im gonna do on test

He's a very good professor. Explains the material very well and always tries to make sure everyone understands the material. The class isn't easy, but his PowerPoint slides are super organized and easy to follow. Considering he's teaching these classes for the first time at NYU, he is doing an awesome job.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lost a bet with my friend. He achieved full marks and I only obtained a mere 89%. His statistics class is probably the easiest among all the statistic professors.

DON'T TAKE HIM if u want to learn. He basically teaches his stats students what he teaches in Econometrics. Stats is supposed to be EASY but hardly anyone understands his lectures!!! Pbly a hard class even if u learned stats. Plus he is TERRIBLE at explaining&has an overwhelming amount of errors on his slides. The TA is better at teaching than him.

Reviews seem a little fishy - he's not horrible, but he's definitely not the best professor and tends to overcomplicate what should be basic stats concepts. Average for first midterm was pretty low at a 75%, which makes me wonder why everyone here says his class is so easy. I have friends in his econometrics class who are struggling too.

Good prof for grad school maybe, but unrealistic expectations for undergrad students taking a required course. Gets impatient easily with explaining things if you're not getting basic concepts. Hard to know if you're doing things correctly bc he doesn't give answer keys for the hw or practice problems (after submission). Take if you're smart.
Tests and HWs are easy.
Curve works in your favor if you know what you are doing.

Part of the required courses for an economics major and he is good at teaching statistics. Lectures are easy to follow and homework load is light. Exams are easy as long as you understand the homework.
A mandatory class for ECONs major. Easy stats.
As an art student, it is an easy A. Shows how easy stats are.
Easy A for the class. As long as you listen attentively, you will get an A. Very lenient professor. What a gem to have.

Bad instructor for Stats but unsure about the other class (Econometrics) he teaches. NOBODY understands his lectures to the point that lectures are about students asking him to clarify EVERYTHING cuz he basically reads off from slides. His explanations just make it even harder to understand... I learned stats from Calc and it's still extremely hard.

ESL students dedicate their lives to learn a totally different language from their mother tongue to communicate and learn from people in the U.S. However,  He does not show any appreciation for their effort as an "Ethic Professor". He ignores students with an accent, even saying he doesn't understand what they are saying, but that is not true!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His behavior toward students can be disrespectful. As an international student, I use my legal name, which is short and not hard to pronounce, but he refused to say it in class, skipped over me when calling on students, and said that I should adopt an English name instead. This is super offensive and exclusive.

Closed-minded, procedural, and slow. Class was unbearable at times due to how much of a waste of time it all was. He speaks at 0.5x speed and does not have much to provide beyond the assigned readings. Took Ethics and Political Philosophy and on first day he said we would not cover any political philosophy. Please avoid.

Some love Prof. Unger and some... find him difficult. I'm in the former group.  He and his classes are certainly out of the ordinary, there's never a syllabus, any clear grading criteria, or clear deadlines. I don't care about that stuff, I came to NYU to learn from the best philosophy professors and with Prof. Unger I was doing that.

His zoom lectures consist of him on his bed ranting out stuff that makes zero sense. When you try to talk ethics to him, he tells you not to talk technical. All his philosophical assumptions are based on thin air. Take this course if you're curious how tenured profs can get away w their bs.

1) If you take yourself too seriously & want to debate him when you know nothing, don't take his class. He isn't going to put up with your crap 2) If you are serious about philosophy, take him at least once 3) If you want to learn & be provoked and aren't focused on grades, take him often. He's amazing & behind the gruffness he is a nice guy

I graduated years ago from Professor Unger's class. With the world coming to ruins, I'm now sure he was correct about a few important things - namely, our utter selfishness and self-absorption that is leading to the destruction of our world. Too bad he can't teach POTUS on some ethical understandings

Avoid. Has a huge ego and won't take what you have to say seriously; it's like talking to a child (he argued that it isn't possible to manipulate the transplant system even if you are wealthy). I work in transplantation and he still wouldn't hear me out. Most definitely will not help you grow. Brilliant? Eh sure in some ways, but mostly obnoxious.

I actually liked the class, and found some of his ideas actually interesting on the subject of human identity. But his penchant for vivasection in every example from meta-physics to ethics is noisome. and his ethical arguments and positions are puerile-- group think and tenure are the only reason he can spout them in any respected circles.

Stubborn and arrogant but also intelligent and friendly. He likes to talk a lot, though if you want to say something, he will listen and try to understand you (though it will probably involve multiple interruptions of him correcting something you've said by modification). Excellent at teaching students to be simple, precise, and clear.
Smart but avoid him.
Stubborn, yes -- arrogant, no. Amazing professor for "mature" students, indeed.

This is man is very brilliant, and very stubborn. He will argue a point with a student until he wins. It is an entertaining class. He teaches with his feet kicked up on his desk, and doesnt hesitate to close his eyes for long periods of time while lecturing. 3 Essays + participation in recitation. I am really glad i took this class, I recommend it.

Peter Unger is clearly an excentric man. But this of course comes with the territory of absolute geniuses. To suggest that he is full of himself is absurd, he is merely very passionate about philosophy and incredibly stubborn..Probably best to have some familarity with philosophy before you take any of his classes.
One of the best, most stimulating lecturers i've ever had. Totally nuts. Totally brilliant. The most under rated philosopher working today

Professor Unger is the most forthright and stimulating professor I've had.  Many students can't deal with his honesty, but talking with him is a breath of fresh air for mature students.  The class was amazing, and office hours with Unger were always a delight.  Take him if you are interested in the material and prefer to be treated like an adult.

Really quite full of himself, and highly doubt he gives all the money that he could to charity (as he says everyone should in his class) his colleague nagel and singer are just as intellegent and dont place themselves on pedestals.

Although I remember absolutely nothing as far as the material goes, I have more memories of this class than any other at NYU.  Like the time unger sneezed and his "capillaries burst" and he taught the remainder of the class with a severe noseblee

Who is this guy kidding?  This is one of the most pompous professors I've ever had.  His book, "Living High and Letting Die", cloaked as something new to the field of ethics, is really just a weak attempt at modern utilitarianism.  If you take his class, get ready not to learn about ethics, but to buy his book and hear him talk about himself.
Though garrulous at times, Unger is a powerful ethics teacher who changed the way I view my behavior and charity. Read his book "Living High and Letting Die" for some powerful ethical arguments.
Funny, honest, self-deprecating.  If you have the right combination of people in your class, he's just amazing.
Perhaps the most obnoxious individual to ever walk the earth.

ILRID 2510, explains diversity/discrimination but in a very scientific phycological way which I found very interesting. Less about personal experience more about how you're brain functions. Usman himself was very very generous, constantly bumping up the grades. Also very knowledgeable on the subject matter and was enthusiastic about class!

Had professor Liaquat on his first semester at Cornell for ILRID2500 and he absolutely killed it. Great slides, great lectures, fun readings, know when to assign long vs short readings. Take home quizzes that were perfectly reasonable. Has great character and charisma and is truly interested in what he teaches. Cannot recommend his class enough!

Prof. Liaquat was great. His lectures were super interesting, and he made the content fun to learn about. Lecture heavy, a few quizzes, midterm and final. The class went really fast, so you had to stay on top of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best profs I've ever had! Managed to make 3hr lectures super engaging. Cares about students' learning over grades, generous w extra cred. Talented presenter, you'll understand even the most complex things with his teaching/explanations. Incredibly kind person/great lectures. Enough work to make you study, but not enough to stress.

I had Usman for summer session one. He is super kind & compassionate. Always thinking about how to really help his students and make their lives better. He did his best every class to make the lectures engaging and was honestly a great guy. I learned a lot and I'm happy I had him as a professor because he truly does care. The class wasn't too hard!
Such a great professor! He is very accomodating to different kinds of students and will help you as best as he can if you just talk to him. Highly recommend!
Excellent Professor

An Easy A Core Class. Do not be intimidated by the course name! The reading was minimal (if not enjoyable and informative)-15-30 pgs PER WEEK. The lectures were extremely entertaining, and he often ended early, which was nice. The prof is super chill, funny, knowledgeable, and accesible.There's lots of American history, if you like that, too.

Before you met him, Prof Baer at first appear to be a overtly liberal professor. Once you met him, you realize he is just a very kind, intelligent person. Eventually, you will realize his ideas actually make sense. His class contributes to a significant change of my view on the interaction between cultures. Strongly recommended for personal growth.
He really cares about people learning thinking skills rather than the textbook stuff. Pretty good professor and his classes are a lot of fun.
Great professor.

Professor Baer is an excellent professor. He is very inspirational and knowledgeable. He really cares for students and he replies to emails very quickly. The class includes primarily group projects instead of personal work, leading you to build a global mindset with in-class discussions and field trips in New York City. Strongly recommend!!!

Had trouble focusing because of my massive crush on him. Discussion heavy with interesting questions and insightful comments. Gets sidetracked & the conversations aren't very structured but no one minds. A lot of reading and talking about reading but it's more conceptual than anything else. He's great & an easy grader!

We would leave every class with a million questions on our minds, confused, and thinking. But all these are very good things. The class is designed to make you think, question what you think you know, and have a more nuanced understanding of many different topics. And Prof Baer is exactly the right person for it.

My opinions and views differed a lot from Prof Baer's, but it surprisingly did not affect my final grade at all. His Expressive Culture was not heavy-lifting, but we had a lot of great and productive conversations. It really helped me to become a better and more thoughtful person. Great Core class if you are into literature.

easily the best professor i've had at nyu. really intelligent and really encourages you to think outside of the box. also really understanding of the covid learning circumstances. great class overall, you won't regret taking it!

For an Expressive Culture class, this was surprisingly interesting. Baer introduces lots of intriguing discussions, and analysis on the texts (which are all very short) leave you thinking. For the essays, Baer lets you rewrite after he comments because he cares less about giving bad grades and more about your improvement as a writer. He's great!
one of the greatest classes i've taken at nyu.

Amazing professor. Very interesting person and extremely interesting lectures. Engages with the class and takes time to get to know the students. Provides plenty of opportunities for his students in and out of the class. Sometimes a little unclear on the assignments, but if you're focused and structured and willing to learn, you should get an A.

One of the best instructors I have every had. Most inspirational and helpful teacher. Class is a bit disorganized, but trust everything will work out. You will get so much out of the class if you put some effort in.
He's obviously extremely smart and knows what he's talking about. Although, sometimes the structure of the class is a bit unclear. I enjoy listening to what he has to say.
Interesting and Intelligent
No Comments
No Comments
He's ridiculously sexy, and a fascinating man.
No Comments
Friendly, brilliant, and articulate.  His class has been tough, but terrifically rewarding.  Look for him for German or Comp. Lit.

Zach completely changed how I think about learning. He's so supportive and really wants us to develop our own ideas, which sounds really basic but is surprisingly rare. His class is a place where I always felt comfortable working through my work even when it wasn't finished or polished. Genuinely thoughtful feedback. Also very funny.

Took WTE second semester with Udko. Lowkey unsettling. Likes to make himself seem really cool by showing us all his connections to famous people and then having us read about them. Wasn't a fan of that at 9 in the morning. Has generally good feedback but doesn't trust students
Challenging and eye-opening. I had a great time. He is very direct and firm but ultimately a nice professor.
He obviously has favorites and ridicules students in front of everyone.

Zach's humor made the class really enjoyable and I think he values connecting with his students. I always appreciated his feedback and how much he helped me (in both courses) and he continues to be one of the best professors I had the privilege of taking.
Zach's class is challenging but rewarding. He pushes you to grow as a thinker, while being understanding and caring. Unstuck ai is a great study tool alongside the free course materials.
Super clear and entertaining. He can be very direct in his feedback, which pushed me to do better. No BS, but it's always coming from a place of kindness and motivation. One of the best.

Zach makes it really fun because he knows how to work the room. I really enjoyed coming to class everyday. Our group really bonded and got to know each other. We worked together, had lively conversations, great experience.
This was easily the best experience I've ever had in a classroom setting. Zach is super understanding and such an amazing teacher. I cannot recommend his class enough!!!

Zach has the rare ability to provide feedback that hits directly at the crux of an issue without being overly critical or humiliating. Each point made about my work has allowed to improve it, rather than discourage my confidence, and I'm really glad I had him as a professor for two semesters.
Not very helpful when confused about assignments. Felt passive aggresive

Zach is an AMAZING professor! He can be a little tough sometimes, but he really means well and you will see tremendous growth as a reader, writer, and critical thinker. I had him for both semesters last year and still think about his class.

Really great course. Zach is warm and welcoming but not afraid to push you to get your best work out of you. I felt that even though I had to work a lot outside of class that I grew a lot from this class. The material is always intellectually stimulating, and he puts a lot of thought into each session.

Professor Udko has a very endearing personality. He is very encouraging and is willing to take time to help all students. The discussions about film and psychology were so great in expanding my knowledge. Very nice guy.
he has high expectations but he is really nice guy. smart and fun. one of the best profs i had.

Studying under Professor Udko is the most enriching experience you could ask for. Professor Udko is punctual, truly talented, an incredible lecturer, and just a wonderfully constructive teacher. I enjoyed every minute of every class and have never seen my writing at the level it is at now. I owe this all to the direction of Professor Udko.

he is low key the worst. He made my roommate cry. He singled her out and critiqued her work in front of the class. He is extremely judgemental and not at all empathetic. I dont recommend having him as a teacher.

Lots of homework. But Zach has a clear love of film and implements a lot of it into his class. He's also great on extensions (as long as you don't ask last minute) and worries and cares about his students' health. Very lax on laptops/cellular devices. One of the best teachers/professors I've ever had and shows lots of respect to his students.
Very knowledgeable of the subject, gives truthful and helpful feedback, very organized, good communicator, wants us to all do well, and willing to let students think deeper. Great professor!

Zach Udko is one of my favorite professors ever. He is so kind and understanding but also has the most engaging class. I really respect him as a person and teacher, and he cares about his students so much. His assignments are very engaging, and you actually learn from them. I highly recommend taking his class.

He really cares about his students and gave us freedom to choose projects we were passionate about. He does a great job at finding the smallest, most specific detail we need to tweak as well as helping to guide us in a better direction overall. Totally efficient, supportive, and understanding (which is hard to find in most profs).

I really didn't like Professor Udko's course. He puts effort into his classes but he's judgemental and perfectionistic. He'll tell you that your essay is ok and then absolutely destroy it in his grading comments. Get ready to be called out in class and receive passive-aggressive comments. Also insane homework load.

It takes a certain kind of person to enjoy his class. He's kind of super judgy/rude sometimes. Definitely picks favorites (aka the ppl that wrote good comments on this) and disses everyone else (grade-wise too). Also forces his own opinions on the class.

Zach's class was the one place on campus that I felt the most seen, heard, safe, and inspired during this difficult year. He provided the hope, motivation, and academic framework that I desperately needed. As a multiracial, queer, nonbinary person of color, I could always feel Zach's encouragement and I know it will resonate for years to come.

Get ready for work every class. They will include a lot films that you may or may not be interested in and more. Also a journal for each film that has to be a full page single spaced. He was disrespectful to me and another student and does not respect privicy of other students personal business. Do not question his class or it will go downhill.

Professor is super knowledgeable about psychology and art. He was very able to share what he thought would be exciting materials to further explore. He was very helpful in the research process and encouraged us to tackle topics that didn't lead to simple answers, but more questions. And he has a way of creating an enjoyable classroom energy.

My closest friends at NYU I have gained through this class, which I will be forever grateful for. Furthermore, Zach completely took control of the medium making it oftentimes much more engaging and fun that an actual in-person course I was taking part in. Zach was able to smash through the barrier of our screens and genuinely stimulate us to learn.

Professor Udko always helped me push past barriers I was encountering in my writing. He always knew how to prompt new ideas out of me and gave me practical steps to achieve my goals. I always enjoyed the energy and the environment the class created.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: His feedback was incredibly useful, as it seemed to pinpoint the exact problems I was experiencing when writing my drafts. It was very personalized and, therefore, very helpful. The open-ended nature of the feedback allowed it to still guide me without trapping me in a box, without forcing me into a specific argument. He's excellent!

This was my favorite class of the year. Professor Udko creates a warm, authentic, fun and still intense learning atmosphere. Not a single class felt wasted, and each case-study was so well-constructed. He shows a ton of videos, films, music, and art that is connected to the main objective in each unit, as well as to my work in my other classes.

His guidance and openness to discussion was very helpful, and he definitely motivated and pushed me to want to continue my work and realize my full potential. It feels like he genuinely cares, which is always helpful and motivating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very no nonsense, will like you if you work hard and show your interest in the class.

He is a very good teacher and gives great feedback, and you will definitely learn a lot from him and leave with an improved style of writing. As mentioned in previous comments, he knows exactly what he wants you to write about and will make sure to push you, very heavily, in that direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The discussions we had in class were some of the best I've ever experienced in a class setting. Zach is fantastic at creating an environment that is conducive to truly opening up a meaningful conversation, and the in-class examples and supplements he showed always incited strong reactions. A wonderful professor who truly cares.
Always seems to have a specific idea of what you should be writing about and tries to corner you into that. Very friendly guy and usually opens good discussions. Tends to go over time.

Zach is really good at connecting with students and motivating them. He also is very organized, prepared, and is very good at teaching lessons. He is very engaging and supportive when it comes to all the different parts of writing. Any time I was struggling or needed clarification I was always comfortable asking for help.

Zach is always incredibly clear about what works in an essay and what doesn't. He gives great feedback and doesn't hold back. The more debate style discussions were incredibly helpful and gave the entire class a chance to voice their opinions of works of art we were studying, leading to some of be best conversations I've had in classes here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I've had Zach for two semesters now, and during each he has been accused by students of forcing his opinions on the class. His lectures are interesting, but he never really gives you comments on your essays until after grading your final draft. Suddenly then your essay will have been a mess the whole time and he can't believe you couldn't see that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Writing the essay. One of the best professors I've every had. Great classroom discussions, brought in tons of amazing articles, videos, etc. to analyze. Helped me transform my writing into something much better. Zach is truly memorable and amazing. DO NOT BE LATE. Lots of dry humor

Zach is a great teacher. His friendly personality made it easy to participate. I was never afraid to fail in Zach's class because I knew I would not be judged and that I would learn something from it. I think the class was challenging, but it made me work harder.
The instructor was really good at creating an open and accepting environment. I always felt supported by him and my peers which allowed me to take more risks in my work.
kind, funny, & supportive. i recommend him highly
Hands down one of the best classes I took last year. I'm now a psychology minor because of Zach. Very inspiring and eye-opening.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Zach inspires you to be the best possible writer, always offering helpful suggestions and rooting for you along the way.  Hes also kind, understanding, and funny and bc of him, I was able to step outside of my comfort zone.

Zach is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He is a formidable intellectual and hilarious which makes the class both enriching and fun. It is also one of the most challenging classes I've ever taken and with that, one of the most rewarding. Highly recommend if you want to push yourself and grow.

Zach is engaging, passionate about the subject, hilarious, and never allows us to slack off. These strengths are what makes this class such a wonderful experience. I felt both supported and challenged during both semesters, and the classroom environment is so much fun to be a part of!

He truly cares about his students and is always prepared to reassess his teaching methods if he feels they are not as helpful as they could be. His class has inspired me as a writer, artist, and person and I am so grateful to have spent this year with him!

I always appreciated that Zach set aside time for every single student to privately meet with him. I felt that he knew what areas I was struggling with right away and was not afraid to offer advice on how to fix it. Zach always pushed us to go out and solve our own problems, but he was always there to make sure we stayed on track.
So nice and smart. If you come to class every day, you'll do very well. He wants everyone to succeed and improve---and is there to help you and challenge you. One of the best.

He's a pretty cool teacher. You can tell that he cares about what he does; at times he takes it too seriously.  Don't bother being late or missing class even once; he will actually feel some type of way. He is great at explaining essay topics and what he looks for in essays. Just listen and do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He helped me understand that there are multiple dimensions to every piece of art. Nothing is as simple as we perceive it to be. It was my favorite class at Tisch this year, and he made me so excited to write about every essay. It is a wonderful class.

Great professor. challenging, but always interesting, and he actually cares that you grow as a writer and thinker. definitely take his course. especially if you are interested in film, sexuality, and psychology. Easily the best class I had freshman year.

He always kept the material fresh and interesting, which I appreciated. Loved all the lessons about Nina Simone, Kanye West, Woody Allen, Chelsea Handler, and Steve McQueen. Discussing issues related to diversity is something that matters to Professor Udko, and he doesn't shy away from having difficult conversations.
Great teacher. The best Writing the Essay teacher. He's really good with class discussions and I feel like I learned so much about the world through this class. TAKE ZACH. He is the best.
Zach is fab. You'll learn a ton and I loved the class.
Extremely generous and kind. Ended up with an A- (not sure I deserved it). His bark is bigger than his bite and he challenged me constantly to improve.
Zac is always interesting and generous with his feedback.
Cared about my progress and pushed me harder more than any other teacher I ever had.

Zach has very specific and very unclear expectations. He is unkind, difficult to work with and stuck in his views. He would often ask impossible questions, reject all of our answers and then proceed to deliver a response that he would have rejected had we said it. He has stunted me as a writer and made me insecure about my work. Do not recommend.
My favorite class. Taking him for "World through art" next semester.
Hard grader but dope person.
He likes to humiliate his students individually in front of the class. Be ready for an emotional roller coaster.

Zach will put in the work for you if you put in the work for him. My writing improved vastly over the course of the semester and he made what could easily be a dreadful course engaging and meaningful.
He is one of the most influential teachers I have ever had. He changed the way I think of both my writing and myself. Zach really cared and it made all the difference.

My personal experience was phenomenal. I was challenged more than any other class; and, frankly, I was satisfied more than any other class. Zach has helped me hone my writing skills, and his class has helped me grow as a person via a large number of mental breakdowns and severe existential art/essay-related crises.

Zach was incredibly charismatic and engaging and I was always alert and excited to be in class. Overall, I have learned so much from his class. His unique teaching style made assignments and discussions engaging and useful. I enjoyed the class and I am walking away with a lot in my pocket. I have recommended him to many other students.

Zach is awesome. He is very interesting and clearly cares about not only his students but also the material. If I had to do the semester over again, I would pick Zach as my professor in a heart beat. He made the material more interesting and relatable - even making it seem more relevant to our majors and careers.
smart, tough, no-nonsense, challenging, entertaining. Go for it.

Really enjoying this class. I've never had the opportunity to spend half a semester studying one artist, and Zach's lessons and discussions about Woody Allen have been highly informative, enjoyable, and thought-provoking.
He's a good professor but lacks a bit of clarity. He gives good constructive criticism that really helps you become a better writer.

Udko is possibly the most dedicated Prof I had last year. He is tough, but fair and patient, funny, but sometimes brutal. I grew a lot as a writer in his class. One thing, though, is that he is really obsessed with having perfect attendance. He sees right through any excuse.

He doesn't know the difference between criticism and constructive criticism which for a teacher is important! He picks favorites. However, I did like that he didn't teach by the book. He made a sucky class a tad bit better. I wouldn't take him again but if you get him you will survive.
Professor Udko explains everything so clearly and makes Writing fun, which is usually my least favorite subject. Definitely a stand out teacher at New York University.
Awesome. Will make you a better writer.

I found Zack to be very helpful and looked forward to his class. He's not the easiest prof (I got an A-), but if you show up to every class and do the work, you'll do fine. Be prepared for a heavy dosage of sex and insanity (his two favorite topics), Camille Paglia, Darren Aronofsky, Paul Verhoeven, Woody Allen, and electro music.
Very Difficult to Please. CHOOSES FAVORITES IN CLASS. IMPOSSIBLE TO GET AN "A"
Zack tries his best to make this class enjoyable for his students. He doesn't always succeed, but from what I can tell, it doesn't get much better than this.

You have to write for what Zach wants. Which is never clear. His opinions are biased- and is never helpful. Will always refer you to the book for simplest of questions. Heard him embarrass a girl in class saying "That was the worst essay I've ever read." "You're a lot smarter than that." Find someone else for this horrid course.

Zack is a highly knowledgeable professor, but he certainly asks a lot from his students.  The words he continually uses to describe students writing (except for those that quickly become his elite favorites) are generic, cliche, bland, unoriginal, and boring.  I found it a struggle to compromise my own writing and write only for Zack.

OH. MY. GOD.  I had Professor Stalla last semester and enjoyed her class, mostly because of the individual attention she gave each of us--but Professor Udko rocks.  He offers up to four conferences (two for each essay) if we need the help--now that's dedication.  Definitely take his class.
Very very demanding, but ultimately a fair prof.
loved him! so yummy. fun fun fun. better writer now for it actually
Stylish, urbane, sassy, and SMART. Lots of lively discussions and creative assignments. And while he's challenging, Zach helps you every step of the way to meet his high standards.
ammmmaaaaazzzzziiiingggg!!!! take this class take this class take this class!!!!!!!
omg amazing class. great professor. so much fun. acutally piques your interest in the subject matter!!
Always finds a way to keep the class interesting.

Zach is a great teacher. He goes out of his way to try and make class inetersting and fun. He presses his students to think about the art and how we view it in new and interesting ways. The class is hard as hell no matter who you have, but having a teacher who really cares about each student makes it much better.
Probably as good as it gets for this class. I will miss him next semester.

Zach probably isn't the best WTE teacher, but he's certainly entertaining and you could do much worse. He's a hard grader, but if you put effort into your writing and follow his suggestions you will do fine. WTE isn't particularly fun no matter what, but Zach somehow makes it relatively bearable. Never a dull moment in class: PRACATAN!

If you're a hard worker, you will be rewarded and Zach will go out of his way to help you. I appreciate Zach's dedication to creating an entertaining (while at the same time, intense) classroom environment.
I would study the phonebook from Zach if I could. I wish I could take another class from him.

He's not one to accept mediocrity. He's clearly a talented and hilarious man. And I always enjoyed going to class---always entertaining. At the beginning of the semester, I struggled becuase I was handing in **** and I knew it. I ended up with an A in the course, and can safely say he's one of the best professors I had this year.

At first he appears like a really cool teacher that will make WTE fun, but eventually you will see that he is extremely opinionated, negatively critical, and almost impossible to please. He does praise some students' work, but for the most part not only is most work not good enough for him, but he does little to help you reach his standards.
Zach is very opinionated and committed to his style.  Write in his style and you'll get a good grade.  If you don't, best of luck to you.
I have never laughed and learned so much in a class. He assigns a ton of work, but what's not to love? Pracatan!
he's pretty rough. funny exterior but full of spite. it's near impossible to comprehend what he's looking for in one's writing.

What a character. This class is typically the bane of people's existance, but I loved it. He pretty much said "screw the syllabus" and did his own damn thing, which is awesome. It can be hard to find what he wants, and if you don't...sucks for you. All in all, he's awesome. If you put in the effort, you'll get what you deserve.
Stylish, quirky."Showgirls" his favorite movie. Last semester, I dreaded the course. This semester I look forward to class. And he gives us candy too....

WTE is one of those classes that everyone complains about. I don't know about other instructors but I found Zach able to demystify the whole thing, while keeping everyone laughing along the way. If you want a professorial teacher stay away. But if you want a quirky, intelligent, and funny instructor hop aboard the "Pracatan" wagon!

Oh Zach.... an unforgettable teacher (no matter how hard you try). Clever, but not as clever as he thinks he is (same goes for talented, knowledgeable, and hot). I OD'ed on Woody Allen by the end, but I say take the class just for the experience.

I actually transfered into Zach's class from another WTE class that just didn't fit with my schedule. I ended up having him at 8 in the morning! He made that morning class pretty amazing. We were forced to listen to his indie music cranked all the way up and read poems every wednesday. Quirky to the extreme but totally worth while.
Not so into WTE...but it's required, and I'm sure there's no better teacher than Zach to help guide you through the progressions...

Zach can be obtuse about what he expects from you in terms of participating in the class and writing your essays but you're fine if you happen to hit on whatever obscure combination of insight and intelligence he's looking for. If you don't find it you're screwed. He's blunt, sometimes to the point of meanness, but in the end a fair grader.

Zach is an aquired taste. But once you develop a flavor for the rigorous insanity of this class (and his zany off-the-wall sense of humor), he'll make all your other teachers seem bland, predictable, and ugly.
Zach is a hilarious, fun, and actually made this class interesting for me...I can honestly say I got something out of this class.
awesome

Zach is a nice enough guy but this class in general is horrible. It's unclear what we are supposed to do and how we are supposed to get it done. And sometimes I feel he just wants us to entertain him.
amazing professor! honestly such a fun class. no complaints.

took fysem w him, rlly chill when it comes to discussions & flexible w projects/papers. the class is basically watching a movie per week & filling out a reflection so it doesnt take too much of ur time. theres 2 presentations, a midterm, and a final but all are easy to do well in. def one of the more interesting fysem classes so highly recommend

Professor Usher is so chill. He was the professor for First Year Seminar and the semester is literally you watching Spielberg films of various types and filling out a straight forward reflection for each. There were two essays and solo presentations as well. However, Professor Usher is incredibly understanding, and the semester was def memorable.

Professor Usher is an amazing professor. He is one of my favorites among all of my French professors. He is funny, nice, and humorous. He allows for extra credits and he gives the topics for papers at the beginning of the semester. It is not really a heavy load class though he gives one quiz every week; but they are not hard at all.
I love Professor Edgar. I wish he was going to be here for longer than just a year. I have loved his class and he is a fantastic person and teacher. I cannot wait to take him next semester!
He's awesome!!
Edgar is the best Spanish professor ever. He makes class so fun and enjoyable. He's easily accessible outside of class and will help out in any way possible. Would take this class again!
One of the best professors I have taken. Take his class. Do your work and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Proffesor is very knowledgeable and gives you a real experience with the language. Shares much insight with spanish culture and makes class fun to attend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very engaged and understanding. Helps as much as possible and a great overall professor.
Teaches you how to really speak Spanish, very verbal class not just textbook work. Would highly recommend.
From Mexico and teaches you how to really speak the language!!! Not just straight form book. Real world
Her grammar and composition class is great.
Sarah Vaussier is the chill prof. she also has cool shoes. I will miss her class.

Sarah Vaussier is a real hoot! Light homework from workbook or packet for each class that we check as a class at the beginning of class. As long as you pay attention in class, ask questions if you're confused, and do the HW exercises you'll be fine.

She doesnt understand how to teach languages, or at least shes out of date. Homework every class, that she doesnt check, and doesnt have much thought put into it. Instructions are often unclear. She doesnt like technology, so prepare to use paper. She can be funny, but class isnt fun. There are cultural differences too. Not fully fluent in English.

She's a good and passionate professor, but she gives sooo much work and it takes up too much time from your other classes. She's also really strict about formatting, AI, and her grading contract. Honestly, if you don't like writing, don't take her class because you're gonna put in a lot of effort for no reason.

Professor Van Houten was a understanding and excellent professor. For the progressions we did, we were guided all the way through and given very thoughtful feedback. Make sure you participate in class and do the extra credit. This class is a Guaranteed B if you do all your work in time and Meet Expectations for everything.
Good professor for expos. There's a lot of build up to essays (with exercises) but she's nice and a pretty good professor. She gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She just talk nicely and give you the bad grade and also give you the bad conference time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you don't like writing, she can be a little hard to understand - she talks about a lot of theoretical/philosophical writing stuff. As long as you pretend to know what you're doing and occasionally participate, you'll be fine. Pay attention to the feedback she gives you and your essays will be great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She does give good exercises to help elaborating essays. But she is not professional during conferences, constantly got lost of her own ideas and feel like she just want to use all the time of the conference and not really give you any useful comments. Super hard grader and sometimes unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good teacher, a little bit tough grading

She gives lots of exercises, blog posts, and papers due. Not a tough grader like most expos teachers. Will take the time to make sure you understand the material. Very nice, chill. Lectures are boring tho. She knows when you're zoned out and/or about to fall asleep too.

Prof Veloso is the best ever. Like many of us I was not excited about the language requirement, but he makes class so fun I actually enjoy going. Even though there's no way he could know this, I am going through a really rough time right now and he has gone above and beyond to help me and be understanding. Just a great teacher & awesome guy.
My favorite professor!!! Very kind and funny. Always there to help and wants to see his students succeed. Love him!

I took SPAN-UA  1 with him and he was very funny and always made the class engaging. Some of his jokes were a bit weird at first but it actually made class more enjoyable! He always emphasizes that he is available to help students and made sure to answer every student's questions.
super chill and tailored the class around my interests
Had him for SPAN-UA 1, but it was not an option. He's so funny and good at his job. Everyone loved him in my class.

He is super weird and made sexual jokes during class which weren't funny and just made people uncomfortable. I didn't find the way he taught to be very helpful either, the textbook used was probably about 40 years old and it was Portugal Portuguese rather than Brazilian (90% of worldwide use), which makes no sense to teach in the United States.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Keep away
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's great. Learned a lot!

Carlos is an awesome professor. Super intelligent guy that understands language well. He expects you to study outside of class and gradually shifts the class so that it's entirely in Portuguese. Not only will you learn the fundamentals but Carlos is also great at teaching Portuguese/Brazilian culture. Can't go wrong with Carlos
