Carlos is an extremely knowledgeable man; he has studied culture and literature extensively and eagerly shares his knowledge. He is an excellent teacher, gives straightforward homework and exams. Carlos wants his students to succeed, but more than that he wants them to learn. 11/10 would recommend

He's a great professor. He's very helpful and he encourages his students to go to his office hours for help. The test are a little tough, so you need to study. He's very funny and makes the class fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Seriously the best professor I've had at NYU so far.

Carlos is, hands down, the best Portuguese teacher within the department at NYU. Not only is he super helpful, always ready to answer any question, and sincerely wants his students to succeed, but he's also super smart. His tests can be a little tough, but he gives you every single thing you need to know for them. It's up to you to study. Love him!
Really nice guy! I would definitely recommend this class.
Carlos is the best Portuguese language and lit teacher ever! He is funny and keeps his classes interesting. Very fair grader but make sure to show up for class!

Basically, I didn't do any of the readings I just read his summaries on brightspace and got an a on every paper, it is lecture heavy but if you pay a little bit of attention you can do it. unfortunate he is retiring.
Very knowledgeable but often repeats himself. Two papers in total which were quite long. Overall I learned a lot and enjoyed the class.
Equally very easy and interesting. In your essays, focus on the concepts he repeats frequently during lecture and you will receive a good grade. Very sweet, funny, caring professor. Will take again!

such a fun class. assignments were leniently graded, professor is an interesting guy and is super passionate about the subject. lectures kind of got old after a while, but mostly just because they're 2.5 hours long. incredibly flexible on deadlines.

Legend. Currently, my favorite professor at NYU. He's extremely intelligent, he'll understand any situation his students may encounter and will accommodate deadlines for you. To succeed, you must take notes during lectures on the concepts he talks about. Don't bother reading the classic novels, instead read the Word Docs & PDF files he emails you.

I love Prof Ulfers. He is the sweetest man you'll ever meet. He is subtly funny, passionate about the readings in class, and extremely caring and understanding towards his students. W/ Covid he has been optimistic & helpful with paper extensions, generous with office hours & is just a lovely person. Would recommend his first-year seminar for sure!

I didn't like this class. He's SO nice but the lectures were dense and the room was hot and I often fell asleep. As long as you mention his buzz-phrases (like duality of opposites) you'll do well on the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ulfers is honestly really sweet and his class is very easy to get a good grade in if you listen to the lectures and take some notes. A lot of people zone out a couple of times but still take notes. The notes and handouts really help with writing his essays and understanding chiasmic unity. I'm glad I took his class.
changed my life with his kindness and generosity of spirit, when he was my dean.

Ulfers very well may be an accomplished and intelligent professor, but in his Freshman Seminar, he basically just rambles about his ideas and thoughts on the books we read - ideas that were entirely based on theories and not the texts themselves. He's SO sweet, and has some brilliant things to teach, but did it in the most convoluted, unclear way.

Had him for Test and Ideas: 19th century and antiquity. AMAZING GUY. so sweeet and intelligent. This was my fave class and professor. His ideas are very fascinating and interesting. The TAs are great and easy graders. TAKE this course! Love Prof Ulfers!
Good class. Good professor. Good lectures. Highly recommended.

Really repetitive, but purposefully so. Sometimes when you sit in lecture it seems pretty boring but it really made me think about things in a different way and gave me a different perspective on texts.

Whether you're taking this class to fulfill a requirement, or you're taking it as a personal interest, it will be a good experience. I took the class as a requirement, but it ended up being my favorite class of the semester. Would take it again if I had the opportunity.

Best professor ever! His repetition of key points is precisely one of the reasons why I am able to get so much out of this class. You will probably be able to remember these ideas even years down the line because Ulfers takes basic concepts and connects them to countless different contexts. He knows just how to explain so that everything relates!

A fascinating and very clear lecturer with an infectious passion for the material (Nietzsche). He moves very slowly and is repetitive, but I counted this a strength since it helped me to grasp difficult concepts. Extremely king and generous in office hours; spent hours on several occasions helping with my paper.
Ulfers is a cute little old man who knows philosophy. He knows his material well and it shows if you talk to him after class--he realizes that he repeats himself,etc. A worthy text&ideas.

Blah blah blah...chiasmic unity...blah blah non-contradiction...blah blah blah Parmenides...Heraclitus...that's all folks. No one deserves to pay $4600 to hear such mind-numbingly boring, repetitive drivel.

Very very smart man.  A little bit old to be teaching but definitely knows what he's talking about. Sends out notes which are very helpful esp. since in lecture he can get lost in his own thought process.TAs are extremely generous; this is a good, easy choice to get texts and ideas out of the way although it wasn't particularly interesting.

I had him for Texts&Ideas: Antiquities of the 19th century. Most grading is done by the TAs, but the TAs for this class are VERY generous. General consensus that he's the best class for your T&I requirement if you're in Stern. Easy A - 2 essays and a midterm which is just identifying quotes and a short 2 paragraph answer.

As a ConWest professor, he does a lot of German philosophers and writers, but the passion he has for them really shows in his lectures and you learn alot. Paper are easy, and he's always there to talk after class.

He is a very easy grader; test are usually 8 quotation identifications and a short essay. There are also two 6 pages response papers to your readings. Although recitation and lecture are both mandatory he can be an engaging lecturer, though sometimes, it can seem his vocabulary is limited to 'Duality', 'Dualism' and 'Chiasmic Unity'.

Prof. Ulfers is a really great teacher, and really passionate about what he teaches. He really only teaches Comparative Literature aside from ConWest, so he is pretty focused. It WOULD get a bit annoying when he would repeat the same things class after class after class, but ultimately it has proven to be one of my most rewarding classes at NYU.

his lectures may be a little tedious but its the only way to learn in his class- reading the books isnt enough, so go to class. hes a nice enough prof and is very enthusiastic about his subject which makes it a more interesting. you dont really have to read the bks b/c he'll tell you what you need to know. i liked his teaching style-learned a lot.
Ulfers is the absolute best at NYU. A junior at NYU recommended me this professor and I am so thankful to her. His classes are interesting, thought provoking, and useful. Take his class at all cost!

REALY REALLY GOOD CLASS. I thought I would hate ConW, turned out to be my favorite class. Stuff talked in the lectures gave me such different perspectives of life. Ulfers is an experienced teacher and obviously very knowledgeable. He can get repetitive sometimes, but only because he doesn't want anyone to want out of the class confused.

very easy class. lectures and recitations are extremely boring because the same thing is said a million times. You WILL be lost at first but it will all come together and when it does it is actually very interesting. Definetely recommend. Attendance is huge.. get hilger as t.a.. coolest and funniest guy ever

This guy is amazing. At first, you would think "WTH is this old man talking about?" But you would eventually catch on and learn a lot. Things he say makes sense and he's not babbling gibberish.   Get Hilger as your TA if possible. Be warned: Don't be absent! Attendance counts in the grading.

Took the Language/Reality seminar last fall. Loved it. He can be a bit confusing at times and often skips over some things because he assumes we know it already. Also repeats some of his ideas. But his ideas are extremely interesting and will definitely stimulate you to think further. Easy grader, good professor. Take this seminar if you can.
Brilliant.  Lectures and readings are well synthesized and so interesting.  Three years later, my best academic experience to date.
He was great! A little repetitive by the end of the semester, but he really was like your grandfather...he made everything easily understandable

He is very boring and repetitive. I enjoyed the first lecture, but then the second one was the same as the first. He takes a very long time on each reading. He often makes up words in describing concepts, but instead of helping clarify the idea, they make it vague. If you take this class try to get Michael Bowen as your TA.

really nice guy, one of the nicest professors at nyu, but is unclear, ta's are your real teachers, and also, your real graders, not a lot of reading, not a lot of work, but a entertaining and decent guy, one of my favorites

Ulfers is really repetitive, but that just helped us learn better. There are some things in class that he taught that will probably stick with me forever. He's very knowledgeable (and so adorable). His passion for the subject makes this class worth going to. But the TA is the grader, be careful. The reading isn't too bad, nor the workload.
He is simply amazing. He's my favorite professor at NYU. He is intelligent, fun, and cares about his students.
An amazing human being. Very lofty thoughts. Really personable. He REALLY cares about his students.

Professor Ulfers is a really nice guy, but I did not like his teaching methods. Every time I walked out of the class I said, "What was he talking about." His lectures are very unclear. He was always available for office hours, and however much he tried to help, he was still unclear.

Ulfers is amazing...definitely like your favorite grandfather.  Although some of the readings are not that good, he makes a required class interesting.  Beware of your TA though since they're the ones that grade.
Very good teacher. I had him for an honors seminar and conwest and he was my favorite teacher. extremely helpful, understanding, willing to be of assistance to a student and loving.
Best teacher I had at the university.  Truly encourages intellectual development and exploration.  Some people have various complaints but everyone should take at least one class with him.

Haha, the grandfather comparison is accurate. He's an incredibly nice guy, and despite the size of the class, always pretty available to talk to. A really interesting lecturer, though he tends to ramble a bit. Has a fascinating way of looking at philosophy and literature, and the course reflects this. (Note: You'll be graded by a TA because of the class size.)
Some readings were more interesting than others, but it wasn't a bad class for a requirement.  He's a nice guy who is obviously very educated on his subject, but lectures can get boring at times.
Just like your favorite grandfather... funny, nice, confusing, and rambles... a great guy!  If only he could grade the papers - my TA was terrible... take the class, but pick your TA carefully
ulfers is fabulous.  the material is boring, but if you contribute, he will get to know you and talk to you and really intellectually stimulate you.
Really adorable and gets engaged in the lectures.  I agree: just like your grandfather :)
Ulfers is really cute.  He gets excited about his ideas and the literature.  Lectures can be hard to stay awake in, but most lectures are like that.  Overall, a great professor.
nice guy but the class overall is extremely boring. probably the best professor to take con west with since he is the most lenient.
nice but boring (attendance at lectures was minimal after a while), the reading list was boring too .. not his fault, just a bad class
Ulfers is intellectually fascinating, and reminds everyone of their favorite grandfather.  :)

He is, in fact, extraordinarily Nietzschean...and he tends to, so far as I've seen, read much of the information through a Derrida lens. He's not incredible so far as clarity's concerned, but he can be engaging.
the man needed some Hotness Total ;p  (great teacher)
He is very entertaining, hilarious, confusing at times, and very Niestzcian(dont know spelling)!
No Comments

She is super caring. Lecture is kinda boring but she speaks slowly so if ur international student it's quite good. Tests are very difficult!!!!! BE AWARE!!!!! But essay grading is friendly. Easy A- but not Easy A

She's really sweet but lectures can get boring and if you don't pay close attention you'll most likely fail the midterm. There's not a lot of graded stuff in the class and everything that is graded is hard, some people got As though so its possible.

3 essays with very clear feedback given. Occasionally can feel lecture-heavy. Attempts to make class fun with special ways of instilling the topics. Midterm and Final are only exams and are easy if the topic is studied. Great conversationalist and fun to talk to after class. Amazing prof who wants the best for students. Take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would definitely recommend Varnum. Class is lecture heavy but as long as you take notes you'll be good. 3 essays 2 exams. The essays are not bad because she prepares you to write through discussion + seminar style games. The final is worth 30% of the grade so you need good notes and watch her lecture videos! Solid class

Very nice. Assignments are super clear, but she says what she wants you to do on the essays and stuff in class. In-class notes matter a lot for the final and midterm, but they aren't hard regardless. Follow instructions, participate, and it is an easy A. Very nice teacher.
Varnum is a very great professor. But...there is a decent amount of readings + exams are difficult. 3 essays. Final was stressful. Def not an easy class by any means.

While Professor Varnum is very sweet, her grading criteria is unclear at times. This is one of the classes in which I have felt I do not have much guidance; I am essentially forced to do things with little direction. If you lock in, this class is doable but definitely not an easy one by any means.
The midterm is hard, multiple-choice, and very detailed.

Professor Varnum is really kind! Her guidelines for papers and exams are very clear and she gives lots of support in advance to make sure you do well. Lectures can get a bit repetitive, but her energy and enthusiasm makes them a lot easier to sit through. She focuses more on the literature, rather than the art history, but overall a great class!

2 short essays, 2 bullet-note "papers", 2 exams.
Straightforward. Not a tough grader. Gives very long and formal essay feedback, which can be scary. Difference between how she interacts via email/brightspace vs in person.
Pro tip: Watch the online lectures! Exam questions are taken word-for-word from them pretty much. No "tricks" on the exams ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Most caring and kind prof!! People don't acknowledge that.
Gives out a lot of As/A- in essays. Final is cumulative but selective, material is revealed up front. You need to read the texts.
Put some effort into your reasoning and use the correct editions.
If you are someone who worries about A- vs A, don't take; can be picky. Read the syllabus!

Tough grader. Even though she gives good lectures, the midterm and finals are so difficult. You need to memorize a lot of terms and understand the books really well. There is also an essay for the final. Wouldn't recommend. Spent so much time revising for the exams. There are also so many papers to write. Suffering for the whole semester.
She'll encourage your essay during office hour, but end up giving you a lousy grade. Not a lot of homework, but no curve
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Varnum is the sweetest and funniest professor. She's so nice and truly cares about her students. Her classes are so entertaining and her projects are really fun. If you have social anxiety, this class is probably not for you, because she makes students present alone in front of the class. Overall, her class is fun and tests are easy.
AMAZING professor. She was so understanding with deadlines, and work was very manageable. Take her!!
Her energy and demeanor is so refreshing and it is very clear that she cares a lot about the course and students in her class.

Reading heavy. Papers are graded harshly (READ THE RUBRIC CAREFULLY!), but overall, this class was a delight. Varnum is incredibly sweet and caring --- but no push-over. Group projects and games were fun. Midterm is very straightforward if you take notes. All in all, a good time.
She is the sweetest Professor ever, extremely caring. She has materials in case you miss class (video lectures). She is always willing to help you out, especially if you go to office hours.
she loves her job but grading is tough with boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dont take her, is not specific about what she wants at all and is such a hard grader
Don't take her. She's awful. DON'T take her!!!

Professor Varnum is the most passionate and sweet professor ever. You can tell she loves what she does and genuinely cares about you. She's super funny and always down to chat. Midterm, final, a few papers, and fun game days. Would definitely recommend. Amazing professor and human being. We need more Prof Varnums in the world!

I love Prof. Varnum. I took her two semester in a row for ACA and ACC. Only a few graded things throughout the semester and short essays. She's a pretty easy graded as long as you just show that you tried. She will love you if you participate. She's super funny and likable, I highly recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Varnum is probably my favorite professor I took her Arts and Cultures class twice and I loved her class both times. The classes this year were asynchronous so all we had to do was watch her videos and write forum posts. She does give a lot of writing assignments, but her assignments are always fun to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: her ACA class for ls core was asynchronous. i didnt do a single lesson or read a single text besides what i had to for the essays and i have an a- in the class. the class isnt fun or anything

Prof Varnum is a fair grader and very clear in what assignments require. She is available outside the class and always has helpful feedback. There were 3 short essays, a midterm and final. There is only one project where you are required to participate in class, but besides that you don't have to. I took her for 2 semesters, would take her again!

Varnum is a sweetheart, if you show up and you participate in class even just a little bit, she is relaxed and rewarding in terms of your participation grade. There were quite a few papers over the semester, including a few that required visiting museums, but she is a fair grader and you get from the class what you put into it.

Professor Varnum is a great professor. Lectures are interesting. Content and readings are not too heavy. She gives possibilities to improve grades on certain papers. Her classes are sometimes based entirely on participation, sometimes you'll have a Theatre Day or in-class debates based on role play. They're fun but not if you don't want to talk.
She's a tough grader, especially on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An absolute sweetheart who cares so much about the class material and her students. Assignments are super fun and there's a lot of freedom with them as well. One of the best classes I have taken thus far.

Disclaimer: The class is hard not because of the material but because of who the professor is. She is a very nice; she is very hard-headed and only believes in one narrow interpretation of the readings she assigns. She will punish you for having a different opinion or perspective than hers. So naturally, her directions are unclear. HAVE FUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You don't need to read the books to understand what she's saying and most of the people in class use Sparknotes anyway. Just pay attention to her lectures, however, she is an extremely hard grader and isn't specific on what she expects. If she doesn't believe with your interpretation, she declares that you're wrong and will receive a bad grade.

Varnum grades strictly off numbers, so you truly get what you get on tests/essays. That being said every assignment is worth 15-20% of the final grade so if you mess up on one thing you can recover. Most of her test questions come from her lectures so paying attention and taking notes is important. she always accommodates people for office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very boring and incoherent. It is clear that she has memorized every lecture and if any student asks a question that is not clearly answered in her notes then she does not know the answer and tells students to look it up on their own. Her midterms and finals for CFII are very hard compared to CFI. I would not take her again.

Dr. Varnum was a complete sweetheart. She gives so much feedback on essays and loves answering questions during her passionate lectures. Her office hours are there for a reason, use them! She loves helping her students and loves the subject she teaches. Pay attention when she speaks and take good notes during her lectures, it won't be hard to pass.

She's such a sweetheart who tries her best to help her students. She assigns readings, but you don't really have to read them all since she explains everything in detail in class. She places more emphasis on Art History though. Her grading criteria is clear. Her CFII "Reacting To The Past" Game was really enjoyable! Tests are fair.

I took Professor Varnum for CF 1 and I liked her CF1 class so much I was able to take her for CF2 as well! So happy I got to take her for the whole year. The second semester was super chill and clear cut because I already knew her/what she was expecting from essays/how her tests were etc. The amount of work is reasonable/doable.
Not too hard but extremely boring classes. Barely any interactions between the professor and students.

She's a sweetheart. She's really sweet and helpful. Even though there's a lot of reading, she goes over the readings in the class and clearly explains them. Tests aren't hard as she will tell you the format and what she expects. She tries to make the material interesting. This is my second time taking her and I'm glad. Highly recommend her.

Varnum was a good professor and was very clear with what she expected. The course requires a lot of reading but you don't have to participate (it might help with the grade though). I really liked her teaching style but she wasn't always available for help and didn't go out of her way to make time. I would definitely take her again!

Joan is a good professor, really inspires u , but her lecture could be a bit boring when it comes to art history part.  Since tests include much detail about note and art history stuff, it's not easy to get A. So get ready for long text of art history. Take notes as much as u can during class. If you are not that into art history, don't take her.
Don't take her!!!!!!!! There is so much work and she is not helpful at all!!!!

Varnum is the ultimate teaching machine. I went into the semester knowing nothing and I came out feeling like an expert on the material. She is a passionate and organized teacher, very professional and well-spoken. Her expectations are clear and her assignments are such that you feel challenged but not overwhelmed. She makes old art seem so human.

Most incredible professor I've ever had the privilege of encountering! I absolutely love her and it kills me to know I can't take her class again next semester. She's wonderfully passionate about what she teaches and will do anything to ensure the best performance from her students. Hands down, one of the best professors at NYU :D

Absolutely loved her; she made cultural foundations great.  Passionate about what she teaches too!  Really wants her students to do well, and will reach out to someone if she thinks you are struggling in her class.  Really bummed I can't take her again next semester :(

Okay so I actually love Varnum so much that I'm willing to take her class next semester at 8am. If that's not a clear sign of how good of a teacher she is, I don't know what is. Varnum is so incredibly sweet, organized and attentive that she really makes it easy to go to class. Her class is very well-structured and not too hard at all. TAKE HER!

LOVE HER!! She's SO funny, SO helpful, and she's VERY passionate about what she teaches. Very knowledgeable and really cares that her students learn. Allows you to get a better grade for your first paper. PAY ATTENTION TO THE ART HISTORY. READ THE BOOK. She absolutely WILL include on exams. Tests are fair. Do your work, and you'll get an A. I did!
This professor is awesome!  Take her! The Shakespeare Marlowe game is so much fun and it challenges you. This is what I hoped my classes would be like.

Although what she teaches isn't the best material to learn at 9:30AM, she is so sweet, caring and thoughtful that you want to participate and learn what she is saying. she is such a dependable professor-- one of the best lsp ones i've ever had. also, her play reenactments are so fun and engaging. i loved having her both times i did!

Dr. Varnum is literally the best professor i've ever had at NYU. She's amazing, extremely helpful and really really cares for her students. If you follow her directions, you're guaranteed an A. TAKE HER. She will never disappoint! Her passion for her field real makes her stand out as a professor. Words can't describe how much I've enjoyed her class
Prof. Varnum is very kind and easy to please in essays and participation but her class is very boring and repetitive.

Prof. Varnum is a very kind, helpful and passionate professor. Her writing assignments are very easy and quick. The only problem I have with her is sometimes her class feels like a kindergarten class....
Prof. Varnum is probably the nicest and most enthusiastic professor you will ever have. She's very helpful and is just an overall great professor that loves what she does. HIGHLY recommended.
lol im in her class now. she is an amazing teacher and really knows what she is talking about. annoying museam visits and sometimes a lot of hw but reallyyyyyy easyyyy

Absolutely LOVE this professor. She is really passionate, unbiased, and professional. Probably the best professor I've ever had. I'm signing up for her class next semester as well, even though getting up at 7:30am is a drag. She's a pretty easy grader, tests are pretty easy as well. She also grades essays fairly and I love her comments!

She is absolutely wonderful.  So passionate about everything she is teaching.  Really pulls the deeper meaning out of all the books she assigns.  Not very easy to get by on SparkNotes.  She makes the class truly interesting and it is just so nice to be around her.  Very inspirational and insightful.

Varnum is the sweetest, most caring woman alive. Yes, I fell asleep in class all the time, but she was so passionate about everything that she made me LIKE the books I thought I'd hate. Assignments are easy A's: she likes giving people good grades. The only pain was the amount of textbook info for exams...I hated that book with a passion.
So wonderful. As long as you write passionately about whatever it is you are writing, she will know and be really happy with your work. She's so sweet and so flexible and so you just want to hug her.

Harmless. Also really clueless and cheesy. Really enthusiastic but not always in a good way. Will take you on a "motorcycle through time."The class may seem meanignless and easy but the midterm was sort of hard and had some really specific stuff that I wasn't expecting so take good notes and re-read the art text.She'll love it if you talk.Nice lady

The class consists of a few essays which you go over and over, but she helps you to give her exactly what she wants in the essay this way. Step by step grading and correcting makes it easy to do well on the essays. She's a great prof who really loves writing
Very demanding, challenging!  My writing was transformed. I learned so much about research. Loved it.
Very demanding, challenging!  My writing was transformed. I learned so much about research. Loved it.

babies her students. i hate the writing workshops and reading essays outloud. the topics are interesting but kind of juvenile. the essays have no real point whatsoever. as easy as she seems, she's not THAT easy of a grader. a really nice person but i would not take her again because she's not helping me improve my writing, very stagnant

I took her 2 semesters in a row, she's VERY helpful; walks you thru the material and KNOWS what she's talking about; if you have problems, see her and she'll help you.  This class is an easy A if you do the work (lotsa little papers), but no stress necessary.  VERY understanding and patient.

Prf. Varnum is an incredibly sweet person. She helps you with essays, is incredibly understanding (will give you extensions if you talk to her), and will give you help if you ever need. Her class is pretty easy, as well. I wish I could have had her for Prose Comp I as well.

shes very easy, i felt like i was being babied the entire class and going back to freshman english in high school. if you want something easy take her, but you dont learn much... shes very nice though, class got a lil boring at times, will help with ur creative writing a bit
I really enjoyed her class especially since she is really interested in hearing what the students have to say. She is really nice and supportive.  I think my writing has improved because of her.

Dr. Varnum is an amazing woman who's very interested in what she teaches.  She's also very invested in her students.  Her writing assignments are generally fairly easy and can be fun.  She's also a very understanding, sweet person.  You couldn't ask for a better professor.

This can be a hard or an easy class. Don't try to skip class and get a good grade. My writing has gotten much better. Varnum is tough, but fair and supportive. She is both entertaining and brilliant, not too common here!

There is a good amount of work for the class. Especially in the second half of the class. But she is extremely understanding if you make the time to talk to her. Its not a class you can blow off, but you have some room for error.

Homeworks are trippy, lectures are trippy. super chill nice guy though. i thought the quizzes were also bad, theres like a 25 minute time limit for 6 questions and he'll be talking for like 10 of those minutes.

Professor Versoza's lectures are super fast-paced so a lot of the time you have to go back outside of class or while doing the homework to understand what is going on. But, he drops a homework and a quiz and you can tell he definitely cares and wants everyone to get a good grade.

He is a good professor and you will learn a lot, but the lectures are incredibly fast and there is a lot of homework. At one point in the semester we had homework, a final project, and in class quizzes all at once.

Also, the curves only benefit those below a B and aren't fair to all.

if you don't have a solid background in python(data in gen) don't take this course. he goes wayyyyy to quickly for anyone who doesn't at least do 4 leetcode problems a day. hw is insanely tedious and quizzes/exams designed to make you not finish. i won't say they're very hard but the workload is crazy. he cares abt us but not the best lecturer.

The man does not give you a chance to take notes. He goes lightning fast in lectures and expect everyone to already know what's going on. Only a snippet of the notes gets uploaded. Getting a response back from him for questions take ages or sometimes don't even respond.
Took AIT with him. GOATED professor of all time, wish I can take his class again to be honest. Easily my most favorite class in my whole academic career at NYU. Learned so much during the course.

Joe is the GOAT, highly recommend him. Homework are time consuming but really not that hard if you pay attention in class. Final project was an easy 100% and exams were designed to give you as many points as possible. Definitely take!

Lectures go at a fast pace as others mentioned, overall a great professor who knows the content very well and is very accessible outside of class. Homeworks are well designed for real world application, expect to spend around 5hrs weekly. Exams are curved to an average around B. Highly recommend him for full stack!

Versoza is the best cs professor that I've had at NYU. His lectures are intense and he gets through an immense amount of material extremely quickly BUT if you are able to engage with him and take everything in it is so worth it to be there. The only thing to be careful of is that it (AIT) is homework heavy throughout the whole semester.

i love his teaching style & he's nice + understanding. BUT always look over notes BEFORE lectures bc he's fast. lots of hw and tests are anxiety-inducing but I learned a lot. the skills I learned in AIT helped me get an internship + I learned how to code fast bc of the amount of hw lol. take him if ur interested in fullstack/know some web dev stuff

VerGOATza 

Versoza gives more homework than most other CS4XX elective courses and that you should be prepared to spend anywhere between 6-10 hours a week (esp. AIT; DMA, not so much)

However, the topics he covers in these classes lean toward applicable skills used in the industry, and I appreciate his lecture style. He also sounds like MKBHD

Yes, he is a nice person. But, his course sets you up for failure. Exams were tough, many students did not finish, homework takes anywhere between 6-10 hours a week, and lectures go at lightning speed, does NOT give you ANY time to take notes. Tests you on HTML when its not even taught in this class, he assumes you already mastered it prior.

Kindhearted and accommodating professor who gives well organized lectures. Very active on ed discussion. There's a lot of material in the course and he taught it well. just don't sleep on the homeworks & exams
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not hard & useful class, especially for those who work with databases and python. HWs take around 3-4 hours. In-class quizzes are announced in advance. Exams are a bit hard but not unmanageable, just go through slides and practice, nothing unexpected there.

If you don't have that much faith in your computer science skills, don't take his course. Most importantly, DON'T EVER LISTEN TO THOSE who recommend his course because "at least he is a good person". I'm not saying they are wrong, but I can guarantee that you will soon be deeply regretful if you listen to them.

If you don't have that much faith in your computer science skills, don't take his course no matter what. Most importantly, DON'T LISTEN TO THOSE who recommend his course because "at least he is a nice person". I'm not saying they are wrong, but I guarantee that you will regret your decision very deeply if you listen to them.

Ok at explaining topics but the course is very dense. Homeworks are reasonably easy. Exams are difficult and, by his admission, pretty much designed not to be finished. Especially bad because they make up ~55% of final grade. Course is designed as though it's project-focused, but isn't. Final project can be good for resume if you try though.

He rushes through everything, not explaining the reason behind it. Homework takes you so much time, but they are worth so little grade. Unclear instructions often appears on tests. He takes a long time to respond on edstem. Dont trust TA or people that suggest taking this course, unless you are a person who's similar to the person who's suggesting.
Professor Versoza is an incredibly kind and helpful professor. This class was certainly a good bit of HW and involved a lot of information, but is definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Fair professor that packs a lot of very good information into the semester. Lectures got very boring for me at times and he made a lot of jokes that I didn't care for but at the end an above average professor.

he's a good person but not a good professor. he needs to structure his classes better so you're not always feeling like you're rushing in every single lecture. it felt like a train wreck this semester, avoid him
High quality materials but NEVER take this course when you choose to overload. You will face tons of assignments, I mean it.
he's not a bad person, he just assigns a ton of work you'll hate before, during and after doing it.

Somehow, each class he teaches becomes some sort of a race. You are ALWAYS playing catch up, because that's just how he designs his classes - he sets you up to fail. That to me is not good teaching, because students aren't learning anything. If you forget every single thing you learnt the moment you leave the exam hall, it's not actual knowledge.

I think he's a nice person, not the best prof with respect to exams and assignments. What he teaches in class is different from what you're graded on, he thinks students don't have other classes and other hw to deal with. Designs incredibly time consuming assignments for no apparent reason. Lmao I'm annoyed I didn't switch

Joe loves giving really difficult and useless exams. No matter how you did well in the projects. You have to face the truth you need to memorize all the trivial outdated knowledge of frontend and wrote all the answer within extremely limited time. And the exams took too much percent in grading. I sincerely recommend you not to take this course

Full stack is not easy, so giving a low score for it is too hard does not make sense. Indeed Prof.Versoza cannot explain everything and is far from explaining everything well. However it is not completely all his fault: with less than 3 hours of lectures in a week, it is just not possible for him to teach every detail of the material.
Take the other section if possible

Be careful when choosing this class! Despite the very time-consuming homework assignments and final project this class is in reality a test-heavy course in disguise. Disappointing how tests are tailored towards cheating and consequently almost impossible. Questions are on obscure info barely mentioned in class or unnecessarily complex and rigid.

Honestly, Versoza is a good and funny guy, but he needs to re-evaluate the structure of the midterm and finals. He outright stated that the "midterm and final" are to not be finished by design like some sick stressful pseudo-Putnam exam ideology. Tests are on useless syntax and a struggle, especially with no extra monitors. Project heavy as well.
Run!!! unless you do not care about GPA

Very knowledgeable and caring professor. I find this class challenging , but prof Versoza is always there to help.  Lots of work but skills gained are worth it. Don't take this class if u have other hard classes. Definitely will recommend those who don't have web dev experiences to get familiar with MERN stack beforehand through youtube or udemy.
Really hate the test and quiz. The test takes too much. Tough grader. Highly not recommended if you want to maintain good gpa

If ur planning to take AIT, go Pass/Fail and do udemy web bootcamps beforehand. Perfect chance to complete a first full-stack project which helps boost my resume. Joe's open to suggestions and adjusts hw to easy mode after we protest against it. Midterm's also not so bad. Despite this, Do PF and Do bootcamps!!! Also, things r better after midterm!!

Moved at a very fast pace and assumed you knew about the material already. Things were not clear and it moved so quickly that you could not even finish reading a sentence. Final-length homework assignments are due every week. Led me to feel hopeless, and crazy amounts of stress, and I withdrew. I hear the testing and midterm were even worse.

The constant tangents and unfollowable speed at which he types code makes this class unbearably confusing. He falls under the fallacy that the entire class understands his jumble of explanations because of a few students with prior web dev experience. He fails to recognize that too much info is overwhelming and ineffective.

Joe is good at giving lectures and his the slides/quizzes are helpful but the midterm and final are crazy. Since they're online, tests are way longer than he expects u to finish and the curve that he gives to try and offset this is totally ineffective. I would only take this course when everything is completely in person and the tests are normal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are OK, but grading is absolutely horrible. Don't take if you want to get a decent grade.

Quite interesting to see his ratings are polarized here. For me, he truly is a good speaker, organized and knowledgeable. Hw is a lot but difficulty OK to me. Yet his grading is terrible. Over 20 quizzes and hws and none of them could be dropped off. The exam is designed to be unfinished and curve is a joke. Many friends around me worry about grade

He is really a good teacher! You can learn so much knowledge from his course! I do not understand the logic of why some students rate 1.0, that is unfair! If they find the hw is way too much for them they can just leave.....
Lot of hw, but relatively easy. Super helpful content.

Run! I joined the class based on Joe's RMF rating(3.8). BUT, the unreasonable amount of HW still is beyond my expectation! I talked to someone who took his class before, and apparently, he is getting tougher now with even more hw! Joe assumes you know python a lot already and always lectures really fast. Think about you spending 25 hrs/wk in hw!

Warning! Do not take his class! True he is a good speaker and is knowledgable in what he is teaching. BUT, too much homework and due in such an unreasonable time! Ruins my life this semester. Think about that, project in your other CS class that is due in 2 weeks or more, Joe only gives you 6 days to finish. WTF? I have other classes to do as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very respected and well-prepared. Answers every question you ask in the forum on time. Makes the BEST slides at NYU, very clear and well-organized. This class is heavy and fast-paced, but professor Versoza really facilitated the learning experience. Exams are hard but reasonable curves are given.

wtf. i'm not even doing badly in this class but this prof sucks. i literally haven't been to class since september because i realized going is such a waste of my time, i just try to learn off his slides and the internet. it's like he expects us to have a bunch of background knowledge on the already very heavy class material.
Huge workload, but well-worth it. A great way to truly understand the foundations of web-development and get started on modern web-dev as well.

Do not recommend in addition to another workload heavy class. Back-to-back quizzes and assignments, which can be draining. The lectures themselves can be rushed, so expect to use outside resources to supplement the knowledge. Tends to present coding demos. Not so accessible outside of class, but will accommodate class' needs (ex: pushing deadlines)

Joe gives an unreasonable amount of work in a very short amount of time. He also teaches too quickly in class and assumes that we have prior knowledge of certain things. I have never spent so many nights in Bobst before taking this class. I will never take another of his classes, and if you're smart you won't either.

Quizzes/tests are made way too long to the point where most people complain about not being able to finish them. I think it would be a good course for people who can handle time pressure but for me it's been difficult to not be overwhelmed by the difficulty of his quizzes, tests, and homework. His teaching also feels rushed and vague at times.

One of the better professors in the CSCI department. Very organized, lectures are clear and to the point, explains concepts very well. The highlight for me was doing workshops once a week, where we can collaborate with others to write code.

He tries to squeeze a lot of things into the lecture, but I don't think he explained it clearly. And he would assume you know a lot of stuff which is actually not listed in the prerequisite of the course. This makes me really struggle at the beginning of the course.

Clear lectures and a lot of detailed slides. The homework he gives isn't that hard but they're time consuming (at least 5 hrs) and once a week. The class (AIT) is very practical and it's worth taking with him. He's very helpful when it comes to questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: practical applications and hands on with the material (through hw), material not really difficult but homework does take long to do (5-10 hours a week). approachable guy, accommodated well during online shift for pandemic

Professor Versoza is amazing. His courses (AIT and DMA) are well structured, relevant to technology today, and really well taught. The homeworks can sometimes take a lot of time, but the grading criteria is very clear and if you read the instructions carefully, you can do very well. The exams are very fair and lectures are very clear
He's generally a nice guy but his tests are just so hard. He did give some extra credits opportunities.

Well versed in his field; however, there were 4 programming assignments every week and not too many tutoring opportunities. Average on both midterms was around the C range, while the max was an A, if that gives you an idea of the difficulty. This class actually made me realize I don't want to do computer science, haha.

Professor Versoza is the reason I pursued a CS career as a non-major. His lectures were super clear & entertaining. He was always there to offer assistance. He was patient and truly wanted to see you succeed. He offered plenty of opportunities for extra credit. His assignments were sometimes a bit challenging, but never felt pointless.

He gives a lot of homework each week that feels never-ending. He is very nice but his lectures can be redundant. The exams were difficult and he does not curve more than 1-2points depending on the class avg unlike some of the other professors.

VERY practical content for AIT. Long weekly HW but again very practical and helps nail concepts/theory. Plenty of deadline extensions & extra cred. Lectures move fast and demos imo aren't super engaging. Can study on your own and do fine. Tests nuances and specific stuff on exams. Final project is an awesome chance to add someth to your portfolio.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the better professors at CAS that knows his stuff, and is very dedicated to teaching students. His lectures were very informative and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 100/100. Prof. Versoza is amazing. He is probably one of the most dedicated instructors of NYU. The course was difficult (tonnes of hws) but it helped me learn technologies which are widely used in the industry. If you're a CS major, don't graduate without taking this course.
AIT is hands down one of the most useful classes I have taken. Joe is lit! He really cares about his students and knows the material so well.

(AIT) It's not an easy A. He's not very friendly in office hours; best time to talk to him is right after class while he's still pretending to be nice. He gives so much hw without any breaks, even while we were working on the final proj he gave us hw. Assignments and exams were not easy. Time consuming class so do not take with other hard classes.
AIT was actually pretty okay with homework, and imho it's very doable. Comes off as a bit pretentious tho.

AIT - With a homework every week, it is a dependable heavy workload, but it is so worth it. It was one of my favorite classes I've taken - you learn a ton of useful material. The reason he gives you assignments every week is so that you actually understand the material he is teaching, and the grading is fair. Take the class if you have time for it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: SO much work!! 12 pages of hw due every week is unreasonable, especially if you are taking any other CS class. Look at an old syllabus! He is a tough grader and his lectures are not interesting. He gives you coding demos and expects you to follow, even if it is a new topic. No hands on coding in class, except for the last two classes.

Versoza's class is the best experience I've had in the CS dept; it's built around tight feedback loops, from the fair but non-triv hw to the lectures (most of the teaching is done through live demos); he can effctvly take the temp of the class and backtrack organically when necc; the class seems designed to teach everyone w/out patronizing anyone.
Versoza is cool and a good lecturer but gives a lot of homework and the midterm was hard. Although final was easier. Take the class if you want to learn JavaScript. If you want an easy A don't do it.
Loved the prof, amazing teacher. Could explain python to a toddler

Took his undergrad data management, and after midterm, he said he's giving average B-, which made me so worried, so I'm writing this review for future students taking this course. His lectures and notes are clear, and there will be tons of materials if you're not a web minor or not on this track. You'll learn, but you need a big and strong heart.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: AIT is a very very hands-on and intense elective, especially if you've never learned Javascript (and HTML/CSS). Hard to follow lectures, so be prepared to learn everything on your own outside of class. Slides are directly related to the hw though, which form the foundation for the exams. Very useful class though.

He actually knows what he's doing and will teach actually useful full-stack skills. Be prepared for a lot of homework, but for the most part, they're manageable and the tutors he's hired are super friendly and accessible. Lectures can feel rushed because he's trying to squeeze in a lot of material in a semester.

Joe was always super clear during class and super fun! He really cares about his students and makes an effort to make homework/projects fun. For Python, don't bother buying the textbook! Do the online modules and homework.

Happily dumping endless hours of weekly homework, offering pathetic quantities of extra credit, expecting perfection on a test that the TA's don't understand, and refusing to curve the class grade, Professor Versoza is lightyears from encouraging students to pursue programming professionally. Joe needs to reconsider his curriculum and beyond.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He quickly learns students names which eliminates intimidation in a class of unfamiliar people. Complaint: his exams do not show accurate representations of a student's skills. Programming heavily relies on continual test runs which a hand written test doesn't allow for. Sometimes, in attempt to let you figure it out, he fails to properly assist.

I had Versoza for Python and Intro to Comp Sci, and he's the reason I'm a CS major. He's extremely clear in his lectures, provides very good resources, and his assignments were always lengthy and tough, which is incredibly helpful. He emphasizes the importance of working hands-on with code, which reinforces the material incredibly well. Great prof.
He is clearly smart, but is not a good teacher. His method of teaching is reliant on giving you an enormous amount of teeth grinding work. Also he talks way too fast.

Joe is an amazing professor, especially if you're just starting out with Python! Lectures are extremely clear and fun and homework assignments are also not hard. It's a shame he doesn't teach Intro to Comp Sci or I would definitely have taken his class!
Gives Lots of homework and focuses on too many details at exam. He has some sort of weird smartness that he would like to show off.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and difficult tests
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Gives a decent amount of homework, but it's very effective at helping you learn the material. Clear lectures and slides, always available and willing to help, and grades very fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Somehow feel the professor overpraised in rmp. Really good for learning but really give assignment more frequently than other professors, and somehow repeating. Understand that practice makes perfect but feel a little bit unnecessary, as least from my point of view. But still I see he is a good instructor.

Didn't open the textbook once. Uses students in higher levels of CS as graders and tutors. They hardly give you the help you want when you go for tutoring or ask questions in class. Two days a week: one class for lecture, one class for in-class assignment (where we worked on HW). HW due every week.

Hands down the best professor ever. I came in this class thinking I'll take it for a semester, but Joe made programming so interesting I'm considering majoring in it. He's really approachable, funny, and cares about his students. His exams are fair and he's an easy grader but homework might be a bit overwhelming. Please take him if you can!

Best Computer Science professor I've had. He really makes the material engaging in a way I haven't had with any other professor. I wasn't sure if CS was the right major for me at the time but his class definitely helped me affirm it. Easy to reach and helpful in every regard to the curriculum.

Professor Versoza was a great teacher who was very organized. He made Python very clear, and provided numerous resources  to improve our knowledge of the language. It's important to look over his review powerpoints because some test questions are fairly tricky. I will definitely take him again for CS101.

prof. versoza is everything a professor should be. his lectures and ppts are very clear, his homework questions are challenging and comprehensive, and he prepares you very well for his exams. (and he's a very generous grader). he doesn't take attendance but i recommend you go to every class because you get a lot out of them.
Love this guy. Will be looking forward to taking him again. I definitely recommend him. He makes everything pretty straightforward and clear.
Clear, pretty engaging lectures, everything posted online, lots of assignmentssome EC can smooth over some rough exam scores. Definitely recommended.
Tried emailing him 3 different times and he didn't answer any of them.
Very good teacher, teaches clearly, gives fun assignments, and likes to use cute cat examples! He is helpful, easy-going and you will learn a lot from his class.
Joe is awesome! Super clear, helpful and a great guy. Wish he taught all my compsci classes.

Joe's lectures are extremely clear and fun. If you go to class, the assignments are a breeze. He makes it very clear what he expects you to know for exams, and he doesn't try to trick you with his exam questions. Easily one of the best professors I've had at NYU.
Joe Versoza is easily the best professor I've ever had. He's clear, concise, organized, and funny. He goes above and beyond to ensure his students know the material and are prepared for exams.

Joe Versoza is an awesome teacher. He is super organized and I can not recommend him enough! The home work is moderately difficult, but if you ever ask him for help you won't have any trouble. Also, he prepares you really well for his midterms.

Knows a lot about the topic and will explain in office hours, but the best way to get a decent grade is to skim the textbook before lecture. Used an old version of the textbook, pay attention in class, and it will be fine. Slow to respond to emails but easily accessible in office hours.

Incredibly difficult to understand as a lecturer. Often goes on long tangents about unnecessary material that doesn't appear on exams only to skim past important topics. Slow to respond to emails, and lectures often left me more confused than simply reading the textbook. Clearly a smart guy -- doesn't know how to teach. Exams are difficult! Beware!

Prof Winawer is a really nice and caring guy, but his lectures are just too boring. I think all the good reviews are because the class was online, it's not anymore. This class is definitely one of the harder psych courses. Not an easy A by any means. This review is not to hate on the prof as a person, but serves as a warning for future students.

Lectures deliver unhelpful material in long tangents. Gets through material slowly, not able to finish material that will be present on test, in which additional lecture videos are assigned to make up for his poor lecture delivery. Overall nice person, but very frustrating to have as a professor. Too much detail on superfluous information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The semester is not over yet, but do not take him.  Lectures are so unclear and he goes on so many tangents, he is not very responsive, lectures go over things not on the test (for half of the lecture too), tests/quizzes are impossible.  Very inteligent guy but is just not good at teaching to students, and focuses on unimportant things.

30% quiz, 20%final, 50% 3drop1 exams. He curved to meet the around 40% A standard so it really was nice of him. 1% ec added if complete pollev. He's lectures were fun, shows lots of visual/auditory examples to help us understand the concepts. But lectures itself wont get you good grades. Be ready exams are a bit hard.
Amazing professor, not a difficult class if you do the readings

(PSY53 - PSS) Prof is kind and understanding. His grading was lenient; 1/3 exams dropped, 4/12 hw assignments dropped, extra credit, & 80% credit on late hw, which went against his original rules. If you have any special circumstances, he is rlly helpful and will find a solution. Attendance isn't mandatory, & he posts all his slides and recordings.

Course: PSYCH-GA 2245 -- fMRI Lab

Overall, Prof. Winawer is a nice person and able to explain challenging topics fairly well.

However, he has a serious grading problem, in that he does not do it. Our first assignment was due in Feb; we never got feedback for anything. It is now 1 week after final grades were due and he has not submitted them.

The lectures can be boring but the class was easy. He drops your lowest exam and 3-5 quiz grades- all open book. His curve is insane (I had a 120% in my quizzes after getting 6/7 on most). Exams are based on lectures and readings (make sure you read). Allott proper time for this class, stay on-track (with COVID it's hard) & you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He curves quite heavily. 3 quizzes and 1 Exam were dropped. He is an absolute sweetheart who tried his best to make the class work through remote learning. Absolutely take him but be ready to read and pay attention in lecture cause the exams are not easy, open book though. Recitation and lecture attendance was not necessary.

Jonathan is one of the kindest, most human professors Ive had. Hes pretty chill and lectures arent so bad - sometimes the material was really complicated though. There are short weekly reading quizzes, take 3 drop 1 exam, & a final. No study guide given. He responds quickly to forum questions & emails. Perception was a good class to take online!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Best professor. I was so sad that he doesn't teach this year. His perception class was just amazing. I didn't even read the textbook and only showed up at the recitation and the lectures. And I didn't even take notes. He made things so clear that all you need to do is listen. He also replies emails in literally seconds.

Professor Winawer is a really considerate and nice guy. Lectures can get a little boring if youre not interested in the material but the class is overall not too bad. 30% of your grade comes from the quizzes in recitation which could be an easy A if you read the chapters before class. You could drop one of the 3 exams.
Professor Winawer is very smart and will make difficult material easier to comprehend. I highly recommend this course.

Winawer is such an understanding professor. He curves both the quizzes and the exams! You can drop 1 exam and 3 quizzes. Read and you will ace the easy quizzes that really help your grade. The exams question can be challenging, but he really helps you out with the curve. Work hard and you'll get at least an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take him! I truly enjoyed his class and learned a lot. One of the most interesting psychology classes I have taken.

I really enjoyed Winawer as a professor. There were weekly quizzes for our semester, based on the textbook chapters. The textbook itself is not a difficult read, so it was feasible. Also, he helps your grade out with both the quizzes and the tests because the material definitely requires deep understanding (yet is manageable).

Really one of the most insane classes, it covers so much so be prepared to keep up on the reading and learn fast. Go to recitation so you can get credit for the easy quizzes which comes out to be 30% of your grade (really helps out). All the tests are insanely specific, he curves every test because its almost impossible to get an A on the first try
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's pure excellence! I would highly recommend him. He's so passionate about the subject & willing to help if you see him during office hours. He's very understanding & wants everyone to do well. Your grade is determined by 2/3 best exams & 10/11 short assignments. You also can earn up to 5 points for extra credit if you go to class. Good luck!

This professor is amazing! I can't believe not more people have rated him because he's so understanding. 3 exams (including the final) and he drops one. He records his lectures so if you missed something in class, you can always rewatch it on nyuclasses. He gives up to 3 extra credit points added to your total grade. Overall, amazing class!

Winawer is such an awesome person and if you go talk to him then he will definitely help your grade. Tests are fair but some questions can be challenging and straight from the book. Do the extra credit and listen to online lectures!
okayish-fair grader but the mandatory readings spike my cortisol. also heavy workload

The teaching style relies heavily on having students repeatedly read aloud in class. Small mistakes result in being asked to reread the same text many times in front of everyone, which can feel discouraging and stressful rather than helpful for learning or confidence.

The classroom environment often feels hostile rather than supportive. I found the professor's feedback style to be demoralizing, which made it difficult to participate without fear of being singled out. I usually love studying Chinese, but the teaching style here made me dread class. Waking up in the morning started to feel like a nightmare.

She literally doesn't care about her students. Has a humiliation kink and is a general bully. Thankfully dropped this class before the add/drop deadline, but prayers to everyone taking her class right now.

did not hate her lectures, but did make me not want to come to class sometimes. cold calls on you sometimes but can be condescending. will not budge on late work or absences (even excused ones). hard class with lots of work, but can be easy if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Syllabus is clear on grading.

Can be very condescending and sometimes just repeats students' mistakes back to them (ie incorrect tones) without providing additional help/context; made 2 people cry in class bc they asked for clarification/misunderstood assignments that were poorly explained.

Wish we were taught more vocab common in novels.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: professor did not let me go to the bathroom during a test. Even though it was an emergency. Even though she had our phones and backpacks. I had to turn my incomplete test in before sprinting to the bathroom

I see none of the other reviews have included this, so I will. Her class policy states that you automatically fail her course if you have 8 unexcused and EXCUSED absences. I saw 2 classmates beg her at the end of the course to be more understanding, one of whom has pneumonia and missed 2 weeks of class. Workload heavy, heart of ice, steer clear.

I had to return home for a week due to a sick relative. I emailed the professor beforehand but returned to find my grade had been docked by a letter. My grandmother passed away that week, and when I tried to explain, she said, "Your lack of preparation will not sway how I grade this class." An awful professor, and an even worse person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great Professor, Amazing Lectures, Learned so much from her class. Take her if you want to learn about Chinese Poetry.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: overall the class is decent because you actually improve at reading and writing in chinese. however, be warned that the workload is quite heavy as you speed through around a lesson per week. professor is funny at times, but sometimes she would put people on the spot.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she's a very caring, funny, and cool professor, but the class is hard as shit. tbh this is not a class for "advanced beginners". better off going to chinese 1 if you actually never learned to write chinese. homework and quizzes every week actually made me braindead, not her fault all the accelerated chinese classes are like this.

There is a lot of daily homework, but Shao Laoshi's class was very informal and she clearly did want us to learn. You can only learn as much as you're willing to work for in Chinese, but Shao Laoshi made that process much smoother.
You will do well in the class if you participate and do the homework. The professor really wants everyone to do well! super recommended

As with any language, how good you get and how much you improve is almost always entirely up to you. Shao does a good job trying to facilitate that growth, but it's still largely up to you to actively learn and practice the materials provided. Classes are chill and non-formal, a truly stress-free environment.

Profisn't considerate with people with disabilities and having traditional + simplified words on the same powerpoint is confusing. But also when she goes over the homework sentences, it is too fast to write it down if youre wrong on something, especially for non-natives. Wish it could be written out for us so we can take time to digest the meaning.

Professor Shao is great, i think NYU has great chinese teachers, and she is no different. I had her for advanced chinese 2 and i think she is a great teacher, she is pretty thorough and yes there's a lot of work but thats expected for this level. She is very eccentric & vibrant & really wants everyone to do well! very funny too!

I loved this class. Though the workload was a lot a times, it definitely made learning Chinese much smoother. Prof. Shao made the class environment fun and interesting, so learning new words or phrases easier to remember. Highly recommend making quizlet sets to help study.

(Advanced Chinese II) The best Chinese teacher ever. So funny, super caring, wants you to do well. Yes there is a lot of work BUT it's not hard to do, you just have to take the time to do it. She wants you to learn. Probably the best/most effective Chinese class I've ever taken. Quizlets for the vocab on account Emma_Iridondo.

It's a pretty tough course, there's homework and something to do in class more or less every day. Attendance and participation is required, but I suppose that's to be expected of a language course. As long as you put in a bit of effort every day, you should be okay. Homework isn't terrible most the time, just time consuming.
Nice experience overall
I didn't learn anything in class. The instructor would refuse to use the definitions given in the textbook and make her own up that didn't make sense. When we asked her to clarify, she was unable to.

Classes can either be engaging or dry depending on whether we are engaging with the text or learning new vocab. The workload is fair (weekly quizzes, oral recordings, occasional written prompts). Make sure to follow. her. instructions--and you'll have a decent time in her class. She cares for your progress and wants you to do well!
Unorganized and poor control of the classroom. Gets angry at students when they pronounce a tone incorrectly (it's a language class). Very discouraging behavior.
She is a kind, caring, and funny professor who explains things well and keeps classes interesting. I enjoyed my class with her

Had her for Elementary Chinese for Advanced Beginners and I think everyone did well in her class. She gave a lot of work but she's a light grader so it wasn't really a problem. Would've taken her again for Intermediate Chinese but she was teaching at 8 am.
super easy and nice!! she's really caring and engages in conservation with you. plenty of extra credit opportunities as well.

Shao laoshi was the best! I was worried about learning Mandarin Chinese but she made learning really easy and fun. If you actually take the time to do the homework and study for quizzes, you'll get an A for sure.

SHE'S THE BEST TAKE HER. She's the funniest professor ever I spend half the lecture laughing @ her jokes. Her lectures are amazing. She explains things really well, gives plenty of examples. Graded by lots of different things so it's easy to get an A even if you do badly on a couple things. I love her so much one of the best profs I've had at NYU.

Shao Laoshi is amazing! She is super sweet and will always help you out if you're feeling lost in the class, and offers tons of resources to practice Chinese. As long as you're polite towards her, participate during class (she is very strict about phones!), and study a normal amount for her tests, you will do well.
don't want to take her again..
