His homeworks are long and exams are very easy. Easy to get an A if you solve the homeworks.

Prof is a nice person, and understands his curiculum very well. Things get very Math heavy a lot of the time, so for people who really want to understand the inner workings in depth, this is a great course, otherwise it might be a little way extra for understanding Algorithms. The Homeworks are way harder than the end-term exams.

Fundamental Algorithms taught a lot but demanded a lot of effort from the students. However, the final grading was curved well and in consideration of the hardness of the course.

On a personal level, Professor Yap really cared about sharing his interest in the field and was very approachable to anyone genuinely interested in the area.

I took this mandatory class with another prof and dropped it as I was failing. Needless to say, I was very apprehensive of taking algo with Yap after reading the reviews below. The homework is difficult and time consuming; so are his tests. Thankfully, the graders were pretty generous and Yap gave a VERY good curve, so I passed. Recommend for algo!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yap is quite boring, and the course is full of homework that is always graded a few weeks later. The course was not too bad if you like math/stat-savvy materials or have affluent undergraduate math courses taken. Otherwise, you wouldn't like this course. However, professor Yap is really generous and gives a good curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you want to learn some ancient and obscure math from the last century that no one is mentioning anymore, you could probably take this course. Otherwise, PLS AVOID.Yap opinionated himself as a master in this ancient math and he wrote his own book on this in chaos.(Yes I know this is algo class, but take it if you want to see him lost in his math)

Prof. Yap is a very generous teacher. If you are lucky enough to find that he offer CSCI-GA-1170 Fundamental Algorithms in your semester, please choose his course. Though the homework is a little difficult, he will curve the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: AVOID Chee Yap like plague. His lectures are totally disaster. He doesn't know what is he teaching about and always make errors on class. The assignments and homework are very hard if you are not smart or you don't have background of algorithms. The lectures are VERY boring and useless for your future career as programmers.

Chee is a nice person, and very easy to speak with him after class or on Piazza, where he and his TA are very active. Lecure is useful, but recitation is pointless and the TA didn't teach well at all. However, you still need to go because of pop-quizzes. Exams are difficult (Midterm had an average below 50%) but he gives a pretty generous curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Don't take his Data Structure course. He can't clearly illustrate this course and his assignments are very confusing--it is very hard to understand what he wants students to do. Also, the exam is difficult.
He only gives 2 HWs for the entire semester and the test was mad easy. He literally posts the test online beforehand with slightly different numbers. Easiest cclass ever!

Chee is the only professor I've met in college who actually cares whether the kids are learning or doing well. He practically begs people to see him outside of class for class-related or for fun discussions. No professor is as generous with their time, and no professor will care about you or your success even 10% as much. Talk to him, you'll be gla

The best thing is that he responds to your emails and Piazza posts and the curve is GOOD  The worst thing is how vage and delayed his responses are. He almost never answers your question directly and is unclear in just about every instruction or comment he has on literally anything in the material, homework, or tests. Please avoid this professor.

If you want to go beyond the materials covered on the book and a get a more in-depth understanding, especially about algorithm analysis, then definitely pick this professor. His lectures and exams are adequately hard, but it's worth the pain. You learn a lot at the end of the day.  The professor is also very chill, and gives a very generous curve.

horrible prof. writes a lot of buggy code on the chalkboard - focus is on the algorithm, not the implementation, but it's CS102 - no one's a pro at java, you have to teach good code! doesn't explain concepts well. hw instructions are unclear. gave a huge hw the last week of classes (worth 1.5x normal) and ignored requests for extensions. avoid!!

Very smart man, but it is often difficult to understand the point he is trying to get across. Homework is really difficult and takes a LONG time. He gave up 3 programming assignments due the day before the midterm. The exams are difficult but not impossible, and he curves generously. If you do all the homework, you will do fine in the class.

Truly brilliant man, but his teaching leaves something to be desired. Expect homework assignments to take longer trying to figure out what he wantsfixing errors than actually coding. Overall learned a lot but it was through his vague homework make out of class work take longer than expected.
He is insanely smart and very helpful in office hours. His exams are very difficult, but he also curves generously. Definitely the best CS professor I've had so far.

Do not expect to understand his lectures if you are not VERY familiar with the topics beforehand. He sometimes even failed to make sense some topics to himself during the lecture. The horrible grader in Fall2013 did not understand most homework problems and expect uniformed answers. This class might kill your interest if you are not strong in mind!
He is a smart guy but poor teacher. He make the ideas hidden behind his formal notations. The exams are too much difficult than homework and lectures.

His course is not easy I have to say, which means if you dont wana attend each lecture but just stay at home or hang out, you may get something around B or even lower however clever u r. Anyway, he is a good instructor and his class is of great help for understanding ( if u have listened 2 other algorithm courses, u know what i m saying )
His class is not for entry level students, especially who has taken any algorithms class before. But if you can make it through, you would really learn a lot out of that class.
Course content is good. The lecture quality and grading is poor
class average was in the 40s-50s but the smart ones got 90s... made us look bad... He should teach only honor courses. his exams are impossible

Professor Yap is more suitable to teach advanced students, so having him to teach introductory class is a bad idea at the start.  The ones that made it through his class are cut out for Ph. D. program.

Professor Yap is the type of teacher who may be tough but makes you learn more than you thought you could.  He does not design the class to be a walk in the park, but if you are able to finish it, you will be a better computer scientist.  Also, he is extremely approachable.

Took three theory courses before this, loved the subject going in, had a newfound hatred of theory coming out.  Smart man, but no clue how to assemble thoughts into a coherent lecture or course.  Wrote a horrible manuscript and made us use it as the main text.  He does try to help you if you have difficulty, but has no ability to actually do so.

Worst Professor concerned only about his research, doesnot know how to teach - unorganized, confused, makes easy things very difficult, difficult HWS, Midterms, Finals. I would give this prof F on my grading. Lectures are word puzzles, notes are terribly badly written- i wasted this class trying to understand them all the time and losing to it
Hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, confusing, hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, hard, confusing, hard, hard hard.  HARD.

Terrible! Lectures were scattered, irrelevant to the homework. Readings were convoluted, error-prone and terse. Homework and exams were ridiculously difficult. Assigned 2 NEW readings the week of the final, with a lecture 2 days before the final. 1 day for review. New material was 30% of the exam.
worst professor! I wonder why he still can teach in the university...
No Comments

Terrible teacher.  Very unorganized in class and homeworks are much too complicated to complete in the given time period.  Lecture notes are overly-complicated and utterly useless.  It's easier to get material from other prof's websites on the Internet.  Smart man but poor teacher for this course...

Just Awful.  His lectures and class notes are disorganized and rambling. The homework assignments cover material not discussed in class or in class notes. Extremely ambiguous requirements for homework assignments.

What else is there to say that hasn't been said. Professor Yanni made me fall in love with History and understanding how everything can be viewed from so many lenses. Its incredible, his class was the first I had taken at NYU and I was blown away. This how I imagine scholars to be. So much respect for him.

I took three undergraduate courses with Professor Kotsonis, and I consider him the most exemplary professor I have ever encountered. He embodies the rational voice of academia, consistently approaching social issues with a humanistic perspective. It is like a wonderful academic exploration during my time at NYU: I will never forget it.

Prof. Kotsonis is definitely one of the best historians at NYU. Some utilitarian students dislike him because they always believe grades are everything, overlooking the intrinsic value of knowledge itself. It's rare to encounter professors with such a strong sense of humanistic care.
Funny dude, hella interesting lectures, and not too much necessary reading (I didn't do any of the assigned readings). Most of your grade is dependent on your TA but they all seem chill
lectures were boring and optional ur grade mainly depends on the TAs who are extremely strict graders i would avoid if u want a easy A

His lectures are heavy on random historical trivia where you can get from Wikipedia. No actual textual analysis. Choose your TA wisely. Ours promised to "consider" our desired grades, then promptly forgot. Her feedback consists of 2 underlines on the first page. No comments, no rubric, making it blatantly obvious she never truly read our work.
he's so funny but lectures could seem to drone on at times since he just spoke the entire class. your grade depends entirely on the TAs tho
Slightly concerned what my grade is going to be in this class. All I can say for future students in this class is actually show up lol.

Prof. Yanni himself is a good Professor. He cares about the subject. The TA sucks. Read at least one novel every week and participate in the class. Some novels are good. No participation leads to a low grade. Two papers throughout the semester, but the grading criteria are bad. No option to rewrite for a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting class that gives you the opportunity to read a lot of major works of literature and get history and analysis on them. There are a lot of readings to keep up with though, and he assigns the hardest ones first so people drop the class. Your grade depends on how strict your TA is.

Course is just as interesting as the name sounds. The assigned texts also get easier as the semester goes on. Yanni is v funny and explains concepts in the text in an easy to understand way. Just write down like 20% of what he says in your papers. Only two papers, midterm and final. Same prompt, second is longer word count. Lana is the goat TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not only a good historian, but also a good professor and lecturer. The readings are hard, but the lecture will show the connection with reading and inspire the interesting part of the readings. Some of my views are established and clarified by him and his lecture, and he is so open to different perspectives. I am glad that I take the course.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You're grade is 99% up to your TA but Yanni himself is hilarious and makes going to lectures worth it. If he says something is important, make sure to remember and quote him on your essays. Entire grade is made up by 2 essays and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Yanni's Core 500 in summer 2023, and I am taking him again this year. Many negative reviews stem from TA' strict grading, but I don't think this reflects the course. Yanni is a highly caring and open-minded professor—a rare quality in today's society. We shouldn't focus solely on grades; the process is just as important. Take it!

Seeing all the reviews regarding Texts & Ideas made me want to write this review. I've taken both Texts and Ideas and an economic course with professor Kotsonis. By far he is he funniest and best lecturer I have had at NYU, this recent texts and idea semester, the TA's were incredibly strict in their grading, but it shouldn't reflect his evaluation
The professor is great. The TAs are extremely RIGID and STRICT.

Yanni is an ordinary professor who doesn't care about his students. The grade is assigned randomly, and almost all of the TAs are tough graders. You can take the class if you want B or lower. Btw, there are lots of text and idea classes in which you can grind for an A, so avoid this class and this boring professor to save your gpa.

Have no idea how the final score was determined... TAs grade unreasonably strictly. The professor is excellent, but unfortunately he does not determine the grades. If you want to take this class, I recommend asking someone who has taken it before what their TA is like.

The final letter grade is assigned without clear cutoff and rubric. TAs are intentionally cutting grades through participation because they expect you to read a book every week. I suggest not putting too much effort into this core because you end up with Bs and lower anyway, unless you are a writing genius. Horrible.
TA gives low grade.
Professor was fantastic however TAs were tough graders. Don't know how you can get past that but good class outside of that

Worst professor I've ever had at nyu. Mumbles for the lecture and leaves everything to TA. TAs are even worse: they are exceptionally strict on essay and grading feedback makes no sense. Avoid at all cost.
B for participation... Not sure about TA's grading criteria

Professor Yanni's lectures is intriguing and engaging. However, the TAs at this class are EXTREMELY strict. They are unclear on the grading criteria for participation. There's not too much workloads but be prepared to receive low grades.
The teaching assistants are unreasonably strict, and many students receive Bs or lower. The professor's lectures are very engaging, but be prepared to receive low grades when selecting this course.
The professor is perfect, but the TAs are so strict.
Prof Yanni is my favorite professor, he is the GOAT.

I do not understand why so many people give such high rates. The course grade depends totally on TA, and my TA is so parsimonious that he did not give nearly a single A! Nearly everyone in this class gets a bad grade like B or B+. So avoid at all cost!

I really enjoyed this class and loved Professor Yanni—he was super funny and made Russian history enjoyable. The only downside is that he doesn't handle the grading; the TA does. If you have any concerns about your grades, he will always refer you back to the TA. The class includes just one midterm, which you need to study for, and a final paper.

His lectures were simply the best ones I had during the semester, he just knows a lot about the subject and makes it easy to follow and understand. All the grading is made by the TAs, which I was really lucky to choose the best one (shoutout to Aviv). I really enjoyed this class and would take it again.

Yanni is lovely, his lectures are engaging and interesting (but sometimes are not very relevant to the main class concepts). Assignments are easy and manageable, but grades depend on your TA - Caitlin was confusing when answering questions, a harsh/unclear grader, and makes you wonder if she knows the material any better than the students do.

Cultures and Context: Russia; Yanni is an amazing professor. He is really knowledgable and clearly passionate about his field (easy on the eyes, too). Lectures usually fly by since they're usually pretty dense (but digestible if you read the chapters occasionally). Recitation instructors grade you; Caitlin was nice but a bit of a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If Professor Kotsonis comes to class prepared he is very good at hiding that behind unrelated ramblings and awkward tangents. This Professor didn't seem to take his class very seriously which was annoying.
"accommodation is a euphemism for incompetency"

Took Utopias and Dystopias. One of the best orators ever. Lectures were extremely interesting and compelling. Talks a variety of philosophical ideas and opens up your mind to new approaches to the topic. Genuinely the only professor that made me enjoy going to class and listening to his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure if I'll have a professor quite like him again. Really focused on actually teaching you how to learn and analyze rather than the material itself. Though lectures are mostly him talking, he is a great orator and manages to make the content interesting. Take his class, wish I had a full semester with him.

Be prepared to read!!! Weekly readings consisted of 300-500 pages. The professor would cold-call students during lectures. Grades primarily depend on you're TA.  Professor rumored to cut down on A's in the course. TAs are crazy, they asked me to change my midterm (35% of my final grade) a few days before it was due. Be prepared to work!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kotsonis is absolutely amazing. His lectures are incredible, and I would recommend everyone to take one of his classes. He cares about his students and tries to keep a light and fun mood when talking and discussing incredibly dense/difficult material. This class had a lot of readings but was very enjoyable!
Great lecturer - makes topics interesting and engaging. Extremely smart guy who is always down to have discussions/answer questions/support his students.

Amazing professor. Cultures and Contexts are known to be on the tougher side, but I took this class as a freshman and was extremely doable. You only have a written midterm and final essay for the whole semester. The lectures are incredibly interesting and Yanni is really engaging. Get ready to see a lot of lollipops!
best professor ive had so far, funny and interesting lectures

no slides or lectures notes, he just talks for an hour or so, but his lectures are incredibly structured and easy to follow! TA's grade everything but they're all incredibly knowledgeable and overall amazing. not enough lollipops in the world i would trade for taking this class again with this prof!

YANNIISTHEBESTPROFESSORATNYU. First off, HE'S SO CUTE...Also, his class is so interesting like its a required class and I wouldve taken it even if it wasn't. His lectures are interesting, entertaining, and hilarious. You learn so much from him because he's so knowledgeable so just be sure to reserve your spot in his class if you get the chance

King of kings at NYU right here and now. His lectures are INCREDIBLE, THOUGHT PROVOKING. Every time I walk into class, its just story time about pre revolutionary Russia. He is incredibly considerate, extremely understanding, a wildly interesting person. IF YOU SEE HIS NAME, PUT YOURSELF DOWN FOR HIS CLASS!!
Well, I would say that Mr. Kotsonis is the best history professor in this university. He is caring, charming, and humorous. Taking his class is the best decision I have ever made.

The most caring, tolerant, and funny professor. A great introduction to the material. You can learn a lot without too much pain. It really helps you think and stay curious about Russia and beyond, which is what the CORE class is supposed to be.

Very polite and intelligent professor for utopias & dystopias, probably the best texts and ideas you can take. Course is graded by 2 papers (6 page midterm, 10 page final) and 2 exams. Very memory intensive and reading heavy, hard to get a good grade.

good selection of books, lectures are funny but veer to tangents unrelated to the book. grading entirely dependent on TA. participation worth 30%. attendance at lecture is taken randomly, which is kinda shady because it wasn't announced at the beginning of the semester. no reason for the final to be 10 pgs long. overall still a solid choice for t&i
Great professor who genuinely cares about the class and the students. Expect coursework to be very memory intensive, graded by 2 essays and 2 close-book paper tests.

Prof Kotsonis was fantastic, and taking this seminar over the J-Term was really great. He was understanding with regards to absences, and only really asked that you do the readings to a degree that would enable you to participate in class discussion. 100% would take this course again, and the Professor was one of my favorites at NYU so far.
Legend. Can't speak for larger lectures since ours was a seminar, and J term was short. He graded fairly and gave quality advice. Take his seminars if you can, you won't regret it.
Yanni is the absolute best lecturer of all time. Witty, kind, flexible, and always up for a good discussion/debate. Take any of his classes at least once before you graduate. You won't regret it.

The professor's lectures were very informative and related to the overall course material. He also made it engaging and was very humorous. However, the readings were a lot. If you've read a good chunk of the modern dystopias, like 1984 or Handmaid's Tale, the course will get easier as you approach the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Barely showed up to class and got an A. You just need to know how to write two papers which are each worth 40% of your grade. A book or two is read per week but you just need to know what books to use to write your papers.

Great professor for Utopias and Dystopias; homework involved reading novels and a short discussion once a week. Two papers, 6 and 10 pages, each worth 40%, and graded by the TA. Lectures were interesting and it is vital to take notes in class. Good guy and very understanding. Would take again.

Yanni gave one of the best history lectures at NYU. The classroom experience is thought-provoking. He is willing to spend so much time outside of classroom talking with you if you are genuinely interested in the concept. TA completely determines your grade, so tragedy might occur. But it's a humanity class, so it's very subjective and it's normal.

This is my 2nd core class with Yanni. He gave us really interesting analysis on utopian & dystopian novels. Remember to take complete notes so that you can reflect these points in two papers. The TAs merely determine your grade, so be aware of that. Overall, a great and solid choice for core and one of my best memories at NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yanni's a great lecturer, really interesting. But he does go on for the whole hour with little visuals (he'll write a few words on the board, but there's no ppt or notes to follow along with) so u have to pay attention and go to class. TAs do all the grading so try to get along with them. Main complaint is the lack of organization
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Kotsonis is knowledgable about Russian history and relevant analysis, and a great person to talk. His lectures are dense and useful, and relevant stuff will be tested, so plz go to his lectures. Readings are not that much, usually textbooks and some novels, but they will be tested in the two in-class midterms. BTW, CHOOSE A GOOD TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible choice for your Cultures and Contexts class. Lectures are just him speaking for the whole time but are very interesting and entertaining. Course material is really good and comprehensive too. A lot of grading is done by the TAs but I had solid ones this semester.

Amazing professor. Take this class for your core. He keeps the lecture engaging and is very passionate on the subject. Exams are solely graded by the TAs so beware of that. You do receive the exam topics beforehand, so you should be good. If you pay attention in lecture you should be able to receive an A. Readings are not necessary before class

Professor Kotsonis seemed like a decent guy, and gave good lectures. The TAs entirely determine your grade, so beware of that. From what I heard, all 3 of them were pretty tough. Recitation attendance was mandatory, but no attendance was ever taken at lecture. Readings didn't matter if you understood the material. Solid choice for Core class.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yanni is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject but his lectures are very dense and sometimes repetitive. There is typically no visual aid; he simply talks at you for the entire (1hr 15min) class. My grade was entirely determined by my TA, as the TA does all of the exam/paper grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a phenomenal lecturer. He does lecture at you for a solid 1hr 30 mins, but he keeps it interesting. He lets the class choose 10 topics that can come up on the exam beforehand and he chooses 4 of those topics and a picture for the exam. In the exam you have to write any tangible argument regarding the assigned topics and pictures.

Great lecturer. I will say that my attention often wandered after 45 min, but only because he would talk about one specific idea or theme to the point of repetition. The textbook's expensive & dull, but other readings were pretty interesting. As far as core classes go, Kotsonis makes his a solid choice, and he's got a good sense of humor to boot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great option for the Cultures & Contexts Core, highly recommend. However, lectures aren't posted, you do need to show up and take notes. I didn't really read the textbook except for the final paper, wikipedia was sufficient for the tests. A large portion of the class is based on your TA, but I didn't hear that any were particularly bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yanni is always engaging in lecture and has a great sense of humor. The only issue I took with the class was the infrequency of graded material, but the exams were never problems if you study notes and readings a bit (I never really did and made Bs and B+s). Even if you aren't huge on history, there is relevant knowledge to be gained in this class.

absolutely brilliant lecturer.  grading in the class depends solely on your TA, so make sure you choose carefully with that (katya, if she's still around).  textbook reading is super helpful for essay exams, but honestly no need to read supp stuff. if you have to take CC, might as well make it one with a good prof, like this guy

Hard class; didn't enjoy it at all. Then again, I'm a business major with no interest in history who had to take a history class as a requirement. If you like history you might like it. Yanni is also a really cool guy

Doesn't seem at all involved with students and all grading and feedback for tests is left up to the TAs. Lectures are hard to understand sometimes because he talks extremely fast and without the use of a microphone while pacing up and down the aisles. Seems rather arrogant and tries too hard to be funny. Make sure to participate in recitation!

I would watch the Yanni Kotsonis Show if it was on tv. Really smart guy, really funny. Lectures are never boring, and while he does call on students it's never in a mean-spirited way. Not too much reading, occasional movies in class. That said, unless you go out of your way you will mostly be interacting with a TA for tests and grading.
Very clear lectures. Your work is graded by TA
Phenomenal instructor. If you attend lectures, you can  read up a little bit online and never touch the textbook. Occasionally calls on students in class.

Professor Kotsonis was an amazing professor. His lectures were clear and students always could understand where he was going and what point he was trying to make. He is also very understanding and genuinely cares for his students. If you attend lectures and recitations the class will be a breeze.

I think Yanni is a great professor. Really interesting lectures and incredibly engaging. However, what I find problematic is that a large part of one's grade is largely dependent on whether or not you are lucky in choosing a TA. I found my TA overall, unhelpful, irresponsible and unclear providing no clear feedback and ways to improve.
He is arrogant and his lectures can be unclear and unhelpful.

So glad I took my senior seminar with him. We all wrote different papers, but used the same collection of novels- classes were interesting because we all saw the books differently depending on the lens we were writing for. He was so helpful, meeting with us outside of class to personally aid our writing. He's the most brilliant teacher I had at NYU
Great teacher! Keeps class entertained. If you attend lectures you should be fine. One of my favorite classes this semester!
He is the best professor I had for my freshmen year, If you just put in a  bit of effort, you will do very well. Class is amazing
Take him, you won't regret. Don't miss him at NYU.
THE BEST TEACHER I HAD AT NYU!!!! he is simply amazing.

One of the best professors at NYU.  I am currently in his summer session course and was not at all excited about taking World Cultures: Russia but decided to take it since it was the only World Cultures course offered and I haven't regretted it at all.  Interesting class, extremely understanding... I definitely recommend taking a class with him.
fair...gives questions ahead of time...yes...but, don't get on his bad side, cuz he won't forgive you...

Yanni is amazing.  His lectures were really great and they went along with the assigned readings...also he gives you the exam questions in advance and is more than willing to help you with them.  During the strike, I visited him during office hours and he offered me an extra credit assignment because the strike interfered with my grade.  Great guy!
brilliant guy. class was interesting and engaging. really stimulated interest in the topic.

This guy is brilliant.  Has been known to use socratic method occasionally but not in a mean spirited way at all - used more to provoke discussion in quiet classrooms.  Definitely definitely take all of his classes...

Very interesting and intellectual professor, while still remaining very approachable.  He also gives exams questions well in advance in order to better prepare.  My only complaint is that he caused a lot of disruption by shutting down class because of the GA strike.
Curve is super easy, 87 and above is an A or something like that

She was the best professor who works hard for students including grading. Her exams were really straightforward, which means all the exams are from the homework. She even allowed one cheat sheet either printed or handwritten so you should be fine if you understand and copy the HW/slide examples to cheat sheet.

Lecture content was difficult, but made more difficult by her unorganized handwriting all over the slides. Can't hear her in the lecture hall either. However, she is a generous grader and curved exams.

Generous grading, 84.5 was the cutoff for an A. Curved exams by a lot. Not the best lecturer, speaks too softly, writes all over the slide in an unorganized manner which makes it very difficult to review later on. She tries, but she doesn't speak coherently, keeps interrupting herself.
For the comment which was talking about NYU math courses self studying - I accidentally hit 2. It should be 5.
As you all now, most NYU math courses requires you a self study. If you understand that, she is a good option to choose, fair exam, generous curve (gave 10 points), and dedication to help students

She gave 50% of the class A or A-, and most B range, which is very generous grading. She does her best all the time. The exams were really straightforward to her slide which is fair and the quiz are pass and fail system. She might not be the best prof by teaching, but, she was the best professor who genuinely work hard and care for students.

She is a really nice person, generous in grading, and accessible through email. Although she may not be the best lecturer I have had (her voice tends to be low in a large classroom), I personally like how she connects course materials to cutting-edge ML applications from time to time. She seems knowledgeable and open-minded in that regard.

Really bad lecturer, uses AI to generate her slides, and scribbles notes during lectures so you have to decipher those too. The class covers a lot of concepts but she ignores all of them and tests only on proofs instead. She curves a lot, but you'll have no idea of your actual grade until the end of the year.

She is not a very good lecturer and has hard-to-read handwriting. But she is really nice and supportive. I didn't do well at all in the two midterms but worked hard and scored high enough above average on the final. I was able to get to an A because she gave a very generous curve.

She's nice, accessible via email, her exams are very fair, and she gave a very generous curve. My problem with her is that she is very hard to understand in class. super easy

superr nice and includes memes in his lectures. didn't get the best grade in his class because of the midterms and finals but they were not too bad. gave a really generous curve since we are first year students. good reviews, records his lectures, very understanding, gives a few extra credit, take him!!

Take him. he was good. awesome. amazing.

Basically graded by TA. Recitation is mandatory, with weekly write ups and 2 presentations. Not a sexy class but a great easy fill for liberal arts requirement.

reviews.comment: lectures got a little boring at times but overall super interesting + amazing readings + we watched 3 very nice films in class! grade was based purely on essays. midterm + final was a take-home essay (48 hours for the midterm and ~5 days for the final.

Grade depends on TA but Professor Zhang is a great professor with great lectures. Her class is reading heavy but they are all engaging and interesting reads that are provided for you. Overall essays and tests are easy and lecture/info given are vehicles for success. Guidelines and grading criteria are also very clear.

Professors Zhangs class was super interesting. Shes one of the best professors Ive had at NYU. The class is reading heavy but the readings are all provided and super interesting. She gives out a lot of info in lectures. She doesnt just read of the slides and makes them really engaging. We had a take home midterm, 2 essays, and a final.

Eloquent lectures, easy to follow. good office hours Straightforward papers, only a total couple assignments for the semester. Papers are graded by TAs- recitations are chill show up and get participation. Prof Amy did asynchronous lectures this semester (fall 20) for remote learning, idk if that's subject to change in the future.
Amazing professor. Adapted to mid semester remote learning change extremely well. Thoroughly enjoyed her class. assignments, communicate with TA/participate, and youll be fine!

Prof. Zhang does a great job with organizing and explaining her main topics and themes in class, but not in the presentations, so you have to go to class to get all the information. As long as you pay attention to lectures and skim the readings, you'll do good in class. She and the TAs also do reviews of the readings before a midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Zhang is so nice! I took her last year for Anth and she was a real gem! However, your recitation professors are the ones who grade you. 3 papers, 2 exams. the midterm and final are based on stuff from the lectures. vocabulary, and a free response was on the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super nice and very accessible outside of class. Weekly quizzes and assignments keep things straightforward, and there's no midterm, so it's easy to stay on track even if you mess up a few quizzes. The final was a bit rushed, but he gave extra assignment points to help boost grades. Overall a fair class and a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
A topic as interesting as databases unfortunately has most of its intrigue squandered by the lecture style of this professor, as it is essentially just him reading slides.

He is a nice guy, grading is lenient and straightforward as long as you are doing the necessary work, but ultimately if you want a class that will help you learn, look elsewhere
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes can be stressful. A lot of people cheat and it is very disappointing that basically nothing is done to prevent cheating, so quiz averages may be high. However, the overall workload of the course is very low, and the final is not a big portion of the grade.

Half the class cheats on quizzes and bro doesn't seem to give a danm. Extremely horrendous lectures and explanations for problems. Problem wording is very confusing on quizzes and the final. And, he never makes any improvement/changes to his material. Do no take and RUN

doesnt teach except reading off of the powerpoint. whats the point? the material covered in class are all useless repetitions that will be the first thing to be replaced by chatgpt. he should just let us know the algorithm of the codes and give us some real data science prompts for us to run instead of snippets of leetcode questions.

RUN WHILE YOU STILL CAN. Quizzes every week account for 50% of your grade. Quiz a final questions have basically no partial credit: if you pass, good. If you cannot pass the test case, good luck on getting some partial credit of the grader is not lazy. Question wording is extremely unclear and stays the same. Lectures are horrible: he just reads.

bro gave an impossible final and decided not to curve it because a few people got a 100%. 1/3 of the class got a C as a result. He started the beginning of the year saying "the CS GPA is too high" and made it his personal mission to lower it.

Cheating was disappointingly overlooked. He told us all sem that we would likely fail the final but there would be a generous curve. I worked hard and got a 94 in the class and which got curved DOWN to an A- because a "surprising amount of ppl got 100s" on a test designed to be impossible. People get away with using AI, do with that what you will.
The worst lecturer I've ever heard. He had no idea what he was talking about.

Not the most engaging lecturer but very accessible material and very sweet. You're allowed to take notes, including code, to quizzes and the quiz problems were extremely similar to the homework problems

Horrible lecturer and his problems are much harder than other profs. But, the curve is insane. Failed both the midterm and final and still managed to get a B+ in the class. Just make sure you do all the homework and if you study more than I did you can definitely get an A.

He gave the most terrible lecture of all the professors I have taken, with a super unclear tone. The Ed notes have been used for a lot of years and never do any updates. He never prepares for lectures at all and reads notes. 16 questions for 75 minutes for the final are impossible to finish. Avoid him at all costs you can!!

The final exam consists of 16 questions for 75 minutes, which is absurd. He claims to grade quizzes with partial credit, but ultimately, only whether you pass the test does matter. Weekly quiz grades remain undisclosed, leaving you in the dark about your performance. It's baffling. You chose this course thinking he is an easy grader but is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: all the past replies shouldve waited for grades to come out… the final got curved anyways and announced it after the exam was done, plus 50% of your grade is basically free and I still ended the class with an A even though I got dogged on the final. The lectures itself were very dry but he knows his stuff

My guy. 16 coding questions in 75 minutes for an intro class? R u for real? The highest score was an 8/16 and many people got 0,1, or 2 of the 16 right with no points unless test cases r passed. Lectures consist of him sitting in a chair and talking into a mic. Kinda hurts to say bc he is nice and caring but u gotta up your game my guy. Best.
16 coding questions in final, but only 75 mins!!! It is impossible to complete it

NEVER gives students homeworks and quizzes back UNTIL THE END OF THE SEMESTER. I didn't even know whether I was passing by the time I took for final. GIVES horrendously difficult final totally different from sample final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He changed the final exam time from 110 min to 75 min two hours before the exam and send out an email which i didn't see it cuz i was in another exam. Final was so HARD he removed all mcq on the final exam only coding question. we had 75 min to finish 16 coding question that are hard af. NOBDOY finished the exam in time because it is impossible.

Zeidenberg is a double edged sword. 

This class will teach you a lot, and it will make you very good at Python and SQL database style programming, which will definitely help in real world careers and in interviews. 

He is also a genuinely nice, funny, and lenient person at his office hours.

So it pains me to say,
MY GOD HE IS A BORING LECTURER.
He replies to emails quickly. The midterm and final exams are easy — just the same questions with different numbers. His lectures are dull, but that's just how CS is; you can totally self-study.
Classic absent-minded professor.  Looks like he just woke up, but sharp as a razor.

Great professor. The exams and quizzes make up the majority of the grade, but they are doable if you stay with the class. He provides good notes to review and is easily accessible outside of class. Amazing guy overall
50% is graded by weekly quizes, which is extremely similar to HW(25%) and final(20%). As long as you are ok with weekly hw and go to class to take quiz once a week, you can excel at this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor with good intentions and good knowledge.

Zeidenberg is frieddddd. Literally the easiest class I have ever taken in my life including middle school. You pretty much just teach yourself the entire course but I feel that I have a pretty good grasp of Python now. The midterm and final are the EXACT same as the practice tests.

Homework is very little and easy, no attendance, but lectures have no organization, exam grading is extremely awful. You can enroll in this course if you just want to get credits and don't care about what you learn and grades at all. Otherwise, please stay away.

I took an intro course, so I can't complain much about the difficulty. We had weekly hw and quizzes, but they weren't too bad. If you just work hard and practice a lot yourself for the exams, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Midterm he told the class no partial credit. Midterm ended up being a disaster and he changed his mind on partial credit which screwed the people who didn't do all of the questions..Curved the midterm. Final was no partial credit and there was no partial credit. When doing final grades for Albert, he uncurved the midterm and no curve for the final.
Homeworks were not difficult at all. Grading was fair. Great person.
Great guy, even if his lectures are a little dry. Super chill and understanding. Best guy once you get to know him.

Textbook and attendance optional for CSCI-UA 2. Dry lectures, used them as study halls. Self-study is completely possible. Asking a question may become a battle of clarifying what your question is. Quizzes and assignments are easy.
he plays charlie brown music during class and most of the class is interactive via edstem, bad lecturer but hes nice. easy exam if u study

tbh not that bad. he's a very very very bad lecturer but it's easy to learn on your own, assignments are not hard, difficult midterm but very generous curve, i got a 40 but still have a B-. you should be fine if you give it a few hours a week to study.

Run for your life. Useless lectures and ridiculous midterm exam. you can barely hear him and he rambles on and on with no point. I don't mind most bad professors if I can study the material on my own but this was my breaking point (this class is genuinely a waste of your tuition). Still better than taking Versoza though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It becomes really easy this year. The midterm is exactly the same as the practice midterm, only data changes.
Overall, he is a very nice and lenient professor. Though the exams can be a big tough, it did somewhat reflect the practice exams. Very friendly professor overall!

The lecture is pretty well structured, but it is hard to hear his voice if you are not in the first row of the class. 
Just took the midterm, extremely hard, I don't know why he gives out his mocks that are so easy but a 10 times harder real exam. Not even finish the test... RUN
Not sure why people are hating on him. Not the most exciting lecturer, but nice and surprisingly funny at times. Long weekly assignments, easy midterm and final. Make use of tutors!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dry and you can honestly get away with just using the learning modules to self-teach. Homework can take a while but very consistent with the assignment schedule. Midterm was easy as long as you understand what you're doing.

He excels as doing anything terrible a professor could legally do: he minus points from students for doing extra credits, he make his online final ten freaking multiple-choices unrelated to what he taught, and his lectures are good enough to to make any coffee bean fall asleep.

Moreover, his replies to students are as rude as my comment.

The lectures did not help me learn the material. The professor speaks in a low monotone voice making it hard to listen for long. If you end up taking this course, expect to end up teaching yourself the material because the professor does not help much. The homework load is strenuous. Take this course with another professor and in person if you can.
He gives crazy finals.
The worest professor I have encountered in NYU so far. He does not put enough efforts into the class. Try some else if possible.
I think commenting on this website to tell people not to take his course is the best thing I can do. He is so disorganized. He gives up assignment grades so slow.
I don't understand those commenters that say he cares and friendly. Are they even real people? He is totally not possible. Please avoid him at all cost.
This is the worest professor you can ever have in NYU CS. He has a monotone tone and it seems he does not care about students at all.
Great professor, really cares about students and making sure you understand the material. Would definitely take again!

Prof. Zeidenberg is nice and knowledgable. He is assecible via Ed, email, and office hours. Given that this is the first time teaching this course, it's totally understandable that the class is somewhat unorganized during the first half. The second half of the course is going a lot better. 3 assignments + 3 quizzes + 2 exams. Very doable A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: During class, he speaks very softly and speaks with a monotone voice, making it extraordinarily hard for anyone to hear him. It might be better to take free online courses. His office hours do help you a lot if you attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Prof Zeidenberg for Data Management/CSCI-UA - 479. Overall he was very fair! Lectures were pretty dry to be honest, but it partially seems like the nature of the material. The number of assignments and grading criteria was very fair. Very doable A or at least a definite pass as long as you put a little bit of effort in.

Was a decent professor to begin learning programming. Assignments were doable and was always easily accessible either through office hours or email for questions. Lectures could get boring although he did try to encourage the class to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He tries to engage the class a little in class but everything can be learnt from lectures. Quizzes and assignments are riddled with logical/grammatical errors. The assignments are enjoyable but the quizzes and exams are just really a way to gauge how well you can look stuff up, or worse, cheat. Yea, take another teacher.
GPU elective course; fair workload; insightful lectures from which everyone learns a lot; lenient grading

Get ready to self-study from the textbook since his slides are kinda useless. Labs aren't much code (number of lines wise), but it is still hard to get your head around the MPI/OpenMP/CUDA syntax especially when you are doing it for the first time, and labs grade is 30%. Has a massive ego and isn't respectful while answering QS on Brightspace
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Z is very nice! He makes class interesting and is good at explaining concepts. He will give you many challenges, but that is part of the learning process and its rewarding when you succeed. Lenient grader and encourages students.

Not hard to get a good grade and homework and exams are super easy, but professor can be extremely condescending and rude to students who have simple questions. Take for easy A- or A but don't expect to receive a lot of useful help.
Without question the easiest CS class I've taken so far, HW is light and exams are open-book and take-home.
The class work is simply easy and straightforward, and he taught it in a very clear way, 10/10

Zahran cares about you learning, giving you the tools you need to succeed. All of his homework and exams are easy and he gave multiple extensions. Understanding some of the concepts can be tricky, but he is always there to help.

Prof. Zahran is a must-take, given the opportunity. His lectures are not all that boring, given his humor and interest in the material. He really does just care about his students learning the material and not focusing on the final grade. If you can, take him!

I strongly recommend Z for neuro-divergent students for tough classes like OS because he refuses to stress out the students. The lectures, slides, homework, and exams are well-organized, and clear. The grading is generous. If you have time to delve deeper, he will also refer you to supplemental material.

Might be the easiest A course I have taken so far with COREs taken into account. Choose if you want to get an A/A- with almost no effort, do not choose if you really want to learn OS. There is almost no source code or real implementation of any kind, what it has are more on the conceptual side.

Zahran is a good lecturer and makes online classes engaging, even though I don't like OS. The labs and homework are also relatively easy if you put in the time. But the exams are dangerously short, so getting a single true/false question wrong means your grade does down by 10% on a midterm or final, and the questions are sometimes confusing.
Professor Z is a master of teaching. His organizes his OS course so well that I feel like it is one of the best online courses I have ever taken! Don't worry about the grades cuz he will curve a lot.

Excellent professor, extremely fluid and clear lectures. Explain topics throughout the course thoroughly and with plenty of examples, always in a concise manner. Fair exam, lab, and homework grading. He is the best lecturer I have had so far at NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof z is laid back, interested in getting the point across clearly, and actually cares about your knowledge building. he set fair deadlines and gave us enough instructions during lectures to help with the structure. OS is a really hard class, but his method makes it interesting and likable. Take him!!!

I was a bit skeptical going into OS with prof Z, but he's structured the class very well, and you actually LEARN so much! He's focused on the material, and you need to attend lecture and pay attention of course, and the exams and labs are also fair given how much he explains them in lecture. Take him for OS!

Z is the most hilarious prof ever. So many excellent jokes to keep us engaged for GPU architecture. You get complementary high quality, stand-up performance in addition to the course content. Very clear, helpful, and kind. Deadline is tight, but otherwise the lecture, the assignment, the learning environment and the slides are all perfect.

he's more interested in being snarky than being understanding. I don't get it because we all know Operating Systems is a hard class, but ok he chooses to be an ass about stuff like deadlines and whatnot. if you can stand that type of a professor, go for it.

If you're used to self-learning with things like a textbook or the internet, you may have a tough time since the lectures diverge from the given textbook and the content doesn't lend itself very well to online study. Exams can also involve tricky/sneaky questions, but if these things don't sound like issues then the course is worth a shot

Zahran is possibly the best CS lecturer I have ever had. He adapted to remote learning very well and makes classes interesting and engaging. His course is difficult, but the subject matter is difficult, so you need to try moderately hard to comprehend the material. Other than that, though, the course isn't much work at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He does not explain things simply. He explains things in a complicated matter. Usually with professors like this I just read the textbook, but the course only has suggested readings that dont follow the course material closely. His homework and exams are fair.

Prof. Z is one of the best professors at NYU. When you take his class you get a better understanding of how a computer actually works, his roasts of Java are hilarious, and I'm glad he forced us to program in C. Overall great dude who really wants students to leave his class with actual knowledge.

Professor Zahran is definitely one of the best professors at NYU. Not only is the material well-explained, he also tests you fairly on it. Hes also really funny which makes the class enjoyable. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Parallel with Z. He's super knowledgeable about the content, pretty willing to discuss the real world applications of what we're learning. He liked to stress that the exam questions were more about understanding concepts instead of memorization, which I liked. He's pretty troll with comic sans slides and some jokes during lecture, I loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Comic Sans slides. Lectures are as interesting as his slides that he has been reusing since the spring'13. I appreciate his acutely dry humor but he does not appreciate doing more for any students so just make sure you submit everything on time and not ask him questions that start with "I am confused about..." bc he wants more "difficult questions"

Took PAC II with him. Great Professor and funny guy. Start your project early. Midterm was medium/easy, final was hard. Make sure you ask him what to expect on the exams. FYI you will not hear back from NYU if you apply to the MSCS until your final grade is submitted. They didn't really tell us that which made for a pretty nerve-wracking April.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zahran is awesome. He constantly roasts the class and is an all around hilarious dude. Explains things really well, super accessible, cares a lot about his students. His exams are hard but fair, and you get 1 cheat sheet for midterm, and 2 for the final. He's very knowledgeable about CSO and very passionate about the material. Highly recommend.

Parallel was probably one of the most enjoyable NYU classes so far. Z is hilarious if you don't mind the jokes directed at you. Homework is infrequent and easy. We only did 2/3 of the labs, and those weren't that complicated. His exams made me feel like I wasted time studying because of how easy they were. Z is the man!!!!!
Prof.Z teaches very well and his class is very well structured. Not an easy A.

Here's the thing about Z. If you're a pretty advanced student, I would recommend him. He's funny, gives few assignments, and the topic is interesting. However, he can also be kind of condescending, sarcastic, and unhelpful. Going to his office hours, he was more interested in being snarky than helpful, but if you don't need the help, he's a blast.

Prof Z is the best pro pf in the cs department for CSO. He assigns the perfect amount of work, and his exams are elegant and short. Plus his lectures are very interesting and funny. His class was my favorite among the classes I ever took at NYU.

Z teaches and organizes his lectures into themes. You wont do well simply by memorizing the lectures. if you understand the major themes for GPUs, you will do fairly well for the final. bulk of the grade is also from the project. hw/labs are on the light side. this class is as hard as you want your project to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the best! CS201 was a good class, did the hws, went to class and I learned a lot
Professor Zahran is by far the most qualified professor in the whole computer science department! Very intelligent, engaging lectures and a great educator.

His slides are oversimplified, you can learn nothing from his slides if you skip the class. And his explanation is not clear enough. Although there are few homework, you have to study really hard before exams in order to get a good grade.

Go to class. Slides aren't enough unless you supplement with the textbook, plus his lectures are great: great explanations and savage jokes. 2 labs and 2 HWs, don't wait until the last minute to do them, and make sure you're well-versed with the material before attempting. He tests concepts so make sure yours are clear. Cheat sheets allowed on exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Z was a very fair professor. Go to lecture, his slides are usually not detailed enough to study from, and you'll also catch his lame, sarcastic humor. Only 2 homework assignments and 2 labs, and they were very straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Z had well structured and organized lectures. His lectures moved fast so try not to skip lecture. He does a good job at reinforcing the different levels of abstraction in CS. Class was light on the HW and it wasnt too difficult. That said, majority of your grade was from exams. The actual exams were a tad harder than his practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Z is a great professor! He's funny and engaging, his lectures are clear, and the homework is pretty straight-forward. The midterm was easy, but I think we did better than he expected so the final was a bit harder. Not terrible if you study but do beware that some of the questions are less about memorizing and more about problem solving.

Good prof for parallel. Really funny and savage. Material is somewhat dense but he teaches in a pretty slow pace. 1 midterm, 1 final, 2-3 hws, 3 labs. Much less work than other electives. Labs, hWs, and tests are kind of challenging but very doable. Allows cheat sheets for exams. Extends deadlines when needed. He curves final grade at the end.

Z is probably one of the better professors in the CS department at NYU. He is so cute with his lame jokes in class and Z is a lenient grader. A real stand up guy and tries to help out his students whenever possible. Z is the best CSO professor by far so make sure you take him and you will not regret it.

My fav prof at NYU. Prof Z's humor suits all CS majors and makes his lectures interesting. Labs and HWs aren't hard but they do take some time to do. Tests are very fair and its answers can be directly derived from slides. Although he works on various research in this field, he knows his stuff and genuinely cares about students.

Teaches CSO only in the fall recently. Final is easy, midterm is challenging but fair. Slides alone wont help, either go to class or read the txtbk. 3 HWs: they short but hard. 3 labs: they easy but long. Overall not too much work, but a bit hard to get an A. He is funny, but has a low voice so sit at the front. Recitation is useless, nobody goes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Z knows his stuff and will teach you everything you can handle (usually less if he doesn't have faith in the class). The labs were simple and midterm was average. As long as you understand his slides and take some notes, you're good. He's also funny and tries to be realistic in terms of structure and difficulty for the class.

Definitely the easiest professor to take for CSO. He keeps his lectures interesting with a lot of jokes but he also really knows his stuff. It's not a difficult class as long as you do all of the work well (which isn't hard) and pay attention. Without a doubt recommend you take CSO with him.

Lowkey one of the best CS profs at NYU. My guy Z is really the man. His lectures are funny and he cares more about your understanding of the course material than your ability to replicate what he teaches. Course material can be dense, but he's more than happy to help with any trouble. Tbh if you're not taking a class with him, you're slacking fam

One of the best professors at NYU. Extremely knowledgeable. Very fair grader (in terms of final grade. Expect uncurved midterms and such during the semester). Important class, great feedback, cares a lot about the students.
Great Class! Easy Grader! Only complaint I have is that he has a low voice so I always had to make sure to sit in front to hear him well!

Professor Z can be hard to hear, and the material is difficult. He's genuinely a nice person, and wants students to do well. His lectures are fun to listen to because he has a great sense of humor. 2 homework assignments, 2 exams, 3 labs. IMO the homeworks were harder than the labs, but labs take a long time to do. Grades very fairly.

Lots of material covered in the lectures, much of which is off the top of his head and not in the slides (so go to class). Z is a great professor and is very clear, and will keep explaining things until you understand.  Very informative and helpful class for CS majors but a little unfair for the minors as the material is pretty in-depth.

While challenging Parallel Computing taught a lot and served as a great introduction to various different languages. The labs were difficult but this was expected and Zahran tried to offer helpful advice for completing them.
Helpful and passionate about his subject. Labs are little tough but manageable.
Decent prof

Sue Zizza is just amazing. As long as you come to class on time and attempt to do your work to the best of your ability, Sue will probably be one of the most caring and fun professors you'll ever have. You learn so much from her class, and if you're lucky, she may offer some amazing outside of class opportunities. Take Sue Zizza. HOORAY!!!!!!

Sue is incredible! Yes, she's tough and you do NOT want to be on her bad side, but you will LEARN. Her biggest pet peeve is being late, that's the one thing. She is patient, will answer all your questions, and is honestly a pretty flexible grader. You will learn so much from her, I love her so much. Definitely my favorite prof. HOORAY!

Sue is hilarious and really cares about her students' learning. 
HOORAY (this word will take on a whole new meaning after this class.)
The goat. Treats everyone like family approaches teaching sound with a passion that resonates.
I LOVE SUE ZIZZA. TAKE SUE SHE IS SO AWESOME NO COMPLAINTS CHANGED MY LIFE. (HOORAY you'll get it soon)

She moves very slowly at the beginning and it can be kind of discouraging and boring but by the end of the first month you will love her! I learned a lot about ProTools and sound. She is very caring and funny and has a lot of professional experience she will discuss in class.
Loved having her for sound image. She is truly passionate about what she teaches and it shows!

She prides in her experiences in the industry. She has her ways of doing things and we have to follow it, because she claims it's the best and only way to do it. But it's really funny when she compliments you after you turn in a recording of a sound you took from youtube. The irony. She's one hilarious woman.

Sue Zizza is a professor you won't ever forget after taking her class. She is quirky, funny, and charismatic, but when the time comes, she is a respected veteran in her field who demands the best of every student in her class. Her technical lectures may drag, but she ensures that you leave with the basic Pro Tools and audio recording techniques.

Sue is a easy grader and treats her student like her grandkids. Has her own rituals which you must accept it. However, if you really want to learn something from the class you better choose someone else. Though Sue is experienced in the industry, she doesn't really teach much technical stuff and she constantly miss the class.

I like how her projects are structured and I think she has a great personality once you get to know her. My only criticisms are that her homework isn't always entirely clear and a few of her more lecture-y classes are a bit boring. The TV shoot tickets are a plus tho.

I don't know why she doesn't have better reviews bc in my my experience, she has been great. You can tell she really cares about her students and is very knowledgable about the sound industry. I will say at the beginning of the year, she was a little hard to follow when learning protools but besides that her class is pretty easy and engaging.

Sue is one of the most passionate and knowledgable professors/mentors I've had the pleasure of working with. Her class is the reason I fell in love with sound; she is clear with instructions and teaches new material at a very reasonable pace. You will truly be missing out on so much if you don't take her class.

Sue can be misunderstood. She genuinely cares about sound design and teaching her students everything about it. As long as you follow her instruction you'll get an A, she gives unlimited redos and doesn't want you to stress about grades but rather learning the skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious
