She does not believe in power points either, which will make lectures kind of dense but honestly what you really need is just to read what's assigned and it will be an easy A.

Prof Khan's class is boring and not what you think: 1-2 classes learning of indigenous peoples, rest based on colonization. Class is based on 4 essays (not hard), but the prompts can be very vague and open ended. Most frustrating parts: lectures w ridiculous tangents; you have to get a 95 to get an A (you can get a 94 on every essay and get an A-)

Prof Khan is one of the kindest professors I've had so far at NYU. Her lectures tend to be very long and often times very boring. She gives readings every week and has required class discussions that EVERYONE must participate in. Definitely take her class if you're looking for an A and can deal with tons of readings & long boring lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she is so kind and understanding. i am currently enrolled in her class and it is not demanding at all. her AIs are also wonderful. she is extremely passionate and cares deeply about what she teaches. the content itself is boring but that is not really her fault, she does her best to make it exciting and is very engaging.

The TA's are amazing, but Mrs. Khan's teaching style is so hard to follow. She refuses to use powerpoints and instead repeats herself constantly, calling out students, who need to use the restroom, as irresponsible. If you have an opinion that is different than hers, good luck. She knows a lot about the subject, but you seem to learn nothing.

Professor Khan is the nightmare of all professors. Her lectures are extremely unfocused, dull, and largely pointless. She tends to over-explain and speaks tangentially very often and is thus an inefficient teacher. Her grading is nitpicky to ridiculous degree. Do not take her course unless you have a lot of patience and are willing to teach yoursel

This will be difficult if you 1. aren't a sociology/anthropology major OR 2. don't engage with the readings and participate in recitation. That said, only 3 response papers (1000 words each) the whole semester and one final. Very friendly and helpful one-on-one, so definitely go to office hours.

Professor Khan is one of the friendliest professors at NYU. She tries to get to know her students even if the class is a lecture. However, sometimes you may feel like you're in high school again. She takes attendance in every lecture, gets upset when people are late, and may even point you out if you're not paying attention in class. Class is okay.

Most obnoxious and pretentious teachers ever met. Shows up 5 minutes late to class and then individually scold any student who comes in after her.   Takes attendance at every lecture. Howls at students who get up to use the bathroom. Picks out individual students who don't raise hands and scolds them for not participating. Easy grading though
Nice person. Lectures are very repetitive. You need to engage with the class material yourself if you want to do well; it's not enough to go to class and take notes.

I took the honors thesis class with Professor Khan as well as grad course. She's amazing- very engaging, very helpful, very sweet! She loves what she's teaching and her excitement is contagious. You may have to work hard, but she's very much on your side and I felt her classroom was a fantastic environment to be a part of.
She's extremely helpful. but you need to do the work. 4 essays. the TA's grade it hard, but if you go to office hours it's very helpful and will boost your grade.

It was her first time teaching this class, so the syllabus was not really followed. There is a LOT of reading, but you just have to skim it. You have to write a paragraph a week about the articles, and there are 4 papers in addition to the final. If you meet with her during office hours you are sure to get at LEAST an A-.
Interesting class although it jumps all over the place, not bad for a map class, grade based on 4 essays, participation, attendance and a final.

This class is really easy and fun. She is the most helpful professor in the entire school. Everyone is always happy to be in her class and she makes the class unbelievably amazing. I LOVE HER. Oh yeah, she's SUPER HOT too

Her lectures are very clear but she can be repetitive. She takes attendance for lectures but its good for participation points. The class is easy if you incorporate class discussion into your papers, especially including key terms. Reading the entire books isnt necessary for getting an A if you take good notes

Honesty I read the rates to this prior 2 taking and thought it was an exaggeration. But, everything they said was the truth. The TAs arent familiar with the Caribbean so they learn about as we do and the essays aren't thought up until a week before they're due. Lecture notes don't help. TA only grade based on grammar. Khan is unorganized DONT TAKE.

Definitely the most boring class I have ever taken my entire academic year. The material is easy, but the grades do not match and TA's were not helpful at all! It also seems as though they do not read the essays and just give you whatever grade they please. do not recommend her

I mean, class is boring and everything, but hey, it's a requirement. Grading is pretty easy. Never did anything and got an A-.  Just don't buy the BS about only 2 absences. I missed about 12 classes, and the rest I signed in and left. It's easy and that's the bottom line. But God is it boring.
the only thing more horrible than this class is being burned alive... actually, its debatable

You wold think a class on the Caribbean would be fun right? I did. Beaches, sun, clear water! What could go wrong? But oh my GOD, Prof. Khan even makes pirates and male prostitution boring. This is absolutely the most miserable class I have taken in my entire academic career.

Khan is a terrible professor.  Not only does she say more "fluff" than stuff, she's not open to true and free interpretation in essays.  Puts on a demeanor of nice, but very transparently fake.  I do not recommend this class at all. Material is easy, but grading does not match up. Repeats phrases 10x and treats the class as if they were in 10.
Do not take this class@! you will regret it- consider "new world encounters" with jill mare instead. this class is total BS
she's boring.

Prof. Khan is very polite and nice in general. Her lectures, however, are somewhat boring. She seems like she'd know more than she decides to show, choosing to oversimplify the material more than she has to. She repeats simple facts frequently. The TA's learn at the same pace we do. The material isn't hard, but essays are graded as though it is.
I hated her lectures. They are SOOOOO boring!Her lectures are not clear. There are five papers to write. The worst experience I ever had in NYU.

Khan puts on this front that makes you think she's nice, but you can tell she's just putting it on. She was not understanding and unwilling to admit that she might have done something wrong. Good luck staying awake during lecture. Also, she seems to pander to students with a caribbean background/interest. TA's have little knowlege of Caribbean. In spite of all this, it's pretty easy.
Easy class. She's overtly nice and repetitive. Class isn't neccesary, but it's interesting. Totally recommend it. Oh, and there's no tests just essays (5 of them, but they're easy).

She's very nice, but lectures are boring.  Doesn't take attendance enough, so you don't have to go.  The TA's are no help in recitations.  They don't study the Caribbean.  My TA would put notes on the board that made absolutely no sense with no organization.  If you're looking for easy, take it.

This class is rather easy and fair.  There are 5 papers, no midterm, and a final. Although the prompts are challenging the grading is lenient (since the TAs grade). Khan only allows 2 absences.  Lecture was kind of boring at times, but Khan made it funny with her jokes and quirky personality.  This is one of the easiest world cultures classes.

She's a very nice lady, and you can tell that she really likes her students. There were 5 papers, and they were all pretty tough to write. That said, the grading is lenient. I wrote a terrible paper and handed it in two days late, and still recieve a B-. I reccomend this class.

Ms. Khan was truly a wonderful teacher. She helped us understand the material and definitely liked for the class to partcipate in discussion even if there were 120 of us lol. She's such a sweet woman. I loved her. Her jokes can be CORNY but they still make you laugh just because she means well. She's great!

She is a pretty good teacher. You have to truly show an interest in the subject for her to really like. She is one of those professors that will bump you up if you kiss a little ass. The TA's and recitation is generally pointless but they are easy graders. Def not an easy A but a solid B+ if you put little effort into it.
One of the best professors I've had. Ms. Khan is a true delight to have as a teacher.
awful prof...everything from her tone of voice to her demeanor is belittling and insulting.  i do NOT recommend this prof.
No Comments

She's very nice & genuine. If you write about something that is important and meaningful and is compatible with the content it's an easy A. Only two papers and a presentation for the entire semester... but a LOT of readings. She goes through each reading during class so I wouldn't say it's completely necessary, but participation helps boost grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives 100 pages to read each week with an optional extra 100 pages that are not optional at all, dont let the optional fool you. All of this doesnt even matter to her, she chose your grade the moment you stepped in her class and will grade you accordingly. She does not like minorities and people who speak an opinion opposing hers. Dont take
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, extremely knowledgeable, learned a lot from this class.

What an incredible professor! Rita explained psycholinguistics to the class in ONE lecture, and before that I wasted a whole semester trying to understand it in Brian McElree's class. That said, she's a great teacher. What an asset to NYU.Very fun class, lots of reading, but you'll learn tons. One of the best psych class I took @ NYU! I miss her!

She does want her students to think, yet she stifles what everyone has to say with some research that SHE has conducted already.(sometimes missing your point completely) She has a huge ego. I certainly wanted to learn and work and didn't expect an easy A, but she was very reluctant to help and listen. She has biases towards some students. MusicPsyc

I loved this Professor. The students that complain about her are most likely "idiots" just because she wants her students to "think" she is hailed as this horrible professor. I really enjoyed her class and I learned a great deal. Take this class if you are not afraid of learning by working and are not in it for an easy A.

She is a great person, but lectures are boring, and there's no space for debating philosophical topics; the focus is on how they are argued. I didn't do the readings in the first half of the semester, got a B on the midterm, did them in the second half and still got a B on the final. I am a good writer and have all A's in humanities classes. Beware
really good prof, lectures entertaining even if material is dense and difficult. pretty easy grading, exams were not too hard either. readings can be skipped, lectures provide what you need
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Aitken is great! SO sweet and always accessible for help. Deadlines are pretty fixed but imo, they're super generous so even if you can't get an extension you'll still probably finish on time. I was a bit scared to take the class bc she was a new teacher without a rep, but I am so glad I decided to take it bc she is such a gem
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: prof aitken is really great! granted how the thick material and readings are, she makes it very comprehendible. super open to help, office hours were always so helpful. lectures were sometimes really hard to stay engaged in, but i think thats just a product of zoom. she generally made philosophy soooo much less daunting, and workload wasnt crazy

What a grumpy old man!  He's so mean and bitter all of the time I actually began to dread class in preparation for what mean things he would say to me. However, he did improve my Spanish skills and understanding immensely. He was very smart and had a good sense of humor.  He really made Spanish class an awful experience three times a week.
Terrible professor, one of the worst I've ever had. I hated going to class every single day.

Native spanish speaker, but not at all helpful. He came to class sick and grumpy when he came at all. I took Adv. Grammer and Comp. from him, and basically had to learn the material from the book. The class was a disaster
Always late, never organized, frequently incomprehensible.  He has managed to offend, annoy or scare almost every student in the class.

I think few people realize that his class is supposed to separate the wheat from the chaff. He expects a little discipline, to be sure, but my grammar was pretty much flawless by the end of the semester. An A is not impossible if you make an effort.

The absolute worst professor I hope to have in my college experience. Often came to class late, impossible to understand, often canceled or rescheduled class, ridiculed students, didn't explain or answer questions. One of the reasons I am not studying spanish anymore. He said he was retiring at the end of last fall, but apparently he's back. beware

Prof. Aiello is a terrible professor.  He is probably the worst professor in the Spanish department because there are some good ones.  The best advice I can give to a student who is taking Spanish is to never take a class with Prof. Aiello.
I didn't know Satan taught Spanish...
One of the worst teachers I know.  He is extremely unorganized and should get it together!  He needs some happiness in his life; he seems so miserable.

While Professor Aiello may seem intimidating in class, meeting with him in person is much different.  He's very kind and helpful and wants you to do well in the course.  The workload is heavy, but you can get by without doing an exercise or two.  Focus on the papers and tests is necessary to do well

He has good days and bad days.  He's definitely a moody person, but he's good at teaching and really knows a lot.  I was lazy and never came to class with the exercises done and he never cared.  He even gave me chances to turn stuff in late.
Professor Aiello was extremely helpful and hilarious.  He was extremely knowledgeable and his mood swings aren't that bad.  He's very nice especially during office hours, very hospitable.
Though at times quite serious, Prof. Aiello is a very knowledgable guy and as long as you do the work he is actually usually pretty hilarious and likeable.
professor aiello is very smart and very fair. as long as you make an effort and participate, he will reciprocate.
don't take any classes with him!!  he's impossible to understand, and very moody, and class is not fun at all.
The course material was easy, as was the material on the tests. However, be prepared to lose a whole letter grade for the slightest mistake.
The lecture quality is poor because of heavy accent.
Bad teacher. Makes simple subject matter seem confusing. Really nice guy though so it's hard to get mad at him. No mandatory hw or attendance by if you want a good grade I'd do both.

Very happy man. Perhaps one of the most talented at teaching. He's the only teacher that I've had in my whole life that can teach. He's very helpful, he barely uses the textbook (!!)--in fact he never uses the textbook, and his exams are relatively straightforward--no tricks, and his sample exams perfectly reflect his actual exams.
Great prof. People are just lazy. Just study the homework and take notes. The only thing is that the class runs on a curve but so does every other stern class. Recommended.
A good professor but he is also very arrogant and lazy about his job. The curve on his tests are ridiculous.

Maindiratta knows his stuff. Very straightforward, helpful, friendly. Provides all the notes, slides, homeworks, practice exams. Just pay attention in class, do your homework, and study the material and you will do well. Highly recommended for Managerial Accounting.

Jovial man, and provides notes, practice exams...but somehow, they still didn't help! Go in for help, stay awake, do hw thoroughly for, and ask all questions for the sake of your grade. TA not much help. Sweaters were the worst.
No Comments

Super passive aggressive, but I found it funny. In class is a lot of discussion which I genuinely enjoyed. "Bonus work" is required to get an A in the class which does not make a lot of sense to me. Grading is super strict despite the essays being graded for completion. Work load is not bad even with the bonus work.

The class definitely has lots of work, but people complaining are not taking into account that her class is completion based. You can get easy A as long as you play along with what she wants... she likes a lot of abstraction in essays. I'd rather take this class than one that grades the essays for content, because you can get an A for trying.
Don't take this woman. Every other rating explains for itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She just does not have a clear grading criteria at all. Doesn't respond to emails at all. I still don't know my grade and it is the final week. She is so picky about essays that she claimed were just completion. Even if you do all the work perfectly, you won't have an A unless you do 4 bonus options outside of class which is just so strange.

Do NOT take her class bro, genuinely one of the worst experiences i have had. 

isn't clear on what she wants, doesn't give you feedback unless you ask her multiple times and the feedback is vague, if you do all of your work, You still get a B, to get an A you have to do "Bonus" work...

VERY passive aggressive

also changes the sylbs mid term????

She is extremely intelligent, passionate about teaching. Often asked for feedback from students- pushed back due dates (made some things ambiguous but always corrected mistakes). Sometimes passive agressive but she openly admitted that she wasn't proud of this- clear to me was trying to catch herself and improve. Overall an amazing, caring person!

Extremly disrespectful&mean.Put sensitive contents though being reported before.Good rates were long ago. Ask her a question she throw it right back questioning you.Volunteered for bonus presentation(took hours to make).Got ignored 3 times bec of her time prob and never got to present.Rewrite whole essay bec tiny prob. Just Run

Figuring out grading criteria is like deciphering ancient runes. Asking for clarification just makes her more vague and passive-aggressive. """Optional""" bonus events outside of class that you have to attend for an A. You don't know your grade until the last week. "Excused absence" means nothing to her. I had to guess my way to an A. Run.

The workload is honestly fine, but it can get annoying. Ajello's contract grading system and assignment instructions are pretty confusing, and her explanations when asking questions are somewhat passive-aggressive. The class and discussions are interesting, but having to go to extra events and conferences outside of class to get an A is a pain.

It is like I'm dealing with two different people, the lecturer and the grader. The lectures are enjoyable and have many open discussions. The grading is very very harsh. Some people I have talked to said they agree with me, and some say they don't. So while I don't recommend you take this class, but if you do you will have to work hard for an A.

Don't trust old reviews—her grading changed. The “grading contract” is vague and you will not know your grade until you recieve it at the end. Incompletes drop your grade a full letter, & marked unfairly. Extra credit? Don't expect to get it if you do it. Excused absences count as absences. I took this class so you don't have to. Don't.

Very passive aggressive and gives the most unclear instructions given to man, seriously had no idea what she wanted throughout the entire semester and had to basically wing it and pray she would like whatever I turned in.
If you love yourself never take this being's class she cannot teach or grade or answer questions

Professor Ajello was my first semester EXPOS professor. She was fair and used a grading contract. You default to a B as long as you show up and turn things in. I don't think her written feedback is very useful, but her conferences were a good litmus test. I would give a 3.5 if I could.
Good professor but kind of passive-aggressive. If you participate in class and meet with her outside of class to work on your essays you should be good.

Prof. Ajello is awesome. My writing improved a lot. Her feedback was helpful and kind. She made me laugh and I enjoyed going to class. I learned to notice details and express myself more clearly, and to write using more complex sentences. My overall structure also improved. I strongly recommend this course!

I got helpful feedback on the first assignment. I don't love lectures but hers are coherent and actually helpful. Surprised anyone is saying she's passive aggressive. I think they mean she's serious. If you put in the effort, you will learn a lot. She has a sense of humor but she's also got a no BS attitude. She brought really good brownies!

Dr. Ajello was my favorite teacher this year. Unlike some other professors, she's really attentive in class. I never felt like she was just recycling an old lecture. You can tell she really cares about the students. If you pay attention in class and do the minimum work requirements you'll get a good grade. Plus she's really funny!

She can definitely be passive aggressive at times, and is often very vague with her instructions. It's hard to tell what she's looking for. 

However, the benefit is that she grades very fairly. At the start of the semester, she'll post an assignment checklist. If you do everything on the checklist, you get an A.

The most impactful teacher I've had, prioritizes student well-being and fosters genuine self-reflection through writing. Instead of fixating on perfection or strict grading, she focuses on reflections and improvement as a writer. Most classes involve open discussions and idea exchange, which is refreshing to the stricter classes of Tandon.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you actually want to be better at writing, take her class. She grades you based on the effort you put in and your technique which makes so much sense since writing is subjective. She is kind of passive aggressive at times but is a pretty understanding professor in general.

I do not like her grading style and she honestly did not help me with improving my writing since her feedback consistently was vague and it requested me to do things such as combine a lot of ideas into a singular sentence. if you want to improve your writing, do not take her.
Made my writing so much worse. Like I don't even understand it anymore, but hey she likes it I guess.
It's the passive aggressiveness that does it for me.
Her feedback is very poor and her instructions are unclear.
She made my hair turn grey with stress unironically. I never knew what she wanted in her papers.
If I could give her a negative rating I would. So passive-aggressive and unreasonable. Not helpful in or outside of class.

She doesn't want to answer any questions or give effective feedback. I can't ask her any questions without her getting angry, passive-aggressive, or refusing to answer. Her grading system is so confusing and stressful. She's so vague on the instructions but really harsh when it comes to grading. She is so frustrating like I cannot with her at all.
Good
Very nice and caring outside class, but her lectures are mandatory and do not help. Lots of assignments and grading system sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading criteria is hard to understand. Lecture is mandatory.
She is a tough grader and some of her grading critique is not clear.

didn't find the classwork very helpful for our projects which make up the entirety of your grade iirc. in fact you could easily get at least a B+ on your projects without even going to lecture, but its mandatory. She can also get passive aggressive with her tone which I find very funny sometimes

She expects student to write like english majors. The work load is way too much. No matter how many times I went to the Writing center and met with her, the instructions given to us was nothing compared to what she actually wanted us to do. A very tough grader and my class spent way too much time getting feedback from our peers ( it did not help).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Ajello. If you show that you care about your work, she will help you become a better writer and help you push your boundaries. She gives excellent feedback and is always available outside of class. Her expectations are evident and directly written in the syllabus. If you put the work and time into your essays, you will get an A.

WTE is a tough class but having a professor like Ajello makes it all the more bearable. She provides clear feedback and is gentle, caring, and supportive. She even does each assignment with the class, so that you get the sense of what she is looking for. Some expos classes seem like a chore to attend, but her lectures were always a joy to attend!

WTE is a must so just get it over with. Prof. Ajello was lovely; soft-spoken and gave great feedback, though she makes you work to understand it. I found meeting f2f with her tremendously helpful. She also brought chocolates and brownies to class!

Not a bad professor for EXPOS. Doesn't bombard you with work, is available outside of class, and is nice overall. My problem is with how her lectures are pretty much pointless. 70-80% of the time they are unrelated to the essay, and I would have preferred skipping class. If you like being exposed to a variety of different topics, you will like her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brings in a wide variety of readings-- you can find something that interests you, rather than figure out what she wants you to say. Supportive, patient, she offers many different ways of approaching the essay, recognizes that one way might not work for all. I was empowered by her class, to find what's meaningful to me and find my own voice.

I felt like I only needed to be there for 3 classes the entire semester. Once the prompt was explained, the rest was pointless. Paper instructions are vague and confusing. You have to figure out a lot by yourself. I have no idea how I did well because I was confused 80% of the time. She was (somewhat) good for individual meetings, but not in class
Pretty solid class not terribly hard on the grades if you're willing to do the work and go through the drafting process that she outlines.

Professor Ajello is an excellent professor that really helped me to improve my writing skills. She shows how much she cares for her students and will really listen and give you the attention that you need. Be willing to work hard and make sure to listen to the advice she gives you in order to do well in the class.

This class was similar to my freshman writing workshop class. Everything is really routined by a step by step process. She doesn't really have a good way of teaching and making sure her students understand what to do in class, but during the individual meetings, she was really helpful in making sure you're on the right track for the paper.

Linell is a brilliant pick for WTE as she offers so much support and genuinely cares about her students. I benefitted greatly from independent meetings and the group discussions Linell encouraged in class. Her method of directing the class made the core requirement far less painful to complete.

Ajello is a great pick for WTE if you can't find someone better. She truly cares about her students and isn't too harsh of a grader as long as you take her feedback and apply it to your work, and do hws. Lectures offer new ways of writing and analyzing pieces of work so it helps to attend regularly and get feedback in the midst of an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ajello really helped me develop my own ideas and the confidence and inspriation to find my own voice as a writer.  She doesn't always collect assignments, which is frustrating because they take time to complete. But she always checks in with the class to give support towards the final essay.

If you have a sucky registration time and could not get anyone better, she's not too bad. But if you have a better registration time, please please take WTE with someone else. For me, "lecture" was literally pointless. The only reason I went was because it was required. She's unclear with what she wants and overall I just would not recommend.

Linell was an incredible WTE professor. She really tries to help you understand the assignments and deepen your writing skills as much as possible while also leaving some unexplained/vague, forcing you to think for yourself and try new things. It's a bit confusing at first, but you eventually find your footing. Great feedback on papers/homework.
Easy A take it if you want gpa boosts

The LIGHTEST class you will ever take. Two presentations, and online midterm, and online final paper (short). The lecture is long but its okay for the amount of work you have to do. If youre gonna take intro to sociology TAKE HER!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great professor!! So sweet! Was always open for questions and helping us for future exams/papers. I had a class right before this one and I was presenting a final Project for that class right before her final exam. She offered to delay the exam 5 mins which i declined but she was so understanding w/ everything.

She is truly a wonderful professor. She cares a lot about sociology and she makes it enjoyable and easy. There are only 4 assignments to do and they are very easy and worth 20% of your final grade. She loves hearing about what you have to say and does whatever to make people feel comfortable enough to participate. Easy midterm and easy final paper.

Very sweet and does not ask much of you other than to participate in class. Has 4 homework assignments you have to do for chapter readings. Doesn't like tests so only has a midterm which is very easy if you do homework and listen to lectures. Final paper is also easy. Class is long but she does her best to never keep you the entire time.
the only thing that I don't like about the class is that its too late. but the homework and quizzes are easy and the class is more discussion based.

Prof Akhtar is a tough teacher but wants his students to learn the course material well and hence assigns a lot of reading but the guest lectures were a great way to hear about practicing artists working with some of the technologies in the readings.

Lots of dense, theoretical readings (100s of pages a week) and will assign films to watch the night before class. No rubric or instructions for assignments. He's a nice guy and seems to care about his students but the workload was far too heavy and he rambles quite a lot in class.

Provided late feedback and it was often unclear. never gave rubrics or assignments sheets so directions were confusing. When asked questions about assignments he wouldn't clarify. Class was suppose to be discussion based but he would go on rants for anywhere from 20-40 minutes . Final paper: 12-15 pages, over 100 pages a week to read
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor by any means. I got an A in the mid-term but unexpectedly, she failed me the class after the term was over. Also, she is rude, dismissive, and hardly teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you want to have peace of mind and do well. This professor fails students at the last minute for arbitrary and minor reasons despite telling them they are doing well thoughout the semester. She makes you write so much and is harshly critical. I heard someone had to go to the ER due to the stress of Akhu.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont take her; if necessary, wait until the following term to take the course. This instructor does not have regards for students and how her actions will impact their future. She can fail students over minor mistakes. Also, she can fail students after the term is over regardless of completion of all assignments and internship site hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I've taken two classes with Anna. Incredible instructor/person––passionate, knowledgeable, and so interesting. If you are looking for an easy A, this is not the class for you. If you are looking to grow academically, intellectually, personally, socially--& willing to put in the work––her classes will give you that. Also ditto the hot comment above.

Tough, but fair. She really loves the subject. Lots of reading, but it's the sort of stuff you'd probably keep on your shelf after graduation to impress people.  Also, I feel bad about saying this given the content of the class, but Prof. A is hot, and I'm not talking teacher hot, straight up hot.

She was right on top of things! Led me through the curriculum like she was born to teach. Would have appreciated a bit more performance feedback, but overall a solid, hard-working, dedicated, erudite star in her field-versatile and a consumate risk-taker. Highly recommended!

class was sometimes interesting but it was a mistake to take. tons of reading and work every week. tons of field research for a huge paper at the end. no tests but a lot of responses and field work. shes crazy into the subject but everything comes from the readings. has nothing to do with comm so i dont know why its an ILA - all sociology.
Boring lectures, poorly written exams, & no curves/grade boosts whatsoever. Don't take this course if she's teaching it.

Don't take CMNB with her and Reyes. They will make showing up to lectures & learning the material feel like an absolute chore. They speak in very monotone voices, make homework assignments unnecessarily difficult, and write exams that are more like cyphers. Can't believe someone made me despise a subject I once loved so much.
soft spoken but very knowledgeable.

Cool person outside of class, but her lectures were a mile wide and an inch deep, heavily focused on rote memorization. The final exam questions were poorly worded, and she emphasized material beyond course scope, like memorizing chemical structures ??? It's hard to say I left with broad conceptual understanding. She should learn from Blau & Siegal

Actually the prof ever. Assignments were easy, and most of the time, you could get away with not having done the homework, although all the assigned readings were very interesting. She did recommend I seek psychiatric help twice throughout the semester, which was a little crazy, but at least she cares! 100% would take this course again.
She is actually the sweetest. She respects everyone's ideas and perspectives and allows everyone to have a voice in class. Assignments are engaging and she grades very liberally. I love her sooo much

She is actually the sweetest woman ever. The readings that she gives are super interesting and our in class discussions are fascinating. She's super understanding when it comes to deadlines. She also grades really fairly. If you put in effort and do a good job she will give an A. I don't at all understand the other reviews my whole class loved her

She is genuinely so sweet. I feel like sometimes she chooses readings based on what she is interested. She gives a lot of time for essays. The homework is only readings, you never have to turn anything in, just be ready to talk about it in class the next day. As long as you participate and show interest, it is an easy A. She's my queen tbh

She is genuinely one of the nicest people I have ever encountered. I'm not sure why her reviews are so low at the moment---her class was not super difficult. Participation definitely matters to her so that she can see that you are engaged with the material. If you speak up in class I think its pretty easy to get an A. Definitely recommend her.

This is quite possibly the worst professor that I have ever encountered in any school setting. Her lectures are non-chronological and messy, she repeats herself frequently and talks in circles, her assignments are not announced and have no grading criteria given, and she grades based on whether or not she agrees with you. Such a vile experience.

Genuinely one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Unable to explain any concept we questioned her on and provided a very Westernized approach to just about every lesson. Art history teacher that knew nothing about art...? Disappointing. Would grade to average out the class, did not provide any rubrics, and picked fast favorites. Don't take her.

She is a good person. The issue I have (which is probably the core issue that everyone else does) is that her questions are frequently poorly worded and unclear. Simple concepts become grade-droppers when you don't know which multiple choice answer is the one she is looking for.

this class is so hard because the quizzes and exams are super difficult. the professor genuinely sucks at teaching and goes over  hard and complex topics very quickly, students have no time to take notes or understand. you have to learn everything on your own but she posts incomplete slides that are difficult to learn from. physiology w her=torture

lecture slides are difficult and hard to follow, and barbara is not a good lecturer. Exams are horribly worded and questions are very roundabout and easy to trip up on. I got a 5 in AP Bio but somehow when I came here I ended up doing very poorly and now my GPA is STRUGGLINGG. avoid her if you can! take POB off track if you want to save your GPA.

akum's lab isn't bad at all. she's barely involved and honestly it all depends on who ur TA is (take matt). the class is easy as long as you do the work for it. but study and you'll be fine. all the quizzes and the final exams are fair and the final has a lot of repeated questions from your quizzes. your grade will be fine, it's an easy bio lab
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She has no care for her students. Very nasty demeanor. Unprofessional and gives NYU a bad image of what a professor is. 

All of my encounters with her has been negative.
The worst professor I've ever had.
She's harsh, but much better than all the other bio professors.  Appreciate her while you can!
Didn't teach well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sometimes she misspeaks during lectures, but overall she's fine. She records lectures so you can review at your own pace. She does a few polls each lecture, helping both her and you see what you don't know. She's accessible via email and office hours. Your final grade is based on exams, quizzes, and problem sets, with the lowest of each dropped.

Barbara's Lectures might be kinda boring as she reads of her slides, participation is taken and graded for every lecture and tutorial. She's chill, tho, lowkey; she is pretty clear with stuff on the syllabus; there's hardly any surprises. HW and participation is 40% of the grade and you can drop a test (I dropped the final) out of 4 tests total.

Akum is one of the worst professors I've had. Her lectures are quite literally just her slides. The tests are solely based on lectures and if you miss anything you're screwed. All her test questions are worded so ambiguously and are very confusing and nit-picky. Each test requires hours of preparation to do remotely well on. STAY AWAY FROM HER!

really good lecturer but will def get some info wrong
awful exam writer
reading the textbook is an absolute waste of time
wont round my 92.69 to an A so f*ck her and this class
My 89.97 cannot be rounded up to an A-

barbra isn't the worst prof ever, she just writes the worst exam questions ever. for studying, always ask yourself "what would happen if x fails," she loves those types of questions. don't study textbook, just her slides. do well on problem sets and quizzes bc they will help ur grade a lot (40%). don't love her but she's not impossible

People giving ones need to grow up. She isn't the best lecturer but gives plenty of opportunities to do well in the course even if you don't do great on the exams. EVERYTHING on the exams is from the slides. Don't bother reading the textbook. Do well on Problem sets and quizzes (both online) so you have wiggle room in grades.

Honestly, she is not as terrible as most people think. She is not the best teacher, but she is not horrible. If you do your homework and quizzes well, then it'll help your grade. I didn't the grades I wanted in the exams, but I feel like I could've studied better. She also drops one lowest test score so that was helpful.
Terrible, cannot write test questions well. No curve
Go to lecture, read the textbook, and you'll be fine. The course is easy by nature but Barbara's unclear questions and grading make it slightly harder.
GPA KILLER!!!! Insanely hard questions on the exams, and her lectures do not prepare you for the types of questions she asks. HIGHLY do not recommend taking her for this class.
She's a pretty decent person but that's probably where it stops. Tests are vague, unclear and badly worded. Definitely had to self learn essentially all the content.

Terrible professor, doesn't know what she is teaching, and doesn't consider students' understanding for Bio...
Flies through weekly lectures without making sure that students understand the topics; 100% self-learning is required.
Random, odd, and difficult exam questions! Be ready for a class average in the 60s, WITHOUT CURVE
RUN when you see her.
Never choose her!

barbara isn't a terrible prof but her exams are written rly bad and are made to trip you up so read each question carefully. don't bother with reading the textbook, most of the stuff she uses on tests is from her slides.
exam 1: easy content but tricky questions
exam 2: hardest content and trickiest questions
exam 3: easiest, most ppl did well
Don't take this class :)

Barbara was one of the worst professors I have ever taken. The success of her students is not her priority, rather an afterthought. Her tests are poorly worded, often misleading students and is very stingy with giving points back even though she's the one who messed up the question. Exam averages are in the 60s, and she doesn't curve the class.

Barbara honestly is not that bad. I think she's just misunderstood. There's so much stigma around her that shes bad or whatever but you honestly just need to get used to her content and wordings on PS and exams. My grades only improved throughout the semester. Just do her practice exams a lot bc she often repeats questions on the real exam.

Akum is an okay professor and honestly I don't get why everyone is complaining about her. I haven't touched the textbook a bit and passed this class with an A-. She drops a lot of things and records her lectures. Everyone on the exam will be based on her lectures and problem sets, nothing more. Everyone complaining honestly needs to grow up.

Professor Akum isn't the best, but any pre-med course is hard. She engages with her students well and will answer any questions you have after class. Her recorded lectures are beneficial and can help you grasp the content. BUT be aware that her exams are tough and be prepared for ANYTHING.  All I can say is study, study, and you will be okay.

Honestly people complain too much. Any class that you take as a premed is going to be rigorous. Barbara gives plenty of practice and helps a lot during office hours. She's also not as bad of a lecturer as people make her out to be. I, for one thought she was a great one that could make me laugh sometimes.

I had her for POB1, and I don't think she is as bad as the reviews say. Is she a phenomenal teacher? No. But she knows her material very well, is extremely organized, and lets you drop an exam. I would highly recommend taking this course after GenChem, however, as you may need strong study habits to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Akum, in simple words, is terrible. Although the content is a bit hard to grasp at first, it is beginner level Bio for college. But Professor Akum makes it much more complicated then it should be. She's caring, and easily accessible after class. It's honestly just better to watch her recorded lectures after lecture.

Her jokes are funny, presence affects wifi. Attend lectures or watch her recordings. Test questions and problem set questions are worded a bit weird, but she admits it. Sometimes she will mention something important once and it will appear on the test so be prepared. Writes all of the work for the class, so get familiar with her writing.

Her class isn't actually that hard. All the test questions are very straightforward and has only had confusing wording once or twice. Just read the slides and you'll be fine. She's very accessible outside of class and will often stay past lecture to answer your questions.

I love her and Im gonna miss her. Her class isn't that bad just come to lecture and read the textbook if you don't understand. Just know everything on her slides. Not a lot of homework at all. She's so funny and always kept my attention in lecture. The things we learned were very interesting.

The material isn't *that* bad, it's standard college-level Intro Biology content, but oh my god is she the actual worst professor I've had in my entire time at NYU. Test questions are inconsistent with the slides AND textbook, and are worded horrifically. Ace PSs and quizzes.

Sincerely, NYU, I beg of you to reevaluate the teaching of this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard to understand but is usually only prof for POB 1. Doesnt follow the textbok in any way shape or form and will usually go on long tangents on unimportant things instead of focusing on material that will be on the exams. Exams short answer sections are often on things she didnt teach//mention.

shes not as bad as people made her seem, just stay on top of your work and do practice problems and you'll be fine. her lectures are super engaging and she makes the material entertaining. its just a lot of work but its doable, she just contradicts herself in lectures sometimes but if you ask for clarification she'll give it to u

her tests r terrible like u rly have to know every specific detail and j be accustomed to the type of understanding that the test requires or else ur cooked but her lectures make the content really easy to understand and she's so unserious about everything lmao it's very entertaining. j solve as many practice problems as u can youll be fine

shes so funny like she doesnt know what shes talking about and contradicts herself but her lectures are so entertaining and shell try to answer ur questions . her tests are sometimes specific sometimes general but honestly all the information is on her slides, just attend her lecture and pay attention
THE OTHER REVIEWS ARE WRONG PROF AKUM IS AN ANGEL SENT TO EARTH!!! HER TEACHING AND ASSIGNMENTS SAVED MY GRADEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE I LOVE HER AND WILL DEFEND HER UNTIL I PASS!!!!

She just kinda reads her slides, but honestly it's not that bad, tests are only like 60 percent of ur grades and she drops ur lowest one, rest are basically homework/participation. The test could be a bit tricky with some super specific, trivia-style questions, but most of it is on her slides lowkey.

Barbara is OK. She's not as terrible as people claim. She is not a wonderful professor that will get all of your questions answered. She does make difficult exam questions but all answers can be found in the lectures. Her sample exams reflect the difficulty of the real exam. Go to lectures and study in-depth before exams and you'll be fine.

Barbara is Ok. She is average as a professor. Her exams are difficult but not impossible. I took about a week to study for both exams and ended up with a 90 for overall course average. Its not that she's a terrible professor, its the course itself is hard. If your not a person that knows how to study in-depth, you are probably not gonna do great.

Her tests are extremely hard with no curves or care if people fail. She puts tricky and misleading questions to try to fail students. In class she briefly discusses topics leaving out essential details to do well on the test. There were topics on the test that I haven't even heard the name of.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The average of midterm 2 is 68 and no curve. GPA KILLER!
Doesn't explain thoroughly what to study for and includes material on exams that were not covered in lecture.

1.Careless lecture: skip details and make mistakes
2.Reading her words take more time than actual thinking
3.Exam way too detailed: meaningless b/c memorization is only needed
4.Replaceable by Chat: dk why she get salary if she contribute nothing in students' learning
5.Advice: quit or transfer to other universities
Thanks Barbara, you makes me hate in BIO.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: By far, the worst professor I have ever had at NYU. Makes the most obscure Problem Set Questions and Exam Short answer questions. Has EXTREMELY unclear grading criteria. If it's not her way, it's wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DOESNT ANSWER EMAILS.

Terrible professor with terrible style of teaching. Exam questions are ambiguous and I'm sure many kids sitting in lecture are clueless as to what they are learning. Class will significantly drop your GPA!!!
Worst professor, does not care for students and wants students to fail.
Literal incorrect information in the lab manuals. She does not respond to emails. Her quizzes are confusing. She is a bad professor.

Barbara just seems confused. She is reading over the slides and I can't even determine if she has a good knowledge of the material she is teaching. She is all over the place and I have NO clue which chapter in the textbook we are. Quizzes are nothing like what she teaches and we have to depend on videos she assigns to learn most of the material.
gpa killer

Guys I've been in this class for a total of three days and I already hate it. The problem sets (aka homework) and quizzes are nothing like the lecture notes. In fact, the lecture notes give you very basic information that is usually information you already knew from high school biology. The actual graded work, however, is much more advanced.

With Barbara, you just have to get lucky to be honest. The material she goes over, like the body systems, is actually pretty cool. But the exams always go too far or get really specific. I feel like some stuff just clicked with me, but it's impossible to ace the material she goes over because there's always a disconnect. The exams are just rough.

she says incorrect information in lecture + her exam questions are like riddles, when poor averages come out her solution is "study more + read the textbook". usually some points will be given back to all students due to unclear wording but its still a pain in the ass. lectures are difficult to get through and she gets behind often.

Her exams have nothing to do with her lectures. Her lectures have nothing to do with the book we bought. I learned nothing from her. Do not take this professor unless you want a permanent scar on your GPA, and your dreams. Advisors force-register freshmen into these sections, NYU doesn't care what happens to them after.
Awful at writing test questions.

Exam questions are ambiguous and she provides only 24 hours to appeal for a regrade. The averages are in the low 70s, yet she refuses to curve or round final grades to the nearest integer. She makes inappropriate comments about gender and disabilities. Her exam question asked about the genetic makeup of a woman who is "apparently female."

I sincerely believe that this professor does not find any enjoyment in teaching and does not care for her students' success. Not only are her tests so poorly worded, but her slides often have mistakes as well. In order to take a test, you need to have some advanced decoding skills or you won't understand what she's asking. I wish I was joking.

She was bad enough when she taught material she had some understanding of but for spring semester POB 2 she taught the first half of the semester not knowing a single thing about the topic and it was so obvious. Good luck to all who have to suffer with her and my deepest condolences.

RUNNNNNNN!!! exams are riddled with errors, like wrong directions, grammatical issues, and even multiple choice questions missing the CORRECT option!!! The content itself is easy but Barbara finds a way to overcomplicate everything. Study guides are completely useless. You can still do fine in the class but get ready to put in a lot of work.....
AVIOD IF YOU CAN. Exams are worded so poorly and filled with mistakes on their part. Even if you try to request a regrade for something they will respond in all caps "NO"

She is not clear about what will be on the exams. Gives us tutorial sheets and problem set to work on which are very insightful in terms of knowledge but NONE of it relates to what will be on the exam. Her exam review sheets are unhelpful, using descriptions like "know the basic characteristics of this" then puts specific information on the exam

A very bad professor. Lectures and exam material have no correlation. Does not care about students' grades and or concerns. Had to take unfortunately because no other POB2 professor. Terrible professor.

The professors dont realize a good amount of students cheat off the exams, assume students are doing well when the other half are struggling. The professors don't explain the material well, just read off the slides. if u request a regrade, they don't even respond appropriately or communicate well. they just say "No"
Ambiguous questions for tests, especially starting second semester.

girl do not walk but RUN in the other direction. if you can take bio off track I would because this is the TRENCHES. she has called students stupid on multiple occasions, teaches the content ineffectively, and writes exam questions that are unclear. words cannot describe how bad of a teacher she is. bout to have me like kendrick on drake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I bet she snickers to herself while writing exams. Lectures are difficult to follow as she often backtracks and does not explain clearly. Wording of her questions are very vague and come out of the blue. By far my least favorite of the 3 lecturers for POB. good luck to those taking POB I entirely with her instead of only half

So unnecessarily hard. This class is a projectile vomit of information and unless you memorize every detail you will not do well on her exams. Lectures are unhelpful as I don't think she knows what she's talking about half the time. Would advise to avoid but she is probably the only option.
Such a difficult class for no reason. Tests are not easy or reflective of the material learned in class.

A really inconsistent, disorganized professor to teach human physiology to freshman students. Her lectures can often be messy and misleading, and cover too much content for a test to be cramped in. Many times, she has to give back credit on test and homework questions because of her vague wording. I often had to fight for my answers to be correct.
Most of every exam written by her is a curve ball and her lectures are confusing. You're better off reading the textbook than going to lectures, but attendance is mandatory.

Prof. Akum has to be one of the worst teachers at NYU. Her long lectures that are mandatory coupled with the unclear guidelines on what she expects us to learn, which are unhelpful compared to reading the textbook. Tests are a matter of luck as to difficulty. Hopefully she can improve as this is her first time lecturing but I doubt it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very picky about attendance polls that she doesn't open for long enough. Had only one poll for today's class that closed in the first 2 minutes. So, if you were late you missed points for today. Does not lecture well and makes exams unnecessarily hard.

she does not care about student success at all cuz she is trying to let us fail by making the exams and ps insanely hard with confusing wording
she makes bunch of mistakes in lectures as well as assignements 
if u want to get a decent gpa, avoid!

Most annoying NYU prof. Exams dont reflect material and barely gives sources for us to study. Lectures suck and especially for lab, extremely uninformative. She writes gibberish for questions to overcomplicate the most minor topics. please avoid to keep your sanity

AP bio knowledge carried me. Not sure if she likes writing trick questions, or she genuinely thinks the questions are fair. If you did not take AP bio and you are now taking this class with her godspeed my friend...

just bad....... wants us to fail... just... dont bother. exams barely ever compose of anything from the lecture notes. basically u just learn random diseases/modifications (prob would better help future med school students), but isn't too helpful when it comes to studying for exams. much studying needs to be done in order to pass her course

Everything I learned, I learned from the textbook. Her slides are confusing and the videos she assigns are unhelpful - don't watch them. Exam questions are about super specific things you'll only know from reading the textbook, and the wording is always awful.
Funny during lectures. Didn't give as much asynchronous work as Duncan, videos were much shorter. Did have to read the textbook as supplementary work though.

Barbara is a funny person and a decent professor, but talks way too fast. Also, a good number of exam questions are BS. For example, she covered the nitrogenous wastes in lecture and their water solubility and energy cost, but an exam question was which one was most toxic, something she did not go over in class. Not curving up is also annoying.

Her lectures are not very well organized, and her asynchronous materials are not relevant to her lectures. She doesn't really take responsibility for students' success and blames it on us for getting low averages. Overall, I think she's a nice person but she isn't the best at explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Def a learning curve switching from Duncan to Barbara. Her lectures focus on things that rnt important on exams (exams focus on processes not components), and she doesn't give as much opportunity to engage in lectures. Exam wording is always AWFUL and confusing, but office hours r usually helpful + clarifying bc the answer keys rnt helpful.

ONE OF THE WORST PROFESSORS IN MY EXPERIENCE!! She overcomplicates the simplest concepts in the course for no reason. Your grade in the course will be heavily weighed on exams which are extremely difficult and the lectures are unhelpful. Professor needs to consider some changes or find a new career!

SO MANY MISTAKES!!!! Not to talk about the factual mistakes made in lectures, in homework problems, and in each midterm, she is not even showing the exam locations clearly ( she said there was a table explaining but there wasn't and the location where google map revealed was wrong)
Prof is a nice person and is helpful to students; however, echoing with what others are saying, her lectures confusing bc of mistakes that she makes, wording on the exam is very confusing

1. Always make basic mistakes like saturated fat contains double bonds, etc, during her lectures.
2. Exams are extremely difficult as you have no idea how and why points off.
3. Unreasonable and unhelpful lectures because of her repitious mistakes so being semi-forced to buy the expensive textbook
She oversimplifies the concepts way too much that you have no idea what the actual concept is.

Very hard exams that do not even closely resemble practice exams, study guide, or info from lectures. You will waste time attending lecture or studying materials she gave because the test has totally different topics with the exception of a few questions. She does not curve, she is very blunt and no-nonsense, and doesnt care about student success.

Not as bad as others here make her out to be. Genuinely helpful outside of class, but she assigns way too much work for a 1-credit course in my opinion. Her quiz questions are usually vaguely worded, and her lab manuals are often self-contradictory.
dont take her. she's literally impossible and is a terrible grader.
She is unreasonable sometimes in treating students and asks students to spend so much more time in this course than they should.

Professor Akum was one of the best profs I had at NYU- pls dont listen to the other reviews! she does give a bit of work but its not hard to do well and she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. she is also always available for help outside of class and is just super nice!

The best bio prof that i have ever had at NYU so far. She's funny, caring and accessible.
Def recommend taking this class with Prof. Akum
Greatest lab taken. She explains everything carefully. The syllabus and grading policy are  clear. Awsome!
I don't understand, why does NYU only allow her to teach one 1-credit course and one 0-credit course? Oh wait---

Yo this lab was so dumb. The quiz questions were sometimes asking for the most specific details from the lab modules and procedures and for some reason there were consistently grammar and wording mistakes on almost every quiz. TA's would sometimes argue over how to grade certain questions, I think I put almost as much time into this as POB II.

I don't know about the course reviews but for a 1 credit lab this was not it. I am taking chemistry and bio but a 1 credit class stresses me out more than the others themselves. Its strange and absurd how difficult the post lab and quizzes are.

Barbara is the lab coordinator of BIOL-UA 123 and has to be one of the WORST professors I have ever encountered here. She expects so much from A 1 CREDIT CLASS: pre-lab quizzes, post-lab questions, quizzes, and even a final! The questions are worded so horribly and ambiguously. Do not take this if you want to have a good GPA
Do not take her class

She's tough, but I notice a lot of people here are saying that's it's "too much work" for a 1 credit class. It doesn't matter. She is preparing you for future in the medical field, this workload is only for our benefit. Professor Akum is a good teacher and if you ask for help she'll give it. Don't let the low ratings fool you, give her a chance!!!
Very helpful and great at explaining difficult topics.
Simply the best. Professor Akum teaches in a way that is simply understandable. Plus she is always available to explain concepts. Overall the best Professor.

I see a lot of bad ratings here and it honestly breaks my heart. professor Akum is by far, the only reason I passed POB this semester. Albeit, I haven't taken her bio lab, so maybe it's different. But honestly give her a chance, she's very helpful and she WILL prepare you for a future in the biology/medical field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Akum's class is very fun and engaging, while at the same time fair in its coursework. There are quite numerous work to do, but they are not insane or too time consuming. The professor herself is pretty silly and very caring - she really wants us to do our best! I'm positive you'll have a great time!

She's a wonderful professor. Her grading methodology is fair. It's really as simple as if you write the wrong answer or miss critical components of an answer then you do not receive the points lol. Her quizzes are easy. The comments below are painfully misleading. Can we also appreciate that she is one of the few Black female stem professors at NYU

Professor Akum is absolutely awful. She is unsympathetic to any situations faced by her students, whether they are grading inconsistencies or life events. Only take this class if you want to meet one of the worst professors NYU has to offer. She's a harsh grader for no reason at all and seems to want to make her students' lives awful.

For a 1 credit class, Professor Akum does way too much. Along with weekly post labs, pre-labs, and lab simulations, she makes us take quizzes and even a final exam?? The quizzes itself have very ambiguous questions that are worded horribly. She also feels the need to email us 10 times a day for whatever reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Akum is not only absurdly harsh, but the grading scheme is so inconsistent that even if you pull material directly out of her videos/modules for pre/post-labs, you somehow get points off. So many aspects of the course are unclear that even the TAs are confused. This class should be worth more than 1 credit for the amount of effort it needs.

Dr. Akum wants to make your life harder. There is a prelab/postlab for every experiment, super long packets to read, and four quizzes that each have 40 questions and are 45 minutes long. The TAs are forced to grade extremely harshly by Dr. Akum and the questions are so ambiguous. Talk to your TAs and make friends with them, you'll need it.

While Prof. Akum seemed very nice, I found her course material to be very sloppy. From the formatting of lab handouts & slides to the wording of question, things were not orderly or concise, which led to overly complicated explanations for fairly simple concepts. She also frequently waited to upload assignments due on Monday until Sunday afternoon.

It really came down to the inconsistent and harsh grading. Although Professor Akum and the TAs would provide study guides for assessments, they took off points for smallest details on quizzes and lab reports.

Do NOT take this course, especially on the pre-health track. This one-credit course will ruin your GPA, and it's not worth it. Writing assignments and lab report instructions were super vague with little instruction on what specifically is wanted. The grading is inconsistent as one quiz was regraded bc there were higher marks.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. This 1 credit class took up as much time as some of my 5 credit classes. She writes vague questions and grades too harshly. She replaced quizzes with massive papers for online class. They were in a highly specific, rigid style. This wasn't in the syllabus, she made class harder after COVID for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst course ever. Three quizzes and a few long assignments determine the majority of your grade. Extremely unorganized class, very slow response times. Unclear grading criteria, very tough grader and does not allow you to dispute your grade. Encourages and enforces tough grading for the TAs. Asked a TA to regrade because the TA was "too lenient".

This was my second time taking a class with professor shehata. She is such a kind woman and really wants her students to understand the material. She brings in guest speakers to talk about auditing in the real world. There's no midterm, but instead 5 quizzes, a group project, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely passionate and knowledgeable about accounting. Makes it easier to learn a boring and difficult topic. Not my favorite class but since it is a requirement, glad I took it with her.

Great prof. I did kind of bad in the start of the semester so fell behind quickly. This is the type of class where you actually have to pay attention during lectures. I figure I could just doze off during class and self-learn the stuff by myself like I usually would with most other classes. Wasn't the best choice I made, and kind of regretted it.

First of all, really knowledgeable, experienced professor who knows accounting very well, also teaching. If u want to learn sth for accounting, definitely recommend. However, exams and work are annoying. I will say a really professional person who look very warm and helpful, but also know students a lot. Not easy
So so lovely. An awesome person and teacher with a great heart and a real passion for what she teaches. Will always recommend!!!

Professor Shehata was amazing. I learned so much from her lectures and she was great at engaging students. Super sweet and always willing to help after class or during office hours. Would definitely recommend. some people say the curve is bad but I feel like the curve was similar to the other PFA classes
I really enjoyed the class. Would 100% recommend.
Best teacher hands down

Professor Shehata is excellent! She really wants to see her students succeed and understand accounting. I definitely recommend going to office hours so that she can get to know you and to make sure you understand all of the concepts in class.

I would say Shehata is great overall. One thing that you should keep in mind that the competition in the class is usually pretty tough, which makes the stern curve tougher. However, if you plan on pursuing a career in finance you need to know accounting and this class drills it.
Debit on the left, Credit on the right

Prof. Shehata cares a lot about the subject and you can tell how passionate she is to teach. However, the Stern curve can definitely be tough and push you down a letter grade. To do well, I recommended reading the textbook for the homework, while for the tests I recommended thoroughly going through the slides but the tests are not too difficult.

The best PFA professor, in my opinion. Yes, you will need to put in the work because of the curve, but GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!! It helped me so much because she literally doesn't let you leave until you understand the material. Interestingly, I don't even want to do accounting/finance, but I still enjoyed the class.

Prof. Shehata REALLY loves accounting. You can tell by her lectures and by the effort she puts in her class. She  explains everything super well, and does a great job. The curve is kind of brutal, but her tests are pretty straightforward so if you put in the effort, you can definitely get that A.
I dont even take her section of the class. But her review videos are the only things keeping me sane. Goat.

She's a good professor. The main issue was that the textbook was meh and didn't help much with reviewing. Also, be wary that this is the only section where you cannot take a single reference sheet for the exams (which make up 75% of your grade), so you'll have to cram in a sea of boring entries, rules, and tedious calculations. Bubbly prof though.

This is for Accounting and the Blockchain This has been my favorite 2 credit course offered at Stern. You can come in with no knowledge about blockchain stuff and still come out with a great understanding of the fundamentals. Presentations are super easy to understand and there is a speaker every class. 10/10 would reccomend!

Auditing had 4 quizzes, 3 software asgnmts, 4 case studies, 4 discussions, a group project, & a final. Everything but the group project was short. Don't bother reading the txtbk. I learned a lot & you can tell she loves her job. She seems to genuinely care about her students & her lectures are fun. I wish I could take her for every class.

GREAT PROF!!! Really cares about her students and makes accounting fun. HOWEVER, beware that the curve in her courses are ROUGH. Top 25% on the last midterm was 97%. Also, it seems those interested in pursuing accounting take her class, therefore, overall the student body is better at accounting.

Professor Shehata's lectures are super engaging & explain concepts very well. I took her for both PFA and Accounting & the Blockchain. For people who are interested in taking Accounting & the Blockchain, it is definitely very fun and I really enjoy the topics she teaches; however, the workload for a 2-credit class is a lot, so be aware of that.

The absolute BEST. Prof. Shehata is a fantastic professor and an even better person. She literally makes accounting FUN! Never thought I'd like accounting, but she genuinely inspired me to change career paths. She has a wonderful and bubbly personality and truly cares about her students. You should absolutely take her as your professor.
I had Shehata for accounting and auditing and she was great for both. One of the really rare professors who just loves her job and it shows!

Great professor in terms of how well she teaches. She goes into a lot of detail to make concepts more understandable. HOWEVER she is the only PFA professor that does not allow open-book/cheat sheet and the curve for her class is brutal (because a lot of people do well). So be prepared to study hard and in depth for her class if you want to do well.

She is great but the curve is too bad. Worst curve among all other sessions. All other classes are curving up but we are curving down. The median of midterm 2 is 87, unbelievably high. Would have chosen Kim.

Incredible professor whose genuine passion for accounting is evident from her lectures. She manages to make accounting fun and easy to understand and is incredibly kind, caring, and engaging. Would highly recommend.

She was really engaging the entire semester and tries her best to make accounting somewhat interesting. She gives a good amount of practice and her exams aren't surprising. There's homework due almost every week. The hardest thing about the class was the Stern curve because everyone does so well.

Every other PFA professor at Stern has open-book exams. But with Professor Shehata, you need to memorize how to do every problem instead of understanding what you're learning. Great class if you enjoy spending hours memorizing stuff from her slides. I had to make ~100 flashcards before each exam. Not a great choice if you want to have free time.

Shehata is an absolute unit! Best professor I've had at Stern. She is extremely fun in class, provides tons of resources, and makes herself available all the time if you need help. Tests aren't very hard, and homework is quite manageable too. The Stern curve will totally screw you over, though. That (and my questionable work ethic) ruined my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Shehata is undoubtedly one of the greatest professors/teachers Ive had in my life. Her clear love for teaching makes learning a tedious and boring topic such as accounting fun, and incentivizes students to want to do good in her course. If you are struggling, go to every office hours and show her that you care and you cant go wrong.

Overall Professor Shehata was an excellent teacher. I highly recommend taking her if you can get into her class. She is very good at explaining different topics and is helpful during office hours. ACCTUB-1 is a difficult course and you have to be very well prepared for the exams.
Best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I would def recommend Prof Shehata's class. It was sometimes hard to pay attention to the lectures, but I was able to understand the material by reading the textbook. The textbook homeworks are easily to get full credit for. I did well on the exams by making detailed formula sheets, and the curve isn't as bad as other accounting profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Shehata is very nice and a good teacher. Lectures are sometimes boring, though, and can occasionally get disorganized. If you fall behind even a little, you'll have no idea what's going on when she's doing problems in class. Also, the curve is pretty brutal, and her questions are often worded awkwardly, so be careful. Still, very good professor.

This professor makes something as boring as accounting fun to listen to, her energy is great. I loved having her and would have her again! I don't understand the complaints about the curve, not much she can do about that. She's not making exams so easy that one mistake puts you to B+ tho. Don't need to read the textbook, but you should participate.

Professor Shehata really cares that you learn the material, but you pretty much need to prepare for class by reading the textbook material before showing up to the lecture. Her lectures are more like worksheets to test your knowledge than purely trying to teach the concepts. Overall a great professor, but the class is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's not a very good lecturer. I wouldn't recommend taking her class - she is an extremely harsh grader, and the curve is brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, I have no clue why the ratings are so high. Maybe its because its online classes. The online version sucks. She goes too fast. Her slides are NEVER in the correct order and it takes a few min to find the slide shes talking about and then shes already moved on. Just circles everything on slides without info. I hate accounting.

Everyone at Stern loves Shehata, but I hated this class. There is a ton of content, and it's not really presented in a way I found easy to understand. Exams are very hard, and the curve in her class is insane. Impossible to get an A. This class made me truly hate accounting. As much as everyone recommends it, it's not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very thorough and good at explaining concepts. Does a good job at making accounting exciting.
Always motivated for class
