An amazing professor. Makes accounting easy and interesting to learn. The only problem is everyone does so well (since she's such a good teacher) that it's a pretty steep curve to get an A. One of my favorite professors at Stern.

Great professor and human being. Handled the mid-semester shift to Zoom very well. You can clearly tell she cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants everyone to do well. Pay attention in class, do all the homework honestly, and you won't have to study much to do well on tests.
really great professor!

Professor Shehata makes all of the material clear and provides a variety of resources to make sure that her students are successful. However, since she makes everything so straightforward and clear, the curve won't do you any favors.
Gem of a woman. Will help you do well. All you have to do is try and this class is an easy A. Do the homeworks and the smartbook assignment and you will know the material 100%

Professor Shehata is the only accounting professor you should take. She turns the boring subject of accounting into a somewhat interesting topic and that by itself is extremely impressive. Also, if you have half a brain you will do well in this course
Great professor! Very energetic and cares about the material / teaching it well. Easy to follow course pack with detailed slides. Lots of practice exams that resemble the actual exams.

TAKE HER!!! Cannot stress this enough. This woman changed my life! She brings so much excitement to her classroom - I've never had a dull day in FA (shocking, but true)! Her grading is fair and always sees when students are trying their hardest. Go to her office hours and get to know her too. She cares so much about her students. YOU'LL LOVE HER!!!

She is awesome!!! There is a reason why she is one of the top 50 professors in the country. Her lectures are spectacular and she makes FA interesting. She actually inspired me to change my major. She is so accessible outside of class and is willing to help you.

Amazing professor!! Explains complex concepts very clearly with lots of great examples. Very accessible outside of class if you need extra help or practice. Highly recommend and would definitely take again!

Hands down the best professor I had my freshmen year at Stern. She is an amazing teacher - makes her points very clear. She made me like accounting. Go to class every day and participate -- you'll get an A. Don't mess up on the homeworks, they're electronic and you get multiple tries.

I love her. You can clearly tell she loves accounting, and she is so amazing at teaching it! I took this class for like 2 days last semester before I was dropped from the waitlist and that teacher made it seem so hard. Choose Prof. Shehata- she makes it seem much simpler and easier and she's very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Challenging but definitely worth it. You learn so much foundation in this course

Professor Shehata is one of the BEST professors you can have! She makes the classes super interesting and it's amazing to see how much she cares and provides help outside her lectures. Hands down, one of my favourite classes. Definitely take her

Taking this course changed my career projections and actually changed my life (no I'm not being dramatic).Professor Shehata is hands down one of the best (or the best) professors I have ever had. I found the class incredibly interesting, especially with the care she took to ensure students took in as much as possible. TAKE HER, TAKE HER, TAKE HER!

The best the Stern Acct dept has to offer. TAKE HER. SO nice and explains concepts until they are crystal clear. Participate. She will help you until you understand and never makes you feel bad when answering questions wrong in class. Exams are fair and her review guides are accurate representations of the real tests. Makes boring material exciting

Awesome professor! Accounting starts off easy, but gets fairly complicated at the end. Prof. Shehata presents even the most complex topics in a straightforward and engaging manner. You will do great if you pay attention during lectures and put in the work to truly understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. Tests are fair based on what is taught and homework. Very inspirational, she really cares and believes in her students.
Very good teacher. Very understanding. Take her.

Professor Shehata is pretty decent. She does her best to make the subject enjoyable. However, she doesn't allow any sort of cheat sheet for her exams, so you pretty much have to remember everything, which is really tough. Her homework assignments are online through Connect, which are really long and boring, and you don't actually learn that much.

Her lectures couldn't be much clearer.  Her class is easy to understand and she gives periodic quizzes which help students stay on task.  If you're even the slightest bit interested in accounting, she also has the ability to get you hooked with her enthusiasm and relevant real-world articles that she shares periodically.  I recommend her 100%.

SHE IS AWESOME. no really.. let's be real.. accounting isn't that interesting. shehata does her best with an otherwise dry subject and works really hard to present information in a CRYSTAL CLEAR way. Financial accounting is one of the first business classes students take at stern and she bridges the gap and introduces the topic really well. TAKEher
she's FANTASTIC. she really really cares about her students and always presents information in a clear, concise way in class!! if you work hard, it'll pay off. TAKE HER TAKE HER
She is amazing!! exams and quizzes are straight-forward and she covers everything in class! and she's funny and helpful!

Prof. Shehata is one of the best professors I've had at NYU. She actually makes accounting interesting and easy to learn. She used to work at PWC and stopped to raise her baby, and I basically want to be her. She's that awesome.

Amanda was an unique experience for me. I've never had a teacher I genuinely disliked. For one, she's so particular about words' meanings that she should have her own dictionary. This wouldn't be so bad if she didn't make you feel slow if you're not on her wavelength. Unless you're of that very select few that can mesh with her, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: she is an incredibly tough grader, no one in my class got higher than a B for writing assignments. insane amounts of reading before every lesson, participation matters A LOT and also she is v strict about ai checks. people in class got accused of ai use pretty occasionally even tho they had solid proof that they didnt. wishing yall the best of luck
She's tough, but I think fair. Knows what she's doing for sure. You'll get a lot out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: How much she likes you in class heavily depends on how much/well you participate in class. Sitting doing nothing will actively hurt your grade. She is also very bad at explaining assignments, genuinely everyone in my class had no idea what we were supposed to write about because her explanation consisted of re-reading the assignment description.

AWFUL. Makes her class feel longer than it is and clearly ruins everyones mood just walking in. She feels over qualified and makes students live up to an unreasonable standard. The strictest professor I have had and will try to subtly degrade you. Tough grader and cannot stand absences or tardiness, thinks she's the only class you are taking. FYSM
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amanda (yes, you can call her Amanda) was my prof 2 years ago and while the experience was positive, I came here to say that I've been working with her in the Writing Center since then on other stuff and my impression of her has only gotten stronger. She can solve ANY writing problem and she always has a relevant life lesson to offer

I just started today with my new prof for the spring and it made me realize how much I already miss Amanda. She's so animated and passionate and invested and like how cool is it to learn from a professional writer? My schedule didn't match with hers this semester but I will def be visiting her in the Writing Center.

Amanda is a feminist diva who leads with confidence, knowledge, and expertise. She won't edit your thoughts. Instead she'll help you convey them. I will never forget the AMA where she answered all of our questions about college and art and life. She treated us like adults and held us to a high standard and I am really grateful for the experience.

While Amanda is very smart and talented, she has the ego to match. She can be condescending and passive-aggressive. She is very particular, with a strict no devices rule and odd pet peeves. The GOOD thing about this is that if you're willing to play by her rules, you'll be fine. I ended up with some work I really liked. Though if you can avoid, do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad Bad Bad. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She allows zero electronics(all paper and pen except for homework), gives hefty assignments, and deducts points if she sees a device without warning. She tries to be nice but ends up tearing up students when their ideas don't match hers. She's VERY rude,sensitive and says she is open to other opinions but is not and expresses her political ideology
She is smart but has weird pet peeves and will pick favorites and grade accordingly. The class was still engaging and she had some fun assignments.

Rudest and most condescending Professor I have ever met at NYU. Was quick to drop her class. Enjoys humiliating students. Avoid at all costs and for your own mental health. You can get just as much out of many of the other professors in this departments. Just plain rude and unlikeable.
She's the worst, period. Had her last semester. Avoid at all costs:)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amanda is an unreasonably harsh grader for the little amount of instruction she gives you. She's smart and talented, but expects her students to already be thinking like her before they walk in the door. GPA killer, there are much better options.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amanda is honestly one of the most passive aggressive teachers I've ever had. She treats you like a high schooler in the worst way possible, like we're babies that know nothing. She rude and makes bad jokes. I learned basically nothing from her class.

Generally very rude to students. Very unhelpful. Will not answer questions from students over email if she thinks the information could be found *somewhere* else or considers the questions stupid. That includes questions asking for clarification about an assignment or specific citation formatting questions. Slow to give feedback on first drafts.
Amanda was a joy to have as a professor. When my cat died, she gave me a week to recollect myself. Great person, and even after graduating, we still get coffee.
Professor is very particular about lots of things. Beware of lots of work. She will lecture you on mistakes you make.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I had at NYU. I made a mistake and was on her bad side for the rest of the class. Her exercises were unnecessarily tedious and did not help me grow as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are engaged, you will do well. Amanda values voice, creativity, and curiosity. She made a required class extremely enjoyable. I learned a lot.

She is not considerate of her students. If you think so otherwise, have fun failing. literally. If your zoom camera is not on, shell put the class on hold and wait for you. Casually flexes her awards as if she doesnt care Do anything wrong and shell make you feel like a failure I try not to eat anything before class, otherwise I might throw up

As long as you show her you are working hard, she will recognise the effort. She may appear cold and her feedback is not so constructive but she will do her best to help. Amanda cares for her students and she wants the best out of them.

Amanda is scary and mean. She does not play around and she is extremely punctual. She basically told me that my draft doesn't qualify as a draft and that I should go to the writing center. She makes you want to cry and give up on your dreams and think that you suck at writing.
Worst professor I've ever had at NYU. No empathy. Brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amanda is a queen, don't even read the other reviews. She's kind of cold at first but once she warms up to you/your class she's really wonderful. Yes, she's tough, but her class is always interesting and you can tell she's really rooting for you to succeed. Also, don't show up late or make up excuses for late papers as she'll immediately hate you.

None of her feedback is ever helpful, because she'll just find other things wrong when you fix it. She decide early on that I was a horrible writer and no matter how often I went to the Writing Center she continued to give me the exact same grade on every paper I wrote. She's just straight up mean and awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great guy

Very structured, Amanda encourages her students to "play with language" and explore their abilities as writers through her class discussions and various writing exercises. She sets a high bar for her students to strive for. Amanda truly cares about her students and provides them with the tools to progress. A class for those serious about writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Amanda Yesnowitz is an inspirational and respectable instructor. She facilitates group discussion over class materials, but doesn't put up with students who disrespect other students. Not only does she teach essay writing exceptionally, but she understands academia within the context of the art world. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Completely turned my writing around. I'm not a good writer, but her love for language is infectious. Her passion for writing brought out my best work. Not to mention that she is an extremely talented musical theatre lyricist. Very stylish and nice to look at. I would definitely take Amanda's class again if given the chance.
love her. the class sucks but she's amazing

writing the essay art in the world sucks to begin with and I don't think ANY teacher could solve that issue. But Yesnowitz works with a tough course and tries to get her students to make the most out of it and I love her for that. She's a difficult teacher, but her spirit in class and work ethic makes it worth it

Amanda is a tough teacher, but genuinely wants her students to excel. She does not give too much work, only one writing exercise or a reading per class. She is a tough grader but respects students that put in work and improve throughout the semester. I love her!!!

Amanda is a tough-cookie on the surface, but she is genuinely passionate about what she is teaching. She wants each of her students to succeed, though it can be difficult to perceive at times. She does have a bit of a cocky attitude, but in the end, at least I knew I had a confident teacher. Show her you care and she gives you the utmost respect.

It's her way or the highway. Also, she has "yes" AND "no" in her last name. That's never a good sign. Even if you write a paper that you believe in and has clear evidence, if she doesn't personally agree with it, she will shoot it down. All of her feedback is geared towards changing your paper to something she wants to hear.

Smart, but mean. Yesnowitz knows what she's talking about, but she creates an absolutely detestable atmosphere in the classroom. She makes a bad course worse. At the same time, I do have some respect for her. Her exercises improved my writing. But she could have done that without making everyone miserable
She is not helpful or understanding at all. While I did learn a bit over the semester, I only learned how SHE likes essays to be written, and not how to become a more proficient writer. AVOID.

This class is not to be taken lightly. Punctuality is key. AY is very strict about her rules She is very clear as to what she expects tho, so if you stick to her guidelines you are golden. Exercises help and the atmosphere in classalthough tensecan be helpful if you use it wisely. Very self driven class. Read texts,participate & turn in all work.

Amanda is truly the worst thing to happen to my academic career.  She is mean, judgmental, condescending, and the opposite of supportive or helpful to the students.  She will only allow you to meet with her for two 15 minute sessions the whole semester, no exceptions.  She is the worst teacher I have ever had, and made me hate writing so so much.

Do not take this professor. She is rude and judgmental, and she will hold a grudge against you for any mistake. She doesn't care if you have a good reason to miss class, such as illness, and will not accept late assignments. Nor will she accept assignments over email. There is no leniency in this course. Either be perfect or hate this class.

I tried to give Amanda the best rating I could, but there was nothing nice to say. She is a awful teacher. Her assignments are unclear, and wont accept any questions over them. She refuses to accept emails, and, is extremely unforgiving. If you slip up once, be prepared to never live it down. Please avoid he at all costs.

Amanda is easily the worst teacher I have ever had. She is self righteous giving little validation or respect to the opinions of others. She is inconsistent with her method of teaching: advocating messy thinking and expecting clear and developed ideas in preliminary writing. Seeking help is useless. Its clear she does not like her job at all

I was ready to bash her on this, but there's not a rating on kindness. She's a wicked, selfish, fake and pretentious woman, but she is really clear about what she's looking for in the writing. She won't grade you well, though, if she disagrees with your argument, no matter how well it's supported. I hate her.

Amanda establishes a negative atmosphere among her students, all the while praising herself. My best definition of her would be a very opinionated and passive aggressive woman that immediately picks her few favorite students to adore and creates a personal bubble that keeps other regular students at the helm of her superiority complex. Worst Prof
Honestly I was scared to go to her class from her stigma but she is an incredibly sweet and intelligent person. She really taught me how to become a better writer. She not easy though

I graduate at the end of this semester. After four and a half years at NYU, I can safely say that Amanda Yesnowitz was the worst professor of my college career. An accomplished writer, but not teacherly at all. Unsympathetic and egotistical to the point where these qualities render anything positive about her and her class mute.

This woman is nothing but evil. I loved my first semester of Writing the Essay and got A's. She made my second semester hell and was nothing but disrespectful to everyone in my class. I did the work, I was polite, I worked to form my writing to her liking, but nothing worked. She also kicked a friend out of the class. AVOID HER.
yeah...don't do it. she picks favorites and is just not respectful of her students if you're not one of her favorites. She's condescending and harsh-she can't empathize. worst first semester ever

Amanda is a nice person, but a useless teacher.  She is very opinionated and set in her ways, she is an extremely harsh grader and has high expectations for her students. She is not helpful in comments nor conferences, and is just over all horrible at teaching WTE. Many of her discussions are interesting but irrelevant to essay help.

Amanda is a nice professor, definitely has her favorites. She not helpful at all while conferencing, and is a relatively harsh grader (depending on how much she likes you). Amanda also likes people to be on time and not tardy to class. Overall, she is cool, but isn't inspiring.
Essentially, she's Carrie Bradshaw. Consider yourself lucky if you get Amanda for WTE.

Amanda is a very good teacher. Her writing exerises prepare you well for writing the essays, however, she is rather unhelpful when it comes writing to the essay itself. Her written and verbal feedback is often vague and useless. She is also very opinionated and will debate with those who disagree. She has very high standards and expectations.

Amanda is proactive in her work and teaching. We have had very interesting conversations in class. She promotes a warm and cohesive classroom environment. She is interesting and fun to listen to. Her methods of teaching are unconventional and full of personal zest. Overall, I enjoyed her class. Fresh, challenging, mind provoking, and an experience.
Amanda is the best, nicest teacher i have ever had.  She's so sweet and really helpful!! I wish i could have her again!!

I actually had a pretty good conversation with her in our one and only writing conference that was completely unrelated to my essay and to writing in general, but regardless, she's an unhelpful teacher who blatantly encouraged/praised only two of the students and refrained from giving me helpful comments on my papers.

Amanda is truly amazing!  She is super sweet and very helpful!  She gives clear directions and tells you exactly what she wants.  She can be opinionated, and this turns some people off however, her opinions are interesting and worthwhile to listen to.  It is obvious that she is very intelligent and passionate about her work!
No Comments

Challenging but rewarding.  Amanda makes you work for your grade (but you'll be glad you did).  Interesting views on art...lots of great discussions so far.  She knows a lot about good writing and is very clear about what she wants.  She offers many useful tips.
very sweet and helpful
Amanda is an energetic prof and provides many practical ways to improve writing skills. Her love for the  English language is surprisingly infectious.
i always got the feeling that she didn't like my writing, and therefore i couldn't get above a b- in the class. very subjective and picky picky picky. didn't learn a thing.
The worst.  No help at all.  Can't look you in the eyes.
Everything drives her nuts.  including her own voice.
My most inconsistant and confused teacher ever. Don't try to learn anything in this class. Annoying. I couldn't stand her.

Agile was the CS course of my dreams.

Taking it was simultaneously one of the best career decisions of my life, one of the most instructive experiences I've ever had, and one of the easiest high grades I've ever gotten.

Prof. Bloomberg's courses are the future of CS education. NYU promote this man before MIT recruits him, lol.
Prof is solid.  A lot of BS from students but he deals with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The course is a mess. The professor insists on using Discord, but graders and tutors reply slowly, if at all. All classes share one chaotic channel. They keep talking about rules, yet changed group selection to random for one person. The grading is unfair. I'll never take this class again.

Prof is lowkey hilarious but doesn't play around—expect to actually learn Python. He keeps it 100, mixes dad jokes with deep dives, and makes sure you don't just vibe, you thrive. If you're down to grind and want a prof who's both chill and big-brain, this class slaps.
Take this class.  You finally learn to make real software.
Challenging but rewarding class. Professor is super engaging, makes lectures fun. Definitely stay on top of the group projects - they can get tricky. unstuck ai was a lifesaver for exam prep!
Recommend this course
Straightforward.  You get as much as you put in.

Earned an A in both Agile and Software Engineering classes, but he ignored my emails and DMs when I asked if he wrote recommendation letters for grad schools, thinking our project-based courses meant more interaction. If you don't write them, just say so—no need to leave students on read.

Bloomberg is strict but kind. You work with the same people on the same project for almost the whole semester.  It's basically an internship where you learn in trial by fire.  Hardest part is learning to deal with teammates who are slacking... Bloomberg helps you avoid team conflict as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hands down the most useful CS course.
I learned so much
One of the most honest nicest professors.  Knows his stuff and likes to go off-script.

TBH, I wasn't a great experience to take this class during summer session I. The workload felt overwhelming for a 6-week class, especially when you're juggling multiple classes. He tends to answer the same questions over and over, which often goes off the topic. Maybe his in-person class during the Spring or Fall sem would be a better option.

Prof Bloomberg was great at getting concepts across, but his lectures will usually get sidetracked either because someone asks an unrelated question or another topic arises. I still learned a lot though. His grading is really harsh. On the final, I made a small mistake on a problem set but got the entire problem set deducted from my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Straightforward class.  Bloomberg is easy and helpful.
the only course in CS where learn real skills
Take if you enjoy carrying free riders

agile is solely based on a. your group mates and b. ur knowledge of web development prior to joining the class. you should go into this class knowing a good portion of web dev or it might be tough to learn everything on the fly. the weekly gradebot constantly miscalculated grades, so clarify your grades w him, especially the final grade.

This course is very useful and enjoyable if you are 1. fine with group projects and 2. have some prior experience with web/software engineering, but not much. Covers useful tools used in software engineering, lectures are more like introductions for you to start learning by yourself. Grading is in general easy but make sure it's the right course 4u
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You do one big fullstack project over the course of a semester and couple quizzes here and there. Very manageable and grading was lenient.
Super sharp and funny.  Nicest prof in CS.
Awesome
Incredible prof in the cs department, the best cs prof in CAS I met
Nice to first learner Pretty good online lectures, hw and quiz are not heavy.
Take him!!!! Really nice professor!
Caring and gives really great feedback, contents relatively easy. You learned, you get an A-
Lots of extra credits so Easy B+ and A-
amazing lectures, exam and quizzes are online which are pretty easy, gives great feedback!
Easy A  Just take him

The whole class is one big group project. Every week we checked in with our project with the TAs and were told it was looking great. When we submitted the final version, we got a 32%(!?). It's one thing to have high expectations, it's another to string students along into thinking they're doing well and then drop a bomb on their grade at the end.
Easy A. He is so nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great course.  Gives students every opportunity to get an A by providing tools to allow students to grade their own work before submitting it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bloomberg is very smart and takes his time to dive deep into the course topics and always had interesting thoughts on any questions I asked.
Very funny

Professor will give you a very subjective and unpredictable grade for the quality of your group project, which takes a great percent of your overall grade. There was no grading rubric for this quality evaluation, and he didn't show the mean or median quality grades of all groups. Very Unfair for project quality grading!
A lot of classes are project work (self study/ group study) without teaching anything, so most people chose to be absent on those days. Totally waste of time and tuition

He sends emails every Monday to release your current grade, which is very messy and contains a lot of errors. Every time students have to report those grading errors to him and course assistant, and wait until next Monday to check the updated grades on emails. You can't check your grade on the course website.
Prof. Bloomberg teaches to the good students in the room.  This is great if you care about learning.

Straightforward class, quizzes, and exams, but projects can be confusing without clear grading / instructions (graders are usually chill). Generally doesn't seem to care about his classes and students, can be condescending at times. However, he does teach highly relevant tools, libraries, skills, and frameworks. Mixed bag prof, wish he curved more.

He made changes to the instruction of assignments on the day before the deadline, which means if you do the homework early, you have to do it in another way again!! He only respond to some questions on Discord, and ignore many questions which might be more important and urgent.
Caring, funny, cuts through the bs.  Wish all professors were like this.

Need to self teach most things. Great opportunity to work on group projects. Highly recommend if you have web-app/JS experience or want some. While he is accessible outside class the tutors are not much help and your grade depends a lot on your group and the project you are working on. Expect some late night debugging. Overall, Great guy and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only course in NYU you could learn tons of engineering knowledge, do recommend you to take if you want to learn some

At first, the course seems to be teaching some trivial, not so useful material. However, if you seriously go through all the quizzes and materials, you do learn a lot about engineering a software and group work.
Amazing professor. Would take his class again.
Very knowledgeable and accessible outside class.  I wish there was more time to learn from him.

Professor Bloomberg is a great professor! If you ask him, he enjoys going deep into all kinds of interesting side topics that give you a real understanding.  I was lucky to get in off the waitlist... register early because his classes are really popular.

With Prof. Bloomberg, what you see is what you get.  He lays out the entire semester for you up-front, tells you exactly how you will be graded, what you're expected to do, and how to get an A.  Even though he doesn't take attendance, students who didn't come to class didn't do well.  Those who did come to class all got As.
The worst. the whole course is a shitshow. My biggest waste of tuition fee.
The worst professor ever. Pissed every single day taking his class. He just never cares much about his classes.

If you read the bad reviews carefully, you will find out Prof. Bloomberg is being blamed for a lot of things outside of his control. He is a very kind person with broad interest. He provides generous feedback, gives out interesting (though not always crystal clear) lectures, and helps students to establish interdisciplinary and practical skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: The prof isn't bad, but due to the structure of the class (a large group project) the course lectures feel pretty decoupled from the work students will have to actually do. Given the scope, I understand that not all topics can be covered in depth, but I found myself searching for more resources to supplement my learning that simply weren't there.

Maybe he's an expert in coding and he is knowledgeable, but he seems to have no interest in passing the knowledge to his students. He barely mentions the knowledge in the quizzes and the instructions for assignments are vague. This is a disaster. Hope he would see my words here and do something about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think that Professor Bloomberg likes or enjoys teaching. It is clear that at least for 101, he is there to get paid. There are multiple choice quizzes and assignments for comprehension. The assignments are optimized my being graded by automated tests he programs (another way he sort of avoids teaching/knowing students)
He does not teach effectively in class and the whole class is confusing.
Everything is beautifully laid out on his website, with clear grading criteria and due dates. The workload is medium, and the content is valuable. You can't go wrong with Prof. Bloomberg.

Clear syllabus, topic schedule, and grading criteria. Weekly quizzes (super easy), assignments usually every 1-2 weeks that take 3-5 hours to complete. Midterm and final exams are fair (easier than the homeworks). Only con is that his lectures are a little boring and when you ask questions he often tells you to just "go back and read the slides."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice guy - he's always willing to discuss and debate just about anything.
Great professor. Very organized and clear. Super helpful... when you ask for help. Recommended for anyone who likes ideas.

I just got an offer for an internship yesterday because of what I learned. After 3 years of CS, this is the first course I've taken that teaches something useful. Prof. Bloomberg is clear that he expects students to work, and he rewards those that do. You get to choose your own project, so the work is hard, but rewarding.

Course: Agile Dev. If you have no prior web dev exp with MERN stack, AVOID unless want to self-study for 4 months and work with trolls in group pj. Lecture is absolute joke, only terminology, then expects you to know everything and start coding. 0 support, arrogant & vauge to questions usually. Grade: A tho cuz I wrote tons. But, AVOID, dont try!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great Teacher!! Absolutely hilarious and funny! He is also a pretty good teacher and knows code well. Loved him!!Take him if you love code.

I had Amos for Web Design. HE WAS AWESOME. My grader sucked...I had all of the appropriate criteria; however, I lacked extra ***subjective*** dedication. I had an 89.67, I asked if there was something I could do for an A-, he liked me so much he rounded to an A. He's awesome if you show you care! Don't be afraid to fight with the grader... ����
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes you work for your grade. Exams can be much harder than the practice tests but he will curve it if the average of the class is low. His lectures are very dry and it is hard to pay attention but they are very informative and helpful for the exams and assignments.

This is an intro-level python class, while he loves give students heavy homework, making me feel overwhelmed. There are 4 lectures per week for this class, which is fine for me, but he also set 4 quizzes a week for every lecture, and the quizzes are 20% for the course GPA, which sucks. He usually make big mistakes in homework and even in exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amos has his unique style - not for me though. His homework usually required you to read ahead what we about to learn and take off a crazy amount of points when bugs are found. (MANY of my classmates went to tutors He doesn't seem like he is invested in the class. I didn't get information when asking his questions and gradually was demotivated.
Amos is ok, lectures can become a bit boring, but he does not seem to care much about the class...

Bloomberg makes you work for the grade and you have to do textbook reading to do well in the class. In my opinion he didn't effectively teach the material, rather he presented it to us with all the info but a lot of self teaching is required for this course. Homeworks require a lot of self learning beyond the basics taught in class. Tough exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomberg is a must take for Java! Even though he is probably the hardest professor in that subject, he teaches the course in a very efficient, organized, and effective way. Class is very textbook heavy and tests are difficult, but this course will prepare you for future Comp Sci courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Explains concepts clearly and in detail. Textbook is not necessary to do well in his class, but do pay close attention during lectures because MC questions have multiple answers (no partial credit for correct answers) and require you to recall obscure info. Practice questions are also recycled and don't reflect the exam. Know your CS concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I mean this: Agile with him was the worst class I've taken. Lectures are dry, exams are oddly worded multiple-choice Google forms, and he blindly grades everything using scripts. For the group project, you have to make a web app and learn to do so on your own in 2 weeks via YouTube. There's absolutely no effort put into teaching this class. AVOID!!
Unfair exams, that's it. Open coding questions are very vague.

Be ready to teach yourself. Homework require you to do work based on the chapter that is covered in the lecture after the due date, which makes it kind of pointless to go to class. But that forces you to read the book which helps with understanding the material well. Entertaining homeworks, easy second midterm (repeats questions from first one).

If you are a cs major student, you should definitely take his class. His lectures are super interesting and inspiring so that you won't be distracted by other things. Be prepared to work hard for midterms and final cuz it is not easy to predict what he would test you, but if you done your readings and pay attention to his lectures, you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: As the negative comments have revealedif you are taking CS just because everyone is taking it, don't take Bloomberg. You have to be really engaged to be successful. But it doesn't shed from the fact that he is a fantastic professor capable to make the material interesting. He will let you to make up for your mistake if you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thorough textbook reading is a MUST in order to do well on the exams. Homeworks are graded rather leniently, some will push you to the tutor center. Tests are not that bad, 30 multiple choice and 2 code writing exercises. Repeats mc questions sometimes. Not a bad class, Bloomberg makes you work for the grade.

Amos is overall very solid. Pros: grading is decently weighted on the hw (which is easy), and he will curve exams. Cons: exams are tricky - only 30 important multiple choice questions. Lectures are often slow. You need to take notes in lecture - obscure things he mentions are on tests. It's not difficult at all to get an A- with moderate effort.

Bloomberg's class is pure torture. He talks about random stuff and his ability to teach is close to zero. He is unable to keep students attention and listening to him is an experience from hell. Unfortunately, I couldn't say that I learned or understood a single thing in his lectures. He makes a dry subject feel like the Sahara. Stay away from him.

Mixed feelings about this class. Lectures are boring but you have to pay attention because the exams are really tough. A big portion of your grade will be homework, which is relatively easy, but the exams are seriously tough. Readings not necessary for class but I would suggest studying them for midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Made me decide to no longer be a computer science major. His practice tests do not prepare you for the exam. I would recommend taking a different professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amos is overall a very solid professor. Pros: grading is heavily weighted on the hw (which is very easy AND graded leniently), gives lots of extra credit, curves 1 letter grade. Cons: exams are tricky - multiple choice w/ MULTIPLE answers, lectures are often slow/boring. It's not difficult at all to get an A-/A with moderate effort.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Amos is a solid choice for intro to web design. The lectures can sometimes be a little dry, but he spices things up with sarcastic jokes. The projects are super easy to get 100 on. The tests are more difficult. Class average for the midterm was 70%. If you attend lectures on a regular basis, you can get at least a B with minimal effort.

The tests in this class can be a little tougher but overall the course is not hard. Amos is a good lecturer and teaches things quite well with good in class examples. His tests are weird because you have more than 1 answer and you have to circle all the correct answers to get the question right so beware. You will learn though so take him!
He is a great professor who has a good pace in class and gives easy exams.
A brilliant professor! He taught the content very well, had a good pace with material, very responsive with questions.

Excellent professor who is dedicated to pedagogy, and driven by a genuine joy of computer science. Although the coursework can be burdensome, he is an incredibly fair grader and will help students who show initiative. An A is totally achievable if you put in the work. Generous with extra credit, textbook is hugely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A very helpful and informative professor, although he didn't seem like it at first. Hard to reach him by email which gave the impression that he didn't want to talk to students, but it turns out he's actually rather helpful and approachable in person. Do the homework yourself and really understand the concepts because the exams are difficult.

His lectures are kind of dull, but they can be helpful if you pay attention. He loves taking questions, so that's good. Just go to him if you have questions. The tests seem hard at first, and then if you get the essentials of the python, the tests will become so much easier. He can be a nice choice, and CS is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes a solid choice. Very clear and thorough and available outside class. However, his exams are very long and often dont test the material in a way thats considered and effective. This leads students who lose focus after a while to do worse in his exams. If youre reading this Amos, and I bet u are, test concepts that dont require much writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomberg gives a very informative presentation of the course material and clear instructions. His handsome look and great personality make it very hard to skip even one lecture. It was also a great time chatting with him during office hours. Exams are reasonable and he replaces lower early exam scores with the later ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs!

Very caring and kind. You learn mostly by doing your homework. He's always willing to help and wants you to know the material. His tests are kind of weird.. Some of his exam questions are structured ambiguously and he doesn't give partial credit, making it fairly difficult to get 100.. overall good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy! Always willing to help you out after class and has office hours pretty frequently throughout the week. His lectures aren't the most exciting thing in the world but he does a great job of teaching relevant material. Exams are basically just rehashed homework questions so, if you can do the hw you should be fine.

His class is fairly easy but his tests are sort of hard. Average for first test was 75 and second one was 70. Def one of the harder web design professors because of the way his questions are structured to have multiple correct answers on a multiple choice and you have to get them all to get the question right. Never went to lecture got a B so eh.

Challenging class for an intro level course given the difficulty of the assignments, but he challenges you to make you a better programmer and coder. His tests and assignments are a little vague sometimes, but he has very clear and engaging lectures.

The class is very easy to follow, with very little work.  There are 10 coding assignments, which we spend class time starting, and 3 tests, which we practice for in class.  For homework, there are online lessons, which are really easy to understand, and then short online comprehension quizzes. In general, if you pay attention, you'll do well.
Gives pretty bad feedback and doesn't care about students.

No required textbook, gave us links to online reading instead. Homework every other night, but if you took notes and followed along in class it was easy enough, though I did seek help from the class tutor. The midterm and final varied wildly from our study guides and I did not feel as prepared as I wanted to be. Otherwise a great professor!

Attendance & textbook not mandatory but lectures are very clear & informative. Go to review sessions before exams because he tells us what we should know/skip. Questions on exams are much simpler than class examples. Homework makes up most of the grade and they're straight-forward if you go to class and keep up. Friendly & helpful in office hours.

I took Intro to Programming because I thought it would be a good minor to go with a business degree. Literal worst experience of my life. Spent hours every week on the assignments and it was only Bloomberg's kids getting extra help every week. The average grade in this class is a C not an A-. Don't expect a curve and don't expect to learn anything.

Lectures and homework are pretty informative. However, he'll pretty much shut you down if you need help unless you're a girl or unless he thinks you have potential in CS. Had to study a lot on my own. Tests are pretty difficult and he only curved the class by 1%

Professor Bloomberg is a good professor and gives you a chance to do better on your second midterm, but you learn mostly through the assignments rather than in class. He's a tough grader and doesn't give partial credit, but is very helpful and has a great sense of humor. It's a great introductory class for Comp Sci minors/majors. Tests are tough.

He's pretty good at teaching programming but ultimately you end up learning both through his lectures and through the assignments and self-modules. It's really all about learning in lecture and trying to think in a logical manner that helps you make it through Python. He's a great professor and very nice if you need help.

Amazing professor with a great sense of humor. Exams are very reasonable and not difficult at all if you show up and pay attention in class. He makes lectures are fun and interesting. Highly recommend taking any of his classes.

I have no idea who everyone else had as a teacher because that was NOT Amos. If you are planning on taking Database Design, take it with Deena Engel. I repeat. Take the class with Deena. I learned more from the tutors than I did from Amos. Avoid his as a teacher at all costs.
OK professor. Not too enthusiastic or interesting. Gives very tough exams far different from the practice material.

Physical Computing was a great introduction to a topic which is basically nonexistent at the undergrad level. The professor is clear and grading is very fair. If you go to class and do the assignments you should easily be able to get an A.

Cannot say enough good things about him. Assignments can be difficult, but they are always enjoyable. Midterms and final are straight-forward and over the basic information learned. Super understanding and helpful if you ask for it. Hope to take more of his classes.

Took for intro to web development. Came in as a complete newbie but left feeling pretty comfortable with basic HTML CSS and photoshop thanks to him. Always to help and will try to get you an A. He's also hilarious. 1010 would take again

AMAZING professor. Highly recommended! He teaches very well and makes the course super interesting. Homeworks can be a little hard but they are fun to do and they really help you understand the material. Exams are multiple choice, fill in the blanks and 2-3 code writing questions. If you study his notes and do the homework, youll get an A/A-.

Great professor, teaches with great clarity and patience. Has a great sense of humor. Exams are all multiple choice and are subject to a flat curve if the class had trouble with it. Homework is also offered with extra credit in case you need the grade buffer. Gives students every opportunity to get an 'A'.
Great professor! Clear lectures. I recommend taking his class.

One of the best professors I have ever had. I was brand new at programming and became extremely knowledgeable at several programming languages before the end of his class. I cant say enough good things about Amos.
Love this class. The professor clears up the course material remarkably and firmly. with Whatever the reason to take this course, you won't regret to have taken the class ever, never!
Kind of a by the books guy. I've a friend in the other class who had it way tougher. If you get the chance to take web design with AMOS then take it.
Excellent instructor. Very knowledgeable. Learnt every track for becoming a web developer from his web development intensive class.
Great teacher! Clear, good notes and easily approachable.

He is an excellent professor highly recommended. He gives real life examples all the time and he teaches you more than you should know. If you take another professor you are seriously stupid. I wish I can take his classes over and over again. And I will take his courses, if he teaches what I need to take
Excellent professor. Anything not understood will be clarified. Challenging hw, but midterms were fair. Grading was also very fair.

Challenging, yet helpful teacher. While going to lectures are not mandatory, he definitely makes it worth it. While homework can be very challenging at times, he is helpful in explaining, and even helps with parts of it in lecture. Midterms are short and usually easy, but he is a tough grader, and will catch your mistakes.
Really solid professor. Thorough explanations and a very fair grader.
Good professor and will help those willing to help themselves. His tests are easy and he'll show you how to do some cool stuff in Python
She is a very nice professor! The final project is interesting, and I really enjoyed the topic I chose.

Amanda was one of my favorite professors. She really ensures that you are heard during class conversations, and she makes it easy to participate. The nature of the course allows for group projects and personal assignments that allow you to apply media theory to topics and themes you enjoy. This helped me really retain information and media theory.

amazing professor! was hesitant because of the ratings but she's caring and clear about her expectations. as long as you show up to class ready to learn and participate this class will be an easy A for you. readings every week and discussion posts but nothing too difficult. interesting midterm and final project topics! I would recommend.

Amanda is a great professor who wants students to have a genuine interest in the culture industries, allowing us to apply our personal interests to projects and assignments. Lots of field trips, overall an easy and meaningful class.

I have never had a professor be so disrespectful and passive-aggressive in my time here at NYU. The way she grades the assignments makes no sense, she doesn't upload slides, and she has been flat out rude to her students multiple times, both in and outside of class. She is also very retaliatory toward those who do stand up for themselves. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: extremely unreasonable and super hard to communicate.
Amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Pierce was an amazing professor who truly cares about her students and the course. If you have the chance to take her class, don't think twice you won't regret it.
Amira is honestly very caring and understanding. She is always open to extensions and has a straightforward grading criteria. She offers many extra credit opportunities to boost your grade.
I normally hate english, but professor pierce genuinely made this class enjoyable. Not sure why she's rated so low. one of the best courses just do your work, show up, and you'll have a good grade.

I took FYSEM-UA 900 (Betwixt and Between: Liminality). It has a grading contract, so if you do 3 extra credit assignments you get an A. I highly recommend taking this course, not just because it's an easy A but because the work was interesting and Amira is genuinely so kind. It's obvious that she loves teaching and cares about her students a lot.

(FYSEM-UA 900: Liminality) Very long, boring, and unorganized class. Amira clearly cares about her students, but it seemed like she was unprepared and she was learning with us rather than teaching us. She uses a grading contract where you get a B from doing all your work and can only get an A by doing 3 extra credit works, which are time consuming.

She is definitely a great teacher. She really cares about her student and is being really nice to us. She now grades on a new contract where you can definitely earn an A by your hardworking.Well organized classes and moderate workload. Some reading materials are confusing and hard to understand, and that is the only problem I can find in her class.

TAKE HER CLASS!!! A+++++++teacher. Best writing prof at NYU. A fair amount of work load and an equitable grading system. The learning process has been enjoyable. Offered multiple extra credit assignments to make up for grades.

I just graduated, but I'm coming to RMP to write Prof Amira a review, because looking back on my time at NYU, she was one of my favorite professors. This was my first class where I felt like I had an original thought that I was eager to write about, and it came from an office hour with her. I've got more to say but too few chars. Very cool person.

I agree that she is definitely underrated. She really gives me useful advice during our conference, and if we are not prepared during the early conference in the week, we can schedule another conference with her later in the week to discuss the essay. She is super nice, and the extra bonus is not that hard.

She is so underrated at RMP. I think she is the best writing professor. She is informative and helpful. Writing can be hard, but she would provide extra credits to boost your grade. Although there are many works, you do actually learn things from her class.

Amira is a kind, flexible, and hard-working professor. The lectures/assignments are carefully thought out and the grading system GUARANTEES a B+ if you complete each assignment. 
Amira cares deeply and integrates multimedia sources into her lectures, is always eager to meet outside of class to discuss progress, and asks deep, pertinent questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Piece is very caring and gives great feedback. She makes class super engaging and is hilarious as well. She gives great feedback on papers and meets with students before the drafts are due. I would highly recommend.

amira is really caring and engaging. not much hw and honestly, you don't need to put much effort in those little hw and exercises as long as you do your main essays properly on time. she's lenient on giving extensions. she's not lenient on grades, however, she gives really detailed feedback and you'll get an A towards the end of the course.

Prof Pierce is the best writing professor and perhaps also one of the best professors I have ever met. She might assign you a lot of homework, but you should always know that she is always there to help you overcome difficulties. If you want to success in her class, use her office hours well.

Professor Pierce is definitely not an easy A, but its totally possible as long as you go to class, do the work and take advantage of extra credit or revision opportunities. Pierce was one of the most caring and kindest professors and she really does want to see you succeed.

one of the best professors I met at nyu! she gives homework basically every class, but that's pretty normal for the expository writing courses. if you show your hard work, you'll receive a fair grade. office hours help

Writing the Essay with Professor Pierce was definitely a TOUGH class, but I found that the challenge was what I needed in order to improve as a writer. Ask her to read over your drafts because she gives great feedback. Sometimes the homework can be tedious and confusing, but as long as you put in the effort, her grading will be fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Her WTE class scared me so much based on what I had heard about her reputation. In all honesty, the class was a lot of work and definitely was the hardest class of the semester. She gives good feedback though which is good for improving your writing.
She is really kind. Professor Pierce cares about her students and tries hard to make the class interesting. I would definitely recommend taking her class.

She's nice and cares about what her students are thinking, changing her way of teaching based on the students' needs. Participate in her class, you will learn things.  Each homework assigned will be related to your essays, so try to think of the main theme of your essay as early as possible. Try not to be late or skip class. Not an easy grader.
She is so nice and not such a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I was enthusiastic about writing at first. After taking this class, i did not learn much, yet felt writing is burdensome.
I choose Pierce for my writing sessions. She was immensely helpful and is bent on helping students no matter what. She also gives really good ideas.
Hard class
she struggles to convey what she expects from her students' works. She is also a very hard grader, most kids get Cs in this class.
Not helpful. Not clear in what she expects.

Pierce is a very charismatic professor however, she struggles to engage and convey information to her students. She is very helpful and is willing to help your writing but is very unclear on what she wants. In addition, she is very proud of keeping her C average in the class, despite the effort put in.
Gives a lot of assignments but is often unclear on what she actually expects. However, I think she's making an effort to remedy this.

Expository Writing is a confusing class and sometimes Pierce struggles to fully explain what she wants her students to do; however, if you ask for help, she will do her utmost and is in fact very useful.
There was a lot of writing in this class but I definitely learned a lot. She's nice, personable, and really helpful if you do the work.
I'd try to look for an easier wte teacher. She's a tough cookie. Not at all an easy grader.
The class is fairly challenging and she is not an easy grader, but she's a good teacher and keeps it at a very intellectual level. She's friendly and personable, as well.
She seems like a sweet teacher but she gives impossible hw assignments every class and takes pride in having a class avg of C no matter how hard you work.
Literally the best professor ever, and helps you with class registration like, a lot! She's so nice and relatable!
i'd give her a 6 if i could
literally so nice, such a good advisor 10/10 i could tell her anything

Amanda's the best. She's the perfect social worker - super empathetic - and an amazing professor. She truly makes spaces for everyone's experiences, and she made a large class feel smaller. The lectures were sometimes boring, but she brought in personal anecdotes from her work that made it more engaging. You'll miss out if you don't take her class.

One of my favorite professors this semester. She invites guest speakers to the class, and provides helpful lectures to get to more familiar with resources around you. The class atmosphere is good, and everyone shares his or her ideas freely. Take her lessons!
One of the best professors at NYU. Her classes fill up quick for good reason. She actually cares about students and likes to be a mentor.
I love Professor Nieliwocki! She's an amazing social worker and advisor! I totally recommend her for any classes she teaches. I hope to have her in the future if possible!

Write what she wants to hear (you get a generally clear idea of that via classes).
Go to her office hours each time before the essay and change according to her feedback (talk to her after class to get extra feedback)
She's a tough grader and I had to work so hard for the grade, but get on her good side and participate.

Overall, an amazing professor. Grades are determined by how dedicated you are to the readings, participating, and attending the class. I would say her grading is tough. If you go to her office hours, she gives great feedback for your essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera seems to be an ok professor who is passionate about what she teaches, but her grading is quite unreasonable. Even when going to office hours and speaking through ideas to get specific feedback, she still finds ways to bring down your final grade.
Amazing professor and really cares if you understand the concept and readings .

OK prof with interesting classes. 3 papers (1 per unit) - she does cap the grade on the 1st paper to do a gradual evolution. Grades rather toughly. Get on her good side from the beginning by participating. She is a rather average/slightly above average prof so idk why there seems to be sm hate in rmp.
Extremely biased, isnt open to your opinion and cruel grader. Avoid her at all costs.
She can be a harsh grader, but you will learn how to improve your writing skills. The readings are engaging, but if you're someone who doesn't like to participate, earning an A will be challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Rivera wants you to participate in her class and I strongly believe if you attend her and the TF's OH you stand a better chance of getting a good grade. Constantly show interest and participate in what is being discussed.

My class had a lot of participation so discussions were always interesting. As a teacher, I think she is underappreciated. She is definitely a tough grader but so is every C&C teacher. Super sweet person and I recommend going to office hours, if you pay attention you can learn a lot about how she wants you to write. TA was great too
DONT TAKE YOUR GPA WILL TANK

Boring as can be. Learned about nothing other than how to yap about what she wants to hear. hard grader. You don't really learn any material just see how business affects culture. She is nice in person but not when grading. No one really talks in class. Go to office hours and get her to like you (helps with grading)

She is so specific about how she wants you to write the essay, and even if you do that, it's somehow still not up to her standards. Seminar type of class so be prepared to discuss the book/movie each day. PARTICIPATE. There's a discussion post and journal every week, but they're easy A's. Sweet lady, but hard grader.

Paper grades were on the brink of the next letter by some decimal amount, which seemed purposeful. She has  specific ideas about what students should write in each paper, but be warned she'll only read one paragraph of your draft, so choose wisely. Ask the TA for more help, or just follow the ideas on her slides.
P.S. She says "right" a lot.

The only reason I got an A- was because I kissed up at the very end and put my literal 100% into the last essay. She wants very specific things and will give you a B if it isn't what she wants. Her in-class discussions are confusing and sometimes she leads the class in a strange way that is received in silence because everyone is confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
"right"
once you realize she says this word, it is super distracting and you also can't improve on essays and also doesn't give good feedback at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is nice but has specific ideas that she wants students to bring up which limits students' abilities to come up with their own points. She talks over many students or will reword their points in order to get conversations going in a specific direction but it feels like she disregards the student. Grades very harshly and takes a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think she is under appreciated. She is not the most lenient grader, but if you show up, participate and discuss ways to improve, she is very accessible and open to helping everyone.

Rivera is a great person and if you put in the effort to participate in class discussions, show initiative, go to her office hours and in general build a relationship with her your semester will go really well. She is a tough grader, definitely not an easy A.

Tough grader. Feedback on essays don't really make sense. On the last essay, I showed her my outline during office hours and she gave some comments on it. She told me to change some parts and to add some parts. I implemented them for the final essay, but in the feedback she told me to write about something completely different. Weird...

She is nice but marks meh. In my 3 essays, there is little (0.1pt) or no improvement. Also didn't publish grade breakdown at the end of the semester. She does give good feedback if you ask, also pushes you to analyze. She is flexible on deadlines tho, if you're a bit late and email her she won't take marks off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is a decent choice for a writing professor. She really challenges you to analyze texts thoroughly by facilitating class discussions. Classes can become quite dry sometimes though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: definitely dont take her class. other professors are much easier and actually grade fairly. you barely improve on essays and if you do maybe by like .1 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I cant say much about her grading style, as she eased her grading system due to COVID, but overall, shes a fair grader. Shes really nice too. Her class can get a bit dry sometimes and the essays you do in the class is often just professional essays. In general, her class was about urban centers and I think that was very interesting indeed.

The class feels difficult to stay engaged with, as lectures tend to repeat similar points without adding much new depth. It would be helpful to incorporate more relevant material to make the content feel more useful. The classroom environment could benefit from a more open and supportive tone to encourage student participation and discussion.

Attendance is mandatory because the exams are solely based on the three hour lectures. The professor says to not review the slides because they are not helpful for the exam. Do not take this class if you can avoid it.

WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER SEEN AT THIS SCHOOL. PERIOD. thinks he's the smartest guy to ever walk on this Earth when honestly he has less skills than most of the kids in the class. No idea how the course is graded and I learned less than nothing during his class. if you can afford to wait, go ANYWHERE else or p/f

Absolutely terrible. Every student in his M&O and Org Comm reported him, and he was under investigation by NYU Madrid and Stern. Stern advisors and the Dean said he should not even be teaching and will be fired soon. Enough said, do it in NYU given all these allegations and reports and if not just report him again to get him fired.

Professor Alfonso is a very chill and happy guy, exams were easy and fair. Classes are long and can be a bit boring sometimes but most of the time he makes class more interesting with interactive activity, this is the easiest Stern elective Ive taken. Totally reccomend!!!

From day one, Muñoz-Acevedo flexed his résumé like that made up for not being able to teach. Bragged about his background, then delivered confusing, disorganized lectures. No clarity, no support, no learning. Arrogant, unqualified, totally disconnected from students. If this is your only option at NYU madrid, think again and take in New York!
Objectively a terrible professor. Had no lesson plan and used up the 3 hours of class time every week to go on random tangents. Avoid at all costs.

I genuinely do not understand how he was hired. He spends 90% of class talking about random things that he thinks is profound. This man is out of touch with reality. For org-comm, until the final project your classmates decide your grade. During every single presentation he was just on his phone (Likely on Grindr). Out of touch with reality.

Actually not a good professor. Seriously. This is my first RMP review, it was that bad. I took him for OrgComm and M&O at NYU Madrid, and he's not even a tough grader, but his lectures are the biggest waste of time. You learn nothing. Worst case of yap I have ever seen. Makes controversial and cancelable statements often. Cool guy syndrome.

not a good teacher. pulls things out of nowhere and tells us to believe him because he "has experience". a ridiculous teacher all around with horrible grading scheme and no feedback whatsoever. entire (super stern curved) grade is dependent on like 2 individual assignments and a semester-long group project. avoid at all costs

STERN CURVED. exams are all worded in a very unclear way that nobody in the class understands. The exams also has no partial credit or anything you can do after. Says a lot of things that are not on the slides that will be on exams. In OrgCom he makes students grade each other basically creating a toxic environment and grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude should not be a professor. Goes off on random tangents in class and overcomplicates subjects to sound smart. Almost half of the final grade was based on group presentations, and he goes on his phone during them and has students give grades to each other. He doesn't provide feedback and is also unreachable outside of class.

Alfonso was awful. Would spend each class talking about something completely random and would not do any work or give any meaningful feedback when asked. Would give us a class to work on a presentation and then spend half the class talking about the most random stuff.

One of my favorite classes from NYU. He changed my view on music composition a lot, and I just loved everything about this class. I feel like if you don't resonate, it won't be as fun, but if you get where he is coming from, an absolute goated class.

Arjomand is such an amazing professor. He is so caring, funny, and very engaging. This course has made me look at music theory and composition in a completely new light, and I am excited to use my knowledge from this course in my writing moving forward. If given the chance, I would absolutely take this class again.

He teaches music theory in a "self-actualization" way where you connect with yourself whilst connecting with the material. At times he gets kind of philosophical and complicates things through abstractions, generalizations, and theories that he has with the given subject, but it was a very engaging and thought provoking experience nonetheless.
he's just a chill guy who wants to discuss theory

Arjomand is very underrated. He might seem a little overwhelming at first since his lectures tend to be very philosophical, but it's just amazing how he always eventually gets to the essence of the topic. His classes are super engaging and thought-provoking. Definitely recommend taking him.

Cool professor, one of the best in the department at nyu. Have had him for theory multiple times and it honestly gets more interesting every time. Not the best student myself, but I didn't ever feel like I was ever being singled out or anything for not understanding. He won't exactly force you to participate but it def helps to do so.
Big time yapper but he's chill

Arjomand knows his stuffs. Very thought provoking and dense for a Theory 1 class, which is a good thing in my book. You learn so much more than your typical theory lectures. Keep an open mind about music, and please participate because that is pretty much all we do in class.

Arjomand is the best professor I have ever had. Every class has the most interesting discussion and after every class you wonder how is it going to get better and it just does. It is definetly helpful to know some theory before hand. The assignments are super easy but informative. I cannot reccomend his class enough. Beyond thought provoking.

Prof Arjomand's lecture is super inspirational. He helps students understand the essence of music theory in an easy way. His lecture sometimes seems abstract or philosophical but trust me it is super fruitful if you really pay attention and join the class discussion. Not many daily assignments but projects in midterm and final.

Arjomand is far and away the most brilliant instructor I've ever had. His discussion-based class format proved incredibly insightful and completely changed how I perceive Music Theory. From his unorthodox teaching style to his wit, I truly cannot say enough great things about him and his class. A real must-take!

I took him all the way from Theory 1-3. Unfortunately, he didn't teach Theory 4 otherwise I would've taken it with him. He is by far my favorite professor within MPAP. I remembered struggling with music theory but he made it so easy. His lectures are easy to understand and compound on the homework. All around great guy. Very highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Arjomand has a very unique way of approaching his classes and leaves you with a good impression of the days work. Through his lectures, I was able to gain a thorough understanding of the roots of music from the perspective of a musician rather than a textbook. I love him as a Professor and musician.

Arjomand is not only an incredible composer, but he also encourages a lot of discussion & diversity in approach. With Theory II, he encouraged compositional discussion, and often, you're allowed to break classical "rules" as long as you can justify why you did it. Definitely one of the smartest people I've ever met and one of my favorite professors

Had him for theory 2. Decent professor, but cares more about having you memorize specific part writing he does rather than learn the rules and how to do it on your own. If you don't memorize the specific way he part writes you wont do well at all.

I swear he just wants you to learn to the point where all the exams he made includes all the hard stuffs he explained in class. He can mark you wrong by the slightest error in your composition. Also if you skip class, you'll miss a lot of stuffs. Be ready to participate so hard and getting cold-called.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Ramin for Aural I and Music Theory II, and both were great choices. For theory, he really emphasized ways we can incorporate music theory into our own musical pursuits rather than just read from the book. He will like you even more when you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have any doubt in your theory skills I wouldnt recommend this class. Especially online, the only kids who are doing well are the kids whove had lots of theory experience before. Hes a tough grader and Lecture heavy so take at your own discretion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Arjomand was a fantastic choice for Aural I. Occasionally cold-called to sight-sing or dictate in class, but it helped to keep me engaged with the material. He definitely doesn't teach straight from the (required) textbook but does use it sometimes for in-class practice. Occasional short homework assignments, but grade is mostly exams.

As a student who got A's in all other theory classes, taking Arjomand's class was one of the biggest mistakes of my academic career. He is extremely knowledgable and a great composer but it seems like he wants to flex his theory knowledge more than actually teach it. He's a harsh grader and very full of himself. Way too much work for 2 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I LOVE HIM! He made ear training seem so easy. His teaching methods are so amazing, and it really is analytical in the way he approaches this class. He doesnt like doing things the textbook way and I really feel that makes a massive difference. He helped me genuinely understand this class and I want to have him every semester.
Best theory professor I have ever had.
