She is one of the smartest Econ profs at NYU, and it really shows in her lectures.  As long as you attend class, pay attention, and study your notes, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Intro to Macro. Capable professor but not particularly inspiring or interesting. Lectures can be dry. For exams, read the textbook + work on the recitation problems & practice midterms. Some Qs on the exam wil be very similar to those. You can skip lectures + recitations if you are willing to put in work for the exams

She's moderately clear in class although her slides make things a little confusing. If you read the textbook, you should be fine but attending lectures definitely helps as well. She is willing to help you and sometimes gives extra credit for scratch work on exams.

Intro to Macro. I took this class with her and she's not bad. If you stick to the book you will do good, if not, her lectures confuse you even more. she has her own slides which she doesn't post on the website, and they are pretty confusing. She is not a great lecturer and very unclear. But if you stick to the book you can get a good grade!!

Class is lecture based so dry at times, but Prof. B does a lot to make the material interesting. She often creates funny examples and expresses herself very well. She is willing to help and allows scratch work credit on the midterms. Study and come to class and doing well is very possible. Prof. doesn't try to hurt your grade.

Maharukh is very clear when it comes to teaching. She presents the information in a way that people will remember. Sometimes what's on the exams doesn't necessarily correlate to the examples you get during recitation. She goes pretty quick during lectures. She's also pretty funny, but can get kinda harsh when answering questions - she has no chill

Intro to micro. The class isn't tough, and she's always willing to help if you go to her. She goes through her powerpoints quickly, so its important to sit in the front so you don't miss anything. Read the textbook and go to class. You'll be fine.

I took her Public Econ course, an upper level Econ elective. Easily the toughest course of my undergraduate career, but thankfully the course material starts off super tough and gets increasingly easier. She's a very fair grader and is very willing to help students out when they need it, but is a confusing lecturer -- the textbook will save you.
She gave terrible lectures. She was rude. She yelled at students and mocked their questions. I learned nothing and had to read the textbook to get by.

She may not be the professor for everyone, but I personally really enjoyed her lectures. Super cute personality, and very straightforward. As long as you listen to class, you don't have to read the textbook and do much intense studying to get a good grade in this class
Intro to Microeconomics. Pretty straight forward class. Attendance not required for lecture or recitation. No quizzes. Grade fully dependent on online homework and 3 tests.

Her lectures are not clear at all and very difficult to follow. She does not encourage students to ask questions in lectures and is not willing to help you herself if you are struggling in the class. Would highly recommend you switch out of her class if she is your teacher.
She is a good professor, has everything published online, few homework, takes about 20mins to finish and exams are not hard

Professor Bhiladwalla is by far one of the best professors I have taken at NYU, so much so that I took her for three of my Econ classes. She is clear in what she expects and actually cares that you learn the material. I would definitely recommend taking her. And so what she has an accent? Most professors do, at least she's good at what she does.

She is great! her accent is annoying but if you really want to learn take her. tests are not easy but expected material (ignore the long review sheets she gives, useless). the day before the exam she hints about what will be asked in the test. She posts notes for each chapter (very helpful). HW is not hard. You can take points back in exams.

Prof. is very dedicated to her students and invites people with bad grades to her office to discuss methods of improvement. Crystal-clear info about the scope and types of questions on exams. Fair grading. Expect up to 10 (easy) homework assignments. You'll learn all the important basics in the field. If you do all the homework, you'll be fine!

It do take some time to get used to her accent, but everything'll be fine soon. She will be kinda intimidating at first. She's really clear about what she's teaching. Make sure you read the textbook, attend the class. The exams are not tricky but by no means easy. I know someone who got 4 in AP micro, but seldom attended her class ended up with F.

She's ok. There's homework every week, which is not hard, just a collection of exercises from the book. You do not need the book at all. I didn't really attend that many classes and usually didn't pay attention. All you have to do is read the notes that she posts. If it's not on there, it won't be on the test. One midterm and the final. Pretty easy

She is one of the few econ professors that actually cares. She might come off a bit intimidating but if you come to her with questions she is extremely helpful. She is not an easy grader, but she puts a lot of time and effort into her teaching so it makes you want to do well.

Tests are really hard but the professor is SUPER nice and extremely helpful. Very straightforward, make sure you attend all the lectures because she explains a lot. The tests took me by surprise because they were so different from what I learned in class and in textbook

Attendance is an important part of her teaching style; she goes over vital concepts in class. The textbook is a great resource. Even if you struggle with the material, she's willing to work with you as much as you need to boost your grade. I recommend her to everyone.

Would recommend her. Her voice is kind of annoying, but she gets the point across clearly. She uses good examples to further explain concepts. Mandatory attendance and online hw. Her first midterm was brutal though. Average was a 53 although they're curved based on class avg. Second midterm was better. No surprises though. You study, you do well.
Really good professor, teaches clearly like a high school teacher would. her strictness makes you want to strive harder.
Do not expect to learn anything from her notes; just read the textbook and you'll be fine. She tends to be surprisingly unfriendly as well.

She provides very detailed notes which make the text book almost useless. She tells you exactly what she wants and is not out to trick anyone. Her tests are straightforward, but not easy. She can be intimidating at first, but an A is attainable if you put a decent amount of effort in. She hates talking during class.

Those who took Intro Micro/Macro that rate her poorly are either intellectually handicapped or did not put in the effort. I dont know what they mean.. she gives you a ton of help if YOU go and get help from her (go to the office hours). She uses clear examples to teach, and as long as you studied you would've been fine for the finals / midterms.

She does a great job explaining things during lecture. She's very clear and wants you to understand what's going on. She hates it when you talk in class, so pass notes if you really need to talk to your friend. She doesn't mind that. She means well. I Definitely recommend her.

The professor seemed really strict at first, but once you get to know her she is funny. She's not out to trick anyone on the tests (mostly), but you really have to understand the concepts. I got an A in the class but I had to study hard. I didn't really need the textbook much. Her notes are great.

I had Prof. Bhiladwalla for Econ Principles I (Macro). I thought she was great. She's a little strict, but very nice and helpful. It's a lot of material so she moves fast, and you have to keep up with the reading. Overall, if you study hard for the tests, you'll do fine. The curve is exactly the econ department's curve. I'd recommend her.

She goes straight by the book. Attendance is definitely not mandatory. Her midterms weren't too difficult but her final was. She's passionate about what she teaches, but sometimes it's difficult to understand her because she has an accent.

It's a bit too early to tell, but she seems really strict - for instance, do not even think of asking your neighbor a question on the material for clarification, she will pick you out in front of the entire lecture (250 people) and yell at you. It's be-littling, she needs to calm down. Other than that, good professor

You have to do work for this class! Because the class is quite easy, she doesn't curve as much. I tried pretty hard but got an A-. I like it how she gives class notes for every chapter, I almost didn't have to use the textbook. No surprises on exams, everything from class notes.

REALLY GOOD PROFESSOR. PRESENTS A TON OF MATERIAL BUT IF YOU GO TO THE LECTURE YOU WILL HAVE NO PROBLEM WITH THE CLASS. NEVER GOT LESS THAN A 90 ON HER EXAMS. PLUS THE TA, RYAN, IS A GREAT TA WHO KNOWS THE MATERIAL. EASY 200 LEVEL CLASS FOR ECON MAJORS AND QUITE FRANKLY A VERY INTERESTING CLASS

Go to the lectures. I skipped most of the lectures before the first test and just read the book and got a B, then stopped reading and went to lectures for the second test and got an A-. Huge scale on the final too. Got a 60%, which must have been good, because I ended up with an A- overall.

Very enthusiastic about the class, but her lectures are very disorganized.  She goes at a very fast pace and expects you to understand everything easily.  Her tests are not straight forward but she thinks they are, average is a C-, and she curves it up 1 letter grade
No Comments

She's quirky and hilarious, makes the class fun. Crams a lot into lectures and is a little disorganized.. the chalkboard often looks like a bloodbath. But you'll definitely learn if you go to class - good prof overall

She has the randomest of jokes and she is awesome! Go to all the lectures and read the blackboard notes and you wont even need the textbook. Is willing to repeat herself in class if you dont get something, and is really helpful during office hours. Tests are long and challenging, but not too hard. It is a difficult course tho, but i recommend her!
Can not understand. Useless to go to class. Read textbook but tests too hard. The averages are Cs and Ds. And she will curve is up one letter grade. Big help.

Prof Bhiladwala is excellent. The material is challenging (at least it was for me, a non-economics major) but she does a great job explaining it and she is always available outside of class to help you out. Tests are fairly difficult but grades are curved. (Note: Yes, she does have an accent, but it's easy to understand.)

She tries hard, but her thick accent really hindered my studies. I had to rely on the textbook to really get through the class. To her credit she does curve up grades but I would recommend taking this class with someone else.

She has a kinda funny accent, an indian accent, but it isn't hard to understand what she says. The class is very straight forward, 2 midterms, and a final, and online homeworks every week or so. She gives practice exams before the test that for the most part have very similar questions to the actual test so that makes the tests easy and predictable
hilarious, crazy, awesome.

WREX and WCI were so much fun with professor Biagini! She has a wide variety of assignments in terms of both genre and prompt. Loved how much creative freedom we had in essays and the final portfolio. No final and the midterm is a fun in class essay. Field trips are beautiful and inspiring. Provides good feedback on each piece. Such a fun class!

This class was one you never really had to stress about, and the content was interesting and fun. Her writing prompts are more adventurous and fun than the other writing teachers and she really focuses on our perspectives. I will say, if you are really hoping to improve your writing, this class may not be it, but still a great class and teacher.
readings were horrible and she is impatient
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved my classes with her. She pushes for participation but it helped me come out of my shell! Would 100% take again. Her assignments and readings are super fun and interesting too!

I used to hate writing poetry, but now I can bust out a poem like it is nobody's business. Biagini is a very interesting and very passionate person. She makes you read your work out loud for the entire class, which is very helpful. Just participate, and submit your work and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Biagini is amazing! Truly one of the most caring and passionate profs I have had. If you take this class though be ready to participate, she will push everyone to talk even if you don't want to, but she creates such a warm and open environment to participate in. I have taken three of her classes because I enjoy them and her teaching so much!

She's simply fantastic! she's an easy A but is still interesting and has lots of personality. highly highly recommend. lots of interesting prompts and lots of readings that are required, but really aren't.

Professor Biagini is the best! She is very kind and helpful. Classes are discussion-based but she allows you to talk about all kinds of important topics through writing. Three essays (three pages single or double spaced), you can choose your own topic and a lot of short writing homework for each class, but it is interesting and doable. TAKE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Heavy emphasis on grammar, so if you can write grammatically correct sentences then you'll be good. other than that, super caring and supportive. You will have to put in the work to get an A. She has the CUTEST dog ever called Emma and sometimes would like to participate in class discussions. So her dog is worth going to class every time.

Prof allowed me to get back into enjoying creative writing, on many different topics. She does want constant participation, especially when talking on the readings. She is understanding and willing to accommodate to working with you outside of class time. Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Biagini is an excellent writing teacher. She has experience in all kinds of writing, is very funny, and takes the time to learn each student's style of writing to give the best possible feedback. I strongly recommend taking her class if you want to develop your creative writing skills or gain experience writing longer essays.
Absolutely amazing. She is a wonderful writer that truly inspires you to try harder.

She is the best writing professor at NYU Florence! I had her for 2 semesters and it was my favorite class. Her assignments are fun and creative, and you can usually pick any topic for your essays (other classes are confined to prompts). On field trips, she brings her puppy, and once she held a movie night at her parents' house. My fave professor!!!

Honestly, I've seen so many horrible reviews of Bishop, but she's really not that bad. If you're willing to show up, participate, and be respectful, you will be fine. She kind of gives high school teacher vibes, so I guess it depends on how you feel about that. Her assignments are interesting, and you can get by without doing most of the readings.

PARTICIPATE AND ATTEND CLASS AS MUCH AS YOU CAN!!! cannot be reached outside of class for anything, also not an understanding teacher. unclear feedback and guidelines. class material is not difficult at all, but she definitely is. take at your own risk and if you do, be on your best behavior.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She will give you comically ambiguous assignment prompts. After you write an essay that satisfies all of the requirements, she will insist that this isn't what she wanted. Submitting a first draft is like opening Pandora's box. I feel like a circus monkey trying to guess what the trainer wants.

The rubric kept on changing throughout her semester. Learned nothing all semester because she was so unclear with everything. But if you were even a minute late you would be a target. Also is very rude in general, cuts you off mid sentence, does not allow for discussion. Super hard to reach outside of class (has never replied to any of my emails.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AWFUL PROFESSOR DO NOT TAKE HER !!!!!! shes so insanely rude, you could give the class discussion your all and she'll make smart side comment, not even acknowledge anything you say. extremely pretentious. Classes r very attendance heavy: show up to class 1 minute late and she'll target you the entire semester. worst professor I've ever dealt with.

Just participate. Her questions are easy and basic, don't really need a comprehensive understanding of the readings she assigns. Every time you have to submit a paper, you will get a chance to get feedback from her and from your whole class. She doesn't have a clear rubric, but she tells you what to fix so you'll be fine

I do not recommend Jacqueline Bishop to anybody unless you really want to be degraded and feel awful about your writing. She will call you out about any flaw and your essays will be shared and criticized every class. She is a slow grader and can be extremely unorganized. Overall the class is easy with a few essays but she is just so rude.
good

PLZ NEVER TAKE HER. I had to withdraw this class bc I never knew this was conducted online and she never told me this. Also very unclear rubric and hard to communicate through emails. Guess what? This class was online. Participation really matters and I think if this class was in-person it could have been much better.

She is just so nice. Three graded papers for the whole semester. She will help you edit your paper first before you submit it, so just do what she wants and you will get an A. Participation is another big part. But NO WORRIES everyone. I am the kind of person who are not good at speaking but her questions are not hard at all. So everyone can do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Participation really matters, and you need to participate A LOT to get a good participation grade. Unclear rubric. But the papers aren't hard, and the peer edit & feedback from her are extremely helpful.

Bishop is a solid choice for writing. She will edit your paper before grading so if you do as she says then you are guaranteed an A. Just begin writing early and you are set. Classwork comes in waves, so plan ahead and ur fine. Be prepared and participate and she will automatically like you. She is super funny but you need to be able to take a joke
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor is interesting and has a lot of advanced thoughts on social focuses. The class project is also good, but you need to pay attention to your grammar details of your essays. Otherwise, you may lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. she has a tendency to go on fun tangents and make playful jokes of her students so she is not for the thin-skinned but will definitely improve your writing. The peer reviews of the papers before the papers are actually due or graded is by far the most helpful things that I wish every class had.

Know what? Although I got a B+, consider this: it is the lowest grade of my entire college life. Tell me how hard the grading could be. She is not a friendly person and often goes on tangents. VERY OFFENSIVE from time to time and didn't enjoy it at all. I really feel I was offended. She might not be your worst nightmare but there are better options
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is tough. She is sarcastic and most people will find her offensive. Take her class if you want to do something more than just writing essays and if you have thick skin.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jacqueline is the most amazing woman and I pray to GOD that I'll be able to take a class with her again. She hilarious and sweet and super caring and you will grow so much as a writer.

Professor Bishop gives a manageable amount of work and it's very easy to handle. There are only 3 graded essays and each has a fair word requirement. She values participation a lot! And she even said it herself that participation will affect your paper grade.

I loved her.  She was an amazing professor, most I have ever learned in a writing course.  I wish I could take the whole class over again.  She cares and gives great feedback.  I am now an expert at showing and not telling.

Great professor. She jokes, talks about her cat a lot, and likes to mention the awards she's gotten and interviews she's been in, but she has great anecdotes. Easy A, but be ready to share some personal stuff - fiction or nonfiction. Wish I had her next semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bishop was a great professor for this class specifically. She taught students how to close read paper and writings and show-not-tell in their own papers. She could be a bit neurotic... but you'll find it funny, albeit a little annoying. Go to class, participate, and offer genuine comments to get in her good graces for that A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You don't have to do the readings because you'll read them out loud in class. In-class workshops make it seem like you'll fail, but most people I know got A's. She pushed me to become a better writer. She's clearly intelligent and interesting to talk to. Class discussions about history and current events were my favorite part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Jacqueline is the best professor you could ever have. She's passionate about what she does, she has a great sense of humor, and she is very approachable. I unfortunately could not take her for Writing II, I will miss her greatly. There's no exams ever, just three papers and occasional essay readings. Very light work if you're a good writer.

An absolutely fabulous teacher! Her assignments aren't as traditional as other writing teachers but the projects that she assigned were very interesting and eye opening. If you participate and have enthusiasm, you will surely get an A!

The most fabulous, inspirational professor at NYU. I found myself talking about how much I loved her to my family and friends OFTEN. She's an inspiration, and the course structure (Writing II) is phenomenal. She does assign some reading, but doesn't actually check if you read. Read anyway! Her selections of novelsreadings are amazing. Best at NYU!

I honestly don't have enough space here to explain how FANTASTIC Professor Bishop is! She is so enthusiastic, funny and is willing to help her students. She wants everyone to do well in the class and I always looked forward to writing. I had her for Writing I and II and wish I could have her for more classes! Take her class, you won't regret it!

Absolutely fantastic --- Professor Bishop is zany, eccentric, and hilarious, but also helpful, kid, and unique. Her prompts are engaging, interesting, and thought provoking; you will WANT to write!!! So many students regard her as  the best writing teacher in LS. They are correct; she truly has it all. To sum it all up, her class is an experience!!

im so bummed by the fact that i didn't get to take her for writing II. She is hilarious, inspirational and so blunt. She is definitely my favorite professor in LS. Please just take her and see for yourself, she will immensely improve your writing and critical thinking....i signed up on rate my professor to tell yall how amazing sheis,thank me later

Rate My Professor says this is my chance to be more specific. I read this as "Who is the best writing professor at NYU, and why is it Jacqueline Bishop?" Seriously, take her course. Once you get used to the idea of "Showing and not telling" you will love coming to class, listening to her crazy stories, and evolving as a writer

Love her class! Makes me excited to go to writing! Would highly recommend her for writing I and II! You have to work for your grade but you will become a much better writer in the process. She has office hours available and if you work hard you will do fine. Take her if you can!!

Professor Bishop was the best part to my first semester in college! I'm so happy I got her for Writing II!!! My writing drastically improved! If you show that you care and go to her office hours it is very helpful! I went every week and each time was greeted with a smile :) She is funny, caring and very inspirational! Highly recommend. Take her!!
She has a really bad attitude & can be really rude at times. We focused on one project all semester which got repetitive and boring. Would not recommend her.

AMAZING writing teacher. Definitely recommend. Taking her again for Writing II; she is great! Class participation is important but she really wants you to get an A and does everything she can to help. Peer revisions in class are super helpful and she gives everyone feedback on their first draft in class.

I absolutely loved Professor Bishop!  She has funny stories that she shares with the class from time to time.  There is no midterm or final- just 3 major papers that make up your entire grade.  She heavily emphasizes class participation, but gives you a chance to get the best grade on your papers and is a fairly easy grader.  She's awesome!

Professor Bishop is AWESOME!! Take her if you can you won't regret it. She is hilarious and makes the class fun. Will inspire you to enjoy art and literature even if your previous interest is low. A fair and easy grader as long as you try. I am in love.

Professor Bishop has been one of my favorite teachers so far. I was always excited to go into her class to see what discussion we would have that day based on the writing style of what we had to read. To do well on her papers, go into her office hours!! She is knowledgeable, funny, and a great person. Extra credit opportunities too!

Professor Bishop is a great person.  She is always laughing and there's never a dull moment in class.  There are lots of opportunities for extra credit in Writing I.  She is great and you learn a lot.  Take her!!!

Professor Bishop is honestly amazing. I have learned SO much in her class, and I am truly thankful to have gotten her. She is funny, entertaining, fair, and a sweet person. If you have the chance to take her, DO IT!!!!!!!

Prof. Bishop is one of those people who can keep you interested in a subject, even if you didn't have an interest in it before. Keep up with the readings, and write more rather than less for the essays, and you should be okay. Also, she makes herself very available for help on any essay assigned, which is helpful if you get stuck.

She is honestly an awesome teacher. I've had her twice for Writing, and she has an amazing personality. She's hilarious when she goes on her tangents. The paper's are fairly easy, and there's reading everyday. Keep up with it because there's discussions. Recommend highly!

Bill Rayner is, by far, the BEST professor I have ever taken with. He is funny, kind, and very knowledgeable on the styles of music he discusses. Both his “Songwriting” and “Creating Music, Composing Worlds” classes focus on music, but you do NOT need to have pre-existing experience beforehand! If you ever get the chance to take with him, DO IT!

I love this man with all my heart. I am in his class as i write this. this is my second class with him and I'm so disappointed I don't have another semester to take another class with him!!! billy rock i will miss you

if u take this class PLEASE participate and chat with him! he's so nice :-)

class for all levels, if ur alr skilled he lets you just vibe on ur guitar
I dont know why I wouldnt take him again. I hope that says everything about him.
Dr. Rayner is really caring and kind, it's such a joy to practice guitar with him!
He is a great professor. Humorous and enthusiastic. Such a relaxing time playing guitar with him.

Only take his class if you are familiar with songwriting it's not intro. His class is not for me cause I prefer structure; there was none and we did not follow the syllabus. I know this works for some and he's a good guy , some people really liked him but it's not for Type A people. But, he's a nice guy and like collaboration and class discussion.

Bill is an amazing professor, not only because he so good at guitar, but also of his leniency and caring attitude towards students. when you meet him, you can already tell that all he wants is for his students to find a passion for guitar, and you will, with practice of course. take him, and you won't regret it.

He's really sweet and super chill. Just show up to his class and get an A! The purpose of the class is simply to introduce students to guitar and get them excited about playing. Although you won't learn as much from this as you would in an individual session, it's fun and he's just trying to develop student's interest in it so they keep playing.

Bill was my advisor. I could not have asked me a more caring, supportive, and passionate person to help me work through my concentration. I actually transferred advisors and when I found Bill I could not have been more thrilled. He is really interested in everything you talk to him about and really wants to know you as a person, not just a student
The sweetest most caring professor you'll ever have in your college career
Bill is the best. 'Nuff said.
Chillest guy ever! ADORE HIM! THE BEST
One of the greatest guys i've met. And yeah show up to class and get an A

Bill's a great guitar instructor. He personally cares about the success of each students and breaks down lessons at your pace. The class is structured depending on what you want to learn, and there is a wide variety of topics that Bill is knowledgeable about. Definitely a good instructor for beginners as well.
AMAZING. wonderful person and great teacher always willing to help his students learn & succeed!
Wonderful professor, wonderful class. What else is there to say?
No Comments

BillyRock is a great teacher. I highly recommend his songwriting class. The emphasis is on completing various types of songs & collaborating with other students in the class. The critiques are helpful, not hurtful. There are 2 live showcases each semester, which are really fun. If you have an interest in songs or writing them, this is a great class

Billy Rock is fantastic.  I came in knowing almost nothing about jazz.  Classes are informal and fun.  Rayner really knows his stuff too!  He's got a PhD in guitar performance.  He makes learning theory easy ad fun (though theory is not a stress of this class).  Take it!
He is the best professor in the world, I can't express how much I love him!!! He made my day whenever i had his lectures. BEST PROFESSOR EVERRRRRRRRRRRRR!!!!!!!!!

He is extremely clear about his expectations and grades very fairly. If you study for the quizzes and show up to them, you will do well in the class. It is extremely easy to get an A in this class if you just put in the work.
Self learnt everything. Don't take him.
Completely blindsided by my grade. Do not take him!
Lots of quizzes but easy if you just do a quizlet. Clear grading criteria. Great professor very old school. as long as you put in a little effort you'll be fine.

This class was great and easy to get an A if you just do what you're expected to - go to class, study for tests/exams, prepare thoroughly. For those of you getting Bs and below, you are just not trying hard enough. This class isn't hard.

Honestly, this class is hella easy. As long as you actually do the readings and study for the quizzes you'll get an A. Also his lectures are very insightful and fun, especially if you actually like hospitality. The only downside is the quizzes and the final are your entire grade. So if you don't do well on them, drop the class.

He doesn't give a damn f about your grade. No opportunities for improvement. Do not even try! Tests 35% of the grade and are every week, final exam 40%. If you are 2 minutes late you receive a 0. Impossible to change it! Prepare for final exam 2 weeks in advance or you will fail! Around 300 terms and questions to memorize, no multiple choice.
He's great and insightful. Catch is, he's strictly by the syllabus and quizzes every single week. If you pay attention, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory because there is a quiz in every single class. None of the course materials or homework are posted on Brightspace. He does not post any grades throughout the semester. The only grade you see is the final grade on Albert. He doesn't provide feedback on the final exam or explain the components that make up your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be ready to have only quizzes every week and then the final. No other methods to earn points for ur final grade. He never explained why you get the grade you get for the final or ur final grade. The class lectures are very boring as well.

This professor is extremely challenging. He doesn't post materials online, has zero tolerance for late work, and contradicts the textbook. If you're even slightly late, you can't take the quiz. Review sheets barely align with quizzes, making it hard to study. In all my years, I've never struggled with a professor like this.
He always forgets who have done or haven't done the homework and randomly gives you a zero. It's impossible to argue for your grades even though it's his problem.
SB
His lecture is totally different from final exams. Don't expect to get a normal grade in this course.

I loved Dr. Bjorn Hanson's class so much! 100% recommended. So people commented that they couldn't hear his voice, but I would say what about sitting in the front? lol. But seriously, he is a respected industry professional, a lot of good guest speakers and industry comments in the classroom.

One of my favorite professors of all time. Super caring, passionate, and informative. Definitely take his class if you get the chance to. Make sure to show up each week because there are weekly vocabulary quizzes. Exam was straightforward and not too hard, only took me about 20 minutes to finish.

Knowledgeable about the industry, but oftentimes contradicts textbook information. Weekly quizzes are somewhat annoying, but helps you retain content better. Sometimes gives vague instructions and is definitely more of an 'industry professional' than a university professor. Forget everything, Dr. Hanson is always right.

Lectures were super long and sometimes uninteresting. We didn't have much homework but expect weekly quizzes. Professor Hanson is very well respected in the industry and it was cool to hear about this experience in the industry.

The professor usually made self-mistakes. If you want to take his class, please keep every record of your homework if you have done.
Or he will forgets you have done this homework and gives you a zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gave us quizzes for every class covering vocabs and the content from previous classes. Even though he incorporated group discussions and presentations, most of his lectures were on his experiences in the hospitality industry. The expectations on both midterm and final exams were difficult, and most of the questions were short-answer/long-answer.

Professor Hanson was so clear and passionate about what he was teaching 100% of the time. There are weekly quizzes on chapters from the textbook but Professor Hanson always goes over the chapters in depth and as long as you read the chapter and studied for a little bit, you'll do great. The lectures can be long but very interesting.

Professor Hanson is an overall great and easy teacher. His expectations are clear and he can be lenient (just talk to him!) I am so thankful he was teaching this course. Very well respected and known by SPS and in the hospitality community. Lectures can be quite long and a bit boring, but he has his own fun stories to add. Loved it!
A really great professor with awesome stories. There are quizzes every week but as long as you study you'll be fine. Seriously such a nice guy. 10/10 reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Hanson is awesome. He knows very well about the concept and he really wants to see everyone's progress. A lot of participation chances, and he respects everyone's ideas. Take his class if you have the chance.

Professor Hanson is extremely well known within the Hospitality industry. If you have the privilege of being taught by him definitely take advantage of it. He's so sweet and always dresses nice for class. He is also very funny and tells tons of stories about his past experiences in the industry. Absolutely loved his class!
The professor is super chill and nice. Not there to fail anyone. Has really good experience in the industry to make connections with. Take his class
Awful. Quizzes and final exams were extremely difficult. Spent the majority of class time telling stories of his glory days at PwC than actual teaching. Glad he finally left NYU.
Bjorn is just a cool guy and he honestly isn't here to fail anyone. I've had him twice and I have liked his classes both times.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hanson is one of the best professors of the department. He is very experienced and always includes insightful anecdotes/stories at his lectures. You will have short quizzes almost every week but it will help you prepare for the final and you will learn a lot about hospitality.  His grading is very straightforward.

His lectures and stories were engaging. NYU is so lucky to have such a remarkable person. Quizzes and final were fair - straight from the textbook and lectures. Hanson even provides a handy review guide for quizzes to guide our studying in the right path. If you pay attention to the lectures and read the book, you will do very well in this course.

Dr. Hanson is an amazing professor, has great lectures, but is a very, very tough grader. Though he is a respected industry professional, he seems to be a bit arrogant about it at times. Would not recommend taking his class simply because he is an extremely strict grader. Quizzes are very short and VERY specific. (As is the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He words everything completely different than the textbooks or lectures on quizzes. so confusing.
Professor Hanson is a respected industry figure. His lectures are helpful with many of his industry stories.

His lectures have fun stories of his experience in the hospitality industry. Not much homework, but a quiz almost every week. Quizzes aren't hard as long as you read the textbook. His study guides are VERY helpful. Overall, a really great professor. He's very friendly, approachable, and understanding.

Quiz almost every single week. (about 8-10). Expect to learn 30-80 vocab words a chapter, with about 8-15 question quiz. No MC, only fill ins! READ TEXTBOOK FOR QUIZZES. He's so nice, just extremely strict on time. If you are a commuter student, it wont matter if your train derails into the ocean, you're still expected to show up on time.

Very knowledgeable about the industry and explains the material clearly. He used to be the dean and he cares about the student a lot. Very professional and kinda have a plainmonotone personality, but he will be there to help you.
Great teacher! Always willing to help.  Prepares you for the real world through placing you in industry mind-sets.  Great man!
Nice guy, strict but only to prepare you for the real world. He's very nice and helpful if you are respectful and eager to learn

I've attended a few schools during my undergraduate career, and Professor Bjorke truly stands out as one of my favorite teachers. What sets him apart is his genuine kindness. His passion for Economics shines through in his lectures, which have opened my eyes to what the discipline is really about. He genuinely cares for his students.

Isaac is a fantastic professor, who teaches very well and with clarity. Yes, his class was very difficult, but that is due to having hard material. He does the best with what he is given, and is clearly a brilliant person, who cares about his students. Highly recommended, and would take again in a heartbeat.

Well, he is nice for reaching out outside of class. BUT the main thing is that HE GAVE THE MIDDLE AND FINAL ON A SUPER HARD LEVEL. His homework and sample exam are fine, at least for the one who just finish listing to his lecture, but his EXAM IS SUPER HARD. He really enjoy the feeling of making his students BREAKING UP DURING MIDTERM AND FINALS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly the best TA ive ever had. Super helpful and clear in his explanations and always available to help out. A lot of people think recitations are useless but for me this class with Isaac was 10x more helpful than any of the lectures. Grades the homework pretty leniently but gives good feedback. 10/10, definitely take him if u can

Had him for IO over the summer and he was not only amazing at reiterating information taught at class/helping with the problem sets but he also was always available on email and for office hours! Pretty generous grading if he sees you put in effort and values questions!

Professor Bjorke was pretty fast in lecture, but I honestly really learned in this class. Tests were hard but just like practice problems, so if you really studied you should have done well. I didn't know anything about probability before this class and now I feel pretty comfortable with a lot of probability problems. His notes were a bit messy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Summer 2021. He sometimes goes way too fast during lecture, maybe assuming that most of the class had at least taken high school stats before. Handwritten notes in most cases are not helpful and you have to re-watch lecture recordings to refresh. Exams are okay, which is similar to HW. HW is lenient, as long as you do it, it's full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Everything about this class and professor is pretty standard. He didn't make things extra hard, nor did he make them any easier. His teaching was disorganized at times, but only slightly. If math isn't your thing, it could be harder, but overall, Isaac is a decent choice.

I tried very hard in this class and still struggled on the exams, which he told me not to fret. By the end of the course I felt that I did in fact understand the material really well, and it turned out that the curve helped me out alot. Great teacher.
very knowledgeable but lectures are hard to follow, no practice that is applicable to tests and no textbook is used, but teaches you to think differently about statistics and calculus

he is a good lecturer, and is very helpful during office hours, but lectures are disorganized, the textbook used is not actually consulted, only used for problem sets that aren't really relevant to class. no calculators on exams, but also doesn't care about math.

AWFUL! don't take him. he doesnt teach anything that's relevant; he doesn't put notes; his handwriting is terrible; he doesn't know what's going on the TA doesnt know whats going on no one has any answers. there's no way to even predict a grade. the textbook is useless. class is not structured at all. content is difficult. terrible experience
Overall ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hard lecture, but easy hw. Exams are somewhat confusing but he curves a lot, which makes letter grade better than expected
never take, nothing is organized, nothing is clear, harsh grader and the TA don't even know whats going on.

He seems like a nice guy, but he is a horrible professor. I just thought I was bad at stats, but for my other stats class I got an A. He makes this class unnecessarily hard. No clear grading criteria, no clear syllabus, lectures are confusing. Exams are even more confusing. For your own sanity, just avoid his class.

Nothing about this class makes sense, no sense of transparency or organization. Nothing he teaches is relevant to the class, and nothing we learned or any of the homework pertained to the exams besides the first midterm. Isn't clear about topics, what to know, and we know nothing about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tried to make the class interesting but ended up teaching a lot of hard theories that are outside of range. Not a lot of workload, but the homework was not even related to questions on the exam. Pay attention in class, most questions will relate to things taught in class

would not recommend taking. lectures are extremely confusing and theory based. his handwriting is illegible. midterms were extremely hard and averages were very low. the only way i learned was by attending the recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JUST DON'T. Textbook was used, but none of the questions on the textbook was related to exam questions. Theory heavy lectures with messy notes that couldn't be understood.

Avoid! Honestly ruined my stats experience. His lectures were unreasonably hard and covers a lot of theoretical concepts that couldn't be understood. Exams were hard too and graded harshly. It was not possible to succeed in this class with his unreadable notes and difficult exams, and you will learn almost nothing about stats.

Highly recommend for those whos serious about econ. He teaches the formula and focuses on intuition, which can be conceptual, theoretical, but AMAZING. He doesnt care about math. As long as you UNDERSTAND it, math doesnt matter (quoted). Exam is graded on procedures, and lose grading. One of my best decisions at NYU, very thankful.
Hes the most terrible one you can have for university. Guys, just dont ��

Tbh the worst prof I have had here. He seems fun and an interesting person, but he's ridiculously bad at teaching. His lectures are SUPER difficult, he uses advanced topics to explain introductory material, no examples. Everything is dry theory but at the exam he asks things he never told us. No one I asked understands him. Ruined my term really
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures may feel a little confusing, but they're actually very interesting. The exams are honestly easier than lecture. Do the weekly homework and the exams will be fine. Listen to your TA's grading criteria and attend recitation. He was fairly understanding of the corona situation too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice guy. But, he doesn't really know how to teach statistics outside of the abstract. Expect theory heavy classes that don't deal with numbers whatsoever. His lectures are confusing and not structured at all; there is no textbook so your only solace is to attend recitations. If you don't attend recitations, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly not an easy A class, but amazing lectures. His class is helpful in a way that he really requires us to understand the material instead of merely how to solve the problem. The class may seem confusing at first, but you will likely find the class interesting when you get to know his style and understand his words.

Bisin is probably a good researcher but he really doesn't know how to teach undergraduate students who are new to statistics. He is terrible at math so he leaves everything to the conceptual level. His lectures are very confusing, sometimes he gets himself lost. It is possible to ace the exams but you need to self study a lot of materials!

Bisin overall is OKAY I would say. Very nice guy, funny and cares about students learning. Make sure you go to class and write down every word because he doesn't go by the book and will test you on what you did in class. If you have Seher Gupta for recitation, you're lucky and make sure you GO FOR ALL OF THEM. She is amazing and taught me everythin

Do not take his class. He is a very nice person and genuinely cares about your LEARNING. But that results in him not caring about your grade. He is extremely vague about his exams and tests and won't tell you ANYTHING. You'll have maybe 2-3 questions for the entire midtermfinal and they'll be mad hard. Just do yourself favor and avoid him.

I'm still not entirely sure why NYU has such great Intro teachers but not one decent Intermediate one. Bisin is a good guy, but he WILL challenge you and make you work hard. He thinks spending 5-6 hours on a problem set (which you'll get every week) is the norm and you SHOULD be stuck and have to think it over. The structure of the class is weird

Curriculum is poorly constructed, involving jumping from topic to topic without much depth or explanation. Lectures are unclear. Bisin frequently goes entire lectures without explaining even the basic concepts behind each problem, leaving even the most interested students lost. However, he is a funny and interesting guy.

He has no book for the class. This is not an Introductory class, but instead, an advanced and quickly moving survey of microeconomic principles and topics.  I don't understand how he is still teaching aside from tenure and research contributions. Arrogant and comes off as unhelpful.

I pay attention in class yet learn little. He skips multiple steps and often tells you more about what you will learn rather than actually teach it. You don't know what is important and things are taught in random order. When I look at homework sets, I don't know what I'm even supposed to do. He's a cool/smart guy, but not a great teacher.

Bisin gives off the charts interesting lectures, they are not always directly related to the material but they are very engaging and entertaining. He is very kind and helpful to students who approach him. He can come off as a bit intimidating at first but he is a great guy. Incredibly helpful to students who make an effort in the class and with him

Bisin is not a great communicator or teacher, making the material difficult to understand. There seemed to be no structure to the class, and many people seemed lost. He asks little of his students, though, making it easy enough to get a good grade without truly comprehending the material.
Bisin moves fast, very fast. Classes seem scattered and material can seem difficult at times, but it makes sense if you can keep up with it. Make sure you're interested in the subject beforehand
Class is in dire need of a real textbook.  Prof's notes are whimsical, unpolished, and not nearly comprehensive enough.  Basically, if you ever don't get something, you're screwed.

Bisin is a brilliant economist, but not that great of a teacher.  He knows and understands the material in his own mind and in his own language (Italian) but struggles to convey the principles simply to his students.  However, he would be a much better teacher if he asked more of his students (i.e. its possible to get by without doing any work).

The class is a difficult one - don't take it if you're not sure about whether you can deal with the amount of mathematics in it. I changed to the Policy track after it. He's a really knowledgeable guy, and he loves what he's doing - but he's not particularly into an easy approach, dives right into it assuming everybody's going to be following him.

Okay everyone who keeps complaining that microeconomics should be a prerequisite obviously never took microecon, therefore has no grounds to say it should be a prereq. Its not for a reason, if your good at math you will do well in this class regardless of prior econ knowledge.
Very intense, not much help if you don't have a background of the course.

You should know principles well and you should be familiar with basic calc. The economic intuition is explained in class, but it might go over your head if you have no econ background and don't spend time reading outside materials (try varian, he puts suggested books on the syllabus for a reason)...he's not the greatest teacher, but you don't really have a choice!

very unorganized but interesting class. very little homework (3 problem sets) doesnt really matter how you do on the tests and problem sets because he gives everyone a B+ unless he knows who you are and he likes you

Extremely interesting class... material is well presented and challenging. He uses good examples and always explains the intuition behind the math. Most of the other people commenting are, uh, lets say "sissies", and should take a econ principles class, or just go back to high school.
He can not teach, he can not even speak, does not even reply the e-mails. You can not learn anything from the lectures, he is not prepared at all!
requires calc 3 and micro. not an intor. with otu a good TA dont even bother taking this class. You might get an A, but you will learn little int he lectures.
No Comments

Nice guy with a good sense of humor, but this class is impossible. It is NOT an introductory class and should not be listed as one--it definitely requires prior knowledge of microeconomics and that should be a prerequisite.
Can barely speak english

Bisin is a cool guy.  He obviously cares about what he's teaching.  The class is indeed hard as ****, but there is a big curve and he does a lot to help grades.  The subject material is a little abstract...  but if you stay with it its fine
Bisin's a good enough teacher. The class and material is just hard as****, half the class dropped after the 1st midterm. Noticeable Italian accent, but actually pretty funny.

Production Safety is a pretty boring mandatory class but Ray made it really fun and also informative, he's a great lecturer who has a lot of experience in the industry and he's very helpful and to the point when it comes to important things regarding safety. He's also really funny which helps.
Talks A LOT but doesn't really matter considering it's a P/F 1 credit course. Just go and you'll be fine.
Kinda boring but overall good and a very experienced guy. Good enough for a 5 session class.
Cares for his students safety. Clear instructions. On time. Keeps the environment fun even when learning about not so fun topics. Only had one class with him about safety, but enjoyed his class alot.
He's mid. Not the greatest, but pretty chill and funny, laid back guy. I didn't like him at first, but I came to appreciate him after taking a class with Moore.
Nice guy. Easy to look at. Reads directly from a sheet of paper so lectures can be kinda slow... but that is the nature of a class like this I think.

He's a nice person but not a great professor. He would bring some papers and read production safety instructions to you half of the time. He did do a nice job teaching when things got hands-on. Easy A.
His class includes one lite group presentation and an easy test. Take it over J-term. Turtlenecks.
Maybe boring, but very useful class. Ray is very caring and even a funny guy. Teaches the safety of the film industry, and makes sure everyone understands what he's talking about.
Ray is a great professor. He teaches the basics of safety on a set, and makes sure you remember everything too. Low stress class, but absolutely necessary for all filmmakers who want to be on set.

I had Ray for Set & Safety Protocol. If you miss a class, you fail (it's only 7 weeks). Ray was a funny, charming professor, and I enjoyed how he tried to make the lecture heavy class more hands-on. I feel like he looks out for his students. If you take the time to talk to him and get him to know you, you're set. He gives a take home final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's really unorganized, late to classes several times, and I know it was specific to our class, but she also cancelled 3ish classes due to her own schedule. Considering how much we pay for each class, it was very disappointing.

Professor Blakeman is the best! She is full of stories from working in the music industry in multiple different areas, and is always down to give advice. You end up working in groups a lot for quizzes/the final project, and it was really fun. Her lectures go by quickly and are fascinating. Highly highly recommend taking her for Music Publishing.

Prof. Blakeman is one of the best at NYU. She is super insightful about the industry and helps her students get involved with industry professionals. I enjoyed her classes. The lectures were super data-heavy, though workable. All the quizzes are teamwork-based, so they will be easy. The final was super easy, too. You must take her class!

One of the best professors at NYU and the reason why I stayed in my major. She is so sweet, humble, yet has so much experience in the industry, both as an artist and executive. Definitely take her class! She will make you love Music Publishing!

Blakeman's class has been the most enjoyable Music Business class I've had. She's very knowledgeable about the industry and encourages students to discuss their opinions. She's very open-minded and actually listens to suggestions. The class itself is pretty easy; there's a lot of group projects though.

HWs are nothing like the exams (I wish they were more similar). Be sure to focus on edge cases when studying. Practice exams are outdated and nothing like the current exams. The big file of examples is a good representation of what will be on the quizzes/exams, but the actual questions that will show up can throw you off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont take this professor unless you want to rethink your whole life and major decisions. I would not wish this class upon my worst enemy. Messed up my first semester at uni and my mental health.

Hws are not at all similar to exams, but they weren't bad; autograded and free resubmits. Goes quickly in class, talking abt stuff not on slides, and doesn't have recordings, so you def miss stuff. Exams are tricky even w/ cheatsheets, but he (slightly) adjusts grades to make up for it. Said he had harder exams last sem, hence some earlier reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaches concepts well, makes time for you outside of class, and is passionate about what he teaches. However, the homework doesn't sequentially reflect the midterm/quiz content. Exams are reasonable for what he has taught, but they are a time crunch and reflect the more difficult end of problems. If you put in a lot of effort, you will learn a lot.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He is accessible outside of class and gives good feedback, but if you haven't taken java in high school, I WOULD STAY FAR FAR AWAY FROM HIS CLASS!!! His homework assignments are so far off from the exams its not even funny and he does not curve them no matter what. More than half the class ends up dropping. RUN PLEASE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: run run run run

He is a nice professor, good teacher for concepts, and is very willing to provide extra help with outside sessions. But for an intro class he is very very tough, homework does not help too much with very hard exams.

Teacher is hard, straightforward but nice, class is extensive and hard but it prepares you for the real world struggle. He expects you to know things and no one asks questions. But he is really willing to help and will make 1-1 time for you if you ask. The class has a lot of math references, and is based on coding syntax not mcq.

While the lectures are very in depth and he does a good job of teaching CS concepts. His tests are extremely difficult and grading system unfair. On Midterm 2 the class average was a 41% and no curve was provided. It almost seems as though he is trying to fail as many students as possible. Definitely much more difficult than other CS101 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework has nothing to do with exams
Great professor but really hard and tricky tests.

blau is super chill, very accessible outside of class (MCBGroup). everything for MCB1 is clearly laid out, and as long as you watch the pre-class videos (normally 5-30min), do the quizzes, do your homework, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. there's a growth bonus if you improve over the course of the class, and extra credit.
Overall a great lecturer and interesting classes! The exams are very long and a bit challenging, but a good reflection of the lecture content. The British accent also makes it more interesting
I could listen to him talk for days on end. What a great guy!!!!!!

i absolutely loved blau. i'm so glad i took mcb1 (not required for me) bc of him. his lectures are so helpful and i learned so much from him. mcb1 was also one of the most helpful class for me (with biochem 1). he makes it very possible to get an A with practice exams and homework. nothing but praise for this british man.

blau is a great professor, he's clearly there to help you and will make it so you can improve. even if you do poorly on exams, there are ways to help save your grade. this class is difficult and his tests are hard but if you put in the work you can do well. you will need to put in a lot of work though.
really good at encouraging discussion using poll everywhere. slides are relatively good. show up to class.

Never showed up to a lecture and this guy is still my favorite professor lol. Every lecture is recorded and he clearly states everything you need to do in order to succeed in the class. As long as you take the time to watch his recordings and do the practice problems he gives you will do fine. Overall, a great guy who wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: loved loved loved his class. expectations and assignments are very straightforward. if you understand the main concepts taught in class, you should have no problem doing well. exams are very similar to practice exams and homework problems. growth bonus can help your grade if you are stuggling. basically, just take him !
As a person who got an B- on POB1 and still managed to get an A on MCB1, he is one of the best professors you can find at NYU.

Really cares about students doing well in the class, has lots of resources available outside of lecture and super easy to approach. Made learning mcb very enjoyable, exams are pretty fair and the growth bonus also gives the opportunity to raise your grade even if you start out poorly. Definitely take him if you can!

LOVED Prof. Blau. Such a nice person, good lecturer, and very willing to help students succeed. His dedication to teaching is so evident and the amount of work he puts into helping students outside of class is inspiring. Super approachable and will explain anything without making you feel stupid. Highly recommend this class I've learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Adorable intelligent British man with humor. Blau takes advantage of active learning over passive learning. He's truly fantastic. If you want an A, my biggest tip is to prime yourself before each lecture by going through slides and understanding them just enough so you are never in the dark during lecture, and you can feel apart of the story.

Decent lecturer, lenient grading, HWs and practice exams are very good prep for the exams. I just wish he would type out concepts & explanations on the slides instead of just having diagrams and a slide title. When you're sitting in a giant lecture hall early in the morning, it's pretty easy to zone out and lose track of what he's talking about.
he's my glorious king.

This man is the goat. Whoever is complaining is wrong. Tests are reflective of homework and lectures. It is exactly what you did for homework. Grading is very fair. Do well on the homeworks and it boosts your grade by a lot.

Definitely not a tough grader, so much partial points given, even to the point where just plain getting the answer wrong could be 50% points given. Very caring and respectful, just put in the time and effort to understand and it will show

Great professor, entertaining, makes you feel like you want to learn, has good attitude which is important. Course isn't easiest but isn't hardest, if you're in research since freshman year you'll have a very easy time. Easier than orgo IMO, great professor, lecture heavy but what isn't, definitely doable and very possible to get A

Overall really great guy. MCB1 concepts can be difficult but he's super dedicated to helping his students understand. Would recommend taking advantage of all the different resources like OH and MCB group. You're graded on many different things so it's possible to end with an A even if you mess up on an exam

Prof Blau is such an amazing and caring professor. If you're struggling I highly recommend going to OH, MCB group or even talking to him after class. He's really patient and will explain everything until you understand it. I noticed my understanding of MCB improved so much after making use of office hours and MCB group, would def recommend going.

For Blau's part of MCB, be sure to pay close attention to his lectures. The pre-recorded videos go over techniques of molecular biology, and the lecture is about a topic in which that technique is applied and proves how/why that topic was discovered using the technique. Application and conceptualization heavy for exams. Good professor though.

the content is hard, but he tries his best to explain it. review and consistent studying is necessary to pass. He truly want his student to be successful. his style of teaching is experiment heavy and there really isn't content, just a bunch of tests to prove something. Would recommend taking him if you are interested in doing bio research

The material wasn't hard, but Blau doesn't know what a flipped classroom means. At least half of the information being tested on the exam was taught in class instead of in videos, which was annoying because I almost always had to rewatch the lectures to take better notes even if I went in person.

Even after going to class, was heavily confused about content. Prepare to take notes and toggle between post and pre slides. Study practice problems, he will repeat similar question on exams and test you on understanding of lecture content. Go to your TA's office hours and ask question in MCB group.

Hes a really good professor and I highly recommend his behavior class. Hes very good at explaining things and makes sure his students understand the material. There is a decent amount of work but it is not too difficult and it is a reasonable amount. Highly recommend.
Dr. Blau is all about being a chairman and forgets what is the purpose of a student pursuing a degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Blau was definitely my favorite of the MCB 1 lecturers. His slides were clearer and he generally helped me to understand better. Make sure you don't skip lecture and study often. There was a generous curve but that doesn't fix everything. Go to review and make sure you do well in rect. (completely separate from lecture but helps your grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Excellent prof!  Prof Blau really tries to get people involved in thinking, so he asks a lot of questions.  Tests aren't too difficult if you study his lectures.  He's very helpful during office hours.  Overall it's a really interesting, fun class taught by an equally interesting professor.  I highly recommend him and Nat Sci Human Genetics!
justin was a great prof, very clear and organized. interesting class and helpful labs. definitely recommend!

Fascinating class. Very clear that Professor Block is an EXPERT in his field. Brings in concepts from cs, cog sci, neuroscience, etc which makes the class more interesting but also difficult. LOTS of reading so don't try to cram. Wish slides were more informative with less pictures and more text. Essays are hard so be specific and start early!
If you are interested in philmind, just take his class. It's not easy to get a A but u will definitely learned a lot.

He's very experienced, knowledgeable, and incredibly well-read on contemporary developments in psychology, neuroscience, and even deep learning. He's passionate and engaged in office hours, and he shows genuine interest in interacting with students in and outside of class. There's lots of concepts, and you do have to understand some deeply.
You have to take one classes from professor Block if you are a phil major! Lecture is super fun learned a lot about mind.

Philosophy of Mind: Philosophy part is not difficult. However, Biology and Psychology are unexpectedly difficult. Recommend not to take his class unless you are highly interested in Biology and Neuroscience.

Ned Block is a respected professor, and he is top in his field. Nonetheless, it doesn't deter him from teaching a boring class. Avoid his class if you actually want to learn something because everything is explained better in the reading material.

Consciousness is NOT for you if you do not have any psychology or neuroscience background. The philosophical aspect of this class is not hard, but the scientific terms and experiments are very complicated. Yet you have to get them straight to completely understand this course. If you are humanity-orientated, this course is gonna be a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible professor! Incredible class! Loved having the opportunity to take a class with Block. It is incredibly an incredibly dense class and at times, lectures and readings are hard to get through. However, if you stay on top of the subjects and pay attention you'll learn a lot.

I agree with the other comments here. Essays are definitely pretty hard to get a solid A on, but as long as you're thorough with your answers you should do fine. A big part of your grade also comes from attendance and the final, so as long as you put in reasonable effort you'll do fine.

Block's lectures are non-mandatory but you DEFINITELY want to turn up, because this man is not only a snappy dresser but he genuinely does his best to make the already engaging course material interesting. This class really is graded by a few things, since 60% of your grade is distributed evenly across 3 essays. Essays are tough but graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures alternate between fascinating, mind-numbingly dense, and both at the same time.  He knows a breathtaking amount about his field, and has written a lot of influential papers  in it.  That being said, his explanations and assigned readings are not always very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Block is the type of professor who makes being on a college campus so invigorating. Although some of the material is complex (esp. for an intro class), Block does his best to allow for questions/discussion during lectures. He is easily at the top of his field and absolutely worth taking. Also... as other noted he has an amazing sense of style.
good professor, interesting ideas
The only assignments for class were the weekly readings (which admittedly sucked), and three 3-5 page papers. Plus a final. Such an easy class and it was extremely interesting.

Professor Block is the nicest guy. He's incredibly passionate about consciousness and is always asking students what they are not understanding, so he can work with them until they get it. Gives you all sides of the debate (though not shy of course about where he stands). Lots of reading, but assignments are just reading comprehension questions.
brilliant teacher at the top of the consciousness field. has no qualms about arguing his own ideas against the material he teaches, specifically his nemesis dennett. also a snazzy dresser woo hoo!

took his class "minds and machines" when he visited harvard.  fantastic. led me not only to study philosophy but to try to pursue it professionally.  only gripe is that he didn't accept harvard's offer...
No Comments
Brilliant man.

Dr. Blaney was a phenomenal professor this semester! Her lectures are clear and easy to follow, with detailed slides and many opportunities for questions or clarification. The homework assignments and tests were all straightforward with review sessions in class. Her office hours were also very helpful, so do go if you take her class!

Dr. Blaney is INCREDIBLE. I loved every lecture & left with lots of knowledge & interest in epidemiology. Her slides and lecturing are straightforward & she always stopped for questions. She dedicated class time for test review. Manageable workload (some homework assignments, a group project, online textbook.) I wish I could take this class again!

Her lectures and slides are detailed - don't need to read the materials assigned. She is caring and you can go to her to talk about anything. She has study slides for 2 exams and 1 midterm. There was like 3 hw assignments and one easy final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Blaney was the sweetest and kindest Professor I met at NYU. She listens when we express that the TAs might have graded something too harshly. I didn't do any readings because her lectures covered all the materials anyways. She has study slides for all exams and there's was't much hw (maybe 4 max). Very accessible and ready to help you.

reviews.comment: great professor, her class is good
