reviews.comment: Participation matters. Also read the books!!
A great professor!!! Classes were always fun and challenging. She rocks!!!!

this is a great class. dopico black is excellent and knows a ton about the subject. sometimes we went off topic a little but it was always related and interesting. the grading is very fair. good to speak up in class.
This is one of the best classes I've ever taken and one of the best books I've ever read. GDB is amazing.
Awesome prof. Awesome class. Take it!
No Comments
No Comments

Never hated writing more, and I came to school for it. Unclear feedback and convoluted instructions. If you are a straight and to the point person communicating with her is difficult. Do not take if you value your creative liberties.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wished I liked this class better, but if you are a writer for film/narrative/non-fiction, especially if your major requires it, taking this her class will not help you. Lessons become tangential and she talks herself in circles. Feedback is redundant and your essays will be boring and by the book, but with no prior expectation set by her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Blag is kind. That comes to grading as well. If you put effort in and participate you'll be good. Zoom when you can, she likes the effort. She doesn't explain what she is looking for in the essays so she'll likely always have you completely change your essay. She gets off topic during class. Use the class to get other work done but pay attention.

Puts more restrictions on topics than pretty much all other teachers, but deeply invested in her students' success. Your papers will be fine as long as you do not go to her for feedback (she will twist your essay into something you don't recognize). Good excursions outside of class!!

You have to write what Blag wants you to write, which goes against the entire principle of Tisch WTE. I received A's on all 3 of my papers this semester because I took no liberties, and my papers were honestly worse for it. She's good if you're not a writer and want to be told exactly what to do in this class. If you're a writer, don't take her.

Absolutely loved her as a person. However, there was never a night without homework. Often long prompts and had extremely tough grading. She would give feedback but it was very obscure. There are fun outside-of-class activities that she offered extra credit for, in the form of excusing absences.

Blagovesta is a nice and sweet person, but not the greatest professor. Her feedback makes little sense, and she'll assign loads of homework for short periods of time. On my 1st progression, she told me that I need to start over with a whole new idea way too close to the deadline. She cares for her students but it's hard to succeed in this class.

Blagovesta is genuinely great, however, her homework's often seem like busy work and more or less ridiculous. Exercises only made sense and were clearly connectible to the progression during the 3rd essay. Her feedback will need follow up, but she wants you to succeed so do it if you want to learn with carefully crafted questions. Also hilarious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I liked her, but her class was just so confusing and overwhelming. Clarity and workload are her biggest issues. Feedback is also not great. She's one of those teachers who says "think deeper" and won't tell you how or why.

This professor's requirements for her assignment are extremely hard to understand. She doesn't articulate her ideas well and something the class thinks she just saying things to say things. She a lovely persona and has the biggest heart. It's just hard to do her assignments because of her requirements/prompts.

This class was extremely taxing. Not very helpful but assigns tons of work regardless. Criticisms can be very harsh and almost impossible to accomodate for. Papers have to be written so specifically to how she wants it, leaving no room for creativity. She's also not very accomodating for lateness, absenses, or late work and makes no effort to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Awful class. My previous writing the essay class was amazing but this one is just awful. The professor gives elusive feedback, is a very tough grader and has a set essay formula in mind which she expects everyone to follow. We learn nothing in class and she assigns plenty of complicated readings wich we never discuss or even mention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The amount of work is ridiculously small compared to other teachers. If you need free time to work on other things, this is the right teacher. She is very nice, and gives good advice.

Like all of the other reviews, she is a very nice person; however, the class itself is not enjoyable. The course load is heavy for the amount of time we have in a semester. The same amount of work due Wednesday from the Monday class as is due Monday from the Wednesday class. She checks everything! Very caring lady- just be ready to work!

Very nice and caring. However, as a professor, you don't learn much and is a complete waste of your time. Her online classes are ineffective. Every class she wastes a lot of time and we don't learn much at all. Her responses in class are very abstract and hard to understand. She also gives lots of homework too with not so useful comments on essays

Caring person, but this course as an online class is absolutely terrible. Her feedback is elusive. Zoom meetings are inefficient so far. She often spends twenty to thirty minutes addressing logistical issues. The purposes of the assignments are questionable. I don't know about how she is in-person, but don't take this class if you're going online!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice and friendly, a great person for no doubt. However, not so much as a professor. Her homework are meaningless and classes are disorganized: she lets students chat randomly for an entire class. She gives a lot of hw and has a very harsh yet equally ambitious grading criteria. Don't take her if you want to learn something from this course.

WTE is kinda an awful course anyways, but she really tries to make it interesting. She can be a bit confusing bc she usually has very specific opinions, so if you're wrong you're wrong. Also she has a tendency to go on tangents in class which is kinda fun because then suddenly you're 45 minutes into the class and you're still talking about birds.
She does not know how to write or grade. She is not helpful. I want to cry.

I absolutely love this woman as a person. However, as a teacher she is not the best. We spend most classes talking about completely random topics that having nothing to do with the lesson. As a result, there is a lot of work to do outside of class. Chill class time, but it leaves you with lots of work to do. Unclear with directions and tough grader

She's the most homely and fun teacher you'll find on campus. While grading is not too easy, classes are breeze and full of interesting discussions. She is an amazing person whose class I would absolutely love to take again. 10/10 recommend.

Blagovesta is a Bulgarian angel. WTE is inherently an awful idea, as the class varies drastically depending on who teaches it, but you really are saved if you choose this prof! She assigns about 2 pages of writing outside of class which may sound like a lot, but these "exercises" end up making up the body of your essay, so drafting is a breeze!

Blagovesta was my favorite freshman year teacher and if I could take her class again, I would. She didn't stress me out, but still motivated me to do my best and I am really proud of the work I did in her class. If you can, take her!

I had a great experience with her class. If I was ever confused she was always available by email to clear something up. She was understanding when I was absent  and helped me through it. She almost was like a second mom more than anything. You'll absolutely adore her class- I signed up for her class again for the Spring term!

Blagovesta is a really awesome person who genuinely cares about you as a person, an artist, and a writer. She helped me improve my writing far more than my teacher first semester. Sometimes she disregarded our time, such as scheduling required conferences on studio days, but overall she's a great teacher. I'd highly recommend her!

Blags is literally one of my favorite people in the world! I went to class, participated and did my homework and essays on time, so she loved me. My conferences with her were most helpful. She has AMAZING stories.  I have no complaints about her at all! I love Blags!

Writing the Essay is just a terrible class, but she assigns significantly less work than other profs.  But I really can't say I've learned much from her.  Good choice if you really dont care about Writing the Essay.
Blogovesta is an awesome teacher. She's funny and so chill. She's a fair grader and helps you a lot with your writing. Definitely recommend getting her for WTE!
THIS WOMAN RIGHT HERE IS THE BOMB. GET TO KNOW HER BECAUSE SHE IS SO CHILL. JUST ACTUALLY LISTEN AND DON'T PROCRASTINATE. AT TIMES IT SOUNDS LIKE SHE ISN'T MAKE SENSE, BUT BOYYY SHE REALLY DOES.
Blagovesta is by far one of my most inspiring professor thus far.  She wants you to own what you write with pride and perfect it in order to accomplish that.  Give to her and she'll give back
She's fun and makes class interesting but she wants to help you as much as possible with your writing so be aware of what she has to say since it works.
Blagovesta Momchedjikova is the greatest thing to come out of Bulgaria. She is the sexiest rollerblader New York has to offer, and her accent is like music to my ears.

Fantastic prof, forces you to learn how to read the texts. So grateful to have taken his class in the first semester, really taught me how to read philosophical texts well, which helped me pass future courses.
Honestly one of the best professors at nyu, really friendly professor def would take again

he is so sweet!! i wish the class was more interesting because it's the same thing every week. there is a discussion post you have to do once every week, but it's not too bad. i highly recommend it if you want a class that you know what your going to do every class.

SO SWEET. such a nice man but his lectures arer incredibly boring. every class feels the same. also gives 4 papers & will grade you on the very specific logic of ur argument. still love him tho but class feels like a bit of a drag
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He always wears black so can someone make sure he's okay
one of the best professors you will ever have! he is super insightful and gives great feedback, super easy to get an A. TAKE HIM

Amazing professor, I was able to learn about the world and more about myself. I grew as a person and a student. He cares about each student and was always ready to help and give feedback. He will also facilitate good discussions with great prompts Take him, you won't regret it!

Amazing professor, TAKE HIM!!! He truly cares for his students and works hard to get to know each one. I appreciate how he connected every idea we've seen to broader global issues and questions. Super interesting lectures!
I love him he's literally perfect and such a cutie. His lectures are so interesting and he relates things to the real world. Ugh I miss him so much

A very good Professor, gives really good feedback on essays early in the semester so there's a lot of room for you to improve. You start the course answering really simple questions about the reading, and you later evolve to dealing with more difficult discussion questions. You will grow as a student throughout the course and will grow as a person
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Bonakdarian is one of the best teachers I have ever had! He is truly caring and inspirational, making the classroom a safe environment for open communication and discussing real-world problems. He has very eye-opening discussion prompts and I enjoy how he structures the class around dialogue and sharing-out. He is a 10/10 professor :)

TAKE HIM!!!! Even though I'm on the quieter side, he is genuinely the most understanding person ever.   Even though the texts can be hard to understand, he makes his lectures so easy to understand and encourages student discussions (as much as you're comfortable with). As a plus, his jokes are funny too!!

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Seriously he is so sweet and not a tough grader. No exams, only papers. He clearly just wants the best for his students. We do weekly forums based on the reading that are super easy and he gives extra credit on them all the time, please take his class he's the best.

Super caring professor, passionate about what he teaches, not a harsh grader in my experience, just all around great guy. Part of your grade is weekly discussion posts on the course material, so stay on top of the readings! Read + participate in class and you will do well!!!
HE IS THE BEST. THE BEST. like my classmates would head out from class and talk about how amazing he is behind his back. BONAKDARIAN SUPREMACY

It's a bird...it's a plane...ITS MANSOUR! He is a perfect professor all around. Very reasonable reading in context of LS at least. He fosters amazing discussions and avoids long lectures. He's funny and super calm, and hey, he's even got a little drip. Absolute legend of a man. All my love to him.

the nicest and most chill professor ever. he values participation but is also okay if you're shy. there's only 2 essays and discussion post grades (which is every thurs). he slayed and his bald head is nice and shiny and taken care of. we stan this man!

Professor Bonakdarian was honestly my favorite professor this semester. He cares a lot about his students, and also made the class engaging and fun to show up to. Definitely recommend taking him if you get the chance.
Prof. Bonakdarian is so lovely. He's interesting, clear, caring and accommodating. He really emphasizes class discussion and is really just looking for meaningful conversation. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

You'll definitely get lost in this class if you don't do the reading because every class is all discussion. He's a nice and understanding professor, though, and I was convinced I bombed every essay and ended up with good grades on them, so I think he's lenient if you can get the gist of what you're supposed to be writing about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: The best professor at NYU!!!! Love this professor so much!! So inspiring! If you like participation, select this class with no doubt!

No tests, just 4 papers and weekly 'forum' quizzes that are on the assigned readings. Class is a lot of work, but the professor is really nice and understanding. I wouldn't say its an easy A, but if you are willing to put in basically a little more then the bare minimum then its easily achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor this semester. His lectures are very interesting, and I feel like I learned a lot from the format of his essays. There is a decent amount of required reading as you have to discuss it in class, but it was very managable.

I took him for Global Works and LOVED him! Even at 8:00am he made it worth it. His class was engaging and, and I feel like I learned so much from his class! Professor Bonakdarian is one of the sweetest professors I've had. Our grades consist of only 4 essays (no midterm or final exam), a weekly in-class discussion post, and participation. Take him!

Prof Bonakdarian was such a great professor last semester. Although the essays were significantly tedious given the course content, his feedback on every essay was so so useful. Be ready to participate in class and make sure that you ACTUALLY read what is assigned to you. It's not a class where you can do nothing and get by.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at NYU. Passionate about what he teaches, adapts to students' needs, easy to get in touch with, and so interesting to listen to. You will learn so much. Course load is manageable, especially with the thorough feedback he provides. A good amount of reading, but it'll help with you with your papers in the long term.

It's clear Prof. Bonakdarian is passionate about the material and really wants the students to engage with the readings and discussions. I really enjoyed that even though participation could be dull. My only issue is that the essays were quite tedious bc they require using readings he provides and they're much more complex than what we discuss.

Had him my 1st semester & could not say enough good things about this man! You could tell he really cared about his students, & was great at communication/giving extensions. No quizzes/tests, just a few essays that he provided excellent feedback on. Class is almost all discussion so at least skim the readings. Love this man 10/10 would take again
the best prof in NYU, take him!!! he's so nice

Highly recommend Prof Bonakdarian-He is so understanding provided you are a genuinely curious learner. He is so accessible with queries. He gives clear feedback on how you should improve, and following up on it helps you in a broader than academics sense. You must put in active effort in this class, but its so worth it. So happy I took this class

One of the nicest teachers ever. He clearly cares about students and the subjects he teaches. Class is very participation heavy and discussion based. He is extremely flexible and understanding, super respectful of students and treats everyone with respect. Good humor in class and he can make boring topics very fun in class. 150% would take again

Many reviews from last semester seem to have disappeared. Be prepared to spend a lot of time studying, as midterms and finals are very different from the practice material provided. Don't rely too heavily on the ratings especially here. If you have the option, consider taking the course with McIntyre instead.

Where do i begin? he is veryyy passionate abt his job and is nice overall. BUT this class is extremely hard. i had absolutely 0 idea what i was doing the entire time and i wouldnt wish this on my worst enemy. He's ok in teaching but the content (lectures, hw, exams) is just extremely hard. pray for a good curve because otherwise 💀

really passionate about the subject and a great teacher. exams are very hard but he curves generously. he actually listens to students' and TAs' feedback about the class. only giving him a 4/5 because the exams & hws were so hard lol but he's a great guy.

Decent and concise slides, speedy replies to questions by email, great cooperation with TA. Willing to take advice (e.g., shorten exams) from TA and students and flexible in assignments and office hours. Super generous curve. Love his 3-year-old daughter's blessing before our final!
Inspiring lectures, man's very enthusiastic about macro topics. However, exams are very, very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An adorable person with a passion in economics
A very tough grader for interm macro
He is a nice man, but his test is incredibly hard, even after curve......

He is a nice person. But his exam is soooooo hard. He usually runs out of time.
My roommate take this course with McIntyre and she said it's easier to get A in his class.
So honestly, I would choose other prof if I can.
Exams are curved generously. Make sure you do the sample exam and you'll be fine.
Borovicka is an incredible professor who is always willing to help. The tests were pretty difficult but theyre curved heavily so getting an A isnt super impossible
Jarda's the best! Take him! Helpful and passionate. Reply to your emails within a second. Tests are hard but doable if you go through all the recitations and prep exams. Huge Curve.

Very nice professor. The lectures were formatted in a super logical way and he explained the contents well. The course itself is pretty difficult, but since it is required, Jarda might be a good choice for you. Also, remember to go recitation, which helps you comprehend the formulas and relationship between variables.

Although this is a hard class and he taught too many materials, he is really responsible and reachable outside class. He explains everything carefully and patiently. You can learn a lot from his class and actually apply this knowledge to your daily life. You probably will not get an easy A, but it is still worthy taking his class.

Nice guy but the class is merely impossible to do well in. Exam averages are consistently low. Problem Sets are basically worthless and yet they require so much time and effort. Your performance in the class is solely based on your exams scores.

Great guy, really cares about what he teaches and is very accessible to his students. That being said, his class was one of the hardest I've ever taken. He tries to teach way too much (he has extra lectures that we have to watch on our own time) and exams are notoriously difficult. Averages were super low and you're graded mostly on tests
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are SO HARD. He always goes overtime, papers are totally undoable (he didnt even release the average of the second midterm because it was so low- I made around 65 which was an A). He's a sweet guy, but tries to cover WAY too much material and sets awfully difficult papers and homework. DO NOT take this prof, this class is HORRIBLY HARD.

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult professor. Lovely person, but tests are brutal. Doesn't prepare you for the questions on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most passionate professors I've had. Lectures are interesting so go to them! Exams are hard, but you will learn a lot on his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: There are very few professors that are worth praise in the Economics department at NYU. Many of them are careless and lecture as a job rather than a passion. This man was one of the best professors I've had in terms of passion for the material. You're doing yourself a disservice if you don't take his class, seriously great guy.

Although a tough class, one of the most dedicated, passionate, helpful professors I've taken. He is clear, timely, organized, intelligent, and simply brilliant. He holds review sessions before exams even if that means changing his flight to a later time. I've truly come to love Macroeconomics after this course!

His passion for the course is infectious. He genuinely loves teaching and that translates into being one of the most approachable teachers ever. It's professors like him that give NYU Econ the high ranking it has. We're lucky to have him.
interesting lecture, reasonable homework with a lot of detailed instructions. He is a very helpful teacher and very passionate about the class

Hardest class I've taken. He's teaching an undergraduate class but assigns 5 hour long problem sets almost every week, and expects us to behave like phD students. His tests are really hard, and you'll have to devote hours to understanding all the theories and models.
Absolutely brilliant prof. Organised and clear teaching style. One of the best economics profs i've taken on the square. highly recommended!!
Absolutely brilliant prof. I didn't know I liked macro this much. Highly recommend the class and especially the prof.

He's the best!!! Very intelligent and insightful, applies theories to real world situations and makes you love the material. I would never skip a lecture. Exams and problems sets are challenging and take a long time to complete but he always offers help and if you do all the review exams and problem sets you'll be ok. I'm ery grateful for jarva!

He's simply amazing!! The class is a little tough but he makes it worthwhile. I've never missed any of his lectures. I never liked Macroeconomics but his class has definitely changed that. He is very sweet and caring about his students. Love his teaching style! Definitely take him!!!!!!!
he's the best professor ever. So sad he's only teaching grad school. TAKE HIM if you can!!
Professor Jarda is very helpful. Willing to answer questions after class. His tests are challenging, but if you understand all the problems he assigned, you will do well in the class.
great professor- really interesting, crystal clear and very helpful through emails and office hours. TAs are great too.Certainly recommended.

Professor Borovicka is the man. I took him for Int. Macro. If you are willing to put the work in you can learn a lot and are given a fair chance to succeed. He is extremely invested in his students learning and understanding the material, which is what I appreciated the most. If you have the opp. I would definitely recommend you take him.

Professor Borovicka is the best professor I've had at NYU. He is very passionate about econ and cares about the students. I learned much more than I expected, but it was a lot of work! It is easy to do well in this class if you keep up.

Very difficult Intermediate Macro course. Incorporates a lot of mathematic concepts. Lectures are interesting and you can tell he is a smart guy and means well, but you have to do some SERIOUS studying to keep up.
This class is very well balanced between the security part and the necessary cryptography you should know before you learn about security. Highly recommended.
Great professor who will help you understand material since this class is information-dense. Gives tough exams but projects and homework assignments are manageable and really help reinforce material.

Lectures are very information heavy and can get dull, but were thoroughly interesting. He clearly knows his stuff and has a ton of interesting anecdotes to share. Textbook is his own that he was writing, shared out via google doc links.

Exams and projects were tough but very fair, expectations were made clear.
Great professor, knows his stuff and really loves it. Hard class though. Debugging that chat assignment nearly ended me
Good professor, fair exams with reasonable grading. Lecture can be a bit dull but information heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was a wild ride, kind of a disorganized mess because he had surgery halfway through the semester. But he is an amazing lecturerer and really cares if you need help. Class was very hard and covered a lot of ground but if you put the time in you will learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading system is ridiculous. If you are trying to argue for the grade, he acts very arrogant and without any real help. Also, his project and homework deviates from the lecture he taught.

In every class, he writes on a piece of paper and projects it to the screen. The handwriting is so bad that sometimes you can't tell what it is. His tone is hypnotic. Overall, his lecture style is terrible. This course also requires you to read plenty of papers.

I really enjoyed this class & thought Joe was an amazing lecturer. Hes great at simplifying complicated concepts. Lectures include a lot more detail than posted lecture notes, so make sure to attend. Also read the textbook notes he writes & posts. Homework & tests are hard, but doable. Highly recommend the class overall.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!! He is so chill and funny and honestly really smart. His lectures are very engaging and easy to follow. Not a lot of assignments - one midterm essay and one final exam + essay. Super interesting. WOULD TAKE HIM AGAIN!!! LOVE HIM

joe is sosososo awesome. cares so much about his students and wants you to ask for help. his projects are engaging and easy to do well on. literally the best professor i've had in college. he's also hilarious. love him

He's a really amazing guy overall. He can be harsh on grading essays, but make sure to really put effort into them and think deeper than you are used to. His classes are very interesting if you take initiative and participate. Once you know how he grades, you can adjust your essays as needed.

Overall, definitely recommend for an easy A!

Essays are usually based on reading, which can be skimmed but on personal opinion and the grading isn't strict. Extensions were given on everything but use your time wisely. Take this class if you need credit and an easy A (with some effort)!

This is the class that made me realize I want to minor in education, thanks to Prof. Brewer. He is very passionate and inspirational, and clearly always knows what he's doing. Over Brightspace, it was an easy A because 40% of the grade was quizzes that you can take 10 times (easy 100%) and 60% was papers that you can't really go wrong with.

Really have a taste and opinion. Sensitive when you are using your device in class. I really don't understand how everyone is getting an A. She's nice, but you really have to be her favorite student, or she won't give you a good grade. Yes, I didn't get a boom on mine. I received an A on each of my quizzes but ended up having an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: There was a decent amount of reading, but Professor Brosh made it pretty easy to understand. Pop quizzes, but she always hinted to them the class before. Really cares about being on time and participation, if you do both she will love you.

She is an amazing and kind professor. Make sure to do all of the reading and come prepared for class and you will be on her good side. Also, pop quizzes are quite frequent-- so yes, reading the material really matters! If you are a good participant, that will really help too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Brosh's class. I think she makes very interesting claims about different literature. No midterm; instead 6 pop quizzes and the lowest one gets dropped. Should be easy to get an A or A- on quizzes if you read. If you write about an opinion she disagrees with, it'll be reflected in your grade. I asked for a slight bump and she got me an A.

THE WORST EVER DO NOT TAKE!!! She caught someone internet browsing on their laptop and literally snatched it out of their hands and held it for the rest of class. Two months into the semester she called me the wrong name like twice when I participated everyday. Was always late to class. Gave the worst pop quizzes. Easy A, but at what cost...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not the best but not the worst. If you miss more than 4 classes your participation grade goes down a whole letter. About 2 pop quizzes per book, one essay, midterm, one art project, and hard final but if your study for a long time you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh was a pretty easy professor if you do the readings and participate in class. Get on her good side because she does pick favorites! She's also very old school and rude sometimes, but occasionally funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading and there can be pop quizzes. But if you did read and participate, you will find this class easy. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Brosh is an interesting professor. Class is super boring but if you do the reading and the work on time and speak here and there she will like you and give you a good grade. it's not a hard class if you put in some work and get on her good side.

This is among one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Despite the fact that this is an ENTRY LEVEL class, it's treated like a weed out course. Honestly I thought she was so funny and kept engaged—cause if I was typing on my computer she'd call me out lol. She's an easy grader and lowkey hints at pop quizzes but like you have to read a little to bs your way out of that. Final took a lot of studying but overall an easy A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's... something. As a person, she's not very nice. As a grader, it's mixed. If you're like me and you're sensitive and start crying in the shower because of what people say a week ago, don't.

Her assignments weren't hard but she was so unclear with what she expected out of us. not really understanding and nit picks everything. not interactive with students and you can tell when does not fw you. smh. would never take again. pop quizzes out of no where too so beware!

definitely have to read thoroughly for class due to pop quizzes, the final, and discussions. grading is based on what she wants to hear/read..it is known she rarely gives A's. she is slightly biased in that you can tell who her favorites are right from the start.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes around 5 times during the semester, where she expects you to memorize everything. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is a very unreasonable grader. There is no logic in how she grades her assignments and she is very inconsistent. the worst ever

"I don't care about your grade"

reviews.comment: tough grader

The worst professor I've ever had. She's super mean and loves giving ppl Fs on pop quizzes. Its all abt her bias. I didn't learn anything from this class.
Just RUN

Brosh is one of the best professors I've had. She is very clear about how she grades and what she's looking for in assignments. She gives so much leeway with assignments and is such an easy grader. Her final exam is challenging, however it is so easy to get an A in her class if you put in the work. She is accommodating and very sweet to talk with.

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh analyzes texts in depth and gives everyone a chance to participate. The readings excessive and you're expected to remember all the details. A lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the funniest and coolest professors I've ever had.

Brosh is such a good professor, especially for this class. She helps you understand the texts you read and helps you with any questions you may have on your assignments. This class has 2 papers, a final and a presentation but she's an easy grader if you put in the work. I really recommend her and this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Brosh is so passionate about what she teaches. She is very thoughtful and much sweeter than she initially seems. Final was tricky, but if you study thoroughly you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh can seem a little intimidating at first, but she's truly a great professor. She's smart and passionate about the material. There are pop quizzes to ensure you keep up with the readings (a lot of readings) but she explains things really thoroughly in class. Lots of opportunities to bring your grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She can seem cold/intimidating at first. Still, she is always fair and only wants her students to engage and perform their best. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her both semesters, and honestly as long as do the readings (not too long, interesting books) and participate in class (literally just say any analysis): youre golden. She is very nice and gives a lot of warnings in regards to pop quizzes, and the assignments are straightforward. Just read and offer "interesting" text opinions and youre good

I was pretty anxious about her classes at first so I put lots of works and time into this class. It turned out my efforts were paid back! She is so caring! The art history part is difficult but she did a great job of explaining it!

She is very caring and very inspirational in class. She makes you want to know arts more. People here give her bad ratings because she is not that kind of professor who gives an easy A to everyone. You need to read the readings for discussion. This is one of my favorite classes throughout the whole year (yes I took her for a year).

Bottom line is if you read and participate you are golden. She is very fair when it comes to grading and loves talking about the literature and art she teaches. She also gives out study guides for the readings and most likely than not one of those questions is going to be your quiz question on that text. She is intimidating at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Brosh was very rude in class and created an uncomfortable environment. She did offer extra credit, though, and was understandable about some things. However, I don't think her attitude in class was worth it. Plus, the readings were hard!

Very kind professor who genuinely cares about her students

Solid professor, tends to lecture a lot before allowing students to participate. Clearly states criteria for assignments and grading. reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

my fav bbb professor Broshie luv her guys

absolutely terrible, do yourself a huge favor by not taking this class. Expects perfect answers on things she doesnt even teach in class

reviews.comment: Brosh is a nice person. She gave me an A-, but I had to work for it. HARD. She relies heavily on class participation to carry discussions, and will call randomly on you. A nice person and gives you second chances on papers if you show that you care. But honestly, I dreaded her class. Even looking back on it, I still wouldn't take again. Mixed...

I love Dr. Brosh, i took her twice. She gives a lot of reading but if you actively read and participate in class, you will get an A. 50% of the class is pop quizzes on the HW so read, take notes on what you're reading so you can bring it up in class. The final is HARD but if you actually read you should be kind of ok.. i got a 90 on it somehow.
Straightforward, informative, never dull. She is not a hard grader but she still expects for you to read and do your work well. Take her if you want to learn new things AND get a decent grade.

This Professor is honestly one of the most straight-forward professors I encountered within my freshman year. Even though she seems to be a bit intimidating in the beginning and gives of the impression that she isn't very approachable, if you read everything you're supposed to and participate in class, you will be perfectly fine.

Extremely disorganized (she was ALWAYS late to our class). She is also not open to other interpretations of the text- she is adamant in having the text seen in her point of view only. An easy A though if you do the reading. During the days she was actually early for class, there would be pop quizzes.

Extremely kind, understanding, and compassionate. As long as you participate and do the reading (emphasis on doing the fking reading), then you will 99% get an A. It's that simple. Do what you are supposed to do and you will be rewarded. However, if you don't, then gluck!

You will learn a lot if you take Professor Brosh!! Professional, informative, and enthusiastic, Professor Brosh will motivate you to work hard and get as much out of the class as possible. There is a lot of reading, but that's just the nature of the course. Also know that she offers plenty of extra credit, and is a fair grader. I'd take her again.

Very good, structured class. A lot of reading but we always discuss the reading in class. Pop quiz on reading most classes. She likes people who participate. If you don't do the reading you will fail, if you do, you'll get an A

Professor Brosh is a passionate, helpful, and instructive professor. She comes to every class very prepared, and is always willing to be a great instructor. She is also a very kind lady, and she creates an entertaining class environment. I could not say anything bad about her or her class. You will love her!!!!!

Although the class would sometimes be put to sleep during her lectures, she also gives the class time to participate. She does get flustered easily when it comes to technology, but she is a nice person. She likes those who participate. There is a lot of reading, and she expects you to do all of it. Sometimes she gives quizzes based on the readings.

Professor Brosh is very intense but also a very sweet lady. She's stressed a lot, but she is always willing to help. She tends to get flustered, but seriously she is so passionate about teaching and about the material it's amazing and she is willing to work with you. Don't even think about using your phone or cheating. She will catch you.

She is THE BEST professor at NYU I've ever had the pleasure of meeting. She is always smiling and is ready to help! Show you're interested in the class and she will love you. Do the reading, participate in class and you will get an A. Do the reading it's sooo interesting and engage in discussion, you will learn so much!  Take her!

She chose good texts. At first, listen to the discussions and learn the type of analysis she likes. Then analyze the subsequent works in that manner.  Not a hard grader, if you follow directions. Lecture is based on class participation so be sure to get your word in there. As a person, she is kind and patient. I would take her for CFIII if I could.

Prof. Brosh is the sweetest woman. She is very helpful and she understands that you have other classes. Mora than once she extended our due dates, which was great. I recommend getting yourself a buddy to keep you updated if you miss class. Other than that, she is great. She taught me how to analyze tets on a deeper level. I recommend her highly.

Best teacher I've had so far in NYU. She inspired me to take interest in something I was previously not and made my experience with the subject all the better. She is a very FAIR grader, holds interesting discussions in class, and is a very nice lady. She may assign homeworks after every class but they are really helpful for the final.

One of the best teachers I've had so far.  She really wants the students to do well in the class and is very helpful with essays.  Her assignments are not that demanding.  You just have to do the reading and the questions.

Prof. Brosh showed a considerable lack of consideration for the students. She was late 90% of the time and has very little interpersonal skills. Unless if you want to be pointed at and called "you" when you raise your hand because your prof. can't learn 20 names don't take her.

Brosh is very interested in and knowledgeable about her subject, but she is often a little too excited. She is late to class more often than not and doesn't know how to use a computer well. She doesn't stick to the syllabus either. She's rather scatterbrained, but her class is easy. If you have her, MAKE FRIENDS(!) in case you miss class.

Incredibly condescending. His essay prompts are a little unclear and it takes a minute to understand. But, the things that make my rating a 1/5 are his consistent general digs at college students' work, his cursing far past the amount that is considered humorous from a professor, and his hostile, personally disrespectful feedback.
He is cute like a rabbit, he is understanding, tho sometimes he may not be offering you enough feedback as he is busy with his children.

bro is SOOOOOOOOO passionate abt writing. like idek. I had some brain cells revived ong. but his rubric is very thought out and clear and all you have to do is just put one ounce of effort in. he's funny. if you take him in the fall or spring you'll enjoy his class a lot if you take it after lunch or something. very entertaining.
His lectures are a lot of fun. He's a humorous and engaging professor who respects students and shows empathy toward international students who come from diverse backgrounds.

Awesome writing professor! Doesn't give much daily homework. I love his daily reading assignments that interest int'l students a lot. Like other expos professors, he uses the labor-based grading system, meaning that you need to do a challenge option each progression to receive a final A in the course. Only two progressions (essays).

reviews.comment: Great professor, he uses labor-based grading (doesn't grade each essay individually) so as long as you complete all the work with effort you will receive an A. Don't be late because that will impact your grade. He allows 4 absences without impacting your grade but do go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
He is the best ACE Prof!
- Teaching style -> lectures + discussions -> material is engaging
- Homework -> MINIMAL (1 writing tasks per week + 1 reading) 
- Lenient with deadlines
- 2 essays in total and a few small graded activities 
- Conferences were helpful --> Prof would make direct edits --> gives good feedback (PLS show him a full draft tho)
Tough grader

Butler is an engaging lecturer and fairly easy grader. Really understanding person too. He would come off as a bit pretentious sometimes (he reaaallly loves classic literature) which made him seem a little inaccessible. If you participate and do all the assignments, you'll be good. Overall I enjoyed the class.
Decently easy grader and helpful in individual feedback sessions, but his classes aren't that engaging. He bangs his hands against the board to make a point which is eh. Also has boomer energy.

My favorite writing prof at NYU so far. Very understanding of personal circumstances but remember to clearly communicate your concerns. Will not be on your case if rough drafts are not fully completed in time, but a good grade requires effort. If feedback is unclear, ASK HIM! Really likes talking during class but content is interesting. Minimal hw

Favorite Writing Professor at NYU. He is so warm and helpful, held individual meetings with you to discuss your papers, and I think he grade fairly while carefully at the same time. Really MINIMAL homework. Recommend!

He is by far the best professor I've had at NYU. Very clear about the criteria and explain things explicitly in class. Individual meetings are extremely helpful and detailed, some of my classmates say he is better than the writing center. Also super understanding and caring, respects the different time zones students could be in.

As an international student, I do believe Prof Butler cares about his students. I learned meaningful writing skills from him, true. And his class is pretty fun. Indeed, receiving an A requires quite a lot of effort. However, LISTEN to his feedbacks in the video conference because they are helpful! Overall, he will be a good choice for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is such a mean person. The most unfortunate thing in this semester is taking his class. He never replies to email nor give helpful feedbacks. Once I was sick and had 5000 words papers. I politely asked for his extension. He didn't reply until four hours later I finished. I said: please ignore this. He immediately replied: ignored. Really hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Butler is the most interesting professor I had in the writing courses. He is really supportive of creative ideas and he tends to give a lot of choices for students to write about, so I ended up enjoying the writing process. Still, get a good grade requires a lot of effort, and he is pretty loud. Btw: I'd suggest stir away from political questions.

I wouldn't say he's a bad professor and I understand that some profs think B's a really good score, but he just grades too toughly (comparing to everyone else's sessions) that it really affects my GPA (which s kinda important). Caring and inspirational. Generally good. But sometimes he wouldn't answer afterclass questions as "it s unfair to others"

Nobody really wants to take expository writing, but Professor Butler is a really great choice. He cares and really tries to make the class interesting and insightful. I can honestly say I am a much better writer after taking this course. One thing to note is that he is quite a difficult grader and was not specific in his feedback.

Amazing professor who really cares about his students. He gives great feedback and is always willing to help. I advise reaching out to him outside of class either through email or after class. Very tough class in general but you definitely learn a lot and become a much better writer. Don't expect to get an A, maybe an A- if you really work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: No one in this class likes this professor. He talks just to hear himself talk and won't listen to any perspectives other than his own. Of course ACE and Writing the Essay aren't the best classes to begin with but he makes ACE HELL.

Butler is fantastic! This class is tough no matter what but he really will make you a better writer by the end of it. He's always willing to help students and classes are engaging. Put a little effort into your papers and he'll like you.
Helpful, tough grader, not clear

Expository writing courses are no joke at NYU. Professor Butler makes sure that students understand the importance of these courses. He may seem intimidating at first, but he's one of the nicest professors I've had. As long as you do all your homework and show that you're putting genuine effort, you should be fine. He is somewhat of a tough grader.
Great professor! Very helpful and makes class entertaining. Not easy workload or grading-wise, but definitely one of the best WTE professors and made me a much better writer.

Great professor, really helped me improve my writing. Readings were not too bad if you actually bothered to read. In-class discussions were heavily dependent on readings and very helpful. Grading contract makes it quite easy to get an A as long as you put some effort. Attendance policies are quite strict, and affects your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Bujnowski's Writing as Inquiry class. She was very encouraging and never judged a student's writing. Rather, she gave helpful feedback to help you improve. Grading criteria is fair, if you do all your work you get a B, and if you want an A you need to complete 3 bonus options, which were interesting and fairly simple to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I enjoyed her class, and it significantly improved my writing skills. The professor provided very detailed and meaningful comments on the essay, but it took several weeks to receive the feedback. I would recommend taking her lecture if you want to improve your writing, but don't want to get stressed by the endless assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bujnowski changed my entire relationship to writing. I started the class feeling totally unprepared and scared, but she was so encouraging and took time to check in with me. The classes/homework break down the process for each essay and her feedback and conferences really helped….she's constructive without being harsh. So glad I got her!

The course felt extremely smooth and interesting. I liked the way professor Ali encourages students and she's very caring.The class has a friendly environment and would not bore anyone. I look forward to this class every week. Though there might be work to do in the class, not all will be extremely tiring, instead, it is fairly enjoyable.

BEST. PROFESSOR. EVER! Ali totally transforms how you think about writing. I didn't expect to enjoy this class as much as I did. She breaks down the writing process and makes it feel manageable. Sometimes challenging, but in a way that makes you grow as a writer and thinker. 10/10 recommend. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN. 🌟
a lot of readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor B is absolutely the best professor you could ask for. She does give a lot of homework but they are very helpful. She is very accessible through email and office hours, or even just after class. She genuinely cares about us and brings us snacks occasionally.
lots of home work, grading criteria is not clear and her opinions towards your paper changes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. B is amazing and so nice! She really created a supportive and engaging class experience. The homework exercises and lessons prepare you to write the essays and overall I've grown so much as a writer. Sign up for conferences and to talk to her! She's super accessible and will offer ideas and suggestions to help you with your essays.
heavy homework and really confusing and strict, you will spend almost 10 hours each week on her course
I spend my whole weekend working on her homework
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ali is so nice and will work with you to make sure you are keeping up and was so easy to meet with outside of class. Her feedback was insightful and, overall, gave a huge boost to my writing. There was a lot of required reading, but the majority was quite interesting. Take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali's seriously the best. She's a tough but fair grader and really pushes you to do your best. It's obvious how much she cares about her students and wants them to grow and succeed. She's the kind of professor I came to NYU for. Also, go to the writing center, getting the right tutor can make a world of a difference in this class.

I found Professor Ali to be a lenient grader, as she is caring and understanding about deadlines. She encourages  participation.  It was the best writing class I've ever taken. Her clear accent makes her easy to understand, and she is the professor I admire the most.

Definitely one of the nicest professors you can meet at NYU. She is so kind and caring:) She made my first semester of college much easier and more comfortable. Regardless, you have homework almost every day, but that homework ultimately helps you to guide your final paper per each progression.

Take her! She may appear crazy in the beginning, but trust me she may be the kindest person you've ever meet. A lot of weekly homework that may need a few hours. Her feedback is always shaky and she mentions stuff when she submits your grade that you've never heard before. She's giving older sister vibes and always asks us how our weekends were.

Professor Bujnowski was one of my first teachers at NYU, and she really made my transition into college very pleasant. She cares deeply about each of her students' success, and it shows. Even though my class was at 8am and everyone was tired, she managed to peak my interest in the topics of discussion. Thank you so much Professor!!
Super caring teacher!

You can really tell that Ali cares about her students. She's not exactly an easy grader, but you can definitely manage an A- as long as you ask her for feedback on your essays. She gives good advice on your writing and it helps a lot to have specific questions in mind before conferences. Didn't do them, but she also offers revisions at the end.

Ali is a really caring professor who just wants to see you improve as a writer. Reading the long homework assignments will help in the long run, and the more you participate the better because then she will be more helpful to you on your drafts. If you do your work, and put in a bit of effort Ali will make this class very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bujnowski might be the best professor I have ever had. I wasn't too excited about taking a writing class and it ended up being my favorite course. She is caring, comprehensive, and incredibly dedicated. I learned more than I ever thought I would. She inspires you to work hard for your essays and grades fairly. Take her class if you can!

Ali is one of the most amazing teachers I've ever had. Puts in the time to make sure the class is up to speed. It is clear she cares about her students. Offers amazing insight into how you can strengthen your essays. Completely successful at transforming your writing and taking your essays to the next level. Allows revisions on certain essays.

Ali is the best! She knows WTE is a challenge but shes super approachable and will help you a ton. She gives lots of targeted feedback on drafts so you know exactly how to improve and I really did become a better writer because of her. The readings and assignments were relatable and interesting, and yeah, theres hw but its manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali loves getting her students involved in classes and is constantly making writing topics relevant to us. However, her commentary is extremely confusing and contradictory. Every essay I wrote she would wait and decide she didn't like my argument during my final draft and my grade would suffer. If you want an easy A do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ali is the best that WTE has to offer. With her class, you get what you give. She does her part to make class interested (Wes Anderson days are the BEST), and she expects you to do your part (i.e. reading the assigned essays, fully investing yourself in drafting, participating in class). She is brilliant, genuinely cares, and is gorgeous. Love her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali is great. She really is the best you can get. However, don't go there expecting an awesome grade if you are not the best writer out there. While she does value effort and commitment, it is very hard to go above the B if you are a 'normal' writer. Homework is heavy but it does help build your essay in steps which helps. Also, she is BEAUTIFUL

Ali was the best writing the essay professor I could ever ask for. Classes and guidelines were very structured which WTE easier to understand. Though her grading is tough, she's so willing to help and gives opportunities to revise that if you put in the effort you can bring your grade up to as high as you try. An incredible and caring professor.

I'm absolutely in love with her. Ali is not only a great professor, but also a genuine person. I learned something from every class and she was very clear on what needed to be improved. I took her class for both WTE and ACE and I do not regret waking up early to take her 9:30 AM class. If you want to learn how to write, she should be your go-to.

Amazing WTE Professor, but grades are a struggle. Coming from a mediocre writer, she made me understand exactly where I was lacking, and expected me to adapt to her expectations. Tonnnnnes of homework, but that's WTE for you. Take her! Very lucid, and no WTE is really an easy A.
Despite the fact that WTE is a huge pain, Ali made it pretty fun. She's very chill and definitely knows her stuff. If I could take a class with her again, I would.

Ali Bujnowski is kind, intelligent, respectful, and fair.  I started off hating her just because of the sheer work involved in Writing the Essay.  However, now that I understand that this workload is common amongst all professors in this class, I have grown to see the value of her assignments.  I would take a class taught by her again.

Ali is a great teacher! I didn't think I would like WTE at the beginning, but she's made it one of my favorite classes this year & I always look forward to it. She's approachable but professional, intelligent, and really engages us with the material. Would definitely recommend her.

Ali was very helpful, and genuinely tried to make us all better writers. This being said, the fact that we had "Writing the Essay" made everything a real pain, but I doubt that it could have been better without Ali. If I ever have to take another writing course, I'll definitely try my best to get Ali again

She is passionate about the subject and likes to have discussions with the class. She is respectful, kind, helpful, and reasonable. However she tries to hold your hand every step of the way which is suffocating, and the amount of work (2 papers a week) got tiring(all writing 101 classes are like this though). Overall I'm happy I got her.

Amazing professor; Writing the Essay is by nature an extremely annoying, tedious,  and somewhat pointless class, but she makes it enjoyable. The actual classes with her are really fun and engaging, but the homework and everything is still as abundant and time-consuming as any other WTE class's is.

Ali is hands down one of the best writing instructors in her department. (I've been to the writing center many times) Her class is well-organized and she engages her students in exciting conceptual discussions. If you have any problems, schedule office hours and conferences with her; they are extremely helpful. All in all, she made WTE enjoyable!

I don't consider myself a writer, and I really dreaded WTE coming into it. The class was certainly a lot of work, but Ali is awesome. Her teaching is really engaging and fun. Schedule a conference with her for each essay because she is so helpful and provides a lot of insight. Her grading is fair and she rewards hard work. Definitely recommend her!
I have her as a writing the essay professor and I really like her teaching. I just wish I actually enjoyed writing. Even still, she is very reasonable and helpful. I would highly recommend her.

Ali is an amazing professor.  Her classes are interesting, she brings in photographs, art, and movies to help get you to understand the writing process.  She is clear in her feedback on exercises and essays.  The more you participate and put in effort, the better grade you'll get (as long as your work is good) Ali is a fair grader and great overall
yes,it's true that policy changed since fall2025
he doesn't know what he is teaching & the grading is super bad and no room for discussion on hws and quizzes grade. make us desperate
Just to let you know that I got C+ and three of my friends got C+ too. Don't say he is easy grader. I am pretty sure I work a lot and do everything he told on class. More than 50 percent got below B.
very harsh grader for fall 2025. don't take his. overall a range less than 15 percent. Fierce competition. I withdrew.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Minimal workload, open book tests. Final project worth 50% of the grade. Nobody got below an A- in it. Pretty sure 100% of the class had A- and up. Easy grader. Gives you an opportunity to build something cool for the final project and gives great suggestions in office hours. Go for the prof, maybe not for the content as it is a bit scattered.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved the class! You'll learn a lot, from bioinformatics to graph theory and cryptography. Professor really cares about students' learning!
The biggest joke of a class in the CS department. Take this iff you want to put minimal effort into getting an A.
Informative but 0 structure. Doesnt seem to care if you learn anything.
barely learn anything, quizzes not related to lectures, most of grade is on hw and final project
you will learn nothing from this course. easy A but not worth it

After the midterm grade for the course was released, he wasted an entire lecture going over every single piece of negative feedback he received on the midterm course evaluations one by one, trying to convince us that they were incorrect. His classes are aimless, and homework is not related to what is discussed at all.

Worst professor ever. Told us quizzes only counted for less than 10% of the grade, made them count for 30% of the grade in the end, and threatened to lower my grade when I pointed this out. Quizzes have no bearing on anything (we were asked about Angelina Jolie's risk of breast cancer), website is never updated. Seems friendly, do not fall for it.

Very nice guy but horrible as a professor. No structure to class whatsoever, no way to check your grades. Quizzes have NOTHING to do with anything, will instead test pop culture knowledge. Never updates website. Expects you to have an idea for final project on Day 1. Really weird guy overall. Probably an easy A, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bud is a nice man but you learn nothing and there is no transparency with how you are graded. You are not given like a guidebook to what your grades look like online. He doesn't use NYU Classes nor does he have any online way to let you know how your grade is looking. Very confusing and no structure don't recommend.
Great class!
Don't think I learned anything in this class

biggest joke of a class. no tests, no exams, hardly any hw, quizzes are riddles, probably the easiest class to get an A in with minimal effort. feel ripped off taking this class, did not learn anything either. put in more effort into 1 algo hw assignment than in the entirety of this class. avoid if you want to learn. take if you want easy A.
the way he puts words together makes things hard to be understood
I wish I could take more courses taught by him!
Awesome professor!
First day in and he already seems snobby and rude. Heavily considering dropping this class

his lecutres r skippable. hes a smart guy and is sometimes interesting but the lectures are extremely boring and useless. paper criteria is weird. midterm and final r rly difficult but its nicely curved. this class made me switch out of the poli sci major

4 two-page papers are 50% of your grade. Extremely forgiving curve on the midterm -- almost unfair to people who scored well. Exams are very similar to practice exams. Go to recitation; game theory learned there is not taught in lecture. Prof is very interesting. If you have something meaningful to contribute to class he won't belittle you.

very intelligent and accomplished man, though arguably not the BEST professor: is pretty harsh to students that try to participate in lecture which i'm sure is good for overall development of politics students but some of it seems unnecessary, and didn't do too well with pacing units and lecture slides were rough to look at. but overall recommend!

Encourages students to answer questions and belittles them when they respond incorrectly, despite having several degrees and decades more experience. 

Your TAs don't grade your material! It's all random, so don't stress whoever you end up taking for recitation. They're also quite flexible about just attending other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Encourages people to ask questions then belittles them when they don't agree with his views. Has very strong ideas of international politics and is not open to students who question him about some biased facts he says during lectures. You don't have to do the readings, everything on the midterm is based on the midterm review and the past midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor would take him again!

Fascinating guy who pioneered the IR field. Goes on tangents a lot, and the pacing was too slow in the beginning and possibly too fast near the end. Attending recitation is important because it equips you with the necessary quantitative skills to succeed. Would recommend, I have learned a lot about IR from this class.

extremely interesting lectures, except theyre pretty info-heavy and its easy to get lost in the content so make sure you keep up. funny and cool and tries to engage with his students. graded on few things so its not an easy A at all. but its a very valuable course. make sure you actually are interested in int pol though and youll like this

He is a good professor but he doesn't take a lot of time to explain things in a way that makes sense without prior game theory knowledge. I took this course as a freshman, but I would recommend waiting until at least your sophomore year and you'll be fine! (He is a funny dude)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very inspiring professor; his lectures are incredibly captivating. This class was just game theory 101, you'll need to be comfortable with some math. There are 4 short papers graded by the TAs, a midterm, and a final. The exams were almost identical to the practice exams. Readings are not necessary, what you learn in recitation will carry you.

BDM is a icon, he is so smart, funny, and edifying to have as a professor. he made international politics super interesting to learn about. however, TA's can vary so select carefully, some are incredibly difficult and like to flex their statistical/game theoretical knowledge j to confuse us. def look at BDM's youtube videos online before tests!

The material for this class is not easy so you will have to do a lot of independent studying. The review problems that are released before the exams are very similar, if not nearly the same, as the exam that you take so do the review problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture and recitation material hardly overlap, and the content is explained poorly. Part of the grade is also based on essays, graded somewhat subjectively by the TAs. Luckily, the midterm and final exams are very similar to what is on the review guides, but you have to teach yourself the game theory/math because it's not discussed in class.

He could do a little better in explaining concepts, but he makes practical applications very clear + the midterm and final were almost exact copies of the study guides he gives you. Very little reading required and the course is designed so just paying attention in lectures and recitations is enough to pass

Bruce is a good professor. Lectures can be a little slow at times, but the material itself was pretty interesting. No homework, just four 2-page papers that are worth 50% total. There are readings, but nothing too crazy. Make sure to attend recitations, since the midterm and final are based on concepts you go over there. All in all, a fair class.

Your experience in this class really depends on the TA you get since they'll be the one grading the 2 page current event papers. Mine was a harsh grader but it got easier once I figured out what they wanted. The readings are quite dense but you can manage without reading everything. The tests don't exactly mirror recitation practice though.

The exams can be difficult and he will actually warn you about it. He curved our two exams but I was quite upset until he informed us about the curve. Doing the readings is necessary as he will test you about the readings, and I will also suggest going to the recitations if you want to do well in this class.

Took his game theory class. Does not go over your assignments carefully. Written comments/feedback were useless, had to go to office hours to figure things out. Rude to students who disagree with his thoughts.

He's an erudite professor who teaches his own compelling theories. Lectures involve basic math; nothing too challenging. He sticks around after class to answer questions, though sometimes his answers are a bit complex. Going to both recitations and lectures is crucial - topics often differ, and both are on exams. No need to spend time on readings.

hands down the most inspiring and also difficult intro politics I've taken. has a fair amount of algebra that you don't normally see in politics classes, that's where most ppl were struggling. That being said it's an interesting class that changed my opinions about politics. readings r hard & unhelpful. recommend read his book dictator's handbook

tbh not as bad as everyone in my class made him out to be. not that much math as it's mostly just plugging in middle school algebra equations that you usually dont have to memorize as long as you understand the basics. TAs pretty much write and grade everything so def go to recitations. his lectures are interesting but hes a bit egotistical.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of math and equations out of nowhere. The final was horrible. TA's did not give an answer key to the practice problems for it. Most of the topics were interesting (P.S lots of content and concepts to learn) but most of the time I didn't understand a thing of what he was saying as well. I fell asleep in all of his lectures.

Do not take this class. The midterm review was nothing like the midterm. The final was worse as my TA only went over 3/7 questions and then all the TAs refused to post the answer key/help as you should've "been in recitation" (when they didn't cover it). As an A student with a 4.0 GPA, I had to make this class p/f. Interesting topic, horrible class

DO NOT take this class. More than an international politics class, this is a calc course. The professor has really interesting ideas and theories, he created most of the material and that's really cool and interesting BUT he comes up with a non sense equation for everything. Neither lecture nor recitation prepare you for the exams (50% of grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: More of a lecturer than a professor. Not the most open when you ask questions and often answers as if you should already know it. Cool that most of the stuff we learn was created by him, but there are sometimes shortcomings of his theories that he fails to mention which makes things confusing.

Do not take this class unless you are interested in the game theory behind International Politics. For an intro class we were learning very complex game theory, and the class average for the midterm was curved 20 points to a 60. Most of the exam is from the recitations and 1/3 is from lectures. Take another core class/ try a different professor.

Comes up with a stupid formula/diagram every single class to explain qualitative principles which makes no sense. Horrible class. Like girl, I did not sign up to be a Politics major so I could memorize 10 different stupid formulas that he literally pulled out of his ass, that i'll never have to use in another class ever.
AVERAGE

I do feel the people who take this class need to get luck with their TA because the exams are highly dependent on the content that are covered on recitation. It was not a great experience since that some of the practice problem answers are just the opposite of what in the slides. So it is perplexing.

I did not enjoy his teaching style. He is kind of arrogant in his knowledge/experience in politics and talks down to students. He teaches really abstract concepts that are hard to apply to real life. I understand he is a well-known and respected professional but that doesn't make someone a good teacher. Relied 100% on TA's to get through.

respected poliscientist, expert in his field (wrote textbook); organized lectures with lots of advanced content, but you will do well on exams by understanding the basic logic, which he truly wants you to learn, so he provides huge curves on both midterm and final, but I still suggest studying outside of class. three easy HWs. great politics class.

You really have to get lucky with your TA, as Bruce does not have anything to do with the grading for the class. However, he has had a very interesting career and gave great lectures with cool real world applications he has experienced.

3 problem sets, midterm, and final make up your final grade. Lectures are optional but very educational and entertaining, but most if not all test material comes from the recitations and textbook. The textbook is very clear/interesting (he wrote it himself) and reading it along with knowing game theory should have you covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most inspiring and knowledgeable lecturers and his class would be worth taking for that simple reason. However, he does go off on tangents quite often and it makes it hard at first to figure out what to jot down. His tests expect understanding rather than raw learning. No need to show up to recitation, they're not graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers that gives you amazing insight into politics and power struggles. The only downside is the grading. It is very tough and one sometimes ambiguous topics briefly described in class or hidden in a random bullet in the powerpoint. The curve should take care of it though, so don't miss out on this class for fear of a bad grade.

Great material, but grading is unfair and unrepresentative of what is covered in lecture. The final is 50% of the grade. It doesn't test major concepts and ideas as much as very abstract concepts that you cannot find a direct answer to anywhere. There was a no-partial credit MC on it worth 10% of that final, or 5% of YOUR ENTIRE GRADE! Absurd!

Gives a bunch of abstract concepts, explains them without clarity, doesn't give you chances to practice applying these abstract concepts and then tests you on them on exams that are weighted super heavily. One question can be worth a bunch of points, for example, circling a multiple choice question wrong can get you up to 10 points off.
Bruce is great to listen to in lecture, but what he says doesn't matter much on the exams. To get an A, you need to go to recitation and learn the math of IR. Easy class overall.

Only take if interested in Politics or IR majors. Teaches IR through math. It is easy to get distracted in class as Bruce does tend to gloss over a lot of things. Recitation is your BFF- if you have a good TA (KJ, Harsh or Pedro). TA matters for your grade, not prof. Go to office hrs. Textbook is useless, got A without opening it, but studied a lot
