You cannot graduate NYU without taking a class with Professor Bueno de Mesquita. This guy know's his stuff & presents thoughts and arguments, based strictly on logically induced positive thinking.  The best professor ever!

Great professor!! Most of the class revolves around material he researched with his colleagues. Must attend lectures and recitations. He gives a new perspective to international relations and politics. Only thing that could be difficult is game theory, but they teach it well and clearly.

International Politics is a fantastic course and very interesting. Bruce can be a bit confusing in class, but recitation usually clears up all confusion. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, but I highly recommend going because Bruce is THE expert in the field. Reading the text is assigned, but it is not essential for a good grade. Take!

The guy knows what he is talking about. Everything he says in class is word for word from the textbook (which he authored). The lecture is more so necessary to understand IR applications rather than just succeed grade wise in the class. The class if basic algebra and logical reasoning, so test shouldn't be that hard if your prepared.

He is really an amazing professor. Great researcher and great mentor. He introduced rational choice into IR and has made it essential part of IR. Ignore negative comments. You should experience one of the greatest professor in history of IR before leaving NYU.

Amazing professor, really knows his stuff and is engaging. He is, however, a bit of an egomaniac and thinks the world of himself. Still, this should not hinder your learning experience, just give you something to laugh at.

(Solving Foriegn Crises)Anyone writing negative comments just doesn't get it.  Take any of his classes, audit... whatever... you MUST experience him before you leave NYU.  You will simply have your mind blown every class.  You will mature as a thinker due to his rigorous methods of examining IR.  His teaching is life-changing.
Disregard all previous comments.  He is a narcissist who just wants his students to buy his book!

While he is enthusiastic about his subject and has a wicked sense of humor, he is not the one to determine your grade but the TAs.  The class is usually 200+ people so make sure you have a helpful TA who is lenient. Despite how much he says the class is like "9th grade algebra".. it's NOT. It's like chemistry... memorization.

i LOVE Bueno De Mesquita.  He may be well past his sexual prime.  But my god, the man gets me all hot and bothered.  I want him to talk nerdy to me. ALL. NIGHT. LONG. <3 .  He knows his stuff, he knows the material, he's incredibly enthusiastic and he wants to challenge you to really understand the topic.  He is BRILLIANT!  One of the best! <3 him!

Prof. Bueno de Mesquita is probably the most amazing professor you will ever have at NYU. I took his Intl Pol class and learned alot. Intl pol is not what you think is, it's highly mathematical. But that's reality; this man speaks the truth. He is highly intelligent and his teaching method is eccentric, yet logical. He is a modern-day Nostradamus.

He told us he hadn't taught the course since the 1970s.  While everything he had to say was always interesting, it wasn't always relevant.  Do all of the reading and understand it BEFORE the lecture, otherwise you'll be lost with him.  Digressions are either wonderful or terrible.
AN IR GOD.
I like International/world politics. Dr. Bruce is intelligent and well-connected but difficult to follow in class.

The very first classes are hard to understand and it might seem like the game theory is going nowhere. However, I was suprised that it all made sense in the end. Great Class!! Very smart man! I loved it!

Heavy on game theory and equations, uses interesting and facinating case-studies, great sense of humor, engaging with students. Highly recommended for for political science and international relations students.
great teacher. Incredibly intelligent on politics and many other subjects. A little hard to understand sometimes, but overall, you'll learn a lot from her.
Hottie 4 eva! Needs to improve teaching skills... i daydream in that class.

I took Professor Busa in the Fall of 25 for her CAMS 147 - Love Actually class. She loves teaching this class, and you can tell. She teaches directly off the slides and from the readings; however, this does not mean skip class. This class has two professors, and she was clearly the favorite. She does teach fast, but it is very comprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took Love Actually with Jeremy and Sam. She is fun and relatable, but tends to rush through content sometimes. Midterm was unfairly difficult, which she warned us about (?), but the final was easy. Lots of reading, which I didn't do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sam is a very relaxed, down to earth professor! She really just wants participation in discussion and on forums, but makes it easy to. The final exam was hard but shes not wholly in charge of what goes on the test - all the Love Actually course instructors give the same exam. She is super quick at responding to emails (never on weekends though).
Took her class "Love Actually" and LOVED it. She's a fun professor and was great about facilitating discussion. Easy grader and takes feedback into consideration.

Great CAMS teacher! She gives you every opportunity to succeed by dropping lowest response and test grades. The lectures are informative and generate great discussion. Some weeks are heavier than others on reading, but they are integral to fully understanding the class. She is very understanding about participation and workload, would take again!

Professor Burgos is a true gem at silver. She cares for her students. PARTICIPATE !!! Show commitment to the material, she doesn't like people to be on your screens. Email is very reliable when communicating with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Burgos was amazing! If you really care about the course and the topics you will find each class incredibly engaging and powerful. Do NOT be late to class, her expectations are very clear. No going on phones or computers while she speaks-- participation matters. Overall a funny, kind, knowledgeable and well respected woman!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HER! She is very caring and smart and passionate about social work! I just enjoyed the class so much. You will learn a lot! If you just listen and participate you'll have no problem! She teaches from the heart and not just reads off the slides. I love her!

She's the best teacher I've ever had. Society and social welfare is the reason I want to be a social worker. She's hysterical and sweet and everyone loves her. most understanding person. I will miss her. Easy A but definitely pay attention, she has so much incredible knowledge, its stupid to miss out.
Professor Buhler skillfully synthesizes a collection of interconnected and important methods in applied mathematics with artistry. Highly recommended.

Prof Buhler is the best math prof I have ever met!! He's nice and caring in his office hour. Although the course is extremely hard (do not expect to understand everything in the lectures), the homeworks and exams are moderate.

Hope this time when Professor Butler browses this webpage, he won't be heartbreaking haha. He really has a good sense of humor. To be honest, among the 20-ish lectures, I only understood one lecture which was about particle paths. However, his office hours helped a lot, though I always asked stupid questions:))
The best prof I had this semester, very inspiring lecture!! Love him!!

Professor Buhler is AWESOME!! He genuinely cares about his students, holds regular office hours, delivers inspiring lectures and encourages critical thinking. The semester was truly exceptional, and I have gained far more than I initially anticipated when I began with professor Buhler. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

I seldom leave a comment for professor but professor Buhler is an exception. He is such a nice person who really care about his student. He hosts 2 hours OH each weeks and willing to schedule extra meeting with you even he has a busy schedule. Very encouraging and knowledgable. I would definitiely take his course in the future if he will teach.
Tough professor but worth it! Exams are based on homework and manageable if you study. He is a great professor, highly recommend

Great professor. Fast-paced lectures with no notes posted. So make sure you don't miss any of them since the homework would be pretty difficult without the lecture material. The difficulty of the midterm and final is at the same level of the homework, so if you take the homework seriously, it shouldn't be hard to get an A.

Professor Buhler is a gem. His lectures are very condensed and he has the ability to convey challenging mathematical concepts fairly smoothly. Learning from him is a great opportunity but make sure not to miss any lecture and to go to his office hours.
Don't understand the negative reviews. Prof Buhler is the GOAT !
Best Prof EVER !!!!!!
Best class ever!
One of my favorite classes Ive taken! Dr. Buhler is clear and willing to help. Tough class but if you study the material properly then you will be fine. Highly recommend taking his class!
Avoid him at all costs. Seriously. Run. No solutions provided for HWs, and then he based the entire midterm on homework. Even if you go to his office hours, you will still come out confused.

Be sure to avoid this prof. Promised to give exam similar to homework problems, which are already hard enough and no answers are provided, and gave a totally different thing in the exam. Be ready to learn by urself and dont expect his lecture could help anything. Always finishes his lec earlier, but why not use the time for more examples?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tara is passionate about linguistics + understands how to explain complex topics to non-linguistics majors. Lectures are very long + info heavy, but all notes/slides are posted online. Expect to have a mandatory 6-question quiz once a week + homework due every week. Tests are not hard, just a lot of info to study prior. Provides many office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Science of Language was a pretty difficult class, and actually very boring at times. There's A LOT of memorization so be prepared. The class is very organized but the material is pretty difficult especially if it's your first time taking linguistics. There were a couple complaints about this class so beware. Studying a ton I only managed to get A-

Tara isnt a bad professor, shes very knowledgable about the field and her lectures are informative. But this is a REALLY hard class. Theres A LOT of work and the material is not by any means easy. If you're taking this to fulfill a NATSCI requirement either take it pass fail or take another class. Our class avg was a B- so yeah. Definitely regret.

There was a quiz schedule that was given at the beginning of the semester. Prof. Byun keeps all her information slides & study guides on NYU Classes which is REALLY helpful. It makes for easy & organized studying. Her class is clear and recitation with Emily was great and informative! Loved it. Also,  just rent the textbook from Amazon for cheap!

I love this Spanish professor. As long as you participate in class and do the homework, this class is basically guaranteed an A. However, he gives 10 pop quizzes in the semester, so make sure you do the homework carefully, especially the readings, podcasts, and videos (series & movies). Lots of fun discussions in the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Goat professor, love him

Professor Burgos is a delight. He's incredibly funny and only speaks Spanish in class (at least for intermediate II idk his rules for other levels); however, during grammar lessons, he speaks English to be extra clear. Also side note he has a very relaxing voice, and he always tells stories and it's been really great for listening comprehension.

Felix is truly the best! The class has quite a lot of work (VHL hw, quizzes, presentations, 3 exams) but he makes it so enjoyable. His classes are very engaging and he's very funny. I'd highly recommend his class.

Incredible professor. Funny, understanding, and incredibly nice. 
He is not afraid to call you out on things and it is guaranteed that he will call on you at-least once per class, so you definitely cannot skip on his homework.
I love this guy. He's so funny and chill, but at the same time such a simple human being. Gracias!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super easy class if you've taken Spanish prior. To receive an A in the class make sure you complete all your MindTap assignments, which is an easy A and practice vocabulary. One way I practiced was making by making my own Quizlet cards. Felix was a really caring professor and super understanding. His classes are comical and honestly fun to attend.

If you need to complete Spanish 1, take him! Mr. Burgos is one of the best professors at NYU; you can tell he cares so much about the language, and helping everyone learn it at their own pace. He does pop quizzes, but if you complete the homework, you should get a good grade on them! There's a lot of work too, but he's very fair with grading :)

Felix is one of the best professors I've had and made me care about Spanish. He made class engaging, which really helps with learning Spanish. He's extremely understanding and a really nice guy. There's a lot to learn but he grades very fairly. The pop quizzes are fine if you're paying attention and doing the homework. Take this class with him.

The class moves pretty fast, and you'll be speaking Spanish from day one. Most of the stuff is done in pairs or groups, so you end up making friends. Burgos has a great voice and is super easy to understand. He brings a lot of energy and makes sure everyone gets involved. There are pop quizzes, but they're chill as long as you do the homework.
Very easy class. Feels a bit like high school though because it's Spanish 1, freshman, terrible Spanish accents, and tons of forced participating in a circle.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, would totally take again, always found a way to keep the content interesting and light even though the readings were dense. Personally not a fan of the final project but loved his teaching style, would def take again!

He's awesome. The homework load is not bad at all and generally straight forward. 3 tests, 3 writing assignments, & 1 final project (have to go & talk to spanish speakers). SUPER nice guy tho, very funny & relaxed. But get ready for pop quizzes (usually when you learn new verbs).

His class is very interesting and himself is very enthusiastic. He's fun and patient. The workload is moderate. Personally speaking, the quizzes and exams are not hard and if preview is well done, then you can get a high score. The grade is very fair.

He makes learning Spanish easy and fun. I looked forward to coming to class everyday. Nobody in our class had a single complaint about him. The class will be an easy A if you come to class, participate, and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Went into class thinking that Spanish was my least favorite class but it ended up being my favorite.  He actually made me want to learn the language and apply it outside of the classroom.  He is everything and more 10/10
Really friendly, patient, and easygoing professor! Still friends and greet him when we meet in campus
Great lectures. Very patient during classes and always ready to help

Definitely a solid and respectable Professor overall. Super chill, well organized, and I have no complaints. Love him as a person too. Take him if you can. Spanish classes require practice and a lot of work, but put in effort and it isn't difficult to get an A. Everything is laid out in the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The whole NYU Spanish department is known to be great, and Burgos really exemplifies that. He is very kind to his students and mindful of their situations, and his lessons are generally planned out perfectly. The Spanish department all follows the same material. Spanish classes are work, but Burgos made it bearable and engaging despite Zoom fatigue
I love him. He's hilarious and he makes classes super fun, you become friends with everyone in class. But he does make you talk to random people to practice.
Felix is my hero loved him as a person more than as a professor.

Professor Burgos is an angel. He made my experience this semester so much better. Hes super funny & class is always fun (you play games like Kahoot), youll make friends in the class because hes always pairing up students for activities. Work load is manageable as long as you stay on top of online HW & writing prompts. Definitely recommend!
nice guy, great voice and amazing beard
Honestly he's my president, great teacher great man
Loves Macchio Picchu
nice guy, great voice and beard

What an amazing, amazing professor and man. He's intimidatingly intelligent, caring, and funny. He genuinely wants his students to learn and develop their Spanish skills, and his passion is evident throughout each class. He appreciates improvement and participation, and workload is very manageable, especially because he follows the syllabus to a T.

He's such a great man!  I've definitely improved in this class and he had great methods of teaching. Make sure you actually try here,  these new concepts aren't that easy. Speak to him if you need any help and he will try to help you. This is a class where you will improve your fluency and knowledge about latin american politics.

Professor Burgos is awesome! He's very patient and willing to help students. The class covers a lot of material, but he manages to explain it well. There are lot of conversation activities, so be ready to talk in Spanish. Highly recommended!

Besides the fact that we had to buy a book we only used like once or twice, Felix is fantastic! The class was small and pretty chill and relaxed. He is very clear during lectures and his presentations are mega helpful. He also always has funny stories to share. He is truly a great professor! Te lo recomiendo!! Es el mejor!

Felix is young-ish, is very clear (both in speaking and in assignmentsgrading), patient, and helpful. He also has funny stories. The homework and assignments were not very difficult, just appropriate for the class. He connects well with students. Would recommend.
Felix is a great Spanish professor. He explains clearly the grammar and has fun stories. The prezi presentations are very helpful, if you ask, he will email them to you

Absolutely loved taking Advanced Grammar with him. He is one of the funniest teachers I have had. Very energetic and clear. Ask him for the Prezi presentations before the exams and he will email them to the class.

Taking Sight & Sound Film with Catherine was amazing! I was lucky to have a good crew, which definitely helped, but she's super caring and her lectures were always interesting. She also invited lots of great guest speakers. Class was very much about collaboration and giving your classmates feedback. Highly recommend!

Lectures can be long but she always tries to let us go early. She's really nice and caring, unintentionally hilarious too. Class was a wonderful space and she was a truly kind person and attentive professor. Not a harsh grader and you have lots of freedom
Wasn't lecture heavy. Wasn't the greatest professor but good person overall. For context pick good crews before you decide to blame the teacher

Had Catherine for S&S Doc. She's AWESOME. She will show you docs currently in the industry, she will push you to make your films happen. Getting feedback from her each time made me grow, and with 5 docs in one semester, you grow fast! can't thank her enough for what she's taught me.

Catherine is straight to the point. She gives really helpful, clear feedback and her class is a fun environment. I really appreciate her comments. Although they can sometimes seem harsh if you're not used to that sort of feedback, it'll help you grow in the long run. Would definitely recommend! One of my favorite classes I've taken at NYU so far.

As long as you follow the prompt, there is quite a lot of freedom. Class structure is loose. Lectures are not too rich but luckily are rare. Gives critiques. A bit of an oldhead- will mention the Godfather. Ultimately allows the class to be about collaboration and practice, which is great.

I had Catherine for both Documentary and Filmmaking S&S. While I'd definitely recommend her more for documentary, she was one of my favorite professors at NYU. If you take the time to get to know her she has such a big heart and also gives super valuable critique. She makes you work towards and recognize your strengths.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. She barely knew anything about the topic she was teaching and would sometimes "teach" us things that were untrue. She was also hostile to anyone who disagreed with her. Ruined what could have been a great class.

Catherine has a lot of knowledge and admiration for the medium and shares it with you. She's also very nurturing and open-minded, providing you with room to roam free with your ideas. Don't take her for granted. She's also honest with criticsm, but presents it tenderly. The class is somewhat loose structurally, but it certainly didn't bother me.

I enjoyed Catherine's class. She wasn't the best lecturer but she's a sweet lady that just wants to see her students succeed. If you come to class (she really doesn't like when students miss class if it isn't for a good reason) and participate in the group critiques and submit everything, you'll get an A.
I am using this professor's Textbook for my class and it's one of the most useless and vague texts I've ever had the displeasure of using in my education.

Professor Cabral is not a good teacher. The textbook you use is written by him and includes so much useless information. The useful parts are written in a very confusing matter. In lectures he just reads off the textbook and really doesn't explain much. His tests are really not that bad if you force yourself to read the textbook, but this is hard.

Lectures were highly ineffective. Even if you attend every lecture that does not guarantee you will do good in the class, as the tests rely heavily on the textbook. The lectures and problem sets are very different and have little to no correlation with one another. Thankfully, problem sets are graded based on effort, but are ultimately ineffective.

Although sometimes you will not be clear about the course content by only listening to the lecture, the course is manageable if you spend some time reading the textbook. The course is analytics/writing heavy so make sure you understand each topic very well!

Prof Cabral is a nice person and likely great high-level econ prof, but terrible for an entry course. He wrote the textbook, which is more real-world examples than econ concepts. Graded debates which don't help you understand econ better. Tests either impossibly hard or so easy you're Stern curved down heavily. Cross your fingers for a good TA.
PLEASE RUN AWAY FROM HIM, THIS GUY IS TERRIBLE, PLEASE RUN AWAY FROM HIM AT ALL COST
Memorize the textbook and hope that the stern curve will save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stern curve saves it all because everyone fails in this class. You need to do the discussion forum although you participated - so if you're a tedious monster who wants to get an A that bad, check the discussion forum every day. Exams are weirdly theoretical heavy, read the book. I repeat READ HIS 500 PAGE BOOK AND MEMORIZE!

He's the BEST professor EVER at Stern. Have no idea why so many people said bad things about him. It doesn't matter how hard the exam is since everything is CURVED at Stern. The slides are clear and the lectures were interesting. He was good at using econ concepts to explain real-world examples, which is the best part of the course.

His lectures are literally a regurgitation of the textbook (which is SO DRY). His tests are hard and when I went to his office hour, he didn't even make an effort to explain the concepts in a new/helpful way.

Professor Cabral is a really nice person but he simply cant teach. His lectures are just him giving his opinions on economic concepts and less of him actually teaching. Youll have to teach yourself most of the material either with the textbook or your own sources. The textbook can be useful at times but is poorly written.
He's a nice person. But be ready to read the textbook to prep quizzes and exams.
Great professor! Please take his class if possible!

Honestly not that bad if you pay attention in class and read the textbook. The quizzes are very similar to the homework. The examples he gives are interesting if you are into economics. A lot of people dont show up to the lectures

He lowered my grade AFTER he released a different grade on Albert. Terrible communication, unclear grading criteria, unclear course material, lectures are useless because everything is taught out of a textbook HE wrote.
Simply. Cannot. Teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are impossible to focus in, and even if you manage to pay attention, nothing he says will appear on any homework, test, or quiz. His textbook is unreadable, covers basically none of the math and equations required for the assessments, and is chock full of useless 'real-life' examples that confuse you more than they help. Horrible class.
Respected professor. But he cant teach!

Lectures is ALL OVER THE PLACE, if I haven't studied myself I would for sure fail this class. At the same time, the textbook of this class is his own task book,which is packed with content but HARD TO READ. He is a genuinely nice guy but there so much room for improvement for the lectures.

Bad professor plain and simple. Cant teach at all very confusing. If your TA isint good your grade is down the drain cuz thats the only way most people managed to pass the tests. He taught for maybe 30 minutes and had these useless speakers in our class who talked abt random stuff i didnt even pay attention. Avoid the class you wont learn anything.

Homework consists of weekly problem sets (2-3 hours). 2 quizzes, a midterm and final; all similar in difficulty to homework problems/ practice tests. Nice person, answers all your questions, but doesn't really teach and instead, invites a lot of guest speakers to take up class time. Essentially have to self study entire course by reading textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice man, but terrible professor. Uses his own textbook for the class, which is not bad at all, but his lectures are all over the place and literally seem like they're for a completely different class. Lots of guest speakers with no relevance to course at all. Tough grading on exams and quizzes. Avoid if you can.

He changed his syllabus this year and used his own textbook which had mistakes in it (making students even more confused). he never really taught in class but just had guest lectures and for HW we were meant to read the textbook and take notes from it. ur TA will literally save you, go for office hours otherwise it can be challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The whole class is a glorified textbook reading session
Textbook is of no use. Quizzes have no clear answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cabral is a nice guy. But unfortunately, being a nice guy doesn't help one cope with the unironically dozens of hours of self-teaching this course requires. He doesn't teach in class in the slightest. All learning is expected to be done independent from his own textbook, which has more pages of errors/typos than not. It's convoluted.

This class will not be as difficult if you've taken AP micro in high school. If not, this will probably be the worst class you take at Stern. He assumes the students have a lot of prior knowledge in the subject and tends to skip a lot of important/fundamental concepts. He only talks about real-world applications that aren't on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He changed the class so that it's entirely theoretical, no math involved. TAs are tough graders and only give full points for including every example, definition/term, and graph in the notes, even if your answer is right. Make sure to read the lecture notes and do all the practice problems he gives!
He never teach you anything but give you hard test. He grades students only on two tests, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes a great guy, but doesnt teach the material thats on the tests and quizzes. He goes off on tangent a lot. I recommend going to office hours if you need help.

Professor Cabral is probably a great guy. However, he is not that great of a teacher. He often goes off on tangents about random stuff like cod and drones which very little to do with Economics. His questions on homeworks/quizzes/tests usually either have nothing to do with the material or include include information we haven't learned yet.

It is definitely a tough course for freshmen, and for this prof especially, you need to do a lot of self-studying. if you do, you'll be relatively fine, but if you just listen in class and go to tests, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was a nice professor but I found he just didn't focus on the right topics during lecture. The course involved a lot of self-study because he would glaze over the more important topics and ramble on real-life applications. Maybe that was appreciated by some students, but the majority of what was covered in lecture did not ever appear on exams.
He's good. Homework and quizzes are easy, but the final is pretty hard.

CB was a wonderful professor! The range of topics covered in his class was so extensive, and I feel like food as I know it has been given all this dimension to it than ever before. Was supportive of every voice in the classroom, and just overall a funny and honest dude who loves the work he does. I had a great time participating in his class!

Discussion-based class and CB makes it very engaging. He gives out pop quizzes but if you do the readings you will be fine, mostly articles and videos, which are quite interesting and fun to read and watch anyways. No midterm just one final with written response questions. Take this class!
His personality is alright and I can see why students here gave him a 5-star rating. However, it is a participation matters class but he never calls on me.

CB is such a nice guy. He is so generous and always gives the extra credit. No midterm, only the final project/exam (you can choose by yourself). There are only 6-8 pop quizzes which is quite easy if you read the material. He is so great!!! You definitely need to take him!!!

CB is a great professor. He's extremely chill, easy to get ahold of, and hilarious. The work is pretty light, and he doesn't really require using highly academic writing in papers, which makes them really easy and fun to write. If you show up, do the readings, and participate in the discussions, you'll do well. Make use of the extra credit opps!

There are four reading responses for the class as well as four in-class quizzes. CB gives out lots of extra credit opportunities. The course is very inspiring as well, heavily based on current issues and innovations. Learned so much about food and the industry.

If you care about your GPA do not take her class. She is very strict with things outside of the quality of people's work, like participation, talking to your friend in class, being late… it will significantly affect your grade even when your works are strong.  Very unclear about grading criteria.

Not creative as an art teacher. Not much freedom for projects. Being too strict on attendance and phone use and no music during studio time. Better follow the rules and finish things on time. Not much critical thinking or discussions. But learned technical sculpture skills, if that's your priority in freshmen, recommend.

She is fine. I don't think I learned that much from this class. Although I got a good grade not many people were happy with their grade. She gives little time with the projects. Once she only gave us a day to finish our work, had to stay extra hours. BE ON TIME that is crucial. Also she doesn't let you use your phone.

A lot of work... be prepared to work 3+ hours outside of class. She is kinder than you might think though, and really cares for her students. Does give strict guidelines and makes you follow a clear set of rules when working on your projects. Do not take this class if you like to create art on your own terms, as you may find it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is so smart and nice. Her lectures were engaging and interesting. She cares about her students and spent a class period teaching us how to use linked in. She understands that to study public health we need to understand how to make connections in the real world and gave us many opportunities to do so! AMAZING! take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very kind and engaging prof! assignments were fun, lots of readings -- but discussions are super fun, kids in the class were smart. prof also hosted lectures on job search, plus let us connect to professionals in PH she knew. always excited to talk, introduced us to sm new things, all assignments equal weightage, attendance imp
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: her class is super interesting, her class is packed with knowledge, and the vibe is immaculate!

Take her!!! She genuinely cares about her students and her lectures are so engaging and interesting. Time definitely flies in this class. All the projects and the midterm/final are take home, and the grading criteria is clear. As long as you do your work and stay engaged, you're set! Best professor I've ever taken, honestly.
I really enjoy the ways her lectures are creative keeps me alert and I find myself interested in stuff I didnt expect to be. Also, really nice!

Avoid this teacher at all costs. I cannot believe she has lasted at the university for this long. She talks down to her students and will not budge if you try to reason reason with her. Her lectures are all over 150 slides and she does not even teach them. Oh, and she provides no study guides for exams. It upsets me that my money is going to her.

Lectures are confusing b/c info keeps repeating. Powerpoints are like 150+ slides and she edits them w/out posting the updated version. Tests are LONG (90 question final). During the midterm she made everyone get up and stretch which is distracting and frustrating. Its hard to do bad b/c of all the extra credit she offers and she is condescending

Dr. Stewart is genuinely invested in her students understanding the material. The way she conducts class aims to promote reasoning and asking the right questions. This makes the class difficult. You need to come to class prepared.

Terrible all around. Condescending even if you are a hard worker. Does not explain things clearly. Mistakes in slides, which are extremely disorganized. When people ask her questions, she tries to shut them up so she does not have to answer them, and makes you feel bad about it on top of it.  Any other professor but her. Ugh.

I liked this professor in the beginning, but then I learned how unflexible she is. She always talks in this soft voice, so it can seem like she is being nice, but actually she is talking down to you. Her lectures are disorganized and hard to follow (and boring). The only good thing is that she wrote the book, so its like a repeat of the lecture.

Agree with everyone else. She is very spacey/disorganized/unclear and it's a drag to sit through her class. She can patronize and disrespect you all while smiling and speaking softy (my guess is she is always trying to reduce her vocal effort, but still wanting to take jabs at you).
she is one of the worst teachers i have ever had.  she is totally unorganized, patronizing, and downright bizarre. she is not helpful and is mean spirited.

unorganized, unhelpful, unfair, mean, makes a lot of mistakes and will never admit to them. on a test, if you wrote something from your notes and she marks them as wrong, but you show her it was what she mentioned in class, points will not be rewarded. total ****

She really wants you to learn the material, which is great, but she doesn't know how to teach it.  She will make errors all over her notes and worksheets, but will never admit to them and will expect you to know what's write and wrong.
Took his class a few years back. He is a super caring professor and genuinely led me to make up mind to do a major in Spanish. Highly recommend.
He was easily the best Spanish professor I have had. He is completely understanding of any problems you may have.

He is the best Spanish professor at NYU 100%. He is so understanding of your work load for other classes and does his best to accommodate any issues. He genuinely cares about his students and wants us all to do well. He is a king!
super super sweet & generous with grading - homework can be boring but syllabus easy to understand and know what's due!

sooooo kind and understanding-- i needed to change the day of a presentation and asked a couple days before and he was so nice about it. although the class is quite work heavy, he's such a great teacher too, really passionate and clearly cares about everyone in the class! would very highly recommend.
So understanding. He sees your effort and rewards you for it. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Michelle is amazing. I would definitely recommend her as a TA for Intro to Soc. She's very laid-back and really knows how to foster a productive conversation. You can also ask her anything and get a good response, unlike a lot of TAs who just regurgitate the textbook at you. Grading-wise, she's pretty chill. The curve is like 60% get an A.
Michelle is super kind - complements what is learned in the lecture w/ really relevant info - very understanding! Def take her rec section
Michelle is the best TA in NYU. Provides solid feedback for your essay and replies email within a day. Defenitly take her session since soc1 is graded by TA.

Michelle was super sweet, caring, and always made an effort to make class fun and easier. She is always available for help and gives really good feedback on papers so you know exactly what you need to do for a good grade. Definitely take her if you can!

The best TA I ever had! She is very caring and inspirational. She doesn't curve grade and give students a second chance to edit their essay. If you have any problems, just talk to her, she is always willing to help. I would definitely take her course again!

Took this class a few years back. Awful TA: no kindness, no tailoring of the material to students' backgrounds, and most of all, exceptionally rigid in her teaching. There was no room for discussion and most students felt extremely scared of asking questions because the responses we'd get were so condescending and mean.
GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tough but interesting. Take it if you like the subject, she loves it and will inspire you.
all i have to say is dont take it

Great instructor, she really cares about her students. Difficult coding lectures and labs for beginners but she provides solid help to get over the initial struggles. Remote instruction didn't make this course easy but I think she really tried her best.
Great prof! loved the lectures, intense but super responsive and helpful. i really feel like i learned a lot, from the basics up

If you're looking for an inspiring professor, DO NOT take class with her. Every lecture was mind-numbing, just her reading straight off slides she refused to post. Also, if you ask for understanding during a pandemic or protests she'll just tell you she's "not your therapist or your friend". I ended up withdrawing, don't make my mistake! ����
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: great professor. very knowledgeable and super smart. she really got me thinking about cool stuff even if I was only taking it as a science requirement. inspiring lectures! her quizzes are really hard but at the end a fair grader and there are other ways to make up for the quizzes. only thing: too much material for a summer course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class, for an online class in the middle of two crises in America, was horrible. Her online quizzes were almost impossible to get a good grade on, and her attitude was unsympathetic to the status of the world. There were some quizzes, 1 paper, and 2 Tests. She read off her slides mostly, and one class legit just read a research paper outloud.

Paola does not care about students and her grading is just based on whether she likes you or not. Not only that, 20% of her grading was for participation but the only way to participate in the course is to interrupt the lecture and ask questions. It was completely subjective. Her quizzes were really difficult for a core class filled with non majors

She is tough and demanding, you need to put in the work and show that you make an effort. She has little patience for students that don't care, but her lectures actually got me genuinely interested and then I realized that she is beyond helpful, patient and knowledgeable. I learned much more from her labs than from lecture! She is amazing!!!

She is without a doubt the rudest professor/TA I have had at NYU. When you ask her a question, she always gives an answer in a condescending manner. I never ask questions on labs, because I know she is just going to give a nasty response. Great class, but choose a different TA.

At first a bad impression: very strict and demanding. In reality super caring and knowledgable. Yes, you need to work hard otherwise you won't pass. Very fair grader. A tough hard working woman - if you like anthropology she is amazing and inspiring!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great TA, and I really got inspired during her lectures to learn more about the topic. However, sometimes she does not really have a lot of patience if you don't understand immediately what she is talking about. She is super knowledgable but other people are not necessarily anthro majors! She is very helpful though and always available!

Paola is an amazing TA, the best I've had at NYU. She is really passionate about anthropology and really wants her students to do well! I'm not an ANTH major, but if she was to teach a class of her own I would take it!

Hands down one of the best TAs I've had. Super knowledgable, funny and interesting. The subject is at times dry and boring but you can tell she tries to make the best of it in her labs. Tough grader and NOT flexible with deadlines, but if you are on top of things you will be fine. Bonus: she's super hot so you really want to pay attention.

Professor Cerfon has done a phenomenal job! He's lecture notes are wonderful, and he gives amazing lectures! Prof. Cerfon is very caring of his student, very assecible (though he's busy), and relly trying to let his students understand the material well. Definitely choose him! He is the GOAT!
The best math prof at NYU
My math sucks but professor Antoine teaches so well that makes me feel I have to come here and give him a rating.

Great Professor and is dedicated toward teaching. Tests/ HWs are extremely difficult so that you will run out of time easily during the exams. Take it if you have significant amount of time to spend on this course.

Took grad complex var with Prof Cerfon as an undergrad. Presented the materials in a palatable manner, cared about his students, and had flexible in grading. He was passionate about the subject and willing to help you solve the hard hw problems during office hours. Exams will be fair if you study hard and understand the hws. DEF TAKE HIM!

Antoine is easily one of the BEST Math professors you can find here at Courant. He cares about students' progress and would meticulously explain anything should anyone comes to questions on it during class. Also has a great sense of humor. Could recommend 11/10

Professor Cerfon is an excellent math professor, he really tries to explain the concepts carefully, gives multiple ways to solve the problems, and is really open to questions both after class and in office hours. He was even willing to talk to me about how I'd learned the material in the past to better teach in the future. Nice review sessions too!

A brilliant Professor. Clear and helpful lectures complemented by his own notes. Exams are not unreasonable and he bundles weekly quizzes together so you only have to deal with them every month or so. Really great guy!

Cerfon is a really good professor. He explains abstract concepts well, and provides very detailed lecture notes (and he tells funny math-jokes in almost every lecture).  Homework is really, really, really hard, but he would help you solve them if you come to his office hours. And he curves the grade pretty generous. Really RECOMMEND his course!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cerfon is a very good professor in many ways. He explains the material well, and he understands how difficult the material is for students. At the end of the semester, he bumps your entire course grade by 1 letter grade if he sees that you have demonstrated excellent effort. Homework is insanely difficult, but his lecture notes should help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: This course was a really difficult course, I had to study like crazy. Prof Cerfon is a pretty average teacher by NYU standards (which, in my opinion, is pretty good!) He wasn't outstanding, but he was fairly energetic, which is necessary in a nearly 2 hr math lecture. Overall, I'd recommend taking him.

Pádraig was my best prof in all of undergrad. He truly gets to know you as a person, is incredibly understanding when personal problems pop up that take precedence, and he cared far more about our passion for the Irish language than our short term retention - he lit a fire in my that will last for a long, long time. Go raibh maith agat a Mhúinteoir

Padraig is the cool Irish dude you never knew you needed in your life. As others have said, he wants you to do well. I forgot what a question word meant on my oral exam, and he skipped the question. Just put in a little effort, and have a little fun. Also, enjoy all the singing. (He does take attendance).
No Comments
No Comments

Funny and passionate. Tests weren't hard but was a decent amount to memorize. Does provide resources. Multiple times, the TA gave out the wrong grades, sometimes a difference of 4 letters so be aware.

Christian is the absolute best! He is by far the most passionate InfoTech professor and curves very generously. There are some presentations and midterms and finals are quite easy. Super available after class for office hours as well!

Info Tech is supposed to be one of the easier Stern classes, but the professor made it a bit too difficult. There were so. many pop quizzes, and the content was vastly different from other sections as well. Don't take this unless you like Computers a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The GOAT. Her lectures are exceptionally well-structured, interactive, engaging, and inspiring. The course itself is extremely practical and useful. The workload is very reasonable. Super chill, kind, accessible, and genuinely cares about her students. One of the best professors I've had!

I took this class with Prof. Chiu two years ago. She is truly a great professor and very knowledgable in her field. The content are well organized and engaging, I also find that the coursework greatly helped me in my internship performance afterwards. Take her if you can! You won't regret it.
Her class is engaging. I would say she is the best professor I met this year. She is truly encouraging and supportive. The class content is well organized in a clear manner. Highly recommend.

Interesting, but lot of notes and information to keep up on. Genuine person and clearly wants to improve the best that he can, as he looks for feedback after every class. There were only two assignments he gave and harshly grades with no chance of extra credit. There's also lecture questions at the start of each class (all on exam which was easy).

MPAVP-UE - 1152 
Professor Citera is such a genuine person. He will seem a little cringy at first, but then you quickly start to realize that his teaching style really works (at least for most people). There was a lot of work for this class, however, that's simply because it's very important information. His call outs are very helpful for me. LOVE!
Long lectures, and random call on questions at the beginning of each week

The worst psychology class I've ever taken. He explained things fast (although NOT in depth) and therefore tended to overgeneralize. Confusing wordings of exam questions, never encouraged students to think beyond the lectures (or to raise questions). Not willing to have discussions after class, even when he was obliged to. Plus real bad TA.

Solid prof! Concise and digestible slides, zoom vids are posted so you can watch whenever on 2x speed. He posts straightforward review sheets for each exam, and exams have a 3-day period to complete, which is a lifesaver. I didn't find the textbook useful for the exams, but still interesting (and free) to read

His lectures are honestly really boring and dense. When he explains things, he tends to overcomplicate. His tests are easy, once you understand how he writes them. His wording can be confusing. But an A is easily achievable. Loved that it was online. He records every lecture so you can go back to it. Talks super fast though.

I had Professor Cimpian for Intro psych, and given that it was online, I still had a good experience. He lectures are very clear, sometimes a bit fast, so be prepared to take good notes to really help with the exams. He does offer an extra credit opportunity and is always willing to answer questions. Great class, and definitely recommend it.
Class was easy but not interesting. I wish it had been in person.

Great Professor!! He is apparently an extra qualified teacher who I guess have utilized knowledge in cognitive psychology to make the exams the fairest for students. He knows how students can really mess things up if they are nervous and how simply memorizing things is meaningless, and had probably structured his exams to avoid these problems.

LOVED Professor Cimipian for Intro to Psych. Lectures are super clear, interesting, and easy to follow. There are no notes on his slides, so be prepared to take notes. He does go too fast, allows for questions and makes sure everyone is engaged. Literally one of the best professor I have had to far at NYU, never had to worry about  his class.
I took him for Intro to Psych. I would definitely recommend his class. Tests were always fair, and the TAs were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cipani is knowledgable and very passionate about his subject. His texts and ideas class was fascinating, and if you pay attention you can get a lot out of it-highly reccomend!! Grading is left up to the TA's, so sometimes its difficult to fully grasp what they want from you, but my TA was pretty accessible outside of class/recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's easy to get a good grade in this class, but way too hard to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Cipani is fantastic! Visual Languages of the Renaissance, while sometimes a bit difficult to wrap your head around, has genuinely made me think differently. It sounds insane, but where ever I go, I am much more aware of symbolism in architecture, art, etc. and it has made me more curious about the world. A great elective Italian studies class
What a great guy and what a great class! Enough Said.

Fantastic. Clearly passionate about the subject matter of visual poetry (which is the class I had him for). Very interactive with students' questions and ideas. Kind and caring. Very smart. Often funny.
Chill lecture, sometimes readings can be hard to comprehend, but overall an easy class

This professor is the best; at first, I was a bit lost since it's not a typical class where you will typically understand the reading at first, which is okay since during your recitation, you and the TA will go over it together and it's going to help. There were about three/four mini papers, a page a two, which were helpful for your final essay.

Looooved his class. He takes attendance in the lectures and there's no notes/recordings so it's better to go---sometimes the readings can get overwhelming/confusing but since the professor explains them during lecture it's all good. Really fun recitations and the papers weren't too hard! I liked what we learned too.
enjoyed his class. engaging and informative.

One of the meanest and most confusing professors Ive had here. Very unclear with his feedback and what he wants out of students, and is an unnecessarily tough grader even when he sees students are trying. Demeaning as well. Would NOT take this professor ever again.

Best Italian prof I've ever had! Nicola is very passionate and knowledgable about his subject. Fun classes/discussions, not a lot of work, and you can get by doing only half the reading. Beneficial if you know something about linguistics, but if not, you'll still be fine. Participate in class and he'll love you.
he's one of the best prof I've had from Italian department. Very caring, his class is rather challenging, but really helpful tho. I am in love with him. period.
very clear, helpful and knows his stuff (obviously-he's f.o.b.) ... and i want his babies
great class - the professor was very helpful, concerned and encouraging
Great professor - thorough, challenging, friendly.
excellent instructor. class is fun and very informative
the instructor is a lot of fun and very helpful. highly recommended.

Great teacher! I would definitely reccomend him.  His classes are usually small, and he gets to know his students on a comfortable level.  He is a great guy.  His quizzes are a little tough, but if you study the material and go to class you will do fine.

Nicola made me love to learn Italian. He kept the class engaged, we all loved him and he is a funny guy. One thing you should know: he tends to come to class late, sometimes as late as 30 to 45 minutes. This gets really old after a while, but no one in the
so ****ing funny.  molto buono!
He's pretty funny.  Challenging though, expects a lot out of students.

I love Nicola! He's super fun/funny, not the easiest teacher, but you'll learn a lot and have a good time with it....except on the days when he comes to class in a bad mood...that happens, and then the party's kind of over...but he's awesome

Fantastic professor. It is very inspirational to talk to him, as when you say something that you think is correct but is actually silly, he would still treat it as if it is a serious theory but would then propose a little objection which makes you soon realize that it is wrong. Anyway, it is a pleasure to take his course.

Fantastic Professor. When you say something that seems to be correct but is actually silly, Professor Dorr would still treat it as if it is a serious theory, and then propose a little objection that makes you realize you are absolutely wrong. It is very inspirational to talk to him and be taught by him.

knows a lot about his subject, but cannot teach to save his life. Office hours are unhelpful, slides are unhelpful, readings are disconnected from material, extremely not approachable at office hours.
EXTREMELY difficult for philosophy students who don't have much previous knowledge of Math. Don't come

Amazing professor, extremely smart and knowledgeable in his field. Open to questions and gives amazing answers. During office hours you can expect to know a lot more beyond the class materials, which is great for any philosophy majors who want to dig deeper into the topics. Very adorable and friendly.
Confusing and not focused

It's been almost a year since I took Cindy's class and I am so glad I got her early on because not many people know how to teach writing. I had some bad profs since her, so now I can say I appreciate her more now then I did back then. At the time I thought she was giving us too much to do and being too picky; now I know why that was so important.

Teaches by "socratic" method; would have prefered to be taught by her- the person with real world experience. Very nice woman though; cares about students a lot; Her edits on papers were the most helpful thing, although she fell behind on those. Good class to get a overview of the journalistic method.
Take her class! She's awesome.

This was a tough class. Lots of writing and rewriting. I thought I was a good writer and came to realize I have a lot to learn about journalistic writing. But I feel I learned a lot in this class. She made us create blogs and I am happy with the way mine came out. I have a nice portfolio now, which I will build on.

She's tough. The class started out easy and then became harder. Just when I thought I was getting the hang of it, Cindy (she lets her call her by her first name) pushed us to do more. We created cool news blogs and I'm proud of the work I did in the class. Looking back, I'm really glad I took her section. So much better than the other ones.

I love Cindy and her class! She is one of the best professors I've ever had.  The class is a lot of work and the papers can get frustrating, but Cindy is so helpful and accessible.  We've had some great guest speakers and my writing has definitely improved.
I've learned a lot about good writing. It's not a conventional class. Her's is more workshop than lecture which works well because to get better you have to do it, not talk about it.
Vry nice and accomodating.  Not very demanding in terms of quantity but values quality.  Guest speakers ere always pretty interesting and very varied in their experiences.

Had her for Inquiry. She takes some getting used to, since she doesn't really stick to the syllabus, but she's a really nice person. Brought us pizza because she was happy with our rewrites. She's interested in our progress and wants to see us succeed. I like her way of giving us three big stories, instead of one every week.

Professor Rodriguez really worked us hard. Lots of rewriting of our stories, but the assignments were fun and just like she predicted my writing improved 100 percent. She's not like other professors who haven't been in a newsroom in years. She has a ton of experience and it shows in the way she conducts the class.

Eugene was a pretty cool professor. He did give a lot of readings, however they were all really interesting and gave different perspectives on environmental thought. I would definitely recommend taking his class!

Definitely a good man who is passionate about the subject, he just is not very open to others people ideas and does not make it clear what he is looking for in his papers. Only consists of 2 fairly short papers and one final research paper. Only take if you are actually interested in the history of disease.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Only take him if you are truly interested in learning more about Darwin/ evolution otherwise this class will probably bore you. This class is heavy reading but lectures are low stress. He requires blog posts which are not graded but will hurt your grade if you do not do them. I feel like he was a fair grader and he gave good feedback on essays.

Eugene is a really kind professor. He obviously is knowledgeable about ecological and environmental history. He connects a lot of the material to his own life, which isn't a bad thing. I enjoyed the range of readings he offered and the class atmosphere. While he grades a bit tougher on papers than other professors I've had, he's still fair.

I wish somebody warned me about Professor Cittadino, probably the worst professor I have had at NYU. His lectures were boring, reading assignments were ridiculously long, and the homework were extremely time consuming. He is a strict and tough grader. He will take off points if he doesn't like your idea and does not allow revisions. Do not take!!!
Amazing professor, extremely passionate and cares deeply about her student's success
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My god if only I knew what I was getting myself into! The class was overall fine, but the reading is quite hefty! The readings averaged around 300-400 pages a week, missed my Halloween. The reading is long and a bit boring with occasional times piquing my interests. The writing is fine and fun because you can choose your topics.
changed my life, let her change yours
idk about understanding, but she's definitely a person who teaches a class about writing

The semester started off rocky because the workload was difficult for the class to keep up with. But once she could tell that was happening, she cut it all in more than half. She was sweet and understanding throughout the semester, and was passionate about nurturing her students as writers. I honestly couldn't have asked for a better professor.
Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Read the book. Don't leave your essays till the day before. And engage in the Proust. Marcelle genuinely cares about your learning, but also about you. She'll read every word you put up on the blog, and rewards you for your hard work. Writing essays on Proust is hard, but your motivation should be the fact that you don't want to disappoint her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is extremely helpful. But read the book, for god's sake.
This semester is not over yet but I just wanna say that Marcelle is amazing. She could be extremely helpful if you follow all her instructions and read the book.

If you love to read and write, TAKE HER CLASS. She is amazing in every way; amazing feedback, involved and passionate about what she teaches, interested in your growth as a student, and a very very fair grader (there's no reason you shouldn't be getting an A with her guidance if you use her resources to your advantage.)

This year (2013-14) Marcelle was voted one of the best professors in CAS. There is no doubt in my mind that she deserved it. Proust is hard to read, especially for college freshmen, but Marcelle makes it worth it. Come to class, participate (both in class and online), and for the love of god, do the reading, and this class will be rewarding.
I am a creative writing minor, and if I could I would take all four of my classes with Marcelle. She is passionate and amazing. TAKE HER! no two ways about it.

Marcelle is FANTASTIC. She is completely dedicated to helping every student improve his/her writing, and she gives her students lots of individual attention. I learned SO MUCH from her--you have a write and read a lot, but it's totally worth it. She will without a doubt make you a better writer. She is definitely the CWP's best kept secret.

I loved taking a class with Marcelle. She is so friendly and warm and she really makes you write a lot so you get better. I didn't even see my progress till she showed it to me! She is really good! Takeee her!

Absolutely the best creative writing teacher I have had at NYU. If you can take her fiction class--or any class that she teaches, for that matter--take it. She completely cares about her students and makes that clear every day.

Marcelle is the best ever. She is such a great teacher and such a hilarious person; so smart, so sweet, so fun to be around. Take anything she teaches. I'd take computer science if she taught it. I love her.
there are a few people in a lifetime that have a dramatic impact on who you become as a person. Marcelle has the potential to be one of those few.
Interesting, passionate, old-world writer.  I want to be her.
Marcelle makes great snacks and likes to invite students to her home.  She also knows a lot about Proust and has all sorts of older lady class.
Can't understand
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like him! He's very smart but very VERY intimidating and pretty impatient when he thinks you're d*mb. You just have to soldier through because the ideas he presents are very valuable and he cares a lot about what he teaches.

The class itself is interesting, but as a professor, he tends to play favorites and is rather blunt against students at times. The grading criteria feels all over the place, especially as it doesn't seem as if there were plans for the finals/major assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content of this class is relevant and stimulating. The way it is taught is a different story. Clementi is a kind person, but he struggles to present material clearly, which makes lectures confusing. There is also no room for challenging his way of thinking. Finally, the grading criteria are unclear, with little transparency about expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If I were a fish, I would describe myself as British Fish and Chips (so fried). I can't focus because of his heavy accent. This amazing professor also likes to talk about random things that come to mind, even if they have nothing to do with the final exam. Please RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clementi, Clementi, Clementi, where do I begin? Both exams spread me wide open and made me feel like a sorority girl being passed around a football team. As I flipped through the exam, every question felt like it touched me from inside because I couldn't even write down a word. You better pray to every person you know because it's mostly luck :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lecture is difficult and unclear, and NO lecture notes so basically we can not find anything to prepare for the exam! Attendance is mandatory, and doing your own staff in class is not allowed!
Interesting class, but he ruins anything good about it. He can be very rude and is very biased. You lowkey have to suck up to him and even then he probably will not like you.

Professor Clementi is passionate about what he teaches. However, he gives unclear guidelines, he overcomplicates easy concepts, and rambles about one or two ideas without reaching the subject matter in the homework (and assigns mountains of readings). He encourages participation but argues with students. He can be disagreeable and rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People don't like Clementi because its a hard class and he's not afraid to tell you you're wrong. However, the class is geniunely interesting and applies economics to real world scenarios. Prof Clementi is definitely difficult and gives a lot of HW, but if you work hard and participate in class, you will succeed and find value in the class.

Evil professor, unclear final exam guidelines (most of your grade), you have to participate to get credit in the class. During debates will show a bias to one argument and will actively interrupt you when speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was genuinely intrigued during all parts of class. good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Old-fashioned, outdated, secluded in their own world, detached from reality

literally the worst class I have ever taken at stern. be prepared to work every week doing work that is useless to education and learning anything about economics other than letting him take half of the week off

Went off on tangents in class, the tests have nothing to do with any of the material. It is impossible to do well in participation. He is not a mean person, but he is an atrocious teacher who makes it extremely difficult to excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a difficult class, very few readings. Lectures alternate between being dense and free, while being only tangentially related to the exams. Exams expectations are unclear (they're case studies and no prior exams are given as examples). Can be difficult to get a hold of outside of class.

Never published the syllabus after changing it, assigns extremely long readings, and randomly pivots in topics. Gets mad if you can't understand what he is saying or if he can't understand your ideas. The final has nothing to do with the content - you can't review it. Still have not received a final grade, and it's spring sem already.

unpopular opinion he wasn't that bad!!! yes the final exam had little to nothing to do with his lectures but some concepts we learned in class were applicable to understanding the reading on the exam. he can be intense but just don't ask dumb questions to make yourself look smarter and it'll be fine

The lectures themselves are interesting, but he goes off on tangents on topics that arent relevant at all to the class. The tests are not related to any of the course material, and are impossible to study for. Participation is almost impossible to do well in. Not a mean person, just an atrocious teacher.

His lectures felt like some kind of fever dream. Changed the syllabus halfway through the semester. Final exam had absolutely nothing to do with in-class content or readings. Gave absolutely no information about the grading criteria or structure of the final. His classes are interesting, to say the least.

I don't really know what to say. He's nice but his exams have nothing to do with the content he teaches. His debates are so convoluted and he will start arguing with you mid-sentence. He knows what he wants he just won't tell you what it is. He's a sweet guy but be warned. Good luck BPEers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Worst professor of all time. Let me explain. 
- Changed syllabus halfway through the course
- Doesn't release readings more then 2 days before the lecture (in most cases)
- These readings range from 10-80ish pages
- No guidance on the final
- Will get frustrated at the class very easily if we don't understand something

Worst prof of ALL TIME
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hear me out, i didn't like most of the professors in my time at stern, but i loved this man - content was great, hes so unintentionally funny and chaotic, and he cooked up the group projects from a fiery fever dream, the tests were really difficult though, it wasn't an easy class, ugh gonna miss him
Honestly not a bad prof, just has a bad temper sometimes but he explains the concepts in a relatively clear manner and can sometimes be nice

Very difficult and stressful class as the lectures didn't align well with homework or tests. Recitation and TA office hours compensated for what the lectures lacked, so pray you have a knowledgeable TA. However, he did try to improve, asking us for feedback, and seems to care about students so I appreciate that.

Very nice guy and wants to teach very well. However, the homework and content can be very difficult. Recitations help a lot. Tests are curved and grading is lenient. Prepare to struggle but if you try and participate you'll be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice and caring guy. However, feels as though the lectures and homework are separate classes. Takes 10 hours to learn and solve HW every week. Unclear grading criteria on attendance/ participation. The final, worth 35%, was on concepts never taught or seen before. Disheartening, because I grinded hard to prepare and it was worthless.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Seems like a nice person. However, lectures have nothing to do with the homework or  tests.

Final was incredibly difficult and covered material that we had not seen at all in homework or class. Only hope is for the curve to save me.

DONT TAKE
Does not know how to teach. His lectures make no sense and has nothing to do with the H.W or Tests. This is essentially a self-taught class. DO NOT TAKE CLEMENTI

Professor Clementi seems like a nice guy. However, he runs the worst read-in-advance, discuss-material-in-class in possibly all of Stern. If you want to do well in this class, you need to disregard lecture and learn all the material online. He does care for his students at the end of the day though, so not the worst prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ruined my first semester, to say the least. You would expect prestigious schools to have decent Professors, but no. Probably the worst I have ever encountered. Do not go to lectures because he will just confuse you, you are better off checking out MIT's website and learning from there. TAs even mentioned that he can't teach for his life. Good curve
Freshmen, do not take this class, it will completely ruin your experience as a first year in college. This man clementi is the worst professor I have ever experienced.

DO NOT take this class as a freshman coming into NYU. Don't do it to yourself, it is not worth it; just take micro with algebra and get an A on that. Worst professor I ever had. The lectures did not help with the weekly homeworks at all, which took hours to complete and was probably still wrong. I had to memorize the solutions to pass the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The weekly homework takes HOURS to do. You have to basically teach yourself how to do it too. The tests are formatted exactly like the HW, but he doesn't give any review sheets or practice problems, and each concept is covered only once in the HW. The lectures are boring and you don't learn anything in them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class ruined my first-semester college experience. Clementi is the worst teacher I've ever had. Extremely bad handwriting and almost impossible to understand. Do yourself a favor and DO NOT take this class. The homework takes on average 4 hours to do and the tests are impossible. The class average for exams is literally around 50%.
Such a tough grader on participation. Homework, quizzes, tests are all extremely difficult. Strong accent. Bad handwriting.

Understanding him wasn't much of a problem for me. However, there is a wide disparity between the lectures and the homeworks. The lectures simply go over the concepts, not telling you at all how to solve any problems. Exams are hard, but are curved heavily. You have to work practice problems by yourself in order to succeed well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesnt ever give feed back so you never know how youre doing in the class. Has never responded to a single email of mine. He is the worst professor Ive ever had and I dont believe I learned a single thing from him. He doesn't allow for opinions, its his way of thought or the highway. He's basically a closeted conservative that thinks theyre liberal

chill guy, encourages students to ask questions and get help, but the content seems way harder than it needs to be. very lecture heavy. the weekly homework takes several hours to get through, and some of the questions are unclear and unnecessarily difficult. the exam is formatted similar to the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class made me hate waking up. Everyday, he drones on and on at 930 am and gets pissed if you ask any dumb question. Zero effort in making things understandable, just trying to flex his intellectual superiority in concepts that will never matter. Homeworks are stupidly long, and the Stern curve makes the midterm and final your entire grade.

Would give a 0 if possible. He teaches too quickly, gets annoyed at students who ask clarifying questions, and makes exams/HW extremely hard. While the university strongly recommended that finals be changed to online format, he decided to keep it in person for a class with more than 100 students, without even considering safety. TLDR: AVOID HIM.

Quite possibly one of the worst professors I've ever seen. He's not a bad person but he cannot teach if his life depended on it and the tests are based on what he teaches. He managed to make an introductory economics class a living nightmare and the homework is ridiculous as well as the tests. Don't take his class if you have a choice.

Lectures are useless and half of us are fighting not to fall asleep. Speaking of halves, half the auditorium is empty bc so many people dropped after the first midterm. HW seems alright bc he lets us do it in groups, but we've sat in the 3rd floor stern room for over five hours losing our minds over externalities and absurd numbers, its insane.

Buddy straight-up sucks at teaching. Couldn't find a textbook that was an appropriate level for the course so just gave us 3 and uses a mix like that makes any sense at all.
